english: How many years does a cocoa tree usually take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take about 3 to 5 years to start producing pods, while improved hybrid varieties can begin producing within 2 to 3 years if well cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaves turn yellow and drop during dry periods because the tree is under water stress, shedding leaves to conserve water and survive the harsh conditions.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei yɛ nu he haomɔ shishi. Ekɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to drop excess flowers if they are stressed by weather, lack enough nutrients, or if the flowers were not pollinated by insects.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi hao amɛ. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii shwieee fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and shade. You can control it by clearing weeds, pruning branches to let in sunlight and air, and removing infected pods so the disease does not spread to healthy trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba. ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa tree turning yellow and the branches swelling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eniji lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is carried from tree to tree by tiny insects called mealybugs. Since there is no chemical cure for the virus, removing and destroying affected trees is necessary to protect the rest of your farm from infection.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Ejaakɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ bɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ koni akɛbu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. They need shade trees or temporary nurse crops like plantains planted beside them to shield them from excessive heat and help keep humidity in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he ni eye ebua ni hulutsoo ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I protect my crop soil from drying out when the dry Harmattan winds start blowing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry leaves, grass, or crop husks—a method called mulching—traps moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents the hot winds from drying out your land.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo tsei ahe tsɔi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs extra fertilizer to support my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: If your plant leaves look pale or yellow, growth is slow, or fruit pods remain unusually small, your soil lacks essential nutrients. Testing your soil or applying recommended cocoa fertilizers helps restore these nutrients for better yields.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ, edalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo, loo aduawai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ loo okɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okɛ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni ená yibii kpakpai.

english: Why is burning my field before planting bad for my crop yield in the future?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ náa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills beneficial soil microbes that naturally feed your plants. Over time, burning leaves the soil dry, poor in nutrients, and prone to severe erosion during heavy rains.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ ahiɛ ni egbeɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa otsei lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off green, living branches from my healthy cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji eŋɔli ni hiɛ ka kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes overgrown or unproductive branches so the tree can direct its energy into producing large, healthy pods instead of excess leaves. It also improves airflow and sunlight, which keeps diseases from developing.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii agboi ni mli wa moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai babaoo baatsu nii. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la hu yaa hiɛ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai anaa

english: Why is letting weeds grow tall under my crops damaging to my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ashishi lɛ yeɔ mikpamɔ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Tall weeds also trap humidity and create hidden breeding grounds for destructive insects and fungi.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ hu mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ yɛ teemɔŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but most of them drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Trees shed flowers when they suffer stress from lack of water, poor soil nutrition, or insect attacks. Ensuring proper shade, pest control, and soil nutrients helps the tree retain its flowers until pods develop.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Shade care pest control Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: While food crops like plantain provide good shade for young cocoa, cassava roots spread aggressively and suck away vital water and nutrients that young cocoa needs, so cassava should not be planted too close to cocoa trees.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni akɛyeɔ niyenii tamɔ plantains lɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo kpakpa moŋ, shi Shi ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni kookoo bibii lɛ taoɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmei tsei tsɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ abɔle mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Shade trees act like umbrellas, shielding cocoa from excessive heat and helping the soil underneath retain the moisture needed for growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu kookoo he kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli.

english: How does direct sunlight help my maize crops yield bigger corn cobs?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ewo ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Sunlight gives maize leaves the energy to make food for the plant. Full sunlight helps the plant build strong stalks and produce large, well-filled cobs of corn.
ga: Hulu la haa ŋmãa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. Hulu la ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa tsei ni wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa agboi ni eyi obɔ.

english: How does covering the ground with dry grass help the roots underneath my crops?
ga: Te mulching yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the sunlight from overheating the soil. It retains soil moisture and turns into organic manure that feeds the roots underneath.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ fe nine. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava plants fail to grow big when the ground is too hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, soft soil to expand. Hard ground restricts root growth, making it difficult for the roots to soak up water and store food properly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ ni wa haaa shishifãi lɛ ada. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu ni amɛkɛ niyenii ato.

english: Why do I see so many small insects flying around my cowpea farm during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii babaoo ni miibɔle mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests become active in the heat of the afternoon to feed and mate. High temperatures speed up insect activity, making afternoon heat a common time to spot crop pests.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo tsuɔ nii ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ haa kooloi bibii lɛ anitsumɔ yaa oya. Ha shwane mli latsaa lɛ afee be ni sa ni akɛyooɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How can I protect my tomato blossoms from being destroyed by tiny flying insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mitato fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ akafite amɛ?

english: Tiny insects like whiteflies are attracted to bright blossoms and young leaves. Spraying organic solutions like neem leaf water early in the morning deters these pests before they become active in the sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi bibii kɛ baai bibii ni kpɛɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem baa mli nu shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa dani amɛbatsu nii yɛ hulu la lɛ mli.

english: What happens to the soil and lower leaves if I plant my crops too close together?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting too closely creates dark, crowded conditions underneath the upper leaves. This blocks light from reaching the lower leaves, traps damp air, and invites fungal diseases.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔ baa ŋwɛi baai lɛ ashishi. Enɛ baatsi la naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain trees turn yellow and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: As plantain trees grow, top leaves block light from reaching the lower ones. The plant naturally sheds these shaded bottom leaves to send more food and energy to the fruiting stem.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsiɔ la naa koni ekashɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Tsei shwieɔ nɛkɛ shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ shade nɛɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo amaje tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up when the sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. During intense sun, pepper plants curl their leaves to reduce the leaf area exposed to the heat and prevent water loss.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni eha baa lɛ he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni sɛɛ efoɔ lɛ naa.

english: How do sudden rains near harvest time affect my groundnuts underneath the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ saa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ahe?

english: Unseasonal heavy rains near harvest cause mature groundnut pods under the ground to rot or start sprouting prematurely, which lowers the quality of your crop yield.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be ni shɛɛɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ he lɛ haa ŋmei ŋmeii ni eda lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant stay green and grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Koolooi ashishi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it better to water my crops early in the morning instead of during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Water applied during the afternoon heat evaporates quickly into the air before the plant roots can soak it up. Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb maximum moisture before the sun gets too hot.
ga: Nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu babaoo dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil solution or insecticidal soap helps control these pests early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra.

english: Why do I find small worms eating holes inside the central funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Niyeli bu ko ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that loves hiding in the central funnel of young maize plants. Checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the funnels stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ awo ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting young cocoa until it is strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow big and healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo ni ewa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the wet ground, preventing leave rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during hot periods and avoiding excess nitrogen during flowering helps tomatoes set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ, kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tomato lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in poorly drained or waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my crops produce more yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds steal the water, nutrients, and sunlight that your crops need to grow strong. Clearing weeds gives your crops full access to these resources and removes hiding places for crop pests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ. ni ajie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for growth. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help restore the green color and boost your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni eda lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need standing water during growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties thrive in standing water because water controls weed growth and keeps the soil consistently moist, which helps the plants absorb nutrients easily.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ kudɔɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and fall off, and gently digging around the base reveals thick, firm tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaale akɛ edara beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni kɛ́ otsa shishigbɛ lɛ he blɛoo lɛ, obaana ŋmei ko ni mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can catch full sunlight to produce food. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground also prevents diseases and allows the plant to direct its energy into growing larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná niyenii. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ bulbs wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack sufficient water, suffer from pest attacks like mirids, or lack soil nutrients. Providing adequate shade, watering during dry spells, and controlling insects helps the flowers set into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛnɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuaa lɛ. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa hulutsoo ni sa Nu ni ehaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Ni kooloi akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Should I cut off the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, you should remove the extra shoots—called suckers—leaving only two or three strong ones per plant. Having too many suckers forces them to fight for water and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei Enɛ haa ŋmei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwieɔ tso kome nɔ. Shikpɔŋhosomɔi babaoo haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark black spots on the bottom while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato aduawai lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents this problem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the plant sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil or an appropriate insecticide controls these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants flower above ground but produce nuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow long stems called 'pegs' that push themselves down into the soil, where the pods mature safely underground away from heat and animals.
ga: Beni amɛwo ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen sɛɛ lɛ Amɛyɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do tiny holes appear in my harvested beans after storing them in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ amli beni mikɛwo kotokui amli sɛɛ.

english: Tiny holes are caused by bean weevils that feed on the seeds and multiply inside the storage bag. Drying your beans completely and storing them in sealed, airtight containers prevents these pests from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bean weevils ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ogbi o-beans lɛ kwraa ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite o-nibii lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed animal manure helps the leaves stay dark green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ akwɛ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and keeps it healthy.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes in the center of my corn leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei bibioo ko ŋmɔ bu ko ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei baa lɛ teŋgbɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of the plant during the day and feed at night. Inspecting crops early and applying recommended neem-based or chemical sprays into the leaf funnel stops them before they ruin the yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli yɛ shwane mli, ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni neem loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ awoɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Ani tsei ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for water, nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in thin plants and tiny fruits. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to bear large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in full sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside them provides living shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ adumɔ yɛ he kome. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb to catch maximum sunlight for photosynthesis. Lifting the leaves off the ground keeps them healthy, prevents rotting, and allows the plant to send more energy into growing large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛfee fotosintɛsis. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them in poorly drained soil during heavy rains. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the tubers safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa bulb lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Extreme heat, dry air, or irregular watering causes stress that makes pepper plants drop their flowers to save energy. Watering regularly early in the morning helps keep the soil moist and saves the blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he lɛ baa. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds fail to sprout during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetable seeds require consistent moisture and moderate warmth to germinate. Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of the soil quickly, so seeds need shaded nursery beds and daily watering to sprout.
ga: Aduawai dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i daa kɛ dɔlɛ fioo dani amɛ kwɛ̃. Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni afɔ amɛ nu daa gbi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when heavy rainwater sits on my land for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When excess water collects and sits on your farm, it stops air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and allowing soil fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa ni eshɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Nu baatsi enaa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why is burning my cleared bush before planting bad for my soil and crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Fire destroys helpful soil organisms and burns away organic matter that holds moisture and plant nutrients, leaving the soil hard and weak for your crops.
ga: La kpataa nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ ni eshãa nibii ni haa tsei lɛ amli nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ toɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni egbɔjɔ kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why does leaving untrimmed bushes around my farm bring more insects to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi tsei bibii ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ abɔle he? Ani miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo miiba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: Overgrown weeds and bushes serve as breeding places and shelters for pests, giving them a safe place to multiply before they invade your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ kɛ he ni amɛhiɔ. Ha amɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛfɔ dani amɛbatutua onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly after heavy rain washes away topsoil from my slanted farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-tilth ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away topsoil, which contains the rich nutrients and organic food your crops need to grow strong and produce good yields.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛ niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ yɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that dry out easily under harsh sunlight; without shade trees to protect them, heat pulls moisture out of the leaves faster than the roots can drink.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛji hulutsoo be ko bɛ ni baabu he lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: Heavy rainstorms quickly wash away fertilizer from around your plant roots into nearby streams, wasting your effort and money before the crop can drink it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli oya kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Fitemɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ oshika dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni anuɔ.

english: How do I know if the first rainy day of the year is enough for me to plant my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: The very first light rain only wets the surface of dry soil; you should wait until rain penetrates deep into the soil so your planted seeds stay moist enough to grow roots.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha hei ni egbi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas together on the same land with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa du yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as a natural food supply to help your maize grow better.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does a disease on one cocoa tree spread so fast to neighboring trees in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ kookoo tso kome nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Small insects like mealybugs feed on infected trees and carry microscopic viruses on their bodies as they walk to healthy neighboring trees.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ mealybugs yeɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ helai bibii yɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei anɔ beni amɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of water as a natural self-defense mechanism to preserve their own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leafy growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or when roots are drowned in waterlogged ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it important to follow a fixed fertilizer schedule for my cassava, or can I just apply it whenever I buy it?
ga: Ehe miihia ni anyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato aha mi-cassava lɛ sɛɛ. Aloo ani manyɛ mawo lɛ be fɛɛ be ni mahe?

english: Following a timed schedule is vital because crops need specific nutrients at distinct stages of growth. Applying fertilizer too late wastes money because the plant can no longer use those nutrients to expand its roots.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ he miihia ejaakɛ tsei biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, eheɔ shika ejaakɛ tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ atsu nii dɔŋŋ ni amɛkɛwo shishifãi amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of green leaves but drop all their flowers without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot, when water supply is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which makes the plant focus entirely on leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my cabbage plants keep growing open leaves without forming a solid head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai ni agbele ni efeee yitso ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when weather temperatures are too high or when they receive excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which encourages outward leaf expansion instead of head formation.
ga: Kaabage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Enɛ woɔ baai lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya kponɔgbɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee bulbs.

english: Why should I treat my seeds with recommended chemicals before planting them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu midumɔwui lɛ ahe nii dani mikɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ mli lɛ?

english: Seed treatments act as a protective barrier that prevents soil-dwelling pests, fungi, and diseases from destroying the seed before it sprouts, helping the young crop establish a strong, healthy start.
ga: Dumɔwui ahe tsofai tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmeii, kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛtoɔ shishijee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that transmit viruses, and heat stress makes the plant show these symptoms more severely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ni dɔlɛ mli haomɔ haa nɛkɛ okadi nɛɛ mli wa waa yɛ tsei amli.

english: Underground yam rot is usually triggered by waterlogging from poor drainage, soil-borne fungi, or small worms called nematodes that puncture the skin and allow decay organisms inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato fitemɔ baa. Fungi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ loo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni tsɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli ni ekɛ nibii ni fiteɔ baa emli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil moist while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, naturally hardy plants adapted to steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to overpower your crops if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ onibii anɔ kunim kɛji akɛ ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do my cowpea bean leaves start turning yellow and drying up once the pods appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: This is natural crop behavior; once flowering ends, the bean plant redirects all its energy and nutrients away from maintaining green leaves and puts it directly into filling and ripening the seeds inside the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii asubaŋ. Kɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Pea tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ ebaa ni ehaa ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow and stop growing when water stays too deep in my farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Even though rice needs plenty of water to grow well, too much deep, standing water smothers the plant's roots and prevents them from breathing air and absorbing essential soil nutrients.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ moŋ, shi nu ni mli kwɔ tsɔ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaaa amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn dark green and grow very tall, but end up producing very few grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ewoɔ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant put all its energy into growing tall leaves and stems instead of spending that energy to form healthy grain heads.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni daraa lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ pee dumɔwu yihi nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds very close to each other instead of leaving spaces?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than my planted crops after the rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil and are adapted to jump up quickly after rain to capture sunlight and nutrients before domestic crops can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Atsake lɛ koni efo oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ koni emɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani maŋ lɛ mli tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do flowers fall off my crops when the afternoon sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni shwane hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop its flowers as a self-defense mechanism to save water and survive the heat wave.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Fertilizer works best when applied during major growth spikes—such as early stem growth and just before flowering—so the plant immediately consumes the nutrients before heavy rains wash them away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo mli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ daa oya, tamɔ be mli ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ daa mra kɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ.

english: Why do insect holes in my crop leaves cause my final harvest to be small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ haa minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaves act like food factories that use sunlight to make food for the crop; when insects eat holes in the leaves, the crop produces less food and yields smaller grains.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii afeemɔ he, ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii. Beni kooloi yeɔ bu yɛ baai amli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii fioo aba ni amɛbaawo dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why do some grains on the same stem dry up while others are still green and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gbɛ́ɔ lɛ? Ani eji eŋɔli ni eyɛ blɛoo lolo?

english: Flowers on a single crop head do not open at the exact same hour, meaning individual grains develop at slightly different speeds depending on water availability and sunlight.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ efɔŋ yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko daa oya yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo nɔ. Edamɔ nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my harvested grain catch mold and spoil after I store it inside my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ beni mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain that is stored before it is completely sun-dried traps hidden water inside, which attracts mold fungi and insects that destroy the stored crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ dani egbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I keep saving seeds from my own harvest to replant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High-yielding seed varieties lose their vigor, uniform growth, and disease resistance after the first harvest, so planting saved seeds leads to smaller yields in following years.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why is my corn plant growing green and tall, but the cobs are not forming at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ? Shi ŋmei lɛ edako kwraa?

english: Corn cobs fail to form when the plant is stressed during its flowering stage. This is usually caused by a lack of water, missing nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus, or extreme heat when the plant is trying to pollinate.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ efeee kɛji tsei lɛ miihao yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa be mli ni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ

english: What causes my corn cobs to have missing grains or empty spots on the cob?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ elaaje loo ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ efee efolo?

english: Empty spots on a corn cob happen due to poor pollination. If the yellow dust (pollen) from the top of the plant does not land on the delicate silks during dry or rainy weather, those specific kernels will not grow into grains.
ga: Hei ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ sũ ni ji ŋmɔŋ (pollen) ni jɛ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ ekpɛtɛɛɛ siliki ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Nakai dumɔwui lɛ edaŋ ni amɛtsɔmɔŋ dumɔwui.

english: How can I estimate how much corn I will harvest before the actual harvest day comes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni makpa dani ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can estimate your total yield by counting the number of healthy plants in a sample row, checking how many full cobs each plant has, and multiplying that across the total size of your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu yibiiwoo fɛɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ ayibɔ ni oookane lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii enyiɛ tso fɛɛ tso yɔɔ. ni okɛ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ abɔ he.

english: What steps can I take to make sure my farm yields a higher harvest year after year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi manyɛ matsɔ nɔ makwɛ koni miŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii babaoo afi fɛɛ afi?

english: To get consistent high yields every year, rotate your corn with beans or peanuts to refresh the soil, use improved certified seeds instead of saved seeds, and regularly add manure or organic matter to keep the ground fertile.
ga: Bɔni afee ni anyɛ ana nibii ni afeɔ lɛ babaoo daa afi. Okɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa lɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔ. Kɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ atsu nii yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ najiaŋ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: What key practices do I need to follow to make sure I am farming my corn well?
ga: Mɛɛ nifeemɔi esa akɛ mafee koni makwɛ akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa kpakpa?

english: Farming corn well involves clearing and breaking up the soil properly, planting seeds at the correct depth and distance apart, removing weeds during the first four weeks, and applying fertilizer at the right growth stages.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmãa nubu ni aduɔ lɛ he ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ emligbalamɔ. Dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ he ni sa kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli

english: What will happen to my corn crop if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting corn too close causes the plants to fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin stalks and weak, small cobs with missing grains.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to grow strong leaves and cobs. Applying NPK or urea fertilizer around the roots restores green leaves and supports cob growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ akwɛ̃. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Does the type of seed I buy affect whether my corn forms full cobs?
ga: Ani dumɔwu henɔ ni miheɔ lɛ baaná bɔ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ baayi obɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, high-quality hybrid or certified seeds are bred to produce uniform, fully-formed cobs and withstand local diseases better than uncertified seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ji hybrid loo ni awo he odase lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ aba fe dumɔwui ni awooo he odase ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer assist me on my corn farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: An extension officer visits your field to inspect crop health, identify diseases or pests early, guide you on correct fertilizer timing, and show you modern methods to increase your crop production.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baasara he ni oyɔɔ lɛ koni amɛyakwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha. Kwɛmɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai mra. Wo bo ŋaa yɛ be ni sa ni akɛbaawo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ he. ni etsɔɔ bo ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni oootsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Which major pests stop corn from forming healthy ears, and how do I protect my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai titrii ni tsiɔ ŋmãa naa koni ekawo toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm eat the central leaves and young ears of the corn plant before cobs can fully develop. Checking your plants regularly and spraying approved bio-pesticides or recommended chemicals protects the ears as they form.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai kɛ amɛtoi bibii lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ otsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu toi lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees act as living covers that protect delicate cocoa leaves from burning, keep the soil moist, and create a cool environment for the seedlings to establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi.

english: Why does my maize grow much taller and greener when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in that same soil first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with beneficial soil organisms to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the next crop like maize is planted, it feeds on this naturally added nitrogen to build strong leaves and stalks.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye nitrogen ni akɛfata he lɛ koni ekɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop curl up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism against heat and drought. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, stopping water from escaping through its leaves so it can survive until cooler weather.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni etsĩ nu naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience severe heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to preserve its remaining energy for survival rather than growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛha wala moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other, won't I harvest more cassava roots from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ Ani minyɛŋ mafo ŋmei shishifãi babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. When cassava stems compete too closely, they grow thin and weak, resulting in small, poor-quality tubers rather than large yields.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ waa koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli beni ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ waa lɛ Tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii ni ehiii kwraa yɛ yibiiwoo babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plant turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle while top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main leaf vein indicates that the crop lacks sufficient nitrogen food in the soil. The plant moves its limited nitrogen from older lower leaves to nourish newer leaves growing at the top.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai wuji lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow and spread much faster than my cultivated crops even when they sprout at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants naturally adapted to steal nutrients, water, and light under tough field conditions. Farm crops are cultivated for yield quality, making them slower starters that require early protection from aggressive weed competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo mli koni amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ la yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Aduɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii koni aná nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishijee lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo, ni biɔ hebuu mra. kɛjɛ jwɛi akaŋshii ni naa wa mli

english: Why should I pinch off the extra sucker shoots growing on the sides of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Side sucker shoots consume water and soil food to make extra leaves instead of fruit. Removing these side stems directs the plant's energy straight into making larger, healthier, and faster-ripening tomato fruits.
ga: Lateral suckers lɛ yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛfee baai krokomɛi ni fata he yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ sɛɛ tsei lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni eha tomato yibii lɛ adara, ehi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack and destroy my maize crop while ignoring the cassava planted right next to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pests are attracted to specific chemical scents and leaf tissues of particular plant families. Fall armyworms prefer soft, sugary grassy plants like maize and cannot easily feed on the tougher, bitter chemical properties of cassava leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei akui srɔtoi amli baai ahe fãji lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Fall armyworms sumɔɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛyeee tsofai ni mli wa ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow plenty of tall stems and leaves during heavy rains but only swell their tubers later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ani yitso lɛ baafu sɛɛ mli pɛ?

english: During heavy rainfall, plants focus energy above ground to catch sunlight and build green foliage. As rainfall reduces, the crop transfers stored energy downwards into roots, causing the cassava tubers to expand.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛwo tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ falɛ ba shi lɛ, Dumɔwui kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ yaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: Why do the rain patterns keep changing, and how does that affect when I should plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ yaa nɔ etsakeɔ lɛ? Ni te enáa be ni esa akɛ madu tsei lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Unpredictable rainfall means traditional planting seasons are no longer reliable. Preparing your fields early allows you to take quick advantage of the rain as soon as it falls, preventing your seeds from drying out in unexpected dry spells.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ kusum naa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ahe saamɔ mra Ehaa okɛ nugbɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ hɔmɔ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ mli.

english: Why do my young crops struggle to grow even when the rain seems to have started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ po lɛ?

english: Early rains can be deceptive and might only wet the top layer of the ground. If the deeper soil underground stays dry, seedling roots cannot find enough moisture to survive short breaks between rains.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ tee nɔ egbi Dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi yɛ be kukuoo ni kã nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ mli.

english: What should I do to prepare my field right after clearing the weeds and bushes?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa he lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ?

english: After clearing the bush, you should mark out proper planting lines and seek advice on soil conditions before sowing seeds so your crops have the best foundation to grow.
ga: Beni ojie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ okadi dumɔwui ni sa ni oná ŋaawoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ he dani odu dumɔwui koni eha onibii lɛ aná shishitoo ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjɛ mli amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important for me to make straight planting lines on my farm instead of scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu ŋmeii ni ja yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã lɛ?

english: Planting in organized lines gives each crop enough space to catch sunlight and absorb underground moisture, while also making it much easier to weed, fertilize, and harvest later.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ daa yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ená hulu la ni ekɛjie shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaajie jwɛi, abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How does preparing proper planting rows help my crops get enough water during dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ line ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Organized planting rows help channel rain deep into the soil around root zones rather than letting it wash away over the surface, helping plants survive when rains suddenly stop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, moŋ fe ni eeeha efo kɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa.

english: How can I find out what is happening under my soil before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Agricultural extension officers can test your soil to explain what nutrients and conditions exist underground, helping you choose the right crops and fertilizers for your field.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ koni etsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow well on one section of my farm but fail on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome shi amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil conditions under the surface can vary across the same farm, affecting how much water and nutrients are available to root systems in different areas.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shihilɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Enɛ saa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know which crop type is suitable for the soil underground on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni sa kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops require specific underground soil types and depth. Getting technical information about your farm's soil structure ensures you plant crops that naturally thrive in that environment.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ henɔi pɔtɛɛ kɛ emlibotemɔ. Kɛ́ ona ŋaa gbɛ nɔ saji ni kɔɔ bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ koni onyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ yɛ nakai shihilɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I visit the district agriculture office before starting a new farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oooya Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ dani okwaayeli be hee lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: District extension officers have technical knowledge about local soil and weather conditions, offering tailored advice that saves you money and prevents crop failure.
ga: District extension officers have technical knowledge of local soil and climate conditions. Kɛtsɔ ŋaawoo ni sa ni ekɛaaha bo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa okɛ shika akafite, ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do input sellers recommend that I speak with an extension officer before buying farm inputs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe nihɔɔlɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ sɛɛkpee nitsulɔ ko awie dani mahe nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Extension officers work closely with sellers to ensure farmers receive technical guidance so they buy the exact inputs matched to their soil and crop needs.
ga: Extension officers lɛ kɛ jarayelɔi lɛ tsuɔ nii waa koni okwaafoi lɛ anine ashɛ ŋaa gbɛtsɔɔmɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii kpãa gbee.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the lower parts of your maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient corn needs to grow strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on it every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests and diseases to multiply.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei fɔɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when the Harmattan or dry season comes to save water and energy, protecting themselves from drying out until rains return.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ harmattan loo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Buu ohe he koni okagbi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their blossoms without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or a sudden lack of water, as a natural way to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ kpe. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ hewalɛ toɔ.

english: When water sits in the soil for too long, it starves the roots of air, which allows water-loving fungal diseases to multiply and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni hydrophilic fungi kɛbaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and hard while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa beni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads quickly when the farm is too shady, damp, and cool during rainy periods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli ewo hulutsoo, hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli, ni fɛ̃i tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: What causes tiny ragged holes inside the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes inside young corn plants are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf whorls to feed on the tender growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji fall armyworm caterpillars ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ lɛ baa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the surface of the soil, so when heavy fruit bunches grow, strong winds can easily pull the entire plant out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai ni atswa amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ dara lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei muu fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why should I avoid watering my vegetable garden during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu ni mikɛhaa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Watering during the hottest part of the day causes most of the water to evaporate before the roots can drink it, and wet leaves in hot sun can get heat-stressed.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni baai ni efɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need tall sticks to lift their leaves up toward sunlight, which allows the leaves to make food and grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ, ni amɛbiɔ niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow big. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding animal manure around the plants helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa Tsei ahe lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave dry corn stalks and leaves to rot on my farm instead of burning them after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmãa tsei kɛ baai ni egbi lɛ koni amɛgbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning removes good nutrients from your land. Leaving crop residues to rot slowly feeds the soil, keeps the ground cool, and helps the soil hold water for the next planting season.
ga: Shãa jieɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ahe nibii ni etse lɛ fite lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye nii fiofio Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny root pods that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. This natural fertilizer feeds the maize plants nearby without you having to buy extra chemicals.
ga: Peanuts kɛ pods bibii ni akɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai krokomɛi.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and moisture to protect the young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: The best planting material comes from the firm, hard middle section of a mature cassava stem. The soft green top stem rots too easily, while the very bottom wood takes too long to sprout.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa ni wa lɛ mli. Tso lɛ yitso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fiteɔ oya tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry period of several weeks. If seeds sprout after that single rain, the young seedlings will dry up and die before the real rainy season starts.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl into the center leaves of the maize plant to feed. Checking your field early and using the right pest spray early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow close to my crops reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors; they steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops. When crops have to fight weeds, they grow small and produce fewer fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni ehe baahia ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi awui lɛ Tsei lɛ baatsɔ bibii ni amɛbaawo yibii loo ŋmaa fioo.

english: Tomatoes split when the plant goes through a dry period and then suddenly gets a lot of water. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji tsei tsɔ be mli ni nu babaoo bote mli trukaa. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil becomes too dry. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and water so it can survive the dry heat.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or is waterlogged. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or compost helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing seeds when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when dry weather or heat prevents proper pollination while the maize is flowering. Planting at the right time and ensuring good soil moisture during flowering leads to fully filled cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination naa be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi. Dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kpakpa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ eyiɔ obɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the center leaves of my young maize stalks early in the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often called fall armyworms, target the soft, newly forming leaves at the center of young maize plants. Catching them early with recommended pest control prevents them from destroying the crop's main growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Okɛ ohiɛ afɔ baai bibii ni eba ehee lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does rice need so much standing water in the field compared to my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in wet conditions, and standing water helps suppress weeds while providing the high amount of continuous moisture that rice roots need to develop healthy grains.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Ni nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo ni yaa nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa shishifãi koni ŋmãa ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ haa.

english: Why does my upland rice suffer so quickly whenever the rains stop for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ yeɔ awui oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Rice has shallow roots compared to crops like maize, so it cannot reach water buried deep in the soil. During short dry spells, soil near the surface dries fast, making upland rice wilt quickly without extra water.
ga: Omɔ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa he. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ enine ashɛ nu ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa baagbo oya ni akɛ nu fataaa he.

english: Why do agricultural officers always tell me to plant beans on the land where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ mi be fɛɛ be akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting beans after heavy-feeding crops like maize restores soil fertility naturally for your next planting season.
ga: Beans ji ŋmãa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beans ni ooodu yɛ niyenii ni tsii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.
