english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of leafy green branches but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes bean plants to spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Using balanced nutrients with more phosphorus encourages the plants to blossom and form abundant pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe fɔfɔi lɛ. Niyenii ni ja ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Why do my bean seeds decay in the soil if I plant them right after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ waa lɛ?

english: Bean seeds absorb water very rapidly. If planted in soaked, oxygen-starved soil, the seeds rot before they can sprout. Planting in moist, well-drained soil yields much better germination.
ga: Peas shwieɔ nu oya waa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi dani amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I make sure I always have crops to harvest throughout the entire year instead of just once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni makpa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ fe shikome pɛ?

english: By alternating crops with different growing times—such as fast-growing beans and maize—and staggering your planting dates across seasons, you can maintain a steady yield of food all year round.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ bei srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. kɛ dumɔ gbii ni tsakeɔ yɛ bei amli Obaanyɛ okwɛ niyenii ni anáa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do insects destroy my stored maize and beans so fast after I bring them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eba lɛ?

english: Harvested grains often contain hidden moisture that attracts weevils and mold. Properly drying grains under the sun until they are completely hard and storing them in sealed, airtight containers protects them from pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ yɛ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la shishi kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa, ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their root systems are still small and their leaves burn easily. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, providing the cooler temperature, moisture, and protection young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo, ni baai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo be, hulutsoo, kɛ hebuu haa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. When nitrogen runs out in the soil, the plant starves its lower leaves to feed the upper growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ ba shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Curled leaves with yellowish patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the leaves from making food properly, which keeps the cassava roots from growing big.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa.

english: Planting seeds too close together actually reduces your yield because the crops will fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. When crops are overcrowded, they stay thin and weak, producing tiny ears or no grain at all.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa toi bibii loo dumɔwui bɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll upward and look tired during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni etɔ amɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick pepper plants use to protect themselves from intense heat. By curling their leaves inward, plants reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun and slow down the amount of water escaping from their leaves.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni pepper tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ awo mli lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather temperatures become too hot or when the soil gets too dry. High heat damages the pollen inside the flower, so the plant sheds the flower because it cannot form a seed or fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui loo amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I see holes in my young maize leaves and small worms hiding deep inside the central funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu yɛ ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? Ekɛ ehe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: The worms hiding inside the central funnel are Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and once hatched, the caterpillars crawl inside the funnel where it is dark, safe, and moist to eat the softest part of the growing plant.
ga: Kplukai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Kpũi lɛ fɔɔ amɛwuji lɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ́ efɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni mli efɔ koni amɛyaye tsei ni miida lɛ amli hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does cassava stop weeds from growing around it after it gets tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsiɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ naa lɛ? Beni eshɛ ŋwɛi sɛɛ?

english: As cassava grows tall, its large broad leaves branch out and create a thick canopy that blocks out the sunlight beneath it. Weeds need sunlight to sprout and grow, so the shade naturally suppresses weed growth on the farm floor.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei da lɛ Ebaai wuji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei ni mli tse ni tsiɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ naa. Jwɛi lɛ taoɔ hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start soft-rotting quickly when I leave them in a closed, hot room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are still alive after harvest and need to breathe air to stay fresh. High heat and poor ventilation cause moisture to build up on the skin, which creates the perfect warm environment for rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni ehe miihia ni amɛmu koni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why do my groundnuts form very small pods when I plant them in hard, unplowed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants produce flowers above ground, but after pollination, growing stems called 'pegs' must push down into the soil to grow pods. If the soil is hard and unplowed, the pegs cannot enter the earth, preventing proper pod formation.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ esa akɛ ashɛ Stems ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni pods lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni atsuuu nii lɛ Pin lɛ nyɛŋ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, pods ni sa lɛ efeee.

english: If I plant mango trees on my farm, how long will I be able to harvest fruits from them?
ga: Kɛji midu mango tso yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Be enyiɛ manyɛ makpa?

english: Mango trees are long-term investments; once a tree matures, it can produce fruit every year for decades, allowing you to harvest continuously long after your initial care costs are over.
ga: Mango tsei ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaanyɛ ewo yibii daa afi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Enɛ haa oyaa nɔ okpaa nii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ beni shishijee kwɛmɔ he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do mango trees take a few years to start producing fruit after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii fioo komɛi dani mango tsei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young mango trees use their early years to develop deep roots and a strong trunk. Investing care into them early on builds the strength they need to bear heavy yields of fruit for many years to come.
ga: Mango tsei bibii yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa Mra be mli kwɛmɔ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ Ebaawo amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛyashi afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: What happens if I stop spending money on weeding and care for my young fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji mikpa shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ mitsei bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ he lɛ?

english: Neglecting young trees allows weeds and pests to steal their nutrients, which stunts their growth, delays fruit production, and reduces the money you will make from future harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ aku hiɛ ashwie tsei bibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aju niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ naa. Ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa shika ni obaaná kɛjɛ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaakpa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it worth spending money every year to care for young mango trees before they bear fruit?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ ooofite shika daa afi koni okwɛ omango tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo yibii?

english: Yes, because the money you spend on fertilizer, clearing, and care during the early years is repaid multiple times over once the trees mature and begin generating steady yearly harvest income.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ shika ni ofiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ nɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Abaawo lɛ nyɔmɔ shii abɔ beni tso lɛ daa ni ebɔi shika ni anáa daa afi lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I know if my investment in a fruit orchard is actually giving me good returns?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ tso yibii abɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You are making a good profit when the total money earned from your yearly fruit harvest steadily grows to significantly exceed what you spend on farm inputs and labor.
ga: Omiiná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa beni shika fɛɛ ni onáa kɛjɛɔ yibii ni okpaa daa afi lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. No fe nɔ ni ofiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii kɛ nitsumɔ he lɛ kwraa.

english: Is growing tree crops like mangoes more profitable than growing seasonal crops like maize?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ mango lɛ adumɔ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kome mli tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: While seasonal crops give quick money, tree crops like mangoes yield harvests for many years without needing to be replanted every season, making them a steady, long-term wealth generator.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ yɛ be mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ afi tamɔ mango lɛ woɔ yibii afii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ daa be mli. Ha efee ninamɔ feemɔ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to produce fruit that can be sold to foreign markets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ aduawai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Selling produce abroad brings foreign currency like dollars or euros into the country, which boosts national income and allows buyers to offer farmers better prices for high-quality crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ maŋsɛɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ kɛ maŋsɛɛ shika tamɔ dɔlai loo euro baa maŋ lɛ mli. ni haa maŋ lɛ shika yaa hiɛ ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do changes in foreign currency values affect what I earn from my crops in Ghana?
ga: Te tsakemɔi ni baa maŋsɛɛ shika mli lɛ saa nɔ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ Ghana lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When foreign currencies grow stronger, Ghanaian crops sold in overseas markets gain extra value, which increases overall demand and market prices for farm produce back home.
ga: Kɛ maŋsɛɛ shika bafee hewalɛ waa lɛ Ghana tsei ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei lɛ naa sɛɛnamɔ kroko. Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni ataoɔ kɛ jarayeli jara ni akɛhaa okwaayeli nibii ni yɔɔ shia lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting fruit trees like mangoes on my land help the environment around my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ mango ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shihilɛ ni ebɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Fruit trees add to the natural canopy, protect topsoil from harsh sunlight, improve water retention in the ground, and support the overall health of nearby forest ecosystems.
ga: Yibii tsei haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ feɔ fɛo. Buu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha nu ni ahiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni eye ebua koo mli nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ fɛɛ ahewalɛ.

english: Can planting tree crops on my land improve the weather and soil for my other crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Yes, adding tree crops increases shade and vegetation cover, which keeps the local area cooler, helps hold moisture in the soil, and creates a healthier environment for neighboring plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni eha hulutsoo kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jɛmɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: My maize leaves have small holes and tiny green caterpillars eating them. How do I treat this crop sickness?
ga: Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii. Ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ ni yeɔ lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela nɛɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms. Much like treating an illness with medicine, crops need specific interventions like recommended biological treatments or approved insecticides, sprayed into the plant whorls early in the morning or late evening when caterpillars are active.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ nɔ. Tsei biɔ kwɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ, tamɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, shaded conditions. You can protect your crop by pruning extra shade tree branches to let in sunlight and air, removing affected pods quickly, and applying approved protective fungicide sprays.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ pods ni ena naagba lɛ oya. Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning yellow even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the plant's sap and transmitting viruses. Inspecting under the leaves and using targeted neem oil sprays or recommended insecticides will control the pests and stop the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaakudɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ni eha egbɛ eshwa.

english: How do I know if my soil has run out of food and needs fertilizer for my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hɔmɔ miiye lɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛha ŋmei?

english: When soil nutrients are low, plants show signs like pale green or yellowing leaves, thin stems, and slow growth. Applying organic compost or the right mineral fertilizer restores essential plant foods so the cassava roots can expand fully.
ga: Kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ baajie okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost loo mineral fertilizer ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa.

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain causes water to sit on the field without draining, the roots suffocate, allowing soil fungi to enter and rot the roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from excessive sun heat and keeping the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do extension officers advise me to space my maize seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafo ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amli moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Staking holds the vines high off the wet soil, maximizing sun exposure while keeping leaves away from ground-dwelling diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa wain tso lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my stored maize get destroyed by tiny insects even when I keep it inside bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli moŋ?

english: Insects like weevils often lay eggs in the maize while it is still in the field. If the grain isn't thoroughly dried before bagging or treated with safe grain storage dust, those eggs hatch inside the stored bags and eat the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwo kotoku mli loo okɛ dumɔwui atoohe sũ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotokui amli he ni akɛ amɛ toɔ lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from sprouting and shrinking in storage before market day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbɔjɔ yɛ nitoohe dani amɛya jara nɔ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to heat and moisture because the tuber thinks it is time to grow again. Storing yams off the ground in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded barn slows down sprouting and preserves their weight.
ga: Sweet potato baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ susuɔ akɛ be eshɛɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ sweet potatoes kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ehiɛ etsiimɔ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the bush and cut trees after clearing my land for planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi lɛ ni mifoɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ beni mijie kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and nutrients in the soil that young plants need. Leaving cleared vegetation to rot naturally keeps the soil rich, moist, and cool for your new cocoa seedlings.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni tsei bibii taoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni edɔ, ni edɔ kɛha o-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ.

english: How do I know if my newly cleared land has good soil for cocoa trees to grow well?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ojie lɛ nɔ ehee lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni kookoo tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, loose, deep, and allows rain water to drain properly without forming long-lasting puddles. If soil is too rocky or stays flooded, cocoa roots cannot spread or breathe.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ mli kwɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛi babaoo loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Cocoa shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo amɛmu.

english: Should I remove every single large tree from my land when preparing it for cocoa farming?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei wuji fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni misaa mihe koni madu kookoo lɛ?

english: No, you should leave a few large forest trees scattered across the land. Mature cocoa trees need permanent light shade to protect them from strong winds and intense sunshine during the dry season.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oshi koo mli tsei wuji fioo komɛi ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ni hiɔ shi daa koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to heat and bright light. Without shade, direct sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out their roots before they can establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la he waa. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛma shi.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting plantains on a new cocoa farm before or at the same time as the cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji heei amli dani adu loo yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Kɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large broad leaves that provide instant shade and cool moisture, protecting young cocoa seedlings while they grow during their first two years.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to transplant cocoa seedlings into my field?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant cocoa is at the beginning of the major rainy season. This gives the roots plenty of water to grow deep into the soil before the dry season begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo ji nugbɔ be ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa nu babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: If cocoa trees are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in weak trees with few pods. Crowded branches also trap damp air, causing pod diseases.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa. Niji ni mli tse lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ. kɛ pod hela baa

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster right after I clear my farm, and how does that harm my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya waa beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Ni te no saa mikoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Clearing exposes weed seeds hidden in the dirt to sunshine and rain, making them sprout quickly. These weeds steal water and soil nutrients from young cocoa seedlings, choking their growth.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baashɛ amɛnɔ. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya Jwɛi nɛɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ. ni haa dalɛ kpaa

english: Why is it important to add compost or manure to the hole before putting in a young cocoa seedling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu lɛ mli dani adu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Manure or compost improves the soil structure and holds moisture like a sponge, giving young roots easy access to slow-release nutrients as they start growing.
ga: Manure loo ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tamɔ sponji. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ oya beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off lower branches from young cocoa plants as they grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches encourages the cocoa plant to grow a strong upright stem and form its main branches at a healthy height, making management easier and improving airflow around the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa, ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ. ni ama tsei niji titrii lɛ kɛyashɛ he ni sa Ehaa nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major nutrient for green growth. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where small roots cannot reach, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa lɛ Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shishifãi bibii amli. not accessible No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni amɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when I clear all the shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or food crops like plantains to shelter them, the intense sun dries out their leaves and stem before their root system is strong enough to pull enough water from the soil.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water stays on my farm for too long after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive and grow. When excess water sits on the field and cannot drain away, it starves the roots of air and creates damp conditions where harmful soil fungi grow and cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ etsi ŋmɔ ko mli ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ. Nu baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ amli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ aba ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ adara ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: Why do small insects attack my pepper flowers and cause them to fall off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛmiiha amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tiny pests like thrips and aphids suck juices from delicate flower buds, causing the plant physical stress. When pepper plants get stressed, they drop their blossoms to preserve water and nutrients rather than building new fruit.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips kɛ aphids lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ baa tsei anɔ. Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ miihao Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii heei.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce very small bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are large and need sunlight to produce food for big fruit bunches. When suckers are planted too close, their broad leaves shade one another and their roots compete for the same soil food and water, leading to smaller bunches.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ dara ni amɛbiɔ hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha aduawai akui wuji lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off without setting fruit during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High heat damages tomato pollen, making it sterile so flowers cannot be pollinated. When a flower is not pollinated, the tomato plant naturally sheds the flower because it cannot form seeds or fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa Tomato Pollen lɛ Feɔ Fɔlɔ No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ pollen haaa. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollination lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui loo aduawai.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready for harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When groundnut plants are mature, their main leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can dig up a test plant; if the inside of the shell has dark brown veins and the nuts fill out the pod completely, they are ready to harvest.
ga: When the peanut tree is fully grown The main leaves will begin to turn yellow and fall off. Obaanyɛ okɛ kaa tsei atsu nii. If the inside of the shell has dark brown lines and the pod is full, it is ready to harvest.

english: Why do my yam vines struggle to grow long when weeds cover the base of my yam mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ miitao ni eda be kakadaŋŋ be mli ni jwɛi miiha mi-sweet potato lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, moisture, and sunlight meant for your yam plants. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil nutrients available for the yam vines to climb and feed the growing tuber.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ o-sweet potato tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ni amɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans improve the soil for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the ground. When these leguminous plants finish growing and decay, they leave behind natural nitrogen fertilizer that feeds the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ daraa ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ, Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmei koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my oil palm seedlings grow very slowly if I plant them directly into hard, unplowed ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛtsuuu nii lɛ?

english: Hard ground makes it very difficult for young, tender oil palm roots to push through and search for moisture and plant food. Digging a wide hole and mixing the soil with organic manure gives the roots loose dirt to spread out quickly and establish a strong plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ji mu lɛ akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli ni amɛna ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei niyenii. Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ ajie oya ni efee tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to give fertilizer to my crops at specific stages of their growth instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ amɛdalɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli moŋ fe ni mawo amɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Just like people need different amounts of food at different times of the day, crops require specific nutrients at key growth stages—such as nitrogen early on for leaf growth, and potassium later for fruiting. Applying it all at once can burn plant roots or waste fertilizer through rain runoff.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii srɔtoi he hiaa gbɔmɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ, tamɔ nitrogen yɛ be mli ni baa lɛ daa lɛ shishijee mli. kɛ potassium sɛɛ mli kɛha yibiiwoo Kɛ́ akɛ fɛɛ tsu nii shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sun and lose water rapidly through their leaves. Shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and sheltering the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains the exact same nutrients every year and allows specific soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ aba afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the hot afternoon is a plant's natural self-defense to reduce its surface area. By rolling its leaves, the plant slows down water loss and protects itself from intense heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba ehiɛ shi. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni amɛbaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots compete heavily for the same water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves block sun from each other, resulting in lower yields and smaller tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the crop lacks nitrogen. The maize plant automatically moves its limited nitrogen from older lower leaves up to feed the newer, growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my main crop help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni mikɛ miŋmɔ titri lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil with food for nearby crops while ground-covering leaves reduce soil moisture evaporation.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa niyenii ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. yɛ be mli ni baai ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ haa sũ mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is my yam crop growing lots of green vines but giving me very small yams underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ yɛ wain tsei eŋɔli babaoo shi amɛhaa mi sweet potatoes bibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer causes yam plants to spend all their energy producing heavy stems and leaves above ground instead of storing nutrients below ground in the tuber.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off some healthy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ mikoko tso lɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning excess branches allows fresh air and light into the middle of the tree, which stops fungal diseases like black pod from spread and directs the tree's energy into developing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ la boteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ agbɛ ashwã. ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even after I have already applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than domesticated crops and actively steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops, leaving your plants hungry despite the added nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shi otsei lɛ hɔmɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ po fata he.

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from my best maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved and hybrid seeds lose their special strength and yield potential in the second generation. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures your crops grow uniformly, resist local diseases, and produce the highest possible yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ adalɛ daa. helai ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni ekɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ni fe fɛɛ baa.

english: What makes some crop varieties produce fruit much faster than traditional crops?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei komɛi woɔ yibii oya fe tsei krokomɛi?

english: Scientists breed fast-maturing crop varieties to focus energy quickly on producing fruits rather than growing tall stems, allowing you to harvest early before dry spells or pests take over.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ tsei ni daa oya koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ ama yibiiwoo nɔ oya moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa nii mra. Dani hulutsoo be loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees grow better when I plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade to cool the young cocoa trees and keep moisture in the soil during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I crowd more plants into my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsei babaoo fata midumɔ he lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving no plant with enough energy to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes transplant shock because their tiny root hairs break and dry out in the midday sun. Planting late in the afternoon or on overcast days gives roots time to recover.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ shwiemɔ he shoofeemɔ baa. Yɛ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi bibii lɛ ahewɔ Amɛfoɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my healthy fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mitso ni woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niji komɛi?

english: Pruning removes extra branches so the tree stops wasting energy on leaf growth and instead sends all its nutrients toward developing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baajie niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ hewalɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ baai lɛ adalɛ he lɛ. Ni yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo tso yibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though it is raining heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean plants are missing key nutrients like nitrogen, which heavy rains often wash too deep into the soil for root systems to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I grow cassava on the exact same patch of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in that piece of ground.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if there are no insects on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital food, fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your main crops underground and above ground, starving your plants before they can mature.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Why do pests attack my green crops more heavily when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: During dry spells, pests search aggressively for moisture and nutrients, turning your watered green crops into the main target in an otherwise dry area.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ hiɛdɔɔ taoɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ha tsei eŋɔli ni okɛ nu fɔɔ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ titri ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ.

english: If I cut the tips off my cocoa branches, won't that damage the tree and stop it from growing?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo nine lɛ naa lɛ Ani efiteee kookoo tso lɛ ni ekpaŋ edalɛ?

english: Trimming branch tips actually stimulates the tree. When you cut the ends, it signals the plant to quickly push out fresh, healthy new shoots right behind the cut, helping the tree grow thicker and stronger.
ga: Niji lɛ ashishifãi ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ akanya tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji ofo naagbee lɛ Etsɔɔ tso lɛ koni ekɛ oyaiyeli ajie ŋmeii heei ni he wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Why do new shoots sprout so quickly right after I prune my tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: When you cut a branch tip, the plant directs its energy to the dormant buds just behind the cut. This causes a sudden push of rapid new growth in those areas.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ nine lɛ naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kpoo ni yɔɔ niji lɛ asɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa yifalɛ hee baa oya yɛ nakai hei lɛ.

english: Does trimming the ends of my crop branches help me get more places for pods to grow?
ga: Ani tso lɛ nine lɛ naa ni aaafo lɛ haa gbɛ babaoo baaha tso lɛ yitso lɛ atsɔ?

english: Yes, trimming the ends forces the tree to produce more side branches. More healthy branches mean more flower cushions where new pods can form in the future.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tso ko naa ni aaafo lɛ baaha tso lɛ niji babaoo akwɛ̃. Niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo tsɔɔ fɔfɔii akushɛi babaoo. ni baaná pods heei Ebaanyɛ eba mli wɔsɛɛ.

english: How does cutting back old plant growth help control the way my crop grows?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni egbɔ lɛ adalɛ ni abaaba shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ?

english: Pruning gives you control over the plant's shape and energy. Removing the tips forces a rapid flush of fresh branches lower down, keeping the plant compact, healthy, and easy to manage.
ga: Kpojiemɔ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ bɔ ni otso lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ, ebaaha tsei niji heei lɛ atsɔ oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ewaa ni ekɛ nitsumɔ waaa.

english: Does a ripe pod keep taking food and water away from the tree if I leave it hanging?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baamu niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ he kɛji mishi amɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he?

english: No, once a pod fully ripens, it naturally disconnects from the tree's feeding system and stops drawing nutrients from the mother tree.
ga: Dabi, be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa. Ekɛ tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kpaa gbee ni ekpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli lɛ jiemɔ.

english: What happens inside a ripe pod if I don't pick it from the tree on time?
ga: Mɛni baa yɛ tso ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli kɛji ajieee lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Because the ripe pod no longer receives food from the tree, the seeds inside will start to germinate or rot. Leaving overripe pods on the branch also attracts pests and diseases to your farm.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ náaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Kɛkɛ lɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ loo fitemɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ, no hu gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ helai. hu ba oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do young pods on my tree grow bigger while fully ripe pods seem to stay the same size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ daraa yɛ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii ni eda lɛ hiɔ shi nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The tree only sends active nutrients to young, developing pods. Fully ripe pods have finished growing and stopped feeding from the tree, allowing the tree to redirect energy to the younger crop.
ga: Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ pɛ. Pods ni edara kwraa lɛ edara ni ekpa tso lɛ niyenii yeli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ yaa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it bad to mix overripe cocoa pods with my newly harvested ripe pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ baafutu mi ŋmeii ni mikpa ehee lɛ?

english: Overripe pods may contain sprouted or rotting beans. If you mix them with freshly harvested ripe pods, it spoils the fermentation process and lowers the overall quality and price of your cocoa.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aná ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpa ehee lɛ futu mli. Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ efiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛ ejara baa shi.

english: If I harvest my ripe pods promptly, will it help my tree produce new pods faster?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ani ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii heei oya?

english: Yes, harvesting ripe pods on time frees up space and tree resources, encouraging the tree to focus its energy on flowering and supporting the next batch of young pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni oookpa yɛ be naa lɛ baaha oná he ko babaoo kɛ tsei ahe nibii babaoo. Wo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔii anɔ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi bibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does delaying my harvest affect the final quality of my beans?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛbaagbe naa lɛ saa mi-beans lɛ naagbee su lɛ he?

english: Delaying harvest causes beans inside the pod to over-ripen or germinate. When dried and mixed with good beans, they create off-flavors and uneven quality that buyers will reject.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ashwere fe nine loo amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ egbi ni akɛ ŋmeii kpakpai futu mli lɛ Ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baakpoo.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight dries out their soil and burns their tender leaves. Leaving large shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a cool environment that protects young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehaa ehe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam plants produce tubers underground using energy from sunlight collected by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which results in larger and healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ toɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them for long periods because they cannot breathe in soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away easily, keeping the roots safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-decomposed animal manure will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so that the rain does not waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akafite shika?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but avoid applying it right before a heavy downpour. Heavy rain washes the fertilizer off the field before the plant roots can absorb it, whereas moist soil helps dissolve it safely into the ground.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni ooowo dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests to multiply. Rotating your maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and starves out crop-specific pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ feɔ babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ hɔmɔ baagbe tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny yellowish dust left inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛyɛ sũ bibii ni ji ŋmɔŋ? Eshwɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides and feeds inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars are active helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by stealing light, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. When weeds crowd your field, your crops get less food and water, leading to smaller leaves and reduced yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni jwɛi ebɔle ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná niyenii kɛ nu fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ bibii ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves droop during hot afternoons even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to save moisture, but they usually recover in the cooler evening as water loss slows down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ gboɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi amɛfɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli be mli ni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that small insects do not eat holes in the grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi bibii akaye ŋmãa lɛ mli buji lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils need moisture to thrive in stored grain. Dry your maize thoroughly in the sun until it is completely hard before storing it in clean, sealed hermetic bags or treating it with safe storage dust to protect it.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii hia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛdara yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Ha ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani okɛwo kotoku ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa mli. Aloo okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ato he koni ebu he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is short on nitrogen in the soil or is sitting in flooded ground. Without enough food or dry soil, the plant cannot produce the green color needed to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eta he ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo kɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shading the cocoa and keeping the soil cool while the cocoa trees grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks into the ground for my yam plants to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread out their leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing disease and helping the plant direct energy into growing big underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny worms hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Akɛtee mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. These pests feed on the tender inner leaves of young maize, which can ruin your crop leaves and stunt growth if left untreated.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmãa bibii amli baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite tso lɛ baai kɛ edalɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime heat is too intense, when the plants do not get enough water consistently, or when there are not enough insects around to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This results in thin, weak plants and a much smaller harvest overall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo kwraa baa yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds during the first few weeks after my crops sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops grow slowly at first and get choked easily by fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli, ni jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tsei lɛ naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: How can I know when my cassava roots are mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground right around the main stem starts to swell and crack from the growing roots below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni efoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Covering the ground with dry foliage (mulching) keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth, holds water in the soil longer, and prevents weeds from popping up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni jeɔ kpo lɛ anaa.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already moist after a mild rain and the crops are actively growing. Applying it to bone-dry soil or during heavy downpours can burn roots or wash the fertilizer away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo ni ŋmɔshi nibii miida lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo efɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I grow other crops on my farm if cocoa gives me the most money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ kookoo ji nɔ ni haa mináa mishika fe fɛɛ?

english: Growing food crops alongside your main cocoa crop protects your family's food supply and gives you extra income during the months when cocoa is out of season.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu yɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oweku lɛ niyenii he. Ni ehaa onáa shika kroko yɛ nyɔji ni kookoo be lɛ bɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: How much of my farmland should I use for cocoa compared to other crops?
ga: Shikpɔŋ enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛdu kookoo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe?

english: Most experienced farmers devote the majority of their land to cocoa for primary income, while saving a smaller portion for crops like plantain and vegetables to feed the household and diversify yields.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo kɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ fa ko haa kookoo akɛ amɛshika jɛɛhe titri. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ shika fioo ko to kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ aduawai ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ shia kɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ srɔtoi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow better when I keep shade trees on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow under forest canopy; shade trees shield cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, conserve soil moisture, and drop leaves that rot into rich natural fertilizer.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei ashishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Will planting cassava near my young cocoa trees affect how the cocoa grows?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaná ŋmei lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cassava feeds heavily on soil nutrients and can block light from young cocoa, so it is better to space them properly or use plantains which provide better shade without overpowering the young cocoa.
ga: Yucca heɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ eha kookoo bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ bɔ ni sa. Aloo okɛ plantains ni haa hulutsoo kpakpa ni tsiii kookoo bibioo lɛ naa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let air flow and sunlight in, which reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ aba shi. ni ekanyaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo

english: What causes some cocoa trees to produce many big pods while trees next to them produce very little?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji waa yɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ? Yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Differences in pod count depend on sunlight exposure, soil fertility around the roots, proper pruning, and how quickly pests or diseases on individual trees are treated.
ga: Esoro pods lɛ ayibɔ yɛ hulu la lɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni baa tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ lɛ yaa oya.

english: Why do cocoa trees start bringing out flowers right after the dry season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ?

english: The return of rain after a dry spell triggers the cocoa tree's natural cycle to produce flowers, as the moisture tells the plant it has enough water to nurture young pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo lɛ kɛɔ tso lɛ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ niyenii yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Pods turn black due to a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads rapidly when excess rainfall and heavy shade trap moisture on the pods.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ hewɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ mɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is rich enough to plant cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, soft, retains moisture well without getting waterlogged, and easily supports heavy-feeding crops like plantains and cocoyams.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ plantains kɛ cocoa lɛ mlɛo.

english: What general practices make a farm stand out as exceptionally well-managed?
ga: Mɛɛ nifeemɔi ni afɔɔ feemɔ haa ŋmɔji feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ?

english: A top-performing farm combines healthy cocoa main crops with proper plant spacing, regular weeding, timely pruning, disease control, and a good mix of supporting food crops.
ga: Okwaafoi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa feɔ ekome. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Jeŋ ni afoɔ yɛ be ni sa mli, helai ni akudɔɔ, kɛ tsei niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a wide, clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat, which dry out their delicate leaves and soil. They need shade from nurse crops like plantain or taller trees during their first two years to protect them while their root systems develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ baaha baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi tamɔ plantains loo tsei kakadaji adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ he be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until the rains become regular before planting my maize seeds instead of planting after the very first shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ aba bɔ ni sa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rainfall is often followed by a short dry period. If you plant too early, the heat and dry soil will scorch the newly sprouted seeds before the main rainy season starts, causing your crop to fail.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baashã dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, onibii lɛ baafite.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizers, manure, or compost helps the plant regain its green color and yield healthy ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai eŋɔlii Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with food that maize plants need to grow strong, reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with wooden stakes while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei akwɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch sunlight for growth and stay away from damp soil where diseases thrive. Staking helps the leaves produce energy to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛdara. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni ji helai srɔtoi ahe lɛ he. Staking haa baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from very dry soil, extreme heat, or a shortage of essential nutrients. Regular watering during dry spells and feeding the soil with compost will help the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ lɛ mli baa lɛ kpe. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when heavy winds blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the soil surface, making top-heavy trees easily fall when carrying heavy bunches. Planting them closer together to block wind and using sturdy bamboo poles to prop up fruiting stalks prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa tsei ni ŋmeii ni tsii yɔɔ mli lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ amɛmiiwo ŋmeii wuji. Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni abu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Ni okɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa atsu nii ni okɛfi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ koni akaje amɛshishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning pale yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in tomatoes are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or fungal diseases that thrive in high humidity. Spacing your plants wider apart allows air to dry the foliage and reduces disease spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo fungal helai ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the base of the stem looks thick and woody. You can gently dig up one root to check its size before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ tso Obaanyɛ Ofo shishifã tso kome fiofio koni okwɛ bɔ ni edara ha dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize lose the special vigor and disease resistance of the parent crop, leading to smaller ears and unequal growth. Buying fresh certified seeds every season ensures high yield and uniform crop growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ haaa hewalɛ ni fa fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ helai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa toi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ tsei adalɛ daa.

english: Why do insects keep returning to eat my maize crops even after I spray the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa koni amɛbaye mi-ŋmã lɛ beni mikɛ tsofa efɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Insects often lay eggs under leaves or in the soil where chemical sprays cannot reach. If you do not rotate your crops or clear surrounding weeds, the new insects hatch and continue eating your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii woɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ baai ashishi loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo jwɛi tsakeee amɛhe lɛ, Kooloi heei baafɔ ni amɛya nɔ amɛye otsei lɛ.

english: Why does planting the exact same crop in the same farm plot every year reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that plant needs from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating different crops gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter what kind of water I use when mixing chemical sprays or liquid fertilizers for my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ nu mikɛfutuɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛhaa mi-vegetables lɛ?

english: Yes, using muddy or dirty water can bind to chemicals and fertilizer, preventing plants from absorbing them properly. Always mix your agricultural inputs with clean water so they remain effective.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji loo muji ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsofai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpɛtɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ okwaayeli nibii lɛ afutu nu ni mli tse koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam plants turn yellow when heavy rains leave standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns the plant roots by blocking oxygen in the soil, which causes root rot. Making raised mounds or ridges with drainage channels helps excessive rain flow away from roots.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baatsi naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is slightly moist and the crops are growing actively, preferably early in the morning or late afternoon. Avoid applying fertilizer during heavy downpours or on dry, cracked soil.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Esa akɛ awo lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni egbɛ eshwa nɔ.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I place them too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and weak while producing very few, small fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa.

english: Why is planting my crops in straight rows better than scattering the seeds across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ fe ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?
