english: Row planting ensures every plant receives enough space and sunlight, while making weeding, fertilizer application, and harvesting much easier compared to scattering seeds randomly.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewaaa kwraa akɛ abaajie jwɛi, abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa trukaa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and look weak right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock caused by heat and root damage. Moving seedlings during late afternoon when the sun is cool and watering them immediately helps them settle into the field.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ shwane mli beni hulu lɛ edɔ lɛ, ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch in strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide living shade, protecting the cocoa from intense heat until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo. Buu kookoo he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi ebaatsɔ shweremɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so it does not spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving cassava in the ground for too long makes the roots woody, tough, and less starchy, lowering its market quality.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tso, amɛhe wa ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jarayeli lɛ mli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an important plant food in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted compost helps the leaves turn green so the plant can grow big leaves and heavy corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji. Tso lɛ baanyɛ afee baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer off the field or pushes it too deep into the dirt before plant roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but heavy downpours are not expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays around them for too long because the soil cannot get air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu kroko ni fa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves keeps the sun from drying out the soil too fast. It keeps the soil cool, saves water, and stops weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye obɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which love hiding inside the center funnel of young corn. Checking your crop early and applying appropriate control methods stops them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii bibii ateŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi nakai tsei lɛ anaa dani amɛfite amɛyitsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves. Removing affected leaves or spraying with recommended organic or chemical treatments helps new leaves grow normal again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni ena hela lɛ loo akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai heei ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are like baby trees and burn under full, direct sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain creates temporary umbrellas that protect young cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ dumɔwui ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly watered helps the plant turn flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa fɔfɔii feɔ aduawai.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans or cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plants. Planting them together improves soil fertility and gives you two different crops to harvest from one field.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ekɛ niyenii haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food that grows large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground toward the sun, preventing leaf diseases and helping the tubers grow bigger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulbs ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings burning and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain alongside them provides necessary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baai lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya. Nurse tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms instead of forming fruits when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ lɛ?

english: When heat is too intense, tomato plants enter a survival mode and drop their flowers to conserve water and energy, preventing fruit from setting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baaya shihilɛ mli ni amɛbaajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkagbee shi

english: Pale yellow leaves on maize are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency, meaning the soil lacks the basic food the plant needs to build green, healthy leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very bushy with lots of leaves but yield very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ pepper fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to put all its energy into leaf and stem growth rather than producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and crooked instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil mounds to expand freely; if the soil is hard or full of rocks, the growing tuber gets restricted and deformed.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa ehe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ Tuber ni miida lɛ tsiɔ naa ni efiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by planting stems taken from already sick plants.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ŋmei baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies loo ŋmeii ni miida ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even if I planted them in good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. amɛfeɔ ekome be fɛɛ be ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's maize harvest yield less crop than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Most commercial seeds are specially bred hybrids whose strong traits only last for one generation, so planting saved seeds results in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji dumɔwui ni afɔ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni yɔɔ sui ni mli wa yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I water my crops in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ tsei anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli?

english: Watering in high afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate instantly before reaching the roots, and water droplets on leaves can act like magnifying glass lenses, causing leaf burn.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa shãa

english: How long should I wait after planting before I apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Kɛ́ midu nii lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Young plants need time for their roots to establish in the soil. Applying fertilizer too early can burn sensitive young roots, so waiting until the roots grow stronger allows the plant to absorb nutrients safely.
ga: Be he miihia tsei bibii koni amɛtswa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛ ni shishifãi lɛ baawa lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni eŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why am I advised not to apply fertilizer during the first four months after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɛɛ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 4 ni adu sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: During the first four months, young crops draw enough natural nutrients from the soil to build roots. Adding strong chemical fertilizer during this early stage can overwhelm and damage the delicate root system.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛfee shishifãi. Ni akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ fataa he yɛ shishijee mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I apply fertilizer at the wrong time of the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ be ni esaaa mli?

english: Applying fertilizer at the wrong time—such as during heavy rains or when plants are dormant—can cause nutrients to wash away, wasting your money and potentially burning the crops instead of helping them grow.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli, tamɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ ehiɛ edɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ nu lɛ mli. Shika ni afiteɔ ni ekolɛ ebaashã ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it safe to mix two different types of fertilizer together before putting them on my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ baafutu mli dani mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Not all fertilizers can be mixed together. Mixing certain chemicals can cause reactions that destroy the nutrients or make them harmful to your soil, so you should always ask an officer which types combine safely.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi afutu mli. Tsofai komɛi ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni fiteɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ obi nɔyeli lɛ mli onukpai lɛ be fɛɛ be nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops look scorched or burnt after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã loo eshã beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when fertilizer is placed too close to the plant stems or applied in heavy amounts. The high salt content in fertilizer draws moisture out of the plant, causing leaf burn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ loo akɛwo mli babaoo. Nu ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa shãa

english: Why do recommended fertilizer rules for our farms change from time to time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mlai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ?

english: Soil loses different nutrients over time depending on what was harvested previously. Recommended rules change so that you only apply what your soil is currently missing for that specific season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli nibii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Edamɔ nɔ ni akpa tsutsu lɛ nɔ. Mla ni atsɔɔ lɛ tsakeɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ elaaje lɛ pɛ atsu nii kɛha nakai be lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is actually ready to receive fertilizer?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo diɛŋtsɛ akɛ ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo efeee klalo?

english: Soil is ready when it is moist and crops have established healthy roots. If the soil is extremely dry or waterlogged, fertilizer will either be wasted or harm the root system.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛji edɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etswa shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Fertilizer baafite loo ebaaye shishifãi lɛ awui.

english: Why are farmers asked to test new fertilizers on small trial plots first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abiɔ okwaafoi ni amɛka ŋmɔshi nibii heei amɛkwɛ yɛ shikpɔji bibii ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Trial plots allow you to test how a new fertilizer performs on your specific soil type without risking your entire harvest or spending money on your whole farm upfront.
ga: Kaa shikpɔji lɛ haa onyɛɔ okaa bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ okwɛɔ. ni ekɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ wooo oshara mli loo ekɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ efiteee kɛtsɔ hiɛ.

english: How long does it take for chemical fertilizer to start showing visible results on my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ náa hewalɛ ni kadiɔ mɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Granular fertilizer usually takes about one to two weeks to dissolve into moist soil and show greener leaves, while liquid fertilizers applied directly to leaves can show results in a few days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ heɔ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ajie yibiiwoo kpo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: How long does a complete crop trial process take before we know if it was successful?
ga: Be enyiɛ tso lɛ he kaa ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ baahe dani wɔle kɛji eye omanye loo eyeee omanye?

english: A crop trial usually takes a full growing season—from planting through to harvest—so you can accurately compare the final yield and quality against your regular farming methods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei akasemɔi heɔ amɛdalɛ be muu fɛɛ. Kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ mli No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ yibiiwoo kɛ naagbee su lɛ ato okwaayeli gbɛi ni okɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from strong sunlight. Big shade trees block harsh sun rays and keep the air and soil cool, preventing the young cocoa leaves from burning and drying out.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Tsei wuji haa hɔnɔ, ni amɛtsĩɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa, ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã ni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow instead of dark green even though there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build strong green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to turn green and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii tso titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni wa, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, won't I get more harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too closely makes crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. When they fight for resources, they stay weak and produce very small cobs, whereas proper spacing gives each plant enough food to produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Beni amɛwu yɛ nibii ahe lɛ Amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Curled and yellow cassava leaves are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties stops this virus from spreading on your farm.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baatsi helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Maize uses up a lot of food from the soil, but leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Abɛi ni ooodu yɛ abele ni odu sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested last season to plant again this year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi nɛɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strong traits in the next generation, producing smaller plants and far less grain. To get high yields every season, it is best to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds each planting time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bibioo, ni dumɔwui lɛ hu faaa kwraa. Bɔni afee ni aná yibiiwoo babaoo daa afi lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli. Be fɛɛ be ni abaadu lɛ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or lack of water in the soil. Giving the plants enough water and covering the soil around them with dry grass helps hold moisture and stops the flowers from falling.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛaaha tsei lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni akɛwo mli. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi lɛ, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my stored cowpea grains get full of tiny holes and turn into powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui stash lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: The small holes are made by tiny insects called weevils that lay eggs in the stored grain. Drying the grains thoroughly until they are very hard and storing them in airtight hermetic bags suffocates the insects and protects your yield.
ga: Kplukai bibii kɛ bu bibii baa. Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmei. ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui ni ato mli lɛ amli Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa waa ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebu onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops immediately after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to steal water and food from the soil faster than domestic crops. Removing weeds early in the season ensures your crops do not get starved of the water and light they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ akaná nu kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting inside the mound before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rain stands around the roots in heavy soil without draining away, or when soil pests bite the roots and introduce rot fungi. Making high mounds with loose soil helps water drain away easily and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ fite. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni sũ ni mli tse yɔɔ mli lɛ ni aaafee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni eha yitso lɛ mli egbi ni ehiɛ hewalɛ

english: Spacing your plantain suckers about 3 meters (10 feet) apart gives each plant enough space to spread its roots, receive sunlight, and grow strong without competing with neighboring plants for nutrients and water.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ o-plantain ŋmeii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa, ni enáa hulu la, ni edaa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why do so many tiny shoots keep growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ. Mi dumɔwui titri lɛ shishitoo

english: These tiny shoots are called suckers, which are the plantain tree's natural way of reproducing. If you leave too many growing together, they steal food and water from the main tree, so you should trim off most of them and keep only one or two healthy shoots.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni plantain tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ efɔɔ bii lɛ. Kɛ oha amɛfee ekome kɛdara tsɔ lɛ, Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ gbɔ tso lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ mli babaoo ni okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi.

english: Can I plant cassava and plantain together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ plantain yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, planting plantain and cassava together works well because cassava stays shorter while plantain grows tall, allowing you to maximize your land space and harvest two different crops from the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains kɛ cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ cassava lɛ yɛ kuku yɛ be mli ni plantain lɛ kɛlɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwereɔ babaoo ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough food to grow healthy plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha plantains ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ?

english: Healthy soil for plantains is dark, rich in decayed leaves, and drains water well after rain. If your soil is sandy or pale, mixing in organic manure or decomposed crop waste before planting will provide the food your plantains need.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha plantains lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ baai ni fiteɔ babaoo ni eyɛ nu kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋã loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛ́ okɛ organic fertilizer loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi ni egbo lɛ futu mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaha o-plantains lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bo lɛ.

english: Is it better to plant my crops right at the start of the rainy season or in the middle of it?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: It is best to plant right at the start of the major rainy season so that young crop roots can establish themselves deep in the moist soil before the heavy rains slow down or dry spells begin.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ ama shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ shɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba shi loo hɔmɔ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and drying from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turning yellow often means the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it could be a sign of soil fungal disease. Clearing away old leaves and applying manure or fertilizer helps healthy leaves grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo ebaanyɛ efee tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he okadi. Kɛ́ ojie baai momo lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do strong winds easily fall my plantain trees when they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ mi-plantains lɛ shi oya kɛ́ amɛbɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots, so when heavy bunches grow near the top, the trees become top-heavy. You can support the trees by propping them up with strong wooden poles placed under the heavy bunches.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tso agbo lɛ bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni wa ni akɛwo jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ ashishi lɛ aye abua tso lɛ.

english: How do I select the best plantain sucker to plant on my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a wide base, rather than suckers with broad leaves. Sword suckers grow faster, produce stronger stems, and yield larger bunches of plantains.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword bud’, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance ni shishigbɛ lɛ mli kwɔ. Yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, Sword suckers lɛ baadara oya. Bɔɔ tsei ni mli wa ni oha plantains babaoo

english: Why are weeds growing so fast around my newly planted crops, and why must I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mihe lɛ? Mi tsei heei ni midu lɛ Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie nakai jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally adapt faster to rain and sunlight than cultivated crops. Clearing them regularly removes competition so your main crops can get all the soil food, water, and sunlight they need to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛya daa lɛ, ebaajie akaŋshii kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ onibii titrii lɛ baanyɛ ana shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when a bunch of plantains is mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni plantains ayibɔ ko da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready to harvest when the individual fruits swell, lose their sharp side ridges to become rounded, and the dry flower ends at the tip easily rub off.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko efuu. Ekɛ esɛɛ tsɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa shi ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains around them to block the intense heat, the sun burns their leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he fɛɛ he Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its power to feed my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ?

english: When soil loses its nutrients, crops grow very slowly, their leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green, and the stems stay thin. If your harvest gets smaller every year even when there is enough rain, the soil is weak and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni tso lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ mli etse lolo Kɛji akɛ onibii ni ofeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant cassava on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives soil pests a permanent home. Changing crops or resting the land allows the soil to rebuild its strength naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eha kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aná shia ni baahi shi daa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛjɔɔ he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which thrives in cool, overly wet, and dark conditions. It spreads when rain droplets splash germs from infected pods or wet soil onto healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod kɛ enɛ baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ Efɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ duŋ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ jɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ amli kɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off the unnecessary small branches and chupons growing on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? kɛ chupongs bibii Jiemɔ nibii ni he ehiaaa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Extra branches waste the tree's energy and water on leaves instead of pods. Removing them lets sunlight and air pass through the tree, which keeps diseases away and encourages the tree to produce bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ moŋ fe ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up like tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water in the heat. By rolling up, less leaf surface is exposed to the hot air, helping the plant save its moisture until the cool evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ latsaa be mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa lɛ hiɛ fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i baa lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops flowers to save its remaining water and energy to survive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This leaves all the plants weak, thin, and producing smaller yields than if they had proper breathing space.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ekɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔ, ni ewooo yibii babaoo fe kɛji eyɛ he ko ni sa ni ekɛmuɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than the cassava stems I just planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmei tso ni midu amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong roots that quickly grab food and water from the soil faster than young crops. Clearing them early prevents them from choking your young cassava stems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni wa waa ni baanyɛ agbala niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei bibii. Ehe saamɔ mra Ebaatsi o-cassava tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cocoa pods from the trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their color changes completely from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. Harvesting when green leaves the beans bitter and flat, while waiting too long makes the seeds germinate inside the pod.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa nɔ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ beni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much sun during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni hulu la babaoo tsoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to protect them until their roots grow deep enough to absorb underground water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya ni egbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ahe tsɔi ni buɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air flow through, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ Efɔ ni edɔ tsɔ, ŋmɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks the growing tip of maize. If left unchecked, they destroy the plant's leaves, but early application of recommended pesticides or organic remedies can control them.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaakpata tso lɛ baai lɛ ahiɛ. Shi atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ atsu nii mra. lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a main food green plants need to grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its green color and produce good cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei eŋɔli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent your crop from getting infected.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni yɔɔ kooloi bibii Akɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whiteflies lɛ yaa tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ otsi onibii lɛ anaa koni hela akamɔ bo.

english: Yam vines need to reach high up into the sunlight to catch enough energy to make food. When the vines climb stakes, the plant can direct more energy down into growing larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ate shi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ babaoo kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce a very small bunch when many shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ niji bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ? mi plantain lɛ

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Cutting away most of the extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the plant to concentrate its energy on producing a large plantain bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains akui wuji amamɔ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and flat before they are even ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or water consistently while the fruit is growing. Regular watering and healthy soil prevent the fruit bottoms from spoiling.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa baatsi aduawai lɛ ahiɛ lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, poor watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. nu ni ehiii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps soil water from evaporating in the heat, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la kɛji edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up when the rains stop earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gĩ ni amɛgbi beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops rely on consistent soil moisture to pull nutrients from the ground. When rains stop early, the roots run out of water, causing leaves to lose internal pressure and wilt, which stops growth and reduces your harvest.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni amɛgbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa oya lɛ, nu faaa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli, ni no haa baai lɛ amli hewalɛ baa shi ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ baaha odalɛ akpa ni ebaaha onibii ni owoɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers when the rainfall becomes irregular during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water stress causes crops to enter a survival mode. To save energy and water, the plant naturally drops its flowers and young fruit because it knows it cannot support them without steady moisture.
ga: Nu he haomɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ wala shihilɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii kɛjɛ ebɔɔ su mli. Ejaakɛ ele akɛ enyɛŋ ehi shi kɛji hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which slows down water loss when the soil is dry and temperatures are high.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa baa lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa.

english: Why do the edges of my vegetable leaves turn brown and crisp during sunny weeks without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ otsi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When sunlight is strong and soil moisture is low, leaves lose water through transpiration faster than roots can drink it, causing the outer edges of the leaves to scorch and dry out.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ latsaa nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ asɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Can I still grow vegetables during the dry season in Ghana, or will the heat automatically kill them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana? Aloo ani latsaa lɛ baagbe nakai aduawai lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can grow healthy crops during the dry season if you provide water using an irrigation system. Strong sunlight actually helps crops grow faster, provided their roots receive adequate moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛji akɛ okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsu nii. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ ná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: What happens to my crop yield if I rely only on rainfall instead of using a planned watering system?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Relying only on rain makes your crop yield unpredictable because rainfall timing and amounts change every year. Controlled watering ensures plants receive steady moisture for maximum production.
ga: Nugbɔ pɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haaa okwɛ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná. Ejaakɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ bɔ ni efa ha lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do crops grown with a proper watering system give bigger fruits than crops that depend only on natural rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe tsei ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: A reliable water system prevents the plant from experiencing water shock, allowing it to continuously feed its flowers and fill out bigger, healthier fruits without stopping.
ga: Nu gbɛjianɔtoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkapiŋ nu afua. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ayeɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be ni akpaaa.

english: What happens to seeds if I plant them and a dry spell suddenly hits before they sprout?
ga: Mɛni baa dumɔwui anɔ kɛji midu amɛ ni hulutsoo be ba dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Seeds require continuous moisture to break their outer shell and grow roots. If the soil dries out right after planting, the seeds will either fail to germinate or the young sprouts will wither and die.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛgbala kponɔgbɛ nɔ ni amɛhaa amɛhe lɛ ni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ loo tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower when I water them by hand with buckets compared to when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa kɛ mikɛ minine wo amɛ nu kɛ baagi fe be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Hand watering with buckets often only wet the surface of the soil, leaving deep roots dry. Rain waters deeply and evenly across the whole field while cooling the air around the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛ nine baagi tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ feɔ ekome yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my crop harvests change so drastically from one year to another even when I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ afi kome mli kɛyaa afi kroko mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Harvests change because weather and rainfall patterns vary each year. Unless you control soil moisture through a dedicated watering setup, your crops remain at the mercy of shifting weather conditions.
ga: Nikpamɔ tsakeɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli ja okɛ nu pɔtɛɛ ko kudɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I use goat manure on my farm instead of buying chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ too ŋmei atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ?

english: Goat manure is rich in nitrogen and organic matter that improves soil structure and holds moisture over time, keeping crops lush and healthy without damaging the long-term fertility of your land.
ga: Too ŋmɔtɔ mli nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni okpataa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Is it really possible to grow a full crop of maize without applying any chemical inputs?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛ tsofa ko tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, crops like maize can grow successfully using only natural animal manure and good field practices, which feed the soil directly and reduce the money you spend on commercial inputs.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ omanyeyeli mli kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi aŋmãa kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai pɛ nɔ. ni haa niyenii yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa shika ni ofiteɔ yɛ jarayeli nibii ahe lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough to support a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua nikpamɔ kpakpa?

english: Rich soil is usually dark in color, holds water well after rain, feels soft rather than hard and crusted, and often contains earthworms or decomposing plant material.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ su feɔ ediŋŋ. Ekɛ nu toɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ mli.

english: Can I put fresh goat manure straight onto my crops right after sweeping it from the pen?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ too ŋmei hee awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ shwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fresh manure is too strong and generates heat as it decomposes, which can burn plant roots. It should be left to dry or compost for a few weeks before spreading it on your farm.
ga: Manɔ hee mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi loo etsɔ ŋmɔlɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How should I store goat manure so rain does not wash away its strength before planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ ato too ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ aha tɛŋŋ koni nugbɔ akajie ehewalɛ lɛ dani ŋmɔtɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Pile the manure in a shaded area and cover it with a tarp or thatch leaves to protect it from heavy rain and bright sunlight, keeping the nutrients locked in until you are ready to use it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni okɛ tarp loo jwɛi aha nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii toɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why does maize grown with animal manure seem to develop differently than maize grown with chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ kooloi ashishifãi duɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Organic manure releases its nutrients slowly and steadily over time, allowing the maize to build a strong root system and sturdy stalk rather than forcing rapid, temporary growth.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio. ni be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ehoɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni enáa shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Mohu ɔ, e nyɛɔ be kukuoo mi hɛ mi nyami nɛ yaa nɔ oya ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the rest of the plant is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Tso lɛ ni miida lɛ he?

english: The bottom leaves turn yellow when the plant moves its stored nitrogen upward to feed young growing leaves or developing cobs, showing that the crop needs extra soil nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii loo ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii krokomɛi he miihia tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: At what stage in its growth is maize most easily damaged if it does not get enough water?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli ŋmãa fiteɔ oya fe fɛɛ kɛji enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ?

english: Maize is most vulnerable during the flowering and silking stage; lack of water at this time prevents proper pollination and results in cobs with missing grains.
ga: Abɛi ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ bɛ dumɔwui.

english: Why does my young maize sometimes look weak and small during its early weeks in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-baby corns lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ bibioo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ? Nɛgbɛ eyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Young maize focuses most of its early energy on developing deep roots underground before fast top growth visible above the soil begins.
ga: Abɛi abifao lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ dani edaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to plant my maize seeds only after the soil has gathered enough moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛ?

english: Maize seeds require steady moisture to sprout evenly; planting in dry soil causes seeds to sit ungerminated or rot if light rain comes and stops suddenly.
ga: Abele dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ loo amɛkafite kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo. ni ekpa trukaa

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to grow or die shortly after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa loo amɛgboiɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need proper selection, planting depth, and adequate moisture to build roots. Planting weak suckers or placing them in dry, unprepared soil leaves them struggling to establish.
ga: Esa akɛ ahala dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ. dumɔ mlibotemɔ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee shishifãi Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ loo akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni asaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha amɛ akɛ amɛaato amɛhe shi.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over during rainy storms before the bunches are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa nii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. Using strong wooden stakes or bamboo props to support the main stem prevents wind and heavy bunches from uprooting the tree.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa loo ŋmei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain plants turn yellow and dry up during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water very quickly in hot sunshine. Yellowing and drying leaves indicate water stress, which can be reduced by applying organic mulch around the base to keep the soil moist.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ nu he haomɔ. Abaanyɛ ajie enɛ shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛbɔleɔ he lɛ nɔ. shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do I need to use commercial fertilizer on my farm if my soil already looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ?

english: Even rich soil loses essential nutrients like nitrogen and potassium after crops feed on them repeatedly. Fertilizer acts as food supplements to restore nutrients so crops can grow big and produce high yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii po baanyɛ afite niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. Beni tsei lɛ eye amɛ shii abɔ sɛɛ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Fertilizer is best applied early in the plant's life once roots have established, and again during fast growth, ensuring the plant gets nutrients exactly when it needs them to build strong stems and leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ wala mli mra be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ebɔi shi. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small harvest when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to build strong stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: What is the proper way to clear and prepare my land before putting my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he dani aduɔ dumɔwui?

english: Clearing weeds, removing debris, and loosening hard dirt helps young roots spread quickly to access soil moisture and nutrients deeper underground.
ga: weeding Debris Removal Ni muji ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya koni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if the seeds I want to buy will produce a healthy crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni misumɔɔ ni mahe lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good quality seeds are clean, dry, free from insect holes or molds, and sourced from certified input dealers or healthy mother plants so they germinate evenly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe tse, amɛgbi, ni kooloi loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. ni anáa kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo nyɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Koni ekwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Why do dark spots show up on my crop leaves, and why does it make my plants stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ duŋ miije kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ etsĩɔ mitsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf spots are caused by small plant diseases or pests that damage the leaves, reducing their ability to use sunlight to produce food for the plant.
ga: Tso hela bibioo ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ he ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tsei yɔɔ ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi.

english: How can using improved seeds and recommended farming inputs help me overcome poor harvests?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni atsake kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maye ŋmaa ni ehiii lɛ nɔ kunim?

english: Improved seeds grow faster and tolerate diseases better, while recommended fertilizers deliver balanced nutrients, turning weak fields into high-yielding farms.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ daa oya ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ mli ŋmɔji ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cocoa or food crops on land that was previously dug up by illegal miners?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo loo niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but deep digging removes the fertile topsoil where plants get food. Before planting, you must fill in the pits, add compost or animal manure to rebuild the soil, and allow the ground to recover so crop roots can spread and absorb nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi shikpɔŋ ni akuɔ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni tso lɛ naa niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Dani obaadu lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ sũ awo bu lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when I plant them on disturbed, sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛdu yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ ni ehao lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen and other essential nutrients. Disturbed or washed-away soil loses its natural fertility, so crops cannot get the nourishment needed to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa bɛ tso lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni agbala mli loo nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do deep holes and stagnant water on my farmland damage my crops?
ga: Te bu ni mli kwɔ kɛ nu ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Deep holes collect standing water that drowns plant roots by cutting off their air supply. Over time, waterlogged roots rot, causing the whole crop to wilt and die.
ga: Buu ni mli kwɔ lɛ buaa nu ni ekã shi lɛ naa, ni no shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni Nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baagboi. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ gboi ni amɛgboi.

english: How does adding animal manure or decomposed leaves help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo baai ni egboi ni mikɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Manure and leaf compost act as natural food for crops. They rebuild worn-out soil, help the ground hold moisture during dry periods, and make it easier for roots to grow strong.
ga: Manure kɛ baa mli ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛtswaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under intense heat. They need temporary shade crops, like plantains or shade trees, to shelter them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni akɛ wɔɔhe aha klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ

english: How many years will it take for my newly planted cocoa trees to produce pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ ni mi-cacao tso ni midu ehee lɛ woɔ ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years if planted in good soil and given proper shade, while older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ ni aha lɛ hulutsoo ni sa. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baahe aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds regularly around my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Aduɔ kookoo tsei bibii daa.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your cocoa seedlings, slowing down their growth and making them weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ, nu kɛ hulu la mli kɛjɛɔ kookoo dumɔwui amli. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Which food crops can I grow quickly to feed my family while waiting for long-term trees to yield?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu oya koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Quick-yielding food crops like maize, cassava, plantain, and cowpeas mature within 3 to 12 months, giving you food and income while slower tree crops like cocoa grow.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ ŋmãa he yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 12 mli, ni ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, tamɔ kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts help the other crops on my farm?
ga: Bean loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds and enriches the ground for surrounding crops.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii baa ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why do cassava plants grow well even in dry or poor soil where other crops fail?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii po nɔ he ni tsei krokomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava has tough, deep roots that store energy and search for underground moisture, allowing it to survive harsh conditions and low soil nutrients better than many other crops.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni toɔ hewalɛ ni etaoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni faaa lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei krokomɛi.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly like straws during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat to conserve water. By reducing the leaf surface area exposed to the hot sun and dry wind, the plant prevents moisture from evaporating too quickly from inside its leaves.
ga: Abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop almost all their leaves during the dry season, and does this mean they are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eegbo?

english: Your cassava plants are not dying; dropping leaves is their natural way of surviving dry spells. By losing leaves, the plant stops losing water through evaporation and goes into resting mode, storing its energy in the tubers underground until the rains return.
ga: O-cassava tso lɛ gbooo. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nu shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ ni eyaa hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do so many small flowers drop off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. Many flowers fall off because tiny insects like midges did not pollinate them, or because the tree naturally sheds extra flowers to save its strength for growing a manageable number of healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ midges nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔii krɛdɛɛi kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ naa lɛ hewɔ. Bɔni afee ni okɛ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ, kwɛ pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: How do groundnut pods end up buried under the soil when the flowers grow above ground?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ afu ŋmei ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower opens and gets pollinated on the stem, it loses its petals and sends out a stalk called a peg. This peg grows downward, pierces into the loose soil, and then swells underground to form the groundnut pod.
ga: Beni ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ tswa ni pollination eba tso lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Efiteɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​tso ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg lɛ. Pin nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shi. Eboteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse mli. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsɔɔ ŋmei ŋmei.

english: Why do my mango flowers fall off heavily whenever it rains during the flowering season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mango lɛ shwieɔ shi waa be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain physically knocks fragile blossoms off the tree branches and washes away pollen needed for fruit set. Rain during flowering also creates damp conditions that allow fungal diseases to attack and rot the flower clusters.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni efoɔ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo lɛ kɛyaa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ hu haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba ni etutua fɔfɔii akui.

english: Yams are climbing plants that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers underneath. Staking lifts the leaves into the light, improves airflow to reduce fungal diseases, and results in much larger yams at harvest.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛba tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ, amɛfeɔ agboi babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the new small shoots growing around my main plantain stem to keep growing together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii heei lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei titrii lɛ miida yɛ he kome.

english: Allowing too many young shoots (suckers) to grow around the mother plant creates competition for water, light, and soil nutrients. Cutting away extra suckers leaves the main stem and one strong successor with enough nourishment to produce heavy, full bunches.
ga: Ha ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ akwɛ̃ yɛ tso nyɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli kɛ nɔ kome ni yeɔ esɛɛ ni he wa, ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli ni baaha efee panicle ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit as it develops. It usually happens when watering is irregular, making it hard for the plant roots to draw up calcium continuously from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my pepper plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually indicate that your pepper plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants make green foliage, and when supply is low, the plant moves available nitrogen from older lower leaves up to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-pepper tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli. ni kɛ́ fioo ko yɛ lɛ Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛ ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants fold up close together at night and open up again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi gbɛkɛ ni amɛgbeleɔ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants close their leaves at night to protect themselves from losing heat and moisture during cool nights. They spread their leaves back out at dawn to catch the early morning sunlight needed to make food.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ gbɛkɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwãa leebi maŋkpa koni amɛná leebi hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛhoo nii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow after many days of heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes essential soil nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground beyond the reach of roots and floods the soil, starving roots of the oxygen they need to feed the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ nu Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when strong rain hits the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall softens the soil around the base of the plant while collecting on the leaves and stalks, making the crop top-heavy and easy for wind and water to push over.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ beni ebua ehe naa yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ tsiimɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ oya.

english: How does heavy rain affect the fertilizer I put on my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rainwater washes fertilizer off the soil surface and sweeps it away from the roots before the crops have enough time to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe ni ekɛshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ dani tsei lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Will using a heavy machine to clear my farm land affect how my crops grow?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛjie miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Heavy machinery clears land very quickly, but the weight can press the soil together tightly, making it harder for crop roots to breathe and spread deep into the earth.
ga: Nibii ni tsii tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya waa. Shi muji lɛ baanyɛ ami shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Is it better to clear my field before the heavy rains start or during the rainy season?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaajie ŋmɔji lɛ amli dani nugbɔnɛmɔ waa lɛ aloo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Clearing land before the rain makes planting easier, whereas clearing during heavy rains creates muddy conditions that make moving around and working the soil very difficult.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔ feɔ mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo muji baa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fãmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa.

english: Why do weeds sprout back so quickly after I cut them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ afo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cutting only removes the top of the weed, while abundant rain quickly feeds the deep root system left underground, allowing weeds to grow back faster than main crops.
ga: Kɛ́ afo lɛ, jwɛi lɛ yiteŋ pɛ jieɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ niyenii oya. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to cut and harvest my crops while they are wet from rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni makpa be mli ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting wet crops traps moisture inside your storage sacks, creating a damp space where mold, bacteria, and rot quickly destroy the harvest.
ga: Nibii ni efɔ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo onitoo kotokui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmeii, helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya.

english: How does using a machine for cutting crops compare to harvesting by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ nine ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: Machines cut large areas quickly to save physical labor, but harvesting by hand allows you to carefully pick only ripe crops without damaging surrounding plants.
ga: Mashiŋ lɛ shwieɔ hei wuji oya koni ekɛ nitsumɔ akafite. Shi nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ pɛ ni ofiteee tsei ni ebɔle ohe lɛ.

english: Why do crop diseases spread faster across my farm when it rains continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: High humidity and rain splashes carry fungal spores and bacteria from infected plant leaves directly onto healthy neighboring crops.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ woɔ fungal spores kɛ bacteria kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do root crops like cassava start rotting in the soil when it rains too much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil fills all air spaces underground, suffocating root crops by preventing oxygen from reaching them, which causes the roots to decompose.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: Why do my hands itch and sting whenever I harvest okra on my farm?
