ga: Mɛni hewɔ miniji shwieɔ shi ni shwieɔ mi be fɛɛ be ni makpa okra yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Okra plants naturally cover their leaves and pods with tiny, prickly hairs to protect themselves from animals. Wearing long sleeves and gloves prevents these small prickles from penetrating and irritating your skin.
ga: Roselle tsei lɛ kɛ yitsɔi bibii haa amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ŋmeii ni akɛbuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe Kɛ́ owo atadei kakadaŋŋ agboi kɛ glɔvs lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei bibii lɛ akabote ohe. Enɛɛmɛi baanyɛ abote mli ni amɛha hewolo lɛ mli afu.

english: Why do my sweet orange trees grow long, sharp thorns on their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ eshishifã lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees naturally grow thorns on younger branches as a defense mechanism to keep animals from eating their shoots. As the tree matures and branches grow higher, thorn production usually decreases.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ amɛniji bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ kooloi anaa koni amɛkaye amɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Beni tso lɛ eda kwraa ni eyɛ niji ni kɛlɛ fe tsutsu lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does the liquid inside raw cashew nut shells burn my hands during harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ cashew nut ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ shã miniji yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Raw cashew nut shells contain an aggressive natural oil called urushiol, which protects the seed from insects. You should always dry or steam raw cashews before cracking them to neutralize this caustic liquid.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli fɔ ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ urushiol yɛ cashew nut ŋmeii ni ahoko lɛ amli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe. Esa akɛ ogbi loo okɛ steam awo cashews ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ mli dani ogbala mli koni nu ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow long, wild branches with very few fruits when left alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ koo mli niji kakadaji ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants grow unchecked, they direct all their energy into leafy stems rather than fruit production. Pruning off extra shoots forces the plant to focus its nutrients into producing large, healthy tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ tomato tsei lɛ dara ni akuuu amɛ nɔ Etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ baai amli moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ koni efee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines spread wildly along the ground if I do not give them sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mihaaa lɛ niji ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally seek height to catch maximum sunlight. When left on the ground, they spread outward, become prone to rot and leaf diseases from soil contact, and fail to build large underground tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã kponɔgbɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ebaafite kɛ baa helai kɛji ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpe. ni enyɛŋ ebɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Maize leaves curl into tubes as a natural defense against extreme heat. By reducing the surface area exposed to the sun, the plant slows down water loss and keeps itself from drying out.
ga: Abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ paipii koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ haa nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaaa ehe agbi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when insects start eating their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji kooloi bibii bɔi baai lɛ yeli lɛ?

english: When pepper plants come under heavy insect attack, they enter a protective stress mode. They drop their flowers to conserve water and food energy so the plant can survive until conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tutua pepper tsei waa lɛ Amɛyaa anti-stress mode mli. Amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ niyenii hewalɛ he koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does wild cassava in the bush taste so bitter compared to the cassava on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli ŋmei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ waa kɛ akɛto ŋmei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Wild cassava plants produce higher concentrations of natural bitter defense chemicals to protect themselves from pests without human help. Cultivated farm varieties have been selected over time to produce fewer defense toxins, making them sweeter and safer.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni ji cassava lɛ feɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni adesa yeee ebuaaa amɛ. Ahala ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli koni ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Ehaa efeɔ ŋɔɔ ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Is the white milky sap from a cassava stem harmful if it gets on my skin during harvesting?
ga: Ani nu yɛŋ ni tamɔ mliki ni jɛɔ ŋmei tsei amli lɛ yɛ oshara kɛji ebashɛ mihewolo nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Fresh cassava sap contains natural defensive compounds that irritate bare skin and eyes. While not deadly on contact, washing it off promptly with clean water prevents skin rashes and discomfort.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hewolo kɛ hiŋmɛi mli fuɔ lɛ yɛ cassava fɔ hee mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ jeee nɔ ni woɔ mɔ wala he gbeyei kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo mli moŋ. Shi kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse tsumɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hewolo nɔ tsɔi kɛ henumɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my maize plants turn thin and fall over when weeds surround them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal light, moisture, and soil nutrients from your crop. Starved of resources, the maize stretches upward competing for light, resulting in a weak, unstable stalk.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ la, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. yɛ nibii ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ Abele lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ la lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehiɛɛɛ shi.

english: What happens if I plant my tomato seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When tomatoes are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin, weak stems and makes it easy for fungal diseases to spread because air cannot flow between the plants.
ga: Kɛji adu tomatoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tomatoi kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baagbɛ eshwa ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why did some of my planted maize seeds fail to sprout out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds can fail to germinate if they were stored in a hot or damp place, buried too deeply, or if the soil lacked enough moisture right after planting. Using certified seeds and planting them at the recommended depth in moist soil improves sprout rates.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ, loo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli tsu nii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the base of young crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwieɔ tsei bibii ashishi lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the soil with dry grass keeps the ground cool, retains moisture during dry spells, and stops weeds from taking over around your young crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it a good idea to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava takes longer to mature. Planting them together gives you an early harvest of maize while the cassava slowly takes over the field, maximizing your land's output.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei heɔ be babaoo dani eshɛɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okpa ŋmãa oya. be mli ni ŋmei lɛ baa fiofio ni ebayeɔ jɛmɛ Koni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii babaoo aba

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying urea or NPK fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps restore green leaves and boosts crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli mra lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ baai lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tso lɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees keep dropping their flowers before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by harsh heat, lack of soil moisture, or insect pests like mirids. Maintaining shade trees on your farm and spraying for sap-sucking insects helps flowers stay on the tree to turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen Tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What should I do if small caterpillars are eating holes in my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji ŋmeii bibii ye bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common corn pest. You can control them by spraying approved bio-pesticides or recommended insecticides early in the morning or late in the evening when the worms come out to feed.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmei ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni kooloi lɛ jeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that block the plant's water channels. Rotating your pepper crop with non-related plants like maize or cassava helps clean the soil of these germs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei loo muawai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ nu gbɛi lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ trukaa nɛɛ baa. Pepper ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni etsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell the right time to harvest my groundnuts so they do not rot underwater?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ nu shishi.

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and begin to dry up. You can pull out a test plant; if the inner shells have dark brown markings, the crop is ready for harvesting.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ ojie kaa tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is ready and fertile enough for vegetable farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai?

english: Healthy, fertile soil feels dark, crumbly, and holds moisture well without becoming waterlogged. Mixing well-rotted animal manure or compost into the soil before planting improves fertility and water retention.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ duŋ, egbɔjɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo sũ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha ewoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni eha nu hu ahi mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient for green leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the leaves turn deep green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant maize on the exact same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pods are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: You can check the color and size of the pod. A mature cocoa pod changes color from green to bright yellow or red to orange and reaches its full length, indicating the beans inside are fully formed and ready.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ pods lɛ ahe su kɛ amɛdalɛ. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo etsuru kɛyaa akutu. ni eyɛ elɛɛmɔ fɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ebɔi feemɔ kwraa ni efee klalo.

english: What is the proper way to cut cocoa pods off the tree without damaging the crop?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni afiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Always use a clean, sharp tool like a harvesting sickle or cutlass to slice the pod stem. Avoid pulling or twisting the pod by hand, as this destroys the flower cushion where future cocoa pods must grow.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, kɛ dɛŋdade ni he tse ni naa wa, tamɔ nikpamɔ kakla loo dade, afolɔ tso lɛ shishi. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ pods lɛ ni okɛ oniji aaagbala loo oootsɔ mli lɛ he. Enɛ baafite fɔfɔii ashishigbɛ he ni ehe baahia ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to consult agricultural extension officers about my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Agricultural extension officers teach you the correct standards for pod size, proper harvesting methods, and disease management so your crop yields high-quality beans that fetch good market prices.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baatsɔɔ bo shishitoo mlai ni ja kɛha pod lɛ dalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa nibii kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara kpakpa nɔ.

english: Can I grow and harvest cocoa on land around my home, or does it require a dedicated farm field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ni makpa kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mishia lɛ nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ ko atsu nii?

english: While cocoa can grow on land near your home if there is adequate shade and rich soil, larger dedicated farmland usually offers the proper forest canopy, soil depth, and space needed for healthier tree development and higher yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ oshia lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ, shi Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji wuji titri lɛ haa hulutsoo tsei ni sa. shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ he ni he hiaa kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: What happens to my crop if I harvest cocoa pods before they reach their full length and maturity?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛdara kwraa ni amɛdara?

english: Harvesting unripe or small pods yields flat, low-quality beans that do not ferment well, which results in lower weight and poor market value when sold to buying agents.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni edako loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa shi ni shwieee jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba. Enɛ haa shwiili lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi ni jara hu baa shi kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ.

english: How often should I harvest cocoa pods from my farm during the main harvest season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ mli?

english: You should go through your farm to harvest mature pods every two to three weeks. Regular harvesting prevents pods from over-ripening or rotting on the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ obote ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni oyakpa ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eda. otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ Nibii ni akpaa daa lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ fe nine loo amɛkafite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Does the size and length of a cocoa pod affect the number of beans inside?
ga: Ani bɔ ni kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ da ha kɛ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ saa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ he?

english: Yes, pods that grow to their full standard size generally hold more plump, healthy beans with higher cocoa butter content compared to stunted or premature pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, pods ni daa kɛyashɛɔ dalɛ ni sa lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Eyɛ kookoo bɔta ni fa fe no. Kɛ akɛto ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ mra lɛ ahe.

english: Should I harvest diseased or black cocoa pods along with my healthy crop?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ŋmeii diji kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe?

english: You should cut off diseased pods to prevent fungal infections like black pod disease from spreading to healthy pods, but keep the infected pods separate from your good harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli koni ŋmeii helai, tamɔ black pod hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Shi gbalamɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: How many days after harvesting cocoa pods should I wait before breaking them open?
ga: Kɛ́ obua kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa lɛ, gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ atswa?

english: It is best to break open harvested cocoa pods within 5 to 7 days after cutting them from the tree so the beans remain fresh and ferment properly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookumɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ mli yɛ gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 mli beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo yibii lɛ ahi shi ehee ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do standard harvesting methods help me prove the quality of my cocoa harvest to buying officers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua nihɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni mi-kookoo lɛ hi ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Following recommended harvesting guidelines ensures that your cocoa beans meet standard requirements for size, color, and dryness, allowing buying officers to grade your crop as Grade 1 premium cocoa.
ga: Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akpaa nii lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni o-cocoa yibii lɛ ashɛ shishitoo mlai ni kɔɔ dalɛ, ehiɛ su kɛ bɔ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ni amɛbuɔ onibii lɛ akɛ Premium Grade 1 cocoa.

english: Why do insects like bees keep visiting the flowers on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yaa nɔ amɛsaraa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Insects visit flowers to feed on nectar, and while doing so, they carry pollen from one flower to another. This process, called pollination, fertilizes the plant so it can form healthy pepper fruits.
ga: Kplukai yasaraa fɔfɔi koni amɛye nu ni mli tse. Ni be mli ni amɛfeɔ nakai lɛ Amɛwoɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ pollination. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ afɔ koni amɛwo pepper yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to stress caused by extreme heat, lack of regular watering, or poor pollination when insects or gentle winds are missing.
ga: Haomɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛhaa daa loo pollination ni ehiii beni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ lɛ laajeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to be planted under shade crops like plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi tamɔ plantains lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and can easily dry out or burn under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide necessary shade and keep the air humid so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi loo amɛshã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, preventing any of them from growing thick, strong stalks.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ tsĩɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why do mango and citrus trees take several years before they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango kɛ akutu tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Tree crops need to spend their early years building a deep root system and strong branches so they have enough stored energy to produce and support heavy fruits later on.
ga: Be he miihia tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ niji ni mli wa. Enɛ ji koni ana hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato koni ekɛwo yibii ni tsii ni ekɛfi sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even though the leaves look very bushy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall leaves on top instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ baai kakadaji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to expand easily underground. If the soil is hard, compacted, or full of stones, the tuber gets blocked and forces its way sideways, becoming twisted.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Atsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa ni ashwieɔ amɛ kɛyaa he kroko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe.

english: Why does planting cowpea or beans make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by viruses carried by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, which weaken the plant's ability to make food from sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni haaa tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when water stays sitting in the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu efo ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns crop roots by cutting off their air supply, making it impossible for the plant to absorb nutrients from the ground to stay green.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why shouldn't I burn my farm land after clearing the bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ beni mijie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter that rots into free natural fertilizer for your crops. It also kills beneficial insects and earthworms that keep the soil soft, moist, and healthy.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo, edɔɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hu.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard very quickly after I weed my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ ni ewaa oya beni mijie jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: When the soil is left completely bare, the direct heat from the sun bakes it hard and dries out all the moisture. Leaving chopped weeds on top of the ground as mulch protects the soil from heat and keeps it wet longer.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. This naturally feeds the soil and provides extra food for nearby crops like maize without buying expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ náa niyenii kroko, ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for growth. It can also happen when too much rain stays in the soil and drowns the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwie nu mli.

english: Flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the plant does not get enough water and nutrients like calcium from the soil to support the fruit forming.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium, ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow big. Because weeds grow faster, they choke your crops and leave them weak.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No hewɔ lɛ efiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads easily in very wet and overly shady conditions. Trimming extra tree branches helps air and sunlight enter to dry out the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: If I plant my crops very close to each other, will I harvest more food?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo?

english: No, planting too close forces the crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This results in weak plants with tiny or empty fruits, lowering your total yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Small seeds only have a small amount of stored energy. If planted too deep, the young sprout wastes all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni amɛgboi dani hulu la lɛ baashɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry completely. This signals that the plant has finished moving all its food and energy down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe eniyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible to fit more crops in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow thin, weak, and produce small ears of corn instead of healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi bibii yɛ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same farm every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the ground repeatedly. It also allows specific pests and diseases that feed on maize to multiply in the soil year after year.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of crops called legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for other crops planted near them.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legume weku ni ale lɛ akɛ legumes lɛ mli bii. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi. ni adu yɛ nakai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay dark green, manufacture food, and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii. ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa

english: Excess rain and cool moisture create a damp environment where a fungal disease called Black Pod thrives. Raindrops splash fungal spores from infected leaves and soil directly onto healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod lɛ daa yɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa kookoo tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: You should plant cassava cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems have to bend awkwardly to reach light, wasting precious plant energy.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ adu ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Esa akɛ tso lɛ abɔle ehe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ koni la lɛ abote mli. Enɛ haa tsei ahewalɛ ni jara wa lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, are caused by calcium deficiency, often brought on by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely and then gets soaked suddenly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni esaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ gbiɔ kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, trukaa lɛ, efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce much smaller harvests even if I give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing thieves that absorb water and fertilizer much quicker than your crops can, leaving your crops hungry and thirsty despite your care.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni daa oya. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ kɛ kumai yeɔ onibii yɛ bɔ ni okwɛɔ onibii anɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do tiny beetles destroy my dried maize inside storage bags, and where do they come from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ladybugs bibii miifite mi ŋmãa ni egbi yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ? Ni nɛgbɛ amɛjɛɔ?

english: Maize weevils often lay eggs inside the grain while the crop is drying in the field. Once the grain is bagged, the eggs hatch into larvae that eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii woɔ ŋmãa mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii miigbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ abɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key food in the soil. It can also happen when too much rain washes away soil nutrients or waterlogging suffocates the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fite niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to clear the small shoots growing at the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi?

english: Those small side shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main tree trunk. Removing them helps the main tree stay strong and direct its energy into producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ shishi. Tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso titri lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, usually from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why must I put tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko yɛ ni sweet potato wain tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live and helps the plant build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ hiɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it bad if I put too many seeds into one hole when planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli beni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This results in thin, weak stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack, showing that the roots underneath have swollen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ efuu.

english: Why should I pile dry grass and leaves around the stems of my plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua jwɛi kɛ baai anaa? Dumɔwu ko tso lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, keeps the soil moist, prevents weeds from growing, and decays over time to feed the plantain roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha plantain shishifãi lɛ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid weather. Clearing bush around the trees lets sunlight and air in to keep pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tso bibii ni ebɔle he lɛ ni afoɔ Tso koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my tomato plants wither and die suddenly even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu ni mikɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting despite watering is often caused by soil pests or diseases like bacterial wilt, which attack and block the stem's inner pipes so water cannot reach the top of the plant.
ga: Trukaa ŋmɔtɔ, eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi loo helai tamɔ bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ Nu baa moŋ. ni tutuaa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa Koni nu akashɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help my soil get ready for the next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have a special natural ability to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which enriches the ground naturally for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and drop leaves when I clear all the big forest trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaaji lɛ sɛɛ foɔ beni mijieɔ koo mli cacao tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive intense tropical heat. Large shade trees shield cocoa leaves from sunburn and keep the soil moist. Without shade, the leaves get scorched, turn yellow, and drop off.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ mli. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo, amɛbuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baashã. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi

english: Why do my food crops grow much slower when I plant them close to the edge of the forest reserve?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ koo ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Big forest trees have long roots that drink up water and soil nutrients before your crops can reach them. Their tall branches also block the sunshine your food crops need to grow well.
ga: Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii shɛɔ amɛhe. Niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa oniyenii tsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day to reduce water loss from heat and dry wind. It is the plant's natural way of saving water until the sun goes down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily during heavy rains and wind storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems supporting heavy, water-filled stems and bunches. When heavy rains soften the soil, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni fiɔ tsei kɛ niji ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: If my cassava plant grows very tall with lots of leaves and flowers, does that mean I will harvest bigger cassava tubers?
ga: Kɛji mi yucca tso lɛ da waa ni eyɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ makpãtã ŋmei shishifãi wuji?

english: Not necessarily. When a cassava plant spends too much energy growing tall stems, leaves, and flowers above ground, it leaves fewer nutrients to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii, baai, kɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ, Niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fioo pɛ baashwɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ bulbs ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high heat, dry spells, or too much water. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, hulutsoo be mli, loo nu babaoo. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: This yellowing is a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left in its old bottom leaves and sends it up to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyaha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts alongside my main crop help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay after harvest, that nitrogen is left in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster on my farm than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive harsh conditions. They have deep and aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer much faster than young farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii bibii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot faster during heavy rains when the bush on my farm is thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo wu lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads in wet, dark conditions. Thick weeds and unpruned branches trap moisture around the cocoa pods, helping the disease spread quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ. Jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct, scorching sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Clearing all shade trees leaves them exposed to intense heat, which causes them to dry out rapidly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ha amɛna hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ mli. ni haa tso lɛ gbiɔ oya lɛ

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the surface of the ground. Planting them deep enough, mounding soil around the base, and using wooden props to support heavy fruit bunches keeps them grounded during storms.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Dumɔ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa, too shikpɔŋ kɛbɔle shishi lɛ he, ni okɛ tsei atsu nii ni okɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. koni eye ebua ni ehiɛ amɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ ahum be mli

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crop roots with dried grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops soil moisture from evaporating in the heat, keeps the ground cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop area.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛmligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away, so adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen lɛ shwiemɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, choking the roots of oxygen and encouraging fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away cleanly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa hetsemɔ mli.

english: Peppers drop their flowers when the weather becomes too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much fertilizer in the soil. Consistent watering and light shade during extreme heat helps the plant retain flowers and set fruit.
ga: Peppers baajie fɔfɔii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Is it really necessary for me to stake my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atswa sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines allows the leaves to spread out and capture maximum sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to produce food, which is then sent down into the ground to make larger, healthier tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni emɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt left inside the leaf whorl?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni eshwɛ yɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides in the central leaf tube of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts protects the young shoot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he pɔtɛɛ aba. Nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea plants mostly when the flowers start showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ babaoo beni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft buds that attract destructive insects like flower thrips and pod borers. Protecting the crop with recommended organic or chemical sprays at the very start of flowering prevents flower destruction.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni gbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ bu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that scorch easily under direct sun. They need shade from temporary companion plants like plantains to hold soil moisture and cool the surrounding air until the cocoa tree matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ajɔɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara.

english: When cocoa trees are planted too closely, their canopy blocks sunlight from lower leaves and their roots compete for soil nutrients. This causes the trees to grow tall, thin, and weak, producing fewer and smaller pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ŋwɛitsu lɛ baatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa. ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, such as dry spells or poor soil fertility. The tree naturally drops flowers to conserve water and nutrients when it lacks the energy to support developing fruit.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaaye amɛbua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot while still hanging on the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, cold, and overly humid conditions. Excess moisture trapped on the surface of the pods allows the fungus to enter and ruin the fruit.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo fe nine mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni ŋmɛɔ tso lɛ hiɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii boteɔ mli ni efiteɔ aduawai lɛ.

english: If I cut branches off my cocoa tree, won't that reduce the amount of fruit I get?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo nine lɛ No efeŋ aduawai babaoo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ, aloo jeee nakai?

english: No, pruning removes unproductive, dead, or diseased stems. This allows the tree to direct its energy, water, and soil nutrients into producing bigger, healthier pods on the main trunk and primary branches.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni wooo yibii, ni egboi, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ eniji bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my maize crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-abele tsei lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, highly adaptable plants with aggressive roots designed to absorb surface moisture and soil nutrients rapidly. They capture nutrients faster than young crop seedlings, which is why early clearing is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe waa ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii oya. Amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya fe dumɔwui bibii. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same plot without harming either crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeee tso lɛ eko kwraa awui?

english: Yes, because maize matures quickly and feeds near the top layer of soil, while cassava grows slowly at first and draws nutrients deeper underground. Properly spaced, they share the land without starving each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni eyeɔ nii yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni shishijee lɛ, ŋmei daa blɛoo ni egbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Amɛjara shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ sa ni hɔmɔ yeee amɛhe.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in dry soil before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require moisture to soften their outer shell and trigger the internal growth process. Without water, the seed remains dormant or burns in the hot soil before it can put down roots.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu koni eha amɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni ekanya amɛmli dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoi. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, dumɔwui baakã he amɛhi shi. loo eshãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani enyɛɔ ewoɔ shishifãi.

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves are turning light green because the soil is hungry or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ loo hela emɔ lɛ?

english: Nutrient deficiency usually causes uniform yellowing, starting from the older leaves near the bottom of the plant. Disease typically causes uneven yellow spots, brown patches, or leaf curling anywhere on the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Kɛjɛ baai momo ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli baa. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. loo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ he fɛɛ he

english: Why do insect pests like capsids attack my cocoa trees more during hot and dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuaa mi-cocoa tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: During hot weather, capsids seek out tender, sap-filled young shoots and pods to get moisture. The stress on the tree during dry spells makes its tissue softer and easier for insects to feed on.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ, capsids lɛ kwɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ koni amɛna ŋmɔtɔ. Haomɔ ni baa tso lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ haa efãji lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmeii yeɔ mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Nitrogen helps plants produce green chlorophyll to make food from sunlight; when the soil is exhausted or heavy rains wash nutrients away, the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ klorofil ni ji eŋɔli lɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ. Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce huge green leaves above ground but very tiny tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems rather than storing food in its roots. Balancing your soil nutrients helps the plant shift its focus to expanding root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛjwɛŋmɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and shrink into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, aphids, or thrips, which transmit viruses while feeding on sap. These pests cause the leaf tissues to grow unevenly, resulting in twisted and dwarfed leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites, aphids loo thrips, ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa be mli ni amɛyeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji ni ejaaa lɛ daa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any fruits begin to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive humidity. Under stress, the plant cannot pollinate its blossoms effectively and drops them to conserve moisture and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo he. yɛ haomɔ shishi Tsei nyɛŋ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollination jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshi fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛgbele koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do extension workers advise me to keep shade trees over my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ mikɛ tso ko ni haa hulutsoo tso lɛ awo mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that easily dry out under full sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from hot sun and harsh winds while preserving soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ egbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mlihiɛmɔ.

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow root networks close to the surface. If stem borers weaken the base or heavy bunches make the top heavy, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ sisi nɛ mi we nɛ e kɛ e hɛ mi nyami. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa shishigbɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo jwɛi lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ mli tsii. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready for planting right after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Soil is ready when it is moist enough to form a soft ball in your hand that crumbles easily when gently pressed. If it stays as a sticky clay ball, it is too wet; if it stays powdery, it needs more rainfall before seeds can germinate safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ nine mli, ni kɛ́ anyɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, efoɔ oya. Kɛji ehi shi tamɔ shikpɔŋ bɔɔlu Etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ Kɛji eji powda lolo Nugbɔ babaoo he baahia dani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow well in dry, poor soil where my maize fails completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ehiii nɔ aahu akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen directly from the air. This natural ability allows them to feed themselves in poor soils where nitrogen-hungry crops like maize starve.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ nɛɛ haa amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant cassava and groundnuts together in the same field instead of just cassava alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ fe ŋmei kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts cover the ground quickly to prevent weeds and fix nitrogen into the soil, which feeds the soil while the slower-growing cassava takes time to develop its broad leaf canopy.
ga: Oya nɔŋŋ ni ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akaje mli ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ heɔ be dani enáa baai ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I clear and burn my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mishã lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the soil waiting for sunlight and warmth. Burning clears the tall bush cover and releases ash into the soil, giving weed seeds ideal sunlight and quick nutrients to germinate before your crops catch up.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, amɛmiimɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ. Shãa haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ejieɔ sũ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ naa hulu la ni sa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: How do I know if my land is naturally suitable for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ji he ko ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, dark, well-drained soil that holds moisture without staying flooded. If your land is too rocky, very sandy, or stays waterlogged like a swamp after rainfall, cocoa roots will rot or fail to grow properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia kokoo tsei. ni baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu shwieee nɔ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛi tsɔ, eyɛ ŋã babaoo, loo nu eyi mli obɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ sɛɛ. Cocoa shishifãi lɛ baagboi loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains around them creates a natural shelter that blocks harsh heat and keeps the air humid while the young trees grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ha tsei lɛ adara loo adu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he Tsei lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe ko ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my cassava stems very close together?
ga: Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, planting cassava stems too close together forces them to compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each stem proper distance allows the roots enough space to expand into big, heavy tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in intense heat to protect themselves. Shrinking the leaf surface area helps the plant save water and stop moisture from evaporating too quickly in the sun.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie baa lɛ hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la mli.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei?

english: Yes, groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This enriches the ground and helps neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani mifeɔ chili lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as dry soil, extreme heat, or a lack of essential nutrients needed to hold and nourish the fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, latsaa ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha aduawai lɛ ahi shi ni eha amɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Wait until the first rains have soaked deep into the soil rather than planting after the very first light shower. Seeds need continuous soil moisture to germinate and survive without drying out.
ga: Mɛɛ ni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why are tiny insects gathering under my cassava leaves and twisting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Those insects are likely whiteflies or mealybugs sucking the sap out of the leaves. They weaken the plant and can spread diseases like Cassava Mosaic, causing distorted leaves and small tuber yields.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii yɛŋ loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛhaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai tamɔ cassava mosaic amɛshwã. Enɛ haa baai ni efite kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: How can I make my farmland stay fertile for many years without losing its strength?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i afii babaoo ni mihewalɛ akafite?

english: Soil loses its strength when the same crop is grown continuously without care. Adding organic manure, rotating different crops like beans and maize, and allowing land to rest helps keep soil rich long-term.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa kɛji akɛ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Organic fertilizer ni akɛbaafata he Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha ejɔɔ ehe lɛ baaye abua ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the lower ones to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Beni tsei daraa Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, the maize uses that trapped nitrogen to grow faster and produce bigger yields.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller cassava tubers when I plant cassava on the same farm plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Over time, pests and diseases that attack cassava also build up in that soil, leading to smaller roots and poorer harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmei lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii kɛ kpamɔ ni ehiii kwraa baa.

english: Why should I wait for steady rains before planting my seeds instead of planting right after the first short rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ? Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ kuku ɔ se amlɔ nɔuu.

english: The first light rain only wets the top layer of soil and often quickly stops for days. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the tender young roots will dry out and die before the real rainy season settles in.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, ekpaa oya gbii babaoo Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my young vegetables with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle aduawai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves or grass (called mulching) blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool, holds water in the ground longer so you water less often, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Etsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ajɔ. Ha nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ nu fioo pɛ haa. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do I need to prune extra shoots and leaves off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo ni mashi kookoo tso lɛ efolo lɛ?

english: Cutting off dead or weak branches opens up the tree so air and sunlight can flow through. Sunlight helps cocoa pods develop properly, while good airflow prevents humidity from causing fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ naa koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji aba.

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly when I leave weeds to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni mishiɔ jwɛi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Because weeds grow very fast, they steal these resources before your crops can use them, leaving your plants weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa. Amɛjuɔ nibii nɛɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny insects like thrips that damage the flower stems before fruit can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ tutuamɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and crinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that live on the underside of leaves and spread viruses that make the plant leaves twist and stop growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ hela ko ni haa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pods are suffering from black pod disease or just scorched by the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ black pod hela loo hulutsoo kɛkɛ?

english: Black pod disease causes soft, spreading dark brown spots with a sweetish foul smell that rapidly cover the whole pod and grow white mold. Sunburn forms dry, hard, lighter brown patches only on the side of the pod directly exposed to the light.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa baa. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ baa Hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi, ni wa, ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fã ni la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to pick out damaged or moldy cocoa beans by hand before taking them to the buying clerk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mikɛ miniji afolɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efite loo ni efite lɛ dani mikɛya mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Removing damaged or moldy beans by hand ensures your batch meets top quality standards. Even a few bad beans can ruin the taste of chocolate or cause processors to reject the whole bag or pay a lower price.
ga: Kɔfi yibii ni efite loo ni efite ni akɛ niji jieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ obatch lɛ shɛɔ shishitoo mlai ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe. Beans gbohii fioo komɛi po baanyɛ afite tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ. aloo ni eha mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ akpoo kotoku lɛ kwraa loo ewo nyɔmɔ ni baa shi.

english: If I put slightly rotten tomatoes into the same crate with good ones, will it affect the good tomatoes?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tomato ni efite fioo wo adeka kome mli kɛ tomato kpakpa lɛ, ani no baaná tomato kpakpa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, rotten or bruised tomatoes release juices and fungi that cause surrounding healthy tomatoes to spoil rapidly. Sorting out bad produce immediately protects the rest of your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tomato ni egbo loo ekpɔtɔ lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. efiteɔ oya Nibii gbohii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ buɔ onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do cashew buyers offer lower prices if I do not clean and dry the nuts right after picking them off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ cashew lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ etsuuu nii ahe ni migbiko amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew nuts left on wet ground absorb moisture, which encourages mold inside the shell and reduces the nut's quality. Drying and cleaning them quickly preserves their value.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii ni ashiɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ baa shi Oya ni agbiɔ ni atsuuɔ he lɛ haa sɛɛnamɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut away damaged parts of my harvested yam before putting it in the yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fãi ni efite lɛ dani mikɛwo sweet potatoes ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rot spreads easily from one yam tuber to another through close contact in dark storage. Removing damaged tubers keeps the fungus from spreading and ruining your stored food supply.
ga: Rot hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ sweet potato tuber kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli kɛtsɔ bɛŋkɛmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa yɛ he ko ni akɛtoɔ nibii ni yɔɔ duŋ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni efite lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite niyenii ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl during hot afternoons to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant save water and survive heat stress until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and turn yellow when I remove all the shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mijie cacao tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong sunlight and can dry out easily. They rely on surrounding shade plants, like plantains, to shield them from intense heat while their roots develop.
