ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe, tamɔ plantains lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall with plenty of leaves but produce very small tubers in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lack of balanced nutrients, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ mli. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baato eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of water. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to put into storage bags safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo baagi mli shweshweeshwe?

english: You can check by pressing your thumbnail into a grain or shaking a handful of grains together. If the grain is hard enough not to dent and makes a sharp sound, it is dry enough to prevent mold during storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ oshishifa lɛ nɔ ni oootsi kɛya ŋmaa lɛ mli loo kɛtsɔ ŋmaa ni okɛ onine shwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, no lɛ amɛgbi bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa beni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea grains develop tiny holes and turn into dust after a few weeks in the room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔɔ sũ beni ehi tsu lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ?

english: Weevil insects lay invisible eggs on the beans before harvest, which hatch inside storage and eat the grain from the inside. Thorough drying and using airtight bags prevent them from damaging the crop.
ga: Weevil lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani akpaa. Amɛfɔɔ yɛ tsũ lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Kɛ́ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ vacuum bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Will planting big forest trees on my farm steal water and nutrients from my crops?
ga: Ani tsei agbo ko ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Not if you choose the right trees. Deep-rooted trees pull water and food from deep underground where crop roots cannot reach, and their fallen leaves rot to create natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Jeee nakai kɛji ohala tsei ni sa. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ lɛ. Ni baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ koni ekɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Why do some of the big trees on my farm drop all their leaves during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trees drop their leaves during the dry Harmattan as a survival trick to save water. Without leaves, the tree stops losing moisture to the dry wind until the rains return.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu he. Kɛji baai bɛ Tsei hu kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfiteɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do young tree seedlings wither and die when I plant them directly in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young tree seedlings have tender roots and thin leaves that dry out quickly under harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantain to grow strong before standing in full sun.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛdara waa dani amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen food in the soil, or the ground is flooded with too much water, which prevents the roots from taking in nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods before they mature into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop young pods, known as cherelle wilt, when the tree experiences water stress, lacks enough plant food, or tries to save energy to keep the main tree alive during dry weather.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni ale amɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Tso niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ Aloo bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni okɛ hewalɛ ato koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without growing into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil lacks moisture. The heat causes stress, making the plant abandon fruit production.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ni ehaa tsei shiɔ amɛ nitsumɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow during the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the surface and do not go deep into the ground. If planted too shallowly or damaged by underground pests, the roots cannot hold the heavy weight of the plant.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ, ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tso lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with huge leafy branches but yield tiny underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Eyɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating different crops or letting the land rest allows the soil to rebuild its natural strength.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Aloo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ama ebɔɔ su mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and spread easily while my crops struggle to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have natural survival advantages, allowing them to suck up available soil food, water, and sunlight much faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli wala sɛɛnamɔ. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ mli niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Can I plant cassava together with young rubber trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ rɔbɔt tsei yɛ he kome?

english: It is best to give them space. Cassava has very aggressive roots that absorb large amounts of soil moisture and nutrients, which can starve young rubber trees and slow down their growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha amɛ gbɛ. Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa waa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ rɔba tsei bibii ni amɛdaraa fioo.

english: Why do my rubber trees look weak and thirsty when I grow cassava right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni kumai miiye lɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are very strong at pulling water out of the soil around nearby plants. When planted too close, the cassava actively takes the water away from the rubber tree roots to feed its own tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he wa waa yɛ nu ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ ni bɔle tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ rɔbɔt shishifãi lɛ amli koni ekɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Root rot happens when excessive moisture builds up in poorly drained soil, allowing fungi and bacteria to attack the tubers underground and decay them while still in the land.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ.

english: Why does rotten cassava give off a harsh smell that stings my nose and skin when I touch it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni egbo lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ waa aahu akɛ kɛ́ mɔ ko ta he lɛ, etswaa ŋmei kɛ hewolo lɛ?

english: Certain rot-causing fungi produce strong acids and irritating gases as they break down the tuber. Touching or inhaling these decaying materials causes skin irritation and a stinging sensation.
ga: Fungi komɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ jieɔ acid ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ mli fuɔ beni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko ta nibii ni egboi nɛɛ ahe loo emu lɛ, ehaa hewolo nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa mɔ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shãa.

english: How can I prepare my land to stop rot from destroying my root crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ koni ŋmeii akafite mi-tubers lɛ?

english: You can prevent soil rot by constructing high mounds or ridges to help excess water drain away quickly, and by clearing out old infected crop roots from the field before planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafite kɛtsɔ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni ooofee koni eye ebua nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni eho oya lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ tso shishifãi momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested crops start rotting so quickly after I move them into my storage hut?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie amɛ kɛtee nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested tubers rot indoors when the storage area lacks proper ventilation, has high humidity, or when tubers damaged during harvest allow rot organisms to spread quickly from one crop to another.
ga: Tubers ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shia mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. hulutsoo ni fa babaoo loo kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli, ni no haa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Can working with rotten crops in the field make me fall sick?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite ni mikɛaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha hela amɔ mi?

english: Yes, handling severely rotten crops can expose you to harmful mold spores, bacteria, and irritating juices that can cause skin rashes, eye irritation, or respiratory discomfort.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite waa lɛ ni oootsu he nii lɛ baanyɛ aha onine ashɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, kɛ nu ni haa mɔ mli fuɔ ni baanyɛ aha ohewolo nɔ tsɔi, hiŋmɛii amli tsɔi, loo mumɔ mli naagbai aba onɔ.

english: Where does cassava get all the water it needs to form big tubers?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ŋmei naa nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ?

english: Cassava has deep, spreading roots designed to search for and extract water from a wide area in the soil, storing that moisture and energy inside its thick tubers.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Afee koni akɛtao nu kɛjɛ hei babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ajie kɛjɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ nakai ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ yitso ni mli edɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do rubber tree roots spread so far underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔbɔt shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Rubber trees develop large, spreading root systems to anchor the tall trees against strong winds and to seek out groundwater needed to produce continuous latex sap.
ga: Rɔba tsei feɔ shishifãi wuji ni gbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛkɛmɔ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni he hiaa koni akɛfee latɛs lɛ ataomɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do we have to press and squeeze out the water from cassava when processing it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmiimiɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ ni wɔmiimɔ mli kɛ́ wɔmiitsu he nii lɛ?

english: Raw cassava juice contains natural bitter liquids and toxins. Squeezing out the water removes these dangerous compounds and reduces moisture so the cassava can be safely roasted into finished products like gari.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ kɛ tsofai fɔji yɛ cassava fɔ ni ahoo lɛ mli. Nu lɛ mli ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ nɛkɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ. ni eha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi Bɔni afee ni anyɛ ashã ŋmei shweshweeshwe ni afee nibii ni agbe naa tamɔ gari.

english: Why should I bother spending time and money to remove big stones and rocks from my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be kɛ shika kɛjie tɛi wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Clearing stones allows crop roots to grow deep and spread freely into the soil. It also prevents damage to your farm tools and helps the soil hold water and nutrients evenly for your plants.
ga: Tɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Ehaa oŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ hu fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa otsei lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to clear out old tree stumps and heavy rocks before I plant cassava?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni ajie tsei akutsei momoi kɛ tɛi ni tsii dani adu ŋmei?

english: Yes, because cassava tubers need loose soil to expand. Removing rocks and stumps ensures the root tubers can grow long, thick, and healthy without getting crushed or deformed.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛshwere. Tɛi kɛ tsei akutsei ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adara kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛhe awa ni amɛkumɔɔɔ loo amɛfiteee.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my crops after the rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients very quickly. If you do not clear them early, they will choke your young crops and starve them of essential food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ojieee mli mra lɛ, Amɛbaatsi oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anaa ni amɛbaajie niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: How early in the season do I need to clear weeds from my young maize farm?
ga: Te ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra tɛŋŋ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: You should clear weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks after planting. This critical early window ensures young maize plants get all the soil nutrients they need to build strong stalks.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli yɛ be mli ni odu lɛ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ shishijee be ni he hiaa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná ŋmãa tsei ni wa.

english: Can weeds growing around the borders of my land bring diseases to my main crops?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihusu lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, weeds around field edges often harbor harmful insects and plant fungi. Clearing weeds around your farm boundaries destroys hiding places for pests before they move onto your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ fɔɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe ŋmeii. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ajieɔ Oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ fiteɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ dani amɛyaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: What does agricultural 'medicine' actually do for my crops when I buy it?
ga: Te okwaayeli ‘tsofai’ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ beni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Crop 'medicine' refers to sprays and fertilizers. Insecticides kill leaf-eating bugs, fungicides protect leaves from rotting spots, and fertilizers feed the soil to keep crops strong and healthy.
ga: Tso ‘tsofa’ tsɔɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ gbeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ. Tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my sickly crop needs chemical spray or just more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mitso ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo kɛkɛ he miihia?

english: If leaves show insect holes, spots, or powdery patterns, pests or fungi are attacking and need crop medicine. If the whole plant is simply limp during hot afternoon sun without insect damage, it usually just needs water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ko miitutua ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tso tsofa awo mli. Kɛji akɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni kooloi efiteee lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, nu pɛ he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning yellow even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are typically caused by tiny pests sucking sap from the leaves or by crop diseases. Applying the right crop spray early helps stop the infestation from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo tsei ahelai ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Is it truly worth investing money to properly clear land before every planting season?
ga: Ani shika ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, spending money to clear weeds and prepare loose soil helps seeds sprout faster and root deeper. Good initial land preparation leads to much higher yields, which repays your investment at harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, shika ni afiteɔ kɛjieɔ jwɛi ni asaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ dani afeɔ lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba. Enɛ baaha okɛ shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛji akpa.

english: Why do my crops still look weak and small even after I applied fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni efee bibii lolo beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔji lɛ amli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If weeds are not cleared before applying fertilizer, the weeds will consume most of the food before your crop roots can reach it, leaving your crops hungry despite the fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ Jwɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛ niyenii lɛ babaoo dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii po wo onibii amli lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye bo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sun. Plantains grow very quickly and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings essential shade and moisture during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and leafy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs extra manure or fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli dani madu?

english: If crops from your previous harvest produced small fruits or light yields, or if wild weeds on the land look stunted and pale, the soil is likely low on nutrients and requires compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni okpa tsutsu lɛ ji bibii loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo Aloo kɛji koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes often drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly from dry to overly wet. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps protect the flowers so fruits can set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa nɔ ni edɔ fe nine nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my sweet pepper fruits turning dark brown and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This soft rot at the bottom of peppers is called blossom-end rot. It happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium, often caused by irregular watering or dry spells during fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo be ni hulu enyɔ shi yɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look weak and refuse to grow well under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ni eda lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Garden eggs need full sunshine to make food and grow strong. Big trees block sunlight and their mature roots steal water and food from the smaller garden egg plants.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia abɔɔ mli ŋmeii koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa Ni amɛshishifãi ni eda lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ eggplant bibii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Curled and yellowing cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems helps protect your farm from this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and pale even during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal soil food, space, and sunlight. Even with plenty of rain, crops will starve if weeds are allowed to crowd their root spaces.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la mli, kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo po. Hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii hu kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛbɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam tubers rot easily if they were cut or damaged during harvesting, or if the storage barn is warm and lacks fresh airflow. Storing uninjured yams on raised, well-ventilated racks prevents premature decay.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afo amɛ loo amɛfite yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ shĩa lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ atomɔ ni pilaaa lɛ to adeka ni nɔ kwɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi fitemɔ naa oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa plants until they grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Which way should I bury my cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ afu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings must be planted with the tiny buds on the stem pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the sprouts to grow downwards into the dirt, resulting in weak plants and very small tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ tso ko ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi nɔ Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch direct sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves receive, the more energy the plant produces to grow large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ náa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the leaves turn dark green and support proper growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa, ni ebaaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the maize, keeping your farmland productive for longer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my tomato plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry material, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under strong sun, prevents soil water from evaporating quickly, and blocks weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving green droppings inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center funnel of the plant. Treating the crop early with approved control methods stops them before they destroy your whole harvest.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akudɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why are my pepper and tomato flowers falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences severe stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or soil that is too dry. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant keep its flowers and turn them into vegetables.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft rot when water sits on my farm after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits on the farm for days without draining away, it drowns the roots and causes rot-producing micro-organisms to multiply.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ehi ŋmɔ ko mli gbii babaoo ni ajieee lɛ kpo. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ehaa nibii bibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo

english: How can I stop small black insects from eating my stored maize grains after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii diji anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni ato lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weevils attack grain that has moisture or is kept in standard woven sacks. Drying your maize until the kernels are completely hard and storing them in airtight (hermetic) bags suffocates the insects and preserves your grain.
ga: Moth lɛ tutuaa ŋmaa ni mli efɔ loo ni akɛto kotokui ni akpɛ́ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa kwraa ni akɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my land seem completely worn out and unable to support new crops after years of cocoa farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite kwraa ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei anɔ yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛdu kookoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous cocoa farming consumes deep soil nutrients over decades without replacing them. Without organic manure, fallow periods, or fertilizers, the soil structure breaks down, leaving the ground dry, nutrient-poor, and unable to support healthy plant roots.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akɛ nakai niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ewoɔ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, fallow period, loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ baakumɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli, ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ tsei shishifãi ni wa lɛ anɔ.

english: If my cocoa farm has failed, what crops can I plant first to help restore the degraded soil?
ga: Kɛji mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ fite lɛ Mɛɛ tso esa akɛ madu klɛŋklɛŋ koni eye ebua ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aba ekoŋŋ?

english: Leguminous crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, or cover crops like Mucuna are best to plant first. They pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, rebuilding fertility naturally so that future cash crops can thrive.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ Mucuna klɛŋklɛŋ. Amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo heei bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown during the bright sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without taller shade trees like plantains or shade timber trees to block the harsh heat, the sun dries out their water supply faster than their roots can absorb it.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ, tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ baaha pɔmpi mli nu lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why is it bad to cut down all the big shade trees when I am clearing land for new cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejeee jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafo tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔji heei lɛ?

english: Removing all shade trees exposes young cocoa to extreme heat, wind damage, and fast soil drying. Forest shade trees also drop leaves that rot into natural manure and help maintain the moist microclimate cocoa trees need to survive.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei fɛɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ, ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ amɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ hu shĩɔ baai ni egboi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ mli fɛ̃i ni he hiaa cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ ahi shi.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black, rot, and spread to other pods?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, egboɔ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii krokomɛi anɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Rainy weather and dense bush allow water to stay on the pods, helping the fungal spores spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa nu hiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Why do the branches of my cocoa trees swell up and stop bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso lɛ niji lɛ fuɔ ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Swollen branches are a symptom of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus clogs the tree's internal tubes, preventing food and water from moving, which eventually kills the tree.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Virus lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ niyenii kɛ nu naa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbe tso lɛ.

english: Why do mirid bugs attack my cocoa trees more during certain times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Mirids multiply rapidly during the warm, rainy months when cocoa trees grow tender new shoots and young pods. They feed on these soft tissues by sucking out sap, leaving dark scars that cause shoots to die back.
ga: Mirids fɔɔ oya yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɛɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛmuɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Eshiɔ ŋmeii diji ni kɛ tu gbele baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but most of them drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pods?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or when the tree is under severe stress from dry weather and poor soil nutrients. Over-spraying harsh chemicals can also kill the beneficial insects needed for pollination.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ haomɔ ni naa wa mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Tsofai ni mli wa babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa kɛha pollination lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die off shortly after I plant them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings often suffer from transplant shock if planted during dry spells or if their roots are bent or damaged during planting. Planting right at the start of the main rainy season gives their roots cool, moist conditions to take hold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ transplant shock mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo kɛji shishifãi lɛ ebɔle loo efite yɛ dumɔ be mli Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some cocoa pods remain tiny, yellow, and dry up before they ever grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi feɔ bibii, ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as cherelle wilt. It is a natural process where the tree intentionally sacrifices smaller pods because it doesn't have enough water or nutrients to feed every single pod growing on the trunk.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Cherel’s Wilt. Eji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii shaa afɔle. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains beside them creates a shaded canopy that keeps the young plants cool and protects soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashiɔ tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow, especially when they carry fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ? Titri lɛ kɛ́ ewo yibii

english: Plantain plants have broad leaves that catch wind like a sail, but their roots grow shallow in the upper layer of soil. Supporting fruiting stems with wooden props and mounding soil around the base helps keep the plants securely grounded.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ tsɔnei. Shi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋwɛi fãi lɛ amli. Yibii ashishifãi ni akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ he kɛ muji ni abua naa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying balanced fertilizer or organic manure early gives the plant the essential nutrients it needs to make green leaves and produce full corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air within the soil to survive. When water stays pooled over the roots for too long, oxygen cannot reach them, causing the tubers to drown and soften into decay underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ ashɛ Oxygen he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam plants are natural vine climbers that produce energy through their leaves. Guiding the vines up wooden stakes lifts the foliage toward sunlight and keeps leaves off damp soil, which helps the underground tubers grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛjieɔ hewalɛ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ ba tso ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ amɛgbee shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Why are small worms eating the central leaves inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-funnel lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the tender center shoot of maize to feed on growing leaves. Detecting them early and applying approved controls directly into the leaf funnel protects the central growing tip.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii amli koni amɛye baai ni miida lɛ. mra mli nibii ni anaa Ni akɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and becoming wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking plant juices and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insect pests early stops the foliage from wrinkling and keeps the plant producing peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips, ni nuɔ tso nu kɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without forming any fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when temperatures rise too high or when water supply becomes irregular. When the plant experiences extreme heat or dry soil, it sheds its flowers to save moisture and stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow thin and weak if I sow many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together must fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds properly gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong stalks and thick leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ awuu koni hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni mli tse.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right after the very first short rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ? Klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: The very first shower often heats up dry soil without thoroughly soaking it deep down. Waiting for steady, consistent rains ensures there is sufficient moisture held in the soil for seeds to germinate safely without drying up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nu ni hoɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli tsɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do weeds and wild bush grow back so quickly after I clear my land with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cutting bush with a cutlass only removes the top part of the plants, leaving the roots intact underground. Those live roots and seeds hidden in the soil quickly sprout new shoots once sunlight and rain reach them.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ pɛ. Kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni hiɛ ka kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii heei oya kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ba.

english: Is it better to burn the dry bush after clearing my land, or should I leave the cleared grass on top of the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni egbi lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ loo esa akɛ mashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving the cleared grass on top of the soil acts as mulch, keeping the soil cool and moist while decomposing into natural food for your crops. Burning clears the land faster but destroys valuable soil nutrients and organic matter.
ga: Jwɛi ni he tse ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni efoɔ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Shãa haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ oya shi efiteɔ sũ mli niyenii ni jara wa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How long should I wait after clearing a fresh forest bush before sowing my seeds?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛji mijie sũ tsei lɛ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait about one to two weeks after clearing. This gives time for the cleared vegetation to dry out or decay and lets you clear away any fresh weed sprouts before planting your seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ beni ojie tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha be aha tsei ni ajie lɛ ni amɛgbi loo amɛgboi. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ jwɛi heei fɛɛ ni ekwɛ̃ dani oduɔ dumɔwui.

english: What should I put on my skin to protect myself when applying chemical weedkillers on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛwo mihewolo nɔ koni mikɛbu mihe kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi miitsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should wear protective long sleeves, rubber gloves, and boots, or apply barrier creams before spraying. Chemical weedkillers can easily absorb through bare skin, causing severe rashes, burns, or long-term illness.
ga: Esa akɛ owo atadei ni niji kɛlɛ, rɔba glɔvs, kɛ atadei. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ awo mli dani okɛshwie nɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ hewolo ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ mli oya, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa, shãa loo hela ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa.

english: Why does spraying farm chemicals make such a strong smell, and is it dangerous to breathe in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ waa nɛkɛ lɛ? Ni ani mumɔ ni amuɔ yɛ mli lɛ yɛ oshara?

english: The strong smell comes from volatile solvents that carry the active chemical into the air. Breathing in these vapors can cause dizziness, headaches, or lung damage, so you should always wear a nose mask and spray with the wind blowing away from you.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii ni kɛ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii yaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ omu lasu nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ohe afee shoo, oyitso agbɔjɔ, loo eflufla lɛ afite. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ owo mask yɛ ogɔŋ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afɔ ohe.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying chemical weedkiller before it is safe to plant my seeds?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani manyɛ madu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: Different weedkillers remain active in the soil for different periods. Waiting at least two weeks prevents chemical residues in the ground from burning or killing your delicate seedling roots.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ etsuɔ ​​nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ omɛ otsii enyɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni ekashã loo ekafite odumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops wilt in the hot afternoon sun after I remove all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Without shade trees, full sunlight causes young crops to lose water through their leaves faster than their undeveloped roots can draw it from the soil, leading to afternoon wilting.
ga: Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi ni edarako lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli.

english: Why do insects seem to attack my crops more when I plant on newly cleared virgin bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei bibii ni ajie amɛ ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing fresh bush destroys the wild native plants that insects normally eat. Without their natural food source, the insects move directly onto your soft, nutritious crop seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ sũ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ, efiteɔ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ amɛ daa lɛ. Kɛji adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhei bɛ lɛ Kooloi lɛ baafã tɛ̃ɛ kɛya otso dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni niyenii yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around the base of my crops while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Clearing them from around the base ensures your crops get all the nourishment needed to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛjiemɔ kɛjɛ he fɛɛ he Shishitoo lɛ kwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow when I plant them in soil that has a lot of freshly cut rotting grass buried in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni jwɛi ni egboi babaoo ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil microbes break down fresh grass, they temporarily consume all the available nitrogen in the soil. Without nitrogen, your crops cannot produce green leaves and will turn pale yellow until the grass finishes decaying.
ga: Kɛji nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fite sũ lɛ Amɛbaafite nitrogen fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ afee baai eŋɔli ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ baagboi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is even mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and make food; when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhaa niyenii. Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees protect young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and help keep the soil cool and moist so the seedlings can establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground if I do not harvest them during a heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When rain saturates the soil for too long, water displaces air in the ground. The submerged cassava roots cannot breathe, making them weak and easy targets for rot-causing fungal spores and bacteria.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without growing into fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, heat stress damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit formation. The plant sheds the unpollinated flowers to conserve energy and water.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Heat stress fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni etsĩɔ aduawai ni baa lɛ naa Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves of my corn plants with dirt-like dust inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ ni sũ tamɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the central leaf funnel of young maize plants during the day and feeds on the soft inner leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani amɛgbele.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller over time even though the main stool has many stems growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei titri lɛ yɛ tsei babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mli moŋ.

english: When too many suckers grow around one main plantain stem, they steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from each other. Removing extra suckers allows all the plant's energy to go into growing one large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and rot when the weather is wet and cool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, moist weather. Raindrops splash fungal spores from wet soil onto low-hanging pods, causing them to turn brown and rot quickly.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ kɛ fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ blɔfo ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and look wilted in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ mɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In strong heat, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves and usually bounce back once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Kɛji edɔ waa lɛ Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the air to receive maximum sunlight, which helps the plant make more food and produce larger tubers under the ground while protecting leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I avoid applying dry fertilizer onto bone-dry soil during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ sũ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve safely into nutrients the plant can use. Applying strong fertilizers to dry soil can concentrate chemical salts near the roots, burning and damaging the plant instead of feeding it.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ niyenii ni tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ aba. Eshãa tsei ni efiteɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: How can I prevent my rice grains from breaking apart when I dry them after parboiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala kɛ́ amɛmiigbi beni mikɛwo la mli sɛɛ?

english: Allowing parboiled rice to cool down slightly before spreading it out gently helps the grains firm up so they remain whole and do not shatter during drying and milling.
ga: Ha ŋmãa ni ashã lɛ mli ajɔ fioo dani okɛgbɛ ashwã blɛoo. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ mli awa. No hewɔ lɛ, efoŋ yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ kɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Where is the best place on my farm to spread my harvested rice so it stays safe?
ga: Mɛni ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni manyɛ magbɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mashwã koni efee shweshweeshwe?

english: Spread your rice in a designated, clean area away from heavy foot traffic, livestock, and vehicles so the grains do not get walked on or crushed.
ga: Okɛ o-rice lɛ agbɛ ashwã he ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni he tse. Ekɛ ehe akabɔ tsɔnei ni hoɔ babaoo, kooloi, kɛ tsɔnei ahe bɔni afee ni akanyiɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ loo akakumɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my hot parboiled rice out on the drying floor immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Spreading rice while it is still scalding hot makes the soft kernels weak and brittle, causing them to crack and split easily when moved.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbɛ ŋmãa lɛ oshwã be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa bibii lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ ni egbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha amɛgbala ni amɛkumɔ oya kɛji ajie amɛ.

english: Why should I spread my harvested grains thinly in a safe spot instead of piling them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ashwã bibii bibii? Yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe moŋ fe ni oookɛto.

english: Spreading grains thinly in a dedicated space lets them cool and dry evenly while protecting them from getting trampled and crushed at the bottom of a heavy pile.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ agbɛɛmɔ bibioo He ni ajɔɔ nɔ aha lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe jɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe hu koni akanyiɛ amɛnɔ ni akumɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ ashishi.

english: Why shouldn't I apply storage medicine to my harvested grain while it is still hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpaa be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ tsuɔ nii?

english: High heat can break down the crop protection medicine, reducing its strength and preventing it from protecting your grain against pests.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ afite tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛhewalɛ baa shi, ni ehaaa amɛbu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How long should I wait before putting pest medicine on my parboiled crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo tsei ni ashã la mli?

english: You should wait until the crops cool down to room temperature so the heat does not destroy the active ingredients in the medicine.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli adɔ kɛyashɛ shĩa mli latsaa he bɔni afee ni latsaa lɛ akafite nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ tsofa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can excessive heat ruin the crop chemicals I use to protect my stored food?
ga: Ani dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine baanyɛ afite tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛbuɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yes, extreme heat causes many crop protection chemicals to evaporate or lose their effectiveness, leaving your stored produce vulnerable to insects.
ga: Hɛɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa haa tsofai babaoo ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛtsuuu nii dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni okɛtoɔ lɛ nyɛɔ efiteɔ.

english: Why is it important to keep my rice grains whole during post-harvest processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ be mli lɛ?

english: Whole rice grains attract higher market prices, store better without spoiling, and cook more evenly than broken grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ gbalaa jara ni yaa hiɛ yɛ jara nɔ. Shwapoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee. ni ebaanyɛ ehoo niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ Fe dumɔwui ni akumɔ

english: Why do my rice grains break into small pieces when I process them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice ŋmeii lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ atsu he nii lɛ?

english: Grains usually break if they are handled roughly while still hot or if they are not allowed to cool down and harden before being moved and spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, omɔ ŋmaa fãa kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. be mli ni edɔ lolo loo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni edɔ ni efee shiŋŋ dani ajie lɛ ni agbɛ ashwã.

english: Does handling my harvested grains roughly reduce their value at the market?
ga: Ani mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Yes, rough handling crushes and breaks the grains, and buyers in local markets pay significantly less for crushed or broken produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ebaagbala ni ebaakumɔ ŋmaa lɛ. Ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo kwraa kɛha nibii ni atswa loo akumɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning up under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade trees or plantains around them because direct sunlight overheats their sensitive leaves, draining their moisture and causing them to yellow and scorch before they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛya. ni eha amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshã dani amɛdara.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft right on the tree when the wet season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water mold that thrives in excessive moisture and cool shade. Trimming bushy branches allows sunlight and air to dry the pods, stopping the mold from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nu mli muji ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i fe nine kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why is my maize turning yellow from the bottom leaves upward before it even forms corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi dani efee abele lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves means your maize is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and strength, so applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer will revive them.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars hide inside the top leaves of my maize plants and chew holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛfoɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the damp, soft inner center of the young maize plant. Catching them early and applying recommended natural or chemical controls into the plant's center will protect your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli efɔ lɛ ateŋ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn watery and rot underground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain saturates the soil without proper drainage, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen, allowing rot fungi to breakdown the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ nu ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ afite ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting in the barn long before the planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to trapped heat and moisture in storage. Storing your yams in a cool, well-ventilated shade barn keeps them dormant until you are ready to plant.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛwo la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkawɔ. kɛyashi be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight rolls and stop the plant from bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant sap, which distorts new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni fiteɔ baai heei adalɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa la kpɛɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry bush grass keep them green during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts as mulch, forming a protective shield that blocks the harsh sun, traps soil moisture, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Mulch ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and weak even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops, starving your plants of the food they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei náaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: If I use water from the river near my farm that looks brown and oily to water my maize, will it harm the crops?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo mu lɛ tsu nii kɛwo mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ nu. Ani ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, if the river water contains dangerous chemicals or heavy mud from upstream washing or mining, it can coat plant roots, prevent them from taking in food, and cause your maize to turn yellow or die.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara loo sũ ni tsii ni jɛɔ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ahoɔ loo ajieɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ yɛ faa lɛ mli nu lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ coat tso shishifãi Atsi amɛnaa koni amɛkaye nii. ni eha ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ loo egbo.

english: Is rainwater better for my crops than taking water from the local stream?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu ni mikɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi fe nu ni mikɛbaajɛ maŋ lɛ mli faai amli lɛ?

english: Rainwater is usually much safer and cleaner for your crops because local streams can carry chemical pollution, dangerous metals, or bad dirt that harms root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa ni ehe tse kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, faai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. dade ni yɔɔ oshara loo muji gbohii ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ awui

english: Can I use water from my fish pond to water my vegetable garden?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ nu ni jɛɔ loo ŋshɔ mli lɛ awo aduawai abɔɔ mli nu?

english: Yes, clean fish pond water is actually good for crops because fish waste acts as a natural fertilizer. However, you must ensure the stream feeding your pond does not contain dangerous chemicals.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nubu ni mli tse lɛ hi diɛŋtsɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, loo mli jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui akafee nu ni hoɔ kɛboteɔ o-pond lɛ mli.

english: Why does nothing grow on the patch of land where people used to dig for gold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni be ko ni eho lɛ gbɔmɛi tsaa shika tsuru yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Digging strips away the topsoil where plants get their food. It also leaves behind hard, packed ground and harsh chemicals that prevent seeds from sprouting and roots from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsei lɛ naa amɛ niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Eshiɔ hei ni wa ni ebɔle ehe kɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni haaa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni shishifãi akakwɛ̃ hu yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava close to those large open pits left in the bush?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ bu agbo ko ni agbele ni ashi yɛ jwɛi mli lɛ masɛi?

english: It is risky because the soil around abandoned pits loses its nutrients easily, and rainwater washing out of those pits can carry toxic chemicals directly into your cassava roots.
ga: Oshara yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Bui ni ashi amɛ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Ni nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nakai bu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛya ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I tell if bad water has spoiled the soil on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu fɔŋ miifite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Signs of damaged soil include an oily film or strange crust on the ground, plants dying suddenly in patches, earthworms disappearing, and crop leaves turning burnt at the edges.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ he ji sini ni mli ewo fɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, tsei ni gboiɔ trukaa yɛ hei srɔtoi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii laaje ni tsei ahe baai lɛ shã yɛ amɛshishigbɛ

english: Can I restore damaged soil so that my yams and plantains can grow well again?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ koni mi-sweet potatoes kɛ plantains lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, but it takes effort. You can heal damaged soil by adding plenty of natural manure, planting cover crops like beans to rebuild the soil, and blocking polluted water from entering your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ebiɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. ni otsi nu fɔŋ ni boteɔ oŋmɔji amli lɛ naa.

english: Why are my vegetable leaves turning yellow even though I give them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant roots are damaged or the water contains harmful chemicals that block the plant from drinking in proper nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ tso shishifãi ni efite. Aloo tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ nu lɛ mli ni haaa tsei anu niyenii kpakpai ni sa.

english: If my crops grow fine near a polluted river, is the harvest still safe for my family to eat?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ faa ko ni mli ewo muji lɛ masɛi Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe lolo ni miweku lɛ baaye?

english: Not always. Some crops can absorb invisible chemicals and dangerous metals into their roots or fruits without looking sick, making the food unsafe for consumption.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni anaaa kɛ dade ni yeɔ mɔ awui awo amɛshishifãi loo amɛyibii lɛ amli ni ekɛ hela baaa amɛnɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, niyenii lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyeli.

english: Why do my plants droop and dry up during the afternoon heat even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: When crop roots are poisoned by chemicals or damaged by dirty water, they lose their ability to draw up water, causing the leaves to wilt in hot sunlight even if the dirt feels wet.
ga: Beni tsofai efite tso shishifãi loo nu ni mli ewo muji efite lɛ. Tse shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhiɛ nu mli dɔŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the necessary shade and humidity for cocoa trees to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni kookoo tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas or beans alongside maize is beneficial because legumes naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize and improves soil fertility without extra fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa kroko afata he.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are common signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies. It slows down the plant's growth and reduces the size of the cassava tubers under the ground.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ cassava mosaic hela he. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants to eat tender leaves. Catching them early with recommended sprays or neem extracts prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before turning into fruit during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat and dry soil. The plant becomes stressed and conserves water and energy to stay alive rather than putting effort into making fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the roots of my garden vegetables start rotting when I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like they need water. When you water heavily every day, water fills all the empty spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots so they decay instead of taking up food.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni okɛ nu woɔ mli babaoo daa gbi lɛ Nu baaha he ni sũ lɛ mli efee efolo lɛ ayi obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ niyenii najiaŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing huge green leaves but failing to produce any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo tomato lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their power into growing stems and big green leaves while delaying flowering and fruit production.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha otsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛkwɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ baai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my corn field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and the plant is actively growing—usually two weeks after germination and again when the corn reaches knee-high—so the roots can absorb it immediately before rain washes it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu, kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ shɛ tsitsi nɔ Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ lɛ afɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly after I dig them up from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they suffer cuts from farming tools during harvest, are left out in direct sun after digging, or are stored in warm rooms without free-flowing air.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ okwaayeli nibii amli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Ashiɔ lɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ. Aloo okɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Can I save the seeds from the maize harvest I bought at the market to plant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ jara nɔ lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?
