english: Market maize is often hybrid seed bred for a single harvest. Replanting those saved seeds will result in weaker plants, uneven growth, and much lower yields compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛkpaa nii shikome. Nakai dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ adumɔ baaha tsei lɛ afee mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ. uneven growth Ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are my maize stalks staying short and turning pale green instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which maize relies on heavily to build strong stems and leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure early in the season gives the crop the food it needs to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ tsei kɛ baai ni wa ni etswaa lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tsei lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, while legumes like groundnuts and beans actually put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating crops keeps your land fertile without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly with broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Plantains daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni kookoo tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yam plants store energy in their leaves from sunlight to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves high into the air so they get maximum sun and prevents them from rotting on the damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ toɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when we get good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight to feeding your crop instead of unwanted wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ koni kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ koo mli tsei ni ataooo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the fresh center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the central funnel of the maize plant to feed. Spotting them early allows you to use recommended sprays or organic controls before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which feed on leaf sap and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate treatments keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsamɔ ni sa tsu nii lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the heavy rains last too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains saturate the soil, excess water blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, causing underground fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow before the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and spreading, making the tree top-heavy once a heavy bunch of fruit grows. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole prevents the tree from snapping or pulling out of the ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Ehaa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ mlɛo kɛ́ aduawai lɛ dara babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo ekaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures and irregular soil moisture cause heat stress, which makes tomato plants drop their flowers to save energy. Adding mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cooler and retains moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Mulch ni bɔleɔ otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key food plants need to grow. It can also happen when roots are sitting in too much water, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Enɛ haaa anyɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnuts produce empty pods with no seeds inside when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks calcium during the pod development stage. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to your soil before planting provides the calcium needed to fill the pods.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘nut shells’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni pod lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha calcium ni he hiaa koni akɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leaf and stem growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their green color and helps them produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans on a plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally pulls nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil. Planting them after nitrogen-hungry crops like maize recharges the soil's natural fertility for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen he hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does mixing animal manure into my soil help crops stay healthy during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a natural sponge under the ground. It improves the soil's ability to hold onto water longer, providing your crops with moisture even when rains are brief or irregular.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be kuku po. loo nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod Disease, which spreads quickly in dark, overly damp conditions. Pruning excess farm shade and clearing weeds lets in light and airflow to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ kookoo diji baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Jwɛi ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling inward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle mli ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking sap from the young leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests. Spraying with neem-based organic remedies or insecticidal soap helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ anɔ Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and placing dry grass mulch around the base protects the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does it matter which way up I plant my cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ mi-cassava niji lɛ he hiaa lɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings have small buds along the stem that must point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new sprouts to grow downward first before curving up, which weakens the plant and leads to smaller root yields.
ga: Yucca niji lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛya shi dani amɛba ŋwɛi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves off the ground and capture as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy, which is sent down into the ground to build big, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie Plantain shishitoo lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from each other, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning extra suckers leaves just one or two strong stems that can produce large, heavy fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when weeds take over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni jwɛi ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that aggressively compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds crowd your crops, they steal the essential food your plants need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi ji jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ jwɛi ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: If my land was previously dug up for gold mining, can I still grow food crops like cassava on it?
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha shika tsuru ŋmɔ dani Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei lolo?

english: Mined land usually loses its top layer of fertile black soil and can contain harmful chemicals. Cassava needs deep, soft soil to swell its roots, so you must first clear heavy stones, break up hard ground, and add lots of compost or manure before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni atsa lɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ, ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ ahi mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia Yucca koni eshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie tɛi ni tsii, ogbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli dani odu.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant cowpeas or beans together with maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer that feeds the neighboring maize plants and keeps the farm healthy.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall but end up producing very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall when they get nitrogen, but they need phosphorus and enough space to form large cobs. If plants are crowded together or lack balanced nutrients, they fight each other for food, resulting in tall stems with small cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen nɔ. Shi ehe miihia ni amɛná fɔsfɔs kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji tsei eyi amɛhe obɔ loo niyenii ni sa bɛ amɛmli lɛ, Tsei lɛ baatswa niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is under heat stress or lacks moisture and shade. Tiny insects called midges are needed to pollinate the flowers; providing shade trees keeps the air humid so these beneficial insects can survive and pollinate.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi loo ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ he miihia kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Shade ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ anyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. When a bunch grows large, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds easily pull the roots out of loose or wet soil unless you support the stem with a sturdy wooden Y-pole.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛji kuu lɛ da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa shishifãi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni etse loo ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya. Ja okɛ tso ni mli wa ni tamɔ Y fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that carry plant viruses. Keeping the farm free of weeds and spraying natural neem leaf solution early helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Ni aaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko kɛ neem tso ni ji adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black rotten spots on the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching with dry leaves prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi ni oookɛwo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ahiɛ akafite.

english: How do I know when yams under the ground are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the green leaves and vines above the ground start turning yellow and dry up. This signals that the plant has stopped growing leaves and stored all its energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I just save grain from my hybrid maize harvest to plant as seeds next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu akɛ dumɔwui yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one strong harvest. If you replant the seeds harvested from that crop, the next generation loses its strength, resulting in uneven growth, weak plants, and low yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha kpamɔ kome ni mli wa. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, Yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ hewalɛ baaje edɛŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster on my land than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miida oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally adapted to sprout quickly and grab available sunlight, water, and nutrients. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your crops of essential food.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛhe hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa onibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do people recommend planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize plants, helping them grow stronger without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller if I keep planting it on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava heavy feeds on specific nutrients in the ground. Planting it on the same spot continuously drains those nutrients completely, giving the soil no time to recover, which results in smaller tubers.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oya nɔ odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ ajɛ mli kwraa. Enɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees curl up and droop during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl and droop to protect themselves from hot, dry winds. By reducing the surface area exposed to the sun, the plant saves water and prevents itself from drying out.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baaha nu akafite, ni ebaatsi ehe gbɛ koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: When yam vines turn yellow and dry up naturally near the end of the season, it means the plant has stopped growing leaves and moved all its remaining energy down into the underground tuber. It is a sign the yam is mature.
ga: Beni be lɛ miihe ashɛ naagbee lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato lɛ egbɔ.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Regular watering and avoiding excessive fertilizer help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light, leaving them weak and without enough energy to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I see tiny holes in my pepper leaves and small green insects underneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ pepper baai lɛ kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: The holes and insects are caused by pests like aphids that suck sap from the plant and eat leaf tissue. Spraying natural remedies like neem oil or recommended pesticides keeps them from damaging your crop yields.
ga: Bu kɛ ŋmeii jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aphids, ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli ni amɛyeɔ baa fãji. Akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni adu lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell if my sweet potatoes under the ground are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are ready when the vines start turning yellow and dropping leaves. You can also dig up one tuber and cut it; if the liquid sap dries quickly without turning black, the harvest is ready.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo beni wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsa yitso kome hu ni ofo mli. Kɛji akɛ mliki lɛ gĩ oya ni etsɔko ediŋŋ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ kpamɔ lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why do maize seeds bought from an agricultural supplier produce better yields than seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred for high yields and disease resistance in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in smaller and uneven crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ baa.

english: Can the seeds or suckers I buy bring disease directly into my farm?
ga: Ani dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni miheɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, infected seeds, stem cuttings, or suckers can carry invisible fungi, bacteria, or viruses inside them. Even if your soil is completely clean, planting infected material will cause the crop to grow sick.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmeii, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, loo helai ni anaaa lɛ awo mli. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse kwraa po Shi nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela.

english: How can I check if my seeds or planting materials are safe before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji midumɔwui loo nibii ni miduɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe dani madu?

english: Inspect planting materials carefully for dark spots, mold, insect holes, unusual soft spots, or bad smells. Always source seeds and stem cuttings from certified dealers or healthy, proven farms.
ga: Kwɛmɔ nibii ni adu lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji hei ni yɔɔ ediŋ, ŋmei, kooloi amli bu, kɛ hei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ. loo ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ná dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Is it possible for the soil itself to make my crops sick?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela?

english: Yes, disease-causing germs like fungi and bacteria can live in the soil for months or years. When you plant susceptible crops, these soil-borne organisms attack the roots and stems from underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai ni kɛ hela baa tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi baanyɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli nyɔji loo afii babaoo. Beni odu tso ni bɛ hewalɛ Nɛkɛ nibii ni fɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɛɛ tutuaa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do crops in one small patch of my farm get sick while crops in the rest of the field stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he bibioo ko No hewɔ lɛ hela mɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ mɔ kome. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kpakpa lolo

english: Soil conditions vary across a field. Low spots that hold water, areas with poor drainage, or patches where diseased plants grew previously can harbor diseases that attack crops only in those specific spots.
ga: Esoro shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Low point that stores water Hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Aloo hei ni tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ tsutsu lɛ baanyɛ ahi helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nakai hei pɔtɛɛi lɛ pɛ.

english: If I plant the exact same crop on the same land every season, will it bring disease?
ga: Kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ani ebaaha hela aba?

english: Yes, planting the same crop continuously feeds specific soil pests and diseases, allowing their numbers to build up over time. Rotating with different crop types helps starve and clear these soil diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha sũ mli kooloi kɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi aye nii be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa amɛyifalɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ yɛ henɔi srɔtoi anaa Eyeɔ ebuaa kɛ hɔmɔ ni ejieɔ helai nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can insects and small bugs spread sickness from one plant to another in my farm?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, insects like mealybugs, aphids, and whiteflies feed on plant sap. When they bite a diseased plant and move to a healthy one, they carry and inject the sickness directly into the healthy crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs, aphids, kɛ whiteflies yeɔ tsei amli nu. Enɛ ji be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ ni amɛjieɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Amɛwoɔ helai ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Do insect bites on my crop leaves create a way for diseases to enter?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni ŋmɔɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ kɛ hela baa?

english: Yes, when insects chew leaves or stems, they create open wounds on the plant. Fungi and bacteria in the air or water can easily enter these wounds and infect the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii ŋmɔ baai loo tsei ahe. Amɛbaafee pilamɔi ni agbele yɛ tso lɛ mli. Fungi kɛ bacteria ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nu mli lɛ baanyɛ abote pilamɔi nɛɛ amli oya ni amɛwo tso lɛ mli hela.

english: What actually causes a healthy crop to suddenly catch a disease?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ hela trukaa?

english: Crop diseases are caused by microscopic living organisms like fungi, bacteria, and viruses. They enter plants through natural openings, wounds caused by pests or tools, or directly through root systems.
ga: Tse helai jɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ ŋmei, muawai, kɛ muawai. Amɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii amli amɛboteɔ tsei amli. Pilamɔi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo nitsumɔ dadei kɛbaa loo kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Can sharing cutlasses and farm tools with my neighbor spread disease to my farm?
ga: Ani dadei kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mikɛ mikutsoŋbii lɛ jaa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛya miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cutlasses, hoes, and even farm boots carry infected plant sap and soil. If you cut a sick crop and then use the same tool on a healthy plant without cleaning it, you transfer the disease.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tso mli nu kɛ sũ ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ dadei, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmɔ mli atadei po amli. Kɛji ofo tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛ nakai dɛŋdade lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni otsuuu he. Etsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ ogbɛ hela oshwã.

english: How does rainwater moving across my land spread diseases between crops?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ helai eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ?

english: Flowing rainwater runoff picks up disease spores and infected soil from sick plants and carries them downstream, depositing the germs onto healthy crop roots and lower stems.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ holeɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa faa lɛ shishi. Amɛbuaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa yɛ tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does the water in my farm soil dry up so fast when the hot afternoon sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ je kpo lɛ?

english: Strong sunlight heats up the soil surface and the plant leaves, turning the water in the soil into invisible vapor that escapes into the air through evaporation. Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves keeps the ground cool and traps that moisture longer.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ lasu ni anaaa ni tsɔɔ lasu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Do my crops still need air to breathe during the night when there is no sunlight?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ lolo koni amɛmu gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu la bɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, crops need air day and night to stay alive. While they use sunlight during the day to manufacture food, at night they rely on taking in oxygen from the surrounding air and soil to process that food and stay healthy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ fɛɛ koni amɛhi shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii yɛ gbi mli koni amɛkɛfee niyenii moŋ, shi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛtsu niyenii he nii ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when water sits on the field for too long after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air trapped inside the soil to breathe just as much as they need water. When flooded water sits on the land, it pushes out all the air spaces in the soil, causing the roots to drown, suffocate, and decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjeɔ kpo, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves droop in the afternoon heat but look fresh and standing again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi kwɛmɔ akɛ ohe ejɔ bo ni ote shi ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: During the hot afternoon, plants lose water into the air faster than their roots can drink it from the dry soil, causing leaves to wilt to protect themselves. During the cool night, the plant stops losing water, allowing the roots to refill the leaves before morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsei baakpa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ. Ha shishifãi lɛ ayi baai lɛ amli obɔ dani je tsɛre.

english: Why do crops planted under thick shade trees grow tall and thin but fail to yield good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Plants use direct sunlight as energy to build strong stems and produce fruits. When shaded, the crop stretches upward desperately searching for light, using up all its energy on height instead of developing thick stems and heavy yields.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo yibii. Beni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi, ni amɛtao la waa. ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa Moŋ lɛ, ewoɔ tsei ni mli tse ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do wild weeds make my crops weak and yellowish even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds aggressively compete with your crops for space, soil nutrients, and air. Even with plenty of rain, the fast-growing weeds absorb the food in the soil first, leaving your crops starving and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ mli waa Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ babaoo nɛɔ moŋ Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Where does the heavy wetness on my crop leaves come from in the early morning before any rain has fallen?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ jɛɔ leebi maŋkpa dani nugbɔ nɛɔ?

english: As the air cools down at night, water vapor floating in the air condenses into tiny liquid water drops when it touches cold surfaces like leaves. This dew gives your plants a refreshing drink of surface moisture before the sun rises.
ga: Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ Nu lasu ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ nu bibii bibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ tamɔ tso baa lɛ kpe Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa otsei lɛ nuɔ nu ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli dani hulu lɛ teɔ shi.

english: How does spreading dried palm fronds on my vegetable beds protect them during the hot season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei tsei ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: The dried leaves act like a protective hat over the earth, blocking direct sunlight from scorching the soil. This prevents soil water from evaporating into the air and keeps the root zone cool enough for the plant to absorb food.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, why do I get smaller tubers than when I space them far apart?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ fe be mli ni mijara amɛmli lɛ?

english: When planted too close, the roots and leaves of neighboring crops crowd each other out and fight for the limited air, water, and sunlight available. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough light and nutrients to grow large, fat tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni faaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni yɔɔ fɔ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and stop growing when the ground becomes hard and tightly packed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil seals off the underground air pockets, making it impossible for roots to breathe and absorb nutrients. Loosening the soil around the plants lets air and water reach the roots so the leaves can become green and healthy again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni wa lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu shɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and falling off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea early in the season keeps leaves green and improves harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots compete under the ground for water, nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each stem enough room and soil nutrients to form big, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi ni mli wa.

english: Why do small worms keep eating the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks the growing heart of young maize. Inspecting your farm early and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended bio-pesticides can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmei bibii tsui ni miida lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem tso mli nu loo bio-insecticide ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits rot at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛtsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually because the soil dries out irregularly. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and adding wood ash helps the tomato plants absorb enough calcium.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ tso ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die during the main dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that burn under strong direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young trees from hot sun and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming any pods during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛbɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers during heatwaves to conserve water and protect themselves from dying. Retaining shade trees on your farm helps cool the air and reduces flower drop during hot spells.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall bushy leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend its energy producing tall leaves instead of tubers. Cassava needs potassium-rich soil or wood ash to direct its energy into swelling the roots underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ loo tso sũ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia cassava koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to capture rainwater and soil food quickly before cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds when they are small prevents them from stealing light and nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛmɔmɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi beni jwɛi lɛ darako lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get tiny holes after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powder ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weevils bore into dry maize to eat and lay eggs. Drying your harvested maize thoroughly and storing seeds in airtight hermetic bags starves pests of oxygen and preserves the grain safely without chemicals.
ga: Weevils shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛye ni amɛwo amɛwui. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli, ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni tsofai bɛ mli.

english: Why do the edges of my pepper leaves dry up and turn brown after I put chemical fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Placing fertilizer too close to stems burns the roots because chemical fertilizer acts like concentrated salt. Always apply fertilizer a few inches away from the plant stem into moist soil so roots can drink it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ ejaakɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi. Koni shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni anuɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ miihoso lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cocoa trees can be caused by a lack of essential soil nutrients, extreme heat stress, or sap-sucking pests. Identifying the specific cause helps you decide whether to apply fertilizer, improve shade, or use pest control.
ga: Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. hulutsoo ni naa wa waa loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ Kɛ́ oyɔse nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ enɛ baa lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpɛɔ oyiŋ kɛji obaawo fɔmɔ nii. Ha shade aya hiɛ Aloo okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ atsu nii?

english: How can I tell if my crop has a real disease or if it is just suffering from poor soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hela diɛŋtsɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛkɛ miipiŋ lɛ?

english: Diseases usually cause spots or rot that spread from plant to plant. Soil issues typically affect a whole patch of plants at once, causing symptoms like leaf curling or yellowing without infectious spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai saa tsei fɛɛ ahe shikome. Ekɛ okadii tamɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmɔŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ egbɛɛɛ eshwaaa lɛ baa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees just standing still and refusing to grow new shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ekpoo akɛ ebaakwɛ ŋmeii heei lɛ?

english: When trees stop growing, it often means the roots cannot absorb necessary food from the soil due to hard soil, waterlogging, or a missing chemical element needed for plant growth.
ga: Kɛ tsei kpa dalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, nu ni hoɔ, loo tsofai ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Can rotting leaves and wet debris on top of the soil harm my plants?
ga: Ani baai ni egboi kɛ sũ ni efɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye mitsei lɛ awui?

english: While organic matter is good, overly wet and rotting material touching the base of your plants can breed surface fungi that attack stems and cause symptoms that look like plant diseases.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ hi moŋ Shi nibii ni mli ewo fɔ ni egboi babaoo ni kɛ otso lɛ shishi lɛ kpeɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni tutuaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni ekɛ okadii ni tamɔ tso hela baa.

english: What does it mean when someone says my crop issue is caused by a missing soil element?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai lɛ jɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ko ni elaaje lɛ hewɔ?

english: Plants require specific nutrients from the earth, like nitrogen or potassium, to grow healthy leaves. A missing element means the soil lacks a specific building block, leading to leaf damage or weak trunks.
ga: Tsei taoɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. koni eha baai lɛ awa Nibii ni elaaje lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsumaa he nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ loo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does the ground around my cocoa roots look slimy and rotted after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle No hewɔ lɛ mi-cocoa shishifãi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rainwater stays on top of the soil without draining away, it starves the soil of air, causing dead leaves and organic matter on the surface to rot in a harmful way.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɔ.

english: How can I stop the stems of my young plants from rotting where they touch the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mitsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite kɛji amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpe?

english: Clear heavy wet mulch and decaying weeds a few inches away from the main trunk so air can flow around the base of the plant, keeping the stem dry and healthy.
ga: Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ kɛ jwɛi ni egboi lɛ ahi tso lɛ tso lɛ he inchi kome mli. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ, ni eha tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbi ni efee shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves twist up when the sun gets very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: In hot sun, cocoa trees twist or curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, helping them hold onto water and protect themselves from burning.
ga: yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe koni amɛha he ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Does rotten soil on the ground mean my cocoa farm has black pod disease?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ black pod hela?

english: No, surface rot on wet ground is caused by poor drainage and decaying leaves, whereas black pod disease is caused by specific fungal spores that attack the pods directly.
ga: Dabi, nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ substrate rot ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa.

english: What should I do first if I notice my cocoa leaves twisting but the main trunk looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji mina kookoo baai ni etsilɛ shi tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Inspect the soil at the base of the tree to ensure it is not waterlogged or rotting, check for missing shade, and consider testing if the soil needs additional fertilizer.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ nu ehiɛɛɛ mli loo efiteee. Kwɛmɔ kɛji shade bɛ. Ni susumɔ he akɛ oookwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he loo ehe ehiaaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and turn yellow when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays flooded with water, it blocks air from reaching the roots. This causes the roots to choke and rot underground, leaving the plant unable to draw up nutrients even though water is everywhere.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ he fɛɛ he moŋ.

english: How does planting my crops on raised soil mounds help them grow better during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Raised mounds allow excess rainwater to drain away from the root area, keeping the soil loose and airy so root crops like cassava and yam do not rot.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu ahi mli. Koni shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei akafite

english: Why is my cassava rotting in the ground even though the top leaves still look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when heavy soil traps standing water. Because the damage happens hidden beneath the surface, the top of the plant stays green until the roots are completely destroyed.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ. Ejaakɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ eŋɔli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: Planting too closely blocks sunlight and air from reaching the lower leaves, creating a dark, damp space that causes weak, thin stalks and invites diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ odu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni ekɛ helai srɔtoi baa.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings struggling to grow under the thick bush on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees need light shade to protect them from heat, complete darkness prevents their leaves from making food from sunlight, causing weak growth.
ga: Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he. Shi duŋ ni mli ewo duŋ kwraa lɛ tsiɔ ebaai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do black spot diseases spread so quickly on my pepper leaves during wet, cloudy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela ni ji black spot lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi ni atatu ewo mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and lack of bright sunlight create the perfect environment for fungal spores to multiply rapidly and spread across wet leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni bɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores lɛ baafa oya ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã baai ni efɔ lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds from around the base of my crops before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aje shishi?

english: Dense weeds trap moisture and dark air around the plant stem, creating a humid hidden space where fungal diseases and stem-rot thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe, ni efeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ stem rot baanyɛ ada yɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings die suddenly overnight in the nursery even when I water them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gboi trukaa nyɔɔŋ kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Overwatering in shady, crowded nursery beds causes 'damping-off,' a soil disease where hidden fungi attack and snap the tender stems at soil level while you sleep.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli fe nine lɛ kɛ ‘fɔmɔ’ baa, ni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ hela ko ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfoɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli beni owɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I catch fall armyworms on my maize farm before they destroy the whole crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mamɔ cutworms yɛ mi-corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ?

english: Check your farm early in the morning when pests are active. Look inside the leaf funnel for small ragged holes and dark droppings, which show pests are hiding inside before major damage happens.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miitsu nii. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ amli koni ona buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ mli dani nɔ ko wulu baafite.

english: Why do leaves on my green vegetables look scorched and sickly when I grow them inside a closed greenhouse structure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni shã ni hela mɔ amɛ beni mikwɛɔ amɛ yɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Enclosed structures with poor ventilation trap heat and humidity like an oven, suffocating the plants if fresh air cannot enter to cool them down.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni aŋã ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Amɔmɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i, tamɔ flɔnɔɔ, ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nyɛɛɛ abote mli ni ekɛha tso lɛ mli ajɔɔ.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting a coconut tree before it starts giving me fruits?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii ogbe naa lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani amɛje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: It depends on the variety you plant. Short dwarf coconut varieties start bearing fruits in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 8 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Kokooi kukuji lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kokooi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How far apart should I space coconut seedlings when planting them on my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should space them about 7.5 to 9 meters apart in a square or triangular pattern. Coconut leaves grow wide, so generous spacing ensures each tree gets full sunlight and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ amɛ abɔ he aaafee mitai 7.5 kɛyashi 9 yɛ sqɛɛ loo triangle su mli. Kokosu baai lɛ daraa babaoo. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: What is the difference between the short dwarf coconut trees and the traditional tall ones?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso bibioo ko kɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ ni ji blema ŋmei tso lɛ teŋ?

english: Dwarf coconut trees stay short, produce fruit much earlier (3–4 years), and are easy to harvest from the ground. Tall coconut trees take longer to fruit (6–8 years) and grow very high, but they live longer, tolerate dry weather better, and produce larger nuts.
ga: Dwarf coconut tsei lɛ hiɔ shi be kukuoo, amɛwoɔ yibii oya waa (afii 3-4) ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ. Kokoo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii (afii 6-8) ni amɛdaraa waa. shi eyɛ wala be kakadaŋŋ Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my young coconut trees while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, you can plant food crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between young coconut trees during their first 3 to 4 years. Because young trees are small and widely spaced, intercropping maximizes your land and provides food and income before the coconuts start producing.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa. ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli ejaakɛ tsei bibii lɛ daraaa ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni eji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do coconut trees grow so well near the ocean beaches in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔnaa ŋshɔnaa hei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Coconut trees thrive near beaches because they love loose, sandy soil that drains water easily, along with full sun and high atmospheric humidity. Their roots are also specially adapted to withstand salty soil and coastal conditions.
ga: Kokoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔnaa hei ejaakɛ amɛsumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ oya. Hulu la babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ hu yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ kɛ ŋshɔnaa shihilɛi anɔ.

english: What kind of manure or fertilizer should I give my coconut tree to help it yield more nuts?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ maha mi ŋmei tso lɛ koni eye ebua lɛ ni ená ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Coconut trees require plenty of potassium and nitrogen to make nuts. Applying well-rotted animal manure, compost, or potassium-rich fertilizers around the soil underneath the tree canopy helps the tree produce more flowers and larger fruits.
ga: Kokoo tsei biɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen babaoo koni amɛnyɛ amɛfee amɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔii wuji kɛ aduawai.

english: Why are my small green coconuts falling off the tree before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young coconuts usually drop early due to extreme dry weather, sudden changes in water supply, or a lack of soil nutrients like potassium. Mulching the base of the tree to keep moisture in the soil helps reduce early fruit drop.
ga: Kokoo bibii lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu jɛɛhe lɛ tsakemɔ trukaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium. Tsei lɛ ashishi ni akɛhaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ baa shi.

english: Should I cut off the hanging brown leaves from my coconut tree or leave them alone?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɛɔ yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ loo mashi amɛ?

english: You should trim off completely dry, dead brown leaves so that pests and rodents do not hide in them. However, leave any leaf that is still green, as it is actively feeding energy to the tree and supporting the developing nuts.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, bɔni afee ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii akatee jɛmɛ lɛ, shi baai lɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ lolo. Enɛ ji akɛ, baai lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: How do I help my young coconut trees survive the long, dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ harmattan be kakadaŋŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Young coconut trees need extra water during Harmattan because the dry winds pull moisture out of the leaves. Piling dry grass or cocoa husks around the base of the tree creates a mulch layer that traps soil moisture and cools the roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ biɔ nu kroko yɛ harmattan beaŋ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my coconut trees turning yellow and dying off one by one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi komekomei lɛ?

english: In Ghana, rapid yellowing and dying of coconut leaves is often a sign of Cape St. Paul Wilt Disease, a serious condition spread by tiny insects. It can also be caused by poor soil nutrients, so it is important to inspect the leaves for insect pests and report widespread yellowing to your local extension officer.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baa ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya ni egboɔ lɛ ji Cape St. Paul Wilt, ni ji hela ko ni naa wa ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Sũ mli niyenii kpakpai hu baanyɛ ekɛba. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ baai lɛ amli kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli, ni abɔ ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ he amaniɛ aha maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii ahe nitsulɔi lɛ.

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and moisten the soil deeply. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a long dry stretch follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni amɛgbi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I space out my cassava cuttings instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ abɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops need room to spread their roots and catch sunlight. Proper spacing prevents cassava plants from competing for water and nutrients, allowing their underground tubers to grow much bigger.
ga: He ko he miihia ni dumɔwui lɛ agbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baatsi ŋmei tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same farm plot alongside my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial. Legumes pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which acts as natural food to help your maize grow healthier.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa o-corn lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the trees before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads in damp, overly shaded conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunshine in helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and refusing to expand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves. Keeping weeds away from the farm beds helps prevent these insects from multiplying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli saatsoi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating holes into the leaves of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which target the tender leaves of maize. Catching them early and applying recommended treatments into the center fold of the leaves will save the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Kɛji akɛ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but drop them without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi eshiɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the soil gets too dry or when temperatures are extremely high. Watering your plants consistently during hot periods helps them hold onto their flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Nu ni oooha otsei lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it better to leave dead leaves on top of my soil instead of burning them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni aaashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Dead leaves rot over time to build rich, fertile soil while keeping the ground cool and moist. Burning destroys this natural plant food and leaves your soil exposed to hot dry winds.
ga: Baai ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii, ni baa nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Shãa fiteɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ. ni oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ he

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up so fast during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The Harmattan wind brings dry air that draws water out of broad plantain leaves faster than roots can drink it up. Placing thick layers of dried grass around the base helps hold moisture in the ground.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni egbi ni mli tse ni akɛaawo shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting quickly when I keep them inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams need cool, airy places off the bare floor to stay fresh. Warm rooms trap heat and moisture, while an open-air raised storage barn keeps air moving around the yams to stop decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ koni ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsu ni mli edɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsũ ko ni agbele naa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ he. Atomɔ ni ŋɔɔ koni ekpa fitemɔ

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense heat and lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. They require shade trees or plantains nearby to block direct sunlight until their branches grow strong enough to withstand the heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛshwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha hulu la lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anaa kɛyashi tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Why are some of the tiny pods on my cocoa tree turning black and shriveling before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi dani amɛdara.

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the tree realizes it does not have enough water or soil nutrients to feed all the pods at once. It can also be caused by black pod disease, which spreads quickly in wet conditions if pods stay damp too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘cherelle wilt’ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa, ni baa kɛji tso lɛ yɔse akɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ aye abua eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ shikome. Ekolɛ black pod hela hu kɛbaa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ hi shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: Why do my harvested cocoa pods start rotting if I keep them piled up on the farm before carrying them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji mito amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ tee lɛ?

english: Even after being picked, fresh pods are alive and continue to generate internal heat and moisture. When piled on damp ground, this creates a warm environment that invites fungi and mold to attack and spoil the beans inside before they reach the factory.
ga: Beni abua naa po lɛ, ŋmeii heei lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kpo yɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo ŋtayaa ko mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ ni fɔ̃ɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei nine koni amɛtutua kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ dani amɛyashɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree make the remaining pods grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: When a tree has too many useless or shaded branches, it wastes its food and water on keeping those leaves alive. Pruning removes unwanted branches so the tree can send all its energy directly into growing larger, healthier pods.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji ni he ehiaaa loo eyɛ hulutsoo babaoo Efiteɔ niyenii kɛ nu koni ekɛha nakai baai lɛ ahi wala mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni ataooo lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen from one flower to another. If there are no midges around, or if the tree experiences sudden dry weather stress, the flowers drop without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛji mɔ ko bɛ he loo tso lɛ naa haomɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli. Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight over the same water and fertilizer in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. This competition causes the plants to grow thin and weak with lower overall yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ daa ni yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered the soil earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra moŋ?

english: During the hottest hours of the day, hot air pulls water out of leaves faster than roots can drink it up. The plant temporarily wilts its leaves to reduce its surface area and conserve moisture until the temperature cools down.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei lɛ baagbii yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do capsids attack my cocoa farm more heavily right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ capsids lɛ tutuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainfall causes cocoa trees to produce fresh, soft green shoots. Capsids thrive in high humidity and love to feed on these tender new shoots to suck their sap.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ woɔ tsei eŋɔli heei ni kpɛɔ. Capsids lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmeii heei. koni ekɛnu mliki

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa tree changing color to red and yellow patterns instead of solid green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ etsuru kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Discolored leaf patterns are often a sign of Swollen Shoot Virus disease, which damages the food transport system inside the tree, preventing leaves from getting the chlorophyll they need to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa lɛ su ni etsake lɛ ji bud swollen virus hela lɛ he okadi. ni fiteɔ niyenii ni akɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná klorofil ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is too hard for my cocoa roots to grow deep?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni kookoo shishifãi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If rain water pools on top of the soil for a long time without soaking in, or if your trees easily fall over during strong wind, the soil is too hard and compact for deep root growth.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni eŋɔɔɔ, Aloo kɛji tsei gbee shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow from the tip downward in a V-shape, it means the crop lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is essential for green leaves and growth; applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore color and boost crop yield.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi kɛbatsɔ V su Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ amɛdalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by severe heat stress. Protecting young plants from insects and maintaining consistent soil moisture helps keep leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stem cutting should face upward when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised buds or nodes along the stem. The buds should point upward toward the sky, as leaves will sprout out from these buds in the direction they face.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. awó nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi Esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli kɛyaa he ni ekwɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ dani ewoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, drought, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring regular watering during hot spells and avoiding over-fertilization keeps the flowers attached so fruit can develop.
