ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni afɔse nu be fɛɛ be yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight and dry winds. Plantain trees or forest shade trees act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity young cocoa needs until its leaves canopy over.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable roots rot after heavy rain stays on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits on the field for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil, causing the roots to drown, turn soft, and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why should I stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves up on stakes exposes them to maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. Leaves on the ground get shaded by weeds and are easily infected by soil diseases, leading to smaller tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee tso ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛha sweet potato tso lɛ niyenii. Jwɛi ewo baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe shade. ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ yeɔ mɔ oya Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why is it better to plant sword suckers instead of broad-leafed suckers for plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu klante tsei yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ kɛha plantains lɛ?

english: Sword suckers have narrow, spear-like leaves and a strong bulb with plenty of stored food energy to establish fast roots. Broad-leafed suckers spend their energy growing leaves too early and produce weaker plants.
ga: Sword suckers lɛ yɛ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ bulbs ni mli wa ni niyenii hewalɛ babaoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni yaa oya. Broadleaf suckers kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas before maize make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plant breaks down, that trapped nitrogen feeds the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Beni tsina tso lɛ gbee shi lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ bafeɔ niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my garden egg plants flower heavily but fail to produce any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Garden egg flowers need insects like bees to carry pollen from flower to flower. If bees are scarce or heavy rains wash pollen away during flowering, the flowers remain unpollinated and fall off without making fruit.
ga: Egg fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii faaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight and intense heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that shields the delicate leaves and helps the soil stay moist during the hot months.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my maize leaves and brown dirt inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ amli

english: This destruction is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the growing shoots of maize plants. Applying recommended organic sprays like neem extracts or approved pesticides directly into the center leaf whorl early in the morning will effectively control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them in heavy or poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy and firm.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Cassava shishifãi ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upward and refusing to produce big fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛwooo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme water stress. Managing whiteflies with insecticidal soaps and keeping your watering consistent prevents the leaves from curling and encourages healthy fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ tsu whiteflies lɛ ahe nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ naa ni ewo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose their leaves to sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to produce large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ adebɔɔ mli hulu la lɛ he. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my newly planted maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo ŋmãa ni adu ehee lɛ mli ŋmãa?

english: Maize needs nutrients at two main stages: a first small application of NPK fertilizer about 2 weeks after germination when the roots form, and a second top-dressing of nitrogen fertilizer 4 to 6 weeks later when the stalks grow rapidly.
ga: Abɛi he miihia niyenii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: shishijee NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fioo aaafee otsii 2 sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ beni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ; kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ni ji enyɔ yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when strong winds and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when too many shoots (suckers) grow around the main trunk, weakening its root base. Removing extra suckers and keeping only 2 or 3 per mat, along with piling soil high around the base, gives the main tree a stable anchor.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle amɛhe. too too main trunk Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ toɔ mat kome nɔ, kɛ sũ ni akɛtoɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ma shi shiŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high temperature stress, irregular watering, or soil lacking essential nutrients like phosphorus. Providing reliable watering and adding well-rotted manure helps the flowers stay on the plant to form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi koni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores natural nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How do I know the right day to sow my seeds when the rain season starts late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbi ni sa ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three consecutive heavy rains that thoroughly wet the soil deep down before planting. Sowing after just one light shower causes seeds to germinate and then dry up if rain pauses for several days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ dani oduɔ nii. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce big bushes above ground but very small roots inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of expanding its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: High heat, lack of water, or insufficient soil nutrients cause stress, forcing the pepper plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛkafite hewalɛ.

english: Why did my crop leaves dry up and turn brown right after I applied fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ trukaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer too close to the plant stems or applying too much burns the roots by pulling moisture out of them, causing the leaves to dry up.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ loo okɛwo mli babaoo lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ni no baaha baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why are there holes in the leaves of my young maize and small caterpillars hidden in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest that eats the growing core of maize plants and needs early control to prevent crop damage.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ni ehe miihia ni akudɔ lɛ mra. Koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli.

english: Why do the roots of my vegetables have small swollen lumps on them when I pull them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii ni efuu lɛ? Be ni mijieɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen lumps on roots are usually caused by microscopic worms in the soil called nematodes that feed on the roots and block water intake.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni baa lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand full sun; their leaves scorch easily, so they require temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them in their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Ebaai lɛ shãa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ anɔ koni ebu amɛhe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant seeds close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, preventing any of them from growing strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli koni dumɔwui akakwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do seeds rot in the ground without sprouting after I plant them in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to sprout; if the soil stays waterlogged and flooded, the seeds suffocate and rot before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ sũ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo ni nu afua miiho lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Can I plant other food crops on the same land where my coconut trees are growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii krokomɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei tso lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can grow crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between rows of coconut trees, especially when the coconuts are young. This helps you harvest food and make income from the land while waiting for the coconuts to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ. Titri lɛ, beni ŋmei lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ni onáa shika kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Is it better for me to farm only one crop or mix different crops on my land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu mli yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Mixing crops is safer because if bad weather or pests destroy one crop, the other crops can still survive and provide you with income and food for your family.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko hiɛ lɛ, ekrokomɛi baanyɛ ahi shi lolo ni amɛha oweku lɛ aná shika kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops and soil get washed away whenever heavy rain falls on my hillside farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater flows quickly down slopes, washing topsoil and seeds away. Planting your crops in rows across the slope (contour planting) or building small soil ridges stops the water from rushing down and protects your farm.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shi oya. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ (tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni etse amɛhe nɔ) loo shikpɔŋ bibii ni afee lɛ Ebaatsi nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi lɛ naa ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: What is the best way to prepare sloping land on a mountain before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa gɔŋji lɛ anɔ dani aduɔ dumɔwui?

english: Instead of clearing all trees and bushes, leave some deep-rooted plants to hold the soil together. You should also dig flat steps or barriers across the hill to keep rain and plant nutrients in the soil.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie tsei kɛ tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ. Shi tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ koni amɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ otsa atswerei loo gbɛtsii nii yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nugbɔ akanɛ ni odu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young coconuts fall off my tree before they grow big and ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Coconut trees drop young nuts when they lack enough water during dry weather, when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium, or when sap-sucking insects attack the flowers.
ga: Kokoo tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Beni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo be mli ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔii.

english: How far apart should I plant coconut seedlings when starting a new farm?
ga: Beni ajeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Coconut seedlings should be planted about 7 to 8 meters apart. Giving them enough space prevents their leaves from shading each other and ensures each tree gets enough soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ aaafee mitai 7 kɛyashi 8 kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ha lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How many years will I wait for my coconut trees to start producing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni ŋmei tso lɛ abɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Improved dwarf coconut varieties can start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall coconut trees usually take about 6 to 8 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Kokooi bibii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant crops in straight lines instead of scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop equal space and sunlight to grow strong, and it makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ náa hegbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do crop leaves turn yellow and rot when planted near low area junctions where water collects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: When roots sit in standing water for too long, they drown because they cannot get oxygen. Digging small drainage trenches helps excess water flow away so roots remain healthy.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shifãi lɛ baagboi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nu tsɔne bibioo ko ni aaatsɔ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: How can I keep my soil healthy without spending a lot of money on chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ shika babaoo akawo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Planting beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas adds natural nitrogen back into the soil, and leaving old plant leaves on the ground to rot forms mulch that feeds future crops naturally.
ga: Beans, peanuts, loo cowpeas ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. kɛ tsei ahe baai momoi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛgboi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct heat and light. Without shade trees or fast-growing food crops like plantain to cover them, intense sun causes leaves to lose water faster than roots can absorb it, causing wilting and death.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya bɛ ni baaha nɔ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ gbele aba.

english: Cocoa grows best in deep, fertile soil that drains water easily while keeping some moisture. If water pools on top of your land for days after heavy rain, the roots will rot, showing the land needs drainage before planting.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ nu fioo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu tee nɔ ehi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi, ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni nu atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu nii.

english: How many years will it take for my new cocoa farm to start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-kokoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ baaje pods feemɔ shishi?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting in the field, whereas older traditional varieties typically take 4 to 5 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated by tiny insects like midges to become pods. Flowers drop naturally if they are not pollinated, or if the tree faces stress from dry weather, poor nutrients, or insect attack.
ga: Esa akɛ koolooi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ awooo amɛ pollin. aloo kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, damp weather. High humidity, excess shade, and dense weeds keep moisture on the pods and accelerate the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine. Ni jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot branches from the main trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted side shoots (chupons) helps air and sunlight move freely through the tree canopy. It prevents disease growth and allows the tree to focus its energy on growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ tsei ni ataooo (chupons) lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes plant weeds to grow directly out of the branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni haa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kokoo niji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasite spread by birds. It grows into the bark of cocoa branches to steal water and nutrients, which weakens the host tree and reduces pod production.
ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji mistletoe. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni okpoi gbɛɔ eshwaa Edaa ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kookoo niji anɔ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my mature cocoa trees turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running out of essential nutrients like nitrogen or potassium. As trees yield fruit year after year, they deplete soil nutrients unless compost or fertilizers are added.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Beni tsei lɛ woɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is ready to be plucked from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color clearly. Pods that start green turn bright yellow when mature, while pods that start red or purple change to an orange-yellow color.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods ni jeɔ shishi eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ etsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei.

english: Why must I cover fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo yibii heei ahe gbii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering wet beans with plantain leaves traps natural heat for fermentation. This step stops the bean from sprouting, removes bitter taste, and creates the rich chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ aba koni ekɛfee ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ, ejieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and weak even after I cleared the land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ beni ajie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are trapped in waterlogged soil. Clearing the land removes weeds, but you still need to feed the soil with compost or fertilizer and ensure water drains properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo shishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi lɛ ajie. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo. ni akwɛ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egboi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during the dry season as a natural survival trick to conserve water. The plant is not dying; it is saving its energy underground to keep expanding its cassava roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni akɛbu nu he. Tsei lɛ gbooo, ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛgbala ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin but produce very small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to fight for light instead of using energy to grow thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛye la he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to nourish a good crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai anɔ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well, crumbles easily in your hands, and contains living creatures like earthworms. These earthworms break down organic matter into food that plant roots can easily drink in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Efoɔ yɛ nine mli oya Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ. Nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbálaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli amɛfeɔ niyenii ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu mlɛo.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the underside of young leaves. They suck out the plant's sap, which damages the leaf structure and stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and soft when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot. Heavy rains can disrupt how the plant takes up calcium from the soil, causing the tissue at the bottom of the fruit to breakdown and rot as it grows.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite bɔ ni tsei gbalaa calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa tree to turn black and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. It destroys the pod from the outside in, which is why pruning tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Efiteɔ pod lɛ kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛyaa mli.Yɛ ​​yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted yam or maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted to local soil and weather over many years. They are tough and quickly absorb water and food before your farm crops get a chance, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Amɛhe wa ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya dani oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Why shouldn't I save and replant the seeds harvested from my hybrid maize crop for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ mi-hybrid corn lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed to produce high yield only in their first generation. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the second-generation crops will grow unevenly and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsɔɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow plenty of green leaves but very few beans when planted at the wrong time of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baa eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ adu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas react to daylight hours and rain conditions. If planted when the rainfall is too heavy or the days are too long, the plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves rather than producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Cowpea tsuɔ nii yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ shihilɛi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo gbii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ baai eŋɔli. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture, but they usually recover in the cooler evening once water loss slows down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli beni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes drastically. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to drop its flowers because it cannot successfully produce seeds.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen fertilizer. Nitrogen moves easily inside the plant, so when nutrients are low, the plant steals nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Nitrogen lɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ tsei amli oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii faaa Tsei lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips, or by a viral infection spread by insects. These pests suck sap from leaves, causing them to grow twisted and curled.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ mites loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller corn cobs, reducing your total harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnuts on my farm help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, this stored nitrogen feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, akɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce lots of thick green leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ miiwo baai ŋmɔji ni mli tse babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cassava to put all its energy into growing stem and leaves instead of roots. Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients, especially potassium, to swell its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe eshishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia Cassava. titri lɛ potassium ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli

english: Why do crops grown inside a greenhouse structure grow faster than crops in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses shield crops from harsh weather, high winds, and destructive insects while keeping humidity and heat at ideal levels. This allows the plant to focus all its energy on fast growth rather than surviving pest attacks.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kɛ koolooi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ koni hulutsoo kɛ dɔlɛ ahi shi yɛ he ni sa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa bɔ ni edaa oya lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeehi wala mli kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make food efficiently. Leaves trailing on the ground get shaded by weeds, trapped in humid soil air, and exposed to fungal diseases that rot the leaves and shrink tubers.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Jwɛi ewo baai ni egbee shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ni anáa.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during Harmattan as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation. Providing shade trees helps protect young cocoa from drying winds and direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ Harmattan beaŋ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛba nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Shading yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cocoa tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize crops turn yellow and stay small even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize plants turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is their main food for leafy growth. Water alone is not enough; the soil foundation needs organic matter like manure or nitrogen fertilizer to nourish the crop.
ga: Abɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ daa Nu pɛ faaa. Shishitoo shikpɔŋ lɛ biɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young tomato plants with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tomato tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which covers the soil like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground, prevents the hot sun from scorching the soil, and keeps the plant roots cool so the crop can continue growing.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ blanket. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together, won't I get more cassava tubers from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Ani maná ŋmei shishifãi babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving cassava enough space allows the roots room to expand into large, healthy tubers instead of many small, thin ones.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe. Kɛ́ oha o-cassava lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifã tsu lɛ mli alɛɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo najiaŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the tall shade trees from the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Ajie fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun and hot winds. Keeping or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides the living cover and moisture the trees need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ kookoo bibii ni abuɔ he loo amɛkwɛɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ wala ato ni eha tso lɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I buy seed packages from government programs like Planting for Food and Jobs instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui akuu kɛjɛ nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo ko tamɔ Dumɔ kɛha Niyenii kɛ Nitsumɔi amli? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii.

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to grow faster, yield more crop, and resist local diseases. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their vigor over time, leading to lower yields and weaker crop growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. Ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni tsei lɛ hu adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my land before planting maize make the maize grow so much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil. When you plant maize in that same field next, the maize feeds on this stored nitrogen and grows stronger.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ oya nɔ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baaye nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ ni ebaada waa.

english: How do weeds in my field cause my pepper plants to drop their flowers before fruiting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal key nutrients and water away from your pepper plants. When the pepper plant experiences this sudden stress and hunger, it drops its flowers to save energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛ hɔmɔ trukaa lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my young maize crops right after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay their eggs on tender green maize shoots that emerge right after early rains. The newly hatched caterpillars feed heavily on the soft center leaves of the growing plant, which can kill the crop if left untreated.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ kpo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Kplukai ni efɔ ehee lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ waa. Enɛ baanyɛ agbe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my tomato plant growing very tall with thick green leaves, but hardly producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani tomato ko kwraa bɛ?

english: When a plant gets too much nitrogen or grows excess side branches, it puts all its energy into leaves instead of flowers. Trimming minor side shoots helps direct the plant's food toward growing big, healthy tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo eyɛ niji babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ gbɛ kɛya tomatoi wuji ni mli wa ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto my soil when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil creates a concentrated salt layer that can burn and damage root tissues instead of helping the crop grow.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmei ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ amli fãji lɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua tsei ni amɛdara lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly in an open field under full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside them acts like a canopy, protecting the cocoa from intense heat until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Ebaafee enii tamɔ ŋwɛitsu. Ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruits during the dry hot heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and water is low, the tomato plant drops its flowers to protect itself from dying. Regular watering at the base early in the morning keeps the soil moist and saves the flowers.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu lɛ hu faaa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ́ afɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ nu daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafiteɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and pale green before the ears are even fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse dani toi lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which gives plants their rich green color. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the leaves so the plant can feed the developing corn.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tso lɛ anyɛ aye abua ŋmãa ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans before planting my maize on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛdu ŋmei loo ŋmei dani amɛdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays behind and acts as natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ baahi shi ni ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same crop family and suffer from the same soil diseases. Planting them continuously in the same soil allows pest populations and diseases to build up and ruin your fresh crops.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aya nɔ akwɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aya hiɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛbua onibii heei ni okɛwo mli lɛ anaa ni amɛfite.

english: Why do I get smaller cassava roots when I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots compete fiercely for the same soil food and moisture. Spacing cassava cuttings properly gives each root enough room and nutrients to swell into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. He ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shishifã fɛɛ shishifã náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmei agbo ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that can scorch germinating seeds in the soil. Waiting for the rains to become regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for young roots to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does removing small extra branches from my pepper plants make them produce more peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mijie niji fioo komɛi kɛjɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa amɛwoɔ pepper babaoo lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary weak branches stops the plant from wasting water and nutrients on useless leaves, directing all its food energy into growing bigger and healthier fruit.
ga: Niji bibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haaa tso lɛ afite nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ daa ni etsɔɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop harvest even when they are not touching my plants?
ga: Te jwɛi feɔ tɛŋŋ ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtaaa mitsei lɛ ahe moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots underground that steal water and nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds keeps all the soil food available exclusively for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ehe koni okɛtsu nii koni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ waa pɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive water sitting in flat soil chokes the root tubers by blocking air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away so roots can breathe.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ta shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: How do I know when the soil has received enough rain for me to start planting my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Wait until rain soaks the soil about hand-deep (around 10 to 15 centimeters). Planting in soil that is only wet on top can cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry weather returns for a few days.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee onineshi (aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15). Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi pɛ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba gbii fioo krokomɛi.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to grow strong and yield larger crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer, chicken manure, or well-rotted compost helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tsina ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers and curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ shi ni ekɛ ebaa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and dropping flowers are natural stress responses to conserve water during extreme heat and dry conditions. Providing shade or watering early in the morning helps the plant keep its blossoms and set fruit.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hetoo kɛha nɔnyɛɛ koni akɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha tso lɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers encourage us to plant plantain trees alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide broad leaf canopy protection, acting like living umbrellas that supply shade and keep the soil moist while cocoa roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛbuɔ baa ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Can I use animal manure from my livestock field to improve my farm soil instead of buying commercial fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mikooloi lɛ amli ŋmeii atsu nii koni mikɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ moŋ fe ni mahe jarayeli ŋmeii?

english: Yes, animal manure is very good for soil because it adds essential nutrients and improves the soil's ability to retain water. It should be composted or dried first so it does not heat up and burn plant roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei hi waa kɛha sũ lɛ ejaakɛ ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa fataa he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ afee lɛ marinade loo agbi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni edɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akashã.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow and spread much faster than my cassava plants after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, so they absorb available water and soil food much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives young cassava plants the room and nutrients they need to get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ aná he kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: What is making small holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I protect them without expensive chemicals?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by hungry caterpillars or beetles that lay eggs on the crop. Spraying leaves with a mild mixture of boiled neem tree leaves and water can act as a natural pest deterrent.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baai ni ahoo kɛ nu fioo ko ni akɛfutu baa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and turn moldy inside storage bags even when it looks dry on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ efite ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nitoo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi moŋ

english: Grains often retain hidden moisture inside the core even if the outside feels dry. Drying grains thoroughly on a clean tarp under direct sunlight until they crack cleanly between your teeth prevents fungal mold and insects from ruining stored food.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi po. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmaa lɛ gĩ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ kɛyashi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ onyanyɔji ateŋ lɛ mli baatse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi akafite niyenii ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbo ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that burn under direct, full sunlight. Big trees or temporary shade plants like plantains act as umbrellas, blocking harsh sun rays and keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yam vines produce food through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and stay away from soil-borne diseases, which helps the tuber grow much bigger under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ ahe Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their healthy green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ehee ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the specific nutrients that maize needs from the soil. It also lets pests and diseases that feed on maize build up in the soil, making future harvests weaker each year.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli nikpamɔi lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: Why do some of the cassava sticks I cut and push into the ground fail to grow leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni mifoɔ ni mikɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi ehiɛɛɛ baai lɛ?

english: Cassava stems will not sprout if they are planted upside down, if the stem cutting is too dry or old, or if the soil lacks enough moisture when planting. The buds on the stem cutting must point upward toward the sky.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ŋwɛi. Niji ni afoɔ lɛ egbi loo egbɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa beni aduɔ lɛ Esa akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi.

english: Why should I cut away extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: If too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only the strong stems, resulting in larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ahi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ feɔ agboi ni amɛtsiii.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn plants look like they have holes eaten out of them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛye bu nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This destruction is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These insects hide inside the middle fold (whorl) of the corn plant during the day and chew up the tender leaves as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei (ring) lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni ekɛ baai bibii shwieɔ shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce tiny yields even when rain falls heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from your crop's roots. When weeds surround your crop, your main plant gets starved of nutrients despite good rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni jwɛi ebɔle onibii ahe lɛ Otsei titrii lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji nugbɔ kpakpa nɛ po.

english: Extreme heat or irregular watering stresses tomato plants. When the plant feels too hot or thirsty, it drops its flowers to save energy rather than spending resources to grow fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ edɔ tsɔ loo kumai miiye lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni ekɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: How do I know the rain is steady enough to start planting my seeds at the beginning of the farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the land receives a few deep, consistent rains that wet the soil thoroughly beneath the surface. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa daa, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwu lɛ akwɛ̃ ni egbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: What does an extension officer mean when they say my crop is in the vegetative stage?
ga: Mɛni extension officials lɛ tsɔɔ kɛ amɛkɛɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ?

english: The vegetative stage is the early period when your crop focuses entirely on growing strong roots, stems, and green leaves before it starts producing flowers or fruits. Taking good care of your crop during this stage gives it the strength needed to produce a heavy harvest later.
ga: Dalɛ be lɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ. He ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ ji shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nakai baai eŋɔlii lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Dani ebaaje shishi ewo fɔfɔi loo ewo yibii Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpa nii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is my crop growing lots of leaves right now instead of producing fruits or cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo bianɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo aduawai loo kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Your plant is currently in its vegetative growth phase, where it spends all its energy building a strong body of leaves and branches to catch sunlight. Once the plant becomes fully established and mature, it will naturally shift its energy toward producing fruits.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ, otso lɛ eshɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Amɛ kɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai kɛ niji ni mli wa koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Beni tsei lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛdara. Ebaatsake hewalɛ kɛya aduawai afeemɔ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young crops seem to grow very slowly during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In the early weeks, young crops spend most of their energy developing a hidden root network underground rather than growing tall above ground. Once these roots are firmly established to absorb water and nutrients, the leaves and stems will start growing much faster.
ga: Yɛ shishijee otsii lɛ amli lɛ, tsei bibii kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e daa kɛ yaa zugba a nɔ. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii, Baai lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baabɔi dalɛ oya kwraa.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my field and inspect my plant stand regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli daa ni makwɛ tsei ni damɔ shi lɛ?

english: Regularly checking your stand allows you to monitor how well your young plants are surviving and growing. It helps you quickly spot empty gaps where seeds failed, identify disease early, and make sure plants have enough room without crowding each other.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ odaamɔhe lɛ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni okwɛ bɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa. Ehaa onaa he ni dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ helai mra Ni okwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkafee amɛhe nɔ ko.

english: How can I tell if my crops are planted too close together in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ adu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If crops are planted too close, they will grow very tall, thin, and weak as they fight each other for sunlight, and their leaves may turn yellow from competing for soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough light, air, and food to thrive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ daraa waa, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa be mli ni amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Ni baai lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: What should I do if some of my planted seeds fail to come up and leave empty spots in the row?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekomɛi edaaa ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should fill those empty spots by replanting fresh seeds or transplanting young seedlings into the gaps as early as possible. This ensures you do not waste land space and prevents weeds from taking over the empty soil.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nakai hei ni etse lɛ awo mli kɛtsɔ dumɔwui heei ni ooodu loo tsei bibii ni ooodu yɛ hei ni etse lɛ amli oya bɔ ni ooonyɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa ofite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small new shoots sprouting around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei bibii No hewɔ lɛ eda kɛbɔle he fɛɛ. Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers or offspring, which the main plant naturally produces to multiply itself. Managing these suckers by leaving only the strongest one or two ensures the mother plant keeps enough energy to produce large fruit bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers loo suckers. ni tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ feɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛfɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii, ni ashiɔ eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ, haa tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ toɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai akui wuji.

english: Should I cut off extra small shoots that grow at the base of my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Ani ajieɔ shweremɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, removing extra shoots is helpful because too many young shoots will steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Pruning away weaker shoots allows the main stem to grow thicker and produce a bigger yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ejaakɛ tsei bibii babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I choose which young shoot to keep at the base of my plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii bibii ni mikɛbaato mitso lɛ shishi kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Look for a shoot that has a thick base, deep green leaves, stands upright, and shows no signs of disease or pest damage. Keeping the healthiest and strongest shoot ensures it will successfully replace the old plant after harvest.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni shishigbɛi lɛ mli tse. Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdamɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ hela loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe okadi ko kwraa. Kɛ́ ahã ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni aaanyɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa tso momo lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ ni yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What signs should I look for to know if my young crops are developing healthily?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ makwɛ koni mana kɛji mitsei bibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy young crops will have firm stems, bright green leaves free of spots or holes, and new leaves opening up regularly. If the leaves look dark green and the stem is sturdy, it means your crop is absorbing water and fertilizer properly.
ga: Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni ŋmɔlɔ loo bu ko bɛ he. ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ daa Kɛji baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe wa Etsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ miihe nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ loo shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point the cassava stem when I stick it into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaatsɔɔ he ko?

english: Yes, you should plant cassava cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the plant wastes too much energy trying to turn its shoots upward, resulting in weak roots and lower yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ odu yucca tsei niji ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: My cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but why do most of them drop off without becoming pods?
ga: Mikoo tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛniji bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers, but heavy dropping happens when trees suffer from drought, lack of soil nutrients, or poor insect pollination. Proper pruning and keeping shade trees helps the cocoa retain more pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Shi fɔfɔi ni tsii baa kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ehiii Tso lɛ he tsemɔ ni sa kɛ tso lɛ ni aaaha ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi babaoo mli.

english: Why do I have to construct high soil mounds to plant yam instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni akɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand deep underground easily. Raised mounds loosen the soil, protect tubers from rot caused by standing rainwater, and make harvesting much easier.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ oya. Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo. Ebuɔ ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ ni nugbɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and becoming small and crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips transmitting a virus to the plant. Spraying with neem oil or recommended organic treatments early on helps control the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni kɛ helai baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ mɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell of hot weather. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but then dry up and die in the hot soil before the main rainy season fully arrives.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba kwraa.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix nitrogen from the air back into the dirt, naturally restoring soil fertility for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker should I dig up to start a new farm—the short one with narrow leaves or the tall one with broad leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui sucker esa akɛ mafo koni maje ŋmɔ hee shishi? Eko kuku, ni mli etse loo eko ni kɛlɛ, ni baa lɛ mli kwɔ?

english: You should choose the short maiden suckers with narrow, spear-like leaves. They store more energy in their roots and establish faster than tall, broad-leaf suckers, which dry out easily when transplanted.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tsei bibii kukuji ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Amɛtoɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ oya fe ŋmeii ni kwɔlɔ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni kɛ́ ajie amɛ awo he kroko lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Why does waiting until weeds grow tall before clearing them reduce my crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mimɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ fa babaoo dani ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Tall weeds steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer away from your crops during their most critical early growth stage. Clearing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni enáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do small beetles eat up my harvested dry maize inside the storage room after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni akpa yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like maize weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the grain while it is still in the field. Drying the maize well and using airtight storage bags (like PICS bags) starves the insects of oxygen and protects your grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmãa mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ vacuum storage bags (tamɔ PICS bags) tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ ana kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni baabu o-grain lɛ he.

english: Why must I put stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to produce energy. It also keeps leaves off the damp soil, which prevents fungal diseases and helps the plant produce much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji babaoo.
