english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to move available nutrients up to the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ shi, baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛjie niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge bushy leaves above ground but end up with very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen from soil or heavy manure, it puts all its energy into growing thick stems and leaves instead of storing starch in the underground tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei náa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmei mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly like small cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by viruses spread by whiteflies. The damaged leaf tissue distorts as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Baa lɛ mli fãji ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before any tomatoes start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or too much nitrogen. The plant drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off extra shoots or suckers growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around a plantain stem, they steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main trunk. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, leading to larger and heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain tso lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: Why is it bad to put chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing it right against the stem or root base burns the plant tissues, which can stunt or kill the crop instead of helping it grow.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛma tso lɛ shishitoo loo shishitoo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ashã. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua tsei ni amɛdara lɛ

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make the soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop season ends, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nakai nitrogen ni aŋã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because plants take up water before heat sets in, and the leaves dry quickly in the sun, which stops damp-loving fungi from growing.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa, ni kɛ́ hulu la shɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaagbi oya. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akpa dalɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cocoa trees about 10 feet apart gives each plant enough space to get air, sunlight, and nutrients, which helps the crop thrive and produce more pods.
ga: Cacao tsei ni aduɔ aaafee ninetalɔi 10 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená kɔɔyɔɔ, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When planted too close, cocoa trees compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which weakens the plants and lowers your harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu Cocoa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Will planting fewer cocoa trees with wider spacing give me more cocoa pods than crowding them?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei fioo ni aduɔ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii babaoo aba fe kookoo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yes, wider spacing allows each individual tree to grow a larger canopy and stronger roots, producing far more healthy pods than crowded, weak trees would.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ŋwɛi ŋta ni da kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Ewoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa fe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: How does leaving enough space around a young cocoa seedling help it grow?
ga: He ni bɛ nɔ ko ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te cacao tsei bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni edaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Adequate space lets the seedling spread its roots underground without competing with nearby crops, allowing it to take in all the fertilizer and water it needs.
ga: He ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hia amɛ.

english: Why does leaving empty space between my crop rows help keep my trees healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi gbɛ yɛ mi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing allows air to flow freely between the trees, which dries wet leaves quickly and reduces fungal diseases like black pod rot.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ aba shi

english: Why are my crowded cocoa branches failing to produce flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo niji ni ebɔle mihe waa lɛ ewooo fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When trees are overcrowded, their leaves overlap and block sunlight, causing the tree to spend all its energy reaching upward for light instead of making flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshɛɔ ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ la nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting enough sunlight and space to thrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiná hulu la kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Cocoa trees with good spacing and sunlight will have thick, dark green leaves and develop healthy flower cushions directly on their trunks and main branches.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la baaná baai ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji wuji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I follow the planting guidelines provided by agricultural extension officers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni anyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ eto lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Agricultural officers share tested methods that have proven to increase yields and keep crops healthy based on research and practical trial farms.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ jaa gbɛi ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni ana akɛ amɛhaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni damɔ niiamlitaomɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli kaai ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to test a new planting distance on just a small part of my farm first?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maka dumɔwui hee lɛ he jɛkɛmɔ lɛ makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko? ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ loo daabi

english: Yes, testing a recommended guideline like 10-foot spacing on a small portion lets you compare the growth and yield against your old methods before converting your entire farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, kaa wo gbɛtsɔɔmɔi tamɔ naji 10 jɛkɛmɔ yɛ hei bibii amli. Ehaa okɛ dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo toɔ ogbɛi momo lɛ ahe dani otsakeɔ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What is the general recommended distance for planting cocoa trees in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni afɔɔ he ŋaawoo akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ koni akwɛ kookoo tsei yɛ Ghana?

english: The standard recommended planting distance for cocoa in Ghana is 10 feet by 10 feet, which balances plant density with maximum yield per tree.
ga: Cocoa dumɔ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ adu yɛ Ghana lɛ ji ninetalɔi 10 x ninetalɔi 10, ni haa tsei lɛ ayibɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tso kome mli baa lɛ yeɔ egbɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stems when planting them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ato he ko beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spacing cassava cuttings about one meter apart gives their roots enough room underground to swell into large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for food and water.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why is it risky to sow my maize seeds right at the end of the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Young seedlings need continuous soil moisture to build strong roots. Planting just before a dry season leaves delicate young crops to wither and die from thirst before they mature.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu nii dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ agbi ni kumai aye amɛ dani amɛshɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: What is causing small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on tender leaves. Catching them early with recommended pest controls prevents them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ ajie ŋaawoo akɛ akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients away from your crops, effectively starving your plants and slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which plants need for healthy leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and photosynthesize properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Alternating with beans or groundnuts restores nitrogen to your soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the base of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai shwieɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture during hot days, and stops weeds from sprouting easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ oya

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden sticks next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Amɛduɔ sweet potato wain tsei

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the damp ground to absorb maximum sunlight while preventing leaf rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make food and stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and little worms hiding inside the tops of the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee tsei lɛ ayitsei amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed on the tender young leaves and growing points of maize, which weakens the plant and reduces your harvest if you do not control them early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ aba shi kɛji okudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for a long time. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do I need to place long wooden poles next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tsei lɛ akakwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for the plant. Staking the vines gets the leaves off the ground so they can capture maximum sunlight, which helps the plant grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ wein tso lɛ fĩ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when there are no bigger trees near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he ko lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates a living shelter that protects the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa anáa he ko ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and dry up while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni mikɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the plant juices and spreading diseases. Spraying the plants early to manage these pests stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips, ni nuɔ tso nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Bɔni afee ni atsu nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant them very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight over the same soil food, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed well and produce a larger harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I wait for a few good rains before sowing my seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ kpakpa? fioo dani amɛduɔ dumɔwui yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Sowing after just one light rain is risky because the dry ground can dry out quickly, killing the newly sprouted seeds. Waiting for deep soil moisture ensures the seeds have enough water to grow continuously.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Be kome pɛ ji oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hei ni egbi lɛ baagbi oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gboiɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: During the heat of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. This temporary wilting is the plant's natural defense to conserve moisture, and it will usually recover by evening once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow and rot when rainwater sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe and pull up nutrients. When water sits trapped on the field, it fills all the tiny air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nu tsɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli Nu lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings droop and look weak right after I move them from the seedbed to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused by disturbing delicate roots and exposing them to direct heat. You can prevent this by transplanting in the late afternoon or on a cloudy day, and watering them immediately so they adjust smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni agbalaa amɛnaa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni akɛwoɔ dɔlɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookɛwo mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ nɔ. aloo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni etsake jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide quick, broad-leaf umbrella shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya haa oya, baa ni mli kwɔ shade. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but the cassava tubers under the ground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen, often from over-fertilizing. Nitrogen encourages leafy growth above the ground rather than storing energy into building large, starchy tubers below.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nitrogen haa baa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa moŋ fe ni eeekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni yɔɔ starch yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni amɛjeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-shape indicate a nitrogen deficiency. The maize plant moves available nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top, showing that the soil needs additional fertilizer or manure.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any fruit can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or sudden weather changes. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy to stay alive rather than spending nutrients on growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛdu aduawai

english: Is it good to plant maize and cowpea together on the same land, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaatswa amɛhe akaŋ yɛ niyenii he?

english: Planting maize and cowpea together is beneficial because cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize and improves your overall harvest.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ he ejaakɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsina ŋmãa lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa okpamɔ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crops as soon as they start coming up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ kɛji amɛbɔi dalɛ pɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and will steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from your young plants, slowing down their growth or starving them completely.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ebaaju hulu la ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ kɛjɛ odumɔwui lɛ ahe Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi loo ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ kwraa.

english: Why do I need to put strong wooden stakes in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ni wa awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to climb high off the ground so their leaves can catch sunlight to make food for the tuber. Leaves lying on the ground are more likely to catch diseases and rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni amɛkɛkwɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Baai ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ helai kɛ fitemɔ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops wither and die after I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Big trees provide shade and shield young, tender crops from harsh sunlight and dry winds. When all trees are cleared at once, the intense sun scorches delicate plants and dries out the topsoil too fast.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Beni ajie tsei lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the cleared trees and bush on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa tsei kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and helpful soil organisms that nourish crops. Letting cut branches rot naturally acts as compost, keeping the soil rich and moist for longer periods.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei niji ni afo lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster right after I clear shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa yɛ be mli ni mijie tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Clearing trees allows direct sunlight to reach the ground, which triggers sleeping weed seeds in the soil to germinate rapidly without competition for light.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye la he akaŋ.

english: Why does my newly cleared farm take a few years before giving me a full harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ hee ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ heɔ afii fioo komɛi dani ekpaa nibii fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared land needs time for the soil structure and nutrients to balance after being disturbed. As old roots break down over time, they slowly release stored nutrients back into the soil for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ he miihia be koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee ekome yɛ be mli ni agbala mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shishifãi momoi lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ Amɛbaajie niyenii ni ato lɛ fiofio kɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my root crops like cassava grow small and bent when I plant them in hard, freshly cleared soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ashishifãi, tamɔ yucca lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieee nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared soil is often compacted and filled with old tree roots. Cassava tubers need loose, tilled soil so their roots can easily push outward and expand into big, healthy tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei shishifãi momo eyiɔ mli obɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia cassava tsei lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre kɛya kponɔgbɛ oya ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do food crops growing right under big living trees stay small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Large trees have wide root systems that drink up most of the water and nutrients in the ground, leaving very little food and water for small crops planted close to them.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu. fioo pɛ

english: How does trimming the branches of large farm trees help my vegetable crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aniji ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Pruning lets sunlight pass through to reach lower crops so they can make their own food, while still keeping enough shade to protect the soil from drying out.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lolo ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young crops turn yellow during the hottest part of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often show that the crop is losing water faster than its roots can pull it from the soil, or that intense heat is stopping the leaves from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu lɛ miiho oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ

english: Why do tree crops like cashew or oil palm take several years before they bear their first fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ cashew nuts loo oil palms heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: Tree crops spend their first few years building strong underground roots and sturdy trunks. They must establish this deep anchor before they have enough energy to produce heavy fruit.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ yeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛnáa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Esa akɛ amɛma ŋshɔŋloo ni mli kwɔ nɛɛ dani amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do plantains grow and shoot up so much faster than cocoa planted on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ daa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya fe kookoo ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots spread fast near the surface to grab quick water and feed fast growth, while cocoa spends its early stage slowly developing deep roots to survive for decades.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu oya ni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ niyenii. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo feɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ nibii fiofio koni ená shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni ehi shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ.

english: Why do farmers tell me to plant plantains on the same land with young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli

english: Can I plant plantain suckers in the exact same hole where I just harvested cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ bu ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: It is better to choose a new spot or add compost first. Cassava pulls a lot of nutrients out of the soil, so planting plantain directly in the same hole without feeding the soil will cause slow growth and smaller fruit.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala he hee loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he klɛŋklɛŋ. Cassava jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu plantains yɛ bu kome mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ blɛoo ni ewo yibii bibii.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my plantain plants turn yellow and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: During dry spells, plantain plants lose water fast through their leaves. The plant naturally drops its older lower leaves to save water and energy for the stem and top growth until the rain returns.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Tsei shĩɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know that my plantain plant is about to bring out fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ miibawo yibii?

english: When a plantain plant reaches full growth, its top leaves grow closer together and a large purple flower bud appears from the center top of the stem, which slowly opens up into fingers of plantain.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Eŋwɛi baai lɛ baabɛŋkɛ amɛhe. Ni ŋmɔtɔ agbo ko ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio ni ebafeɔ dumɔwu ko nine.

english: Why do plantain stems feel soft and full of water when I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe yɛ blɛoo ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ́ mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are not true wood like trees. They are made of tightly overlapping leaf sheaths filled with stored water and sap, which helps the plant grow rapidly in warm weather.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ jeee tsei diɛŋtsɛ tamɔ tsei. Akɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni nu ni ato kɛ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ fee amɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall down so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; their roots spread out shallowly near the top of the soil. Because the mature bunch makes the plant heavy at the top, strong winds easily tip the plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, be mli ni ŋmeii ni eda lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo.

english: Why do plantain roots stay close to the top of the ground instead of growing deep into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots naturally stay near the soil surface to easily breathe oxygen and soak up surface rain and nutrients from decaying leaves. Placing organic mulch around the base feeds these shallow roots.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ mlɛo ni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ baai ni miifite lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ niyenii.

english: Is it good to cut away the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafolɔ tsei bibii? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he Ajie?

english: Yes, pruning extra shoots—called suckers—is necessary. If you allow too many shoots to grow at once, they steal food and sunlight from the main plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni afo tsei niji krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome lɛ, Ebaaju niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: What makes plantain fingers stay thin and light even when the main tree is tall?
ga: Mɛni haa plantain niji lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ tso titri lɛ po kɛlɛ?

english: Thin plantain fruits mean the soil lacks essential plant nutrients like potassium or the plant did not get enough water while the fruit was forming. A tall stem uses energy, but good soil food fills the fruit.
ga: Plantain aduawai ni mli tseee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ beni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Tsoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi niyenii ni jɛ sũ kpakpa mli lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba.

english: What happens to my plantain plants if rainwater collects and sits around the stem for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: When standing water stays around the base, the plantain's shallow roots drown from lack of air and begin to rot, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and the fruit bunch to fail.
ga: Akɛni nu damɔ shi ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he hewɔ lɛ, plantain lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni aduawai akui lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I stop planting new cocoa seedlings when December approaches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa kookoo dumɔwui heei adumɔ be mli ni December miibɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: December marks the beginning of the dry harmattan season in Ghana. Young seedlings planted during this time will not receive enough rainfall to establish strong roots and are likely to dry up and die.
ga: December ji be ni harmattan ni mli egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana. Tsei bibii ni adu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ naaa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. ni esumɔɔ ni egbi ni egbo.

english: What happens to my cocoa plants if I plant them too late in the year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli sɛɛ tsɔ?

english: Crops planted late miss the main rainy season. Without steady water, their growth gets stunted, and they cannot build enough strength to survive the upcoming dry season.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ. Kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ lɛ, abaatsi Dalɛ naa. ni enyɛŋ etswa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to follow a strict yearly calendar for planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔnyiɛ kalanda ni mli wa ni kɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ sɛɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: Following a natural rain calendar ensures your young trees get maximum water during early growth and experience the proper dry conditions required for pod ripening and harvesting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ he kalanda lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni odumɔwui lɛ aná nu babaoo yɛ amɛdalɛ be mli mra. ni amɛna shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni sa kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ amɛkpamɔ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa farm has reached its mature phase?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ eshɛ shweremɔ he?

english: A cocoa farm enters its mature phase when trees stop focusing mostly on branch growth and start flowering and producing pods regularly, usually around 3 to 5 years after planting.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ boteɔ dalɛ be mli beni tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛjwɛŋmɔ babaoo kɛyaa niji adalɛ nɔ lɛ. ni ebɔi fɔmɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii daa Enɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why can't cocoa trees yield fresh pods all year round without taking a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei nyɛŋ awo ŋmeii heei afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpaaa amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow a natural lifecycle linked to seasonal changes. They need a transition phase between growing, flowering, and pod development to direct energy into ripening healthy beans.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala shihilɛ ni kɛ be mli tsakemɔi yɔɔ tsakpaa. Amɛmiitao tsakemɔ be yɛ amɛdalɛ, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ ateŋ koni amɛkudɔ amɛ hewalɛ kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ.

english: How does dry weather towards the end of the year affect the behavior of my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ ená mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ ajeŋba nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Towards the end of the year, drier weather triggers the tree to slow down leaf growth and concentrate its stored energy and nutrients on ripening the existing cocoa pods.
ga: Yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni ato yɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Can I keep planting new crops on my farm while I am harvesting mature cocoa pods?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ madu tsei heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mikpaa kookoo ŋmeii ni edara lɛ?

english: It is best to stop planting during harvest time so you can focus all your farm labor and energy on gathering, pod-breaking, and drying cocoa beans before they spoil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa dumɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli bɔni afee ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ ama oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kɛ ohewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaabuamɔ, amɛshwiemɔ, kɛ amɛgbimɔ nɔ dani amɛfite.

english: What should my main focus on the farm be once my cocoa pods start ripening fully?
ga: Mijwɛŋmɔ titri yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ji be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ.

english: Once pods mature, land preparation and planting must pause so you can prioritize harvesting on time, fermenting properly, and drying your crop for good market quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Esa akɛ akpa shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kɛ dumɔ koni onyɛ okɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ atsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be naa. Ferment jogbaŋŋ ni oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi koni jarayeli kpakpa aba.

english: Why shouldn't I clear and plant new land right when my main cocoa harvest begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mijieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ kookoo kpamɔ titri lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Harvesting mature cocoa demands heavy daily labor. Attempting to clear new land and plant at the same time spreads your resources thin, leading to unharvested, spoiled pods.
ga: Kookoo ni egbɔ lɛ kpamɔ biɔ daa gbi nitsumɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ obɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni odu tsei heei yɛ be kome too mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ afite. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni akpaaa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How does stopping new farm work at the end of the year help my overall harvest yield?
ga: Te ŋmɔ hee ni abaakpa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ baanyɛ aha mi nibii fɛɛ ni mifeɔ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pausing new planting gives you time to finish harvesting all remaining pods safely, allowing your land and mature trees to rest and reset for the next farming cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa dumɔwui heei lɛ, ebaaha oná be ni okɛkpa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ shweshweeshwe. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei ni eda lɛ hejɔɔmɔ kɛ shishijee hee kɛha okwaayeli nitsumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and build strong stems. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How come my cassava roots are small and woody even though the leaves look tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? He ni baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stem branches and green leaves instead of storing starch in the ground. Using balanced nutrients with more potassium helps the plant build larger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei niji kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔlii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ starch ato shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ewo bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines spread all over the soil without forming big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes need loose, well-drained soil to expand their roots. If the ground is too hard or compacted, or if there is too much water, the plant stays on top of the soil growing leaves instead of pushing tubers underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia atomoi koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ mli Tso lɛ baakã baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsi bulb lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that burn quickly under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates temporary shade and holds moisture in the air until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu nurse tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛfee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrition. Maintaining good shade trees and applying organic mulch keeps the soil cool so the plant can hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Shade kpakpa ni akɛhaa kɛ organic mulch ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to produce fruit compared to my neighbor's?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛtoɔ mikutsoŋbii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from each other. Pruning extra suckers so only two or three strong stems remain allows the main plant to fruit much faster.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔle ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii oya kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt suddenly in the afternoon even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by root diseases or tiny worms in the soil called nematodes that damage the roots, blocking water from traveling up into the rest of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ahe hela loo ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ mli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Enɛ haaa nu akabote tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi amli.

english: What is making the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding under the leaves. Spraying with organic mixtures like neem oil helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are small dark spots and holes appearing on my bean plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji bibii kɛ ŋmeii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-bean tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Dark spots and holes are caused by fungal diseases that spread in damp weather or by small beetles eating the foliage. Spacing plants out so air flows freely helps leaves dry fast and stops disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ buji baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ to he ko koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my yam crop produce short, twisted tubers instead of long straight ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yitsei kukuji ni ebɔle ehe yɛ yitsei kakadaji ni ja lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downward and need soft, deeply tilled soil or high mounds to expand freely. When planted in hard soil, the tubers hit obstacles and become stunted or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã amɛhe. Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ Yitso lɛ kɛ gbɛtsii nii baatswa ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees right next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kookoo lolo yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient that helps crops grow green and strong. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK, urea, or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK, urea, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which way I stick a cassava stem cutting into the ground when planting?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mafee madu ŋmei tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni miduɔ lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, direction matters a lot. You must plant cassava stems with the small growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky; if you plant the stem upside down, the sprouts will struggle to reach the surface, leading to weak growth or dead plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛtsɔɔmɔ he miihia waa. Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmeii bibii adu ŋmeii tso lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo egboɔ.

english: What insect is eating holes inside the center funnel of my maize stalks and leaving dirt-like powder behind?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloo kooloi miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ muji yɛ esɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. Because the worm hides deep inside the leaf funnel, you need to spray your recommended treatment directly down into the center whorl of the plant early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Ehe baahia ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa akɛ akɛtsaa hela lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli.

english: Why do I have to clear the land and build high mounds of soil just to plant yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oma gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni okɛdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, soft soil so their tubers can grow long and wide underground without hitting hard earth. High mounds also keep water from clogging around the roots, preventing the yam tubers from rotting in heavy rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkanáaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to heat stress or irregular watering. If the plant gets too dry or faces high temperatures, it drops its flowers to save energy; watering regularly and mulching the soil with dry grass keeps the roots cool and keeps the flowers on the vine.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛji tso lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli lɛ Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a big rainstorm comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ wulu ko aba?

english: No, you should avoid spreading fertilizer before heavy downpours because severe rain washes the nutrients away from your field before the roots can absorb them. Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp or when only a gentle light rain is expected.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo beni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ fioo.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even when my crops are taller than the weeds?
ga: Te jwɛi ji oshara kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds act like secret thieves under the ground, stealing water, fertilizer nutrients, and root space from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the food in the soil goes directly to your crops to give you a big yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ koni eha oná yibii babaoo.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain tree, they all fight for the mother tree's food and water, resulting in very small bunches. Keeping only one main fruiting stalk, one medium sucker, and one small shoot ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii waa. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ yitso titri kome pɛ, tso lɛ yitso kome ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ tso lɛ yitso bibioo kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why does my harvested dry maize turn to dust and get small insect holes after a few months in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ feɔ sũ ni eyɛ kooloi bibii bibii lɛ? Beni ewo baagi lɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ

english: This destruction is caused by grain weevils that bore into dried corn to feed and lay eggs. Ensuring your maize is thoroughly sun-dried and storing it in sealed airtight bags (such as PICS bags) cuts off oxygen and suffocates insects naturally without chemical sprays.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmaa mli ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli kɛtaoɔ niyenii ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni o-abele lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotokui) lɛ amli lɛ, ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting food crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that cools the plants and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb on to give me a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ koni eha mi kpamɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Yam vines use their leaves to catch sunlight and convert it into energy to build big tubers underground. Lifting the vines up on stakes keeps the leaves exposed to maximum sunlight and prevents soil-borne diseases from rotting the stems.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛheɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn pale yellow or purple early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow or purple leaves on young maize are a sign that the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus. Adding compost, manure, or the right fertilizer gives the leaves their rich green color back so the plant can grow heavy cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ loo purple ni yɔɔ abɛi bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crops' growth even when I give my farm enough fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ fioo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ha yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the root zone. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to produce a strong yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: How do I know if I am giving my vegetable crops too much water when pumping water to my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine beni mikɛ nu miiwo miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Too much water drowns crop roots by cutting off their air supply, causing leaves to turn yellow, feel soft, and drop off even though the soil is wet. Soil should feel damp like a damp cloth, not flooded like thick mud.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ anu he akɛ edɔ tamɔ mama ni efɔ. Ejeee nu afua tamɔ sũ ni mli edɔ

english: Why are the blossom flowers falling off my tomato plants before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛwo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience severe heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture level steady and watering consistently during hot weather helps the flowers set into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slanted angle instead of straight up and down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanted angle encourages the roots to spread out horizontally near the upper soil layer, giving the tubers plenty of space to grow larger and making them easier to harvest.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ naa gbɛ babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, drain valuable water and food away from the main plantain stem. Removing excess suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ jieɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do the center shoots of my young maize plants look shredded with tiny holes and brown dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli fãi bibii.

english: Shredded leaves and brown dirt inside the center shoots are caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm eating the soft growing leaves. Treating the heart of the plant early protects the growing tip so the plant can continue to mature.
ga: baai ni egbɛ eshwa Ni muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai bibii ni miida lɛ kɛbaa. Tso lɛ tsui lɛ tsamɔ mra Ebuɔ ŋmei ni miida lɛ he. koni tsei aya nɔ ada

english: Can I harvest seeds from my current maize crop and save them to plant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ mli ni mikɛto kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ?

english: It is better to buy fresh certified seeds each season rather than planting saved seeds. Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their vigor, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants in the second generation.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli moŋ fe ni ooodu dumɔwui ni ato. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the tree seedlings I buy from the market will yield good fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai?

english: Look for certified nurseries that sell grafted seedlings. Healthy seedlings have bright green leaves, sturdy stems, and well-developed root systems without signs of spots, mold, or insect damage.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni edara jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo kooloi bibii efiteee lɛ bɛ he.

english: If I plant a seed from a very sweet orange, will the tree grow fruit that tastes just as sweet?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ waa mli lɛ Ani tso lɛ baawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ?

english: Not always. Citrus trees grown directly from seed often change in flavor and quality compared to the parent fruit. To get the exact same sweet taste, you should plant a grafted citrus seedling.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ, citrus tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe fɛo kɛ amɛhe kpakpa kɛ akɛto shishijee aduawai lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni oná ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ Esa akɛ odu ŋmei tso ni akɛwo ŋmei mli lɛ.

english: My cocoa trees are very old and stopped producing many pods; should I cut them down or replant?
ga: Mi-cocoa tso lɛ egbɔ waa ni ekpa ŋmeii babaoo ni ewoɔ lɛ. Ani esa akɛ mafo mli loo madu ehee?

english: If an entire farm is old and diseased, cutting down and replanting with new hybrid cocoa seedlings is best. However, if individual trees are weak, you can cut back main branches or graft high-yielding shoots onto old stumps to rejuvenate them.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ egbɔ ni hela emɔ lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaafolɔ ni adu hybrid cocoa dumɔwui heei, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ loo okɛ tsei niji ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ awo tsei akutsei momo lɛ anɔ koni eha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry up and die shortly after I replant them in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers die if planted during hot, dry spells or if too many leaves are left on the sucker during replanting. Trim back the leaves before planting to reduce water loss, and plant during the early rainy season.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii baagboi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa, ni nu hɔmɔ bɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ baai babaoo eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai dani odu koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli

english: How many years will it take for a newly planted grafted mango seedling to start producing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango dumɔwu ni akɛwo mli ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Grafted mango seedlings usually start producing fruit in 3 to 4 years, whereas trees grown directly from seeds can take 7 to 10 years to produce.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my crops too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows air to flow, reduces disease spread, and helps each crop produce maximum yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli. Ha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi ni oye obua tso fɛɛ tso ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive drought. Adding mulch around the base retains soil moisture, and applying fertilizer helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli. Mulching around Konus lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ni kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to prune excess branches from our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ wɔ kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to put energy into pod production.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee black pods.

english: Apply fertilizer when the crops are actively growing and the soil is moist, usually 2 to 3 weeks after germination or transplanting. Avoid applying fertilizer during heavy rains so it does not wash away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tsei miida ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsake lɛ sɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekafo.

english: Cocoa trees often drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or inadequate pollination by tiny insects called midges. Ensuring proper shade and soil moisture helps the tree hold onto its flowers so pods can develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ aná hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce smaller tubers if I do not give the vines stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji mihaaa wain tso lɛ akwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and good air flow, allowing the plant to make more energy and grow larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha hulu la ni fa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do plantain plants produce smaller bunches if I leave all the young suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain ko woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers leaves energy concentrated in the main plant, allowing it to produce a larger, healthier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsei bibii kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ aba tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa, ni efeɔ plantains akui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a critical nutrient for leaf growth. The plant starves and pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the newer growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I plant maize on the same field continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Repeatedly growing the same crop on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil faster than nature can restore them. Rotating crops, especially with beans or groundnuts, puts nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni adebɔɔ baanyɛ aku sɛɛ aha amɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii aku amɛsɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer directly to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve safely so plant roots can absorb it. Applying it to dry soil causes high concentrations of chemical salts to scorch and burn the plant roots.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni fa babaoo lɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni amɛshã amɛ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing, aggressive plants that steal applied fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight directly from your crops before your crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. dani ŋmɔshi nibii aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. Excess water from heavy rains drowns the root system, allowing soil fungi and bacteria to multiply and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved abruptly from shaded nurseries into hot, open fields. Slowly exposing them to full sun over a few days and watering them well during transplanting prevents this die-off.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Okɛ amɛ awo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli fiofio yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli ni okɛ nu aha amɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ ateŋ koni enɛ akagbo.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hide deep inside the central leaf whorl of young maize where it is moist and safe, feeding on leaves before they expand.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Ye baai lɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as natural umbrellas, protecting their tender leaves and keeping the soil moist while they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Buu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and why are the centers of the plants rotting?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa, ni mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ mli fã lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl into the center leaves of young maize plants to hide and feed, which stunts plant growth if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛkplekeɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛyatee amɛhe ni amɛtao niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akpa dalɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When rain water collects around the roots for too long without draining, it suffocates them and causes fungal rot beneath the soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni efooo Ebaaha egbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmeii agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efo mli dani madu nii?

english: If your previous crops grew very slowly, had pale yellowish leaves, or gave you very small harvests despite good rainfall, it means your soil has run low on essential plant food like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa nɛɔ moŋ No tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. When they die, they leave this free fertilizer behind for the next crop to use.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛhaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. kɛ amɛgboi lɛ Amɛshiɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ koni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Will I get more harvest if I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and very small or missing corn cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa loo amɛbɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks from sucking insects like whiteflies that spread crop viruses.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo tutuamɔi kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ nɔ.
