english: Small shoots (suckers) steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main stem to grow a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ plantains akuu ko ni da ni tsii.

english: The very first rain is often followed by weeks of hot, dry weather before the main rainy season truly starts. Planting too early causes sprouts to germinate and then dry out and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Does clearing weeds while my crops are still very small really make a difference?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ baaha srɔtofeemɔ aba diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, early weeding is critical because young weeds grow faster than crop seedlings, stealing nutrients, water, and sunlight during the exact weeks your crops need them most to survive.
ga: Hɛɛ, ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ he miihia ejaakɛ jwɛi bibii lɛ daa oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la yɛ otsi lɛ mli be mli ni ehe hiaa otsei lɛ fe fɛɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune my cocoa trees before the flowering season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei dani fɔfɔii aba lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead branches and excess leaves, allowing sunlight and air to reach the tree trunk. This gives the tree the energy it needs to produce strong flowers and pods instead of wasting food on useless branches.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite niyenii yɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: What actually happens to my cocoa trees if I leave them bushy without pruning?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ ni efee ŋmɔ mli ni mifolɔko tso lɛ he?

english: Overly bushy trees trap moisture and block light, creating a dark home where pests and fungal diseases like black pod thrive. It also prevents flowers from getting enough light to mature into full cocoa pods.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsiɔ kane naa. Enɛ haa shia ni mli ewo duŋ baa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ black pods lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mli. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hu náa la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to trim the branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tso?

english: It is best to trim your trees right before the main flowering and rainy seasons begin. Trimming at this time prepares the tree to put all its strength into flower development and fruiting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ tso lɛ mli dani fɔfɔi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi. Kɛ́ afo yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni esaa tso lɛ he kɛha fɔfɔii ni baa lɛ kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ.

english: How do my cocoa flowers actually turn into full cocoa pods?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers need pollen transferred from one blossom to another, usually by tiny insects called midges or by hand. Once fertilized, the flower stops dropping off and starts growing into a cocoa pod.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi biɔ ni ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ nakai. Atsɛɔ nakai akɛ ŋmei loo kɛtsɔ nine nɔ. Kɛji akɛ awo mli fɔfɔi lɛ baakpa gbee ni amɛbaabɔi dalɛ ni amɛbaafee kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do some farmers manually pollinate cocoa flowers by hand instead of waiting for nature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ amɛdɛŋ woɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaamɛ adebɔɔ lɛ?

english: Natural insects are very small and might miss many flowers. Hand pollination ensures that almost all healthy flowers get fertilized, which can greatly increase the number of pods your tree carries.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii waa ni ekolɛ amɛbaafee fɔfɔi babaoo. Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha pods ni otso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Flowers fall off when they are not pollinated, when the tree lacks nutrients, or when dense branches shade them too much. Keeping the canopy clear through pruning helps flowers stay healthy and get pollinated.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Beni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo be mli ni niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ lɛ Kpojiemɔ ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Where on the cocoa tree should I expect flowers and pods to appear?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ makpa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii gbɛ yɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Unlike many fruit trees that bear fruit at the tips of thin branches, cocoa trees produce flowers and pods directly on the main trunk and old thick branches so the tree can support the heavy fruit.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ aduawai tsei babaoo ni woɔ yibii yɛ tsei niji bibii anaagbee lɛ ahe. Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ kɛ tsei niji momo ni mli tse lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ yibii ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: What kind of support can I get if I go to the local District Cocoa Office?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ manyɛ maná kɛji mitee Kpokpaa nɔ Cocoa Nitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: District Cocoa Offices provide technical advice from extension officers, register farmers for government input programs, and teach modern practices like proper pruning, hand pollination, and pest control.
ga: Kpokpaa nɔ kookoo nitsumɔhei lɛ kɛ ŋaawoo ni kɔɔ ŋaawoo he haa kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Ŋmaa okwaafoi awo wolo nɔ kɛha nɔyeli lɛ data mlibotemɔ nitsumɔi ni otsɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔi tamɔ tso ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ. nine mli pollination kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ

english: Why do government extension officers ask me to submit a list of my farm details?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Nɔyeli lɛ Extension Officer lɛ biɔ ni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he saji ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Officers need your farm size and tree count so they can accurately plan for supplies like fertilizers or spraying, and schedule training teams to visit your farm without leaving you out.
ga: Amralofoi lɛ baasumɔ bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ da ha kɛ tsei ayibɔ. Koni anyɛ ato nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ. ni oto tsɔsemɔ kuu ko he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛbasara oŋmɔ lɛ ni amɛshiŋ bo.

english: How can an extension officer help me improve the yield on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te extension nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi koni nibii ni afeɔ yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: An extension officer visits your farm to inspect tree health, teach you the correct sequence of farm activities, and show you step-by-step how to care for your crop to get maximum harvest.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyakwɛ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni etsɔɔ bo bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni oná yibii babaoo lɛ fitsofitso.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct heat. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains or shade trees to keep them cool and retain soil moisture while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my maize stalks grow very tall but produce tiny ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi daraa waa shi amɛyɛ toi bibii lɛ?

english: This usually happens when maize seeds are planted too close together or lack key soil nutrients like nitrogen. When plants compete for light and soil food, they use energy to grow tall leaves instead of building full corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná niyenii. Akɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai kakadaji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Healthy cassava plants keep bright green, firm leaves. If they lack water, the lower leaves will turn yellow and drop off to save moisture for the underground tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ haa amɛbaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji nu bɛ lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when I plant many of them together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni mikɛ tsei babaoo ebɔ he kome yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Plantains require a lot of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting suckers too close together forces them to fight for resources, which slows down their overall growth and delays fruiting.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la babaoo, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛwu yɛ nibii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa dalɛ fɛɛ baa shi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and curl up at the edges?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in peppers are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, or by a lack of plant nutrients in the soil. Checking the underside of the leaves early helps identify insects before they spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo tso mli niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ana kooloi bibii dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before any fruit begins to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when soil temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Mulching around the base of the plant helps keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving cowpeas too much water can suffocate their roots by pushing air out of the soil. Cowpeas need well-drained soil and moderate moisture, as their roots naturally capture their own nitrogen from the air.
ga: Cowpea ni akɛ nu woɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha eshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ he miihia tsina ŋmeii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How does spreading dried grass or cocoa husks around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ afɔ he fɛɛ he. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket over the soil, keeping it cool under the hot sun, trapping moisture, and suppressing weeds that would otherwise steal food from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni egbeɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ aju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the main vines and leaves naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up at the end of the rainy season. Leaving mature tubers in wet soil past this point can lead to rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai titrii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛje shishi amɛgbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Kɛ́ ashi bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ kɛho nɛkɛ he nɛɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛgboi.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay loose and soft instead of forming hard, tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to firm up when temperatures are too high or when watering is uneven. Cabbage needs steady moisture and cool soil conditions to wrap its leaves tightly into a solid head.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee shiŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Cabbage he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ koni ekɛ ehe baai lɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ ni efee yitso ni wa.

english: Why do my crops still get sick even after I clear all the weeds and crop leaves from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Even when your field looks clean, tiny disease germs like fungi and bacteria can remain hidden inside the soil, travel through the air, or get carried from neighboring farms by wind and rain drops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔji lɛ mli tse po Shi helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. gbɛfaa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kɛyaa

english: Is it possible for seeds to carry diseases into my farm before I even plant them?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ dumɔwui kɛ helai aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu amɛ po?

english: Yes, seeds harvested from sick parent plants often carry hidden fungi, bacteria, or viruses inside or on their skin, which will infect the seedling as soon as it sprouts.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli loo yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatswa dumɔwui lɛ hela kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Can a crop disease travel from one sick cassava plant to a healthy one right next to it?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ aya kɛjɛ ŋmei tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, diseases spread easily between plants through sap on farm tools, insects carrying plant viruses, splashing rainwater, or even your hands and clothes as you work in the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ okwaayeli nibii anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kplukai ni kɛ helai baa tsei amli lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ nu loo oniji kɛ otadei po anɔ beni otsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize plants are sick and not just suffering from heat or water shortage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ni jeee hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Thirsty maize leaves usually roll up tightly during the hot afternoon and open up in the evening, whereas sick plants show permanent spots, yellow streaks, or rot that do not disappear after rain or watering.
ga: Abɛi baai ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe yɛ gbɛkɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni baahi shi daa. Ha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni fiteɔ ni sɛɛ efooo yɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni awo mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What are the very first signs I should look for to know that a disease has entered my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni esa akɛ makwɛ koni mana kɛji hela ko ebote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Check for unusual tiny dark spots on the lower leaves, pale yellow patches on fresh shoots, sudden wilting of top branches, or strange powdery coatings under the leaves.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ. abnormalities yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ Ayɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse yɛ tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ. Tso nine ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gboi trukaa. Aloo powda ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni akɛwo baai lɛ ashishi.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even though I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves do not always mean lack of food; they can mean the soil is too wet, tiny worms called nematodes are damaging the roots, or a plant virus is stopping the crop from using the fertilizer.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ miifite shishifãi lɛ. Aloo tso mli hela ko miitsi ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akatsu nii?

english: At what time of the year or weather condition should I be most careful about crop illnesses?
ga: Mɛɛ afi loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be esa akɛ makwɛ mihe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ahe helai ahe?

english: Plant diseases spread fastest during warm, wet rainy seasons because high moisture and wet leaves create the perfect environment for fungal spores to hatch and infect crops.
ga: Tsei ahelai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hela.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to inspect my crops for sickness?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji hela yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: Walk through your field at least twice a week, checking under leaves and stems early in the morning when pests and early symptoms of disease are easiest to see.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Kwɛmɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishi leebi maŋkpa be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai okadii ni jeɔ shishi mra lɛ naa mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do you advise farmers to wash cutlasses and hoes before moving to a new section of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ okwaafoi afɔ amɛ cutlass kɛ hoe lɛ he dani amɛya ŋmɔ lɛ fã hee ko mli lɛ?

english: Farm tools get coated with infected plant sap and soil containing microscopic germs, which will contaminate healthy plants if you use the dirty tools on them.
ga: Akɛ tso mli nu ni hela emɔ lɛ kɛ sũ ni helai bibii ni anaaa lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe. Enɛ baafite tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ nibii ni he tseee tsu nii yɛ nɔ.

english: Why do crops planted too close together seem to catch sickness much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ hela mɔ amɛ oya kwraa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, air cannot pass between them to dry the leaves, keeping them damp for longer periods and helping fungal diseases grow and spread rapidly.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni eha baai lɛ agbi. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient found in healthy soil. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tsei nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ niyenii ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist, usually early in the morning or right after a rain. If you apply fertilizer when the ground is dry, the heat can burn the roots and the crops will not be able to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli leebi maŋkpa loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans together on the same land with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize is very beneficial because bean plants pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the maize, while maize gives structural support for climbing bean vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ be mli ni abele haa yelikɛbuamɔ kɛha bean wain tsei ni akwɔɔ lɛ,

english: Why do weeds make my crop plants grow weak and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to the soil's nutrients so they can grow big and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa otsei titrii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my maize leaves, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ baa ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa amɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves (the funnel). You can control them by regularly checking the plants early in the morning and applying approved neem oil or recommended insecticides directly into the funnel.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ (cones) lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ daa leebi lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ neem fɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the plants get too hot or don't get enough water regularly. Keeping the soil cool with dried grass mulch and watering at the base of the plant helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi babaoo kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi kɛ nu ni awoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: How can I keep the soil on my farm wet during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmath be mli kɛji egbi pɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass or fallen leaves—a method called mulching—traps moisture in the dirt and shields the soil from hot winds, keeping root zone cool and wet for longer.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe - gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put bamboo or wooden sticks next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ama sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can climb high to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to build large, heavy tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia akutsei koni baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ yitso agbo ko ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Which plantain suckers should I cut from an old plant to start a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo plantain ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso momo ko mli koni maje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You should pick 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. They have stronger energy reserves and produce healthier plantain trees with bigger bunches than 'water suckers' that have wide leaves early on.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘Sword Bud’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtoɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhe tsɔi lɛ dara fe ‘ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots don't spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off. Leaving cassava in the ground too long after it matures makes the tubers tough, woody, and watery.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tso, kɛ nu.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which acts as essential food for green leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant's juices, or by a virus. The curling is the plant's reaction to stress, which prevents it from capturing sunlight properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo nɔ ni hela ko kɛbaa Curling ji bɔ ni tso ko tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ haomɔ mli. Enɛ haaa hulu la lɛ amɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees drying up and turning brown so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by leaf spot diseases or drought stress. During dry spells or disease attacks, plantain trees sacrifice their oldest bottom leaves to save water and nutrients for the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa mli hela loo hɔmɔ haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Yɛ hɔmɔ loo hela bei amli lɛ, Dumɔwui kɛ amɛshishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ niyenii kɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when there is sudden dry weather, which damages the pollen inside the flower. Without successful pollination, the flower dies and drops off.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi trukaa. Enɛ haa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose many of their tiny young pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called 'cherelle wilt.' When water is scarce, cocoa trees naturally drop some of their youngest pods to conserve moisture and keep the parent tree alive.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Cherelle withers’ kɛ́ nu faaa Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ekomɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛha tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow very small while others grow big on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow small when the soil in the mound is too hard or lacks rich organic matter. Loose soil allows the yam tuber to expand easily, while hard soil restricts its growth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni wa baatsi dalɛ naa.

english: Why do some crops die when planted under shade while others grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi gboiɔ kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shia lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Sun-loving crops like maize and cassava need full, direct sunlight to make their food. Other plants, like young cocoa, evolved to grow under forest trees, so direct sun burns their delicate leaves.
ga: Tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Amɛhe miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ kookoo bibii, daa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ashishi yɛ koo lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa ebaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How exactly do weeds stop my crops from growing properly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for survival. They steal soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight, leaving your crops weak and unable to produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhi shi. Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni ehaa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kpo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays flooded or waterlogged for too long. The roots need air to breathe, and excess water suffocates them, allowing fungi to enter and decay the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha mɔ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout after heavy rain falls right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash seeds away, pack the topsoil down into a hard crust that sprouts cannot push through, or flood the soil so seeds drown before taking root.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui kɛya. Okɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ awo ŋmei ni wa ni dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli. Aloo okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ nu mli dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: When is the best month to start clearing my farm land for the main growing season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri lɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Starting land clearing in February is ideal because it gives you enough time to clear bushes, prepare the soil, and have the field fully ready before the major rains begin in March or April, preventing rushed work and late planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ February mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa onáa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛjie jwɛi, osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ March loo April mli. Etsiɔ oyaiyeli nitsumɔ kɛ dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I delay clearing my land until the rains actually start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efeŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ to sɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaje shishi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If you wait until the rains start, the ground becomes muddy and difficult to work on, weeds quickly overrun the field, and you miss the optimal early planting window, which reduces your crop yields.
ga: Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ bɔi nɛmɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaawa akɛ oootsake. Jwɛi ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya. Ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ be ni sa ni okɛbaadu nii lɛ he mra. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: How does clearing my farmland early in the year help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni mikɛbaajie yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Early land preparation exposes soil pests and weed seeds to the hot sun so they die off, gives the soil time to settle, and ensures your crops get the full benefit of the very first rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aya hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaagboi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛba shi. ni oye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is properly ready before I put my maize seeds in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ shi dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Land is ready when all bushes, tree stumps, and debris are cleared, and the soil is loosened or plowed neat and flat, allowing seeds to germinate evenly and roots to spread easily without competing with weeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo beni ajie brɔshi, tsei akutsei, kɛ sũi fɛɛ ni efite lɛ. ni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend foreign or improved maize varieties over my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ jieɔ maŋsɛɛ loo ŋmãa ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yi fe mi shishijee dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved and foreign maize varieties are bred to produce bigger cobs, yield more grain per acre, and resist common pests and diseases far better than older, local seed varieties.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji aba. Yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ acre kome mli ni amɛhe wa fe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi ni etsɛ.

english: Are foreign maize varieties difficult to grow compared to local ones?
ga: Ani maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ wa fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa srɔtoi lɛ?

english: They are not difficult, but they do require good timing, well-prepared soil, and proper care. If planted on time in well-cleared land with proper nutrients, foreign varieties perform significantly better than local seeds.
ga: Ewaaa. Shi ebiɔ be kpakpa. Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ be naa yɛ he ko ni ajie ŋmɔji jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ, Maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why does maize perform poorly when planted in fields that are not completely cleared of weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔji ni jwɛi bɛ mli kwraa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize needs a lot of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow tall and produce big cobs. Weeds grow faster than maize and will steal these vital nutrients, leaving your crop weak and stunted.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la babaoo, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni ebaaju nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Is it better for my farm if I use machines like tractors to clear my land instead of clearing by hand?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsɔne ko tamɔ traktɔ tsu nii kɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baatse shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Using machines saves a massive amount of time and physical labor, allowing you to prepare large areas of land quickly so you can plant on time across your entire field.
ga: Tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haaa afite be kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ babaoo. Ehaa osaa hei wuji oya. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be naa yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Does using heavy machinery to clear land affect the soil quality for my crops?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Machinery clears and plows land very fast, but it is best done when the soil is dry around February to prevent compacting wet soil, which can make it hard for plant roots to grow.
ga: Mashiŋ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii oya waa. Shi gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi, aaafee February. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha ewa aha tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: How can I avoid wasting time and labor during the busy farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafite be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ yɛ okwaayeli be ni nitsumɔi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: You can avoid wasting time by starting land clearing early in the dry season, organizing your labor or machines in advance, and buying your seeds and inputs before the rains arrive.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa be ni ofiteɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shishijee mra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Too nitsumɔ loo tsɔnei ahe gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ. ni nyɛhe dumɔwui kɛ niyenii dani nugbɔ lɛ aba

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when I do not add fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants turn yellow when they lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, which acts as plant food. Without enough nutrients in the soil, crops cannot produce green leaves or grow strong.
ga: Tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha tso lɛ bɛ amɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu nyɛŋ afee baai eŋɔli loo amɛdara waa.

english: How does chemical fertilizer actually work to make my crops yield more food?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni ekɛ niyenii babaoo aha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Chemical fertilizer supplies concentrated nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium directly to the soil. These nutrients feed the plant roots, helping the crop grow faster, produce more flowers, and bear larger fruit.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus kɛ potassium baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii nɛɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya. Ha fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why did my crops wither and burn after I applied fertilizer during a hot, dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts. Without water in the soil to dissolve these salts, the fertilizer sucks water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, causing the crop to scorch and dry up.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔ mli lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shãa ni egbiɔ.

english: Why does my soil feel hard and dry even though I regularly use chemical fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni egbi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii daa moŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant, but it does not feed the soil. Without organic matter like decomposed leaves or manure, soil loses its ability to hold water and stay soft.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii shi amɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo kooloi afɔfɔi bɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu mli ni ehi shi blɛoo.

english: Can I get a good harvest from my crops without buying expensive fertilizers from the shop?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa ni miheee ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛɛɛ shwapo mli?

english: Yes, you can feed your crops by mixing compost, decayed plant waste, or animal manure into the soil. These natural materials feed the soil over time and improve its structure without relying on store-bought inputs.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii aha onibii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafutu mli lɛ nɔ. tsei amli ŋmeii loo kooloi amli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ be kɛ bei amli ni ehaa egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔɔ nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ anɔ.

english: Which crops can I plant that do not need expensive fertilizer to grow well?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa fataaa he?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, and soybeans are great choices because they capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it naturally into the soil, requiring very little extra fertilizer to produce a good harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas, peanuts, kɛ soybeans ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ afata he koni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I apply my fertilizer late in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: If you apply fertilizer too late, the plant has already passed its main growth stage and cannot use the extra food to build cobs or fruits, resulting in wasted money and low yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he sɛɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ eho edalɛ fã titri lɛ he. Ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ niyenii krɛdɛɛ afee cob loo aduawai. Enɛ haa shika ni afiteɔ kɛ nitsumɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly when transported in long-distance trucks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo lɔlei ni fãa gbɛ kakadaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops continue to breathe and produce heat after harvest. When packed tightly in hot trucks on bumpy roads, the heat and bruising cause the crops to soften and spoil rapidly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo lɔle ni mli edɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why are buyers offering me low prices for my crops even though I spent so much money buying inputs to grow them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mifite shika babaoo kɛhe nibii ni akɛduɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ.

english: Market prices depend on crop quality, overall supply in the market, and customer demand, not on how much money you spent growing the crop. Damaged or undersized produce naturally attracts lower market prices.
ga: Jarayeli jara lɛ damɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ. Nibii fɛɛ ni akɛhaa yɛ jara nɔ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahiamɔ nii Jeee shika ni ofiteɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔ he lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni efite loo ni yɔɔ bibioo tsɔ lɛ baagbala jara ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I prevent my harvested maize from getting damaged by insects while waiting for market prices to go up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ naa koni ŋmeii akafite yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni jara nɔ jara lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Drying your grain completely until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags keeps out moisture and starves insects of oxygen, allowing your crop to stay fresh until prices improve.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛhe wa ni akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he, ni ebaaha kooloi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ehee kɛyashiɔ be mli ni jara lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What is the main difference between hybrid seeds and the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred from two selected parent plants to combine high yield and strong disease resistance. Saved seeds from past harvests lose these powerful traits over time, resulting in smaller harvests and weaker crops.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni ji nyɛmɛi ni ahala koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Can I harvest seeds from my hybrid maize crop this year and plant them again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ hybrid corn mli afi nɛɛ ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended to replant seeds harvested from a hybrid crop. The second-generation plants will lose their uniform strength, grow unevenly, and yield much less grain compared to buying fresh hybrid seeds each season.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli. Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe lɛ. uneven growth Ni ehaa dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some crop varieties perform well near the main town but fail on my farm outside the village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ wulu lɛ masɛi shi amɛtsuuu nii yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ akrowa lɛ kponɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops react to specific local soil types, water retention, and land conditions. A crop variety that meets standards in town may fail in remote areas if the local soil lacks key nutrients or retains too much or too little water.
ga: Tsei lɛ baaha hetoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. nu ni ahiɔ mli kɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ Tsei srɔtoi ni kɛ shishitoo mlai ni yɔɔ maji wuji amli lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli nibii titrii loo ekɛ nu babaoo loo fioo pɛ toɔ,.

english: Why do hybrid crops require more fertilizer than my traditional local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mimaŋ tsei lɛ?

english: Hybrid crops grow much faster and produce far higher yields, which means they consume nutrients rapidly. Traditional crops grow slower and produce less, so they can survive on lower natural soil nutrients.
ga: Hybrid tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Kusum nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛtsɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, often because heavy rains have washed the nutrients deeper into the soil or waterlogged soil is suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, bei pii lɛ, ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do some plants on my farm grow tall and produce big ears while others right next to them stay stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ toi wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ daa lɛ? Na hiɛ ni egbɔjɔ

english: Uneven plant growth occurs when seeds are planted at unequal depths, soil nutrients are unevenly distributed, or insects attack the root systems of certain young plants early in the season.
ga: Tso lɛ dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mlijaa ejaaa. Aloo kooloi bibii tutuaa tsei bibii komɛi ashishifãi yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do improved hybrid seeds seem to suffer more from insect pests than my local seeds if I don't spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-hybrid dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo fe mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsofa shwieee nɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid crops are bred for high yield and often have tender, sweet tissues that insects love to eat. Local varieties have developed tougher skins and natural defenses over decades, though they yield less.
ga: Akwɛ tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛyɛ fãji ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kooloi sumɔɔ ni amɛye. Kuu lɛ mli kooloi lɛ ená hewolo ni mli wa kɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ewooo yibii babaoo moŋ.

english: Why are my planted seeds taking so long to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a precise mix of moisture, warmth, and proper planting depth to sprout. If planted too deep or in dry, hard soil, the seed wastes its energy struggling to break through the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my crops to start flowering early when the plants are still very short?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi mra be mli ni tsei lɛ eshɛɛɛ kuku kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Early flowering is a stress response usually triggered by drought or poor soil. When the plant senses it might dry up, it tries to produce flowers and seeds quickly before it dies to ensure its survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni baa mra lɛ ji nɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, ni bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ ekolɛ egbi lɛ Ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui oya dani egbo bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: How can I check if a recommended seed variety will grow well on my land before buying a large quantity?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui srɔtoi ni ajie yi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mahe babaoo?

english: You can set up a small test demonstration plot on a section of your farm to plant a single bag of the seed. Observe its germination, drought tolerance, and yield before committing your entire farm to the new seed.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee kaa nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko. Yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fã kome nɔ koni odu dumɔwui kotoku kome pɛ lɛ, kwɛmɔ bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa, bɔ ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi amɛhaa yɛ hɔmɔ mli. ni owo yibii dani odu dumɔwui heei yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english: Why should I pluck off the early flowers from my young pepper plants before they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ dani amɛje yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plucking off early flowers allows the young plant to direct all its nutrients toward growing strong roots and stems. Once the plant develops a sturdy structure, it will produce many more flowers and healthier peppers overall.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ kɛya eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi ni wa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ yɛ shishitoo ni mli wa Ebaawo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni fɛɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow while the crop is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the essential nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the crop the nutrients it needs to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii agboi ni fa babaoo.

english: Is it helpful for my farm if I plant cowpeas in the same field alongside my main maize crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi ŋmãa titri lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the maize. Their low leaves also cover the ground to shade out weeds and preserve moisture in the soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa Baai ni baa shi lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I cut off the extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers forces them to compete with the main plantain tree for food and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves only one strong replacement stem for the next season.
ga: Nibii ni amɛshwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ plantain titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ ajie sucker ni fa lɛ, eshiɔ tso kome pɛ ni wa ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems helps protect your farm from this infection.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by severe heat or dry conditions. Applying mulch around the roots and keeping the soil evenly watered helps flowers stay on the plant and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni akɛ nu awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni eha tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why do my bean leaves droop and curl downward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bean leaves curl or droop in high heat to shrink their surface area, which slows down water loss and protects the plant from scorching. They naturally uncurls and recover when the evening temperature cools down.
ga: Bean baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ la ni mli wa koni ekɛha ŋwɛigbɛ he lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni ehaa tsei lɛ shãaa. Amɛbaajɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni gbɛkɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my yam crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and climbing vines dry up and turn yellow naturally. This shows that the plant has finished growing above ground and transferred all its stored energy into underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ naa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to thoroughly sun-dry my harvested maize seeds before storing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ dani akɛto?

english: Moisture in stored seeds causes mold to grow and attracts insects like weevils that destroy the grain. Drying seeds properly keeps them healthy so they germinate successfully when you plant them next season.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni tutuaa dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi odumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ be kroko mli.

english: How many years does it usually take for a new cocoa tree to start giving a full harvest?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko baashɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ he?

english: Cocoa trees start giving a few fruits in their first 3 years, but it typically takes about 6 to 7 years for the trees to reach full maturity and produce a large, complete harvest.
ga: Cacao tsei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 lɛ amli, shi bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani cacao tso ko daa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni eda.

english: Is it a sign of crop disease if my newly planted cocoa trees don't produce many pods at first?
ga: Ani eji ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela he okadi kɛji akɛ kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛjeɔ shishi?

english: No, low yield in the first three years is natural for cocoa trees. They naturally build up their fruiting capacity slowly over 6 to 7 years as they mature, so sparse production early on is completely normal.
ga: Dabi, yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛha kookoo tsei. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛtswaa yibiiwoo fiofio fiofio yɛ afii 6 kɛyashi 7 mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ mra, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni gbɛ eshwa lɛ jeɔ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: What is happening to my cocoa plant during its first three years in the soil?
ga: Mɛni ba mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ ni amɛye yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: During the first three years, the cocoa seedling spends most of its energy establishing strong roots, building trunk strength, and growing leaves. Any fruit it bears during this time is just early development before full maturity.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo shishifãi ni wa. Bɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha tso lɛ yitso lɛ ni baa kɛ aduawai fɛɛ ni baa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ji mra be mli dalɛ pɛ dani eda.

english: Why is my young cocoa farm only producing a few pods here and there in its third year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ wo ŋmɔji fioo komɛi pɛ yɛ afi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the third year, cocoa trees are just beginning their reproductive stage. Because the tree is still growing, it can only support a small number of scattered pods before it reaches full strength in years 6 to 7.
ga: Yɛ afi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, no mli lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ eje efɔmɔ fã lɛ shishi pɛŋ. Akɛni tso lɛ miida lolo hewɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ ekwɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ anɔ dani eshɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ he yɛ afii 6 kɛyashi 7 mli.

english: What kind of care do my young cocoa trees need before they reach their main production years?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ he hiaa mi kookoo tsei bibii lɛ dani amɛ nitsumɔ afi titri lɛ aba?

english: Young trees require protection from direct harsh sunlight, regular weed control, pest management, and sufficient soil moisture so they can build the strength needed to produce heavy yields later on.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa Jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni tsei nɛɛ anyɛ ama hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ amɛma shi.

english: How can I handle my family's daily expenses while waiting several years for my cocoa to yield a full harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miweku lɛ daa gbi shika nɔ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ afii babaoo dani kookoo lɛ ashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Because cocoa takes 6 to 7 years to fully produce, farmers usually intercrop with fast-yielding food crops like plantains, cassava, or vegetables to generate immediate food and income during the waiting period.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eheɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani anyɛɔ afeɔ kookoo kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ bei pii lɛ okwaafoi duɔ niyenii ni woɔ yibii oya, tamɔ plantains, cassava, loo aduawai, koni amɛná niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ mɛmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Is cocoa farming a reliable business to take care of my children's future?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ ji nitsumɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni akɛkwɛ mibi lɛ wɔsɛɛ be nɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa farming is a long-term investment that can support a family for decades, provided you plan for the initial 6 to 7 years it takes for the trees to start producing high yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ akwɛ weku ko nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Kɛji oto klɛŋklɛŋ afii 6 kɛyashi 7 lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni tso lɛ aje yibiiwoo babaoo shishi.

english: Can I plant other food crops alongside my cocoa trees while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii krokomɛi. Yɛ kookoo tso lɛ masɛi beni emɛɛɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantain or cocoyam alongside young cocoa trees provides short-term food and income while also offering helpful shade for the growing cocoa plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain loo cocoa ni akɛfataa cocoa tsei bibii ahe lɛ baafee niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe yɛ be kukuoo mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kokoo tsei ni miida lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: How many years can a well-maintained cocoa farm continue producing crops?
ga: Afii enyiɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: With good farm practices such as pruning, weed management, and soil care, a cocoa farm can remain productive for 40 years or more, supporting a family across generations.
ga: kɛ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi kpakpai tamɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ Cocoa ŋmɔji baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Kɛtsɔ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekwɛɔ weku lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli lɛ nɔ

english: How do I ensure my cocoa farm stays healthy enough to serve as an inheritance for my family?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaafee gboshinii kɛha miweku lɛ?

english: Maintaining soil fertility, replacing aging trees, controlling pests, and protecting young saplings will keep the farm productive for several decades, making it a sustainable asset to pass down to your children.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Kɛ tsei bibii ni abuɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmɔji lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Ha ŋmɔ nɛɛ afee nibii ni hiɔ shi daa ni obaatsɔ nɔ okɛha obii kɛ obii.

english: How does a crop disease spread so fast from my neighbor's field to my own farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko gbɛ eshwa oya kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crop diseases move through air currents, water runoff, infected farm tools, insects, or even on shoes. Just like sickness spreads between people, plant pathogens spread quickly when healthy crops are nearby and exposed to wind or shared farm equipment.
ga: Tsei ahe helai tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nu ni hoɔ, okwaayeli nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ, kooloi bibii, kɛ tokotai po anɔ. Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa gbɔmɛi ateŋ lɛ hu he. Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɛŋkɛ. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ mlibotemɔ.

english: Can using dirty or chemical-polluted water make my crops die?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji loo tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ agbe miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, water contaminated with toxic chemicals, high salt levels, or harmful pathogens can poison crop roots and stop them from taking in nutrients, leading to root rot and crop failure.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni tsofai fɔji ewo mli. ŋmei ni fa babaoo Aloo, helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ awo tsei shishifãi amli ni amɛtsi amɛnaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants flowering when they are still very short and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi fɔfɔi lɛ ji kukuji ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Plants often flower early when they face severe stress like poor soil nutrients or water shortage, or if you planted a dwarf improved variety designed to produce yield quickly without growing tall.
ga: Tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi oya kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa. loo nu ni faaa Aloo kɛji odu tsei bibii ni afɔ amɛ ni afee koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii oya ni amɛdaraaa lɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects like whiteflies destroy a whole farm of cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies fiteɔ ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects act as carriers for deadly plant viruses. As they fly from plant to plant sucking sap, they transmit diseases like cassava mosaic virus, which stops leaves from feeding the crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ tsei amli helai. Beni amɛfoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ. Amɛgbɛɔ helai tamɔ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is waterlogged, which prevents roots from breathing and absorbing food even if water is plenty.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ po.

english: Should I cut off crop leaves that show strange spots or yellow marks?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, removing and burning infected leaves prevents fungal spores or bacteria from multiplying and spreading to the healthy parts of the plant or neighboring crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ ni ashãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa fungal loo bacteria spores lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ loo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I stop diseases that live in the dirt from attacking my crops every season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa be?

english: Practicing crop rotation—planting a different family of crops like legumes after cereals—starves soil-borne diseases because the pathogens cannot survive without their preferred host crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe nitsumɔ—ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii akuu kroko, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmaa sɛɛ lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa ejaakɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛji tsei ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛhi shi lɛ bɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids, or viral infections they carry, which damage the leaf structure and stop normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo hela ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ hela Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ ni sa lɛ kpaa.

english: Are short, small plant varieties better than tall ones for a good harvest?
ga: Ani tsei bibii kɛ kukuji hi fe tsei ni kwɔlɔ kɛha ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Short or dwarf crop varieties are often bred to invest their energy into producing larger fruits or seeds rather than tall stalks, and they resist falling down during heavy rains and wind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ tsei kukuji loo tsei bibii koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo awo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji fe tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ. Ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ shigbeemɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: Why do my vegetable crops drop their flowers before forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Crops drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat, insufficient water, or lack of soil nutrients, as the plant tries to save energy to survive rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why should I switch to improved rice seeds instead of using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake kɛya ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ anɔ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved rice seeds are specially bred to grow stronger, resist common crop diseases, and produce much more grain per plant, giving you a significantly bigger harvest than reused seeds.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara waa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ tso kome mli Enɛ haa onáa ŋmãa babaoo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can I plant rice on dry land, or does rice always have to grow inside standing water?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ? Aloo ani esa akɛ ŋmã akwɛ̃ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo mli be fɛɛ be?

english: You can grow rice on dry land using 'upland rice' varieties that rely on regular rainfall, while 'lowland rice' varieties are designed for fields that hold water or flood.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ‘Upland’ henɔ ni biɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. yɛ be mli ni afee ‘Flat Rice’ henɔ lɛ aha ŋmɔji ni nu loo nu afua baanyɛ aba mli lɛ.

english: How does the way I space my rice plants affect how much harvest I get at the end?
ga: Te gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajaa ŋmãa tso lɛ he lɛ saa ŋmãa ni akpaa yɛ naagbee lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting rice in neat rows with the correct distance gives every plant enough room, sunlight, and nutrients to grow large rice heads without fighting nearby plants.
ga: Omɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fɛo mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa ŋmãa tso agbo ko ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu.

english: What type of soil and land setup do I need if I want to start farming rice?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ sũ he hiaa mi kɛji miitao mabɔi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Rice grows best on flat land with clay or loamy soil that can hold water well, situated in an open area that receives full sun all day.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ loo sũ ni mli tse ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ he ko ni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ nɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me get a better yield on my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni maná yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extension officers guide you step-by-step on proper planting methods, correct fertilizer use, weed control, and how to identify and treat plant diseases early.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsɔɔ bo gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ he gbɛ kome kɛyaa gbɛ kroko nɔ. Fertilizer ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛkwɛɔ jwɛi anɔ kɛ bɔ ni afeɔ ayɔseɔ tsei ahe helai mra ni atsaa amɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young rice crop so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutua mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than rice and aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and light, which stunts your rice plants and leads to a much smaller harvest if not removed.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni amɛjuɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli hewalɛ ni la lɛ mli wa waa Enɛ haa o-rice tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni okpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa kɛji ajieee amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my rice crop needs fertilizer to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your rice plants look pale green or yellowish instead of deep green, or if they grow very slowly with thin stems, they are lacking key nutrients like nitrogen and need fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji o-rice tsei lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Aloo kɛji edaa blɛoo waa ni eyɛ tsei bibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen ni amɛhe miihia ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Rice is ready for harvest when most of the field turns a golden-yellow color and the grains at the bottom of the plant stem feel hard when you bite into them.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ babaoo feɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: What should I do right after harvesting my rice to make sure it sells for a good price?
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ afee koni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ kɛ jara kpakpa?

english: You must dry the harvested rice grains thoroughly on clean tarpaulins to prevent mold and rot, ensuring the grains don't crack when milled into white rice.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbi oŋmaa ni okpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tarpaulin ni he tse nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fãaa kɛ́ atsɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ nɔ.

english: Why is growing quality rice locally in Ghana so important compared to buying imported rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ aaadu ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ hemɔ he lɛ?

english: Growing high-quality rice locally keeps money in the community, reduces reliance on expensive foreign imports, and provides fresher rice for Ghanaian families.
ga: Omɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ haa akutso lɛ mli bii lɛ shika baa shi. Tsɔɔmɔ maŋsɛɛ nibii ni jara wa ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ hiɛnɔkamɔ. kɛ ŋmãa hee ni akɛhaa Ghana wekui.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or drowning in waterlogged soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to make leaves green and grow tall and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen loo efo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when weather temperatures get too hot or when soil water drops suddenly. Heat stress makes the plant conserve energy by shedding blossoms instead of growing fruit.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa Heat stress haa tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yɛ yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my maize producing tassels and flowers when the stalks are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔii lɛ? Ani tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: When crops face severe drought or low soil fertility early in life, they get stressed and panic. The plant flowers early to produce seeds for survival before it dries up.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni baa shi kpe yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra lɛ Amɛbaahao ni amɛbaafee gbeyei. Tsei fɔɔ mra koni amɛwo dumɔwui ni amɛhi shi dani amɛgbi.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground instead of storing starch in roots. Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients like potassium to build large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmei baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii nibii ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, he miihia cassava koni enyɛ efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help my farm soil produce better maize next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ewo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural plant food for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboi. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants grow better and yield bigger tubers when I stake the vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ mikɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up off the ground toward the sun. Leaves catch sunlight to manufacture food for the plant, and the more sunlight leaves absorb, the more food gets sent underground to expand the tuber.
ga: Staking woɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Baai mɔɔ hulu la koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Ni bɔ ni hulu la ni baa lɛ ŋmɛɔ lɛ fa ha lɛ, nakai niyenii babaoo yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, soil water, and fertilizer away from young crops. Clearing them early ensures your crop seedlings get all available nutrients so they can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛha shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil when I plant right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain can leave soil too cold or soggy, suffocating seeds without enough air. If dry weather follows immediately, seeds germinate and dry out. Planting works best when rainy conditions become steady.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi. Dumɔ nitsumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ shihilɛi lɛ yɛ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and wrinkle like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaf. The feeding damage destroys leaf structure and makes leaves warp.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Niyenii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛ baa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa.

english: Why do my ripening tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Dark spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium. Irregular watering makes it difficult for plant roots to draw up calcium from the soil.
ga: Blossom end rot, ni baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize during the major rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Maize needs steady rainfall to germinate properly. In southern and central Ghana, the major rainy season usually starts around March or April, but you should wait until the rains fall consistently for about a week before putting seeds in the ground, rather than planting right after the very first rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ March loo April aaafee. Shi esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa aaafee otsi kome dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow better during the minor rainy season than the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be bibioo lɛ mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli lɛ?
