english: The minor rainy season (around September to November) has shorter, lighter rains. Crops that mature quickly or need less water, like cowpeas, sweet potatoes, or short-duration maize varieties, thrive better during this season because they suffer less from waterlogging or heavy rains.
ga: nugbɔshiimɔ be fioo (Aaafee September kɛyashi November) nugbɔshiimɔi ni baa kuku ni baa shi waaa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ni biɔ nu fioo, tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ, loo ŋmei srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo. Ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli. Ejaakɛ amɛnaaa nu afua loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin, but producing very small ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ŋmãa toi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing your maize properly allows each plant to absorb enough nutrients to grow thick stalks and full, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso nyɛɔ enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni etoi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your cassava is short on important soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it is suffering from a drought spell or cassava mosaic disease. Adding manure or compost to your soil gives the plants the strength they need to hold healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-cassava lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo hɔmɔ loo cassava mosaic hela miipiŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛ tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my tomato farm produce plenty of flowers, but the blossoms fall off before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ŋmɔji lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when temperatures get too high, when rainfall is overly heavy, or when there are not enough beneficial insects like bees to pollinate them. Nutrient imbalances from using too much nitrogen fertilizer can also cause blossom drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ. Niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa ni jɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why is my farm producing less harvest every year even though I plant the same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ?

english: When you plant the same crop on the same piece of land year after year, it drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every time. Rotating your crops—for example, planting beans or groundnuts after maize—helps rest restoring goodness back to the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ kpakpafeemɔ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough for growing vegetables like pepper and garden eggs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil is dark brown or black, crumbles easily in your hands, holds water without staying soggy, and contains living creatures like earthworms. If your soil turns hard like concrete when dry or washes away easily during rain, it needs organic matter like animal manure or compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli Ni bɔɔ nii komɛi yɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ kɔnkrit kɛji egbi loo nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are small worms eating holes into the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a very common pest in Ghana that feeds on tender young leaves in the plant's funnel. Checking your farm early and applying recommended biological or chemical controls before the worms grow big will protect your crop from total damage.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii dani ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ kwraa he.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over before the bunches are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when heavy winds blow, especially if their roots are weakened by tiny worms called nematodes or root rot. You can protect them by propping up heavy trees with strong wooden poles and planting healthy, pest-free suckers.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii egbɔjɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ tsei ni tsii ni okɛ tsei ni wa shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why did I spend so much money on seeds and land preparation this season but still didn't make enough profit to cover my costs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ shika babaoo miisaa dumɔwui kɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ? Shi sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he lolo bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo mishika ni mifiteɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: Profit depends on yield, market timing, and post-harvest losses. If harvest yield is low due to poor spacing or weeds, or if you sell right during the peak harvest period when market prices drop, your income may not cover your input expenses. Proper planning helps align your harvest with better market prices.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ damɔ nibii ni afee lɛ nɔ. Jarayeli Be kɛ nibii ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ Kɛji ŋmaa lɛ faaa yɛ sɛɛ ni jɛkɛmɔ loo jwɛi ni ehiii hewɔ Aloo kɛji ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ naagbee be mli pɛpɛɛpɛ beni jarayeli jara lɛ baa shi lɛ. Ekolɛ shika ni onáa lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe nii. Gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni okɛ okpamɔ lɛ kɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Young cocoa trees have very delicate leaves that burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Taller trees provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the young plants until their roots are deep enough to handle full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need their leaves spread out high in the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akaje mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farmland help my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of plants that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller even when I add fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong, fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures all nutrients go directly to your crop.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya. Enɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills the spaces in the soil, preventing air from reaching the cassava roots. Without air, the tubers drown and begin to rot quickly in waterlogged earth.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Tsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Tsobii lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my tomato plants early in the morning instead of during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ nu leebi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the day's heat sets in. In the afternoon, water evaporates too quickly from hot soil, and water droplets on leaves can cause sun-scorching.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ jeɔ shishi, ni shwane mli lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu lɛ ashã mɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips hiding underneath the leaves. As they feed on the plant's juices, they cause the leaf tissue to twist and distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ Amɛbaatsɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their yellow flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air temperature is too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Extreme stress stops the flowers from turning into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Haomɔ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tomato.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow roots near the surface. When rain makes the soil soft and the fruit heavy, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ shishifãhi nɛ a mi ku we nɛ e kɛ nyu ɔ hɛ mi kpata. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni aduawai lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantain or temporary shade trees protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching, retains soil moisture, and helps the seedlings establish strong roots during their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to grow healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost around the base of the plants early in the growing season can correct this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa lɛ aná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ tso lɛ shishitoo mra yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is ready for harvesting without digging up all the roots?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa ni okɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava plants show maturity when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a tuft of leaves at the top. You will also notice the base of the stem swelling and small cracks appearing in the soil around the plant where the tubers are expanding.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni amɛshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ashiɔ baai lɛ yɛ kuu mli yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Obaayɔse akɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ efuu ni ŋmeii bibii eje kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã lɛ mli.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes in the middle whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that attacks the central leaves of young maize. Finding them early and applying recommended organic treatments or insecticidal sprays directly into the center funnel of the plant stops them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baatsɔ asraafoi ŋmeii. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Spraying your crop with neem oil solution or insecticidal soap reduces whiteflies and prevents the virus from spreading to healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni whiteflies lɛ aba shi, ni ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Will my crops produce more food if I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha niyenii babaoo aba kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil food, resulting in thin stems and small yields. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough light and nutrients to grow large, healthy fruits or tubers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa enáa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Pruning extra branches to let air and sunlight flow through the farm, removing infected pods quickly, and applying protective copper sprays helps save your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Ni okɛ akɔɔble ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua ni okɛ nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ akafite.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying out quickly during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi oya yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crop roots with dry grass, fallen leaves, or crop remnants—known as mulching—keeps moisture trapped in the ground, lowers soil temperature, and shelters roots from dry winds.
ga: Mulching ni bɔleɔ Root otsei lɛ kɛ jwɛi. Baai ni egbee shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa baa shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni okɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves into direct sunlight away from weeds. Sunlight enables the leaves to manufacture food efficiently, which the plant then sends underground to build larger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛbaawo baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ni jɛ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ aba tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, nitsumɔhe lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii.

english: Why didn't the maize seeds I stored from my last harvest germinate when I planted them this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Stored seeds can lose their ability to sprout if they absorb moisture, get too hot, or suffer damage from weevils during storage. Storing thoroughly dried seeds in airtight containers mixed with clean wood ash or approved storage dust keeps them alive and safe from insects.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji amɛmu ŋmɔtɔ, amɛdɔ tsɔ, loo ŋmeii fite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni akɛ tso sũ ni he tse loo sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ lɛ efutu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi adɛŋ.

english: Why should I bother starting my crops in a nursery first instead of just scattering the seeds directly on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbɛ dumɔwui ashwã mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Starting seeds in a nursery protects young seedlings from extreme weather and pests when they are most vulnerable. Once they grow strong roots, transplanting them into your main field leads to healthier plants and higher crop yields compared to scattering seeds directly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ amɛdu shishifãi ni wa pɛ kɛkɛ ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ooogbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Does transplanting my seedlings in neat rows actually give me a better harvest than just throwing seeds across the field?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ fɛo mli lɛ haa mináa yibiiwoo ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, transplanting in organized rows gives each crop equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients without overcrowding, which significantly improves your overall harvest compared to random scattering.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli tsɔ. Enɛ haa okpamɔ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ akɛto random scattering he.

english: How do I know if my seedlings in the nursery are ready to be transplanted into my main farm field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaawo miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings are usually ready for transplanting when they have developed three to four true leaves and a firm stem, which gives them the strength needed to survive the move into the open field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔwui krokomɛi beni dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 3-4 kɛ tso ni wa. Enɛ haa amɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves sometimes wilt right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, which happens when delicate roots get disturbed or exposed to harsh sunlight. You can prevent it by transplanting late in the afternoon and watering the plants immediately.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hao loo hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni ooodu yɛ shwane mli ni okɛ nu aha tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I broadcast chemical fertilizer across my whole field, will my crops get enough of it?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ?

english: Broadcasting chemicals across a wide area wastes a lot of the product because much of it lands on bare soil or weeds instead of reaching your crop's roots where it is needed most.
ga: Tsofai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa he ko ni da lɛ haa nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai babaoo shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ loo jwɛi anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e suɔ o tso ɔ sisi ngɛ he nɛ e he hia wawɛɛ ɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I spray too much chemical on my field at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa babaoo shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Applying too much chemical spray can burn crop leaves, harm beneficial organisms in the soil, and waste your money without providing any extra benefits to your plants.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. Eyeɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui. Ni eji shika fitemɔ ni akɛ sɛɛnamɔi krokomɛi fataaa tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Is it good practice to spray agrochemicals over empty soil where no crops are growing?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafɔ okwaayeli tsofai anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni tsei bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, spraying empty soil wastes expensive chemicals, risks polluting nearby water sources during heavy rains, and can damage soil quality over time.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsofai ni jara wa. Oshara ni yɔɔ nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli mujiwoo he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. ni ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is the best way to place fertilizer so my crops get maximum benefit without wasting money?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ awoɔ ŋmɔshi nii koni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli ni mikɛ shikatoohe lɛ akafite?

english: Applying fertilizer directly near the root base of each individual plant ensures the crop absorbs maximum nutrients quickly before rain washes the fertilizer away.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso fɛɛ tso shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo oya dani nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and produce less when I plant many seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, which stunts their growth and reduces the size of your harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋshii mli waa. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la, ni baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my main crops when I scatter seeds loosely over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ beni migbɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Scattering seeds leaves empty gaps in the soil where fast-growing weed seeds receive full sunlight and space to grow before your crops can shade them out.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ feɔ he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni jwɛi dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ naa hulu la ni fa kɛ he ni amɛdaraa dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop rolling up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is very hot. By curling, less leaf surface is exposed to the heat, helping the plant save moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, baa lɛ hiɛ shɛɛɛ hulutsoo he tsɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their leaves are delicate. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to shield them from heat while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce plenty of big green leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen manure or fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below. Balancing soil nutrients helps the plant feed its roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Without steady moisture, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji hulutsoo bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines into the air so the leaves get maximum sunlight and good airflow, which also prevents leaves from rotting on the damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni eha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ. Enɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants twisting and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by a plant virus spread by these insects. It damages the leaves and stops the plant from growing fresh fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tso mli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Efiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná aduawai heei.

english: Why am I seeing small holes on my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni muji tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the central funnel of the maize plant during the day, eating young leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like wet sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily from the roots when a little wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ eshishifãi amli oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that can be destroyed by tiny soil worms (nematodes) or stem borer insects. When pests damage the roots, the tree loses its anchor in the soil and tips over easily.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ. (nematodes) loo kooloi ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi Kɛ́ kooloi ni fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ oya ni egbee shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family. They have natural bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the next crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ ebafeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young oil palm trees turn yellow during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry seasons, oil palms slow down their growth to save water and nutrients. The plant moves stored food from older, lower leaves to nourish the fresh green leaves at the center, causing the old leaves to turn yellow.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Mu tsei lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai momoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its bright green color and build large ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli tse ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii agboi.

english: Why do farmers say that planting beans or cowpeas in the same field with my corn improves the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and lock it into the soil. When they grow alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil and make it richer for your corn without requiring as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛha oŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ŋmãa babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli.

english: Why does the rich top soil on my farm wash away down the slope whenever heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni baa nii lɛ hoɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ?

english: Bare soil left exposed to direct heavy rain gets broken apart by raindrops and swept away by flowing water. Planting crops along the ridges across the slope or leaving grass cover slows down water runoff and keeps your farm's fertile soil in place.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ashi ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsɔ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ amli ni nu lɛ baaho kɛya. Nibii ni ooodu yɛ gɔji lɛ ahe, yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ loo ni oooshi jwɛi aha nɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eye ebua ni oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants die when I clear all the big trees away from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate full direct sunlight or harsh dry winds. Leaving some large shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cool, moist environment that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ naa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni aaashi loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ baaha shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ buɔ cacao bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot under the ground when the rainy season stays longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays trapped in the soil without proper drainage, it drowns the roots and creates the wet conditions that rot-causing microbes love.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni nibii bibii ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ sumɔɔ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or water is erratic, the tomato plant gets stressed and drops its blossoms to save its own strength. Providing regular watering at the root level and slight midday shade helps the flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ ni amɛbaagbee shi bɔni afee ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛná hewalɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ he daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ shwane mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes right inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, hidden growing point at the center of young corn leaves. Checking fields early and applying neem leaf extract or recommended control measures directly into the leaf center stops them before they ruin the growing shoot.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛkwɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ he lɛ mra ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ekpaa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, light bunches when many shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: All the extra shoots, called suckers, share the same root system and drink the water and nutrients meant for the mother plant. Pruning away the weaker suckers and leaving only one or two main shoots gives the plant enough energy to yield heavy bunches.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi fɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, jaa shishifã kome ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛhaa fɔlɔ tso lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ amli ni ashi tso lɛ shishifã titri kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo niji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to give my yam vines wooden tall stakes to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to swell the tuber under the ground. Staking also keeps the foliage away from hot soil and wet leaves that cause fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Staking hu haa baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ baai ni efɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ he.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my own harvest last year fail to sprout as well as new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ ni amɛwooo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength if they absorb air moisture during storage or if they come from high-yield hybrid varieties that are only meant to be planted once. Stored seeds must be kept completely dry, cool, and protected from insects to stay alive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli kɛji amɛjie kɔɔyɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ejɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni esa akɛ adu shikome pɛ mli. Esa akɛ aha dumɔwui ni ato lɛ agbi kwraa, amɛhe ejɔ, ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ koolooi ahe koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my crops taking so much longer to mature than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops often take longer to grow when the soil lacks essential nutrients or when local seeds are used instead of improved, fast-maturing varieties that are bred to grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ akɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui tsu nii yɛ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe, ni shwereɔ mra ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛdara oya lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do crops planted on newly cleared land grow faster than crops on land I have farmed for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu nɔ afii babaoo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Newly cleared land has rich topsoil packed with natural organic matter and unused nutrients, whereas old farmland loses its natural nutrients over time from continuous cropping.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni eyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛtsuuu nii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, okwaayeli shikpɔji ni etsɛ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ daa lɛ mli.

english: What is the benefit of visiting a local demonstration farm before I plant my own field?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko ni akɛtsɔɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ saramɔ he dani okɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ otsei lɛ atsu nii?

english: Demonstration farms let you see correct plant spacing, proper fertilizer application, and modern field management in practice so you can apply proven techniques on your own farm without guessing.
ga: Demo ŋmɔ lɛ haa onaa tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ tsuɔ nii No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ ŋaai ni ana he odaseyeli atsu nii yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ jwɛŋmɔ ni ejaaa tsuuu nii.

english: Why do crops on agricultural demonstration farms look much healthier than crops on regular farms in my community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ okwaayeli he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ daa ŋmɔji amli yɛ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Demonstration farms use tested high-yield seeds, precise spacing to prevent crowding, and balanced soil nutrients, which prevents common diseases and produces greener, stronger plants.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo tsuɔ nii. He ni ato pɛpɛɛpɛ koni akafee nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ naa ni ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni he wa lɛ baa.

english: How do I know if my land is big enough to make a good profit from growing food crops in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ maná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa kɛjɛ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: While small plots can feed a family, commercial success usually requires larger land—around 2 to 5 acres or more—to produce enough yield to cover your costs for seeds, labor, and transport to major market centers like Kumasi.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ bibioo ko po baanyɛ akwɛ weku ko Shi bei pii lɛ, jarayeli mli omanyeyeli biɔ shikpɔji wuji, ni ji acre 2 kɛyashi 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Koni afee nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha awo dumɔwui, nitsumɔ kɛ gbɛfaa kɛmiiya jarayeli hei wuji tamɔ Kumasi he nyɔmɔ.

english: Why should I keep my most fertile land for major cash crops rather than letting others use it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ kɛha shika ŋmɔshi nibii wuji akwɛmɔ moŋ fe ni mahã mɛi krokomɛi kɛtsu nii?

english: High-value cash crops require deep, rich soil to produce maximum yield, so saving your best land ensures your biggest agricultural investment yields the highest financial return.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii koni ená yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okɛtoɔ lɛ haa shika ni okɛwoɔ okwaayeli mli ni da fe fɛɛ lɛ baaha oná shika babaoo fe fɛɛ.

english: Is it better to farm one crop on my entire large piece of land or divide the land for different crops?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ wulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ? Aloo aja shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi?

english: Dividing your land for different crops protects you from total loss if a pest attacks one crop type, and it keeps your soil healthy by balancing how nutrients are used.
ga: He ni ajaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kwraa he kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua ŋmɔshi nibii kome. ni eye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ bɔ ni okɛ niyenii mli nibii tsuɔ nii ohaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is a short drought during the growing season in Kumasi?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hɔmɔ ba yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ Kumasi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant cannot draw nitrogen from dry soil, because crops need water to absorb nutrients through their roots and carry them to the leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei hia nu koni amɛ gbɔmɔ niyenii kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛkɛya baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops shed their flowers without forming any fruit when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause plants to drop their flowers to save moisture and energy, protecting the main plant from dying rather than growing new fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he. Buu tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbo moŋ fe ni ooowo yibii heei.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that adapt quickly to local weather and compete aggressively with crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients as soon as rain falls.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni tsakeɔ ehe oya kɛyaa jɛmɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to absorb food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli obɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves with yellowish patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or spread when you plant cuttings taken from diseased plants.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Amɛji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni woɔ amɛ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛ́ ofo ŋmeii ni ajie kɛjɛ tso ko ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off the stem without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant lacks steady water, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to grow foliage instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu daa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing thin and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ mli tse ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become thin or deformed when planted in hard, compacted soil or stony ground that prevents the tubers from expanding freely underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo loo amɛfiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide temporary shade and moisture to help the cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upwards to reach light rather than spreading out to bear fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ la lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ eshwa koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Ragged holes inside the central leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the plant's growing tip and chew through fresh leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why does striga weed keep growing right next to the roots of my maize and sorghum?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi lɛ miida yɛ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Striga, or witchweed, is a parasite that attaches directly to the roots of cereal crops to steal their water and nutrients, and it thrives mostly in tired, low-nutrient soils.
ga: Striga loo Witchweed ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmaa tsei ashishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju amɛnu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ni amɛshwereɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni etɔ, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ofee klalo akɛ obaafo ŋmei shishifãi lɛ?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the stems become thick and woody, and cracks appear in the soil near the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei. ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to powder and get small holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powder ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: The holes and powder are caused by grain weevils, which lay eggs inside dry maize kernels and eat the grain from the inside if it was not dried completely or treated before storage.
ga: Bu kɛ sũ jɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli lɛ amli. Ni oye dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛji egbiko kwraa loo atsuuu he nii dani akɛto.

english: How can I spray weedkiller on my farm without damaging my young onion plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mashɛre tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni mifiteee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Onions have thin, waxy leaves that can absorb chemicals easily if applied incorrectly. Using selective weedkillers designed specifically for onions and spraying in the cool early morning when there is no wind keeps the chemical on the weeds and off the crop.
ga: Sabolai yɛ baai bibii ni tamɔ wax. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai oya kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi ni ahala ni afee aha ŋmeii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ni okɛshwie nɔ yɛ fɛ̃i mli leebi maŋkpa beni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsofai lɛ ahi jwɛi lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to spray farm chemicals when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Strong midday sun makes liquid chemicals evaporate too fast and creates heat spots on wet leaves, which burns the crop. Hot weather also stresses the plant, making it harder for the crop to recover from chemical contact.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. ni efee hei ni mli edɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaatsake amɛhe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ amli.

english: Why should I wait a few days after clearing weeds before I apply chemical sprays to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ gbii fioo komɛi beni ajie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ dani mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ atsu nii?

english: Hand-weeding or using a hoe creates tiny cuts on your crop's roots and leaves. Giving the plants a few days allows these wounds to heal so the spray doesn't enter the plant and cause chemical burn.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nine loo ŋmei shwie jwɛi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ feɔ pilamɔi bibii. Kɛ́ oshi tso lɛ gbii fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni pilamɔi nɛɛ atsa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ eyaaa tso lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsofa shãa tso lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crop actually needs fertilizer to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia mi diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your plant leaves look pale green or yellowish instead of deep green, or if growth has slowed down, the soil is lacking nutrients. Fertilizer acts as food, giving plants nitrogen and other minerals to grow strong leaves and large stems.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. aloo kɛji akɛ dalɛ ba shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii. Ehaa nitrogen kɛ mineral krokomɛi haa tsei koni amɛfee baai ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji

english: Will giving my crops too much fertilizer at one time make them grow faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tsei amli shikome lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara oya?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer at once can burn the plant's roots like hot salt, drying them out and turning the leaf tips brown. It is better to apply smaller amounts of fertilizer in stages as the crop grows.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, tamɔ ŋoo ni mli edɔ, ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli fioo fioo yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Be ni tsei lɛ daraa

english: Does heavy rain wash away the fertilizer I put on my field?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ kɛya?

english: Yes, heavy rainfall can wash away fertilizer that is left sitting on top of dry soil before the roots can take it in. Covering fertilizer with a little soil near the base of the plant protects it from being washed away.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ fioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekaho.

english: When is the best stage in an onion plant's life to give it fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ sabala tso ko shihilɛ mli ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Onions need fertilizer early when they are building green leaves, because leafy plants store the energy needed later. Once the bulb starts swelling under the ground, reduce nitrogen fertilizer so energy goes into the bulb instead of more leaves.
ga: Sabala he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii mra. Beni ebɔɔ baai eŋɔli Ejaakɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ baato hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha sɛɛ mli lɛ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ Tsi nitrogen ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shi koni akɛ hewalɛ babaoo awo ŋmeii lɛ amli moŋ fe ni akɛ ŋmeii babaoo baafata he.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crop leaves to look weak and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow aggressively, they steal the plant food first, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli klɛŋklɛŋ. Shi oŋmɔshi nii lɛ hɔmɔ kɛ shweremɔ.

english: How does an onion plant actually form a bulb under the ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni onion bulbs lɛ feɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: The green leaves above ground capture sunlight to make food. The plant sends this food down to the base of the stem, causing the leaf layers underground to swell and form the onion bulb.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la lɛ koni ekɛhoo niyenii. Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii nɛɛ baa shi kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi baa lɛ mli fũuɔ ni efeɔ onion bulbs.

english: Why do the tips of my crop leaves start turning yellow or brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf tips turn brown when the plant is under stress. This usually happens from lack of water in the soil, nutrient shortages, or burn caused by improper fertilizer or chemical application.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɔfo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo shãa ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli baa.

english: Why should I buy specific types of certified maize seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred to resist local pests, diseases, and dry spells, giving you a bigger harvest. Saved seeds from past harvests lose their strength over time, resulting in weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai kɛ hɔmɔ. Ehaa okpaa nibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: How do I know the right amount of bean seeds to put in one hole so they do not choke each other?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmeii abɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛwo bu kome mli? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akakpɛtɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting 2 to 3 bean seeds per hole gives each stem enough space to spread its roots and leaves. Planting too many seeds in one spot makes them fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and fewer pods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwa. Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: How do groundnuts produce nuts under the dirt when their flowers grow above the ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi beni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant grows long stalks called pegs that bend down and push themselves into the soil. Once underground, the tips of these pegs swell up to form the groundnut pods.
ga: Beni ajie ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tsei yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛji akɛ eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Pin lɛ naagbee lɛ baafu aahu kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmei ŋmei.

english: Why are some of my corn cobs missing seeds at the tip when I peel back the husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa yɛ naagbee beni mifoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Missing seeds on a cob happen when the silky threads at the top do not catch enough pollen from the tassels, often caused by dry weather, high heat, or planting corn stalks too far apart from each other.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ siliki kpãai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo ŋmãa tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my bean plants turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the bean plant is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, is receiving too much or too little water, or is being attacked by sap-sucking insects like aphids.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bean tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo fioo tsɔ. loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my tall maize stalks fall over easily whenever there is a moderate wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fioo mli?

english: Maize stalks fall over when they are planted too close together, forcing them to grow tall and thin instead of strong. Weak root systems and lack of soil heaped around the stem base also make them fall easily.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ shwilafoi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee hewalɛ. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni abua naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ hu haa efoɔ oya.

english: Why do my maize plants grow better in the soil where I planted beans during the previous season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the beans are harvested, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as free fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmeii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmeii krokomɛi.

english: Can I plant groundnuts and maize together on the same land, or will one ruin the other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo mɔ kome baakpata mɔ kroko hiɛ?

english: You can plant them together safely. Maize grows tall to catch sunlight at the top, while groundnuts grow low to shade the soil, keep moisture in the ground, and add nitrogen that helps the maize grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome shweshweeshwe. Abɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shi fioo koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hulutsoo. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha nitrogen ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to be pulled out of the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Pull up a few sample plants and crack open some pods. If the inside of the shell has darkened slightly and the nuts fit tightly inside the skin, your groundnuts are ready for harvest.
ga: Gbalamɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ fioo ni ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ efo ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I keep planting groundnuts on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts in the same spot year after year allows groundnut-specific pests and fungal diseases to build up in the soil, which reduces your harvest over time even if you add extra nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmaa lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii krokomɛi fata he po.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the food plants need to grow green and strong. Applying a balanced fertilizer like NPK or adding well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nitrogen your maize needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo okɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha o-ŋmãa he hiamɔ nii.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes, which means they can pull natural fertilizer from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside maize, they feed the soil with nitrogen, making the soil richer for your maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Amɛkɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves end up filled with small holes and tiny green caterpillars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmei bibioo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ hu?

english: Those holes are caused by caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae that eat the leaves to grow. Spraying your farm early with neem leaf extract or an approved insect spray kills these caterpillars before they ruin your whole crop.
ga: Buji nɛɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii, tamɔ diamondback moth larvae, ni yeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ. Okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ baagbe nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Yam rot is caused by fungi or tiny worms in wet, waterlogged soil, or from using already infected seed yams. Planting in well-drained soil mounds and selecting clean seed yams keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Fung loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛ sweet potato ni fiteɔ baa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu ehi shi loo kɛjɛ yams ni ehiɛ dumɔwui momo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛ sweet potatoes ni he tse ni ahalaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my farmland soil become hard and cracked during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil cracks when it lacks organic matter like dry leaves and compost to hold moisture inside. Leaving crop residues or spreading mulch over the ground protects the soil from direct sun and keeps it soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fãa kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni efee blɛoo.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my crop seeds after the major rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground gets two or three heavy rains that thoroughly wet the soil deep down. Planting too early after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a short dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ, ni no baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba.

english: Why do you advise us not to plant cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ owoɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkadu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ wɔhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives the roots enough room in the soil to expand into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I clear weeds early when my cassava stems have just sprouted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ mra? Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ kɛkɛ?

english: Young cassava plants grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures the young plants get all the sunshine and soil food they need to grow strong roots.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara waa.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops on raised earth ridges or on flat ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Raised ridges are best for heavy soils or rainy areas because they keep roots out of standing water and make harvesting root crops easier. Flat ground works better in dry, sandy areas where holding onto water is most important.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔji ni tsii loo hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhaa shishifãi lɛ shɛɛɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ he. ni ehaa shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo Flat bottoms tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni egbi, ni ŋã yɔɔ ni nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I prune my farm trees differently if I want fruits instead of timber?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ miitao aduawai yɛ tso najiaŋ hu?

english: Timber trees need to grow tall, straight, and branch-free to make strong wood, while crop trees need low, spreading branches so they can hold more fruit and make harvesting easier for you.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni akɛ tsei tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni kwɔlɔ, ni ja, ni niji bɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo tsei ni wa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni adu lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛná tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shwereɔ koni amɛhiɛ aduawai babaoo ni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ afee mlɛo aha bo.

english: Will cutting branches off my young crop trees hurt them or help them yield more?
ga: Ani mitsei bibii lɛ ni mikɛbaakpa lɛ baaye amɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Proper pruning actually helps your crop tree produce more. By removing extra branches, the tree directs its energy into growing stronger fruit-bearing branches rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ ni oookpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa otso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa niji ni woɔ yibii ni mli wa. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: I am afraid that pruning my tree might kill it, is that true?
ga: Gbeyee ni sheɔ akɛ tso lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baanyɛ agbe lɛ, ani eji anɔkwale?

english: It is normal to be cautious, but pruning does not kill a healthy tree if you use sharp, clean tools. Trees recover quickly and will bounce back with stronger growth.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ wɔɔkwɛ wɔhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi tso ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ egbeŋ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsu nii. Tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ oya ni ebaaku esɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to make my crop tree form a wide shape with many side branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi tsei lɛ afee shɔŋŋ ni amɛhiɛ niji babaoo lɛ?

english: A wide canopy allows the leaves to catch more sunlight and air, which gives the tree the strength it needs to produce plenty of flowers and fruits.
ga: Kpoji ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibii babaoo.

english: How many days will it take for me to see new shoots emerging at the base of my tree?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mana ŋmeii heei yɛ mitso lɛ shishi?

english: Depending on the tree type and soil moisture, you will usually start seeing new shoots or suckers popping up at the base within 14 to 30 days after planting or pruning.
ga: Edamɔ tso lɛ henɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ obaaje shishi ona ŋmeii heei loo ŋmeii ni miije kpo kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ yɛ gbii 14 kɛyashi 30 mli yɛ be mli ni adu loo afo mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What should I do if I see small stems growing out at the very bottom of my main tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina ŋmeii bibii? Ekwɛ̃ yɛ mitso titri lɛ shishi.

english: These bottom growth stems are called suckers. You should cut them off early so they do not steal water and food away from the main trunk where your crops grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Esa akɛ ofo mli mra. Enɛ baaha amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are some of my trees developing good branches while others stay weak around the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi miitswa niji jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu bɛ hewalɛ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Trees grow differently based on sunlight, soil quality, and weed competition. Clearing weeds and adding manure around the weaker trees will help them develop strong branches.
ga: Tsei baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ jwɛi akaŋshii naa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aná niji ni mli wa.

english: How many workers or team members do I need to help me prune my tree farm properly?
ga: Nitsulɔi loo kuu mli bii enyiɛ he baahia mi koni amɛye amɛbua mi ni mafolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: For a standard one-acre tree farm, two to three trained farm hands can usually complete all the pruning work safely within one to two days.
ga: Kɛha tso ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre kome ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni atsɔse amɛ lɛ baanyɛ afo tsei lɛ aniji lɛ fɛɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ gbi kome kɛyashi gbii enyɔ mli.

english: How do I train my timber trees to grow straight and tall without wide branches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔse tso ni akɛ tso fee lɛ koni efee ja ni ekwɛ ni niji ni mli kwɔ bɛ he?

english: For timber trees, you regularly remove the side branches while the tree is young so that all its growth energy goes straight up into building a long, clean trunk.
ga: Kɛha tsei ni ji tsei lɛ Ehe baahia ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ daa be mli ni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni haa mɔ daa lɛ atsu nii kɛya ŋmeii kakadaji ni he tse lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to trim my tree branches for the best response?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji koni maná hetoo ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: The best time to trim branches is usually at the start of the rainy season or right after harvesting, so the rain helps the tree recover quickly and sprout new growth.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afo tso lɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee loo kpamɔ sɛɛ, no hewɔ lɛ nugbɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi oya ni ekwɛ̃ɔ tsei heei.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods as a natural way to save water, just like shedding extra clothes in hot weather. When the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue growing its tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ nu hɔmɔ be mli, ni eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Nakai eji yɛ atadei ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Pepper leaves curl during intense afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing water loss. If the leaves unfold again in the cooler evening, the plant is healthy and simply protecting itself from heat stress.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsi nu ni laajeɔ lɛ naa Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures are extremely high or when soil moisture fluctuates too much. Consistent watering and light mulch help keep the soil cool and prevent flower loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its green color and yield healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my yam vine growing lots of bushy leaves but producing only tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi ejieɔ tuber bibioo ko pɛ?

english: When yams receive too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of food underground. Balanced soil nutrients ensure the plant develops larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Beni sweet potatoes nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa, ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings grow thin and weak when kept in a very dark nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ waa lɛ?

english: Seedlings need filtered sunlight to build strong stems. If a nursery is too dark, the seedlings stretch upward rapidly searching for light, leaving them tall, weak, and easy to snap when transplanted.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni mli tse koni amɛfee tsei ni wa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛtao la. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ, amɛkuɔ oya.

english: Why are weeds slowing down my maize growth even when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi-abele lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with maize for nutrients, root space, and light. Even with plenty of rain, weeds will consume the soil's nutrients before your maize roots can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ la, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Jwɛi hu yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves have so many small holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baa lɛ mli buji bibii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by tiny caterpillars or insects feeding on them. Checking under the leaves early in the morning and using natural sprays like neem oil helps protect the crop.
