ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ripe and ready to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can check maturity by pulling up a couple of sample plants and opening the pods. If the inside of the shell has dark vein markings and the nut skins are firm and fully colored, the groundnuts are ready to harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni oootsi kɛya ŋwɛi ni ogbele amɛmli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ nii ni ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ sui. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: How do I know if my farmland has good soil for planting new cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni mikɛduɔ kookoo tsei heei?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, soft, loamy soil that allows roots to go deep and drains water easily. If water sits on top of your land like a pond for days after rain, the roots will rot and the trees will not grow well.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ he hiaa amɛ. Kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nubu gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni tso lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree take so many years to start producing its first pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mi cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties naturally take 4 to 5 years to bear fruit, but newer hybrid varieties can start producing in 2 to 3 years if they get enough shade, water, and rich soil nutrients early on.
ga: Kusum mli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani ewoɔ yibii, shi henɔi heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ Ebaabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji ená hulutsoo, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off instead of turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or when there are no tiny midges (insects) around to pollinate them. Keeping shade trees and moist soil helps flowers set into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha tso lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my tree growing small and flat instead of round and full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee kokroo ni amɛyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Small or deformed pods happen when the tree lacks key nutrients like potassium or when the tree is trying to feed too many pods with too little water in the soil.
ga: Pods bibii loo ni ehiii lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ potassium, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu fioo pɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aha epods lɛ niyenii fe nine.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn under direct sunlight and hot winds. They need temporary shade, like plantain trees planted next to them, to keep them cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hɔɔŋ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni eha edɔ ni edɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during heavy rains and cool, damp weather. Clearing tall weeds and pruning excess branches lets sunlight in to keep the pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ. Jwɛi kakadaji ni ajieɔ kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: What is causing dark spots on my cocoa stems and making the branches die back?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ehaa tso lɛ nine lɛ gboɔ?

english: This is usually caused by small pests called mirids or capsids that suck sap from young shoots and pods. Spraying approved treatments at the start of the dry season helps protect the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo capsids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why is green moss growing all over the trunk of my cocoa trees, and will it kill them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii eŋɔli ebɔle mi-kookoo tso lɛ he fɛɛ lɛ? Ni ani ebaagbe amɛ?

english: Moss grows when your farm is too damp and dark due to overgrown trees. Moss itself does not eat the tree, but it holds moisture against the bark where plant diseases can easily grow.
ga: Moss daa be mli ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ duŋ yɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ahewɔ. Mos lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yeee tso lɛ. Shi emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ yibii amli he ni tsei ahe helai baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over before the food bunches are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani ŋtayaai lɛ afee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be eaten by tiny worms in the soil called nematodes or weak stems attacked by borers. Supporting the plants with strong wooden stakes helps keep them standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii bibii ni borers boteɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent your leaves from curling and losing yield.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛji woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden sticks to stake my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei kakadaji koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch plenty of sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant grow much bigger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ bulbs ni da fe tsutsu lɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds once the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays wet for several days. Planting after just one light shower can cause your seeds to sprout and then die when the sun dries the soil out again.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii babaoo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome nɛɛ pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi be mli ni hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen nutrients in the soil, or the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding animal manure or the right fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on top of raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when plants suffer from lack of water, or when tiny pests attack the flowers. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so tomatoes can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni tomatoi lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from under the leaves. Protecting the young leaves from these insects allows the plant to expand its leaves and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ abu tso lɛ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ebaa lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot year after year drains all the specific food maize needs from the soil and lets maize pests multiply. Rotating with crops like groundnuts gives the soil a rest and starves the pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ abɛi niyenii he hiamɔ nii fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni hɔmɔ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your crops. When weeds share the field, your crops get less nourishment, making them stay small and produce fewer fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji akɛ aja jwɛi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná niyenii fioo. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛwooo aduawai loo ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap plant food directly from the air and store it in the earth. When the season ends, this natural food stays in the ground to help the next crop grow strong.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa saplings turn yellow and scorch in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and hot, dry air. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a cooler environment with soft light, protecting their tender leaves until their roots grow deep enough to survive harsh weather.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni kane ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why are small worms hiding inside the leaves of my young maize plants and chewing hole patterns in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai amli ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana. They crawl deep inside the central shoot funnel of the maize plant to eat soft leaves, which can severely stunt or kill the crop if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛshwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsu nii yɛ yiwalɛ gbɛ nɔ loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many green leaves but produces tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are overcrowded, cassava spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of roots. The plant needs proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients to direct energy into storing starch in the tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ yɛ babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná he ko ni sa kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni sa koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small, hard cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni ebafeɔ nɔ ni wa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects that distorts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, which is usually caused by dry weather or irregular watering that prevents roots from absorbing minerals properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be ni haaa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ minerals lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems holding a very heavy bunch of fruit. If planted shallowly, or if root-damaging pests like nematodes weaken the roots, the plant easily topples over under heavy weight and rain.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hiɛɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, tamɔ nematodes lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Tsei shwieɔ shi oya yɛ muji ni tsii kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shishi.

english: Why do my cut seed yams rot in the ground before sprouting into healthy vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mifo lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbatsɔ wain tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot when planted in waterlogged soil or when cut pieces are not allowed to heal and dry before planting. Soil fungi and bacteria enter open wounds on the seed piece and destroy it before roots and shoots form.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ agbi ni amɛgbi dani adu. Fungi kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ pilamɔ ni agbele yɛ dumɔwu lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfiteɔ dani shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Will planting three maize seeds in the same hole give me a bigger yield at harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmãa 3 ni adu yɛ bu kome mli lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: No, planting multiple seeds close together makes plants fight intensely for light, water, and soil nutrients. This produces thin, weak stalks with tiny or empty cobs compared to planting single seeds spaced properly.
ga: Dabi Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ waa koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ ni amɛhe afee mlɛo ni amɛná dumɔwui bibii bibii. loo efolo Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui komekomei ni aduɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly against the main stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem causes chemical burns that can rot the plant's skin and kill it. Fertilizer should be placed a short distance away where the outer feeder roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ashã tso lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ hewolo lɛ agbo ni egbo. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛɛɛ. ni kponɔgbɛ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my maize crop grow stronger when I plant it where groundnuts grew last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa waa kɛ́ midu yɛ he ni adu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When groundnut roots rot naturally in the soil, they release this nitrogen, providing free food for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen kpo. koni efee niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni akɛhaa kooloi lɛ

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant plantains on the same land as young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wɔduɔ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from excessive heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Will planting plantains alongside my cocoa steal all the nutrients from the soil and ruin my cocoa yield?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-kooko lɛ masɛi lɛ baaju niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ebaafite mi-kooko lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: When spaced properly, plantains and young cocoa feed at different soil depths. Furthermore, plantain leaves that fall off decompose naturally, enriching the soil with nutrients that actually help the cocoa grow.
ga: Beni jɛkɛmɔ lɛ sa Dumɔwui kɛ cacao tsei bibii yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ srɔtoi anɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, plantain baai ni egbee shi lɛ baafite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: What happens to a cocoa tree if it stays under complete shade for its entire life?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo tso nɔ kɛji ehi hulutsoo be mli ewala be fɛɛ mli?

english: While young cocoa trees need heavy shade, mature cocoa trees need balanced sunlight to produce plenty of flowers and pods. Keeping full shade forever leads to low harvest yields and increases fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa. Kakao tso ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni sa koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Shade ni yeɔ emuu ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: How do plantain plants react when the weather gets extremely hot and dry?
ga: Te dumɔwui feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli?

english: During hot and dry spells, plantain leaves will turn yellow, roll inward, and drop lower down the stem to conserve water, which slows down growth and leads to smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Plantain baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. shwieɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ shishi koni ekɛ nu ato Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi ni ehaa aduawai bibii baa.

english: How does growing broad-leaf plants like plantain help me control weeds on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ baai babaoo tamɔ plantains ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Broad plantain leaves create a heavy shade over the ground. This canopy prevents sunlight from reaching the soil, naturally preventing troublesome weeds and grasses from sprouting.
ga: Plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋwɛitsu nɛɛ haaa hulu la lɛ ayashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ naagba lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does a single plantain plant produce so many shoots around its base, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain kome yɛ suckers babaoo ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, ni esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: Plantain plants multiply underground by growing shoots called suckers. If you leave all of them to grow, they compete for nutrients and produce small bunches, so you should prune them, keeping only one or two strong suckers.
ga: Dumɔwui shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oha amɛdara Ebaatswa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ, ni okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my plantain bunches turning out small even though the mother plant looks tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛlɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Small bunches occur when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium during the flowering stage, or when too many suckers are fighting the mother plant for food and water.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ miiwu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up starting from the lower leaves going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This pattern usually signals either a lack of nutrients in the soil, natural aging of older leaves, or a fungal leaf disease that thrives during humid and wet conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Adebɔɔ mli baa momo dalɛ loo fungal baa helai ni daa yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli

english: How can planting plantain alongside long-term crops help my household finances?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baadu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishia lɛ shika helɛtemɔ?

english: Cash crops like cocoa take three or four years to bear fruit, but plantains yield within twelve months. Planting both allows you to harvest and sell plantains for continuous income while waiting for your cocoa to mature.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo heɔ afii etɛ loo ejwɛ dani ewoɔ yibii. Shi dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii yɛ nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, onyɛɔ okpaa plantains ni ohɔ̃ɔ koni onine ashɛ shika ni yaa nɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is plantain usually so abundant in the market during the main cocoa planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains babaoo yɔɔ jara nɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many farmers plant plantains at the same time to nurse their new cocoa farms. As a result, large quantities of plantain mature simultaneously across farming communities, making them plentiful in regional markets.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo du dumɔwui yɛ be kome mli koni amɛkɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmɔji heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome yɛ okwaayeli akutsei amli. Enɛ haa efeɔ babaoo yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when there are no plantain trees grown next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni aduko dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight during their first years. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide necessary shade and keep the soil cool and moist, acting as protective umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmei nine miiwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You need to look at the small buds or nodes along the cassava stem where leaves used to grow. These tiny nodes should point upwards toward the sky; planting them facing downward makes it difficult for roots and shoots to sprout, causing weak growth or crop failure.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii. Yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ, esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ewaa akɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and stake my yam vines off the ground with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei shwieɔ jwɛi ni mikɛduɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach light. Elevating the leaves on stakes allows them to trap maximum sunlight for energy while keeping foliage away from wet soil, which prevents fungal diseases and leads to larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baakwɔ kɛyashɛ adebɔɔ mli la he. Kɛ́ awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off before the corn is fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant starves and draws remaining nutrients from its oldest leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni ebaagbala niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ebaa ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting groundnut or cowpea makes my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnut and cowpea have natural nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When these crops finish growing, they leave extra plant food in the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gbe amɛkwɛ̃ naa Amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the earth when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season warms up the dry ground without soaking it deeply. Planting too early traps seeds in hot, muddy soil, causing them to heat up and rot from fungal infections before they can properly germinate.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ adɔ ni ekɛ nu shwieee nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ baamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ muji mli. Enɛ haa edɔɔ ni egboɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko mli dani ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants dropping off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato and pepper flowers fall off when the air temperature becomes too hot or when soil water levels change abruptly. Extreme heat or lack of consistent water stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato kɛ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake trukaa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ daa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, thin bunches of fruit when many shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: When extra shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain trunk, they steal water and nutrients from the soil. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only two or three main stems, ensuring all plant food goes toward making thick, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii krokomɛi (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tsei titrii fioo komɛi pɛ. Enɛ haa tso niyenii lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my green pepper plants curling up into tight shapes and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso ni eŋɔli lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are caused by tiny, invisible insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves to suck out sap. Their feeding damages the leaf tissue, causing leaves to twist, harden, and stunt the plant's overall growth.
ga: Kplukai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai ashishi koni ekɛnu nu. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji, ni ehaa baa lɛ tsɔɔ, ewaa, ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why do I find large holes eaten out of my cabbage leaves even though I do not see insects on them during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji wuji yɛ kaabii ni miyeɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Ni onaaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Many leaf-eating pests, like armyworms and caterpillars, hide under soil clods or leaf litter during the day to stay cool and escape birds. They emerge at night when it is cool to eat the cabbage leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kooloi ni yeɔ baai babaoo ahe ji cutworms kɛ caterpillars. Okɛ ohe awo muji loo baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ashishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni ohe afee fɛ̃i ni okɛ ohe akabɔ okpoi ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ koni amɛye kaabii baai.

english: If I do not apply manure or fertilizer to my plantain farm, will the trees still yield big fruits?
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔtɔ fataaa he Ani tso lɛ baawo yibii wuji lolo?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that need lots of nutrients like nitrogen and potassium. Without feeding the soil, the plantain trees will grow weak and produce very small bunches with thin fruits.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. Kɛji okɛ niyenii haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ aduawai ni mli tseee.

english: Is it helpful to leave dry leaves and crop waste on the ground around my plantain trees?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mashi baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-plantain lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, leaving organic materials around the base creates a mulch layer that traps soil moisture, keeps roots cool, and breaks down into natural food for the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ashiɔ yɛ Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni egbɛɔ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ

english: Why do my crops stop producing good yields when I plant on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ yibii kpakpai kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Crops continuously pull nutrients from the earth as they grow. If you farm the same spot repeatedly without adding organic manure or fertilizer, the soil becomes empty of food and crops can no longer thrive.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji otsu okwaayeli yɛ he kome shii abɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ Niyenii baaho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the young shoots growing around my main plantain stem producing very small bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mitso titri lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii waa?

english: When too many young shoots grow around one parent tree, they steal water and nutrients from each other. Pruning extra shoots and keeping only two or three strong ones allows the remaining plants to get enough food to yield large bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ nyɛ kome tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ajie tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when fruit starts to grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are made of soft water-filled layers rather than solid wood, making them weak. When soil nutrition is poor or roots are shallow, the weight of the fruit pulls the tree down, so farmers use wooden prop sticks for support.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ feɔ plantain tsei lɛ, shi jeee tsei ni wa. debilitating Kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ gbalaa tso lɛ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtswaa okwaayeli tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees turn yellow and dry up before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Premature yellowing often means the plant lacks water or essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or it is affected by leaf spot disease. Cutting off infected leaves helps air flow and keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo hela ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ emɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees grow very tall and thin when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too close, plantains compete for sunlight and stretch upwards as fast as possible. This makes them slender and weak, so proper spacing is needed for sturdy stems and heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Plantains lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ekɛ ehe baawo ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni aná gbɛ ni sa kɛha tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni wa kɛ tsei akui ni tsii.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest plantains so they do not spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantains koni amɛkafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantains should be harvested when the individual fruits look full and rounded instead of sharp and flat-sided, but while the outer peel is still completely green.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa plantains be mli ni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛibɔfoi. Yɛ fãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ Shi yɛ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ ji eŋɔli kwraa lolo lɛ.

english: Why do some fingers on my plantain bunch grow big while the rest stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ mi banana tso lɛ nɔ lɛ dara waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: Uneven finger growth happens when the tree runs low on food and water while developing the bunch. The top fruits consume most of the available nutrients first, leaving very little for the bottom ones.
ga: Nine ni dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji niyenii kɛ nu faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli beni ekɛ niji shwieɔ shi lɛ. Yibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ. Eshiɔ nɔ ko fioo pɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and turn soft faster than I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpaa lɛ miikwɛ̃ ni efee blɛoo oya fe bɔ ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Once cut from the tree, plantains naturally release a ripening gas. Storing harvested bunches in a hot or sunny place speeds up this gas, while keeping them in a cool, shady spot slows down ripening.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Plantains lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa amɛshwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni edɔɔ loo hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaha gas nɛɛ aya oya. Yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight. Big trees provide shade and keep the soil cool and moist, acting like a natural shield while the cocoa plants build strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tso lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Yam plants produce tubers underground by catching sunlight with their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing leaf rot and helping the crop store energy into bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ ŋmɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ sweet potatoes wuji amli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves from the bottom up are usually a signal that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is food for the plant. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores the green leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do elders say planting beans or groundnuts in the same farm with maize improves the crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, naturalizing fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting instead of spreading wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa babaoo lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves, sucking out the juice and transmitting plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsei ahe helai ni fiteɔ amɛdalɛ lɛ yaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the rain becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water in the soil starves the roots of air. When plant roots cannot breathe underwater, decay microorganisms quickly multiply and rot the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Beni tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ nu shishi Nibii bibii ni fiteɔ lɛ faa oya ni amɛhaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruits during the hottest dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot form fruits. The plant drops the dead flowers to conserve water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ, ni ehaaa amɛwo yibii. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni egboi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and tall, watery trunks. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, the top becomes too heavy for the shallow roots to hold up without wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni kwɔlɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli wa lɛ Ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ baafee tsiimɔ tsɔ kɛha shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. ni abaanyɛ aná ni akɛ tso tsuuu nii

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear and clean the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔji lɛ amli ni mijie amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lay hidden in the soil for years waiting for clear sunlight and cleared land to explode into growth, making them naturally faster to adapt than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni amɛmiimɛ hulu la ni mli tse koni amɛjie he ko ni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ haa amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya fe shia tsei.

english: Why is it dangerous to sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat dry spell that dries out the topsoil, which will scorch and kill newly germinated seed sprouts before the main rainy season sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baashã ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning brown and dying when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct heat from the sun. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains planted next to them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young leaves until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the ears are formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves near the base of a maize plant mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to stay green. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plants will help them regain strength and yield good ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛbɔle he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni efee toi kpakpai.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when pushing them into the ground?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the small growing buds pointing up toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the roots will struggle to grow properly underground, resulting in very low root harvests.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋwɛi Shishifãi lɛ baaná naagba ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do experienced farmers build raised dirt mounds before planting yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ maa gɔji ni awó nɔ dani amɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose dirt to expand deep underground into large roots. Mound building loosens the soil so the yam can grow freely and prevents roots from rotting during heavy downpours.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia muji ni yɔɔ blɛoo koni amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyashɛ shishifãi wuji amli. Gɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or beans together with my corn crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa tsei duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take food directly from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil. Planting them with corn helps feed the corn plant while preventing the soil from getting exhausted.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ amɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha abele tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ hu naa koni ekafite.

english: Why are small worms creating holes and leaves looking eaten inside the center whorl of my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifee bu kɛ baai ni esaaa yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on tender leaf centers. Inspecting your farm early and putting a small amount of clean sand mixed with ash or targeted neem spray into the leaf funnel stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ ŋã ni he tse fioo ko ni akɛ sũ loo neem spray ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ efutu mli lɛ awo baai lɛ amli. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my green tomato fruits develop black, rotten patches at the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by calcium deficiency, often triggered when soil water goes from too dry to too wet. Keeping soil moisture steady by watering regularly and mulching around plants prevents this rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni faaa lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha daa kɛ sũ ni okɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. tsei koni amɛkafite

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and yield very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crops get all the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: How do I know if the first rainy day of the season is enough water to plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaadu midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Sowing immediately after a light first rain is risky because the soil can dry out quickly, scorching seeds. It is best to wait until the ground is thoroughly wet to a hand's depth, showing the rains are consistent enough to support seed germination.
ga: Nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni eshãa dumɔwui lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be bɔ ni sa koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or sudden water shortages. Covering the soil around the plant with dry leaves or straw keeps the ground cool and moist, helping flowers stay on and produce pods.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ pods.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen food in the soil or the ground is soaked with too much standing water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps moisture so you water less, and slowly rots to feed your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ shi bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli, ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that loves feeding on tender maize leaves. You can control them early by applying recommended crop protection sprays or putting neem leaf mixture directly into the center of the plants.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fɔɔ baa ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa baai bibii. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ neem baa ni akɛfutuɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing off infected pods helps stop the sickness from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ aniji ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la babaoo baa ni ejieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from the leaves. Spraying your pepper plants with a mild neem oil or soap solution helps clear these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni mli ejɔ Loo samla shwie pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their small flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Ni efeee pods kwraa?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry, or if there are no tiny insects like midges around to pollinate them. Providing light shade and keeping the ground moist helps flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ teŋgbɛ nibii ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ bɛ. ni akɛ hulutsoo be fioo haa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to hold up heavy bunches during high winds. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden props or planting them in protective rows helps keep them standing.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔ ŋmeii wuji amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei titrii lɛ asɛɛ loo adu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni abuɔ he lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Why are my planted yam seeds taking so long to sprout out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period after harvest called dormancy. If planted in dry soil, they will wait safely underground until the first steady rains come before they start sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Amɛbaamɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ dani amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu kroko ni fa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering or a lack of calcium in the soil while the fruit is growing. Keeping the soil evenly damp and adding compost helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Instead of spending energy to produce big cobs, the plants stretch tall just to reach the sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji Moŋ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ elɛɛmɔ nɔ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often tricks farmers because the deep soil remains hot and dry. If a dry spell follows that initial rain, your seeds will sprout, run out of soil moisture, and burn up before the true rainy season established.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ lakaa okwaafoi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lolo. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ko nyiɛ shishijee nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ etee. ni eshã kwraa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die if I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct, intense sunlight. Larger shade trees act like living umbrellas, providing the cool shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why did my pepper plants wilt and turn brown after I applied fertilizer during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ egboi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve properly into food for plants. When applied in dry soil, strong chemical fertilizer acts like salt, pulling water out of the crop's roots and causing the plant to burn and wilt.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni mli wa wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋoo, ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi amli ni ehaa tso lɛ shãa ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why does placing dry grass around the base of my plantain trees help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwo mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the sun from drying out the soil, retains moisture near the roots, and slowly rots into rich organic food for the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my tomatoes grow poorly if I plant them in the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases specific to tomatoes to build up in the ground. Rotating crops keeps the soil healthy and starves pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ tomato pɔtɛɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi.

english: Curled, yellow leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food efficiently, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I pinch off the small side branches growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Those extra side shoots (suckers) consume a lot of water and nutrients just to grow leaves. Removing them forces the tomato plant to send its energy into growing larger, healthier fruits instead.
ga: Lateral shoots (shoots) ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛhaa baai lɛ adalɛ. Tomato ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛya aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Why do weeds take over my farm so much faster than my cassava crop can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni mi-cassava lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants adapted to take over land quickly and steal light, water, and plant food. Because cassava takes time to establish leaves, weeds will dominate the space if they are not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛye shikpɔŋ nɔ ni amɛju la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei heɔ be dani efeɔ baai. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi yeɔ jɛmɛ nɔ kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Ragged holes inside the growing center (funnel) of young maize are typically caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the plant leaves during the day and eat the tender inner growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ mligbɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How do I know if a seed variety brought from outside Ghana will grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛba kɛjɛ Ghana kponɔgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds from other countries or regions are adapted to different climates and soils. Before planting a new foreign variety on your main land, test a small plot to see how its growth traits and yields perform under your local weather and soil conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ loo kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. Dani obaadu maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi heei yɛ oshikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ Kaa he bibioo ko okwɛ. Koni ona bɔ ni edalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo sui lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ shishi.

english: Why would a crop variety perform very well in Accra but yield poorly if I plant it in Agogo?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso henɔ ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Accra shi ewoɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu yɛ Agogo lɛ?

english: Accra and Agogo have different rainfall levels, temperatures, and soil compositions. A crop variety bred for dry coastal conditions may suffer from diseases or poor growth in cooler, rainier forest zones like Agogo.
ga: Accra kɛ Agogo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii sɔrɔtoi. Tsei srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ amɛ kɛha ŋshɔnaa shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ baanyɛ ana helai loo amɛdalɛ ni ehiii yɛ kooi ni mli ejɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli tamɔ Agogo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell the character and strength of a new crop variety before buying it in bulk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni tso hee ko yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ shiŋŋ ha dani mahe babaoo?

english: You can observe demonstration fields managed by extension officers or try a small sample batch. Look at how quickly it germinates, its resistance to local pests, and how well it handles short dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ he ni hiɛyaa nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ loo oka nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko okwɛ. Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Ni te etsuɔ ​​hulutsoo be kukuji ahe nii ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is waterlogged, which prevents roots from breathing, or that heavy rains have washed away nitrogen, the nutrient that keeps leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo nitrogen lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like potassium and phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What causes my cassava roots to get hard and woody instead of soft when boiled?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee blɛoo kɛji akɛ ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become woody if left in the ground too long past their maturity stage or if the plant went through severe drought stress while the roots were forming.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ fe bɔ ni amɛdaraa lɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa kpeɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that enters the plant roots and blocks water from moving up into the stem and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni boteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni ehaaa nu aya ŋwɛi kɛya tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and deformed under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when they hit hard, rocky, or unplowed soil underground. Preparing deep, loose soil ridges allows the tubers to expand straight and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato lɛ yitso tsake beni etswa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ lɛ. tɛi loo nɔ ni atsuuu he nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ he saamɔ haa bulb lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does planting shade trees help my main crops during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ harmattan be ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees block harsh direct sunlight, lower soil temperatures, and reduce water evaporation from the soil, helping delicate crops retain moisture during dry months.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need rich, organic soil and steady moisture to build strong root systems. If planted in poor soil or during a dry spell, their growth stalls until root growth recovers.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Dalɛ baakpa kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsake.

english: Leaf yellowing and curling usually indicate that your maize lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or is under attack by sap-sucking pests like aphids or early fall armyworms. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or applying proper pest control early can save your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-ŋmã lɛ mli, loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ, tamɔ aphids loo fall armyworms lɛ etutua lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he loo ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatsu nii mra. lɛ baanyɛ ahere owala yiwala

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and heavily shaded environments. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight into your farm and clearing away infected pods prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hulutsoo waa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if my soil is suitable for growing cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cassava grows best in loose, sandy-loam soil that drains water easily. If rain water sits on top of your land for days or the soil turns into hard clay, the cassava roots will rot or fail to grow big tubers.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he gbii babaoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ batsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Kasava shishifãi lɛ baagbo loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it harmful to burn my land when clearing it for a new crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã mishikpɔŋ lɛ beni ajieɔ tsei heei kɛjɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and beneficial organisms in the topsoil that feed your crops. It also leaves the ground exposed, causing rain to wash away vital nutrients needed for growth.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ faŋŋ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant groundnuts together with cassava in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil, which feeds the cassava plant. Planting them together improves soil health and gives you two crops from the same piece of land without soil exhaustion.
ga: Adebɔɔ naa ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, ni no haa ŋmei tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fee ekome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains grow quickly and develop broad leaves that act as living umbrellas. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops droop during the hot afternoon even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: In intense sun, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Placing dry grass or leaves around the plant base (mulching) keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young crops are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem can burn the plant tissue and damage its roots due to concentrated salts. Fertilizer should be placed in a shallow ring a few inches away from the stem where roots can feed safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni baa tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ fãji ni efite shishifãi yɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Ekɛ tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye shweshweeshwe lɛ

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines on top of the soil turn yellow and dry up completely. Harvesting while the vines are still green leads to watery, underformed tubers that spoil quickly in storage.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Kɛ́ akpa wain tso lɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni bɛ su kpakpa, ni nu yɔɔ mli ni baafite oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so fast when a heavy rain falls right after a hot sunny period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sunlight gives plants the energy to make food, but when water suddenly hits the warm ground, the roots absorb it quickly, causing the cells in the plant and fruit to expand rapidly.
ga: Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Shi kɛ́ nu lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ lɛ, edɔɔ trukaa. Shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ lɛ oya. Ehaa wala yibii ni yɔɔ tsei kɛ aduawai amli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya.

english: Why does the water disappear from my farm soil so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dry or sandy soil has big spaces between dirt particles that let water drain straight through. Adding compost or covering the ground with dead leaves helps the soil hold water like a sponge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo ŋã yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ muji lɛ ateŋ ni haa nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eŋɔ nu tamɔ sponji.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops wilt and curl during the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is slightly wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo po

english: In intense sun, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than roots can drink it up from the ground. Curling helps the plant reduce leaf exposure to heat to prevent drying out.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Curling yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa baa lɛ baa shi yɛ hulutsoo mli koni baa lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the plant after sudden heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When a dry plant receives sudden abundance of water, the inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack.
ga: When a dry tree receives a sudden large amount of water. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off without producing any fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme sun and heat heat up the plant stems and dry out pollen, causing flowers to drop off before they can form fruit.
ga: Hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha tsei lɛ amli adɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛpuɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my fruit growing big very fast, but turning soft and rotting before it ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyibii lɛ miida oya nɛkɛ? Shi etsɔɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ dani ahooɔ?

english: Too much water coming all at once causes rapid growth, but if the soil lacks key nutrients like calcium, the cell walls of the fruit remain weak and easily rot.
ga: Nu babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo shikome lɛ kɛ dalɛ baa oya. Shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, aduawai lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ebaafite oya.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick my fruit so it does not spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa aduawai? Bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops show distinct signs when mature, such as changing color from dark green to yellow or red, stems turning brown, or the fruit giving off a sweet smell and coming off the branch easily.
ga: Tsei baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ su ni tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru mli. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo. Aloo aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ejɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do vegetables harvested in the middle of a hot sunny afternoon rot faster than those harvested early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni akpa yɛ shwane mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ oya fe aduawai ni akpa leebi lɛ?

english: Crops picked under full sun trap heat inside themselves, which speeds up rotting. Harvesting in the cool morning keeps the fruit firm and fresh longer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli. Enɛ baaha fitemɔ aya oya. Kɛ́ akpa yibii lɛ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfee ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil turn as hard as a rock after sunshine follows rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni hulutsoo be ni nugbɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain packs heavy clay soil tight, and strong sun bakes it hard if there is no shade or organic matter like compost mixed into it to keep it loose.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni hulu ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni naa wa ni hulutsoo be loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very little fruit when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for sunlight and spend all their energy growing upward to reach the light instead of using energy to grow fat stems and heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la lɛ he akaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛduɔ tsei ni yɔɔ fɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants burn and turn brown when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their young leaves dry out quickly. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains nearby provides protective cover that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong.
