ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut down my old cocoa trees that are barely producing pods and plant new seedlings instead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso momo ko ni eshwɛ fioo ni ebɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni madu tso hee yɛ esɛɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow very old, their ability to take up nutrients drops, making them yield few pods and vulnerable to diseases. Replacing unproductive old trees with new, high-yielding seedlings restores full farm production over time.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ waa Hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛyeɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ baa shi Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli ni helai srɔtoi baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ. Tsei momo ni wooo yibii lɛ ni akɛ dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo baatsake lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ mli yibiiwoo lɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize regain its dark green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the roots and leaves fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures every maize stalk gets enough food to build strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: What is making ragged holes in the middle of my maize leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Those holes are caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the central shoot of the maize plant. Inspecting fields early and applying approved neem sprays or recommended insecticides directly into the plant funnel protects the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ bu nɛɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli lɛ feɔ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ neem spray ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of big leaves but produce tiny cassava roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi eyɛ cassava shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in its roots. Planting in balanced, well-drained soil encourages the plant to store food underground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ja ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for the growing yam underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sunlight while preventing leaf diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha sweet potato ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa baa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is lacking, or when tiny pests attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting during favorable weather helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ, kɛ́ nu bɛ amɛmli, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni adu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie Mi plantain titri lɛ.

english: Too many sucker shoots compete with the main plantain stem for food and water, leading to small fruit bunches. Pruning extra suckers and leaving only two or three strong ones directs food into making big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. kɛ aduawai bibii baa Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii afee plantain tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, soil food, and space from your crops. Removing weeds early keeps the soil's nutrients available exclusively for your crops to grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ pɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya.

english: Why do some modern maize varieties mature in three months while traditional ones take five months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmãa lɛ heɔ nyɔji enumɔ.

english: Short-duration maize varieties are bred to complete their life cycle faster so farmers can harvest quickly before dry periods set in or fit two planting seasons into one year.
ga: Atsɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ anɔ koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpaa nii oya dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa loo amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ bei enyɔ he yɛ afi kome mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow much slower and take longer to produce fruit if I plant them in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo kwraa ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains need constant soil moisture to build strong root systems quickly; during dry periods, the plant slows down its growth to conserve water, which delays fruit production.
ga: Plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni enyɛ efee shishifãi ni mli wa oya. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni amɛbu nu he. Enɛ baaha aduawai ni anáa lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why do I need to start my tomato seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are tiny and delicate, so raising them in a protected nursery guards the fragile seedlings from heavy rainfall, hot sun, and pests until they are strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Therefore, growing them in protected nurseries protects fragile seedlings from heavy rains. hot sunlight and insect pests Until they are strong enough to survive in open fields.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings grow very tall, thin, and weak when I keep them under heavy shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ beni mikɛ amɛ woɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ?

english: Seedlings need sunlight to make food; when kept in too much shade, they stretch upward rapidly in search of light, making their stems thin and easily broken.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii. When kept in too much shade It quickly stretches upwards in search of light. Ehaa tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efiteɔ oya

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops during their early weeks rather than waiting until they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mɛ nɛ tso ɔ maa wa saminya.

english: Young crops need extra nutrients early on to build strong roots and healthy stems; feeding them early establishes the foundation required for high yields later.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hiaa niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he mra. Koni afee shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni wa Amɛ niyenii mra Ebaafee shishitoo ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my green pepper plants turning light yellow during early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili tso ni ji eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves early in growth usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overwatering, which prevents the roots from taking up essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni daa oya lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their lower leaves during dry weather to stop water from escaping through leaf surface areas, helping the plant stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ehaa tsei hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer as a self-defense mechanism to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, forcing the plant to spend energy competing instead of swelling its cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha amɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: If I harvest my yams earlier than usual to sell quickly, will they keep for a long time in my barn?
ga: Kɛji mikpa sweet potatoes mra fe bɔ ni mifeɔ daa lɛ koni mahɔ̃ɔ oya Ani ebaahi mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Early-harvested yams contain higher moisture levels and have thin, soft skin, which causes them to rot and spoil much faster in storage than fully mature tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpaa mra lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni amɛhewolo lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nitoohe mli fe bulbs ni eda.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which gives plants their rich green color and energy. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the base of the plants helps them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ su eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo kooloi ashishifãi ni fiteɔ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ eŋɔli ni edaa waa.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year, why do my harvest yields keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and lets plant diseases build up. Rotating maize with beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas naturally restores nitrogen to the soil and stops pests from multiplying.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tso helai baa shi. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni etsĩ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them creates living shade trees that shield the young cocoa until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni buɔ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with very few peppers when I crowd them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ pepper fioo ko pɛ kɛ mikɛto he lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and soil food instead of growing fruit. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures enough sunlight and air reach every branch to produce healthy peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ nine fɛɛ nine he koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water gathers around them in heavy, undrained soil. Planting cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater flow away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my maize leaves during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-corn baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Ragged holes are usually caused by fall armyworms, small caterpillars that hide inside the funnel of young maize leaves. Checking your field early and spraying natural remedies like neem leaf extract or approved insecticides inside the funnels keeps them under control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni etse lɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nibii nɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the root level early in the morning keeps the soil moist and helps the flowers stay on to set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe leebi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I stop small insects from eating and destroying my harvested maize while in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii ni mikpaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛkafite lɛ naa be mli ni eyɔɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive in moist grain. Thoroughly drying your harvested maize under the sun until the kernels are hard and storing them in sealed, airtight bags suffocates pests without needing dangerous chemicals.
ga: Picker kooloi tamɔ weevils shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. Gbimɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni okɛto kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli. Ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my harvested fresh tomatoes spoil so quickly before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting vegetables in the hot afternoon heat causes them to lose water quickly and rot faster. Harvesting early in the morning while it is cool and packing them in shallow, ventilated crates keeps them fresh longer for market transport.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ aduawai shwie shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ afite oya ni ebaafite oya. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ leebi beni hulu lɛ miitso ni okɛwo adekai ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ koni akɛya jara nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the early rains keep stopping suddenly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ kpaɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: First rains can be misleading and cause seeds to germinate and dry up if the rain stops. It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently moist for several consecutive days after the rains begin before planting your main seeds.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ni eha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ je shishi dani odu dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting coconut seedlings before I get my first harvest?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tso lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onine ashɛ oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Improved coconut varieties like dwarf trees start producing fruit within 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 5 to 7 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Kokooi srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tsei bibii lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kokooi srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How many years can a coconut tree continue producing fruits for my family?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ŋmei tso baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii aha miweku lɛ?

english: Coconut trees are long-term assets that can produce fruit consistently for 60 to 80 years, providing steady harvests and income for over 20 years when properly cared for.
ga: Kokoo tsei ji nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ awo yibii ni yaa nɔ daa afii 60 kɛyashi 80, ni ehaa yibii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ shika ni fa fe afii 20 kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I consider planting coconut trees instead of only growing seasonal crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ŋmei tsei adumɔ he yɛ be mli nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei pɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: While seasonal crops like maize give quick, one-time income every few months, coconut trees provide continuous monthly harvests and stable income for several decades after reaching maturity.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni be mli nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa haa shika ni anáa oya shikome daa nyɔji fioo lɛ, ŋmãa tsei woɔ nyɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ beni amɛdara lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What kind of soil or land is best for planting coconuts in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Coconut trees grow best in well-drained sandy or loamy soils with good sunlight, but they can adapt to most soil types in Ghana as long as the land does not stay flooded or waterlogged.
ga: Kokoo tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo sũ yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔji ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo mli, kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiɛɛɛ nu loo nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: How much space should I leave between coconut trees when planting them?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ?

english: You should space coconut trees about 7.5 to 9 meters (25 to 30 feet) apart so their wide leaves get enough sunlight and their root systems do not fight for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-coconut tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 7.5 kɛyashi 9 (naji 25 kɛyashi 30) bɔni afee ni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ sũ mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: Can I plant other food crops between my coconut trees while they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tsei krokomɛi yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first 3 to 4 years while the coconut trees are short, you can intercrop with food like cassava, maize, or legumes to earn income and keep weeds under control.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmei tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu nibii ni fata he tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa. Koni ana shika ni akudɔ jwɛi

english: How do I keep my young coconut seedlings alive during the dry season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmeii bibii ahi wala mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Young coconut seedlings need regular watering during their first dry season (about 20 liters of water per week) and a thick layer of dry grass mulch around the stem to trap soil moisture.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔse ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ nu daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli (aaafee lita 20 yɛ otsi mli) ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni mli tse aha amɛhe. ebɔle tso lɛ he koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ

english: What does it mean if the leaves on my young coconut tree start turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign of nutrient deficiency, lack of water during dry periods, or early signs of diseases like Cape St. Paul Wilt, which requires immediate treatment or field sanitation.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee niyenii ni esaaa he okadi. Nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo hela he okadii ni jeɔ shishi mra, tamɔ Cape St. Paul’s wilt. ni biɔ ni atsa lɛ loo afee hetsemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: How often can I harvest coconuts from a mature tree in a single year?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso ni eda mli yɛ afi kome mli?

english: A healthy, mature coconut tree produces new flower bunches continuously, allowing you to harvest fresh nuts every month or every two months throughout the year.
ga: Kokoo tso ni eda ni ehe wa lɛ baawo fɔfɔi akui heei be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmeii heei daa nyɔŋ nɔ loo daa nyɔji enyɔ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my coconut is ready to harvest for drinking water versus making oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-koko lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛha nu ni anuɔ kɛ mu feemɔ?

english: Harvest coconuts at 7 to 8 months old when green for sweet fresh water, but wait until 11 to 12 months when the outer shell turns brown and dry if you want to extract oil or dried copra.
ga: Kpãa ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 8 mli beni amɛji ŋmɔji lɛ koni onine ashɛ nu kpakpa nɔ, shi mɛ kɛyashi nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 12 be mli ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni egbi kɛji oosumɔ ni ojie fɔ loo ŋmeii loo ni egbi.

english: How can I test if my stored maize seeds are still good before I plant them across my entire farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hi dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: You can place ten seeds on a wet cloth inside a warm room for a few days to see how many sprout. If eight or more sprout, your seeds are strong enough to give you a good harvest across your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui 10 awo mama ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi koni ona bɔ ni amɛyi fa ha. Kɛji dumɔwui kpaanyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ Odumɔwui lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do tiny seeds like pepper and tomato need to start in a nursery bed before moving to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aje dumɔwui bibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato shishi yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani ajie kɛya ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ?

english: Tiny seeds produce very fragile sprouts that can easily be washed away by heavy rains or eaten by insects. A nursery protects them until they build strong roots to survive in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii woɔ dumɔwui ni waaa kwraa. ni abaanyɛ ahoo oya kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ loo kooloi ŋmɔ amɛ Tso lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaafee shishifãi ni wa koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When maize is planted too close, the roots fight over water and soil nutrients, and the leaves shade each other from sunlight. This makes the stalks grow tall and thin with very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe tseee, ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why should I pinch off the small extra shoots growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Extra shoots steal food and water away from the main stem and fruits. Removing them allows the plant to focus its energy on growing larger, healthier tomatoes instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ aduawai lɛ amli. Tomatoi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baafata he.

english: My cassava leaves are turning yellow even after applying fertilizer, why is this happening?
ga: Mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli po sɛɛ. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil is too waterlogged and choking the roots, or the soil is too acidic. Fertilizer cannot work properly if the roots are unhealthy or unable to absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji shishifãi lɛ waaa loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii.

english: If a patch of my land keeps producing weak tomato crops every season, what should I do?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mimaŋ lɛ tee nɔ ewo tomato ni bɛ hewalɛ daa be mli. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Specific pests and diseases build up in the soil when you plant the same crop repeatedly. Instead of forcing tomatoes to grow there, switch to legumes or maize to clean the soil and break the disease cycle.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyɛ tomato nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ Moŋ lɛ, tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ koni okɛtsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛfo hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in a field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and dry out quickly under intense sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to protect them while their young roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: I see tiny dark spots on a few leaves of my pepper plants, should I pluck those leaves off?
ga: Mina he ko diŋ fioo ko. Yɛ pepper baai komɛi anɔ Ani esa akɛ majie nakai baai lɛ?

english: Yes, plucking leaves with early disease spots prevents fungi or bacteria from spreading to the rest of the plant and surrounding crops on your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants drop their flowers without forming pods during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce and weather is extremely hot, the plant drops its flowers to conserve moisture and keep itself alive rather than spending limited energy on growing seeds.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni eha ehi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ baatsu nii kɛdu dumɔwui

english: Why do my yam vines wilt and stop growing during short periods without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa shweremɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves wilt to reduce water loss through their broad surface when soil moisture drops. Once rain returns, healthy vines revive and continue feeding the growing tuber underneath.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko ni da lɛ aba shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Wein tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba wala mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛha bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter which way I stick a cassava stem into the ground when planting?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ miduɔ lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, it matters. The small buds on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the plant will waste energy trying to correct its growth, leading to weak stems and fewer tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia. Buu bibii ni yɔɔ yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ejaje edalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛyitsei lɛ hu faaa.

english: Why do I have to spend time lifting and tying my yam vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be kɛwo sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni mikɛfi tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need as much sunlight as possible to make food for their underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where they could rot and ensures they catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akatara hei ni efɔ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa hulu la babaoo

english: Why should I cut off some of the tiny plantain shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ banana tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi plantain shishifãi titri lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around the main plant, they will steal food, water, and sunlight from it. Pruning away the excess shoots leaves just one strong replacement shoot, ensuring your main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Tsei titrii babaoo he lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi. Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: My maize leaves are turning pale yellow starting from the middle, why is this happening?
ga: Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ. Mɛni hewɔ enɛ ji nakai lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize crop is starving for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding a nitrogen-based fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛshishijee ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the dirt. This naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer that nearby maize crops can feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil so plant roots can absorb it. If you apply dry fertilizer to parched, dry ground in direct heat, it can burn the plant roots or simply get blown away by the wind.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo hei ni egbi, ni egbi kɛtsɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ nɔ. Tso shishifãi baanyɛ ashã loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa amɛ kɛya.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding on the undersides of leaves and sucking out plant sap, or by viruses spread by these insects. Treating the crop with neem oil or appropriate sprays can help control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the plant doesn't get enough consistent water. Maintaining regular watering and covering the soil with dry leaves can keep the soil cool and retain the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Nu ni awoɔ amɛ daa kɛ baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: How does spreading dry grass over the soil around my crops help them survive dry hot weather?
ga: He ni akɛ jwɛi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass (mulching) acts like a shield that keeps the hot sun from evaporating water out of the dirt, keeping the roots moist and cool for much longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe jɔɔ be babaoo.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has enough good nutrients to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Soil nutrients are like food for your plants; if the soil is dark, moist, and mixed with decaying leaves or compost, your crops will get the proper food they need to grow strong, stay green, and produce healthy harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ tamɔ niyenii kɛha otsei lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, edɔ, ni baai ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Hiɛ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni okɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba

english: What can I add to my soil to make my crops grow better without spoiling the land over time?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Adding natural organic manure, compost, or farmyard animal waste improves the soil naturally. It helps the land hold water and feeds the plants continuously without destroying the natural wealth and structure of your soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi aŋmɔji fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei daa. ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ninamɔi kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava and maize plants turn yellow or develop dark spots while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-cassava kɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni edara lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves or spots usually mean the crop is suffering from a plant disease, an insect attack, or a lack of basic soil nutrients like nitrogen, which prevents the plant from growing normally.
ga: Baai loo ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ tso hela mli, koolooi miitutua lɛ, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni miitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my crops from diseases naturally so that the food remains safe and healthy for my family to eat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ahe koni niyenii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni ehi aha miweku lɛ?

english: You can protect your crops by clearing away sick plants early, planting different types of crops together (crop rotation), and spraying natural remedies like neem tree leaf extracts to repel pests safely.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie mra lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ he kome (ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ) ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem baa mli nu afɔ nɔ. Koni ashwie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my young crops stay very small and stunted even when I plant them at the start of the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛgbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shishijee mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops stay stunted when their roots cannot access nutrients in the soil, or when fast-growing weeds crowd around them and steal their water, sunlight, and underground food.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What actually makes harvested crops considered good, high-quality food?
ga: Mɛni haa nikpamɔ ko feɔ niyenii ni hi, ni nɔ kwɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Good quality crop produce comes from plants grown in fertile soil with proper care, harvested at full maturity, and kept free from harmful chemical residues, insect holes, or early decay.
ga: Nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni baa lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Kpamɔ be mli ni edara kwraa. ni oha tsofai ni eshwɛ, kooloi amli ŋmeii, loo nɔ ni fiteɔ oya akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my tomatoes and peppers start rotting right on the farm before I even pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato kɛ mi-pepper lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ po shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Vegetables often rot on the plant because of high moisture trapped around the fruit, poor air movement between plants, or fungal diseases that splash up from muddy soil during rainstorms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai fiteɔ yɛ tsei amli yɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni ebɔle aduawai lɛ ahe kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ hewɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Does applying too much chemical fertilizer affect the quality and natural taste of the food I harvest?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ saa niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ mli kpakpa kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ fɛo ha lɛ he?

english: Yes, overusing chemical fertilizer makes plants absorb too much water rapidly, which can weaken their natural flavor, soften the crop, and cause it to spoil much faster after harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ lɛ aba shi. ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kwraa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and wither so fast whenever rain stops for just one or two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbiɔ oya ni amɛgbiɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa otsi kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops wither quickly if their root systems are shallow or if the soil lacks organic matter like leaf mulch that acts like a sponge to store underground water during dry periods.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ.

english: Which local Ghanaian food crops are easiest to grow healthy so that local traders will buy them quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa bɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi baanyɛ ahe oya?

english: Local staples like plantain, cassava, yam, and indigenous green leafy vegetables are well-adapted to local soils, require simple care to grow healthy, and always have strong demand in Ghanaian markets.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ plantains, cassava, sweet potatoes kɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha akutso lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ebiɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo koni etsɔ hewalɛ. Ni be fɛɛ be lɛ, mɛi babaoo taoɔ nibii babaoo yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Can rubber trees grow well in Ghana, and where are they usually planted?
ga: Rɔba tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana. Ni nɛgbɛ ji he ni bei pii lɛ aduɔ yɛ?

english: Yes, rubber trees grow well in Ghana, particularly in high-rainfall zones like the Western, Central, Eastern, and parts of the Greater Accra regions, where warm temperatures and humid weather allow them to produce latex.
ga: Hɛɛ, rɔba tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ tamɔ anaigbɛ, teŋgbɛ, bokagbɛ kɛ Greater Accra kpokpaa lɛ fãi komɛi, he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be haa amɛfeɔ latɛs lɛ.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting a rubber tree before I can start collecting latex?
ga: Kɛ́ odu rɔbɔt tso sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi latɛs ni ooobua naa lɛ?

english: Rubber trees typically need about 6 to 7 years to grow and develop a trunk thick enough before you can safely tap them to extract latex.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa bɔ ni sa dani obaanyɛ otswa amɛ shweshweeshwe ni ojie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground so it doesn't dry out quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, ekagbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost, animal manure, or a balanced fertilizer will give the plants the nutrients they need to turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves, and how can I stop it?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ nɔ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. You can protect your farm by checking plants early and applying recommended pesticides, neem oil, or wood ash inside the plant leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei ni okwɛɔ mli mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi, neem fɔ, loo tso sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural shield to save water. When the afternoon heat is strong, rolling the leaves hides their surface from the direct sun to keep water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ tsei ahe koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ shwane lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why is it important to cut off extra branches from crop trees like cocoa or mango?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo tsei tamɔ kookoo loo mango niji krokomɛi amli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Trimming or pruning opens up the tree so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts. This stops mold and diseases from spreading and encourages the tree to put its energy into growing bigger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ loo afolɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ gbɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is too much heat from the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil before their tender roots can grow deep enough to tap into underground moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi dani shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbote shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or is waterlogged, preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients needed to produce green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot underground when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes water to collect around cassava roots in poorly drained soil, which suffocates the tubers and creates humid conditions where rot-causing fungi thrive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu buaa ehe naa kɛbɔleɔ he. Cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems; when heavy fruit bunches grow on top, strong winds or pests damaging the roots can easily cause the plant to lose balance and fall.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Beni aduawai akui ni tsii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans together in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ ko yɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ he?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is beneficial because beans trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: Young crops have small roots and leaves, so fast-growing weeds will easily steal sunlight, soil water, and nutrients away from them, stunt their growth early on.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ hulu la, sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ mli oya. ni okɛ dalɛ aba shi mra

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat hole patterns inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli?

english: These are pests like the Fall Armyworm, whose moths lay eggs on crop leaves; when the larvae hatch, they crawl into the leaf funnel to eat the soft leaves before the plant matures.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ lɛ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Efoɔ kɛboteɔ baai amli koni eyaye baai bibii dani tso lɛ daa.

english: Why do I need to put long wood sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to sunlight so the plant can produce energy to grow large tubers, while keeping leaves off wet soil to prevent leaf diseases.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ ni ekɛwo bulbs wuji amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni baa helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: How does adding dried animal manure to my farm soil help my crops produce more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure like a sponge to hold water better while slowly releasing essential nutrients that roots absorb continuously throughout the growing season.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo tamɔ sponji koni nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Eyaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ kpo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather becomes extremely hot, when water supply is irregular, or when there are no bees present to transfer pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie pollen awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dry under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji hulu lɛ tso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains planted next to them to block the hot afternoon sun, their soft leaves scorch, dry out, and turn yellow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Koni ekɛtsi shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa lɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ shãa, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I drop four or five maize seeds into the exact same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ shwie ŋmãa bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds together causes the young plants to compete for the same small pocket of water, light, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nyɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ tsei bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Does it matter which end of the cassava stick points upward when I plant it in the soil?
ga: Kɛji oodu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ naagbee baatsɔɔ ŋwɛi?

english: Yes, planting a cassava stem cutting upside down forces the buds to grow downwards before turning up, which wastes the plant's energy, weakens growth, and causes a very poor root yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, yucca tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara. ni fiteɔ hewalɛ lɛ haa dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ baa ni ehaa shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi waa

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to create energy to feed the growing yam tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves off the damp ground, which also protects them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot Ghanaian sun, retains moisture longer, and stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my farm help improve the soil for my next crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they leave behind natural nitrogen fertilizer that helps future crops like maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ abele, ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black rotted bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot get enough calcium. This is usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells that prevent the plant from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be ni haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dirt that looks like sawdust inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worm hides inside the central growing point of the maize plant, chewing through leaves and leaving behind sawdust-like droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ. Ekɛ baai shwieɔ shi ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, prolonged dry weather, or if too much synthetic nitrogen fertilizer was used, causing the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii Ha tsei lɛ aná baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoot plants growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ ni fata he ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain baai titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plantain stem. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, allowing the main stem to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Too many young shoots or shoots steal water and nutrients from the main plantain stem. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. This allows the main stem to form large, heavy bunches.

english: You can tell cocoa pods are ripe by their color change. Green pods usually turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow when ripe. Harvesting at full ripeness ensures optimal bean quality.
ga: You can tell that a cocoa pod is ripe by the color change. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. And the red or purple pods will turn orange-yellow when ripe. Harvesting when fully ripe ensures optimum bean quality.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and rot before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa amɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Keeping your farm weeded and pruning dense branches improves airflow and helps prevent this disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ. too wet and has humidity Keeping your farm clear of weeds and pruning dense branches will increase air circulation and help prevent this disease.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune or cut branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive, dead, or diseased branches so that the tree sends nutrients only to healthy parts. It also lets in sunlight and air, which reduces humidity and helps prevent crop diseases.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii, ni egboi, loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni tso lɛ akudɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛ kɛya fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Eha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli lolo. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Should I cut off the shoots growing straight up from the base of my cocoa trunk?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, these shoots—called chupons—drain valuable water and nutrients away from the main tree. Removing them early keeps the main trunk strong and encourages better pod growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ jieɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ni ajieɔ lɛ mra Enɛ baawo tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo pod lɛ dalɛ kpakpa he hewalɛ.

english: My old cocoa trees are no longer giving me good harvest, so how do I renew my farm?
ga: Mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ. So how do I renew my farm?

english: Farm renewal involves cutting down old, unproductive, or diseased trees and replacing them with young, disease-resistant seedlings. Doing this in phases helps you maintain some income while new trees mature.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmɔ ko ni abaaku sɛɛ afee lɛ he ji tsei ni egbɔ, ni wooo yibii loo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni akɛ dumɔwui bibii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ awo amɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ ni ooofee yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baaye abua bo ni oná shika ni onáa lɛ mli be mli ni tsei heei kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. eda kwraa

english: How far apart should I space my young cocoa trees when planting a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ hee?

english: A standard spacing is about 3 meters by 3 meters. Proper spacing gives each tree enough room for roots and leaves to capture soil nutrients and sunlight without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ ji mitai 3 x mitai 3. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa eshishifãi kɛ ebaai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but only keep a small percentage to develop into mature pods. High leaf drops or flower fall can also happen if the soil lacks nutrients or water.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi akpaa fioo ko pɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eda kwraa. Baai ni kɛlɛ loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji niyenii loo nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow during dry seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during dry spells indicate heat stress and lack of soil water. Planting shade trees alongside cocoa helps protect the soil from drying out too fast and guards young crops against strong sunlight.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi oya tsɔ, ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: When is the best time for me to feed my crops with fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer is best applied early in the rainy season when the soil is moist, allowing roots to easily soak up nutrients as the tree prepares to grow new leaves and pods.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai oya be mli ni tso lɛ saa ehe koni ekwɛ̃ baai kɛ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why do government extension officers come to collect data and measure my farm size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli mli nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ buaa saji anaa ni amɛsusuɔ miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ he lɛ?

english: Extension officers measure farm sizes and collect crop data to accurately plan support programs, supply adequate amounts of subsidized fertilizer, and map out disease control assistance for your district.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ susuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛi ni amɛbua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛ to yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Na ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa lɛ babaoo bɔ ni sa. ni ofee yelikɛbuamɔ he shikpɔŋ he mfoniri kɛha okpokpaa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into straws during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves during hot hours to protect themselves from losing water. It is the plant's natural way of reducing leaf surface area exposed to the sun so it can hold onto moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa ebaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛnyɛ amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is dying from too much water or from drought?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu babaoo loo hɔmɔ miigboi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: If leaves turn soft and yellow while the ground is muddy, the crop is drowning from too much water. If the leaves are dry, crisp, and the soil is cracked, the plant is dying from drought.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo muji Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse lɛ Tsei hu miigboi kɛmiijɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: How does watering my crops during the dry season turn into a profitable business for me?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni nu ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ bafee nitsumɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha mi?

english: Most farmers can only grow crops during the rainy season, which causes market gluts and low prices. If you water crops during the dry season, you can harvest fresh produce when supply is low and sell at much higher prices.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo baanyɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔ be mli pɛ. Enɛ haa jarayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa fe nine kɛ jara ni baa shi baa. Kɛji okɛ nu wo oŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Obaanyɛ okpa nibii heei beni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa lɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with huge leaves but tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows under deep shade, it puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing energy in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or sudden water stress. When the plant feels threatened, it sheds its flowers to preserve its own life.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ tso ko nu he akɛ awo ehe gbeyei lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he.

english: What happens if I plant too many maize seeds in the same small hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu bibioo kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants compete heavily for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la, kɛ nu mli, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I see damaged maize leaves in the morning even though I don't see worms on them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmãa baai ni efite leebi lɛ? Ni minaaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm hide deep inside the funnel of the plant or in the soil during the hot day to stay cool, and they only come out at night to feed on leaves.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei amli shɔŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli koni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Ni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai pɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and die after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash fungal spores from the soil onto the lower leaves of the tomato plant. Combined with moisture on the leaves, this allows fungal diseases to spread quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eshwieɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my crops start turning pale yellow when they are growing in the same spot for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he kome afii etɛ sɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull essential nutrients out of the earth every season. Growing the same crop repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil's nutrients, causing new crops to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees stop bearing as many pods as they used to when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ ekpa ŋmeii babaoo ni ewoɔ beni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their internal water pathways become less efficient at moving nutrients up from the soil to the branches, leading to lower pod production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda Nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa eniji lɛ anɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow green and healthy leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does adding poultry manure help my farm soil stay moist during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Poultry manure adds organic matter that acts like a sponge in the soil. It binds soil particles together so the land can hold onto water longer, keeping crop roots hydrated even when rain stops for a few days.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fataa he. Efiɔ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ ekome bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ekpa gbii fioo komɛi po.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that provide living shade, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough for open sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa kɛha kponɔgbɛ hulu la.

english: Why do many farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly over a full year. Planting them together allows you to harvest maize early while the cassava takes over the field later, maximizing food output from the same land.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmã daa blɛoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Hefatalɔi dumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa mra yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yeɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii babaoo jɛɔ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I give them tall sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mihaa amɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers using sunlight collected by their leaves. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, allowing all the leaves to catch full sunlight and air without crowding each other, resulting in bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ hulu la ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ebaai lɛ amli lɛ feɔ niyenii ehaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo.

english: Why do groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the ground after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the stems bend downward and burrow into the dirt. The groundnut pod actually grows and ripens beneath the soil where it is safe from heat and birds.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ abɔi pollination lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanut ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eji he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The central leaf funnel of a maize plant, called the whorl, provides tender young leaves for the caterpillar to eat while shielding it from heat, heavy rain, and direct spray from pesticides.
ga: Atsɛɔ abele tso baa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ akɛ whorl. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa bibii ni amɛyeɔ. Kɛfata he lɛ, ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without growing into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress or when soil moisture changes too quickly from dry to wet. The plant sacrifices its flowers to survive the stress before it can set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya tsɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Tsei kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛye nɔnyɛɛ mli dani amɛwo yibii.

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before the real rainy season settles in. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the tender young seedlings will quickly dry up and die from lack of soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baashɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Excess rain fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil with water, suffocating the roots. Without oxygen in the soil, cassava roots cannot breathe and naturally begin to decay and rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji oxygen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ amu. ni ebaaje shishi efite yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: How do I know if I am cutting too deep into my rubber tree when tapping?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mifoɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: Tapping should only shave the thin outer bark to reach latex vessels. If you cut too deep into the hard wood underneath, you will permanently damage the trunk, reduce latex flow, and make the tree vulnerable to snapping in high winds.
ga: Esa akɛ nɔ ni afo lɛ lɛ atsɔ hewolo nɔ fã bibioo ko ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nɔ. pɛ koni onine ashɛ latex tsɔne lɛ nɔ Kɛji ofo tso ni wa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baafite kwraa. Ehaa latɛs ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa tsei fãa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko ba

english: What happens to my tree if the outer bark gets scratched or peeled off?
ga: Mɛni baa mitso lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ajie kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ loo ajie lɛ?

english: Bark acts like human skin to protect the plant. When it is peeled or wounded, water escapes, insects can enter, and fungal diseases can rot the inner wood, weakening the entire stem.
ga: Tso lɛ hewolo tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɔmɔ hewolo koni ebu tso lɛ he. Kɛji ajie loo epila Nu lɛ baajo foi. Kplukai baanyɛ abote mli Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aha tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ agbo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do the stalks of my maize plants snap so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks break easily when plants lack potassium or are planted too close together, making them thin and weak. Proper field spacing and balanced fertilizer help build thick, flexible stems that can withstand wind.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ potassium bɛ tsei lɛ amli loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he kɛ fɔmɔ nii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni mli tse ni nyɛɔ amɛtsiɔ amɛhe ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa.

english: Is it safe to tie my tomato plants tightly to wooden stakes so they stay upright?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaakpɛtɛ tomato tsei ahe jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ?

english: No, tying stems too tightly cuts into the plant tissue as it grows wider, which can choke the stem and cause it to snap. Use soft cloth ties and leave plenty of room for the stem to expand.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ fĩ shi waa tsɔ lɛ, ebaafo tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ amli be mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ akumɔ tso lɛ ni eha efo. Kɛ mama kpã ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ atsu nii ni oshi gbɛ babaoo kɛha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do the stems of my young cassava plants break when I weed near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca bibioo lɛ tsei lɛ fãa kɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young cassava stems are filled with water and soft tissues, making them very brittle. Hand-pulling weeds right around the stem rather than using a heavy hoe prevents accidental snapping.
ga: Nu kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ eyi kasava tsei bibii amli obɔ. making it very brittle Ni akɛ niji agbala jwɛi lɛ kɛbɔle tso lɛ he yɛ shɔvel ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi lɛ akafo yɛ oshara mli.

english: How can I keep my heavy plantain tree from bending over and snapping before the fruits are ready?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ ni amɛkakumɔ dani aduawai lɛ afee klalo?

english: A heavy bunch of plantains shifts the tree's center of gravity. Propping the main trunk with sturdy bamboo poles or wooden crutches supports the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantains babaoo tsiɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni wa fĩ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shwiili lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I forcefully pull down branches on my cocoa tree to harvest high pods?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji mikɛ yiwalɛ shwie cacao tso nine ko nɔ koni mikɛkpa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa branches are brittle under pressure; bending them too far will snap the wood and ruin future flowering points. It is better to use a sharp harvesting hook on a long pole.
ga: Cocoa niji lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ ohe shwie shi tsɔ lɛ, ebaakumɔ tso lɛ ni efite wɔsɛɛ be mli fɔfɔii ahe hei lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei ni naa wa atsu nii yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ.

english: Can trimming too many branches at once make my fruit tree weak?
ga: Ani tsei niji babaoo ni afolɔ shikome lɛ baanyɛ aha mitso ni woɔ yibii lɛ agbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, heavy pruning creates severe shock for the tree. Removing more than a third of the branches at once starves the tree of energy and makes the main stem weak and brittle.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afolɔ waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ he afee shoo waa. Kɛ́ afo niji lɛ amli nɔ ni fe mlijaa etɛ mli ekome shikome lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye Hewalɛ Tso lɛ. ni ehaa tso lɛ tso titri lɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops so I do not pick them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni okaŋɔ oya tsɔ?

english: Crops show natural maturation signs such as color changes, drying of lower leaves, or firm skin. Waiting for these signals ensures the crop is fully developed so fruits release easily without damaging the stem.
ga: Tso lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ he okadii akpo, tamɔ su tsakemɔ, shishi baai ni egbi, loo hewolo ni wa. Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo oya ni efiteee tso lɛ shishi.
