english: Why do the young shoots on my crops snap so easily during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ fãa oya yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the hot sun, young shoots lose water fast and become stiff and fragile under heat stress. It is best to handle, train, or prune crops early in the morning when plants are full of moisture and more flexible.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii, otsɔse amɛ, loo ooofolɔ amɛmli leebi maŋkpa be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ eyi mli obɔ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over right when the heavy bunch starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa beni ŋmeii wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay close to the top of the soil. As the fruit bunch grows big and heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, and strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the ground unless you prop up the stem with a strong Y-shaped wooden pole.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ daa ni ehiɛɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ waa. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Ja okɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How many suckers should I allow to grow from one plantain stem?
ga: Esa akɛ maha ŋmeii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ dumɔwu kome mli?

english: You should only keep three suckers per plantain stem at different stages: the bearing mother plant, one medium daughter sucker, and one small granddaughter sucker. Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to fight for soil nutrients, which leads to very small fruit bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii etɛ pɛ ato plantain tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he yɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli, ni tso nyɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fata he. Biyoo kome ni dalɛ ji mlɛbo lɛ tu. kɛ nabi yoo bibioo kome. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii waa ni ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to spread dried leaves and organic compost around the base of my plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ ehe lɛ? mi plantain shishitoo lɛ

english: Plantains need a lot of water and food because of their large leaves and shallow roots. Covering the soil with dried leaves keeps the dirt cool and moist during hot days while naturally breaking down into rich food for the plant.
ga: Plantains biɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ amɛbaai wuji kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ahewɔ. Muji ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa muji lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛha tsei.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and turn yellow during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up and yellow as a self-defense reaction to heat and drought. Rolling their leaves reduces the amount of leaf area exposed to direct sunlight, helping the plant hold onto whatever moisture is left in its stem.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa baa lɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: How do bean plants help improve the soil for other crops in my farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bean plants have tiny bumps on their roots called nodules that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into liquid plant food. When the bean plant dies, this extra nitrogen stays behind in the soil to help your next crop grow stronger without buying excess chemical fertilizer.
ga: Bean tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ akɛ nodules ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ tso niyenii ni ji nu. Kɛ ŋmei tso lɛ gbo Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofa ni fa fe nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ.

english: Can cowpea plants grow successfully in dry soil where other crops struggle?
ga: Ani cowpea tsei baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ he ni tsei krokomɛi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, cowpeas are very tough, drought-tolerant crops that have long taproots capable of searching deep underground for water. They also shade the ground quickly, preventing the little moisture in the topsoil from evaporating.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpea ji tso ko ni wa, ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa, ni eyɛ shishifã kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ atao nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya koni ŋmɔtɔ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants covered in green leaves but showing very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich soil, they focus all their energy on growing heavy foliage instead of flowers. To get plenty of pods, cowpeas need balanced soil nutrients and full sunlight to trigger flowering.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo lɛ, tsina tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni tsii ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. koni ená pods babaoo Cowpeas he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekanya fɔfɔi.

english: How can I tell when my dry beans are fully mature and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-kɔfi ni egbi lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Dry beans are ready to harvest when the leaves on the bush turn yellow and drop off, leaving brown, dry pods behind. If you shake a dry pod and hear the seeds rattling clearly inside, the beans are ready to be harvested.
ga: Beni ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Shi ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji okpokpo ŋmɔtɔ ko ni egbi ni onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miihoso yɛ mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my bean leaves develop a powdery white layer on them during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ powder yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease that spreads when humidity is high and plants are packed too closely together. Giving your crops enough space allows fresh air to blow through, keeping the leaves dry and reducing fungal growth.
ga: White powder ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Is it a good idea to plant cowpeas and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ ji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas and maize together is a smart practice called intercropping. The cowpeas cover the soil to block weeds and feed the dirt with nitrogen, while the tall maize grows upward without taking away the cowpeas' underground space.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ ji nifeemɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ intercropping. Cowpea shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli ni ekɛ nitrogen haa shikpɔŋ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ daa ni efiteee ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow and brown at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Corn consumes a lot of nutrients quickly, so applying well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abele kɛ niyenii babaoo tsuɔ nii oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields when I plant corn on the same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Corn feeds heavily on the same soil nutrients year after year, which weakens the land. Rotating corn with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and keeps the land fertile.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ sũ mli niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli babaoo afi fɛɛ afi. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaku esɛɛ ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants stay alive during dry seasons while my corn plants dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yeɔ wala yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mi-abele tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a tough crop with deep roots and thick tubers that store water and nutrients. During dry spells, cassava drops its leaves to conserve moisture and re-grows them when the rains return, whereas corn has shallow roots and needs steady water.
ga: Cassava ji tso ni wa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni toɔ nu kɛ niyenii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni nu he miihia lɛ daa.

english: Why do my tall corn stalks bend and fall over whenever strong winds and heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa?

english: Corn roots grow close to the soil surface and can struggle to hold up tall stalks. Mounding up soil around the base of the stalks—known as earthing up—gives the roots stronger support to stand against wind.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi, ni ale lɛ akɛ potting lɛ baawo shishifãi lɛ ahe hewalɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Can I plant corn and cassava together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because corn grows rapidly and is ready for harvest in about three months, while cassava grows slowly at the start. Once you harvest the corn, the cassava has plenty of room to spread out and mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ, eshɛɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Kɛji okpa ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaná he babaoo ni egbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning and turning brown in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or banana next to young cocoa protects them from harsh sun and keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ŋmɛɛɛ amɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ kookoo ni mli jɔ he lɛ baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branches before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Blackened cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, shaded conditions. Pruning dense branches and weeding around the base lets sunlight and air in, which prevents moisture from trapped fungi.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmeii ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have missing kernels and empty spots when I peel the husk back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii lɛ elaaje kɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli beni mifoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Empty spots on a corn cob mean poor pollination, which happens if hot, dry weather damages the delicate corn silks during flowering. Planting corn in blocks rather than single rows helps wind carry pollen efficiently to all the silks.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ pollination ehiii. Enɛ baa mli kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ fite ŋmãa siliki ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ blɔki mli moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ yaa siliki lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves naturally turning yellow and falling off, and the ground right around the stem base starting to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaayɔse akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do cassava tubers start spoiling and turning dark if I leave them in the ground too long after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ diŋ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fully mature cassava tubers absorb excessive water from soaked soil. If the soil remains saturated with water, the tubers cannot breathe, causing them to rot underground before you can harvest them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ gbalaa nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu lolo lɛ Tubers nyɛŋ amu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa seedlings burning and turning brown in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains around them creates a canopy that blocks harsh sun rays and retains moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ Tsei ni haa hulu la tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baaha hulu la ni naa wa lɛ aba shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow along the middle vein?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of lower leaves is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay dark green and grow heavy cobs, so applying well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot under the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits on flat, heavy soil without draining away, it drowns the roots and encourages soil fungi that cause the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsii nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences water stress. Without constant moisture and moderate temperatures, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo aduawai.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines off the ground using wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the growing subterranean tuber through sunlight. Staking lifts the vines into the open air so every leaf catches maximum sunlight, preventing leaf rot and producing bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. Nɔ ni fata staking he ji wain tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛyaa he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni amɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Why should I cut away the smaller shoots growing at the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: If too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they fight over the same soil food and water, resulting in tiny fruit bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong plants that yield large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji plantain tsei lɛ dara kɛbɔle Tso titri kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Amɛbaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii bibii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baawo yibii wuji ni tsii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas make my soil better for the maize I will plant next season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil. When the cowpea roots decompose, that extra nitrogen stays in the earth to feed the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Beni cowpea shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Curled, wrinkled pepper leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap or spreading a leaf curl virus. Controlling these insects early protects the fresh foliage from twisting.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu lɛ loo amɛgbɛɔ baa curling virus lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai heei lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it better for my crop yields if I water my vegetable garden early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ebaahi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plant roots to absorb water before the sun gets hot. Afternoon watering causes most water to evaporate into the air before reaching the roots and can stress hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into white powder with small holes after sitting in storage for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ

english: Small insects called maize weevils bore into dry corn kernels to feed on the inner starch and lay eggs. Thoroughly drying maize before storage and keeping it sealed in airtight sacks prevents weevils from damaging the grain.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ corn weevils lɛ boteɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmãa mli ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmãa. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛto ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if I choose not to apply any chemical spray on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mihala akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieee nɔ?

english: Without protection or proper pest management, insects like capsids and fungal diseases like black pod can quickly attack your crop, destroying up to 80% of your harvest and weakening the trees over time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsĩii tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa loo akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids kɛ fungal helai tamɔ black pods baanyɛ atutua onibii oya. Efiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni shɛɔ 80% ni ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp shade; clearing heavy weeds, pruning branches, and removing infected pods helps keep it under control.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tso ni shwieɔ jwɛi ni tsii kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. baaye abua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: Why do officers ask us to cut down cocoa trees that have swollen shoot disease instead of treating them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ biɔ ni wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei ni ŋmeii efuu lɛ moŋ fe ni wɔkɛ tsofa baatsa amɛ lɛ?

english: Swollen shoot is caused by a virus that has no chemical cure; cutting down and removing the infected trees is the only proven way to prevent the virus from spreading through insects to the healthy trees on your farm.
ga: Virus ko ni bɛ tsofa tsamɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei ni efuu baa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ amɛ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kooloi amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it harmful to prune or cut off branches from my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, light pruning helps the tree by opening up the canopy to let in sunlight and air, which reduces disease moisture and encourages the tree to direct its energy into producing pods.
ga: Dabi, tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ ni egbeleɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short, fragile roots that need continuous moisture from regular rainy seasons to settle; dry soil and direct hot sun dehydrate them before their root systems can fully develop.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni waaa ni biɔ nu ni yaa nɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ amɛmli dani amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does heavy rainfall right after I put fertilizer on my farm affect my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer off the topsoil or drains it too deep into the ground before the crop's roots have a chance to take in the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ loo ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava on the same plot of land where my young cocoa trees are planted?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is best to avoid planting cassava close to young cocoa because cassava roots feed aggressively on soil nutrients and moisture, which starves the delicate young cocoa trees.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ waa. Enɛ baaha kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agboi.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to keep large shade trees on our cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ wɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting cocoa leaves from hot sun stress, helping the soil retain moisture during long dry spells, and creating a stable environment for cocoa growth.
ga: Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. ni efee shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛha kookoo lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a lot of flowers, but only a few turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi tsei fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Many flowers drop off if there are not enough tiny insects like midges to pollinate them, or if the tree lacks adequate water and soil nutrients to feed all the pods at once.
ga: Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ shikome.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning pale yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of a nutrient deficiency, such as a lack of nitrogen, or an indication that the soil is waterlogged and preventing the plant roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa, tamɔ nitrogen ni faaa, loo nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the dry weeds on my land before planting my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but it burns away important nutrients and kills beneficial living organisms in the soil. Leaving cleared weeds to decay naturally adds food back into the soil and helps it hold moisture during dry periods.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Mohu ɔ, a sãa níhi nɛ a he hia wawɛɛ ɔ, nɛ a kpataa níhi nɛ a he hia nɛ a ngɛ zugba a mi ɔ a hɛ mi. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni he tse lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa niyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop turn yellow even though I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil. Giving water is good, but crops also need nutrient-rich soil with good drainage to stay green and healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpa ko, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ hi. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak without bearing good fruit when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ yibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each crop its proper distance allows the roots and stems to grow thick and strong enough to support good fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli: Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua aduawai kpakpai.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every crop gets equal space and sunlight. It also makes it much easier for you to walk through the farm to remove weeds, apply fertilizer, and harvest without damaging the plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ náa hegbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ ooonyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ni ofiteee tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense to protect itself from losing too much water in extreme heat. Once the sun goes down, the leaves should open back up; if they stay curled in the cool morning, the soil is far too dry.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe he kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo ni efiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Esa akɛ baai lɛ agbele ekoŋŋ kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji amɛfo amɛhe yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi tsɔ.

english: How can I tell if holes in my crop leaves are caused by insects or a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo tso hela ko ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ba?

english: Insects physically bite, chew, or cut holes into leaves. Plant diseases usually start as small colored spots, powdery marks, or rotting patches that weaken the leaf until parts of it fall out.
ga: Kplukai ŋmɔɔ, amɛyeɔ, loo amɛfoɔ bu yɛ baai amli. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ shishi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni su tsakeɔ, ŋmeii ni tamɔ powda, loo ŋmeii ni egboi ni haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally restoring soil food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to grow cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, this works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly underground. Once the maize is harvested, the cassava takes over the open space to finish growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Beni ŋmãa lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ agbe naa lɛ, Yucca heɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ nɔ koni egbe ŋmãa lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee tomatoi.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions. Cutting back extra tree branches lets sunlight and dry air reach the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops, like plantains or bananas, planted beside them to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo banana he miihia amɛ. adu yɛ masɛi Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller leaves and lower yields when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for space, sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the maize leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa ni efeɔ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei baai lɛ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass keep them from drying out so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haaa amɛgbi oya tamɔ bɔ ni eji lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shades the ground from the direct sun. This prevents moisture from evaporating quickly, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil. This acts as a natural food supply that feeds the soil and helps nearby crops like maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing holes in my maize leaves and leaving powdery dirt inside the center of the stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ feɔ bu?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the central growing funnel of the maize plant to feed on young leaves. Checking fields early and using recommended treatments like organic extracts or targeted pesticides can prevent major crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii, tamɔ tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ bɔɔ nii amli loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Abaanyɛ atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni laajeɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and growing small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus spread by them. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or proper spraying keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ ni sa loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots so they cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Mulching the ground and keeping the soil evenly moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its blooms so they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ahaa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to gather energy through their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground and exposed to light, which sends food down to make the yam tubers big and healthy.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛbua hewalɛ naa kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akagbee shikpɔŋ ni la akashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa niyenii baa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee agboi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the soil and prevent roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaba ni amɛbaye nii.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops now compared to when I first cleared the virgin forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe be mli ni mijie koo ni bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Every harvest removes nutrients from the soil. Over time, without replacing those nutrients through compost, animal manure, or proper fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and exhausted.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shoo ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from prolonged dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks. Ensuring the trees have proper shade and adequate soil moisture helps keep flowers on the branch.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ni akwɛɔ koni tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and need protection from direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Leaving some large trees provides living shade to keep the environment cool and moist for the young plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛbiɔ ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda lɛ ekomɛi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hidden inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa? kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm. The caterpillars feed inside the tender central whorl of the maize plant during the day, which damages the leaf growth if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ baafite baai lɛ adalɛ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. These insects suck sap from the leaves and can spread plant viruses that stunt overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei ahe helai ni haaa amɛdalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: If too many young shoots grow together, they compete with the main plant for food and water. Removing extra shoots allows the plant to send all its energy into producing one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei wuji ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Cassava is ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Cassava efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering patterns where the soil gets too dry and then too wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even if it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from dry topsoil. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass (mulching) helps trap moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting at the tip and moving down the middle, it means the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the essential plant food that creates green leaves and gives the crop strength to form big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni feɔ baai eŋɔli ni ehaa tsei hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni wa.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and thin without producing many fruits when I plant them under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to make food for flowering and fruiting. When planted under heavy shade, the crop stretches upward trying to reach light, using all its energy on tall stems instead of branches and peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo. Kɛji adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baagbala ehe kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔɔ koni ekɛ la aha. Hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Moŋ lɛ, okɛ tsei tsei kɛ ŋmɔtɔ atsu nii.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees dry up and fall off instead of forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree suffers from dry weather, lack of soil food, or when tiny insects called midges are not available to pollinate them. Without pollination or enough water, the tree drops flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Anyɛɛɛ afee nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ pollination. Kɛji akɛ pollination loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato fruits crack open on the sides before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when a long dry spell is followed by sudden heavy watering or rain. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to split open.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu loo nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil when heavy rains stay long on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits in the field for too long, the roots choke from lack of oxygen, allowing rot-causing fungi and bacteria in the wet soil to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams spoil in the soil instead of sprouting when planted during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ kɛ́ adu yɛ he ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam sets enter a natural sleeping period called dormancy when soil is hot and dry. If the soil stays extremely hot, the unsprouted seed yam loses moisture and gets damaged by heat, making it easy for soil pests to cause rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes boteɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lolo lɛ, sweet potato dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lɛ baafite ŋmɔtɔ ni latsaa lɛ baafite amɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akɛ amɛbaafite.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many young plantain shoots grow around one main plant, they all fight for the same soil nutrients and water. Cutting away extra shoots leaves energy for the main plant to grow a heavy bunch.
ga: Beni plantain tsei bibii lɛ daraa yɛ Tso titri kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves fold up and droop in the middle of the afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun, usually bouncing back once the afternoon cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ yiŋtoo ko shwieɔ tsei anɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ beni shwane lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my dried harvested maize grains turn into powdery white dust after sitting in the crib for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ batsɔ sũ yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda beni mita saatso lɛ nɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils and small insects lay eggs inside the stored maize grains. As the young insects hatch and grow, they eat the inside of the dry kernel, leaving behind hollow shells and powdered grain residue.
ga: Grain weevils kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli. Kɛji kooloi bibii fɔ ni amɛdara lɛ Amɛbaaye dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji ŋshɔŋloo ni mli ewo muji kɛ dumɔwui ni afee lɛ powda lɛ pɛ.

english: Why does my freshly harvested cassava spoil and turn dark within three days if it is not processed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa ehee lɛ fite ni efee duŋ yɛ gbii etɛ mli kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii lɛ?

english: Once cassava is pulled from the ground, natural chemical reactions inside the tuber react with oxygen in the air. This rapid self-breakdown causes blue-black streaks and spoilages within 48 to 72 hours unless preserved or processed into dough or flour.
ga: Beni ajieɔ ŋmei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni yɔɔ yitso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ feɔ ekome. Nɛkɛ he ni efiteɔ oya nɛɛ haa bluu-diŋ ŋmɔlɔi kɛ fitemɔ baa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli ja akɛto loo afee lɛ ashikishaŋ loo ashikishaŋ.

english: Why is it important to completely clear all weeds from my land before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Clearing all weeds before planting gives your seeds a fresh start. Without existing weeds competing for soil nutrients and water, your crops can sprout quickly and grow strong from the very beginning.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani odu lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ aje shishi ekoŋŋ. Kɛji jwɛi komɛi bɛ ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ adara oya ni amɛdara waa kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: If I plant my crops in a field that already has small weeds, what will happen to my seedlings?
ga: Kɛ́ midu nii yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni jwɛi bibii yɔɔ mli momo lɛ, mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ?

english: Your seedlings will struggle because existing weeds already have established roots that quickly steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer from your young crop, slowing down its growth.
ga: Odumɔwui lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ waa ejaakɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ momo lɛ etswa shishifãi oya ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How does starting with a clean field make work easier for me later in the season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni mijeɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni ehaa nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo kɛyashiɔ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: When you plant on a clean plot, the weeds that eventually grow back will be very small and few in number by the time you do your first weeding, saving you time, labor, and money.
ga: Beni oduɔ nii yɛ he ko ni he tse Jwɛi ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ naagbee lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa ni amɛyi faaa beni okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa be, mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika baa shi.

english: Should I spray weed control chemicals when the weeds are small or wait until they grow big?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ darako loo mamɛ ni jwɛi lɛ adara?

english: It is best to spray when weeds are still very small. Small weeds require less chemical to destroy, are easier to kill completely, and cause less damage to your crop's roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ beni jwɛi lɛ darako kwraa lolo lɛ. Jwɛi bibii lɛ biɔ tsofai fioo ko pɛ koni amɛfite. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooogbe amɛ fɛɛ. ni ekɛ fitemɔ fioo ko baa tsei shishifãi anɔ

english: When is the best time for me to do the first weeding after planting my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafo jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ beni midu tso ko sɛɛ?

english: You should do your first weeding as soon as tiny weeds start to appear. Removing them early stops them from establishing deep roots and choking your growing crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee oklɛŋklɛŋ jwɛi lɛ kɛji jwɛi bibii komɛi je kpo pɛ. begin to appear Ojie amɛ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ naagbai aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Does applying weed control early protect my soil quality?
ga: Jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ he nitsumɔ Ani ebaaye ebua ni ebu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Yes, controlling weeds early prevents them from drying out the topsoil and draining essential nutrients, keeping the soil rich and healthy for your main crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbi ni ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aya. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why do small weeds harm my crops even if my crop plants are much taller than them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi bibii miiye miŋmɔshi nibii awui lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ kwraa fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Even small weeds hidden beneath tall crops steal water and fertilizer right from the topsoil, which deprives your main crop of the food it needs to produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po ni akɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ ashishi lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ náaa niyenii kpakpai ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why does my field stay clean for a longer time if I weed early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishia lɛ mli tseɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛji mijie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Early weeding destroys weeds before they can mature and produce seeds. Without new seeds dropping into the dirt, fewer weeds will pop up later in the season.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ekpataa jwɛi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛyaa dumɔwui amli. Kɛji dumɔwui heei komɛi egbeeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Jwɛi fioo pɛ baaje kpo yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: How does keeping my farm free of weeds affect my harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Te jwɛi ni bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A clean farm ensures that all the natural soil food and added fertilizers go entirely to your crops, resulting in healthy plants and a much larger harvest.
ga: Okwaafoi ni mli tse lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yaa onibii amli kwraa. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: What happens if I delay removing weeds from my field during the early growth stage of my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwie shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Delaying weed removal allows weeds to grow thick roots that pull away vital resources, causing your crops to become yellow, weak, and stunted in growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha jwɛi lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse ni heɔ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛdalɛ baafee mlɛo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the plant roots are receiving too much water. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the crop develop strong, green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eŋɔli.

english: How can I test if my soil has enough moisture to plant seeds after the rain falls?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛdu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a small handful of soil into a ball in your palm; if it holds together lightly without dripping water and breaks apart when gently poked, it has the right moisture for seed germination.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛ wɔkɛ wɔhe kpɛtɛ he blɛoo ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ fioo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive tender leaves that burn under strong, direct sunlight. Planting plantain trees alongside cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nuɔ he waa. Plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant the seeds very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the crops to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems, smaller harvests, and an easier spread of plant diseases between crowded leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite hulu la ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii. Nikpamɔ lɛ faaa kwraa. Ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ahe baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ateŋ oya.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open from root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yams rot easily if they get bruised or cut during harvest, or if they are stored in warm, damp places with poor airflow where mold and bacteria thrive on damaged skins.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa yɛ hewolo ni efite lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tall maize plants easily fall over whenever strong winds blow across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize falls over in strong winds when its roots are shallow or weak, which often happens if seeds are planted too close to the surface or if soil around the base of the stem is not mounded up during weeding.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛbɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ atooo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper and vegetable leaves curl up during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ greens lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up in the hot afternoon heat to conserve water by shrinking the surface area exposed to the sun. If the leaves unfold again by morning, the plant is simply protecting itself from dry weather.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to absorb nutrients, water, and sunlight faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛ nuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when air temperatures get extremely high, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus that help flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Aloo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crop yields dropping every year even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Farming the same soil repeatedly without resting it or adding fertilizer drains its natural nutrients, leaving less food for your crops each season.
ga: Okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Kɛji akɛ ajɔɔɔɔ he loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do crops grow much stronger and bigger on freshly cleared forest land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa waa ni amɛdaraa waa yɛ koo shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Forest soil builds up rich organic matter and nutrients over many years from fallen leaves, providing a rich natural boost for new plants.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ buaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ amli yɛ afii babaoo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei heei adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is burning my land before planting harmful to my soil in the long run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: While burning clears land quickly, the fire destroys important organic matter and kills beneficial earthworms and microbes that keep soil healthy.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi la fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Beans and groundnuts draw nitrogen from the air into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground so your next maize crop can grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Bɔni afee ni o-mai ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin with small ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli tseee ni eyɛ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, preventing full growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, a nyɛ we nɛ a wa kɛ pi si.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive intense heat and keep moisture in their roots; removing big trees leaves them exposed to burning sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo fioo koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Tsei wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo baa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and take over my field right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with tough roots designed to soak up rainwater and topsoil nutrients faster than domesticated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ mli ni afee koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia.

english: Why does heavy rain carry away the top layer of dirt on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil without leaf cover or tree roots gets washed away by heavy raindrops, taking the most nutrient-rich soil down the hill.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni baai loo tso shishifãi ehàaa nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are crop leaves turning yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil is lacking essential nitrogen, or that waterlogged roots are suffocating and unable to feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do insect pests destroy my crops more during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry conditions weaken plants from lack of water, making them vulnerable targets for hungry insects searching for moisture in green leaves.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitao ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ amli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and wither when I irrigate them with water from the nearby river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: When river water is contaminated by muddy runoff or illegal mining, it carries heavy mud and toxic chemicals that clog soil pores, damage root systems, and block plants from absorbing essential nutrients and clean water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sũ ni hoɔ loo sũ ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ efite faa mli nu lɛ Faa mli nu lɛ hiɛɔ sũ ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni tsiɔ sũ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa. Efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nu ni mli tse.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon heat but stand fresh again every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi ani obaanyɛ onu he akɛ ohe ejɔ bo daa leebi?

english: In hot afternoon sun, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can absorb water from the ground to cool down. Overnight, the plant drinks from the damp soil and restores water pressure inside its leaves.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ. Yɛ gbɛkɛ kome mli lɛ, tsei nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhaa nu lɛ mli hewalɛ baa amɛbaai lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow before the corn yields are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the key food crops need to maintain healthy green foliage and grow large, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn into hard crust that rainwater runs off instead of soaking into?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa beni nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ mli lɛ?

english: Hard soil occurs when organic matter like decayed leaves and compost is cleared away or burned. Organic matter acts like a sponge to keep soil soft, porous, and able to absorb water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa baa kɛji ajie nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ loo ashã. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, ehiɛ ŋmeii, ni enyɛ eŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves above ground but only small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil receives too much nitrogen or excessive early rain, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing top foliage instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ mra Yɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures become too hot, when water supply is inconsistent, or when there are no insects or wind around to help transfer pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ he fɛɛ he. Koni eye ebua ni ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikpaa tsei ni eda lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight which scorches their foliage and dries out the topsoil. Taller trees provide essential shade and humidity needed for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni kookoo tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my crops growing small and thin when I plant maize and cassava close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close causes roots to fight beneath the ground for food and moisture, while leaves block sunlight from each other above ground, resulting in stunted growth for both plants.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ haa hulu la ni jɛɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ egbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight shapes and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves, or by plant viruses transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and greener on my plot than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally aggressive plants designed to steal water, sunlight, and ground nutrients much faster than farm crops, which is why clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni afee koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do many farmers plant plantains on the same land where they want to grow cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo miidu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛdu kookoo yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and provide essential shade to young cocoa seedlings, protecting them from harsh sunlight while giving you food and income while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ waa. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika aha bo be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: I don't have enough money to plant my whole land with cocoa at once, so how can I start small?
ga: Mibɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaadu kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome. No hewɔ lɛ, te abaafee tɛŋŋ aje shishi bibioo?

english: You can clear and plant your land in small sections year by year, using the profits from early food crops like plantain to fund the next section of your farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fãi bibii ni okwɛ nɔ daa afi, ni okɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ niyenii ni aduɔ mra tamɔ plantains mli baa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfi oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it realistic for someone like me with little experience to successfully start a cocoa farm?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mɔ ko tamɔ mi ni bɛ niiashikpamɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aje kookoo ŋmɔ shishi yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Yes, cocoa farming is very manageable if you start step-by-step, plant shade crops first, and follow the proven methods used by experienced farmers in your area.
ga: Hɛɛ, anyɛɔ atsuɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji oje shishi shikome shikome. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ. ni onyiɛ gbɛi ni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them directly under the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu ni mli tse lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct heat and drought; they need temporary shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to keep the air and soil cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he waa. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i

english: What happens to my plantain trees once my cocoa trees grow tall and spread out?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-plantain lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da ni egbɛ eniji lɛ eshwa?

english: As cocoa trees mature and create a full canopy, they block out sunlight for the lower plants, causing the plantains to naturally yield less fruit until they are eventually removed.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ eda ni efee ŋwɛi ŋta ni eyi obɔ lɛ, Kookoo tsei lɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ajieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: How can I make money from my land during the first few years before my cocoa trees start bearing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli dani cacao tsei lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: By intercropping with quick-yielding food crops like plantain, cassava, or cocoyam, you can harvest and sell produce within 9 to 12 months while your cocoa is still growing.
ga: Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ plantains, cassava loo cocoa ni ooodu lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okpa onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli be mli ni o-cocoa lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my entire cocoa farm in one season or do it gradually little by little?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli loo fiofio? Dumɔ fiofio?

english: Planting gradually in phases makes it easier to manage farm labor, lowers your upfront expenses, and allows you to learn from smaller mistakes before scaling up.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ fiofio lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakwɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ shika ni okɛwoɔ hiɛ lɛ nɔ Ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ nii kɛjɛɔ tɔmɔi bibii amli dani okɛ sɛkɛl lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: How do I start over on a piece of farmland where the old crops have stopped producing well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maje shishi ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii momoi ekpa yibiiwoo jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can clear old trees in small portions, plant plantains or cover crops to restore the soil and provide temporary cover, and then introduce new, healthy seedlings step-by-step.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie tsei momoi lɛ yɛ fãi bibii amli. Dumɔ plantains loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi be kukuoo ko. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kpo fiofio.

english: Why does my plantain farm produce less fruit after a few harvests compared to when I first planted it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ ŋmaa fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni midu klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ he

english: Over time, plantain stems multiply and compete for soil nutrients and moisture, which reduces bunch sizes unless you remove excess shoots and add fertilizer or manure.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Plantain tsei lɛ ayi fa babaoo ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha panicle lɛ dalɛ aba shi ja ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: How can I learn the best techniques to get high cocoa yields like the top farmers in my community?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makase ŋaai ni hi fe fɛɛ ni baaha maná kookoo ni fa babaoo tamɔ okwaafoi ni fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can improve your yield by joining local cocoa farmer groups, visiting successful farms to observe their shading and pruning methods, and consulting extension officers regularly.
