ga: Obaanyɛ oya hiɛ yɛ onitsumɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli kookoo okwaafoi akui ni okɛ ohe aaawo mli lɛ nɔ. Yaa ŋmɔji ni yeɔ omanye lɛ amli koni okwɛ bɔ ni amɛfeɔ shading kɛ bɔ ni amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amɛhaa lɛ. ni okɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ hiɛyaa mli lɛ agba sane daa

english: Why does my harvested cassava turn dark and go bad just two days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bafee duŋ ni efite gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots continue to breathe and lose moisture rapidly after harvest. This triggers a natural breakdown process called vascular discoloration, turning the root dark and ruining its taste within 48 to 72 hours unless it is processed into gari or flour.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛshwieɔ nu oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ni atsɛɔ lɛ vascular coloration. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli, ja afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn soft and rot so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes produce a ripening gas called ethylene and have high water content. When packed tightly in hot containers or bruised during transport, the gas accumulates and speeds up decay, causing soft spots and quick rotting.
ga: Tomato jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene, ni nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo tsɛnsii ni mli edɔɔ loo ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛfaa mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Gas lɛ buaa ehe naa ni ehaa efiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa mɔ gbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Why do small insects destroy my dry maize grains even when I keep them stored in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ tsu ko ni aŋã mli moŋ?

english: Maize grains often carry hidden insect eggs from the farm. If the grains are not dried thoroughly below 13% moisture before storage, the warm air in the storage room helps the eggs hatch into weevils that feed on the inside of the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii hiɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shɛɛɛ 13% dani akɛtoɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa wɔji lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli niyenii.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing sprouts and shrinking during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that break their natural rest period when temperatures warm up. As they begin to sprout, they consume their own stored water and nutrients to feed the sprout, which causes the tuber to shrink and turn tough.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni fiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Kɛ amɛbɔi ŋmɔshi nibii Amɛkɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ewaa.

english: Why do my harvested groundnuts develop a bitter mold when I store them in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: If groundnuts are bagged while still slightly damp, heat and moisture get trapped inside the sack. This trapped moisture encourages a dangerous fungus to grow, which produces a bitter, unsafe mold.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo kotoku mli be mli ni amɛmli edɔ fioo lolo lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmeii baatsi kotoku lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli nɛɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmei ko ni mli edɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe baa.

english: What makes my green plantains ripen and turn yellow all at once before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ shwereɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ shikome dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: As plantains mature, they release ethylene gas which speeds up the conversion of starch into sugar. Storing harvested plantains together in warm, unventilated spaces concentrates this gas and causes the entire batch to ripen simultaneously.
ga: Kɛ́ plantains lɛ dara lɛ, ejieɔ ethylene gas, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛfeɔ sugar. Kɛ́ akɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ afee ekome ni eha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ashwere yɛ be kome mli.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my pineapple so it stays sweet and doesn't spoil fast?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ okpa ŋmei lɛ koni ehi jogbaŋŋ lolo ni ekafite oya?

english: Pineapples stop getting sweeter once cut from the plant because they do not store extra starch to convert into sugar. Harvesting them when the base turns slightly yellow ensures maximum natural sweetness and a longer shelf life.
ga: Pineapples kpaɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛtooo ŋmɔtɔ kroko ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ sugar. Nikpamɔ beni shishitoo lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ fioo lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni fe fɛɛ kɛ wala ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my red pepper fruits turn pale and lose color when I dry them directly under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-chili yibii tsuji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ migbi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Direct and harsh sunlight breaks down the natural red pigments in peppers over time. Drying peppers in a warm, shaded, or well-ventilated room preserves their bright red color and keeps their market value high.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli su tsuru ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛsu tsuru ni mli tse lɛ ahi shi, ni ebaaha amɛjara wa waa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why do I need to cover my harvested cocoa beans with banana leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ banana baai haa kookoo ni akpa lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Covering cocoa beans traps heat and starts fermentation, where natural microbes feed on the sugary pulp around the beans. This essential chemical process removes bitterness and develops the deep chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, emɔɔ dɔlɛ lɛ mli ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ hei ni adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ebɔle kɔfi yibii lɛ ahe lɛ, tsofafeemɔ gbɛ ni he hiaa nɛɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does palm oil made from fresh fruit bunches taste sour if I wait too long after harvesting to press them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei fɔ ni akɛ aduawai heei fee lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani okpa lɛ dani okɛmiimi lɛ?

english: Once oil palm fruits are cut from the tree, natural enzymes inside the fruit rapidly break down the fats into free fatty acids. Delaying processing for more than 48 hours causes these acids to build up, giving the oil a sharp, sour taste.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo mu tso lɛ yibii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ Adebɔɔ mli enzymes ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa fɔ oya ni efeɔ fatty acids ni bɛ nyɔmɔwoo. Kɛ́ akɛ nitsumɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo fe ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ acid nɛɛ abɔle ehe. Enɛ haa fɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma.

english: How can I tell which end of a cassava stem cutting should go into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small nodes or bumps along the stem where leaves used to grow. The small leaf buds on those nodes should point upwards toward the sky before you insert the bottom end into the soil; planting them upside down will prevent the plant from growing properly.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii. Nyiɛmɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: The first rain is often a 'false start' followed by a hot dry spell. If you plant right away, the hot dry soil will scorch your germinating seeds before they can grow deep enough roots to find groundwater.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale shishijee’ ni hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ baashã dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ dani amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight. When the leaves get full sun, they make food that travels down to build large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebɔɔ niyenii ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing the extra ones allows all the plant's energy to go into making one large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or taller forest trees above them to act as natural umbrellas until they are older and strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing starting at the bottom of the plant usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant is moving whatever food it has left from the old bottom leaves up to the new leaves at the top to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛmiijɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛmiiya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass on top of the soil around their tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, covers the soil to block the burning sun. This keeps the soil cool and prevents water from evaporating quickly, giving the roots constant moisture.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ daa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that pulls nitrogen from the air and stores it in their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay, that stored food stays in the soil for future crops like maize to use.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata tsei aweku ko ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛtsu nii.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and water so that the main plant can survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tso ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like thrips or aphids are hiding underneath, sucking out the plant's sap and spreading viruses that distort normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ thrips loo aphids, kɛ amɛhe ewo amɛshishi. shwieɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ bɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ amɛshwãa

english: Why do my crops produce much smaller fruits and tubers when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii kɛ bulbs bibii kwraa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to grow big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa amɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients, especially nitrogen. Planting it in the same spot repeatedly drains the soil of those nutrients without giving it time to recover, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my seeds not sprouting even though I planted them and watered the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ ni miwo amɛ nu sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they were buried too deep in the dirt to reach sunlight, or if the soil was kept too wet, which causes the seed to rot before it can shoot up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔ ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its top leaves to survive, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya eŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and displaying yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, yellow-patterned leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It prevents the leaves from trapping sunlight properly, which stops the cassava roots from swelling.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle yucca he lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi cassava shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafuu.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants shrinking and curling upwards into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Upward curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the underside of the leaf. As the leaves lose sap, they dry up and twist upwards.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall trees provide shade and keep the air moist around the seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei kakadaji haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛo. Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. Extreme heat stops the flowers from pollinating properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over so easily as soon as the bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛmiitsii pɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like oak trees; they have shallow root systems that stay near the surface. When the heavy fruit bunch grows, the top weight easily pulls the shallow roots right out of soft wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ odum tsei. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu agbo ko dara lɛ, muji ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baajie shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions, allowing their roots to grab water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: What makes my harvested maize grains go moldy and spoil when I store them inside a shed?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛto mi-shĩa lɛ mli?

english: Grains spoil when stored with too much moisture or in rooms with leaks, because molds and fungi thrive in damp, dark environments that lack fresh air movement.
ga: Ŋmãa fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo yɛ tsu ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni duŋ ewo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does keeping good airflow in my storage room protect my dried yam chips from rotting?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ onitoohe lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ akafite?

english: Continuous airflow reduces heat and humidity build-up in the store, keeping the yams dry and preventing molds and insects from multiplying.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa nɔ etsɔɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Gbimɔ sweet potato lɛ ni otsi ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo

english: Why do my cassava plants get sick and rot if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei yeɔ hela ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, air cannot pass between them easily. This creates trapped moisture around the stems and leaves, which encourages fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔ he babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ nakai tsei lɛ ateŋ mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ baa, ni no woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I squeeze as many plantain suckers as possible into a small space?
ga: Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛji mikɛ plantain tsei babaoo shwie he ko bibioo bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: No, overcrowding forces plants to fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller bunches.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ kui bibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning pale yellow when they grow under big tree shades?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs full sunlight to manufacture its own food and keep its leaves green. Without enough light, the plant starves and turns yellow.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ efee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii ni eha ebaai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Kɛji la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when exposed to full, bright sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate roots and leaves that burn and dry out quickly under harsh sun, so they need temporary shade trees to protect them while they are young.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Enɛ baashã ni ebaagbi oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and drop their leaves when water collects on the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaaji lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to survive. When water stands on the field for too long, it suffocates the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu damɔ ŋmɔ ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Tsi niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa

english: Why do black spots appear on my vegetable leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii diji yɔɔ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil onto the leaves, and the continuous dampness creates the perfect conditions for these spots to spread.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism plants use in high heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and stop water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Leaf curling ji hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni etsĩ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and thin without producing many fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants stretch upward and become spindly when they are trying to search for more sunlight or when high temperatures prevent flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii beni amɛtaoɔ hulu la babaoo lɛ. Aloo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa aahu akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, a key plant food. The plant naturally moves its remaining nitrogen to feed the top young leaves so it can keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ abɛi tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛye ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that works with beneficial soil organisms to capture nitrogen food directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the legume plant dies, that natural nitrogen stays in the soil to nourish the maize crop planted after it.
ga: Peas kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei gboi Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni adu yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their tiny flowers without producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? yɛ yibɔi babaoo mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa efeee?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to carry pollen between them to form pods. If the farm is too dry, lacks organic leaf litter where these insects live, or lacks proper shade, the flowers dry up and drop off without developing into fruit.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges, ni amɛwoɔ pollen yɛ kooloi ateŋ koni amɛfee pods. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Organic leaf litter ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɔ nɔ lɛ ni bɛ. loo hulutsoo ni bɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Special ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: The small extra shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and nutrients. By cutting away the extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones, all the food energy goes directly into making a bigger, heavier bunch of plantain.
ga: Tso bibii krokomɛi (tso) kɛ plantain wulu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ahiɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛfeɔ plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Extreme heat puts severe stress on pepper plants, causing them to lose moisture faster than roots can absorb it. To protect itself and save energy during heatwaves, the plant naturally drops its blossoms instead of trying to nourish new fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe he ni okɛ hewalɛ ato yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ e diɛŋtsɛ ehe moŋ fe ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ aduawai heei.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaves dark waste in the center funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni mishiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This destruction is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the soft, central growing funnel of the maize plant during the day, eating the leaf tissue before it even unfolds.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo mli ni edaa yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ yɛ gbi mli lɛ. ni amɛyeɔ baa mli fãji dani egbɛɔ eshwaa po.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a plant virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. When whiteflies suck sap from the plant, they infect it with the virus, which distorts leaf growth and stops fruits from forming properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji whiteflies miimu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Ebaaŋɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when planted in an open, completely cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni mɛi yɔɔ ni mɛi yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and tender roots that burn easily under full sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside them provides living shade and holds moisture in the air and soil while the young cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause standing water in poorly drained or flat soil, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen, allowing rot-causing organisms in the wet soil to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How can I tell if my yams under the soil are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Yams signal maturity above ground when their vines and leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up completely. This shows that the plant has finished sending energy down into the root and the tuber has reached full growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ beni wain tso lɛ kɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa, ni bulb lɛ egbɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow thin and weak when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe tseee ni amɛhe waaa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are crowded, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight for the same water and soil nutrients, leaving all the plants starved and skinny.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ye hɔmɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii beni shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water during the hottest part of the day. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu akafite yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji tsei adebɔɔ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my vegetable field needs water when the top of the soil looks dry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia nu beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Push your finger about two inches into the soil; if the soil at that depth feels damp and cool, your crops still have water, but if it feels dry and warm, it is time to water.
ga: Nyɛɛ onine nɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai shɔŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni edɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná nu lolo. Shi kɛji enu he akɛ egbi ni edɔ lɛ Be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo nu.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their lower, older leaves when the soil lacks nitrogen or during dry spells so they can save food and water for the growing stem and roots underneath.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi kɛ nɔ ni edara lɛ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Enɛ ji koni enyɛ ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu ato tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my yam vine keep growing long leaves but isn't making big tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji shi ewooo ŋmeii wuji yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes yam vines spend all their energy producing leafy green growth above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are there sticky drops and tiny black insects covering the stems of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ? kɛ kooloi bibii diji ni Haa mi-cowpea tso lɛ shishi

english: Those black insects are aphids sucking sap from your plants, and the sticky liquid is their waste, which attracts ants and encourages black mold to grow on your crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii diji nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ otsei lɛ amli nu lɛ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji jwɛi, ni gbalaa ŋmeii ni ewoɔ ŋmeii diji hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why do my garden eggs get dark rot spots on them during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni egboi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash soil onto the fruits, spreading fungal spores, while high air humidity gives the fungus the moisture it needs to cause fruit rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ shwieɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ naa fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha aduawai lɛ agbo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when daytime temperatures get too high because extreme heat dries out the pollen, preventing the blossom from turning into a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni ekatsɔ tomato.

english: Why should I spread dry palm leaves or cut grass around the base of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ ŋmei tsei ni egbi lɛ ashwã loo mafolɔ jwɛi mabɔle mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya ni etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why is having water the first thing I need to check before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni mikwɛɔ dani miduɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Water is the essential starting point for farming. Seeds cannot sprout and roots cannot absorb soil nutrients without moisture, so you can only successfully plant when you have a reliable water source.
ga: Nu ji he ko ni he hiaa ni akɛjeɔ okwaayeli shishi yɛ. Dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃. Ni shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli kɛji oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ pɛ.

english: If I have access to a river or well, can I plant crops outside the rainy season?
ga: Kɛji oyɛ gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ oyaa faa loo ŋshɔnaa Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, having water allows you to plant crops at almost any time of the year, though you must still watch out for weather extremes like cold temperatures that can harm sensitive crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni oyɔɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei yɛ afi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ, ehe miihia ni ole kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa, ni baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ awui lolo.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow in the savannah region around December?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ Savannah kpokpaa lɛ nɔ yɛ December aaafee lɛ?

english: December brings very cold weather to the savannah region. This severe cold disrupts normal plant growth, causing many crops to struggle even if they are watered.
ga: December kɛ fɛ̃i ni naa wa baa Savannah kpokpaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ fɛ̃i ni naa wa nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu po.

english: Is giving my crops water enough to make them grow well, or does temperature also matter?
ga: Nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo hulutsoo hu he miihia.

english: Water is necessary, but temperature also plays a big role. Even if you give your plants plenty of water, extreme cold weather can still prevent them from thriving.
ga: Nu he hia. Shi dɔlɛ hu tsuɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ ko ni he hiaa he nii. Kɛji akɛ oha tso lɛ nu babaoo po lɛ, Shi kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: How does cold weather affect crop growth compared to warm weather in Ghana?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ saa tsei adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ he?

english: Warm weather encourages steady growth in most crops, whereas sudden or severe cold weather—like December in the savannah—slows down plant growth and keeps crops from developing properly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yaa nɔ amɛdaraa. Kɛji fɛ̃i ba trukaa loo efee fɛ̃i waa, tamɔ December yɛ Savannah lɛ, Ebaaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant groundnuts at any time of the year in Ghana if I have irrigation?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ Ghana be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli kɛji miyɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ.

english: Generally yes, as long as you have enough water, groundnuts can be planted year-round in Ghana, except during the very cold December period in savannah areas.
ga: Ehi, kɛji oyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Abaanyɛ adu ŋmei afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Ghana. Ja December mli be mli ni fɛ̃i waa waa yɛ Savannah kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my groundnuts in the savannah during December?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ Savannah yɛ December mli?

english: Your groundnuts will not thrive. The weather in the savannah gets very cold in December, which prevents groundnut seeds and seedlings from growing healthy.
ga: O peanuts ɔ be hɛ mi. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ Savannah lɛ baanyɛ afee fɛ̃i waa yɛ December mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ waa.

english: Why are groundnuts sensitive to cold weather when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii nuɔ fɛ̃i he waa kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need warmth to sprout and grow strong. Cold weather chills the plants, stalling their growth and reducing your harvest.
ga: Peanuts he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa tsei amli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ dalɛ naa ni ehaa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: If I live in a savannah area, should I wait for the cold December weather to pass before planting groundnuts?
ga: Kɛji mihi Savannah kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni fɛ̃i ni baa yɛ December mli lɛ atsɔ dani madu ŋmeii?

english: Yes, waiting until the extreme cold of December passes gives your groundnuts the warm conditions they need to thrive and produce a good yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛmɔ kɛyashi December mli fɛ̃i be lɛ baaho. No hewɔ lɛ o-peanuts lɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Does groundnut planting depend entirely on the rainy season?
ga: Ani ŋmei ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ nɔ?

english: No, groundnuts do not depend only on rain. If you have an artificial water source like irrigation, you can plant them in almost any month, provided the weather isn't too cold.
ga: Dabi, jeee nugbɔ pɛ nɔ ŋmeii damɔɔ. Kɛji oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni akɛfee, tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ, obaanyɛ odu nɔ ni miihe ashɛ daa nyɔŋ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ tsɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight overheats them and dries out the soil quickly. Planting shade crops like plantain or banana around them creates cover and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ fe nine ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ sũ awo mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water in the hot afternoon sun. By rolling up, the leaf reduces its exposed surface area to conserve moisture until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Beni amɛkpãa amɛhe lɛ, baai lɛ baa shi yɛ he ni amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ nɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomatoes often shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. When the plant feels stressed by extreme heat or drought, it drops flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛ tsei miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ mli lɛ Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: This yellow pattern indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is necessary for plants to stay green and grow, so adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia koni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it beneficial for my soil if I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Ani ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting leguminous crops like cowpeas with maize improves soil fertility. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which helps feed neighboring crops naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ. Legumes lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to produce large, healthy ears.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: How does covering my soil with dry grass help my crops grow during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, reduces soil temperature, and stops weed growth. This helps crop roots stay cool and hydrated during hot dry periods.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa baa shi ni ekpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because sitting water blocks oxygen from reaching the roots. Without air in the soil, harmful fungi thrive and cause the tubers to decay underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Fungi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are there small holes in my cassava leaves and why are the leaves curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ebaai lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by small pests like green mites or mealybugs feeding on the plant's sap. Using healthy, disease-free planting stems and keeping the farm free of weeds helps reduce these pest attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ green mites loo mealybugs ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii, ni aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ atutuamɔi aba shi.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting and shrinking while kept in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi shweremɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni mikɛtoɔ shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally break dormancy after a few months to try and grow again. As they sprout, they use up their stored water and starch, causing the tuber to shrink; storing them in a cool, well-ventilated yam barn slows this process down.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni baafo wɔɔhe lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ koni amɛka amɛkwɛ ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ. beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ Amɛye nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato lɛ fɛɛ. ha yitso lɛ afee bibioo Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why is it more important for me to fix my watering setup before doing other field tasks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi waa akɛ matsu nu he saji ahe nii dani matsu ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Crops cannot absorb nutrients or survive without adequate water. Water is the primary engine for plant growth, so securing a reliable water supply first ensures that fertilizer, land preparation, and labor investments are not wasted.
ga: Tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai loo amɛhi shi kɛji nu ni fa bɛ amɛ. Nu ji gbɛ titri ni haa tsei daa. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni anáa klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kɛ nitsumɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ akafite.

english: How do I know if my crops are wilting from drought or suffering from too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ mli?

english: If crops are dry and lack water, the soil will feel hard and leaves will droop and dry up. If there is too much water, the soil will be soggy and leaves will turn pale yellow because drowned roots cannot breathe or take in nutrients.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baawa ni baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi. Kɛji nu fa babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ ni baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ejaakɛ shishifãi ni ebote mli lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Lightly watering every day keeps moisture in the topsoil, but heavy, less frequent watering encourages roots to grow deep into the soil where water stays longer, making plants stronger during dry spells.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo daa gbi lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi nu ni mli wa Bei pii lɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni nu lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Haa tsei lɛ ahe waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli

english: Should I plant all my crops on the same day, or is it better to plant them in batches over several weeks?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ loo ehi akɛ madu amɛ yɛ kui amli yɛ otsii babaoo mli?

english: Planting in batches spreads out your harvest over time. This prevents all your crops from maturing at once, making harvesting easier to manage and protecting you from sudden drops in market prices.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ kui amli lɛ baaye abua ni ogbɛ okpamɔ lɛ ashwã yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ anaa shikome. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo feɔ mlɛo ni ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ jara ni baa shi trukaa lɛ he.

english: Why do some of my crops grow faster than others even though I planted them on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daa oya fe ekrokomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Small variations in soil nutrients, sunlight exposure, depth of planting, or moisture across your field cause plants to mature at slightly different rates.
ga: Sũ mli niyenii srɔtoi fioo, hulu la, dumɔ mlibotemɔ. Aloo, hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ haa tsei daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo nɔ.

english: What happens to my farm if I prepare the land early but delay planting the seeds?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mra? Shi dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Clearing the land exposes the bare soil to the hot sun, drying out essential soil moisture. Delaying planting also gives weeds a chance to sprout first and steal nutrients before your crops take root.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ agbi. Dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hu haa jwɛi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi.

english: If I harvest my vegetables bit by bit as they mature, will it damage the remaining crop?
ga: Kɛ mikpa aduawai fiofio beni amɛdaraa lɛ, Ani ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: No, harvesting mature fruits continuously actually helps the plant by freeing up energy and nutrients to feed the remaining green fruits and encourage new flowers to grow.
ga: Dabi, aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ yeɔ aduawai ni eshwɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ. ni ewo fɔfɔi heei hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why do my young crops dry up so quickly if the rain stops early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top layer of soil. If rains stop early, the topsoil dries up fast and the short roots cannot reach deeper soil moisture.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa oya lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni shishifãi kukuji lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ sũ mli nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: How long does it usually take for fast-growing crops like pepper or okra to start producing after planting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmeii loo okra lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ nii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fast-growing vegetables like pepper and okra usually begin flowering and producing harvestable fruit within two to three months after planting, provided they receive steady water and light.
ga: Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ okra Bei pii lɛ amɛjeɔ fɔfɔi shishi ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Esa akɛ amɛná nu kɛ kane daa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when rain water gathers and sits on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water blocks oxygen from reaching the plant roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop feeding the plant, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ ebaakpa tsei lɛ niyenii Enɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why did my watermelon plants droop and die just a few hours after I sprayed them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon tso lɛ gbo ni egbo yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Watermelons have very soft, tender leaves that absorb liquids quickly. If you spray them with an incorrect or overly strong chemical, it destroys the plant's internal cells almost immediately, causing rapid wilting and leaf burn.
ga: Watermelon yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ okɛ tsofa ni ejaaa loo ni mli wa tsɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, Ekpãtãa tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ ahiɛ aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa oya ni ebaa shãa.

english: Can using the wrong spray on my farm kill my crops completely?
ga: Ani tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa?

english: Yes, crops have different tolerance levels. Chemicals designed for tough crops like maize or cassava will easily burn and kill sensitive vegetables like watermelons, tomatoes, or peppers.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei yɛ bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha lɛ srɔtoi. Tsofai ni afee aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaashã ni egbe aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ watermelon, tomato, loo ŋmɔtɔ oya.

english: Why do some crop leaves burn when I apply farm chemicals under strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ahe baai shãa kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai tsu nii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: When you spray in intense heat, the water in the spray evaporates quickly, leaving concentrated chemical droplets on the leaves. The sun heats up these droplets, acting like tiny magnifying glasses that burn the plant leaf.
ga: Kɛ okɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shwie nɔ lɛ Nu ni yɔɔ shwiemɔ mli lɛ baaho oya. Eshiɔ tsofa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Hulu lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ mli dɔɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibioo ko ni shãa tsei ahe baai.

english: What are the early signs that my crops are having a bad reaction to a chemical I sprayed?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee nɔ ko ni ehiii yɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Watch out for sudden curling of the leaf edges, yellow or black burnt spots appearing on the leaves, rapid drooping of stems, or leaves turning dry and crispy within a few hours of spraying.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shãa he ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya. Aloo baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can my crops recover if they start drying up right after I spray them?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ebɔi gbimɔ?

english: If only a few outer leaves are slightly burnt, the plant might produce new leaves with proper care. However, if the main stems collapse and leaves dry up within hours, the plant's leaf cells are ruined and cannot recover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ shã fioo Kɛji akwɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ ajie baai heei. Shi, kɛji tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ fite ni baai lɛ gĩ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli lɛ, Tso lɛ baa mli wala yibii lɛ fiteɔ ni enyɛŋ ehi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Does washing crop leaves with clean water immediately after a bad spray help save them?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ tsofa ni ehiii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni etsa lɛ?

english: If done within minutes of spraying before the leaf absorbs the chemical, rinsing thoroughly with clean water can dilute the liquid and reduce the severity of the chemical burn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashwie tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ minitii fioo komɛi amli dani baai lɛ ŋɔ tsofa lɛ, Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse shwie nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ mli agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tsofa lɛ shãa lɛ mli awa lɛ aba shi.

english: Will putting more chemical into my knapsack sprayer kill pests faster without harming my crop?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ misɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ oya ni eyeee miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: No, putting extra chemical beyond the recommended rate turns medicine into poison. Overdosing damages the crop's leaves and roots, which can stunt growth or kill the plant entirely.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛfataa he fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ afee tsofa ni gbeɔ mɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa nɛɛ tsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaafite tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dalɛ naa loo eha tso lɛ agbo kwraa.

english: How do I know if a spray sold at the market is safe for my specific vegetable crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji jarayeli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mi-vegetable tsei pɔtɛɛ lɛ?

english: Always check the chemical container's label to see if your specific crop is listed under approved uses. If the crop is not listed, the chemical is not safe for it.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe saji lɛ be fɛɛ be koni ona kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ yɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ateŋ. Kɛji atsɔɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ko Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ tsofai lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are vegetable crops more easily destroyed by spray chemicals than crops like cocoa or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai anɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Vegetables have thin, watery leaves and soft stem tissue with thin protective coatings. Cereal and tree crops have thick, waxy coatings on their leaves that protect them better from chemical burns.
ga: Aduawai lɛ yɛ baai bibii, ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli kɛ tsei yɛ ŋmei ni mli tse ni buɔ tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni shãa lɛ ahe.

english: What is the best time of day to spray my crops so they don't get stressed or damaged?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikahao loo mifite?

english: The best times are early morning before the sun gets strong or late afternoon. During these cooler periods, the plant leaves absorb the liquid safely without the risk of high heat burning the crop.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi dani hulu lɛ mli wa loo shwane mli. Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baai lɛ baaŋɔ nu lɛ shweshweeshwe ni oshara ni ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baashã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to plant my yams in raised mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji amli moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow underground and need loose, soft soil to expand properly. Building mounds loosens the earth so the tuber can grow large without restriction, while also providing good drainage so the crop does not rot in waterlogged soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ adara ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei fiteee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Training the leaves upward on stakes allows them to absorb maximum sunlight, which the plant turns into energy to feed and expand the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ atsɔse baai lɛ ni amɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni tso lɛ baatsake lɛ efee hewalɛ ni ekɛye shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni ekɛgbala amɛmli

english: Why do the leaves on my yam plant turn yellow and dry up toward the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a natural sign that the yam crop has reached maturity. The plant stops growing green leaves and moves all its remaining energy down into the underground tuber, letting you know it is time to harvest.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ eda. Tso lɛ kpaɔ baai eŋɔlii lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ ole akɛ nikpamɔ be eshɛ.

english: What makes some yam tubers grow very big while others on the same land stay small?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato tsei komɛi daraa waa ni ekrokomɛi hu daraa bibii yɛ he kome?

english: Tuber size depends on how much sunlight, moisture, and soil nutrients each plant gets, as well as the size and quality of the seed yam you planted in the mound.
ga: Bulb lɛ dalɛ damɔ hulu la, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji sweet potato dumɔwui ni oduɔ yɛ okpɔŋɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni ehi ha.

english: What happens to my crop if I put my mounds too close together on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ gɔji to mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When mounds are spaced too closely, the growing leaves shade each other from the sun and the roots fight for the same soil nutrients, which leads to smaller yams and lower overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ muji ni ato lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Baai ni miida lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe baawuu koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akpa yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How do I know how many mounds my land can support for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gɔji enyiɛ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua nikpamɔ kpakpa?

english: The number of mounds depends on giving each plant enough space to spread its roots and leaves. Measuring proper distances between mounds ensures every crop gets equal access to water, soil nutrients, and sunlight.
ga: Pii lɛ ayibɔ damɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ahaa tso fɛɛ tso koni eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ asusu gbɛ ni sa ni kã gɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ náa nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Why does a piece of land produce different amounts of crops depending on how I lay out the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi lɛ? Ani edamɔ bɔ ni mikɛ gɔŋ lɛ toɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Proper mound arrangement ensures efficient land use and prevents soil erosion. A well-planned layout gives each crop enough room to thrive while allowing you to fit the optimal number of plants on your plot.
ga: Gɔji ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Gbɛjianɔtoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okɛ tsei ayibɔ ni sa fe fɛɛ woɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I estimate how much crop yield I will harvest from my total land size?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni makpa kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can estimate your total yield by counting the number of mounds you planted per acre and multiplying that by the average weight of yams a single mound produces in good soil conditions.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ gɔji enyiɛ ni oduɔ yɛ acre kome mli lɛ ni oookane lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sweet potatoes ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome baanyɛ ajie yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ lɛ mlijaa mlijaa lɛ abɔ he.

english: Why do I need to know the total number of mounds on my farm before calculating my profits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni male gɔji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ dani mabu sɛɛnamɔi ni baaná lɛ he akɔntaa lɛ?

english: Counting your total mounds tells you how many total tubers you are likely to harvest. Knowing your total production allows you to calculate your total earnings against your expenses so you know if you made a profit or a loss.
ga: Kɛ́ okane o-pile lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo ŋmeii ayibɔ fɛɛ ni ekolɛ obaakpa. Nibii ni afee lɛ fɛɛ ni ole lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ shika ni anáa kɛ shika ni afiteɔ lɛ he akɔntaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ole kɛji oná sɛɛnamɔ loo ofite nii.

english: How long does a yam crop usually take from planting to harvest time?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani aduɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa?

english: Most yam varieties take between 6 to 9 months from the time you plant the seed yam in the mound until the tuber is fully developed and ready to be dug up.
ga: Sweet potato henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9 kɛjɛ be mli ni oduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kwraa ni amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakumɔ.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to build a larger tuber underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Staking baaye abua ni awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas between my maize rows reduce the weeds on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas spread along the ground and form a thick green carpet that blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds. This stops weeds from growing while also adding natural nitrogen to the soil to feed your maize.
ga: Cowpeas gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efeɔ kapɛti eŋɔli ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekɛha o-corn lɛ niyenii.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or infected stems used for planting. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi susuɔ akɛ eji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa lɛ.

english: What is eating holes into the leaves and central funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji niyeli bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of maize. Catching them early and applying bio-pesticides or recommended sprays inside the leaf funnel will protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai amli ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Yellowing in a V-pattern on lower leaves shows that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is needed for healthy green growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ V yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-ŋmei lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during very hot days without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants get hot and thirsty, they shed their flowers to protect themselves from dying. Watering the base of the plants early in the morning helps them hold onto flowers so they can produce peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ pepper tso lɛ mli edɔ ni kumai miiye lɛ Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ ashishi nu lɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Planting maize on the same spot repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Alternating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii momo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I save and replant the seeds from my hybrid maize harvest next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ato ni madu ekoŋŋ?

english: Saving and replanting hybrid maize seeds leads to weak growth and much lower yields in the second year. Buying fresh certified seeds each season guarantees strong plants and high yields.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shweremɔ ni waaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ naa nɔmimaa.

english: How do I know when my maize is completely ready to harvest for drying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa koni egbi?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and a small dark layer forms at the tip of each kernel where it joins the cob. Harvesting at this point prevents grain rot and insect attacks in storage.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naagbee he ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni kooloi akatutua amɛ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Big shade trees act like natural umbrellas that keep the air cool, hold moisture in the soil, and protect the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni obu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get too hot, lack water, or miss key nutrients in the soil. When the plant experiences stress, it sheds flowers to save energy for its own survival instead of spending it on making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ, nu faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei kɛ haomɔ kpe Efɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to get as much sunlight as possible. When you give them stakes to climb, their leaves can spread out to catch light and air, which helps the plant make more food and produce larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ oha tso lɛ kwɔ Amɛbaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni ekɛ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii babaoo ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai ni miida lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source in the soil. Without enough nitrogen, the leaves cannot stay green or produce the energy the plant needs to grow tall and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi eŋɔli loo amɛjie hewalɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Heavy rain makes standing water sit in the soil, which cuts off the air supply to the cassava roots. Without air in the soil, tiny fungi and bacteria grow quickly and turn the solid cassava roots into soft, decayed waste.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni kɛyaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Fuji bibii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaatsɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni wa lɛ etsɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fiteɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass over the soil help my vegetable crop survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, blocking direct sunlight from evaporating the moisture underneath. This keeps the ground cool and moist for a longer time, allowing your crops to drink water even during hot, dry spells.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ po.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot uses up the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows maize pests to settle in permanent homes. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts helps restore soil nutrients and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ ekɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii daa afi. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli ŋmeii lɛ toɔ amɛshiai amli daa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and fall over when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward rapidly to steal light from their neighbors, making their stems thin, weak, and easily broken by heavy rain or wind.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛju kane kɛjɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ adɛŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo, egbɔjɔɔ ni nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra small stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ mɛi krɛdɛɛi komɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Midumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: The small stems, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main mother tree. By removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones, the main tree gets all the strength it needs to produce large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baaná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do holes keep appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by leaf-eating pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillars lay eggs in the soft center of the young plant, and as the larvae hatch, they chew through the emerging leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛyeɔ baai ni jeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are missing essential plant food like nitrogen, which gives leaves their green color. Adding manure or well-rotted compost helps feed the plant so the leaves stay healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ niyenii koni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee eŋɔli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out easily under harsh sun. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade and holds moisture in the air to protect the young trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Niyenii nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops end up fighting each other for soil food, water, and sunlight. Giving each seed proper space allows every plant to grow strong stems and produce big ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa ŋmeii ni wa ni ewoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why does my cassava grow lots of leafy stems but leaves very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tso ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much leafy plant food or if plants are shaded, the cassava puts all its energy into growing tall above ground. Cutting away excess shade and ensuring loose, well-drained soil helps energy go down into swelling the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji niyenii ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo loo ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Kasava lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Kɛ́ ajie hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ hewalɛ aba shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ baafu.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and drop off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the plant experiences severe heat or sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil covered with dry grass or mulch keeps the roots cool and moist, helping flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli dɔ loo egbi trukaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Ye obua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest when I plant maize on the same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally and gives the soil a chance to recover.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant beans alongside my maize, or will the beans steal food from the maize?
