ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi? Aloo ani ŋmeii lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: Beans and maize work as good partners because beans capture nitrogen from the air and share it with the soil. This natural food boosts the growth of the surrounding maize while covering the ground to stop weeds.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jaa. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ daa. yɛ be mli ni ekɛ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekpa jwɛi lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to wake up and drink in early rainwater faster than cultivated seeds. Clearing weeds early in the season stops them from stealing the water and nutrients meant for your crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛte shi ni amɛnu nugbɔ nu oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cabbage plants filled with small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by tiny caterpillars or insects feeding on the soft tissue. Checking under the leaves early and applying simple neem water sprays can keep pests away before they ruin the head.
ga: Holes in cabbage leaves are often caused by tiny caterpillars. loo kooloi ni yeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ mra kɛ neem nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mlɛo Ebaanyɛ eha kooloi ni yeɔ fãji lɛ akabote mli dani amɛfite bulb lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly after I collect them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they get bruised during digging or if they are stored in hot, unventilated rooms. Storing uninjured yams on open wooden racks in a shaded, airy shed keeps them cool and dry for many months.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Storing uninjured sweet potatoes on open wooden shelves in a shaded, airy shed. Enɛ haa amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the topsoil. Leaving a few large shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa trees until they mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: What causes my tomato flowers to dry up and drop off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing consistent moisture and light shade during very hot weather helps flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be ha fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize crop turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer helps the maize stay green and yield well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔji ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize crop make my soil better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and puts it naturally into the soil. This feeds the soil and enriches it for the maize plants grown alongside or after them.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni adu yɛ emasɛi loo yɛ esɛɛ lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, their roots compete heavily for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Giving stems enough space allows underground roots room to expand into large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifã ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli alɛɛ ni etsɔ tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to make raised mounds of soil before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep and wide underground, so soft, raised soil mounds make it easy for tubers to expand without hitting hard ground. Mounding also prevents excess water from collecting around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ. Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ blɛoo lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Mounding hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Covering the ground with dry plant materials, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture in the ground during dry spells, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I loosen hard soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mijie shikpɔŋ ni wa dani midu lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil creates air spaces that allow roots to spread easily, absorb nutrients, and drink water. Soft soil also helps rainwater soak deep into the earth instead of washing away topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo lɛ baa. Gbalamɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni onu nu. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ hu haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeefɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the underside of young leaves. Treating plants early with organic sprays like neem oil or recommended insecticides stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer when the soil is dry or right after a rain?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil right after a rain because water dissolves the nutrients so roots can absorb them quickly. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can burn plant roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow starting from the leaf tip downward when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential plant food needed to keep leaves green and build strong stalks.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛma ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any peppers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo pepper yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress pepper plants, causing them to drop their flowers to save water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ akɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛba fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big bushy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much manure or plants are spaced too closely, cassava puts all its energy into leaf and branch growth instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo loo akɛ tsei ebɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ niji ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee yitso ni tsii.

english: This black patch is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually because of irregular or inconsistent watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sun; high canopy trees provide vital shade and hold moisture in the air to protect the seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli nu shwieɔ shi koni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my sorghum seeds rot in the soil after heavy rainfall instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to sprout. When heavy rain leaves the soil waterlogged, oxygen is blocked, causing the seeds to drown and rot underground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaatsi oxygen lɛ naa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my cowpea crop have plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pea pods lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas make their own nitrogen in the soil. Adding extra nitrogen fertilizer tricks the plant into growing leaves continuously instead of forming flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baawo baai lɛ adalɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines curling up and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense reaction by the yam plant when tiny sap-sucking insects or viruses attack, which weakens the plant and slows down tuber growth.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ko ni sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ kɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu loo helai bibii tutua amɛ, ni no haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tuber lɛ daalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold down and droop during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves fold down during the hottest hours to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the direct sun, helping the plant conserve internal water.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ amɛmli.

english: Why do my millet crops grow healthier when I plant groundnuts alongside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-millet lɛ he wa fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii fata he lɛ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil through their roots, which feeds and strengthens neighboring crops like millet.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ amɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut down my old cocoa trees if they are still giving me a few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ? Akɛni kookoo tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii komɛi lolo kɛha mi hewɔ lɛ?

english: Old or sick cocoa trees yield fewer pods over time and can spread viral diseases to nearby healthy farms. Cutting them down allows you to clear diseased roots and plant high-yielding hybrid seedlings that will produce far more pods in a few years.
ga: Cacao tsei ni egbɔ loo ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Kɛji ofo amɛ lɛ, obaanyɛ ojie shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okwɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni baaha ŋmeii babaoo aba yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact same spots where I just cut down old cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni mifo kookoo tso momo lɛ yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to plant in slightly different spots or wait a while after clearing old trees. The roots of old trees can leave behind pests or diseases in the soil, and the soil directly around the old root system is often depleted of essential nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo loo ooomɛ minitii fioo komɛi beni ojie tsei momoi lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Tso shishifãi ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashi tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi momo lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong direct sunlight and high heat. Without temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to cover them, their tender leaves scorch and their shallow roots dry out quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ, Ebaai bibii lɛ baashã ni eshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baagbi oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa tree turning yellow and the stems getting swollen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eshishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and yellowing leaf veins are signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, which is caused by a virus spread by tiny mealybug insects. Because there is no chemical cure for the virus, infected trees must be removed so they do not infect the rest of your farm.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni efuu kɛ baai lɛ ahe fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji kookoo bud hela he okadii. Virus ko ni mealybugs bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji akɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa hela lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni okagbɛ hela lɛ oshwã oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa tree get dark spots and dry up before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ ni egbiɔ dani eshɛɔ?

english: This is usually caused by pests like capsids or fungal infections like Black Pod disease. Capsids suck the sap from young pods, while damp conditions allow black pod fungus to spread and rot the pods before they mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Capsids lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ haa black pod fungus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni egboɔ dani edaa.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers they cannot support, but heavy flower drop happens when the tree is stressed by lack of water, poor soil nutrients, pest damage, or a lack of small insects like midges that pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi. Shi fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa kɛji nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ Akpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ. aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ midges ni haa fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni bɛ

english: If I cut down my cocoa trees and plant food crops like cassava, will my soil stay fertile?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo tso ni midu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei lɛ, ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baawo nii?

english: Cocoa trees protect the soil with leaf canopy and fallen leaves. When you remove them to plant food crops, heavy rain and direct sun wash away topsoil nutrients much faster, so you will need to add manure or fertilizer to keep the land fertile.
ga: Kokoo tsei buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ. Beni okɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛdu niyenii Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite oya kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do I need to prune the branches of my cocoa trees if they look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo niji lɛ kɛji amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛji eŋɔli ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that block sunlight and trap damp air inside the tree. Opening up the tree frame allows air to circulate, which stops fungal diseases from breeding and encourages the tree to grow pods instead of just leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ agbele tso lɛ shishi lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ kpaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akwɛ̃ moŋ fe baai kɛkɛ.

english: What will happen to my soil if I replace my cocoa trees with oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ mu tsei tsake kookoo tsei?

english: Oil palms drink a lot of soil moisture and draw heavy amounts of nutrients from the ground. While oil palm can be profitable, it changes the land's water level and soil structure, making it harder to grow sensitive crops on that land later without heavy soil treatment.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei fɔ baanyɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ moŋ Shi nu lɛ mli ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsake. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsuuu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii waa.

english: Why is my cocoa farm not yielding many pods even though I put fertilizer on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ bɛ ŋmeii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkɛ ŋmeii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture, healthy roots, and sunlight to work. If your trees are too old, infected with diseases, choked by heavy weeds, or shaded too much by dense forest trees, the plants cannot absorb or use the fertilizer effectively.
ga: Fertilizer he miihia shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ hulu la koni etsu nii Kɛji otso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ Eyɛ fɔmɔ mli hela Jwɛi ni mli ewo muji ehà nɔ loo koo mli tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ fe nine. Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛkɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die even when I plant them after the first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: Early rains in Ghana are often 'false rains' followed by short dry spells. Planting immediately after the very first rain leaves young seeds stranded without enough water; waiting until the steady rainy season establishes ensures seeds get the continuous moisture they need to build deep roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana shishijee be lɛ ji ‘nugbɔ ni nɛɔ amale’ ni nugbɔshiimɔi kukuji nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli daa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni yaa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the hot afternoon or in the cool evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ loo fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Watering in the cool early morning or late evening allows water to soak deep into the soil so roots can drink it. Afternoon watering wastes water because the hot midday heat evaporates it before plants can use it, and water droplets on leaves can act like magnifying glasses in the sun, scorching the foliage.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ Enɛ baaha nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ fiteɔ nu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tsei nyɛɔ amɛkɛtsuɔ nii. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when left in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a living canopy that provides shade, keeps the soil moist, and protects the cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baashɛ enɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up into tight tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl during hot weather as a natural self-defense mechanism to preserve moisture. By rolling up, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to heat and wind, slowing down water loss until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛ buɔ fɛ̃i naa. kɛ roll up Tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa lɛ baa shi. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei adu tsina loo ŋmei?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have microscopic organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This acts as free, natural fertilizer for hungry crops like cassava, while the low-lying legume leaves cover the ground to prevent weeds.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli.

english: How can I tell if my maize plants are hungry and missing food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-abele tsei lɛ ni amɛbɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants show their hunger through leaf colors. If the lower leaves turn yellow along the middle vein, the crop lacks nitrogen; if the leaves turn purplish-red, the plant is missing phosphorus needed for root development.
ga: Abɛi tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe su nɔ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ midrib lɛ he lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ purple-red Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What kind of crops can I grow on my farm if I work another job and can only visit the farm on weekends?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mitsu nitsumɔ kroko ni manyɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ otsii lɛ anaagbee pɛ?

english: Hardy tuber crops like cassava and yams are ideal for part-time farming because once they establish roots, they require minimal daily maintenance compared to delicate vegetable crops like tomatoes or green peppers that need daily watering and pest monitoring.
ga: Shishifãi ni wa tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be-fã okwaayeli. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ adu shishifãi lɛ Amɛbiɔ daa gbi saamɔ fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ akɛto aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato loo chili eŋɔli lɛ ahe. No biɔ ni afɔ lɛ nu daa gbi, ni akwɛ koni ana nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my land than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally adapted to fight aggressively for sun, space, and soil nutrients. Because your crops are cultivated plants, clearing weeds during the first month of planting gives your crops a fair chance to grow tall enough to shade out future weeds on their own.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛwu amɛshi hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, otso lɛ ji tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ogbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛha jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly while sitting in heaps before I take them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fite oya beni mitara ŋmei mli dani mikɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that produce heat and moisture after harvest. Heaping them together in closed, warm spots traps moisture and breeds fungi; keeping them spread out in a cool, shade-covered, well-ventilated barn preserves their skin and stops rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ obua amɛnaa yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ, ni afo he lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba. Gbalamɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsaa hewolo lɛ ni ekpaa fitemɔ.

english: Can I save seeds from the corn I bought at the local market to plant on my farm next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Corn bought at the market for eating may be a hybrid variety or treated for storage. Planting those grains often produces weak, uneven plants with tiny ears; using certified seed maize bought from accredited agricultural dealers ensures uniform growth and a high harvest.
ga: Abele ni aheɔ yɛ jara nɔ koni aye lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni akɛfutu loo akɛto he. Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmaa nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shweremɔ yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil or excess water choking the roots, which prevents the plant from taking up essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing, usually 2 to 3 weeks after germination, so the roots can absorb the nutrients without burning.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni shãaa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases that target that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tsei amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young corn crops?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Holes in the central whorl of young maize are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which feed on new leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai heei dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in heavy or poorly drained soil, cutting off oxygen to the roots and encouraging fungal diseases.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ faaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela baa

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, tough root systems that react faster to moisture and steal sunlight and soil food from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni haa ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ onibii bibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in full sunlight without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni tsei ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out easily; they require partial shade from larger plants like plantains to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain suckers when planting them?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ abɔ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Spacing plantain suckers about 3 meters apart ensures their large leaves do not block sunlight from each other and allows their roots enough room to draw nutrients.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee mitai 3, no hewɔ lɛ baai wuji lɛ tsiii hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɛɛ amɛhe. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when weather conditions get too hot or dry, or when the plant lacks sufficient water and nutrients during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli

english: Will removing extra leaves from my garden crops help the fruits grow bigger?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mijie baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Yes, pruning unnecessary branches and old leaves allows the plant to send its food energy directly into developing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji kɛ baai momoi ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting from the tip of lower leaves usually means your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, su ni tamɔ V ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland dry out and crack so quickly just two days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi ni egbɛ eshwa gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ lɛ?

english: Soil cracks quickly when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves and compost to trap moisture. Covering the bare ground with organic mulch or mixing in compost acts like a natural sponge, keeping the soil moist for longer periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the young pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, overcrowded farm conditions. Pruning dense branches to let sunlight and air flow through your farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves twist up with yellow spots and stop growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects or infected stems used for planting. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties recommended for your region.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee kɛha okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars eat the inside leaves of my young maize plants during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the leaf funnels during the hot day and feed at night. Checking your field early in the morning and applying appropriate treatments directly into the leaf funnel will protect your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni amɛtsuɔ nii gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni odu lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ tsofai ni sa wo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any fruits when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme daytime heat causes tomato pollen to dry up, preventing the flowers from getting pollinated and setting fruit. Providing light shade or ensuring regular watering early in the morning helps the plants retain their blossoms.
ga: Gbi lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkawo yibii. ni haa hulutsoo fioo loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves above ground but tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of building tubers. Balancing your soil nutrients with potassium helps direct the plant's food production into growing big roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee bulbs. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ niyenii feɔ shishifãi wuji ni miida.

english: Why do my maize plants bend and fall over easily when a gentle wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Weak anchorage happens when seeds are planted too shallow or when root damage occurs from pests. Heap additional soil around the base of the stalks when weeding to give the roots extra support against wind.
ga: Nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite shishifãi lɛ. Okɛ sũ krokomɛi abɔle tso lɛ shishi beni okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ koni eha shishifãi lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ kroko yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last hybrid harvest produce much weaker crops this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee hybrid kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kwraa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for one high-yielding generation, and their saved seeds lose that strength in the next planting. Buying fresh, certified seeds every season ensures your crops retain high yields and disease resistance.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ ahaa yinɔ kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Ni dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ lɛ yɛ dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aya nɔ amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wilt and die shortly after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved suddenly into hot direct sunlight without time to adjust. Slowly exposing young seedlings to full sun over a week before planting, and transplanting in the cool evening, keeps them alive.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ amli kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli trukaa ni be bɛ ni amɛkɛbaatsake amɛhe. Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli blɛoo otsi kome dani odu. ni akwɛɔ nɔ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or waterlogging around the roots, which prevents the plant from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow big with plenty of green leaves but produce very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes tomato plants to focus all their energy on growing stems and leaves instead of producing flowers and fruit. Adding fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young corn plants, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yeli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms. Applying recommended biopesticides or neem leaf extracts directly into the center leaf whorls early in the morning or late evening helps eliminate them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp shade. Pruning excess tree shade and clearing weeds around the base allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and reduce infection.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ fe nine lɛ afolɔmɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Why do agricultural officers encourage me to plant cassava together with maize on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai woɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ he hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Intercropping maize and cassava helps maximize land use; maize matures quickly for an early food harvest, while cassava grows slower and stays in the ground longer, protecting the soil and providing food later.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii babaoo. Abɛi daa oya kɛha niyenii ni akpaa mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni okɛ niyenii aha sɛɛ mli.

english: Is it good for me to save seeds from my harvested maize to plant during the next rainy season?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ abaato ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ koni akɛdu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted local open-pollinated seeds, you can save them for next season. However, if you planted hybrid seeds, saving them will result in poor yields and weak crops, so fresh seed should be bought each season.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni agbele naa lɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛto kɛha be ni baa lɛ, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid. Shika ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni ehiii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, hemɔ dumɔwui heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why does my land become dry, hard, and cracked shortly after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbɛ eshwa beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa shi etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic matter like compost or animal manure, and when left uncovered under direct sunlight. Covering the soil with dried leaves or straw helps retain moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. ni kɛji akɛ ashi ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How can I protect my vegetable crops from drying out when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Applying a thick layer of dry grass or mulch around the roots of vegetables keeps the soil moist, while planting windbreak trees reduces the drying effect of hot Harmattan winds.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ awo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Aduawai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ aba shi.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off and soil cracks appear around the base of the plant stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Weeds are natural wild plants adapted to survival; their seeds lie dormant in the soil and absorb water and sunlight instantly, competing with cultivated crops for nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi. Edumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ hulu la amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Okɛ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ aka akaŋ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when exposed to direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and holds soil moisture, protecting the cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to spread out and capture maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed for the plant to produce large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I choose the right plantain shoot to plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain ni sa kɛha dumɔ kɛha ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which are young shoots with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a thick base. These shoots root faster and grow stronger than shoots with wide, fully open leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tseee, ni tamɔ lance, ni eshishigbɛ lɛ mli tse. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ baawo shishifãi oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛgbele amɛhe kwraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding well-decomposed animal manure or appropriate fertilizer replenishes soil nutrients and turns the leaves healthy green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plant flowers dropping off before fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Covering the soil around the plant stem with dry grass keeps the soil moist and cool, helping flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei ni egbi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by fall armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana. Checking your farm early and applying organic neem seed extracts or recommended sprays directly into the central leaf funnels controls them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛwoɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkudɔ nakai ŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on sap and spread plant diseases. Spraying soapy water or neem oil under the leaves controls these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso helai amɛshwaa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla nu loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it safe for my soil if I plant cowpeas together with maize in the same field?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ani ebaafee shweshweeshwe kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas with maize improves the soil. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, which naturally nourishes the maize while giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmãa enyɔ baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my field for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and sprout as soon as clearing exposes them to sunlight and rain. Planting cover crops or covering exposed soil with organic mulch blocks light and stops weed seeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa he loo akɛ organic mulch ha hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to dig up from underground?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaaku kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally dry up and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside them provides living protection and retains soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. kɛfata shihilɛ mli nibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ he.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, and prevents weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the center of my young maize plants and leaving holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ni amɛmiishi bu yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. They hide in the leaf whorls of young maize plants to feed, but spraying recommended organic or chemical treatments early in the morning can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli koni amɛye niyenii. Shi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning patches of yellow instead of solid green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa najiaŋ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why are the bottom parts of my growing tomatoes turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni miida lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani tomato lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, usually caused by irregular watering which prevents the plant from absorbing enough calcium from the soil. Watering your tomato plants consistently helps stop this rot.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni oooha o-tomato tsei lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni akpa nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in that field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil needs extra nutrients before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi dani madu nii?

english: If your previous harvest was poor, or if crops in that field grew slowly with pale, weak leaves, the soil lacks nutrients. Adding well-rotted farmyard manure or appropriate fertilizers restores the soil's strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okpamɔ ni okpa tsutsu lɛ ehiii loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when they start carrying big bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and weak pseudostems that struggle with heavy weight and strong winds. Supporting them with strong wooden or bamboo poles (staking) under the fruit bunch keeps them upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ pseudostems ni bɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ ekɛ muji ni tsii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akpee. Kɛ tso loo ŋmei tso (tso) ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ yɛ aduawai akuu lɛ shishi koni ehi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from an agro-dealer instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ dɛŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to produce higher yields, resist local diseases, and handle dry spells better than seeds saved from past harvests, which lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni ebaanyɛ etsu hɔmɔ shihilɛi ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ. ni baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli

english: How do I know the right time to start planting after the very first rain falls?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after just one rain can be risky because a dry spell often follows. It is best to wait until the rains become regular and wet the ground deep enough so seeds do not dry up after germinating.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ baanyɛ afee oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make food and grow green. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the root area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsi niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall and full of thick green leaves, but the roots under the soil remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miida ni eyi kɛ baai eŋɔlii ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji bibii kwraa lolo?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from overly rich soil or fertilizer, it puts all its strength into growing branches and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa tsɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaawo tsei niji kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi tuber lɛ mli yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the strong dry season sun starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and short roots that cannot handle full sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing trees like plantains or leguminous trees to protect them from burning until their own roots go deep into the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la fɛɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo legumes lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when the atmospheric temperature gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. The plant drops flowers to save energy so it can survive the heat stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ trukaa lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize crop overnight?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center leaf funnel during the hot daytime and crawls out at night to chew the soft foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. ni efoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni eyaye baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain trees easy to push over or falling down in light winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi loo egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems often fall because microscopic worms called nematodes or banana root weevils have eaten away the underground roots, leaving the plant without a strong anchor in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana shishifãi lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Should I put fertilizer into the hole at the exact same time I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Putting strong chemical fertilizer directly against raw seeds can burn them before they sprout. It is better to wait until the seedling emerges and forms roots before feeding it fertilizer.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in tiny bumps on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, leaving natural plant food behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Why is the bottom tip of my ripening tomato fruit turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This black soft patch is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium up from the soil into the fruit, usually caused by irregular watering patterns.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ agbala calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds even when the vine is high up on a stake?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ he, eyɛ mli akɛ wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds around the base of the mound steal water and food directly from the root zone, leaving less nourishment for the yam tuber to expand fully underneath the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni bɔle gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ.

english: When yam mounds are packed too tightly, the crop roots end up fighting each other for space, water, and food under the ground. Giving them proper distance ensures each tuber has enough soil room to expand and grow big.
ga: Beni sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi wuɔ yɛ ŋwɛi, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa bulb fɛɛ bulb naa shikpɔŋ nɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa ni eda.

english: Why does my maize fail to come up if I bury the seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: A seed only carries a tiny pack of energy to push its first leafy green shoot out of the ground. If buried too deep under heavy dirt, the seed runs out of power and suffocates before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni amɛkɛtsiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ muji ni tsii shishi lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baaho ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a cry for help showing that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to stay green and grow tall. The plant is pulling nutrients from its older leaves to keep the top growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji haomɔ tsɛmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni ekwɛ̃. Tsei miigba niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛmiijɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves when the dry sun season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop leaves during dry weather to protect themselves from losing water. The plant goes into a sleeping state to keep its underground roots alive until the rains return to sprout fresh leaves.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he. Tso lɛ yaa wɔɔhe koni eha eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ ebatsɔ baai heei.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. When hot weather dries out the blossom, the plant sheds the flower to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the same patch of land where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize eats up a lot of nutrients from the dirt, but beans and cowpeas do the opposite by capturing food from the air and putting natural fertilizer back into the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii feɔ nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ nakai kɛtsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ amɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass works like a shield against the sun. It holds water in the soil longer so you water less, and it blocks weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. koni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra branches growing on the sides of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tso ko masɛi lɛ

english: Trimming extra side branches stops the plant from wasting food on unnecessary leaves. This forces the plant to send all its water and energy directly into making larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛ ni afolɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite niyenii yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ enu kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekɛfee aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the middle leaves of my young maize plants look chewed up with dark dust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ sũ ni mli edɔ yɛ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Chewed inner leaves with dark sawdust-like dirt are a clear sign of caterpillars called armyworms hiding inside the stem. They hide in the center of the stem to eat the sweet, fresh leaf growth away from the sun.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ mli ni ashɛre ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ armyworms lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Amɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ teŋ koni amɛye baai ni ŋɔɔ ni ehe tse ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: How do I know if the crop medicine I buy at the market is genuine and safe for my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni ehi kɛha mi tsei lɛ?

english: Genuine crop medicines have approved registration numbers from regulatory bodies like Ghana's EPA, intact factory seals, and clear expiration dates. Buying from licensed agro-dealers ensures you do not get fake chemical mixtures that can burn your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni jɛ tsei amli diɛŋtsɛ lɛ ekpɛlɛ gbɛi aŋmalamɔ nɔmbai anɔ kɛjɛ nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ Ghana EPA lɛ adɛŋ. Nitsumɔhe lɛ naatsii lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. kɛ gbi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni esa akɛ okɛtsu nii Kɛ́ ohe nii kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ, ehaa onine shɛɛɛ tsofai ni ji amalei ni baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical medicine on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cooler and the wind is calm. Spraying during hot afternoon sun causes the medicine to evaporate too quickly and can burn the leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu baa shi. Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofa lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaaha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together to spray my field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ afutu mli koni mikɛshwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Mixing chemicals without expert advice can cause them to react negatively, reducing their power or harming your plants. Always consult an extension officer before combining different pest or weed treatments.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ŋaawolɔi komɛi bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ afee nɔ ko ni ehiii. Ebaanyɛ eba tsofai lɛ ahewalɛ shi loo eye otsei lɛ awui. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, bi o-extension nitsulɔi lɛ dani okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo jwɛi tsofai komɛi afata he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, overly shaded fields during the rainy season. Pruning excess branches and removing infected pods helps keep the air dry and stops the spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be mli fe nine lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbi ni ekpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants curling up and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow when they should be green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ efee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil, or the roots are damaged by excess water or pests. Applying appropriate fertilizer or compost gives the crop the energy it needs to grow green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu babaoo loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by soil pests like nematodes or stem borers. Supporting heavy plants with strong wooden stakes and using clean planting material stops them from falling in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ afite. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ kɛ dumɔ nibii ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii Enɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does my maize produce cobs with missing grains at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when the plant experiences heat or water stress during its flowering stage, preventing complete pollination. Planting with the early rains ensures the crop gets enough water when forming seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination naa kwraa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ́ amɛdu dumɔwui.

english: How does leaving some shade trees on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Shade trees protect delicate crops like young cocoa from harsh sunlight, keep soil moist during dry periods, and drop leaves that rot and naturally fertilize your soil.
ga: Shade tsei buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni oha baai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What should I do immediately when I notice a strange sickness spreading across my crop field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ? Egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ?

english: Separate the healthy crops from infected ones by avoiding moving soil or tools from sick plants to clean areas, and contact a local extension officer right away to identify the disease and get the right remedy.
ga: Gbalamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ loo nitsumɔ dadei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa he ni atsuuɔ nii yɛ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ maŋ lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ helatsamɔhe lɛ anɔ lɛ abɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛyoo hela lɛ ni amɛná tsamɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an important plant food, or the soil is too waterlogged around their roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or decomposed manure will help them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stem cuttings in the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings about one meter apart gives each plant enough space in the soil to form big tubers without competing with neighboring plants for nutrients, sunlight, and water.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu he akaŋ

english: What causes my tomato fruits to rot and turn black at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato yibii lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃?

english: This problem is called blossom end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil dries out too much between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ

english: Is it better for me to put fertilizer on my farm right before it rains or after the rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer right after a light rain when the soil is moist. Putting fertilizer down right before a heavy downpour can cause the rain to wash away your expensive fertilizer before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nugbɔ lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Can I plant groundnuts together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts with maize is very good because groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps your maize grow stronger and improves your soil over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni o-abele lɛ adara ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my yams are fully ready to be harvested from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yams are generally ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above the ground dry up and turn yellow or brown, showing that the plant has finished feeding and stored all its energy into the tuber below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eye ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster right after I clear my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain gives weed seeds hidden in the dirt plenty of water and warm conditions to sprout quickly. Clearing weeds while they are still tiny prevents them from taking away nutrients meant for your main crops.
ga: Nugbɔ jieɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ kpo. Ni yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otso titri lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?
