english: Pepper leaves curl during dry weather to protect themselves from losing water too quickly in the heat, or it could mean small sucking insects like thrips are hiding under the leaves feeding on the sap.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu akafite oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Aloo ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips, yɛ ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai ni yeɔ nu lɛ shishi.

english: It is not recommended to plant saved seeds from hybrid maize because the second harvest will grow unevenly and give you a much lower yield compared to buying fresh hybrid seeds certified for planting.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ mli, ejaakɛ kpamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ abaadu lɛ ahemɔ.

english: Why are wild animals coming to eat my cassava roots before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli kooloi yeɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dani amɛdaraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Field pests and small animals dig up roots when water and food are scarce during dry spells. Clearing farm boundaries and planting bitter edge crops can create natural barriers that keep animals away from your main harvest.
ga: Shia mli kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii baafo shishifãi beni nu kɛ niyenii faaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ. Okwaafoi husui ni ooogbɛ ashwã kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ afee adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni haa kooloi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ okpamɔ titri lɛ he.

english: How can I protect my young crop seedlings from being destroyed by small pests without buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui bibii ahe koni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii akafite amɛ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: You can protect tender seedlings by using natural barriers like wood ash around the stems or light netting over nursery beds. These simple steps block insects and small pests from chewing young plants while they are growing strong.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko, tamɔ tso sũ, ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe loo shade netting ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe saatsoi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akaye dumɔwui lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How do I stop termites from chewing through the wooden stakes and shade supports on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye miŋmɔ lɛ tsei kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ?

english: Termites attack dry, untreated wood buried in the soil. Coating the bottom of wooden supports with used motor oil, neem oil, or using termite-resistant local wood species keeps them from destroying your farm structures.
ga: Termites tutuaa tsei ni egbi ni asaaa he ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Akɛ tsɔne mli fɔ ni akɛtsu nii, neem fɔ, loo maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ amɛye nɔ lɛ awo shishitoo tsɔne lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and curling up early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen or when young stems are attacked by stem borers. Adding manure or the right fertilizer early gives the maize the food it needs to produce dark green, healthy leaves.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo kɛ́ stem borers lɛ tutua tsei bibii lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baawo mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers instead of producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when soil temperatures get too hot, water is irregular, or the ground lacks calcium. Mulching around the roots with dry grass keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the plant hold its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and bushy with green leaves but give me very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi ehaaa mi tomato fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much animal manure rich in nitrogen, the tomato plant focuses all its energy on making leaves instead of fruits. Balancing the soil with phosphorus helps the plant shift energy into flowering and fruiting.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baa feemɔ he moŋ fe aduawai. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔsfɔs ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when the trunk looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Microscopic worms in the soil can eat away the underground roots silently, leaving the plant with no strong anchor. Cleaning suckers before planting keeps root pests out and ensures the roots firmly hold the plant in the soil.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ dioo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa. Kɛ́ atsumɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ akafite amɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on all their leaves to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage into the light and keeps leaves off hot soil where plant diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni ehaaa amɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ amɛgbee shi, he ni tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow better when I plant them together in the same field with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and share it with the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for nearby maize plants while shade from the maize keeps the soil moist for the cowpeas.
ga: Cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jaa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo ni jɛɔ ŋmãa mli baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha tsina ŋmãa.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry like a brick just two days after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbi tamɔ brikii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil hardens quickly under the sun when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves or manure to hold water. Leaving crop residues or mulch on the ground protects the soil surface and keeps it soft and moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ mli waa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ́ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha nu ahi mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni efee blɛoo ni edɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly under intense sunlight. Shade plants like plantain or banana act as natural sunshades and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes strong roots.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small yields when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough air and resources to grow thick stems and big fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the ears are fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for keeping leaves green and healthy. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant pulls it from the lower leaves to keep the top growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe koni eha ŋmeii lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil fertile for maize next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that can pull nitrogen food from the air and trap it in tiny balls on their roots. When the plant harvested and rots, that trapped food stays in the soil to nourish the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbala niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ ni amɛfite. Niyenii ni amɔmɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eya nɔ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same field drains the specific soil nutrients that maize needs and allows soil pests that love maize to build up. Alternating with different crops keeps the soil balanced and pests away.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, abaajie shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Tsei srɔtoi adumɔ Tsɔɔmɔ ohe ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ato he ni ojie tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any peppers during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When heat and dry weather get too severe, pepper plants experience stress and drop their flowers to conserve water and energy so the plant itself can survive.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ ni amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the soil without draining away, it drowns the roots and allows rotting fungi to attack them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and stop the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny whiteflies carrying a plant sickness (virus) or by extreme heat. The curled leaves cannot capture enough sunlight to make food for big tomato fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni ji tsofai ahe helai (virus) loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee niyenii aha tomatoi wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and reduce my yield even after I apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have wild, aggressive roots that swallow up soil moisture and fertilizer nutrients much faster than cultivated crops can, leaving your crops starving despite the fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Enɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii po wo onibii amli lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye bo.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if they were stored in warm or moist conditions where mold damaged them, or if they were dried under direct hot sun which killed the tiny living embryo inside the seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ he ni ŋmei lɛ kpataaa dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ egbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha fɔmɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ aba. Dumɔwu lɛ mli baanyɛ agbo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their small roots can drink it up. Shade trees protect them from overheating and help keep moisture in the soil so the cocoa can grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Akɛni baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ fe nine lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure feeds the plant so it can stay dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my maize yield improve when I plant it on land where I harvested cowpeas or groundnuts last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ hi fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decompose, they leave that free plant food behind to nourish your next crop of maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi tsei niyenii yɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛha o-ŋmãa niyenii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When rain floods the farm and water sits around the roots for a long time, the roots drown because they cannot breathe, allowing rot-causing fungi and bacteria to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu damɔ shi ebɔle he. shishifãi be kakadaŋŋ Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: What makes my pepper leaves curl up tightly and stop growing big fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ?

english: Tightly curled leaves are caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking the juices from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by insects. The damaged leaves can no longer trap sunlight properly to make food for growing large fruits.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe waa lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anɔ Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ hulu la lɛ mli dɔŋŋ koni ekɛ niyenii aha aduawai wuji ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the center tops of my young maize plants look eaten up and filled with dirt-like powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ayiteŋ tamɔ nɔ ni aye ni muji ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows inside the soft center funnel of the maize to eat the tender leaves. The dirt-like powder is its waste, and treating the crop early stops the worm from destroying the entire plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Powda ni tamɔ shikpɔŋ ji jwɛi. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ mra Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants grow much bigger tubers when I support them with tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ daa bulbs ni dara kwraa beni mikɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food. Staking keeps the leaves in full sun and prevents ground rots, sending more energy down to build a large tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu ni eyi obɔ ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ naa. Etsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee yitso agbo.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave many shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ feɔ kui bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: All those extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, allowing the mother tree to put all its food into one big bunch.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛkɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ buaa eniyenii fɛɛ naa ni efeɔ kuu agbo kome.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When afternoon heat becomes too intense, the pollen inside the tomato flower dries out and fails to fertilize the bloom. Unable to form seeds, the plant drops the useless flower to save its remaining water and energy.
ga: Kɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔmɔ nii amli. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings fall over flat and die right at the ground line soon after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This seedling collapse is caused by a fungal disease called damping-off, which thrives when nursery soil is kept too wet and shaded. Keeping the soil damp rather than soaked and giving seedlings morning light helps keep the stems firm and rot-free.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli shwiemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off, ni daa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ, ni aha dumɔwui lɛ leebi la lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛkafiteɔ.

english: Does planting a larger seed yam guarantee that I will harvest bigger yams?
ga: Ani sweet potatoes ni dumɔwui wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ ni miduɔ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Not necessarily. A smaller seed yam that is clean and disease-free will produce a much healthier and stronger harvest than a large seed yam that carries hidden diseases inside it.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni mli wa fe ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Where do most of the diseases on my farm actually come from when a new season starts?
ga: Nɛgbɛ helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ kɛji be hee ko je shishi?

english: Most crop diseases come directly from infected planting materials saved from previous harvests. Using certified disease-free seeds prevents sickness from entering your soil in the first place.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni hela emɔ ni aŋmala ashwie shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ hela bɛ mli lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akabote oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my planting material is strong enough to survive in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔ nii lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Strength in planting material comes from being free of diseases rather than its size. Clean planting materials build strong natural defenses that prevent local pests and diseases from attacking them.
ga: Hewalɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔ nii amli lɛ jɛɔ bɔ ni helai bɛ mli lɛ mli fe bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ. Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni he tse lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni mli wa koni ekɛtsi he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ naa koni amɛkatutua amɛ.

english: Why are the new crop varieties I am given smaller than the traditional ones my father planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei ni mikɛha lɛ bibii fe shishijee tsei ni mitsɛ du lɛ?

english: New varieties are often bred for disease resistance and quality rather than just size. Even if the harvest looks smaller, the tubers are often denser, healthier, and richer in nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ srɔtoi heei kɛha helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe kɛ sui ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ moŋ fe amɛdalɛ kɛkɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni faaa moŋ Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii. amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa ni amɛyɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo

english: If my yams turn out small this season, does that mean the crop is weak?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ faaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ?

english: No, smaller tubers do not mean a weak crop. A small yam that grew without disease is actually stronger in nutritional quality and lasts longer than a large, diseased yam.
ga: Dabi, bulb bibii etsɔɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Atomɔ bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni hela bɛ amɛhe Amɛyɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe akpɔlɔi wuji ni hela emɔ amɛ.

english: Why do some smaller yams feel heavier and taste better than larger ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii komɛi nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛhe ŋɔɔ fe ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When a plant is completely free of disease, it spends all its energy storing rich nutrients and strength inside the tuber instead of fighting off sickness, resulting in a smaller but denser crop.
ga: Beni hela bɛ tso lɛ mli kwraa Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ato tso lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hela lɛ baawu Enɛ haa tsei bibii shi amɛhe wa waa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops get sick even when my farm soil is rich and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Rich soil cannot save a plant if the seed planted in it was already carrying a disease. Healthy soil only yields great crops when paired with clean, disease-free seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nyɛŋ aha tso ko ahi shi kɛji akɛ hela emɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ mli lɛ momo. Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai pɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ fata he.

english: How do some crop varieties stay healthy even when neighboring farms have disease outbreaks?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ helai egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ po?

english: Certain crop varieties have strong internal defenses against common environmental diseases. Because pests and sickness cannot easily attack them, they remain healthy while vulnerable crops get infected.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ mligbɛ hebuu ni mli wa ni teɔ shi ewoɔ shihilɛ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ atutua amɛ mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ hela.

english: Why do my yams rot so quickly after I put them in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rotting during storage usually starts from tiny, invisible infections that were inside the yam while it was still growing. Planting disease-free varieties ensures the harvested yams stay healthy in storage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ helai bibii ni anaaa ni baa sweet potato lɛ mli beni edaa lolo lɛ. Helai bɛ mli ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nitoo.

english: How can I protect my yam crop from getting attacked by sickness while it is still growing in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-sweet potato lɛ he kɛjɛ hela he be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: The best protection is starting with disease-free seed materials. When crops are clean from the start, diseases present in the environment struggle to break through and harm the plant.
ga: Hebuu ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ dumɔwui nibii ni hela bɛ mli lɛ aje shishi. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tse kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛfite tsei lɛ ni amɛye amɛ awui.

english: What actually happens to my cocoa pods if I leave them on the tree too long without harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa amɛ?

english: Leaving cocoa pods on the tree past their ripe stage causes them to over-ripen, which makes the seeds inside start germinating or rotting. Over-ripe pods also attract pests and diseases like black pod, which can quickly spread to healthy pods on the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi kookoo ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛho be ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ashwere fe nine. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ loo amɛgboɔ. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai, tamɔ tsei diji, ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How often am I supposed to go through my farm to harvest ripe cocoa pods during the peak season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ?

english: You should harvest your crop every two weeks during the peak season. Regular harvesting prevents pods from over-ripening on the tree and keeps diseases from multiplying on old or decaying pods.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Otsii enyɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yaa nɔ lɛ Nikpamɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni tsɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. ni atsĩ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni egbɔ loo ni egboi lɛ anɔ

english: Is it fine if I harvest my cocoa pods today but leave them in a heap for a few weeks before breaking them open?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɛnɛ shi mishi amɛ otsii fioo komɛi dani amɛtswa?

english: No, waiting too long after harvesting causes the beans inside to spoil or start germinating. You should break your cocoa pods within two to five days after harvesting so that the beans ferment properly and retain high quality.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite loo amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Esa akɛ ogbala kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ gbii enyɔ kɛyashi enumɔ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha kookoo yibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, wet weather. If you leave those black pods hanging, the fungal spores will blow onto healthy pods and ruin more of your harvest.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji oshi pod diŋ lɛ Fungal spores lɛ baatswa pod ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ ni ebaafite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ babaoo.

english: Why is it dangerous to let tall weeds grow around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle mi cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Tall weeds steal water and nutrients from your trees. They also trap moisture around the base of the tree, creating a humid environment where fungal diseases thrive and insect pests hide.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Emɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ hu, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ daa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees when they seem to be growing fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni eekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or unnecessary branches so sunlight and air can reach inside the tree canopy. Good airflow dries off wet leaves and pods faster, which stops fungal diseases from growing on your cocoa.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha baai ni efɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akakwɛ̃ yɛ o-cocoa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many small flowers and tiny young pods fall off my cocoa trees before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can feed, but heavy pod dropping usually happens when the tree lacks water or nutrients, suffers from severe heat, or is attacked by insects like mirids.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa beni tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni baatutua mɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight, which can scorch their leaves and dry out the soil. Shade trees act like protective natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and the trees cool while they establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛma shi lɛ.

english: What will happen if I dry my cocoa beans directly on the bare ground instead of on raised mats?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji migbi kookoo yibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni mikɛbaagbi yɛ tsɔne ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Drying beans on the ground exposes them to dirt, damp soil, and animals, causing mold to grow inside the beans. Buyers reject moldy cocoa beans or pay a much lower price for them.
ga: Beans ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa amɛnaa muji, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, kɛ kooloi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ yɛ kɔfe yibii lɛ amli. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efite lɛ loo amɛwoɔ jara ni baa shi kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my crop trees are lacking nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When trees lack plant food, their leaves turn pale or yellow, their growth slows down, and they produce fewer pods. Applying the right fertilizer gives the trees strength to carry a full, healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ bɛ tsei niyenii lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. ni oha pods fioo Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen or is getting too much water. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so applying the right fertilizer or improving field drainage will help.
ga: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is lacking nitrogen or is getting too much water. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Therefore, using the right fertilizer or improving drainage in the field will help.

english: Is there a single magic chemical I can buy to automatically revive my dying cassava plants?
ga: Ani majik tsofa kome yɛ ni manyɛ mahe ni baaha mi yucca tso ni miigbo lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: There is no single chemical that cures all plant problems. You must first identify whether the cause is cassava mosaic virus, mealybugs, or poor soil so you can treat the exact problem safely without wasting money.
ga: Tsofa kome pɛ bɛ ni baanyɛ atsu tsei ahe naagbai fɛɛ ahe nii. Esa akɛ okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji nɔ ni kɛbaa lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela, ŋmeii, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii. Bɔni afee ni onyɛ otsa naagba lɛ shweshweeshwe ni ofiteee shika babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato fruits rotting from the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ shishi dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: This is blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium and irregular watering. Keeping your soil evenly moist and adding lime or organic manure helps the plants absorb calcium.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ, ni calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni esaaa lɛ kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ lime loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aŋɔ calcium.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids and thrips, or a virus they transmit. Controlling these insects early with safe, recommended sprays prevents leaf damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids kɛ thrips. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite baa lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and hard while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, dark conditions. Pruning extra branches to let air and sunlight in, along with removing infected pods, stops the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Additional pruning to allow in air and sunlight. Including removing infected pods. will stop fungus

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep dropping off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by heat, lack of soil moisture, or insect attacks from mirids. Providing shade trees and spraying recommended insect treatments protects the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ edɔ amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ Shade ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Can I use unapproved yield-boosting chemical sprays to guarantee a bigger harvest this year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ yibii ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii koni manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ afi nɛɛ mli?

english: No, applying unverified chemical boosters without proper testing or soil diagnosis can burn plant roots and ruin your harvest. Always consult extension officers for certified fertilizers.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akaaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo akwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, bi extension nitsulɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during high winds even when they look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛji eŋɔli moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes eat their roots underground, weakening their hold. Planting clean suckers and supporting stems with props prevents falling.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ye amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa amɛhe ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ adu tsei ahe tsei kɛ tsei ahe tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akagbee shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and crooked instead of large and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams grow crooked when planted in hard, compacted soil or when soil pests attack the tubers. Moulding high, soft mounds gives the yams plenty of space to grow large.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔle kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ. Ekɛ sweet potato lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni eyɛ he ko babaoo ni ebaanyɛ eda.

english: Why do my garden egg plants shed their leaves immediately after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Garden egg leaves fall when water collects around the roots, causing fungal root rot due to lack of oxygen. Planting on raised beds lets excess rainwater drain easily.
ga: Eggplant baai ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and wither when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily scorched by direct heat. Providing shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantain protects them from sunburn and keeps the soil moist enough for the roots to feed.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ha tso lɛ loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye nii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can turn sunlight into food for the growing tuber underground while preventing leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ afee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tso helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the cobs are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to build green leaves and large cobs. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the crop the energy it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Ni akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei baafata he mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful if I put too much chemical fertilizer on my crops at one time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli shikome lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer at once increases the salt level around the roots, which actually pulls water out of the plant instead of feeding it. This 'burns' the plant, causing leaves to dry up and die.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ‘shãa’ tso lɛ, ni no haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets pests multiply. Switching to crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How long can I store my harvested maize seeds in a sack before planting them again?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ awo kotoku mli dani madu ekoŋŋ?

english: If seeds are dried thoroughly and kept in an airtight, cool place away from moisture and insects, they stay good for about a year. Storing them longer or in damp conditions reduces their ability to sprout.
ga: Kɛji akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi abɔ he. Dumɔwui lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ aaafee afi. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to be kakadaŋŋ loo yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ, ehaa nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots because they cannot breathe. The soggy environment encourages fungal diseases that cause the tubers to decay before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shwiemɔ mli. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ dani akpaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and getting tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus they carry. As the leaf loses juice, it twists up and stops growing properly.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ baai lɛ nu fite lɛ Ebaatsɔ ehe ni ekpa dalɛ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat weakens the flower's pollen, so the plant sheds the flower instead of producing a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa fɔfɔii amli ŋmeii lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ laajeɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my crop chemicals in the middle of the afternoon when it is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes liquid spray to evaporate quickly before the plant can absorb it, and the combination of hot sun and chemicals can scorch and burn the green leaves.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ amɛ. Ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ tsofai baanyɛ ashã baai eŋɔli lɛ.

english: I want to start growing cashew on my land, but will cashew trees harm my cocoa trees if I plant them close together?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi cashew ŋmeii dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ani cashew tsei lɛ baaye mi cacao tsei lɛ awui kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Cashew trees grow deep roots and wide branches that take up a lot of sunlight and water. If planted too close to cocoa, they will shade out the cocoa and compete heavily for soil nutrients, so it is best to plant them in separate fields.
ga: Cashew tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ niji ni mli kwɔlɔ ni hulu la kɛ nu babaoo baa amɛnɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tsɔ Ebaaha kookoo lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatswa akaŋ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting cashew before I can start harvesting nuts?
ga: Kɛ́ odu cashew lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Grafted cashew seedlings usually start bearing nuts within 2 to 3 years, whereas trees grown directly from raw cashew seeds take about 3 to 5 years before producing their first crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛ cashew dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I plant shea nut trees on my farm like cocoa, or do they only grow naturally in the wild?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu shea nut tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tamɔ kookoo? Aloo abaanyɛ akwɛ lɛ yɛ koo lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Shea trees can be planted intentionally on farms using nursery-grown seedlings. While wild shea trees take up to 15 years to fruit, modern nursery techniques help managed shea trees grow faster and produce nuts earlier.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ atsu nii kɛdu Shea tsei yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ koo mli shea tsei baanyɛ ahé afii 15 dani amɛwo yibii moŋ, shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛ̀i haa shea tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to keep the moisture in the soil and protect them from heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa tsei anɔ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he

english: Why do my crops produce small yields when I plant many seeds close together in the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots fight over the same water and soil food, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them properly allows every plant to get enough food to grow full fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cashew trees fall off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers fall off mostly due to insect attacks, fungal diseases like powdery mildew, or a sudden lack of water during the flowering stage. Spraying approved treatments and keeping the soil moist helps fruits form.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ cashew fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi fe fɛɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew, loo nu ni bɛ trukaa yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Pruning removes excess foliage so the tree can send its strength, water, and nutrients directly into growing pods rather than useless leaves. It also lets sunlight and air flow through to prevent diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ejieɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amaje tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni miida lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ mli koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the soil is running low on essential food like nitrogen, or that the plant roots are soaked in too much standing water and cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tso shishifãi ewo nu ni ekã shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: What happens to my tree crops if the rains stop earlier in the season than normal?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: When rains end too early, crop pods and nuts cannot fill up completely, leading to light, shriveled, or poor-quality harvests that sell for less money.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ oya tsɔ Tso kɛ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ awo mli kwraa. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbo, loo nɔ ni ehiii kwraa, ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ shika fioo pɛ.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my crops help stop insect pests from attacking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai atutua amɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds give insect pests and plant diseases a place to hide, multiply, and feed. Keeping the farm clean removes these hiding spots, forcing pests away from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahelai naa he ko ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe, amɛfɔɔ bii, ni amɛyeɔ nii. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ hei ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ nɛɛ. ni onyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct, strong sunlight. They require partial shade from larger shade trees or plantain plants to protect them from overheating and losing too much moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers but then drop the tiny green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Egbee shi dani etsɔ agbo

english: Cocoa trees drop young pods—a process called Cherelle Wilt—when they lack sufficient nutrients, water, or when stress levels are high. It is the tree's natural way of reducing load, but severe dropping usually means the soil needs feeding or pests are attacking.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni ji nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt, kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, loo kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ haomɔ ni mli wa mli lɛ bɛ amɛmli. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa jatsu lɛ shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ yibii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miitutua lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants manufacture green leaves, so when it runs low, the plant pulls nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nɔ ko fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when a light rain or wind comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over easily when its brace roots are weak or shallow, often caused by planting too shallowly, soil compaction, or pests like rootworms eating the root system underneath.
ga: Abɛi gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ shishifãi ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛbaa ji dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ shishifãi ni yeɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with thick branches but produce small, watery roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ niji ni mli tse, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive foliage growth with poor tuber development happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Potassium is the key nutrient cassava uses to store starch and build big, heavy tubers.
ga: Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni tuber lɛ shweremɔ ehiii lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Potassium ji niyenii titri ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛhiɛ starch mli ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Curling leaves with yellow mosaic patterns are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by whiteflies. Infected plants cannot process sunlight efficiently, which reduces your total yield.
ga: Baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ yɛ mosaic he mfoniri ni ji ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji cassava mosaic hela ni ji hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu hulu la he nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my crops wilt so fast even though it rained just a couple of days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboi oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soils with low organic matter or high sand content cannot hold onto moisture for long. Adding compost or dry mulch helps the soil retain water like a sponge so crop roots can drink over many days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ nɔ loo ŋã babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu gbii babaoo.

english: Why does leaving weeds near my crops slow down the growth of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Because weeds grow aggressively, they steal essential food before your crops get a chance to absorb it.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ.

english: What causes white dust-like spots to form on the leaves of my garden crops after humid morning weather?
ga: Mɛni kɛ sũ yɛŋ ni tamɔ sũ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baa yɛ leebi ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It spreads in warm, humid weather when leaves stay wet for too long without adequate air circulating around the plants.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ebaagbɛ eshwa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ hi shi ni efɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, tsei ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why do insect pests seem to attack my crops more when the rainy season is coming to an end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ?

english: As wild grasses and bushes dry up at the end of the rains, insects move into active farms searching for the remaining green, juice-rich crops to feed on.
ga: Beni jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei lɛ egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ naagbee lɛ. Kplukai fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ amli koni amɛyatao ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ koni amɛye.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when planted in an open field without tall crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need temporary shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out soil moisture. Intercropping them with fast-growing plants like plantains provides living shade and protects them until they mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains du amɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do grasscutters keep targeting and cutting down my cassava and sugarcane stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛifolɔi lɛ kwɛɔ mi-cassava kɛ sugar cane tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Grasscutters prefer soft, succulent crop stems like cassava and sugarcane because they provide rich carbohydrates and high moisture, especially during dry seasons when natural pasture grass is scarce.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli ewo nu tamɔ yucca kɛ sugar cane. Ejaakɛ eyɛ carbohydrates babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni adebɔɔ mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ kooloi alɛɛhei lɛ bɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small droppings left inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ashi yɛ kɔni lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest hides inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants to feed on new leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei dani ŋmãa bibii lɛ afee.

english: Yellowing lower leaves signal a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from older, lower leaves to nourish newer growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans help my maize grow better when I plant it in the same soil afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when plants suffer heat stress or irregular watering. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy and survive rather than spending resources on fruit production.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni amɛhaaa amɛ daa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni ekɛwo yibii

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by viral diseases spread by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot underground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ hoɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching cassava roots. Without oxygen, root tissues break down and become easily infected by rot-causing fungi.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to full sunlight for food production while keeping them off damp soil, which prevents fungal diseases and leaves room for large tubers to expand underground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ naa hulu la ni fa kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa ehi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ anaa, ni ehaa gbɛ kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I prune away some of the small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates heavy competition for water and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller bunches and longer growth times for the main plantain tree.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui titrii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛdaraa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for healthy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure helps the plants stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Crops like groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after nutrient-hungry crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility for the next season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei ji ŋmei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ he hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the dirt around my crops with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching ebɔle he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔji ewo mli lɛ baa mli.

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava stick upright, at an angle, or flat in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ ama shi shiŋŋ, yɛ koŋ nɔ, loo mafee tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree slant or upright helps them root deeper and produce more tubers compared to laying them flat, especially in areas with light rainfall.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji 45-degree angle loo ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmei lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ tsɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which travels down to make the underground yam tuber grow big and heavy.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ.

english: How many young suckers should I leave growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii enyiɛ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he?

english: It is best to leave only two or three strong suckers of different ages around the main stem. Leaving too many suckers creates competition for water and soil nutrients, leading to smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Tsoi babaoo ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my crops yield so much less if I delay clearing weeds early in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your plants need. Weeding early prevents your crops from getting choked and stunted during their most critical growing phase.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe ni amɛkafee shoo yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep dropping off the branches without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when they are not pollinated by tiny insects or when the tree is stressed by hot dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or damage from pests like mirids (capsids).
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ myrids (capsids) lɛ amli baa.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying with neem water or safe agricultural insecticides gets rid of them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ okwaayeli mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why are my green tomatoes getting black, rotten spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni fiteɔ yɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the roots to absorb the calcium the fruit needs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear all the big trees off my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their tender leaves lose water too fast. Leaving a few large shade trees or planting plantains beside them shields the tender crops from intense heat until they are mature enough to stand the sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ Ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize so that the crops grow well and give me good yield?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋma lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Planting maize too close together makes the crops fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small cobs. Using a standard spacing of about 75 cm between rows and 40 cm between plants lets each plant grow strong and produce big cobs.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Kɛ akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ji aaafee 75 cm kɛ tsei ateŋ ŋta ni miihe ashɛ 40 cm tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant my cowpea seeds at a specific depth instead of just scattering them on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpea dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ pɔtɛɛ ko? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Seeds planted too close to the surface can dry out in the heat or get eaten by birds, while seeds buried too deep run out of energy before reaching sunlight. Planting them at a standard depth of 2 to 3 centimeters ensures they stay moist and can sprout easily.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbi yɛ latsaa mli loo okpoi baanyɛ aye. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ji sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves in hot, dry weather to save water and stay alive. It is a natural self-defense behavior, and once the rainy season begins, the plant will grow fresh leaves and continue feeding its underground roots.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu su. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ baai heei ni ekɛ niyenii baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are receiving too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If tomato leaves yellow and droop while the soil is wet, they are overwatered and their roots are drowning. If the leaves curl upward and feel dry or crispy, the plants are thirsty and need a regular watering schedule.
ga: Kɛji o-tomato lɛ baa lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tomato lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ miiho. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi ni enu he akɛ egbi loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ nu daa.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall with lots of green leaves but fail to produce peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi ewooo pepper lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of fruits. To get plenty of peppers, the plants need balanced soil nutrients, including phosphorus and potassium, which encourage flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Niyenii ni ja ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei. Kɛji ootao ni oná chili babaoo ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni haa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo fata he lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my yam plants curl up and develop sticky sap on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and sticky sap are signs that tiny insects like aphids are sucking juice from the leaves. The sticky substance is waste from the insects, which can attract black mold and slow down the growth of your yam tubers.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ nu ni mli tseɔ lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids, miinu nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni ŋmɛɔ lɛ ji kooloi amli jwɛi. ni baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii diji kɛba ni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why does letting weeds grow near my bean plants reduce the amount of beans I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ mi-bean tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa bean ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your bean plants. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the food they need to produce thick, full pods.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ o-bean tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my okra plants without turning into okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi okra tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee okra ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Okra flowers often drop off if the plant suffers from sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or a lack of insect pollinators like bees. Keeping the soil moist and avoiding strong chemical sprays during flowering helps the flowers stay on and form pods.
ga: Rosella fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ agbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: How do I know when my sweet potatoes are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes show they are ready when their leaves begin to turn yellow and die down, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack. You can carefully dig up one tuber to check if the skin is firm and fully formed before harvesting the rest.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa ŋmei kome mli koni okwɛ kɛji hewolo lɛ mli wa ni efee jogbaŋŋ dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree stay alive and keep producing pods on my farm?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ ahi shi ni ewo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A well-cared-for cocoa tree can live and produce pods for 30 to 40 years or more. Giving your trees good soil nutrients, proper shade, and protection from pests when young ensures they remain productive for decades.
ga: Kakao tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo ŋmeii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai ni oooha otsei lɛ Ha hulutsoo ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce fewer pods compared to when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛ akɛto mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age beyond 25 to 30 years, their root systems become less efficient at absorbing nutrients from the soil, and branches become more susceptible to disease. Pruning old wood and replenishing soil fertility helps older trees maintain their yield.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ye fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni niji lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya. Tsei ni egbɔ ni afoɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot absorb water fast enough to withstand intense heat. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong enough to endure direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it helpful to plant plantains on the same land where I am starting new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu plantains yɛ he ni mije kookoo hee shishi yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from harsh sunlight and heavy wind. They also provide food and income for your household while you wait for the cocoa trees to mature.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Amɛhaa oshiabii lɛ niyenii kɛ shika hu yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ lɛ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect the way my cocoa trees grow?
ga: Te Harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ saa kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The dry Harmattan air pulls moisture out of plant leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil. To survive, cocoa trees may shed leaves to save water, which temporarily slows down flower and pod growth until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. koni amɛhi shi Cocoa tsei lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed many of their leaves during the dry months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Shedding leaves is a natural survival defense. By dropping leaves, the tree reduces the amount of water lost through evaporation, allowing it to keep its main trunk and root system alive until water becomes available again.
