ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ wala he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmɛ baai lɛ, ehaa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛyaa lasu mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ etsitsi kɛ eshishifãi titri lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers grow directly on the thick trunk of my cocoa tree instead of at the ends of branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anaagbee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally bear flowers and fruit on their main trunk and thick wood because cocoa pods are heavy. The thick trunk provides strong support for the weight of full pods while protecting them from strong winds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai yɛ amɛshishifã titri lɛ nɔ, ni amɛji tsei ni mli tse. Ejaakɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ tsii. Tsoi ni mli tse lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. If the tree lacks sufficient water or soil nutrients, or if insects fail to pollinate the flowers, the tree deliberately drops excess flowers to conserve energy for the pods it can support.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛji kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ Tso lɛ baajɛ etsui mli ekɛ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm become weak after growing crops on it for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ beni midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every harvest removes vital plant nutrients like nitrogen and potassium from the ground. Without adding compost, organic manure, or fertilizers back into the soil, the ground loses its fertility over time and yields begin to decline.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni nibii ni anáa lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa tree turn black and rot before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight through the trees helps keep the pods dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji black pods lɛ baa. Efɔ ni edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my cassava become too watery for making fufu when I harvest it during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ mli nu babaoo tsɔ ni ekɛbaatsu nii kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb a lot of excess water during heavy rains, which lowers their starch content and makes them too soft or watery for pounding into firm fufu.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ashikishaŋ lɛ nɔ aba shi. ni ehaa efeɔ bɔdɔɔ loo nu tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etswa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the best time of year to harvest my cassava to get the highest price at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei koni maná jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Cassava demand and prices peak during dry periods or transition seasons when fresh crops are scarce, and when buyers are actively looking for dried cassava like konkonte.
ga: Cassava taomɔ kɛ ejara yaa ŋwɛi yɛ hɔmɔ loo tsakemɔ be mli. Beni nibii heei ni anáa lɛ faaa Ni beni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ miishɛɛ taoɔ ŋmei ni egbi tamɔ conconte lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick where the cassava plant reduces water loss to keep its underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa. Cassava tso lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi koni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the field during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the roots and encourages fungal growth, which causes the roots to rot if left too long in soaked ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why should I dry my harvested cassava into konkonte instead of trying to sell all of it fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-cassava ni akpa lɛ mawo konkonte mli moŋ fe ni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ fɛɛ ehee?

english: Fresh cassava roots spoil within two to three days after harvest, but drying them into konkonte preserves them for many months so you can sell when market prices improve.
ga: Cassava shishifãi heei lɛ baafite yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ ogbi amɛ yɛ conte mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi nyɔji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ kɛji jara nɔ jara lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: Why do some types of cassava make smooth fufu while other types are only good for making konkonte?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei henɔi komɛi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmei henɔi komɛi feɔ con conte pɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties have different amounts of starch; high-starch varieties give fufu its stretchy texture, while lower-starch varieties dry out better for konkonte flour.
ga: Kasava henɔi srɔtoi Ashikishaŋ falɛi srɔtoi yɛ. Starch henɔi ni fa babaoo haa fufu lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Yɛ be mli ni starch henɔi ni baa shi lɛ gbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha con conte ashikishaŋ.

english: How can I keep my harvested cassava from turning dark and spoiling if I cannot get to the market immediately?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ akatsɔ duŋ ni efite? Kɛji akɛ onyɛɛɛ oya jara lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: You can prolong fresh cassava for a few extra days by storing the intact roots in moist sawdust, or you can peel and dry them immediately to stop spoilage completely.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha ŋmei hee lɛ wala aya hiɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ ni oookɛto ŋmei ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo obaanyɛ otsi amɛhe ni ogbi amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkpa fitemɔ kwraa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots under the ground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or planting stems too close together causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding its roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha eshishifãi lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: What is the advantage of planting my cassava at the start of the first rains rather than later in the year?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe afi lɛ naagbee?

english: Planting early gives young plants enough moisture to establish strong root systems before the dry season comes, leading to bigger harvests.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni afeɔ.

english: Why does my cassava yield reduce every time I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava heavy feeds on soil nutrients like potassium, so planting it repeatedly without resting the land or adding fertilizer drains the soil nutrients.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ adu lɛ shii abɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaho.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. This happens when the soil is poor, after heavy rains wash nutrients away, or if fertilizer is not applied on time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Enɛ baa mli beni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ, hoɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli yɛ be naa

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In hot weather, pepper leaves lose moisture into the air faster than their roots can drink water from the soil. If the plants bounce back by evening, it is normal heat stress, but watering deeply around the root zone early in the morning helps reduce this.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ ku esɛɛ efo gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Shi kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni naagba nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and developing yellow patches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaf curl is commonly caused by tiny pests like whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread a virus. In dry weather, pest populations increase, making the damage more visible and stopping the plant from growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ whiteflies, ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ baaya hiɛ. Ehaa nɔ ni efite lɛ jeɔ kpo faŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to get more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in weak, thin plants that produce smaller fruits or ears instead of a larger yield.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni woɔ yibii bibii loo toi yɛ yibii babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Maintaining steady moisture in the soil helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they can develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ haa tso lɛ kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni etsɔ aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain strong salts that can draw water directly out of young plant stems and roots, causing chemical burns that can kill the plant. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem in a circle or line.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai ni baanyɛ agbe tsei lɛ shãa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ kooyigbɛ loo line mli.

english: Covering soil with dry organic material, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil water, keeps the ground cool, suppresses weed growth, and breaks down over time to enrich your soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛwo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in tough conditions, and their seeds sit hidden in the soil waiting for sunlight. Clearing the land gives these dormant seeds full sun and rain, allowing them to sprout faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Ni amɛdumɔwui lɛ etee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛmiimɛ hulu la. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ baagbe dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ. Enɛɛmɛi naa hulu kɛ nugbɔ ni fa babaoo. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides inside the funnel of young maize plants where leaves are fresh and soft. Inspecting your farm early allows you to control them before they destroy the growing point of the stalk.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ehee ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ he ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant tomatoes in the exact same field where I just harvested garden eggs or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ ooodu tomato yɛ ŋmɔ ni mifolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes, garden eggs, and peppers belong to the same crop family and suffer from the same soil diseases and insects. Planting them repeatedly in the same spot allows those pests and diseases to build up in the soil and attack your new crop.
ga: Tomato, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo aba. Ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etutuaa oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ.

english: Can I just collect coconuts from the market and plant them on my new farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua ŋmeii anaa yɛ jara nɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Planting random seeds from the market often leads to weak trees with very low yield. To get a profitable harvest, you should use certified hybrid seedlings from trusted extension officers, which grow faster and produce far more fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa baa. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ hybrid dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ extension agent ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ enɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some coconut trees start bearing fruit in three years while others take up to seven years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii etɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi heɔ afii kpawo lɛ?

english: The time it takes to produce fruit depends on the variety planted; high-yield dwarf and hybrid coconut varieties mature much quicker than traditional tall varieties.
ga: Be ni eheɔ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ damɔ tso sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. Dwarf coconut henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ hybrids lɛ daa oya kwraa fe blema henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to leave so much space between my coconut seedlings when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ babaoo kã ŋmei tsei ateŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees need at least 7 to 9 meters of space between them so their wide leaves get enough sunlight and their deep roots do not fight each other for soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 7 kɛyashi 9 bɔni afee ni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe etswaaa akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land in Ghana is good for coconut farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmeii adumɔ?

english: Coconuts grow best in well-drained, deep sandy-loam soil where water moves easily. Clay soils that trap stagnant water around the roots will cause the tree to rot and fail.
ga: Kokooi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni nu hoɔ oya Shikpɔŋ ni sũ ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbo ni egbee shi.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my coconut trees while they are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping young coconuts with short-term crops like cassava or maize is a great way to earn quick income and suppress weeds while the trees grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei duɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa shika oya ni agbeɔ jwɛi be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young coconut trees turning yellow and dropping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that poor water drainage is damaging the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ miifite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my coconut tree fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ akokoso tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Premature flower dropping happens when the tree experiences water stress during dry spells, pest attacks, or a lack of essential soil minerals like boron.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa kɛji tsei na nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutuaa loo nibii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ boron.

english: Why are some of the coconuts on my farm coming out small and dry instead of big and full of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛgbi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee wuji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Small, dry fruits are usually caused by long dry seasons without irrigation, unfertilized poor soil, or using low-quality unimproved seed varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai bibii ni egbi lɛ jɛɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ mli baa. shikpɔŋ ni awoko mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni baa shi ni afeee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii

english: Why did my coconut tree stop bearing good fruits after producing well for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tso lɛ ekpaa yibii kpakpai womɔ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees drain nutrients out of the soil constantly over time. If you do not replenish the soil with manure or fertilizer, the tree becomes exhausted and stops fruiting.
ga: Kokoo tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ekpa yibiiwoo.

english: How can I prevent beetles from boring holes into the top of my young coconut trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ladybugs lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo ŋmeii tsei bibii lɛ ayiteŋ?

english: Rhinoceros beetles are attracted to decaying wood and farm waste. You can protect your farm by clearing out rotting logs and using pheromone traps recommended by extension officers.
ga: Tsei ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi gbalaa rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei ni egboi ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ pheromone tsɔnei ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Where can I go to buy quality crop seeds if my local market runs out of them?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ? Kɛji mimaŋ jarayelihe lɛ nɔ ko bɛ

english: You can get certified seeds from registered agro-dealers, district offices of the Ministry of Food and Agriculture, or approved seed producer associations to ensure you get healthy seeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ Kpokpaa nɔ Nitsumɔhe lɛ loo dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi akuu ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ onine shɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ anɔ.

english: Why do some farmers in Ghana buy imported crop seeds instead of local ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ heɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ moŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Imported seeds are often specially bred for higher yields or specific pest resistance, though local Ghanaian seeds are often better suited to our local weather and soil conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo loo amɛnyɛ amɛshi tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, ghana dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔmaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ.

english: Can I bring seeds from another country to plant on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ abadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Importing seeds requires official permission and inspection by plant protection authorities to ensure new pests or crop diseases are not brought into the country.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ biɔ maŋ lɛ hegbɛ kɛ kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ Tsei Ahe Buu Nitsumɔhe lɛ koni ana akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei loo tsei ahe helai ebaŋ maŋ lɛ mli.

english: What should I do if a specific crop seed variety I want to plant is not available in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mibɛ dumɔwui kɛha tso pɔtɛɛ ko ni misumɔɔ ni madu yɛ Ghana?

english: You can speak to an agricultural officer or a licensed seed importer who can help request or find approved alternative varieties that grow similarly well.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko loo mɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni kɛ dumɔwui baa maŋsɛɛ ni baanyɛ aye abua ni obi loo otao dumɔwui krokomɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ awie.

english: Why are there so many different varieties of the same crop seed available to buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo yɛ ni abaanyɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Different varieties are developed for different needs—some grow faster, some handle drought better, and others produce larger fruits or resist common local diseases.
ga: Afee srɔtoi yɛ hiamɔ nii srɔtoi anaa. Henɔi komɛi daa oya. Henɔi komɛi nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa fe tsutsu lɛ. ni tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii wuji loo amɛhe waaa helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What does it mean when a seed is called a 'certified seed'?
ga: Beni atsɛ dumɔwu lɛ Mɛni ji ‘dumɔwu ni awo he odase’ lɛ shishi?

english: Certified seeds are inspected and tested by government agricultural officers to guarantee that they will sprout well and are free from major diseases.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli ni amɛkaa amɛ amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni helai ni naa wa bɛ amɛhe.

english: How do I know which seed variety will perform best in my area's soil and weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Agricultural extension officers conduct local field trials to know which specific crop varieties thrive best in the rainfall and soil conditions of your district.
ga: Okwaafoi agbɛjianɔtoo he nitsulɔi lɛ feɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔ mli kaai koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihereɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid varieties often leads to smaller yields and weaker crops in the next harvest compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ hu baa shi yɛ kpamɔɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ hemɔ he.

english: How can I test if the seeds I purchased are still good before planting them on my whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ hi dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: You can do a quick test by placing 10 seeds in a wet cloth; if 8 or more sprout within a few days, the seed batch is healthy enough to plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee kaa oya kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu.

english: Why do some seed varieties require more fertilizers and care than traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ babaoo fe blema maŋbii dumɔwui lɛ?

english: High-yielding or improved seed varieties grow faster and produce more, so they consume more soil nutrients and water to reach their full potential.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo loo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why can't I just buy crop seeds brought directly from overseas and plant them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛba kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds from other countries are bred for different weather, soil, and rainfall patterns. Planting them directly in Ghana without testing them locally first often leads to failure, as local pests and high heat can destroy crops that aren't adapted to our environment.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ Akwɛ amɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, shikpɔji, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ Ghana ni akaaa amɛ akwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ kɛ shigbeemɔ baa. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ wɔ shihilɛhe lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do seeds saved from my harvested hybrid maize yield much less corn when I replant them the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ mi-hybrid corn lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two different parent plants to give a huge yield only once. When you save and replant those harvested seeds, the offspring lose that special vigor and produce weaker plants with smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kome. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ, Seshibii lɛ laajeɔ nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and burn easily. Keeping large shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the young plants and keeps moisture in the soil until their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ atsa tsei ni eda ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawa.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry spells as a survival mechanism to save water and keep its root tubers alive underground. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, eji gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rainstorm arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away the fertilizer before the plant roots can drink it in. This wastes your money and sends nutrients into nearby water bodies instead of feeding your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ amaje nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ moŋ fe ni oooha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I apply the same amount of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ baawo mli?

english: Fertilizer gives plants quick food, but it does not fix worn-out soil. Over time, continuous farming removes organic matter and beneficial microbes, making the soil hard and unable to hold water or nutrients properly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii oya. Shi enyɛŋ esaa sũ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize stems grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete against each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water. This struggle leaves them with too little energy to build strong stems or big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, nɛkɛ nɔmɔ nɛɛ haa amɛnáaa hewalɛ fioo tsɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa loo tsei wuji.

english: Why do I need to use wooden poles to support my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni mikɛfiɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ he hiaa mi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make food. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases and directs the plant's energy down into growing large tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ahe helai anaa, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ shi kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants get attacked by more diseases when I plant them on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ náa helai babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly allows disease-causing germs and pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the soil. Changing to a different crop family starves those pests away.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ooodu shii abɔ Enɛ baaha helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tsei aweku kroko mli lɛ, ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up pollen, preventing flowers from being fertilized. Without proper fertilization or sufficient water, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo fɔ Kɛji fɔmɔ ni sa bɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Tsei hu baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and develop broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa plants grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛ naa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baadara waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crop turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen nutrient in the soil or that heavy rains have waterlogged the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or clearing drainage paths helps restore the green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea, loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo baatsu nii Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest them, these root deposits remain in the ground, fertilizing the soil naturally for crops like maize planted afterwards.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. beni okpaa lɛ Shishifãi nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients from the undersides of the leaves. Spraying an organic neem leaf solution or standard extension-recommended pesticide controls these insects so fresh leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem tso lɛ mli tsofa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni afɔɔ he ŋaa ni akɛhaa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ koni baa heei lɛ anyɛ ashwere.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller harvests if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and plant nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to build strong stems and produce large yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my tomato plants with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are soft and easily bend under the weight of growing tomatoes. Staking lifts the stems and leaves off the damp ground, preventing wet soil diseases from rotting the leaves and fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛfoɔ oya yɛ tomato ni adu lɛ tsiimɔ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei kɛ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni otsi baai kɛ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto tall stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate food that feeds the growing tuber beneath the soil. Staking the vines elevates the leaves to catch maximum sunlight while protecting them from rot on hot, wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni fata wain tso lɛ ni akɛbaawo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ he ji baai ni awóɔ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa efite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain mother tree divides the food and water in the soil among too many plants. Removing extra suckers leaves just one or two strong shoots, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ baaja niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsei babaoo. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in heavy soil that holds excess standing water for too long. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain freely away from the roots during heavy rainfall.
ga: Kasava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three steady, deep rains rather than planting right after the very first light shower. Deep moisture ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to germinate without drying up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ daa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni mli kwɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have delicate root systems and sensitive leaves. Watering them in the middle of a hot day can scorch the foliage or boil the tender root zone. Watering early in the morning or late in the afternoon, along with providing partial shade, helps young plants absorb moisture without stress.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ loo atswa shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ leebi loo shwane kɛ hulutsoo be fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa nu ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds for planting instead of just planting grain saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase akɛ adu lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ i ngɔ kɛ je ye nyagbe ngmɔ ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected and treated to resist common local diseases, tolerate dry spells, and grow uniformly. Saved grains from previous harvests often lose these protective traits, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ daa Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ ŋmaa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ hebuu sui nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to produce foliage and food. Applying balanced fertilizer or manure during early growth gives the leaves their rich green color so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni tsei kɛtsu nii koni amɛkɛfee baai kɛ niyenii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale after heavy rains, even though plants need water to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia tsei koni amɛdara moŋ.

english: Heavy rainfall can wash nutrients out of the topsoil where crop roots feed. This process leaves the soil temporarily empty of plant food, causing crops to look pale until new soil nutrients or fertilizers are supplied.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aye nii yɛ lɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ahe niyenii bɛ mli yɛ be kukuoo mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛyashi ebaaná niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops produce small fruits and thin stalks when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ tsei bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant adequate spacing allows every crop to access full sunlight and feed properly.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ náa hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively absorb water, fertilizer nutrients, and sunlight intended for your main crop. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Flower drop occurs when plants face high heat stress, irregular watering, or a shortage of key nutrients like phosphorus and calcium. Maintaining steady moisture and balanced soil nutrients helps flowers stay on the stem and form healthy fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ phosphorus kɛ calcium ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ ni ehaa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Will removing extra lower leaves from my cassava or tomato plants harm their growth?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mijie shishigbɛ baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi yucca loo tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaafite amɛdalɛ?

english: Pruning dead or lower leaves actually helps crops by directing energy toward producing roots and fruit rather than sustaining unnecessary foliage. It also improves airflow around the base of the plant to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Baai ni egboi loo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa shishifãi kɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehiɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ hu yaa hiɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant groundnuts or beans alongside crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei ahe lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them alongside crops like maize enriches the soil naturally, helping nearby crops grow healthier.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ebuaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why are there small holes in my vegetable leaves even though I do not see insects on them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai lɛ yɛ bu bibii eyɛ mli akɛ anako kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Many crop pests, such as beetles and caterpillars, hide under leaf cover or in the soil during hot daytime hours to avoid heat and predators. They emerge at night to feed on leaves, leaving behind holes by morning.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Hiɔ ehe yɛ baai ashishi loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Bɔni afee ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛbaye baai. kɛtsɔ bu ko ni eshiɔ yɛ leebi lɛ nɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea gives them back their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards during the middle of hot dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense response where the plant reduces its surface area to save water during extreme heat. If the leaves recover in the cool evening, the plant is managing heat, but if they remain curled, the plant needs watering.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hebuu hetoo ni tsei baa shi koni amɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ he wa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miikwɛ amɛdɔlɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lolo lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ.

english: What is eating hole-filled paths inside the central leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛjegbɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ yeli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest common across Ghana. They crawl into the central funnel of young corn to hide from daylight and moisture while eating the growing shoot.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛyatee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads in cold, damp shade. Pruning overhead branches and clearing undergrowth lets sunlight and air dry out the pods, halting the rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ yiteŋ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekpa fitemɔ

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of soil before planting my yam sets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii akuu ko lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick underground and need loose, soft earth to expand smoothly. Heap mounds keep the soil loose around the growing yam while preventing water from settling around the tubers and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Pile lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Sweet potatoes ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. yitso kɛ fitemɔ

english: Why does cassava decay in the soil if heavy rain sits on the farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air within the soil to remain healthy. Stagnant rainwater blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot due to fungal activity in wet soil.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Efoɔ ni egboɔ yɛ ŋmeii nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and give small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil food directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all available nourishment to grow tall and produce a strong harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ náa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni ewo yibii ni mli wa.

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, draw water and plant food away from the mother stem. Keeping only one healthy follower shoot allows the main stem to produce a big, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ gbalaa nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akwɛ tso lɛ yitso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ afee plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without making any tomato fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when exposed to intense heat stress, extreme dryness, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil moist and encouraging insects or shaking the plant gently helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ni awoɔ kooloi hewalɛ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ni akpokpoɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it bad if I bury my crop seeds too deep in the dirt when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Seeds carry limited food energy inside them. If buried too deep, the young sprout uses up all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is key for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or composted manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji nɔ titri ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my rice crop need to stand in water, but my maize crop dies if the field floods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmãa tsei ahi nu mli lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ gbo yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli?

english: Rice plants are adapted to thrive in flooded soils that hold water around their roots, which also stops weeds from growing. Maize roots, on the other hand, need air in the soil to breathe and will rot if submerged in water for too long.
ga: Atsakeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every year if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts gives the soil a rest and puts essential nutrients back into the earth.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe jɔɔ ehe ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my poultry farm directly onto my crop plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee ni jɛ mikooloi alɛɛhe lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure is very strong and produces high heat as it breaks down, which can burn your crop roots. It is best to let the manure dry and decompose for a few weeks before spreading it on your farm.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa, ni kɛ́ efite lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ babaoo baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni efite otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛgbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants have to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough food to grow thick stems and large yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ Tsei lɛ atswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open as the tubers expand underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to quick growth and fast water absorption. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing water and nutrients meant for your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni sa akɛ amɛdaraa oya ni amɛmɔɔ nu oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Why are my vegetable plants growing tall and thin instead of bushy and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee shwiili moŋ fe ni amɛmiifee bushy ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Vegetables grow tall and thin when they are shaded and do not get enough direct sunlight. They stretch upward searching for light, which makes their stems weak.
ga: Aduawai daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji amɛyɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛtao la lɛ. ni haa eshishifã lɛ gbɔjɔɔ

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or tiny insects like thrips attacking the blossoms. Keeping the soil evenly moist and managing pests helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni ŋmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why did some of the seeds I planted fail to come out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they were buried too deep in the soil, if the soil was too dry, or if birds and insects ate them before they could germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji okpoi kɛ kooloi ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important for me to dig and turn my soil before putting seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni matsɔ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Tilling softens hard soil, making it easy for water and air to enter. Softened soil allows young plant roots to spread out quickly and absorb nutrients, giving the new crop a strong start.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atswaa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo. Ehaa nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni efee blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii heei jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in untilled soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Untilled soil is usually too packed and hard for tiny seed shoots to push through. When the ground is softened first, the emerging stem can easily break through the surface into the sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni asaa he lɛ mli etse tsɔ ni ewa kɛha ŋmeii bibii. koni enyɛ etsɔ mli Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ Tsoi ni jeɔ kpo lɛ baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni amɛha hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: When is the best time for me to prepare my land for planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ masaa shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔ nii?

english: It is best to till your land just before the rainy season begins so the freshly loosened soil can capture the early rains and stay moist for your seeds to germinate immediately.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaatsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa mra lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What actually causes a seed in the ground to sprout and push out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: A seed drinks in water from moist soil, which wakes up the living plant inside it. It pushes a root down into the earth for support and sends a green shoot upward toward the sun.
ga: Dumɔwui nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ baate tsei ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shi. Ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​eshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow taller and stronger in loose soil compared to hard dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni wa he lɛ?

english: In loose soil, roots grow deeper and collect more water and food from the earth. Deep roots support a bigger stem and leaf system, helping the plant grow tall and healthy.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛhiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ fiɔ shishifãi kɛ baai gbɛjianɔtoo wulu ko sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: How deep into the soil should I place my seeds after preparing the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ beni misaa saatso lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds should be planted near the surface—usually two to three times as deep as the seed is wide—so they stay moist while still having enough stored energy to reach the open air.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ—bei pii lɛ, elɛɛmɔ fe dumɔwu lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ lɛ toi enyɔ loo shii etɛ—koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo koni amɛje kpo kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Does turning the soil over before planting help me stop weeds from taking over my farm?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛbaatsɔ dani midu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni jwɛi akaye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, tilling buries wild weeds and unearths buried weed seeds, exposing them to the sun to dry up before your main crop starts growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nitsumɔ baafu koo mli jwɛi ni ejie jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ kpo. Feemɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ hulu lɛ ni oooha egbi dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aje shishi eda lɛ nɔ.

english: How does the condition of my land affect the yield I get at harvest time?
ga: Te shihilɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Soil acts as the bank account for your crops. Well-prepared, healthy soil holds water and plant food throughout the season, leading to bigger crops and higher yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shikatoohe akaunt kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha nu kɛ tsei ahe nibii ahi shi yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Why do extension officers say that soil, seeds, and water must all work together for a crop to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ shikpɔŋ, dumɔwui kɛ nu afee ekome kɛtsu nii koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: A crop cannot grow on seeds alone; loose soil holds the moisture and nutrients that the seed needs to wake up and feed the plant as it grows over time.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ dumɔwui pɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa dumɔwu lɛ koni ekɛte shi ni eha tso lɛ niyenii be mli ni edaa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to prepare my soil again for every new planting season instead of just once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooosaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shikome pɛ lɛ

english: Over time, rain and foot traffic pack the soil hard again, while the previous crop consumes the nutrients in the top layer. Tilling each season refreshes the soil structure for new seeds.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nugbɔ kɛ naneshi tsɔnei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ be mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ ehee kɛhaa dumɔwui heei.

english: Why do my crops mature at different times instead of ripening all at once for me to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome koni makpa lɛ?

english: Crops often flower in stages based on weather variations, soil nutrients, and seed differences. To get a uniform harvest that meets large buyer requirements, farmers use synchronized planting dates, uniform seed varieties, and balanced fertilizers so the entire field matures together.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa lɛ naa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui amli Bɔni afee ni aná nibii ni anáa daa ni atsu mɛi babaoo ni heɔ nii lɛ ahiamɔ nii ahe nii. Okwaafoi kɛ gbii ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baatsu nii. dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ ekome kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja bɔni afee ni ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he kome

english: Why do commercial buyers sometimes reject my traditional crop varieties in favor of new hybrid seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ kpooɔ mishishijee tsei srɔtoi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛyaa dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Commercial buyers look for crops with specific traits like longer shelf life, uniform shape, and resistance to bruising during transport. Hybrid varieties are specifically bred to meet these physical standards required for distant markets.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ taoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ shihilɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. eyɛ su kome ni enyɛɔ etswaa mɔ he yɛ gbɛfaa mli Akwɛɔ Hybrids lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ shishitoo mlai ni he hiaa kɛha jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ aba mli.

english: What causes my crop yields to be too small to meet the bulk quantity targets of big buyers?
ga: Mɛni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ miifee bibioo tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eshɛ shwapotsɛ wulu lɛ otii ni ekɛmamɔ ehiɛ akɛ ebaahe nii babaoo lɛ he?

english: Low yield usually happens when crops lack essential nutrients, are planted too close together, or suffer from early pest attack. Proper soil nourishment, correct field spacing, and timely pest control allow plants to reach their full harvest potential.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. Aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baa amɛnɔ mra Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ŋmɔ mli jɛkɛmɔ ni ja kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛshɛɔ amɛkpamɔ he hewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Are there crops or farming techniques that can allow me to harvest and sell produce every week?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo okwaayeli he ŋaa ko yɛ ni haa manyɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mahɔ̃ɔ daa otsi?

english: Yes, crops like peppers, tomatoes, and okra yield fruit continuously over several weeks if harvested regularly. Farmers also use staggered planting—planting small batches every two weeks—to create a steady supply of produce for daily buyers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tomato, kɛ okra yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii otsii babaoo kɛji akɛ akpa daa. Okwaafoi kɛ dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ hu tsuɔ nii. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kui bibii amli daa otsii enyɔ koni akɛfee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ni yaa nɔ daa aha mɛi ni heɔ daa gbi lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my harvested vegetables soften and spoil so quickly before the buyer comes to collect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani hɔlɔlɔ lɛ baa koni ebakpa lɛ?

english: Harvested crops continue to breathe and lose water rapidly under heat. Harvesting during cool early mornings and storing produce in shaded, ventilated crates slows down crop decay and keeps vegetables fresh for market buyers.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya yɛ latsaa be lɛ shishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii ni adu lɛ ni akɛtoɔ adekai ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli lɛ amli. Ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni eye ebua ni eha aduawai ahi shi ehee aha mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the fruits on the same plant different sizes, with some too small for market standards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kome nɔ yibii lɛ adalɛi srɔtoi lɛ? Ni ekomɛi yɛ bibioo tsɔ kɛha jarayeli he mlai?

english: Fruits compete with each other for the plant's food and water. When a plant carries too many fruits or lacks nutrients, some stay tiny; pruning excess flowers or weak fruits helps the remaining ones grow larger and more uniform.
ga: Yibii kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná tsei aniyenii kɛ nu. Beni tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei komɛi baafee bibii. Kɛ́ ofolɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine loo aduawai ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ afee wuji ni amɛfee ekome.

english: Why do my crops stop producing during the dry season when market prices are highest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni jara nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need consistent moisture to absorb soil nutrients and form flowers. Without irrigation or organic mulching to trap soil moisture during dry months, plants shut down production to protect themselves from dying.
ga: Tsei taoɔ nu ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Kɛji akɛ nu shwieɔ shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ, Bɔni afee ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he lɛ, tsei lɛ kpaɔ nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do buyers refuse to pay good prices for my vegetables even when insect damage is very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaawo mi aduawai lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ kpakpa lɛ? Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii lɛ efite fioo pɛ po

english: Buyers want clean, unblemished produce because consumers avoid damaged food. Even minor insect punctures allow rot-causing bacteria and fungi to enter the fruit, reducing its shelf life during transport.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miitao nibii ni he tse, ni muji ko bɛ he, ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni efite lɛ he. Kplukai bibii po akadii haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ aduawai lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, be ni akɛtoɔ tsɔne mli yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my crop flowers falling off without turning into fruits for me to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when crops experience extreme heat, drought stress, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil adequately watered and encouraging beneficial insects like bees helps flowers turn into full fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni awoɔ he hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kwraa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale and yellow even when there is enough rain falling on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or its roots are damaged by poor drainage. Rain provides water, but plants still need balanced soil nutrients to grow deep green and healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ efite yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: If heavy rain falls right after I plant my maize seeds, will it kill them and prevent them from growing?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmãa ni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ Ani ebaagbe ŋmãa lɛ ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekakwɛ̃?

english: Rainwater itself does not stop corn from germinating; in fact, seeds need moisture to sprout. If your corn fails to come up after rain, it is usually because the seeds were bad, planted too deep, or eaten by soil pests.
ga: Nugbɔ etsĩii ŋmãa kwɛ̃mɔ naa; yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ he miihia dumɔwui dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa kwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ehiii hewɔ. ni adu yɛ mli tsɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: How many days should I wait to see my corn sprout before I realize the seeds failed to germinate?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ dani male akɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ?

english: Healthy maize seeds usually sprout within 4 to 7 days under good moisture conditions. If nothing comes up after 10 to 14 days, the seeds have likely failed and you may need to replant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli yɛ hulutsoo shihilɛ kpakpa shishi. Kɛji nɔ ko baaa yɛ gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ afite ni ehe baahia ni okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: If my planted corn fails to sprout, how can I tell what actually killed the seeds?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni adu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male diɛŋtsɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni gbeɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: You can dig up a few non-germinated seeds to inspect them. If they are rotten or chewed, soil fungi or insects killed them; if they are completely hard and dry, there was not enough moisture in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa dumɔwui fioo komɛi ni ekwɛko lɛ koni okwɛ mli. Kɛji egbo loo egbo Fungi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi gbeɔ amɛ. Kɛji akɛ ewa ni egbi kwraa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa.

english: What is a crop protector for corn and tomatoes, and why do I need it?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛha ŋmãa kɛ tomato? Ni mɛni hewɔ eko he hiaa mi lɛ?

english: A crop protector is a chemical or treatment applied to seeds or plants to shield them from harmful soil insects, fungi, and diseases, helping young plants survive their early growth stage.
ga: Nibii ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe ji tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ahe koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ mli, ŋmeii, kɛ helai ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Will applying chemical seed protectors stop my corn seeds from germinating properly?
ga: Ani tsofai ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baatsi mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, seed protectors are designed to help seeds germinate safely by preventing soil pests and fungus from destroying the seed before it can sprout, provided you apply the correct amount.
ga: Dabi, afee nibii ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ koni eye ebua dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛnaa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shika ni sa tsu nii

english: Can I use the same crop protection chemical for both my corn and my tomato crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ ŋmãa kɛ tomato fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Some general protectors work for multiple crops, but tomatoes and corn often suffer from different pests and diseases, so it is best to check the product label or ask an officer before applying it to both.
ga: Nibii komɛi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei srɔtoi anɔ. Shi tomato kɛ ŋmãa baanyɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai srɔtoi, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ nɔ ni aŋma yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ loo obi najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko dani okɛ eko fɛɛ eko atsu nii.

english: Why would an extension officer advise me to wait two weeks between planting my first and second batch of crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mamɛ otsii enyɔ dani madu tsei akuu klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ?

english: Staggering your planting by two weeks spreads out your harvest time so you don't harvest everything at once. This makes labor easier to manage and reduces the risk of losing your entire farm to a sudden dry spell or market price drop.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ otsii enyɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbɛ okpamɔ be lɛ eshwa. No hewɔ lɛ, onyɛŋ okpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome. Ehaa nitsumɔ nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baafite yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo jarayeli jara ni baa shi lɛ hewɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Should I plant my whole tomato farm on the exact same day?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ?

english: It is often better to plant in stages every two weeks. This allows you to harvest tomatoes over a longer period, ensuring you have produce to sell continuously rather than a huge flood of perishable tomatoes all at once.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ otsii enyɔ fɛɛ otsii enyɔ teŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa o-tomato lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyaa nɔ ofeɔ nibii ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni akpa tomato babaoo ni fiteɔ shikome lɛ,.

english: Why is it important for me to know the exact size of my land before buying seeds and chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ male mishikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ dani mahe dumɔwui kɛ tsofai?

english: Knowing your exact acreage ensures you buy the right amount of seeds and chemicals, saving you money and preventing you from under-dosing or burning your crops with too much chemical.
ga: Kɛ́ ole he pɔtɛɛ ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa bo ni oheɔ dumɔwui kɛ tsofai ni sa, ni ehaaa okɛ shika akafite, ni ehaaa okɛ tsofai babaoo akatsu nii fe nine loo okɛshã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I grow tomatoes on the same piece of land where I just grew corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, rotating corn with tomatoes is good practice because different crops feed on different soil nutrients and help break pest and disease cycles in the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ tomato ni atsakeɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso henɔ fɛɛ tso yeɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli

english: Why do my yams harvested in June look and taste different from the ones I harvest in July?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa yɛ June mli lɛ hiɛ yɔɔ srɔto kɛ nɔ ni mikpa yɛ July mli lɛ?

english: Yams mature in stages. Early-maturing yam varieties mature around June to July, while late-maturing varieties take longer, resulting in different textures, moisture levels, and storage capabilities depending on the month they are harvested.
ga: Yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ahooɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Atomɔ henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ June kɛyashi July mli. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo. nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji texture Humidity level Ni nyɛmɔ ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ srɔtoi yɛ nyɔŋ ni akpaa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How does the time of year I harvest my yams affect how long they last after picking?
ga: Ani afi lɛ mli be ni mikɛkpaa mi-sweet potato lɛ baaná be ni amɛhiɔ shi beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Early yams harvested around June usually contain more water and spoil faster, making them best for quick consumption, whereas main-season yams harvested later in the year have less moisture and store much longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpaa yɛ June mli lɛ fɔɔ nu babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii ni ayeɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, sweet potatoes ni akpaa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ yɛ be titri mli lɛ mli nu faaa, ni abaanyɛ akɛto be babaoo.

english: Should I plant early-season yams or main-season yams on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu mra be mli ŋmeii loo be titri mli ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting early-season yams allows you to harvest around June or July when supply is low and market prices are high, while main-season yams give higher yields later in the year but face more market competition.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, no haa onyɛɔ okpaa yɛ June loo July beaŋ, be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ faaa ni jara nɔ jara hu yaa hiɛ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ. Shi esa akɛ ekɛ akaŋshii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ akpee.

english: Why do yams left in the wet soil during the late rainy season rot so easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ?

english: Excess moisture in the soil during heavy rains around late harvest periods causes mature tubers to absorb too much water and rot, which is why proper harvesting timing is critical.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ haa bulb lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni egboɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni kpamɔ be ni sa he hiaa waa lɛ.

english: Why do buyers offer me very low prices for my yams around September and October?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ haa yɛ September kɛ October teŋ lɛ?

english: September and October are peak harvest months when yams are produced in high quantities across many farms. When supply greatly exceeds buyer demand, market prices drop significantly.
ga: September kɛ October ji nyɔji ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji babaoo amli. Beni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ kwraa. Jarayeli jara lɛ baa shi waa.

english: What does it mean when a trader says my selling price is a 'condemn' price?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ jarayelɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ ‘abu’ mijara ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ fɔ?

english: In local market terms, a 'condemn' price refers to an extremely low buying price offered during a market glut, where buyers force farmers to sell at very low rates due to the heavy oversupply of yams.
ga: Yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ gbɛfaŋ lɛ, jara ni ji ‘damn’ lɛ tsɔɔ jara ni baa shi waa yɛ be mli ni nibii babaoo fa fe nine lɛ mli. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ nyɛ okwaafoi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi waa nɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Is there a way I can hold off on selling my yams during October to get better prices later?
