ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsi sweet potatoes ni mihɔ̃ɔ yɛ October mli lɛ naa koni maná jara kpakpa sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can hold yams back by storing mature late-season tubers in a cool, well-ventilated yam barn, allowing you to wait until market gluts clear and prices rise again.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okudɔ sweet potato kɛtsɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ ni oookɛto yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa omɛɛɔ kɛyashiɔ jara lɛ baaho ni jara lɛ yaa ŋwɛi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do traders come from far places like Burkina Faso to buy yams from markets like Techiman?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi jɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ tamɔ Burkina Faso kɛbaa koni amɛbahe ŋmeii yɛ jarayeli hei tamɔ Techiman lɛ?

english: Techiman serves as a major trade hub in Ghana because surrounding areas produce large quantities of durable, high-quality yams that can withstand long-distance transport across regions and borders.
ga: Techiman ji jarayeli he ko ni he hiaa waa yɛ Ghana. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ babaoo. ni baanyɛ adamɔ gbɛfaa ni yaa shɔŋŋ ni tsɔɔ kpokpai kɛ husui anɔ lɛ naa

english: How do buyers transport yams long distances without the tubers getting damaged?
ga: Te mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛkɛ sweet potato aya he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ efiteee?

english: Traders select fully matured, dry-skin yams harvested later in the season and pack them carefully with grass padding in ventilated trucks to protect them from heat and bruising during travel.
ga: Jarayelɔi halaa ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni hewolo egbi ni akpaa yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli. ni akɛ jwɛi ni akɛfee lɛ woɔ lɔle ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Koni akafee dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: How can I store my harvested yams safely so they do not rot when the market is full?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe? Koni ekafite beni jara lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Constructing a shaded, raised yam barn with good airflow keeps yams dry, protects them from direct sunlight and soil pests, and prevents premature rotting during high-supply months.
ga: Kɛ́ ama sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni awó nɔ ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni sweet potato lɛ akagbi. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. ni atsĩ fitemɔ ni baa oya lɛ naa yɛ nyɔji ni anáa nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ mli egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and delicate leaves that cannot handle direct sun and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside them keeps the air moist and shields the young trees from harsh sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ hu yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ hulutsoo be mli Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay healthy, so when there is not enough in the ground, the plant steals it from older lower leaves to feed the growing upper leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants have thick green leaves but very few flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer makes plants produce excessive leaves and stems instead of flowers. Legumes like beans naturally fix their own nitrogen, so giving them extra makes them focus on foliage rather than setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awo baai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Legumes, tamɔ ŋmeii, ji amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen lɛ saamɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha amɛ babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛjwɛŋmɔ ahi baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the growing tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot soil, exposing them to light while preventing leaf diseases caused by damp ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha baai lɛ aná la ni otsi baa helai ni hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot when left in wet ground after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain saturates clay soils for too long, water displaces the air, suffocating the roots and causing fungal rot organisms to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain farm yield small bunches when I allow all the young shoots to grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni miha tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: Multiple young shoots (suckers) steal food, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, allowing the main tree to put all its energy into making large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) bibii babaoo juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa, ni no haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting like cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like mites, thrips, or aphids sucking sap from the undersides of leaves. Their feeding damages leaf tissue and can spread plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites, thrips, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso mli helai ni fiteɔ dalɛ lɛ eshwa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings rapidly between wet and dry. These stress conditions prevent successful pollination, causing the plant to shed the useless blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ shihilɛi nɛɛ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing seeds and empty spaces on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii ni elaaje kɛ he ko ni bɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Missing maize grains happen when pollination fails. If hot dry winds dry out the sticky silk threads before pollen grains land on them, the unpollinated seeds on that part of the cob will not develop.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ha siliki ni wa lɛ gĩ dani pollen lɛ baanyɛ aba nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni pollen bɛ mli ni yɔɔ cob lɛ nakai fã lɛ nɔ lɛ baakwɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and fall over easily when planted under tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ ashishi lɛ?

english: When crops do not get direct sunlight, they stretch rapidly upward searching for light. This rapid vertical growth makes their stems thin, weak, and unable to support heavy grain heads or withstand wind.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya koni etao la. Nɛkɛ dalɛ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni yaa oya nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ loo amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: My stored seed yams are starting to sprout in the barn, but the main rains haven't started yet. What should I do with them?
ga: Mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ ebɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi nugbɔ titri lɛ ejeko shishi lolo. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amɛ?

english: Seed yams sprout naturally when the warm season begins. If the rains are delayed, keep your seed yams in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded barn to stop the sprouts from drying out and losing energy before you can plant them.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ Too sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi ni amɛkafite hewalɛ dani adu amɛ.

english: How do I know if the seed yams I saved from last harvest are still healthy enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu?

english: Healthy seed yams should feel firm when you press them and show fresh, strong sprouts. If a tuber feels soft, watery, or has rotten patches and pest holes, it will not grow well and should not be planted.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ kɛ́ onyɛ nɔ ni ejie ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kpo. Kɛji bulb lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ nu, loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii Edaŋ jogbaŋŋ ni esaaa akɛ aduɔ.

english: If my yam sprouts grow very long while still in storage, will it affect how well they grow in the soil?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ dara be kakadaŋŋ waa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ mli lolo lɛ, ani enɛ baaná amɛdalɛ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Very long, thin sprouts drain energy from the seed yam tuber. It is best to gently break off long, weak sprouts so the tuber can produce a fresh, stronger shoot once it is planted in wet soil.
ga: Bean tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ amli. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ afo mli fiofio. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ aná ŋmeii heei ni mli wa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: How can I store my harvested yams so they stay fresh until the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ato koni ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Store yams in a raised yam barn built under tree shade. Tying tubers vertically on wooden racks allows air to flow around them, which keeps them cool and prevents rots caused by heat and ground moisture.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ shĩa ko ni awo nɔ ni ama yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ yitsei lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ yɛ tso shĩa ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa amɛhe jɔɔ ni ehaaa fitemɔ ni dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: It rained just once early in the year. Is that a sign that I should start planting my crops immediately?
ga: Nugbɔ nɛ shikome pɛ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli. Ani no ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Early rains can be deceptive in Ghana. Planting after only one rainfall is risky because a dry spell might follow, causing your young seeds to dry up and die in the hot soil. Wait until the rains come regularly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ yɛ Ghana. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ hɔmɔ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ. Ha odumɔwui bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa.

english: Why is it important for me to write down or remember the date when the first rain falls each year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋma loo makai gbi ni nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Tracking early rains helps you estimate when the main rainy season will start so you can clear your land and buy your seeds early enough to avoid planting too late.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni otsɔɔ be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaje shishi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ohé dumɔwui mra bɔ ni sa koni okadu nii sɛɛ tsɔ.

english: Can I plant my crops when the rains are light, or do I need to wait for heavy downpours?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii beni nugbɔ miinɛ fioo loo esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa?

english: Light, steady rains are actually ideal for early planting because they moisten the soil without washing away seeds or topsoil. However, the ground must stay consistently wet enough for the roots to survive.
ga: Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, nugbɔ miinɛ fioo. Uniform hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui mra ejaakɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ tsuuu nii. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do climbing crops like yams need tall wooden poles after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɔɔ tamɔ sweet potato he hiaa tsei ni kwɔlɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb upward to spread their leaves toward the sun. Using stakes lifts the leaves off the hot ground, helping the plant catch sunlight to grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni edɔ lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I check if the ground has enough water before I put my seeds into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa dani madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Dig a small hole hand-deep and squeeze a handful of soil. If it sticks together in a soft ball without crumbling or dripping water, the soil has the right moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Okɛ oniji atsa bu bibioo ko ni okɛ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ awo mli. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo. ni nu etswaaa loo efooo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃.

english: When is the best time for me to start clearing my bush and making mounds for planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei bibii lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ gɔŋ ko ni mikɛbaadu nii?

english: Start clearing your land toward the end of the dry season. Preparing your mounds or ridges early ensures you are ready to plant as soon as the steady rains begin.
ga: Je oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha ofee klalo akɛ obaadu nii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ bɔi nɛmɔ be fɛɛ be pɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important plant nutrient. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards when the sun gets very hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves inward on hot days to protect themselves. By reducing the surface area exposed to the sun, the plant loses less moisture through its leaves.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Kɛ́ ajie he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baatsɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ efo ŋmɔtɔ fioo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water stays on my farm after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for a long time, it drowns the roots and creates the wet conditions that rot-causing fungi love.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Yams need loose, soft soil or well-made mounds to expand smoothly. Hard or compact soil physically stops the tuber from pushing downward, making it bend and stay small.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse loo gɔŋ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkami shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibioo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting beans together with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans are special plants that can pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the soil. Maize plants feed on this added nitrogen, which helps them grow taller and greener.
ga: Beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele tsei yeɔ nitrogen ni fata he nɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or poor pollination. The plant drops flowers to save its energy for basic survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather. Excess shade and stagnant air allow wet conditions that help the disease thrive.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekã shi lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa helai yaa hiɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why does planting my maize seeds too close together give me smaller cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves less energy for each individual plant to form full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso fɛɛ tso bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: How can I estimate how many bags of maize I will harvest before I cut the cobs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa enyiɛ ni esa akɛ makpa dani mafo ŋmãa lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can count the cobs on a small sample of plants in a few spots, calculate the average number of cobs per plant, and multiply that by your total plant count to get a close prediction of your total harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okane ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei bibii ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii lɛ anɔ lɛ. points fioo pɛ Buu ŋmeii ayibɔ ni yɔɔ tso kome mli lɛ mlijaa mlijaa he akɔntaa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tsei lɛ ayibɔ fɛɛ abɔ he koni onine ashɛ okpamɔ fɛɛ ni obaakpa lɛ he akɔntaabuu ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shelter and moisture, acting as shade umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ edamɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow instead of stay deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow green. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf color and plant strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe su kɛ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil grow better cassava after I plant groundnuts on the land first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ beni midu mi-peanuts lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and feeds it into the soil. Rotating your crops with groundnuts enriches the earth with free food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha je lɛ ayi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What causes small worms to eat the center leaves of my young corn during the rains?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on young corn plants after heavy rain. They hide deep inside the leaves to eat the tender heart of the plant, but early detection and targeted biological or chemical sprays can stop them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye tso lɛ mli fã ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Shi mra be mli ni ana Kɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Why should I trim off the bottom leaves of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Trimming the lower leaves keeps them from touching wet soil where fungal diseases live. It also allows air to circulate around the stem, keeping the plant dry and reducing disease outbreaks.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai lɛ, ehaaaa amɛta shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: When plants are overcrowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, producing smaller yields.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa fioo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni no haaa amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does covering the soil with dry leaves help my vegetable bed?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-vegetable saat lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with organic material, called mulching, blocks sunlight from reaching weeds, traps moisture in the soil during dry days, and breaks down into natural compost over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akashɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds instead of planting seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from high-yielding hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to mixed growth and lower yields. Certified seeds guarantee uniform, disease-resistant plants designed for maximum harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni futuɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa. Dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli haa tsei ni hiɔ shi daa, helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Afee amɛ koni amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause stress, forcing pepper plants to drop their blossoms to save energy and water so the main plant can survive until conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ aba amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Bɔni afee ni pepper tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers go soft and rot in the ground if heavy rain falls right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills air spaces in the soil and starves the cassava roots of oxygen. This waterlogging allows destructive soil fungi to enter and rot the tubers quickly.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ bɛ. Nu ni hoɔ nɛɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani odu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Maize seeds require steady moisture in the soil to sprout and build strong roots. Planting during early, irregular rains can cause the seeds to dry out and die if a dry spell suddenly follows.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔwui ni duɔ mra kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings need to be planted at a slant instead of standing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni etse ehe shi moŋ ni ekɛ ehe afɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle helps roots spread out wider and deeper in the soil, which gives the plant better stability and yields bigger tubers.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ 45 degree koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need shade from plantain trees when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa ni ená hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ adɛŋ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that shield the young cocoa plants from harsh heat while preserving soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and naturally put it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the nearby maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make energy. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows plant diseases and pests that target cassava to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmei lɛ anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or sudden flooding. The plant drops its blossoms to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do worms hide inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms hide in the central whorl of the maize plant because it offers shelter from heat and predators while providing tender, young leaves to eat.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai bibii hu ni ayeɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Excessive wetness and shade create ideal conditions for fungi that cause Black Pod disease. Trimming overgrown tree branches allows sunlight and wind to dry the pods and prevent fungal growth.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmei ni kɛ blackpod hela baa lɛ. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering that disrupts nutrient uptake.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Planting plantains or leaving larger shade trees gives young cocoa the protection and moisture it needs to grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ loo ni aŋmɛɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu kookoo bibii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ he.

english: Why do we make high soil mounds before planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand and grow large tubers underground easily. High soil mounds give the tubers space to grow downward while preventing excess rainwater from standing around them and causing rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ko haa bulbs lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekadamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crop roots with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with plant materials, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, holds soil moisture longer during dry periods, and stops weeds from sprouting and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei ahe nibii haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient crops need for healthy leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the plant green up and make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni ehaa niyenii baa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer as soon as I plant seeds or wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo amɛ ŋmɔshi nii kɛji midu amɛ pɛ loo mamɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: It is best to wait until seeds sprout and develop small root systems before applying main fertilizers. Strong chemical fertilizer can burn unsprouted seeds, and plants need roots to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi bibii. Dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baatsu nii Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lɛ. Ni shishifãi he miihia tsei koni amɛnyɛ amɛmli niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Wait until the soil stays consistently wet after two or three heavy rains. Planting after only the first light rain is risky because the seeds may sprout and then dry up if rain stops for weeks.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji oshara ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava stems about one meter apart gives each plant enough space to spread leaves for sunlight and allows tubers to grow large underground without competing with nearby plants.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant garden eggs or tomatoes on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii loo tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot continuously allows soil-borne pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like maize or cowpeas starves those pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni sumɔɔ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow slowly and look weak when weeds are growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and groundwater. Clearing weeds early ensures all the food and water in the soil goes directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu mli, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving caterpillars inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms. Inspecting your farm early and spraying targeted treatments directly into the central plant funnels early in the morning or late evening helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or lacking water. Nitrogen gives leaves their healthy green color, so adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the crop regain its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo nu efo amɛmli. Nitrogen baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava sticks at a slant instead of pushing them straight down or laying them flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi lɛ shi tɛ̃ɛ Aloo oookɛma shi shiŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant helps the plant grow roots deep into the soil for water while keeping the growth buds positioned nicely above ground to catch sunlight easily.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ naa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni enine ashɛ nu nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe oya.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the soft growth center of maize. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps kill them before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni agbe amɛ dani amɛfite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I measure space between my seeds instead of planting as many as possible close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, which results in thin plants and small yields. Giving them proper space helps each plant grow big and produce a strong harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if the soil lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold its flowers and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my cowpea seeds failing to come up out of the soil after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to come up if they were planted too deep in the soil, if the ground was too dry, or if ants and soil insects ate them. Planting seeds at a shallow depth in moist soil gives them the best chance to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye nakai dumɔwui lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mifo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds are already sleeping deep in the dirt and are naturally tough. Once you clear the land and rains fall, weeds quickly absorb nutrients faster than cultivated crops, which is why clearing weeds early is critical.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni ojieɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Jwɛi lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn hard and crack open when the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Soil cracks when it contains a lot of clay and lacks organic matter like dry leaves or manure. Adding compost or leaving crop residues on top of the farm keeps the ground soft and helps hold water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛji shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɛ mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo oshi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni eye ebua ni ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts under the soil are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts show they are ready when the main leaves turn yellowish and drop. You can pull up one test plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown or black patterns, the crop is mature for digging up.
ga: Peanuts tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo kɛji baai titrii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which gives plants their rich green color. Rain often washes this essential food out of the soil, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts in my field help improve the soil for my next crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut roots work with helpful bacteria in the soil to catch nitrogen gas from the air and store it underground. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanut shishifãi kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant drop all its leaves during the dry season, and is it dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ efo yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli ni eegbo lɛ?

english: Your cassava plant is not dying; dropping leaves is its natural way of saving water during dry weather. Once the rains return, it will sprout new leaves and continue growing its underground roots.
ga: O-cassava tso lɛ gbooo. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Ebaakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi.

english: What makes my tomato plant leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during intense heat to shrink the area exposed to direct sunlight. This self-defense mechanism helps the plant conserve water and protects its tissues from burning.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ dɔlɛ be mli koni egbɔjɔ yɛ hei ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ hebuu gbɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ebuɔ fãji ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why do my watermelon vines look wilted in the afternoon sunshine even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense sun, watermelon leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can pull it up. The plant temporarily wilts to survive the afternoon heat and naturally bounces back once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Watermelon baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Tsei lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhi shi yɛ shwane latsaa lɛ mli. ni ebaaku esɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do so many flowers drop off my cocoa trees without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support with food and water. The tree drops extra flowers on purpose so it can send all its energy to developing a smaller number of healthy pods.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná kɛjɛ niyenii kɛ nu mli. Tso lɛ eto eyiŋ akɛ ebaashɛre fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni ekɛkudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛfee fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fioo komɛi.

english: Why are my hot pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho amɛbaai dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat or severe dryness. When stressed by severe weather, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo he ni egbi lɛ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii nyɛ amɛnɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why is my main plantain tree producing small bunches when there are many young shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei titrii lɛ daa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ he fɛɛ he hewɔ lɛ

english: The young shoots, or suckers, act like extra mouths to feed and suck away water and plant food from the main stalk. Cutting away all but one or two suckers ensures the main tree gets full nutrition to produce large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii loo tsei bibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabu krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ niyenii ni amɛmuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli, ja tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo niji wuji.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb high up on wooden stakes to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba lɛ?

english: Yam vines need height so their leaves can spread out completely and catch full sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which travels down to swell the tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛkwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa ni amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why are the top leaf funnels of my maize plants sticking together and full of dark sticky dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni muji ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ shi ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: This happens when tiny insects called aphids nest inside the growing leaves and feed on the sap. They produce a sweet, sticky waste that glues the leaves together and attracts mold, which stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids lɛ feɔ amɛtsu yɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nu lɛ. Amɛfeɔ jwɛi ni ŋɔɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe ni egbalaa ŋmeii. ni haa tsei nyɛɛɛ adara

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the heavy rains start in June?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ June mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away nitrogen and other essential nutrients deep into the soil where young maize roots cannot reach, causing the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa. Yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmãa bibii shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What makes my cassava leaves curl up and shrink during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Tiny insects called mealybugs and whiteflies hide under the leaves to suck plant juices during hot dry periods, which causes the cassava leaves to curl up and stunt the crop's growth.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs kɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tsei amli nu yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants die after standing in flooded water for just two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbo beni edamɔ nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli gbii enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the farm for too long, it suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and killing the plant quickly.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions, especially when cocoa branches are crowded and sunlight cannot dry the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ kookoo niji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi.

english: How can I stop tiny insects from eating and destroying my stored dry maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbe mi? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye ni akpata ŋmãa ni egbi ni ato lɛ hiɛ?

english: Weevils attack stored corn when there is moisture and air inside the storage room. Drying the maize completely and sealing it in airtight bags cuts off oxygen so pests cannot survive.
ga: Weevils tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ kwraa ni akɛwo vacuum kotoku mli lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ mli. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɛɛ ahi shi

english: Why do my garden eggs get soft and develop dark spots right after I harvest them for the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mikpa amɛ koni mikɛya jara nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvesting vegetables in the hot sun makes them lose moisture rapidly and stress. Harvesting early in the morning when the air is cool keeps the produce fresh and firm for buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ aduawai to hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i oya, ni ehaa amɛhaoɔ. Nikpamɔ leebi beni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nibii ni akpaa lɛ feɔ ehee ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛhaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the soil surface. When heavy bunches of fruits grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to pull the roots out of wet soil.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very big green leaves but producing no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi fɔfɔi loo aduawai bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why does my harvested yam take a long time to sprout even after I plant it in moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go into a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. The tuber will not sprout until this sleeping phase naturally ends, regardless of water or soil conditions.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Bulb lɛ ekwɛŋ kɛyashi nɛkɛ wɔɔhe be nɛɛ baagbe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni nu loo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he

english: Why do the bottoms of my cabbage heads rot and smell bad when the crop is almost mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabe yitsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ beni tso lɛ ebɛŋkɛ shweremɔ he lɛ?

english: Soft rot bacteria get inside the cabbage through tiny wounds made by insects or farming tools, especially when wet soil splashes onto the lower leaves.
ga: Muawai ni fiteɔ nii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ boteɔ kaabii lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii amli. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmeii loo okwaayeli nibii Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shwie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How does leaving dried leaves on top of my farmland soil help my crops grow better during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi ni mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Dried leaves act as mulch, which covers the soil like a blanket. This keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the hot sun, and turns into natural food for your crops as the leaves rot.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kuntu. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ebatsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha onibii beni baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land makes the soil richer for my next crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas pull nutrients directly from the air and store them in their roots. When the plants die, those nutrients stay in the soil and act as free fertilizer for crops like maize planted in the next season.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough water for me to start planting my maize seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil from a short distance beneath the surface into a ball. If it holds its shape without dripping water and crumbles easily when you poke it, the soil has just the right amount of moisture for seeds to sprout.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko kɛjɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. shishigbɛ ni etsɔ bɔɔlu Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tswa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and burn easily under direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees creates shade and traps moisture in the air, protecting the young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main tree for water and nutrients from the soil. Removing all but one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam plants to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make the energy required to grow large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, which also protects them from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning light green and yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tips usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves and strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellowish-green and curling up tightly at the ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe waa yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Curled and twisted cassava leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and weaken the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep center funnel of the maize plant during the day and feeds on young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil still has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: On very hot afternoons, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it out of the ground, causing temporary wilting. If the leaves stand up fresh again by morning, it is just heat stress.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ baa Kɛji baai lɛ fee ehee ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ No ji hulutsoo haomɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Applying well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growth stage helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally restores fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn hard like concrete shortly after the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter. Adding dry leaves, crop residues, or compost improves the soil structure, keeping it soft and helping it hold water much longer into the dry season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excess moisture and shade. Pruning overhead branches to let sunlight in and removing infected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo fe nine mli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from producing new peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee pepper heei lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil or soapy water helps control these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my harvested yam tubers small and covered in strange rough spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ji bibii ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Rough spots and small tubers are often caused by microscopic worms in the soil called nematodes. Planting clean seed yams and avoiding planting yams in the same spot every year keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii kɛ yitsei bibii baa. Dumɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ he. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anaa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my vegetable roots help them grow better?
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi afɔ shi. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mishishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It stops sunlight from evaporating soil moisture, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Hay ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to dig up without disturbing the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbaaa gbɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare main stem, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shi tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ni ehi shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ bulb ni mli elɛɛɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off during hot days without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents pollen from setting fruit, causing the blossoms to drop. Giving plants shade during the hottest afternoon hours and keeping soil moist helps retain flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ woɔ yibii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ afee tso lɛ he hulutsoo yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Young cocoa leaves are very sensitive to direct, harsh sun and burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a cool environment that protects tender cocoa plants while their roots get established.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛshãa oya waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I plant fail to sprout after the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are damaged by insects, planted too deep, or if the soil is waterlogged and causes the seed to rot. Using certified seeds and planting them at a shallow depth of about 2 to 3 centimeters ensures strong germination.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji kooloi fite amɛ. adu mli tsɔ Aloo kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ fite. Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli tsu nii ni adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃ waa.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready for planting before the main rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ dani maŋtsɛ nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi?

english: Soil is ready when it is moist enough to crumble easily in your hand without forming a sticky ball. Preparing ridges or mounds and mixing in decomposed manure before the heavy rains start gives young roots quick access to nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni okɛ oniji baagbala mli mlɛo ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ asaa ŋshɔŋ loo gɔŋ lɛ he ni akɛfutu ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen or the ground is flooded with water. Applying NPK or Urea fertilizer early during the first weeding helps the crop regain its rich green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. NPK loo urea ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra lɛ baaye abua. Klɛŋklɛŋ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and woody even though the leaves look large and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or remains very hard and compacted, cassava puts all its energy into growing thick top leaves instead of expanding its underground tubers. Loosening the soil during mound preparation helps tubers grow large and soft.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo ehi shi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Cassava lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni bulb lɛ feɔ agbo ni efeɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up and droop during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a natural defense to stop water from evaporating too quickly from the plant. However, if they stay rolled up into the evening, it means the crop lacks soil moisture and needs mulching or watering.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, nu akajɛ tsei lɛ amli oya tsɔ. Shi, kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛkpãtã kɛyashi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni atsɔ nɔ awo nɔ loo awo nɔ nu.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites that suck sap from the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying recommended organic neem extracts or mild insecticides early stops these pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Akɛ organic neem extract loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie kooloi nɛɛ anaa mra. dani ekpãtãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ

english: Why is it important for me to weed my field early before my crops start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔji amli mra lɛ? Dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil food away from crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get full nourishment when they are forming flowers, which directly leads to bigger and healthier harvests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii babaoo beni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni da ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are extremely hot, during sudden dry spells, or when the plant lacks calcium and phosphorus. Regular watering during dry weather and applying balanced fertilizer prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli trukaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ calcium kɛ phosphorus Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: How can I tell that my yams are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam plants show they are fully mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. Harvesting at this point ensures the tubers have accumulated full starch and will store for a long time without decaying.
ga: Sweet potato tso jieɔ dalɛ kpo kɛji akɛ baai kɛ wain tso lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ buaa ŋmeii anaa kwraa, ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. This often happens after heavy rain washes nutrients away or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up right on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in warm, overly humid conditions. It spreads when farms are too bushy or shaded, trapping moisture around the tree pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei bibii loo hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ mli. Emɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to save water. Supplying enough water at the roots and mulching can help keep the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛba amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and can burn easily. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves, acting as living umbrellas that provide shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo tso ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans helps put vital nutrients like nitrogen back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and covered in a sticky white powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni akɛ powda yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Your cassava is infested with cassava mealybugs or whiteflies. These tiny insects suck the sap out of the leaves, causing leaf deformation and releasing a sticky residue that attracts black mold.
ga: O-cassava lɛ mli eyi kɛ cassava mealybugs loo ŋmeii yɛŋ. Kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ejieɔ nɔ ko ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni gbalaa ŋmei diŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by bacterial wilt, a soil organism that enters through the roots and blocks the plant's internal water pipes, preventing water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛboteɔ mli ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ amli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to cut away small extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Too many extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother plant, which results in smaller bunches of plantains at harvest time.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei loo tsei babaoo ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why is it necessary to lift and stake my yam vines off the ground using tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to air and sun while protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do small insects bore tiny holes into my dried maize grains after I put them in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu bibii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli beni mikɛwo nitoo kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These are grain weevils. If maize is not thoroughly dried before bagging, or if insects laid eggs in the field, moisture trapped inside allows the eggs to hatch and eat through the grain kernels.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani awo lɛ kotoku mli Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔji amli Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ amɛye nii.

english: Why do my young plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy stems. As the fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds can easily uproot it if it is not supported with a wooden prop or earth heaped around its base.
