ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kɛji akɛ tsei loo muji ni ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ efiii amɛsɛɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for expanding the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off wet soil where they might rot, allowing maximum sunlight exposure so the tubers can grow large.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa enine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. This natural fertilizer stays in the ground to nourish your maize crop and keep the soil healthy.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha o-corn tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn pale yellow when water sits on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess standing water pushes air out of the soil spaces. Without oxygen, plant roots cannot breathe or absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the foliage to lose its green color.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and lose leaves during the dry hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛbaai lɛ miiho yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and thin leaves that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight or dry winds. They require temporary shade plants, such as plantain, to protect them from losing moisture too fast while their root system develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: What makes tiny ragged holes appear inside the growing leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ahe tsei ni miida lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl deep inside the central leaf funnel to feed on soft new tissue during the daytime, leaving behind leaf damage and tiny droppings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye fãji heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Shi baai ni efite kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ sɛɛ.

english: When crops are spaced too tightly, individual plants compete against each other for sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients. Energy goes into growing tall to reach light instead of filling out thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ ni haa mɔ daa koni enyɛ ená la Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, okɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei wuji afata he.

english: How do I choose the right part of the cassava stem to use for new planting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: Use the middle, mature section of healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 18 months old. Avoid the soft green tips which dry out fast, and the very bottom hard parts which sprout slowly.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18, ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni amɛdara lɛ amli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ atsu nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ ahe. kɛ shishigbɛ fã ni wa ni daa blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing green tomatoes turn dark brown and rotten before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when plants experience irregular watering. Inconsistent soil moisture prevents the plant from transporting essential calcium from the roots to the tip of developing fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ nine shɛ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkajie calcium ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers begin to rot underground if I leave them in the field late into the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall leaves soil waterlogged, which prevents roots from getting air and creates damp conditions that allow fungal diseases and soil bacteria to infect mature tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I wait until the rains are fully established in my area before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: If you plant right after the very first early rain, a sudden dry spell can occur immediately after. This dries out the young seedlings and kills them before their roots can grow deep enough to find moisture.
ga: Kɛji odu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Trukaa hɔmɔ shihilɛi baanyɛ aba yɛ no sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni egbe amɛ dani shishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛna ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers grow very thin and weak even when the leaves on top look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ.

english: If cassava plants are placed too close together, the plant spends all its energy growing foliage above ground competing for sunlight instead of expanding the underground tubers. Proper spacing gives the roots room to expand.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkɛye hulu la he akaŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛ bulbs lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa gbɛ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. They require partial shade from crops like plantains to retain leaf moisture while their root systems develop during their first couple of years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains mli koni amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same piece of farm every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or beans helps restore natural soil fertility.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ cowpeas loo beans ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is losing its strength and needs extra feeding before I clear it for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii kroko dani ajie lɛ kɛha dumɔwui?

english: Signs of weak soil include crops growing slowly, pale yellow foliage on young plants, soil that turns hard and crusty quickly, and lower harvests compared to previous seasons.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ewaa oya. kɛ ŋmaa ni baa shi kɛ akɛto nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ he.

english: Why are there small worms eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These are typically Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest in Ghana. They hide in the center leaves of young maize to feed, so early detection and applying targeted organic or chemical treatments is necessary to prevent severe crop damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ana mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii waa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before they ever turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛmiitsɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, which usually happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering where the soil swings between very dry and very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster and overpower my young crops right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa ni eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ kunim amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to compete aggressively for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because young crop seedlings grow more slowly at first, early weeding gives them the head start they need to establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo fe shishijee lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ afee klalo ni amɛfee shishifãi.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be trained up wooden stakes instead of letting them spread across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tso atsɔse mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa he ni agbele lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth and improves airflow around the vine, which prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil and protects the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: Why should I remove some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Leaving too many side shoots (suckers) creates heavy competition for nutrients and water between the main plant and the suckers, resulting in smaller plantain bunches. Pruning back excess suckers ensures large, heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii ni naa wa aba tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa yibii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: How do I know if my farmland in Ghana has good soil for growing tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ tomato?

english: Tomatoes thrive best in loose, well-draining sandy-loam soil rich in organic material. Heavy clay soil that stays waterlogged after rain will cause tomato roots to rot, so good drainage is key.
ga: Tomato daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu shwieɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaha tomato shishifãi lɛ agbo. No hewɔ lɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant tomatoes so they don't get destroyed by rain?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu tomato koni nugbɔ akafite amɛ?

english: Tomatoes prefer dry weather with controlled watering. Planting toward the end of the main rainy season or during the dry season using basic irrigation prevents wet-weather diseases like fungal blights.
ga: Tomato sumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ akudɔɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ naagbee loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ shishijee nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ he helai tamɔ fungal leaf blight lɛ naa.

english: Should I buy certified tomato seeds from agro-dealers, or can I just dry and plant seeds from tomatoes I buy at the market?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe tomato dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ? Aloo manyɛ magbi tomato dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Market tomatoes are usually hybrids, and their saved seeds often produce weak plants with low yields. Buying certified seed varieties bred for Ghana's climate gives you strong plants that resist local pests and soil diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛfee nɔ ko. Ni bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ ahemɔ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes repeatedly in the same soil allows tomato-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in the ground over time. Rotating your field with crops like maize or cassava starves those pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tomato mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baatsake. Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye nakai kooloi lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do I really need to stake my tomato plants with sticks, or can I leave them to spread on the ground?
ga: Ehe bahia waa akɛ mikɛ tso adu tomato tso. Aloo manyɛ maha ekɛshwie shikpɔŋ?

english: Tying tomato plants to wooden stakes keeps the leaves and fruits off the damp ground. This prevents ground rot, improves airflow, reduces disease spread, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tomato tsei fĩ tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akabote he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Ha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi Ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Is it better to splash water over the whole tomato plant or pour it directly at the root base?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ nu ashwie tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ anɔ loo oooshwie amɛshishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Always apply water directly to the soil at the base of the plant. Wetting tomato leaves creates a damp environment where fungal diseases spread quickly in warm Ghanaian weather.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tomato baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop usually happens when plants face extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady and providing partial shade during very hot weather helps the blossoms stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo fã ko yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: What causes the leaves of my young tomato plants to turn yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi?

english: Bottom leaves turning yellow is a common sign of nitrogen deficiency or early blight disease from wet soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or balanced fertilizer usually helps restore plant strength.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ nitrogen ni faaa loo mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit due to irregular watering. Consistent, moderate watering helps the plant absorb nutrients evenly and stops the bottom rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa, ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How can I stop caterpillars from boring tiny holes inside my tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmei ko naa koni ekafo bu bibioo ko? Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ehi tomato mli?

english: Caterpillars hatch from eggs laid on the leaves and tunnel into the fruit. Inspecting your plants regularly to pick off damaged fruits early and using safe neem-based or approved extension sprays will keep pests under control.
ga: Kplukai fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛboteɔ aduawai lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli daa koni ojie aduawai ni efite lɛ mra. Ni kɛ akɛ neem ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akabote mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nutrients, especially nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer early in the growing stage helps the leaves turn deep green and make food for strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eha niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and get scorched under direct, heavy sunlight. Keeping or planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a cooler environment and holds soil moisture to help young cocoa survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa, ni hulu lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce small and weak fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa onibii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes through the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely pests like Fall Armyworms that feed on tender leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying recommended pest control measures stops them before they destroy the growing shoots.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ baai bibii. Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ amli mra. kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ekpaa tsei nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch max sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves healthy and off the damp ground, allowing the plant to make food to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛ bulb agboi baa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for light and soil food. Giving crops proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough room to grow strong stems and roots.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ baawu amɛhe kɛha la kɛ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ he ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them and starves them of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. and suffocate Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Seeds need steady soil moisture to sprout properly. It is best to wait until the ground is thoroughly wet from two or three good rains before sowing so seeds do not dry up.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ hewɔ dani odu dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkagbi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing consistent water and mulching the soil keeps the roots cool and helps flowers stay on to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food plants need to stay green. When the plant cannot find enough nitrogen in the soil, it takes it from its older bottom leaves and sends it to feed the newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaagbala kɛjɛ shishigbɛ, baai momo lɛ amli ni etsu koni eyaye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field with no trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Without taller shade trees or plantains nearby to shield them, the intense sun burns their delicate leaves and dries out their soil before their roots can properly develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baabu amɛhe lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to hide inside the middle of my young corn plants and chew holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Mikɛ mihe miiwo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni mikɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ miiye.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs on young corn. They crawl deep into the central leafy funnel of the plant to eat the soft, growing leaves where they are safe from birds and direct weather.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ. Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ okpoi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot in the ground during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the farm and water sits in the soil for too long, oxygen gets cut off from the roots, allowing fungal rots to attack and destroy the cassava.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ha ŋmei lɛ atutua ŋmei lɛ ni efite.

english: What happens if I plant several seeds together in the exact same hole to save space?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of getting healthy plants, you end up with thin, weak stalks that produce small, poor-quality yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaaná tso ni mli wa lɛ Ebafee akɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ ni amɛhiii kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience high heat or prolonged dry spells. When the plant senses stress or lack of water, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛbote latsaa ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiihao loo nu efo amɛmli lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi shi.

english: How does adding dried animal manure or compost help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Manure and compost act as natural plant food that slowly releases nutrients over time. They also help sandy soils hold on to moisture longer and loosen hard soil so crop roots can easily spread and drink water.
ga: Manure kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni yaa hiɛ fiofio. Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii fiofio Beni be hoɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hu ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ agbɔjɔ Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛnu nu.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water and nutrients out of the soil before your crops can reach them. They also block sunlight, starving your main crops of the light energy they need to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ hu naa. Enɛ haa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ náa la hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for me to plant seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the early rains become regular and soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light shower is risky because if the sun returns for a few dry days, your newly germinated seeds will dry out and die underground.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baagbee shi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Be kome pɛ ji oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ni egbi gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are white powdery spots spreading on the leaves of my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miigbɛ eshwa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is a leaf disease called powdery mildew, which often appears in humid weather when plants are packed tightly together. The fungus feeds on the leaf sap, causing the leaves to dry up and drop off prematurely.
ga: Powda yɛŋ lɛ ji tso hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli beni tsei eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ. Fungus yeɔ baa mli nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential plant food, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil that prevents them from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni no haaa amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if insects or a plant sickness is making my tomato leaves curl up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi loo tso hela ko miiha mi tomato baai lɛ miiho?

english: If tiny whiteflies are under the leaves, they are spreading a virus that curls the leaves. If there are no insects, extreme heat or dry soil can make tomato leaves roll up to conserve water.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii yɛji bibii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, amɛmiigbɛ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ amɛshwãa. Kɛji kooloi bɛ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe koni nu akafite.

english: What causes tiny holes to appear all over my cabbage leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa bu bibioo lɛ feɔ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ kaabe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: Tiny holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae, which hatch from eggs laid on the leaves and feed mostly at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ daimondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii babaoo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my cassava stem cuttings slanting instead of standing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu yucca tsei aniji yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at a slant buries more nodes under the soil, which encourages more roots and larger tubers to grow along the stem, making harvesting easier.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava tsei yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaafu nodes babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ woɔ shishifãi wuji kɛ bulbs hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa ekpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more crops on my small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize too close forces the plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, tall stalks with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni dumɔwui bibii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: How can I tell when my yams under the ground are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Yam leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally when the tuber has reached full maturity and stopped growing underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛkpaa shikpɔŋ shishi shweremɔ lɛ.

english: Saving seeds from hybrid maize leads to lower yields and uneven growth because hybrid seeds lose their strength and uniform traits after the first harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise leaving dry grass on top of the soil around my crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ashi jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry grass on top of the soil acts as mulch, keeping the soil cool, reducing water evaporation during hot days, and suppressing weed growth.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi ni egbi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates a protective umbrella that keeps the air humid and the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shade ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yam plants store energy in their underground tubers by gathering sunlight through their leaves. Staking gets the vines off the damp ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases, resulting in much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛbuaa naa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baajie wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a vital food for growth. When nitrogen runs out, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, signaling that it needs fertilizer or compost immediately.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ ba naagbee Tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does chemical fertilizer burn or kill my plants if I put it right next to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shãa loo efiteɔ tsei kɛji mikɛ amɛ ma tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts. When placed right against the stem or main root, it sucks water out of the plant leaves and root cells like a sponge, causing the plant to wither and burn.
ga: Mineral salts ni mli wa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tamɔ sponji. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei agbi ni amɛshã.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up, shrinking, and turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miiho, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers prevents this damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛhaa lɛ baatsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stem before any tomatoes can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani tomato lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. Irrigating regularly during hot spells helps keep the blossoms cool and healthy enough to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is causing ragged holes and powder inside the funnel leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu kɛ powda ni bɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of the corn plant during the day and eats through the young leaves before they open.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni eyeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai bibii lɛ anɔ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil if I leave them planted during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in clay or poorly drained soil for too long, oxygen gets trapped out, causing rot fungi to multiply and destroy the roots before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Oxygen lɛ efo mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ shishifãi lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over completely when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? He ni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ agboi yɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and soft compared to trees. As heavy fruit bunches grow, strong winds pull the root mass right out of loose soil; placing a strong wooden prop stick under the heavy stalk stops the tree from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe yɛ blɛoo kɛ akɛto tsei ahe. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni wa wo tso lɛ shishi ni tsii lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishifãi.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that bakes the ground. Seeds germinating in moist soil will die if the rain stops completely for two weeks right after sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baagboi kɛji nugbɔ kpa trukaa otsii enyɔ yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green. This often happens when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when the land has been farmed continuously without adding manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛ́ aya nɔ atsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. The temporary wilting is the plant's way of conserving moisture, and leaves usually bounce back in the cooler evening once heat stress drops.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be kukuoo mli ni tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ sɛɛkuu yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli beni dɔlɛ he haomɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air temperature gets too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to wet. High heat damages pollen, preventing fertilization, so the plant sheds the flower to save energy until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branches before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and dark conditions. The fungus enters through the pod skin, turning it black, but clearing weeds and pruning tree branches lets in sunlight and air to stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ duŋ. Fuji lɛ boteɔ pod lɛ hewolo mli, ni ehaa efeɔ ediŋŋ. Shi jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli koni ekɛkpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout when I plant them into dry soil after a brief rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need a steady supply of moisture to wake up and push out roots. If you plant after just a light rain, the topsoil dries out quickly, leaving the seed stranded without enough water to complete germination.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛje kpo. Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if left in the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain saturates the ground and water sits without draining, air is pushed out of the soil, causing the roots to suffocate and rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu bɛ jɛmɛ. Akɛ hewalɛ nyɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of young leaves. As these pests suck out plant sap, they distort the leaf tissue or spread viruses that make new growth twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Amɛbaafite baa lɛ mli fãji loo amɛgbɛ helai ni kɛ dalɛ hee baa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crop after I clear my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for years and are adapted to grow aggressively in low-nutrient soil. As soon as you clear the land and expose the soil to sunlight and rain, wild weed seeds germinate instantly before crop seeds get established.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo hulu kɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli pɛ kɛkɛ ni Wild weed dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and crooked instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards by pushing through loose earth. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the tuber cannot expand easily downwards, forcing it to bend, branch, or stop growing big.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa kɛyaa shi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo, ni no nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkoto, amɛfee niji, loo amɛkpa amɛdalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall shade trees off the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and creating a cool environment until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ofee shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged; applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants keep falling off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop off mainly because tiny insects like flower thrips attack them, or because the plants lack water during flowering; spraying an approved, safe insecticide at the first sign of buds protects the flowers.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo ejaakɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ tutuaa amɛ. aloo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling tightly and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by severe heat stress; controlling whiteflies early and covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Early Whitefly Control Ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to build food for the tuber; staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to prevent leaf diseases and allows maximum sunlight to reach the plant, making the yams grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ bulbs lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsei lɛ ahe hela naa ni eha hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ he. Ha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ babaoo.

english: Does the direction I point my cassava stem cutting into the ground really matter?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mitsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he hia?

english: Yes, planting cassava cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upwards ensures stems grow straight up quickly and roots develop properly underneath; planting them upside down slows down growth and severely reduces tuber yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, yucca tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adamɔ shi oya ni shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo ni ebaaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the soil, leading to smaller harvests each season.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ fioo pɛ baaba yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-corn lɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil and provides extra food for the nearby maize crop without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa niyenii kroko ni awooo he nyɔmɔ kroko.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when the crop is actively growing—usually 2 to 3 weeks after the seeds sprout—and again around flowering, provided the soil is moist enough for the roots to soak up the food.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ beni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ—bei pii lɛ, otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ—kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why does millet survive dry weather and heat in the savanna much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ latsaa ni yɔɔ Savannah lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Millet has deep, efficient roots and tough leaves that stop water from evaporating quickly, allowing it to withstand long periods without rain where maize leaves would wither and die.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, kɛ baai ni mli wa ni haa nu shwieɔ oya. Enɛ haa ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Abɛi baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ edara ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and when you open a few sample pods, the inside of the shell displays dark brown or black markings instead of staying white.
ga: Peanuts lɛ efee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni kɛ́ ogbele sample pods komɛi lɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli jieɔ su ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ kpo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehi shi yɛŋ

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the soil is low on nitrogen. The plant is moving remaining nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the young leaves growing at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny organisms on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. When the crop finishes, this trapped nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu nii agbe naa Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, mites, or whiteflies, or a virus they spread. These insects drink the plant's juices, which starves the leaves and causes them to distort and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye baai lɛ. ni eha etsake ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni ehiɛ edɔ.

english: Why are the middle leaves of my young maize plants full of holes with green dust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ sũ eŋɔli yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm. They hide in the central funnel of the plant, chewing young leaves before they unfold and leaving behind their powdery droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ fall armyworm. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii dani amɛgbele ni oshi ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfee powda.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots compete underground for food and water, while their leaves compete for sunlight. Spacing them correctly ensures every plant gets enough resources to form full, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ. Beni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ amɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the suckers grow around my main plantain tree at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces the main plant to share its food and water with all of them, resulting in small fruit bunches. Keeping only one main stem, one medium sucker, and one small sucker concentrates energy for larger bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ fɛɛ aja niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii bibii. Ni aaahi tso titri kome pɛ nɔ Sucker ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ sucker bibioo kome Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ hewalɛ ama shi kɛha tsofa-kɛ-ŋma agbo.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep dropping off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from dry weather stress or a lack of tiny pollinating insects like midges. Maintaining soil moisture and shade encourages pollination and helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli loo ŋmeii bibii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii baa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their blossoms without forming tomatoes during hot dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato wooo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme dry heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making it impossible for the flower to form fruit. When stressed by heat, the plant naturally drops its flowers to save water and stay alive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo yibii Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when it rains heavily for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen from air pockets in the soil to stay alive. When water covers the ground for too long without draining, the roots drown and soil bacteria cause them to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi.

english: Why do I need to lift and tie my yam vines onto tall stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni mikɛfiɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce energy for root growth. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, giving leaves maximum sunlight while protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain and cassava on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside young cocoa is beneficial. Food crops like plantain provide early income and food for your family while giving the young cocoa seedlings the necessary shade and protection from direct sunlight in their early years.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains haa shika kɛ niyenii mra kɛhaa oweku lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to clear all the big trees from my land before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkajie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ dani wɔdu kookoo lɛ?

english: Leaving selected tall trees provides controlled shade that protects cocoa leaves from sun scorch, keeps the soil moist during dry periods, and helps the cocoa trees stay healthy for many decades.
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni ahala lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cacao tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal attack common during rainy seasons. It spreads when farms are overly humid and shaded, but regular harvesting and cutting away diseased pods helps protect healthy ones.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni fɔɔ baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ. Shi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akpaa daa ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do young leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and droop during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow and drooping leaves during Harmattan indicate water stress and excessive sun exposure. Mulching around the base of the trees and providing shade trees helps soil retain moisture and shields the leaves.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ tsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ha tsei lɛ ashishi ni akɛ hulutsoo ha lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them fall off without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee pods?

english: It is natural for cocoa trees to produce far more flowers than they can feed, shedding up to 90% of them. However, extreme flower drop can be caused by lack of water, insect pests, or poor pollination by tiny insects called midgets.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua. Fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ 90% baagbee shi. Shi kɛlɛ, nu ni bɛ, kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ dwarfs lɛ ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afite babaoo.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting before my new cocoa trees start bearing fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ midu migbe naa lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani kookoo tsei heei lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years to produce their first full crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: When planted too close, cocoa trees fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin trunks, low pod yield, and creates a damp environment where diseases spread easily.
ga: Kɛ adu Cocoa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my plot is good for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark in color, crumbly, and rich in decaying plant matter. It should drain water easily so roots do not sit in flooded water, while still holding enough moisture during dry periods.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni tsei ni fiteɔ babaoo yɛ mli. Esa akɛ etsɔ mlɛo. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ akabote nu ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lolo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: If I plant a cocoa farm now, will the trees keep producing pods when I get older?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo ŋmɔ bianɛ Ani tso lɛ baaya nɔ ewo ŋmeii be mli ni midaa lɛ?

english: Yes, a well-managed cocoa tree can remain productive for 30 to 40 years or more. Proper pruning, weed control, soil nutrition, and pest management keep aging trees bearing healthy pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. jwɛi ni afoɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni edara lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield very few pods in some years and many pods in other years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ afii komɛi amli, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afii krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa yields vary based on weather patterns, rainfall timing, and farm management. A year with good rainfall during flowering followed by proper insect and weed control results in a much higher harvest.
ga: Cocoa yibiiwoo srɔtoi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, nugbɔnɛmɔ bei, kɛ ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ. Afii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji kooloi kɛ jwɛi ni akudɔɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep wilting and dying when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. Keeping tall shade trees or planting plantains next to them creates a cool shelter that holds moisture and protects the young plants until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛhe ko ni mli ejɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa.

english: Does it make a difference which end of the cassava stick I put into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei lɛ, ani esoro lɛ yɛ naagbee ni?

english: Yes, cassava stems have small buds that must point upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stem has to bend unnaturally to reach the surface, leading to weak growth and very small tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋwɛi Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ abɔle ehe yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ koni eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛyitsei lɛ hu feɔ bibii waa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I harvest more corn from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, when maize plants are packed too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This struggle leaves you with thin stalks and small, empty cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ ta nɛɛ haa onáa ŋmeii komɛi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the rest of the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and manufacture their food.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he hɔmɔ miiye onibii lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛfee niyenii.

english: How does spreading dry grass or palm fronds around my vegetables help them during the hot season?
ga: Jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi-aduawai lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, blocking the fierce sun from evaporating water and keeping the roots cool and moist.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛjɛɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do I need to heap dirt into big mounds to plant my yams instead of placing them in flat soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee sũ agbo ko ni mikɛdu sweet potatoes moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam roots need loose, soft soil to expand easily into large tubers. Planting in raised mounds loosens the hard dirt and allows heavy rains to drain away so the yams do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, efiteee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray insect medicine on my crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the afternoon heat, liquid spray evaporates into the air before it can kill the insects, and the combination of strong sunshine and chemical spray can scorch your crop's leaves.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani agbeɔ kooloo lɛ. Ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that specific plant to multiply in the dirt, making your future crops sick much faster.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni yeɔ tsei komɛi lɛ babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa owɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ yeɔ hela oya kwraa.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more when I allow tall weeds to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mihaa jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds serve as natural homes and breeding grounds for harmful insects, making it easy for the pests to move directly onto your crops and damage them.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shia kɛ he ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience severe heat or dry soil, as the plant sacrifices its flowers to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashã afɔle koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water. Nitrogen is the plant food that makes leaves green and healthy, so adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer can help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are tiny green insects clumping together under my pepper leaves and causing them to curl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: These insects are aphids, small pests that suck the sap out of leaves, which weakens the plant and curls the foliage. You can spray them with a mixture of soapy water or a wood-ash solution to clean them off.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji aphids. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tso mli sũ mli tsofa afɔ nɔ ni okɛtsumɔ he.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yams need loose, soft, and deep soil mounds to expand properly. If the soil is hard, compact, or full of stones, it squeezes the growing tuber and prevents it from forming a smooth shape.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Ebaaha bulb ni miida lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Should I start planting my maize immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for two or three steady rains before planting. The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that can dry up the soil and kill young seeds before they get established.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani oduɔ nii. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui bibii dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold up heavy bunches during windstorms. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden props or bamboo poles helps keep the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔ panicles agboi amli yɛ ahum be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when the plant does not get enough consistent water. Providing light shade and regular watering during hot dry periods helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko ha tso lɛ, ni aha lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp, and overly shaded farms. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight and air reach the trunk helps dry out the farm and prevent the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Tso niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: Why are the stems of my young bean seedlings getting cut off near the soil surface overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ afo mi-pea tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by cutworms—caterpillars that hide in the soil during the day and come out at night to chew through tender stems. Clearing weeds around your seedlings removes their hiding spots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛyaye tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baaye abua ni ejie hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava on the same spot every year drains the soil of specific plant food and lets pests and diseases build up in the dirt. Switching to leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha tsei komɛi aná ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni aaatsake kɛya ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the excessive leaves and branches from my crops when they are growing so big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛdara waa lɛ?

english: Removing extra or excessive branches gives your crops space and sunlight to breathe. This helps the plant focus its energy on producing healthy fruit rather than just growing leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa loo ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ naa gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni ekɛmuɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai ni ebaakwɛ̃ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant them too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are packed too tightly, they fight each other for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. Spacing them out properly clears room for each plant to feed well and produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ni he hiaa lɛ koni eye nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: My old farm is not producing as much as before; how can I make it fresh and productive again?
ga: Miŋmɔ momo lɛ wooo yibii babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee lɛ ehee ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can make an old farm feel new again by pruning overgrown branches, clearing out thick weeds, and removing diseased plants to allow fresh light and air into the farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha ŋmɔ momo ko anu he akɛ eji ehee ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ooofolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. ni ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli.
