english: Why does clearing bushes and weeds regularly help my main crops grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ?

english: Weeds and thick bushes steal water, space, and food from your main crops. Clearing them gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can grow healthy and strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ juɔ nu, he ko, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my crops look weak and produce little fruit even though they have lots of heavy green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant grows excessive leaves, it wastes all its energy on leaf growth instead of making fruit. Trimming back the excess helps redirect energy into growing better food.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ baai babaoo Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. Nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does removing sick plants or rotten pods stop sickness from spreading across my farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ loo ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hela akagbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Diseased plant parts carry germs that travel to healthy crops through rain and wind. Clearing out infected parts breaks the chain of infection and protects the rest of your harvest.
ga: Tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ hiɛɔ helai ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ, efoɔ hela lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli, ni ebuɔ onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees get diseased more easily when the farm is very dark and crowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai baa mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ oya be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Dark and overcrowded farms trap damp air and block sunlight, creating a warm, wet environment where fungal diseases like black pod thrive and spread quickly.
ga: Okwaafoi ni ewo duŋ, ni eyi obɔ lɛ mɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya lɛ

english: What simple step can I take during the rainy season to keep my crops from catching fungal diseases?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛi komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Prune extra branches and clear space around your crops so the wind can dry the leaves quickly after rainfall, making it hard for fungal diseases to survive.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji krokomɛi kɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ agbi baai lɛ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akɛ amɛaahi shi.

english: Why is taking proper care of my crop fields so important for my community and Ghana as a whole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa mi akutso lɛ kɛ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Healthy farms produce clean food and strong cash crops like cocoa. When farmers harvest abundant crops, food prices stay affordable and the entire nation prospers economically.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ niyenii ni he tse kɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa, tamɔ kookoo, kɛ́ okwaafoi lɛ kpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Niyenii jara baafee nɔ ni jara waaa. ni maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ tee hiɛ yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm leaves have become too dense and need to be cleared?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ebɔle tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni ajie amɛ?

english: If sunlight cannot reach the soil beneath your crops during midday, or if air feels very trapped and hot inside your farm, the growth is excessive and needs to be cleared for better air space.
ga: Kɛji hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane mli, Aloo kɛji onuɔ he akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ emɔ ni edɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, shweremɔ lɛ fa fe nine, ni ehe miihia ni ajie mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their roots are still small and delicate. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted nearby to act as living umbrellas that trap moisture and protect the leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo ni amɛhe waaa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsiɔ baai lɛ ashãa naa.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain tree, they fight with the main tree for food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Pruning away extra shoots and leaving only two or three allows the main tree to get enough energy to produce large bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Ekɛ tso titri lɛ baawu koni ena niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ashi niji fioo pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ niji wuji.

english: Why do my maize leaves have small ragged holes in them and look eaten overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ ná bu bibii, ni egbɛ eshwa, ni etamɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes on young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the central leaves during the day and feed at night. Catching them early and applying natural neem extracts or recommended treatments helps stop them from destroying the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ yɛ shwane mli ni eyeɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem mli nu loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmɔji akpãtãmɔ.

english: This rot is usually caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. When the soil dries out completely and then gets soaked, the plant cannot move calcium properly to the developing tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa ni edɔ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛya tomatoi ni miida lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with natural nitrogen.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When a crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, it takes whatever nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves and sends it to feed the new leaves growing at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Eheɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​koni eyaha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy green leaves but leaves me with small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus or potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of feeding and swelling the tubers hidden below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ atsɔ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on sticks instead of letting them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ miniji lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce the food needed to grow big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air and prevents them from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Maize plants fall over if they are planted too shallowly or if the soil around their roots is too loose. Mounding dirt firmly around the base of the stems gives the brace roots a firm hold in the ground.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli etse tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi shiŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efiɔ shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and drying up even though there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your crops are suffering from a nutrient shortage or a fungal disease attacking the roots. Applying the correct, genuine crop treatment helps protect the plant so it can take up nutrients and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni sa ni ji anɔkwale ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ahe koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Using approved fungicide sprays protects the pods by creating a shield that prevents fungal spores from growing on the cocoa tree.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly when they start producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔi shishi pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Sudden wilting is usually caused by pests or bacterial diseases in the soil blocking the stems. Treating the soil or seeds with registered crop protection products prevents these hidden enemies from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni baa trukaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni abuɔ tsei ahe ni aŋmala awo wolo nɔ lɛ tsu shikpɔŋ loo dumɔwui lɛ ahe nii lɛ, ebaatsi henyɛlɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why are fall armyworms still eating my crops even after I sprayed pest medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Pests can survive if the spray is unapproved, fake, or improperly mixed, or if the worms hide deep inside the plant leaves. Using authentic, EPA-approved insecticides ensures the active ingredients are strong enough to kill the pests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ahaaa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ hegbɛ, amale, loo akɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi shi. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tee amɛhe amɛwo tso lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni EPA kpɛlɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ agbe kooloi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my farm than my actual food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that aggressively steal water and light from your crops. Applying proper weed control products clears the field early so your crops do not have to fight for survival.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni juɔ nu kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ yiwalɛ gbɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaajie jɛmɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahi ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do insects destroy crop leaves without me seeing them during the daytime?
ga: Te ŋmeii feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛfiteɔ tsei ahe baai ni minyɛɛɛ mana amɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Many crop pests come out only at night or hide under the leaves to avoid heat. Certified crop sprays leave a temporary protective layer on the leaves that stops these hidden insects when they feed.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo jeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ pɛ loo amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ashishi koni amɛkafee hulutsoo lɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ anaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why did the leaves on my cabbage burn and turn brown after I sprayed them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage lɛ nɔ lɛ shãa ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop leaves burn if the chemical product is too harsh, unapproved, or mixed incorrectly. Using genuine, EPA-certified products ensures the spray is tested and safe for your specific crop leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ baai baashã kɛji tsofa ni akɛfee lɛ mli wa tsɔ. bɛ nɔmimaa loo akɛfutu mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Nibii ni EPA tsɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ aka tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ akwɛ ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha otso lɛ mli tsei pɔtɛɛ lɛ.

english: Will spraying medicine on my vegetable farm make the food unsafe for my family to eat?
ga: Ani mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ tsofa baashwie nɔ lɛ baaha niyenii ni miweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Registered crop medicines are safe when used properly, as they break down before harvest. Choosing official EPA-approved products and waiting the recommended days before harvesting guarantees the food remains safe to eat.
ga: Tsofai ni aŋmala awo wolo nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ejaakɛ ebaagbo dani akpa. Kɛ́ ohala nibii ni EPA lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ eji nɔ ni sa, ni omɛ gbi ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashɛ he lɛ dani akpa niyenii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ.

english: How do I know if the spray medicine I am buying for my crop is safe and real?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni eji anɔkwale?

english: Real crop medicines come in properly sealed containers with an official EPA registration number on the label. This seal and number prove the product has been tested to protect your crops without harming them.
ga: Tsofai diɛŋtsɛ ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ baa yɛ tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa mli, ni amɛyɛ EPA nɔmba ni aŋmalaa awoɔ wolo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ naatsii kɛ yibɔ nɛɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ aka nibii nɛɛ akwɛ koni ebu onibii ahe ni eyeee amɛ awui.

english: Why do some crops stay small and stunted while other plants right next to them grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi hiɔ shi bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Stunted growth happens when young roots are damaged by soil pests or diseases early on. Protecting seeds and young plants with certified farm treatments gives every crop an equal chance to grow strong.
ga: Nɔ ni haa shishifãi bibii lɛ daa lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fite shishifãi bibii lɛ mra. Dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui ni abuɔ he kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji ni awo he odaseyeli mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ hegbɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow and drop due to plant stress, which can be caused by a lack of water during dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or serious infections like cocoa swollen shoot virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ haomɔ hewɔ. Ekolɛ nu ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo helai ni naa wa tamɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm has been attacked by swollen shoot disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji bud swollen hela lɛ etutua mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You will notice swollen red veins on leaves, swollen stems or roots, small rounded pods, and a gradual dieback of tree branches until the whole tree dies.
ga: Obaana ŋmeii tsuji ni efuu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo, ni tso lɛ niji lɛ daa fiofio. Egbo kɛyashi tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbo.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, very wet, humid weather, especially when farms are overgrown with weeds or trees are planted too close together.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ waa, titri lɛ kɛ́ jwɛi ebɔle ŋmɔji ahe loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Is it safe to plant new cocoa seedlings on land where old trees died from disease?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei momoi egboi yɛ hela hewɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but you must first completely remove and cut down all infected trees, clear the farm properly, and allow shade trees or temporary crops to establish before planting new seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ofolɔ amɛhe. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni oha tsei lɛ aha hulutsoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii be kukuoo ko dani odu dumɔwui heei.

english: Why are my older cocoa trees yielding very few pods even though I weed the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso ni egbɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural yield capacity declines, soil nutrients become exhausted, and the trees become more vulnerable to pests and aging diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, nɔ ni ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli lɛ baa shi. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Ni tsei lɛ baafee mɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni haa mɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry weather to reduce water loss through their leaves and protect themselves from harsh sun intensity.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why do cocoa flowers fall off the tree trunk without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: High flower drop happens when the tree is stressed by drought, lacks nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects like midges present to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ baa kɛji hɔmɔ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ gbɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: Why do cassava plants grow well near young cocoa trees, but my cocoa stays small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ? Shi mi-kookoo lɛ ji bibioo lolo.

english: Cassava grows very fast and has aggressive root systems that compete with young cocoa trees for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight.
ga: Cassava daa oya waa ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite niyenii mli hewalɛ beni miduɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: If your seedlings grow very slowly, leaves remain small or yellowish, and yields drop consistently despite good rainfall, the soil nutrients have likely been depleted.
ga: Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ dara blɛoo waa lɛ Baai lɛ hiɔ shi bibii loo ŋmɔŋ. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Ekolɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baafite.

english: What causes small holes in my young cocoa leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi kookoo baai bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by insect pests like mirids (capsids) or leaf-eating beetles that feed on the soft, fresh growth that appears when rains start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ mirids (capsids) loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ ehee ni jeɔ kpo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cocoa on land where floodwaters have recently receded?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, receded floodwater often leaves behind rich, damp soil that gives young cocoa seedlings a strong start. However, you must make sure the soil is moist rather than waterlogged, as standing water can rot the tree roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ nu afua shĩɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni mli edɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, obaasumɔ ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni nu baabɔle he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi agbo.

english: How can I tell if my land has the right moisture level for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be ni sa kɛha kookoo dumɔ?

english: Dig a small hole about hand-deep and grab a handful of soil. If it squeezes into a damp ball without water dripping out, the land has good moisture for planting young cocoa trees.
ga: Tsɔmɔmɔ bu bibioo ko ni miihe ashɛ onine mlibotemɔ he ni omɔ shikpɔŋ ni okɛ onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ashɛre ŋmɔtɔ ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa kɛha kookoo tsei bibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if the ground stays flooded for too long?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If soil remains soaked without draining, the roots cannot breathe and will rot. Excess water also brings fungal diseases like black pod, so good land drainage is necessary.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛbaagboi. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji aba, no hewɔ lɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia waa.

english: How many years do I need to wait after planting cocoa before I can start harvesting?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani enyɛ ekpa?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties start bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years, while older traditional varieties take 4 to 5 years. Proper care during these early years ensures long-term high yields.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Kwɛmɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua. Enɛɛmɛi haa sɛɛnamɔi babaoo baa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How long does a coconut tree take from planting until it starts yielding fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties begin fruiting within 3 to 4 years, whereas tall varieties take about 6 to 8 years. Regular weeding and care are needed while you wait for them to mature.
ga: Kokooi bibii lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni kokooi ni kɛlɛ lɛ baahe afii 6 kɛyashi 8. Ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ daa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do tree crops like cocoa and coconut require so much patience before they produce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei amli nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmei biɔ tsuishitoo babaoo dani afee amɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike quick crops like maize or vegetables, tree crops build deep root systems and strong trunks in their early years. Once established, this early growth allows them to produce fruit continuously for decades.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ahe. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli. Kɛji ato amɛ shishi pɛ Nɛkɛ mra be mli dalɛ nɛɛ baaha amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa crop taking longer to produce fruit than my neighbor's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii fe mikutsoŋnyo cacao tso lɛ?

english: Differences in crop timing usually depend on the specific variety planted, the soil's moisture and nutrient levels, shade protection, and weed control. Consistent farm care helps trees reach maturity faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔ bei amli lɛ damɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shade hebuu kɛ jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ daa yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Can I plant coconut trees on parts of my farm where cocoa does not grow well?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei tso yɛ he ko ni ŋmei kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ?

english: Yes, coconut trees are very tough and can thrive in sandy or drier soils where cocoa struggles. Planting coconuts in those sections allows you to make productive use of your entire farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ he ni kookoo bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni oookwɛ yɛ fãi nɛɛ amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I make good use of the leftover space on my farm after planting my main cash crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ beni midu mishika ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can plant short-term food crops like plantain, cassava, or vegetables in the open spaces between young trees. This provides food and income while your main tree crops grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku tamɔ plantains, cassava loo aduawai yɛ hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ tsei bibii ateŋ. Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ shika baa yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to ensure my cocoa trees give a abundant harvest once they mature?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi-cacao tsei lɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛ́ amɛdara?

english: To get plenty of produce, space your trees properly during planting, clear surrounding weeds, prune shade branches so light reaches the trees, and protect the pods from pests and diseases.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná nibii babaoo Too tso he he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shade lɛ koni la ashɛ tso lɛ he. ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ahe.

english: Why should I spray my farm early when I haven't seen any pests on my young seedlings yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ mra lɛ? Be mli ni minaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi yɛ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying early acts like a protective shield for tender young crops. It prevents pests from settling on your farm and multiplying before they can destroy your weak seedlings.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe. Ye obua ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akabote oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛkafɔ dani amɛfite odumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: How soon after planting my crops should I start protecting them from insects?
ga: Beni adu tsei sɛɛ Etsɛ tɛŋŋ esa akɛ mabɔi tsei ahebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: You should protect your farm within the first two weeks after planting. Young shoots are soft and sweet to insects, so protecting them immediately prevents heavy pest attacks.
ga: Esa akɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ ni okɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ. Tsobii bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ ŋɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ abu he amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa waa lɛ anaa.

english: Can insect pests destroy my whole crop field in just the first two weeks of planting?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afite midumɔ nii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ ni mikɛdu lɛ mli?

english: Yes, young crops are fragile. A sudden pest attack can wipe out a newly sprouted field in a matter of days if you do not protect the farm right from the start.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii waaa. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui trukaa lɛ baanyɛ akpata hei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ ahiɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Kɛji obuuu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ shishijee

english: How often do I need to walk through my farm to check on my seedlings after planting?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You need to keep checking your farm regularly during the first few weeks. Frequent inspections help you catch pest invasions early before the insects can spread across the entire farm.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mra. Dani kooloi bibii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why is it important for me to physically inspect my field instead of just spraying and leaving it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli moŋ fe ni makɛ tsofa ashwie nɔ kɛkɛ ni mashi amɛ pɛ?

english: Spraying alone does not guarantee complete protection. Inspecting your farm allows you to see if the spray actually worked, if rain washed it away, or if new pests have arrived.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ haaa mɔ he ajɔ lɛ kwraa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ona kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ. Nugbɔ shwie lɛ kɛtee. aloo kooloi heei yɛ Ba loo baa?

english: How will I know if the pest control I used on my farm was successful after two weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eye omanye yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ?

english: You must closely examine the leaves and stems of your crops two weeks after spraying. If you still see live insects or fresh damage on new leaves, it means pests are still present.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji ona kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lolo loo nɔ ni efite yɛ baai heei anɔ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ lolo.

english: Is it necessary to spray my crops a second time if insects are still on the farm after two weeks?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ shii enyɔ nɔ kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, if you inspect your farm after two weeks and pests are still present, you must spray again. A second treatment ensures you clear the remaining insects before they recover and ruin your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ jɛmɛ lolo. Ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ ekoŋŋ. Tsamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ ogbeɔ kooloi bibii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛhe baajɔ amɛ ni amɛfiteɔ onibii.

english: What happens if I ignore the farm after the initial spray and pests come back?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miku mihiɛ mishwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni shishijee tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If you do not monitor and re-treat the farm, surviving pests will quickly multiply and take over your farm, wasting the effort and money you put into the first spray.
ga: Kɛji onyiɛɛɛɛ sɛɛ ni okwɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni hiɛ ka lɛ baafa oya ni amɛbaaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Eji mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika ni okɛwo klɛŋklɛŋ spray lɛ mli lɛ fitemɔ.

english: Why do pests sometimes stay on my farm even after I have sprayed the young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ moŋ?

english: Some pests may hatch after the first spray or migrate from nearby fields. Checking after two weeks helps you spot these survivors so you can apply another spray to finish them off.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ekomɛi baanyɛ afɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ loo amɛfã kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona mɛi ni ehiɛ ka nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni ojie amɛ.

english: What is the biggest risk of waiting until pests full take over my farm before taking action?
ga: Mɛni ji osharai wuji ni yɔɔ mɛmɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baaye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani mafee nɔ ko lɛ mli?

english: Once pests take over, the damage to your crops is often permanent and cannot be reversed. Taking preventative action early keeps the pest population low so your crops can grow strong.
ga: Beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni efiteɔ onibii lɛ hiɔ shi daa ni anyɛɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Nifeemɔi ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa mra Ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ aba shi kɛyashɛ he ko ni baa shi. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara waa

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen. The maize plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left up to its newest top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which leaves use to make food for the roots. Lifting the vines off the ground also prevents soil diseases from attacking the leaves, resulting in larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Akɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akatutua baai lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of leaves, or by viruses they spread. As the plant loses sap unevenly, the leaves curl up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have natural partners in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. When you harvest them, that extra nitrogen stays in the ground to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, it drowns the roots and allows soil fungi and bacteria to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ ashwie shi. ni eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when the plant suffers from water stress. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from successfully pollinating, so the plant sheds them to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ lɛ kpo koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; their roots spread out shallowly near the surface. When heavy fruit bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, allowing wind to easily pull the roots out of the soft soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ fioo beni aduawai akui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwereɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ baatsii waa. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must compete with each other for limited sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, they all produce small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize under the sun before putting it into my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ migbiɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize contains hidden moisture inside the grains. Drying the cobs under the sun removes this water, which stops mould from growing and prevents insects from easily destroying the stored grain.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulu shishi lɛ, ejieɔ nu nɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii afite dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the dry season even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cool protective cover that keeps the air humid and stops soil water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i baa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves around the base of my pepper plants help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ baai ni egbi ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Dry leaves act as mulch, forming a blanket over the soil that blocks direct heat from the sun. This keeps the ground cool and traps moisture underneath so the plant roots can drink for a longer period.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Where do armyworms go after they finish eating all the green leaves on my maize farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ yaa beni amɛye baai eŋɔli fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When armyworms exhaust the food on one field, they crawl or fly to nearby wild grass or neighboring farms searching for fresh green foliage and water to stay alive.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ ye niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ Amɛfoɔ loo amɛfoɔ kɛyaa koo mli jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ loo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyatao baai eŋɔli heei kɛ nu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do whiteflies attack my tomato crop much more heavily when the weather gets hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛji tutuaa mi-tomato tsei lɛ waa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: In hot dry weather, insects seek out juicy green crop leaves to suck their sap for water. At the same time, high temperatures cause pest eggs to hatch much faster.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Kplukai taoɔ tso baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛnu nu ni jɛɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ̃ɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow next to maize, they naturally feed the soil with nutrients that maize needs to produce strong ears.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmãa toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why do my crop harvests become smaller when I plant cassava on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava heavy-feeds on specific soil nutrients over time. Planting it continuously on the same spot without letting the land rest or rotating crops empties the soil food reserve.
ga: Cassava yeɔ sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afiteɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When planted too close together, crops compete for the same sunlight, soil food, and groundwater. They spend all their energy growing upward to reach sunlight instead of developing thick stems and large fruit.
ga: Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kome. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛshɛ hulu la he, ni no najiaŋ lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops wilt much faster during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ oya kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal groundwater before your crops can reach it. Clearing weeds ensures all available moisture in the soil goes straight to your crop's roots.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the main leaves of my plantain tree yellow and die after the fruit bunch matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ baai titrii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni aduawai akui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once a plantain stalk produces its fruit, its life cycle comes to an end. It sends its remaining moisture and nutrients down into the ground to feed the young sucker shoots growing at its base.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ Ewala be lɛ eba naagbee. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ eshishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and small when the soil on my farm is hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand downwards smoothly as they absorb food and water. Hard or stony soil stops the tuber from pushing deep, resulting in stunted or misshapen yams.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi loo efiteɔ.

english: Why do some maize varieties produce much higher yields than the traditional seeds I save from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo fe blema dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ koni akpa lɛ lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specifically bred by scientists to resist local pests, tolerate dry spells, and absorb soil nutrients better, allowing them to grow stronger and produce more grain than seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi efɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right crop variety for my farm's soil and weather conditions?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei srɔtoi ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ?

english: Different varieties are developed for specific regions—some are bred for dry areas with low rainfall, while others thrive in wet soils. Agricultural extension officers can test your soil and guide you to certified seeds tailored to your local environment.
ga: Afee henɔi srɔtoi kɛha kpokpai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Aduɔ srɔtoi lɛ ekomɛi yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo yɛ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi krokomɛi Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Agricultural Extension nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ ni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni kɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ he.

english: Why does my traditional cassava take over a year to harvest while new varieties are ready much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kusum ŋmei lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani akpaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi heei lɛ baafee klalo oya kwraa lɛ?

english: Early-maturing cassava varieties are developed to focus their energy on expanding tubers quickly, reaching full size in 6 to 9 months, whereas older varieties grow roots much more slowly over 12 to 18 months.
ga: Afee ŋmei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ oya koni akɛjwɛŋmɔ ama yitso ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ nɔ. Amɛshɛɔ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni edara lɛ shwereɔ blɛoo kwraa, yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 teŋ.

english: If I plant a drought-tolerant crop variety, does that mean it doesn't need rain at all?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ, ani no tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ he ehiaaa amɛ kwraa?

english: Drought-tolerant varieties are built to survive with very little water and recover quickly after dry spells, but they still need some moisture—especially during flowering and seed formation—to produce a good yield.
ga: Atswa tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛ nu fioo pɛ, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ oya yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ. Shi ŋmɔtɔ he miihia lɛ lolo. Titri lɛ, yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔ be mli. bɔni afee ni aná nibii kpakpai

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme weather, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients like calcium. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of conserving energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ, fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean a nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the nutrient responsible for green leaf growth, and when soil runs low, the plant steals nitrogen from older leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very bushy with lots of leaves but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmɔ mli nɛkɛ lɛ? Ani oyɛ baai babaoo shi aduawai fioo pɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes tomato plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha o-tomato tso lɛ atsu ehewalɛ fɛɛ he nii yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do soybean plants make the soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ soybean tsei baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Soybeans are legumes that work with beneficial bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots, naturally enriching the soil with fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Soybeans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can participating in agricultural programs like 'Feed Ghana' help me get better crop yields?
ga: Te okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ ‘Feed Ghana’ lɛ mli ni mikɛ mihe woɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Agricultural initiatives connect farmers directly with certified high-yielding seeds, proper fertilizers, and expert advice, helping you adopt proven field practices that significantly boost your crop production.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ lɛ kɛ okwaafoi lɛ tsaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ ŋaawoo ni jɛ ŋaalɔi adɛŋ Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni ana he odaseyeli ni baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ waa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do new hybrid seed varieties require specific planting distances compared to how I usually space my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ biɔ he pɔtɛɛ ko ni aduɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto bɔ ni mifɔɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛmamɔ he lɛ he.

english: Recommended planting distances ensure each plant gets adequate sunlight, airflow, and soil space to reach its maximum yield potential without competing with neighboring crops for nutrients or spreading diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aná yibii babaoo ni akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Can mango trees really grow well in the dry Northern region of Ghana, or do they need a lot of rain?
ga: Ani mango tsei baanyɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ aloo nugbɔ babaoo he miihia amɛ?

english: Yes, mango trees actually thrive during dry periods. While young seedlings need water to get established, mature trees require a distinct dry season to trigger flowering. This makes the climate in the Northern and Middle regions of Ghana very suitable for expanding mango cultivation.
ga: Hɛɛ, mango tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa nu koni amɛdara lɛ. Esa akɛ tsei ni eda lɛ aná hulutsoo be ni mli ka shi faŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mango ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ.

english: I live in the Western Region where it rains frequently; will heavy rain affect my mango flowers?
ga: Mihiɔ anaigbɛ kpokpaa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ shii abɔ yɛ lɛ nɔ. Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaná mi mango fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Heavy rain during the flowering stage can wash away pollen or cause fungal diseases like anthracnose, which rots the flowers before fruit can set. In wetter zones, farmers need to monitor flowering carefully and manage fungal risks to secure a good yield.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe loo ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose, ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ aba. Yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ Ehe miihia ni Okwaafoi lɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ aba lɛ anɔ koni amɛná yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are more farmers across different parts of Ghana choosing to plant mangoes these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei srɔtoi yɛ Ghana ŋmɛnɛ lɛ halaa akɛ amɛbaadu mango babaoo lɛ.

english: Mango is a high-value tree crop with growing demand for both local consumption and export. Once a mango orchard is established, the trees can continue producing fruit for 30 to 40 years or more, providing long-term income with less daily labor than annual crops.
ga: Mango ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni jara wa waa. kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ fɛɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Beni ama mango tso yibii abɔɔ lɛ Tsei baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 krokomɛi loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Amɛhaa shika ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ daa gbi nitsumɔ fioo fe afi ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting a mango seedling before I harvest my first fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ odu mango lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa oklɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: If you plant a grafted mango seedling, it usually starts bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years. If you plant a seed directly without grafting, it takes much longer—about 7 to 10 years—to produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji odu mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ amɛbaabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛji odu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli ni okɛwooo mli. Ebaahe aaafee afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani ewo yibii.

english: How far apart should I space my mango seedlings when planting them in the field?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, te esa akɛ mango dumɔwui lɛ afee tɛŋŋ?

english: Mango trees grow large canopy branches, so they should be planted about 8 to 10 meters apart. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight and airflow, which prevents overcrowding and reduces the spread of diseases.
ga: Mango tso lɛ yɛ niji agboi ni shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu amɛ aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10 kɛjɛ amɛhe. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mɛi akayimɔ obɔbɔ fe nine, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the fresh young leaves on my mango tree turning reddish-brown instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mango tso nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: This is completely natural. Young mango leaves produce a reddish pigment to protect their tender tissue from direct sunlight and insect damage. As the leaves mature and harden, they will turn deep green and produce chlorophyll.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ naa nɔ kwraa. Mango baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. Kɛji baai lɛ egbɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ klorofil.

english: Will cutting back the top branches of my young mango tree hurt it, or does it help?
ga: Ani mango tso niji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha nɔ ko afite? Aloo ebaaye ebua?

english: Pruning the top branches actually helps the tree. It encourages the trunk to grow wider side branches, keeps the tree at a manageable height for harvesting, and opens the center to sunlight.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niji ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha nikpamɔ. ni agbele yɛ teŋgbɛ koni hulu la lɛ atsɔ mli

english: Do I need to water my fully grown mango trees every day during the dry season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mi mango tso ni eda lɛ nu daa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: No, mature mango trees have very deep root systems that extract water from deep underground. Regular watering is essential for young seedlings, but mature trees actually need a dry spell to encourage strong flowering.
ga: Dabi, mango tso ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ daa lɛ he miihia waa. Shi tsei lɛ edara kwraa diɛŋtsɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ehe miihia ni be ko ni mli ejɔ koni ewo fɔfɔi ni mli wa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why did my mango tree produce a huge harvest last year, but has almost no fruit this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ? Shi afi nɛɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni nɔ ko kwraa bɛ ni baajɛ mli aba?

english: This behavior is called alternate bearing. After a tree uses a huge amount of energy to produce a large crop, it often spends the following year resting and rebuilding its nutrient reserves before it can produce heavily again.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ sɛɛkuu-kɛsaramɔ. Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ be yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli dani ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ema shi ekoŋŋ dani ebaanyɛ ewo yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do so many small, newly formed mango fruits drop off the tree before maturing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango bibii ni afee ehee lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This is natural fruit drop. A mango tree produces far more flowers and tiny fruits than it can physically support. The tree sheds excess fruits naturally so it can focus its remaining water and nutrients on maturing the healthiest ones.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli tso yibii ni shwieɔ shi. Mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii. fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua Tso lɛ fɔɔ yibii ni fa fe nine yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji koni anyɛ akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ama aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava planted nearby to provide soft shade and keep the air moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli adɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long after heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Watering your plants consistently at the root level and planting them during slightly cooler windows helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni okɛdu yɛ samflɛ ni mli ejɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing tip of the maize. Applying recommended neem-based sprays or early treatments directly into the leaf funnel kills the pest before it destroys the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Neem-based sprays ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo mra be mli tsamɔ Akɛwoɔ baa lɛ mli lasu tsu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni egbe tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stunted even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for space, light, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops get all the soil food and sunlight they need to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná he ko, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck sap and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early with soapy water or appropriate sprays prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ nu ni sa loo spray ni sa nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ otsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Yam vines produce long stems that need to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight. The more sunlight the upper leaves catch, the more food the plant makes to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ ŋwɛi baa lɛ nɔ lɛ naa lɛ, Babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ niyenii lɛ, babaoo ni niyenii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit at the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with a strong bamboo or wooden fork prop prevents strong winds from blowing the tree down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. make it top heavy Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa tso lɛ shi.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my garden vegetables help them survive the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that shields the ground from hot sun. It traps moisture in the soil longer and prevents roots from getting too hot and dried out.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ adɔ fe nine ni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do the weeds on my farm grow much faster than my main crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri, ni ji ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally absorb soil nutrients and water faster than farm crops. Because they are adapted to harsh conditions, they will quickly outgrow your maize and starve it of food if you do not clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛbaatsɔ oya fe o-corn lɛ ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ kɛji otsiii amɛ mra.

english: If I leave tall weeds around my oil palm trees, will it affect how much palm fruit I harvest?
ga: Kɛji mishi jwɛi kakadaji yɛ mu tsei lɛ ahe lɛ Ani enɛ baaná mu tsei ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, heavy weed growth steals fertilizer and water away from the palm tree roots. Overgrown weeds also block sunlight from reaching the lower leaves and make it difficult for natural pollinators to reach the flowers, which reduces your fruit yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ waa lɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei shishifãi amli. Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Ni enɛ haa ewaa ahaa adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha aduawai ni owoɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves start turning yellow when my farm becomes bushy and overgrown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: When weeds grow too thick around cassava, they choke the root system and steal essential nitrogen from the soil. The lack of nutrients and sunlight causes the lower cassava leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ shwere tsɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ, amɛhaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjuɔ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it risky to change my planting schedule to a different month than I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ midumɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ kɛyaa nyɔŋ kroko nɔ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Crops rely heavily on predictable rainfall patterns and daylight hours. If you change your planting month, your crops might flower during dry periods or face severe insect invasions that ruin your young plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo be nɔ waa. Kɛji otsake nyɔŋ ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ Onibii lɛ baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli loo okɛ kooloi bibii ni baatutua bo ni fiteɔ otsei bibii lɛ akpee.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the dry hot weather lasts longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi be kakadaŋŋ fe bɔ ni efɔɔ daa lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants experience severe stress during extended hot and dry spells. To survive and conserve moisture, the plant naturally sheds its flowers so it does not waste energy trying to grow fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei naa nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ, ni egbi. Bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi ni amɛhiɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ efiteee beni abɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni akwɛ aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do smaller crops planted near big palm trees stay weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei wuji ahe lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Large palm trees cast heavy shade and have broad root networks that swallow up most of the water in the ground. Smaller food crops need direct sunlight to make their food and will stay small if they are shaded out.
ga: Palm tsei wuji haa hulutsoo waa, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni miɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Niyenii tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. ni ebaaya nɔ ahi shi bibioo kɛji akɛ awo lɛ shade.

english: Does clearing bush and weeds around my plant roots really help the crop grow better?
ga: Ajieɔ tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ Ani mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, clearing away bush frees up air circulation around the base of the crop, allows rainwater to sink directly into the roots, and prevents damp fungal diseases from breeding near the plant stem.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle he. tsei ashishitoo babaoo Ehaa nugbɔ nu boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni etsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ashishifãi lɛ ahe

english: If I clear the overgrown grass around the border of my field, will it stop pests from eating my crops?
ga: Kɛ mijie jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ Ani ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa?

english: Yes, overgrown grasses and bushes act as breeding sites and hideouts for insects like grasshoppers and caterpillars. Clearing field borders removes their shelter, forcing pests away from your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ kɛ he ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ. Husu lɛ ni abaajie lɛ baajie amɛbobaahe lɛ kɛjɛ amɛdɛŋ. ni onyɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, but it bounces back when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Shi efoɔ ehe kɛyaa sɛɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds sprout back so quickly right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds can sleep safely in dry soil for many months. The first rain acts as a wake-up call, causing hundreds of dormant weed seeds to germinate instantly before your planted crop seeds even have a chance to sprout.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni teɔ mɔ shi. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui ohai abɔ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani dumɔwui ni odu lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants curling up and turning yellow during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during dry spells to reduce surface area and cut down water loss. When they turn yellow, it means the plant is stressed from lack of water or missing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni bɛ loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and leaves above ground but very small roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience sudden water stress. Heat makes the pollen sterile, so the plant sheds the unproductive flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ haa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do some of the tiny young pods on my cocoa trees turn black and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed excess young pods—a process called cherelle wilt—if they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all the fruits on the tree.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel wilt. Kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ lɛ,.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leads to thin, weak stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants drop off after heavy continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Excessive water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without air, root systems fail to absorb nutrients, causing the plant to drop its leaves.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. haa tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops after I clear and plant my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie amɛ ni midu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can sleep in the soil for years. When you clear the land, you expose these dormant seeds to sunlight and moisture, causing them to germinate and grow faster than planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Kɛji ojie jɛmɛ dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ Enɛɛmɛi baashɛ hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and develop mold quickly inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite oya ni miifee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi-nitoo kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize spoils in storage if it is bagged before being fully dried. Moisture trapped inside the grains creates warm, damp conditions that allow mold and insects to thrive.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ mli dɔɔ, ni mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii shwereɔ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to shoot up from the soil after I sow them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if soil insects eat them before they break through the ground surface.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and drop off when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside them acts like a living umbrella, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are mature enough to stand the sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shade ni hiɛ ka. Kɛtsɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni abuɔ he lɛ nɔ Kɛyashi tso lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small holes in them with little worms hiding in the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo baa lasu tsu mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft growth inside the center of the maize leaf funnel. Spotting them early allows you to crush them by hand or apply recommended treatments before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ onine atswa amɛ loo okɛ tsofa ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big green leaves, but the tubers under the soil are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rainfall, the cassava plant spends all its energy building leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Hard, packed soil can also physically stop tubers from expanding properly.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo tsɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ baato niyenii yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ bulbs lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like boron and calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa tamɔ boron kɛ calcium ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather when water drops splash spores from the soil onto the pods. Pruning extra tree branches lets air flow in to dry out the farm and reduce infection.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ mli beni nu mli nui shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Tsoi krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Why do my tomatoes get dark, sunken rotten spots on the bottom ends while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It often happens when water levels fluctuate drastically, preventing the plant roots from drawing calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni nu lɛ mli shwereɔ waa lɛ. Etsiɔ tso shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in my field after I harvest my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Corn feeds heavily on soil nutrients, leaving the soil tired. Groundnuts and cowpeas have special microbes on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, etɔ sũ lɛ. Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds even when they look healthy and green?
