ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily be weakened by underground pests like nematodes or weevil borers that chew through the roots. Staking the mature plants with strong poles gives them physical support when heavy fruit bunches form.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. Tsei ni edara ni akɛ tsei ni wa fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baaha gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ aba beni aduawai akui wuji feɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, increasing food production for the tuber while keeping leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa niyenii ni anáa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ koni ŋmeii helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Yellowing leaf tips that move inward in a V-shape indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps the plant recover its healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves roll up to conserve water when the air gets very hot and dry. By curling, the leaves hide from direct sunlight to prevent their water from evaporating into the air.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni nu lɛ akatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Cassava drops leaves to save water and stay alive during long dry spells. The plant goes to sleep to protect its roots underground, and fresh leaves will grow back as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ wɔɔ koni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops need water before they start dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛgboi?

english: Check your crops early in the morning before the sun gets strong. If the soil is dry to the touch and the leaves look limp or dull instead of firm and bright, your crops are thirsty.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli leebi dani hulu lɛ atswa waa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kɛyashɛ he ni baa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shiŋŋ ni ekpɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when rain water stays standing on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Roots need air underground just like humans need air to breathe. When excess rain fills up all the space in the dirt, the roots drown, turn soft, and rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai koni amɛmu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo ni eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does rain water wash away my soil instead of sinking down to my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo kɛyashɛ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil forms a crust that blocks water from entering. Loosening the dirt and adding organic matter helps the soil absorb rain like a sponge so water can reach the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabote mli. Muji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ sponji bɔni afee ni nu lɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does putting dried grass around the base of my crops keep them healthy in heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It shades the dirt from the burning sun, stops water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the root area cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ muji kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Yellow bottom leaves mean the plant lacks water or food nutrients. The crop moves its remaining strength to the young top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the heat becomes too intense or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my young seedlings stretch out tall and weak instead of growing thick stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tsei ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch out when they do not get enough direct sunlight. The plant stretches toward the light to catch energy, making its stem long, thin, and easily broken by rain.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa la lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ mli tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, eyɛ mlɛo ni efoɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: What happens to my seeds if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain can trigger seeds to sprout, but if hot weather returns immediately after, the soft young roots will dry up and die. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ Young shishifãi lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it important for me to walk around my farm regularly instead of just leaving the crops to grow on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ manyiɛ? ŋmɔ mli daa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ akwɛ̃

english: Walking through your farm regularly allows you to notice early signs of pest attacks, crop diseases, or soil dryness before they spread and destroy your whole harvest.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ ni ofeɔ daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mra. Dani ebaagbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small roots that burn easily under intense heat; they need shade from taller plants like plantains to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetable crops curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot periods to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant reduce water loss and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Why does my farmland soil turn hard and crack when rain stops for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Soil hardens and cracks when it lacks organic material like dried leaves or compost, which normally helps the ground retain moisture and stay soft during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehiɔ shi blɛoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops turn pale and weak when rainwater sits on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns crop roots by blocking air, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing the essential nutrients needed to keep leaves green.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Will my maize yield more food if I plant many seeds very close together in one place?
ga: Ani mi-ŋma lɛ baawo niyenii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo? Dumɔwui bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ he kome

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii baa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans together with my main grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which enriches the land and helps nearby crops like maize grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any fruits form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Flower dropping is usually caused by environmental stress such as extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or tiny sap-sucking insects disturbing the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ mli haomɔ, tamɔ shwane dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni gbaa tso lɛ naa lɛ

english: Why are my cassava roots staying small even though the leaves above ground look large and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to waste energy growing leaves and branches instead of sending starch down to build thick root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaa kɛ amɛniji baa. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ starch kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee bulb nɛ sisi mi mi wa.

english: Yam rot happens when water pools around the tubers in heavy or poorly drained soil, allowing fungal infections to develop in the root zone.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni egbo lɛ baa kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Tubers ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ waa loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their root systems are still weak and leaves burn easily. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young plants from drying out until they are mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when many shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plant for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the mother plant to direct all its energy into producing a large, healthy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi, loo tsei lɛ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ, eshiɔ tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni enɛ haa tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tso agbo ni mli wa mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, a vital nutrient for leafy growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, showing that your soil needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tsei yeɔ baa momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in my young corn leaves with powdery dirt inside the center stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji ni tamɔ powder yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing center of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves. Early detection and applying recommended treatments into the funnel are necessary to stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ he miihia waa koni akɛkpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when there is a lot of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil because standing water cuts off oxygen to the roots, encouraging fungal infections and decay. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots, preventing rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa

english: Why do I need to guide and stake my yam vines on tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔɔ gbɛ ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ama tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant needs to feed growing tubers underground. Keeping vines off the wet ground also protects leaves from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo. Ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture is irregular. Without steady water and moderate heat, the plant experiences stress and sheds its flowers to save energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji nu ni tamɔ ekome kɛ dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ bɛ lɛ Tsei naa haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee nibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on leaf sap, or by a virus spread by these insects. Managing these sucking pests early prevents leaf distortion and keeps the plant growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Tsa kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ mra. Ebaatsi baai lɛ ashishi ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my crop yield drop if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that target that crop to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients and breaks insect cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛto amɛhe shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaku ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: How do crops like cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for other plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Legumes have beneficial bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When legume plants die and rot, they leave this natural nitrogen behind, enriching the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmeii gboi ni amɛgboi lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants turn yellow while the rest of the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source for plants. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in the season keeps the leaves green so they can make enough food for big, healthy corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii jɛɛhe titri kɛha tsei Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ awo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa toi wuji ni wa.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani pepper lɛ kwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme afternoon heat or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering and mulching helps flowers stay on the plant to form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba amɛnaa yɛ shwane mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli oya tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up before the fruit bunch has even finished growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani aduawai akui lɛ egbe naa lɛ?

english: Early yellowing of plantain leaves is often caused by leaf diseases or small root worms that block water from reaching the top. Clearing weeds, applying manure around the base, and planting disease-free suckers help keep the leaves green long enough to feed the growing bunch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa hela loo shishifã mli ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ plantain baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ baa. ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmeii ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua jwɛi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers split open or grow into weird crooked shapes underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miijara loo amɛmiida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers split or grow crooked when they hit hard, tightly packed soil or experience sudden heavy rain after a long dry season. Building deep, soft mounds or ridges gives the tubers room to expand smoothly without cracking.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbala loo amɛbaabɔle kɛji akɛ amɛmi shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa tuber he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ ni etseee.

english: Why do some of the cassava roots from my farm taste sweet while others turn out bitter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots produce bitter natural chemicals when the plant experiences heavy drought or pest stress during its growth. Keeping the soil covered with organic matter to retain moisture helps keep the roots mild and sweet.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe haomɔ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ehi shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ oblahii kɛ oblayei ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in dark, damp shade under thick branches. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm canopy, preventing the fungus from ruining your harvest.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛitsu lɛ gĩɔ. Tsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and rot so quickly before I can transport them to Techiman market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani akɛyaa Techiman Jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly during transport if harvested fully red or crushed under heavy weight in deep wooden crates. Picking them at the 'breaker stage' when they just start turning pink allows them to ripen safely on the journey without getting bruised.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ ni amɛfee tsuru kwraa loo akɛ muji ni tsii shwie nɔ yɛ tsei adekai ni mli kwɔ amli. Kɛji akɛ amɛhi 'breaker stage' lɛ mli beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ pinki lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛshwere shweshweeshwe yɛ gbɛfaa lɛ mli ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my groundnuts so the pods are full?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii koni ŋmeii lɛ ayi obɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the inside of the pod shell turns dark brown with distinct veins and the plant leaves start turning yellow. Harvesting too early leaves you with small shriveled nuts, while harvesting too late leaves pods behind in the dry soil.
ga: Peanuts lɛ efee klalo kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ fãji ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. ni tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ ŋmeii bibii ni egbo lɛ ahi ohe. Akɛni kpamɔ lɛ eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ hewɔ lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why do my garden eggs get dark, soft spots on their skin right after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ ahewolo nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mibua amɛnaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Dark spots on freshly picked garden eggs happen when the fruits suffer heat burns or bruising from being harvested during the hot afternoon sun. Picking early in the morning and keeping the produce shaded in cool baskets prevents skin damage.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni ajie ehee lɛ anɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ Ebaa kɛji ashã aduawai loo ŋmeii kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni oookpa leebi ni okɛto tsɛnsii ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni hewolo lɛ akafite.

english: Why do buyers in large urban supermarkets reject my fresh vegetables even when they are big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni hɔɔ nii yɛ maŋtiasei wuji amli shwapoi wuji amli lɛ kpooɔ mi-aduawai heei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdara moŋ?

english: Supermarkets and premium buyers look for clean produce that is uniform in size, free from soil or pest marks, and neatly handled. Sorting your harvested crops by size and gently cleaning off dirt makes your produce look attractive enough to command higher prices.
ga: Shwapoi wuji kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni jara wa waa lɛ taoɔ nibii ni he tse ni amɛdalɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Ebɛ sũ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ okɛ onikpamɔ lɛ to bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ naa, ni otsumɔ muji lɛ he blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha jara aya hiɛ.

english: What is the difference between certified seeds and the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase kɛ dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Saved seeds often lose their strength and yield potential over time. Certified seeds are specially tested and produced under strict supervision to ensure high yields, good germination, and resistance to common pests and diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be ni sa mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni afeɔ yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi koni ana akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: I keep hearing officers talk about 'foundation seeds'. What does that mean for a local farmer like me?
ga: Mi nu ni onukpai lɛ miiwie Always ‘seed foundation’ he, mɛni ji nɔ ni no tsɔɔ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi tamɔ mi?

english: Foundation seeds are pure seeds grown directly by agricultural research institutions. They are not usually sold directly to farmers; instead, seed companies plant foundation seeds to produce the certified seeds that you buy in the market.
ga: Primer dumɔwui ji dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei duɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔɔ amɛ ahaaa okwaafoi tɛ̃ɛ. Mohu ɔ, dumɔwu he ní tsumi he ɔmɛ duɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ a he hia wawɛɛ konɛ a kɛ pee dumɔwuhi nɛ a wo he blɔ nya nɛ o heɔ ngɛ jua a nɔ ɔ.

english: Why do hybrid seeds produce a huge harvest the first year, but give very small yields if I save and replant those seeds next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji mikɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Hybrid seeds get their strength from a special cross between two distinct parent plants. This extra strength only lasts for one generation, so planting seeds saved from a hybrid crop causes the plants to lose vigor and yield far less.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ naa amɛhewalɛ kɛtsɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni ji fɔlɔi lɛ ateŋ gbeekpamɔ krɛdɛɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shi yinɔ kome pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni jara waaa ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahe ajɔ amɛ ni amɛwo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: How can I be sure I am buying genuine certified seed and not fake or low-quality seed at the shop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miheɔ dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ, ni awo he odaseyeli, shi jeee amalei loo dumɔwui ni ehiii kwraa kɛjɛɔ shwapo ko mli?

english: Genuine certified seeds come in sealed bags bearing an official government certification tag or scratch code. Look for tags from the seed inspection authority that clearly state the crop variety, purity level, and expiration date.
ga: Dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni ana he odaseyeli baa yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa ni yɔɔ maŋ nɔyeli odaseyeli okadi loo kood ni akɛfoɔ mli. Taomɔ kadimɔi kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔ nitsumɔhei ni tsɔɔ tso henɔi lɛ. Hetsemɔ he kɛ be ni ebaagbe naa lɛ mli ka shi faŋŋ

english: Why do my crops grow unevenly when I use seeds bought from the local market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ maŋ lɛ jara nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Market seeds are usually a random mix of different crop varieties, ages, and health conditions. Certified seeds are uniform, meaning every plant sprouts at the same time and grows at the exact same speed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ fɔɔ tsei srɔtoi, afii, kɛ hewalɛ shihilɛi. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yaa nɔ daa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: How can I test if the maize seeds I have will actually sprout before I go through the stress of planting my whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miyɔɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani mikɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ mli baa lɛ akpee?

english: You can do a quick germination test by placing 10 seeds on a moist cloth inside a container. Keep it damp for 4 to 5 days; if at least 8 or 9 seeds grow strong sprouts, your seed batch is very good for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛbaawo mama ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ha amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ gbii 4 kɛyashi 5; Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ, dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ 8 loo 9 kwɛ̃ lɛ, odumɔwui akuu lɛ hi kɛha shweremɔ.

english: Why do some certified seeds I buy come coated in a bright pink or blue powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ powda ni mli tse loo bluu ni mli tse woɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ ni awo he odase lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: That bright color is a safe chemical treatment applied to protect the young seeds in the soil from fungal decay, diseases, and hungry insects right after you plant them.
ga: Sui ni kpɛɔ lɛ ji tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbuɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ, helai kɛ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe kɛji odu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some new crop varieties stay green during a dry spell while my traditional crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mishishijee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Newer improved seed varieties are bred specifically for drought tolerance, meaning they develop deeper roots to draw underground water or have leaves that reduce water loss during hot dry days.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbala shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Aloo ná baai ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: How should I store my leftover planting seeds so they don't rot or get eaten by insects before the next rains?
ga: Te esa akɛ ato dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ aha tɛŋŋ koni amɛkafite loo kooloi akaye amɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Store your clean, fully dried seeds in airtight containers or sealed bags in a cool, dry room off the floor to keep out moisture, heat, and pests like seed weevils.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni egbi kwraa lɛ ato tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni abu he kɛjɛ hulutsoo, dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning light yellow even though I planted good seed on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ midu dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ be naa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the young plant is lacking nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are waterlogged from heavy rains and cannot breathe properly to feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ eyi nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ pɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their tender leaves burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees or companion crops like plantains act as natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the young cocoa can survive and establish strong roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi ni ekwɛ̃ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen. When there is not enough nitrogen food in the soil, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the young growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge, leafy stems above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or raw manure, cassava plants focus all their energy on growing lush leaves and stems. To get thick underground tubers, the plant needs balanced nutrients with more potassium, which tells the plant to store food underground instead of making leaves.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ babaoo lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe nii. Bɔni afee ni aná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni ja babaoo kɛ potassium babaoo. Enɛ kɛɛ tso lɛ akɛ ekɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe ni eeefee baai.

english: Why does my maize grow much stronger when I plant it on land where I harvested groundnuts last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the groundnut plant dies, this trapped nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop of maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli bibii bibii. Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ gbo lɛ, Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes for them to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves are like solar panels that need maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so all leaves catch the sun easily, which sends energy down to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii, ni ehe hiaa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he mlɛo. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee yitso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cabbage plants spread their leaves wide open instead of forming tight, round heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee yitsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages form tight heads only when they have cool weather and steady moisture. If the weather gets too hot or water is irregular, the plant gets confused and grows open leaves instead of wrapping them tightly into a ball.
ga: Kaabaji baahi shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ hu yaa nɔ daa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa lɛ Tso lɛ baafutu ni ebaana baai ni agbele yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaawo mli bɔɔlu.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects. The damaged leaf tissue shrinks and twists as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Baai lɛ ahe fãji ni efite lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ mli beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rainstorms even when they have fruit on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ani nakai feemɔ tsuɔ nii lolo?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily rot or get damaged by root pests like nematodes and stem borers. Without strong, healthy roots anchored deep in the moist soil, the plant cannot support the heavy weight of its bunch during strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbo oya loo shishifãi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes kɛ stem borers lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ bɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into fruits when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from being fertilized. When temperatures get too high, the tomato plant drops its flowers to save water and energy until cooler weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting when I plant them in dry land right before a light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ sũ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ fioo ko nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a steady supply of moisture to sprout completely. A light rain gives just enough water to start the seed swelling, but if dry heat follows immediately, the weak young sprout dries out and rots underground before it can reach the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ la ni mli egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small root systems that lose moisture quickly in strong heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them shields the tender cocoa trees until they grow tough enough to withstand full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii, ni kɛ́ edɔ waa lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ masɛi lɛ ni aduɔ Ebuɔ cacao tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Applying well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any pepper fruits during hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ewoɔ pepper yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When heat is too high and water is short, plants experience stress and shed their flowers to preserve water and keep themselves alive. Regular watering during hot spells helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Tsei naa haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close together so I can fit more onto my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ mikɛ babaoo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build thick stems and large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa baa.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into high mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa sũ naa yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ dani miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yams grow deep tubers that need soft, loose earth to expand without obstruction. Mounding also raises the plant roots above heavy rainfall so the tubers do not rot in waterlogged soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ, ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi enaa. Shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hu haa tsei shishifãi yaa hiɛ fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fiteee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes up heavy nutrients from the soil, leaving it weak. Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground through their roots, naturally restoring fertility for your next crops.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha egbɔjɔ Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does clearing weeds early in the season make my crops yield so much more food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the moisture, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your plants. Removing them early gives your crops full access to food when they need it most.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei lɛ. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii kwraa yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are small green worms eating holes through the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack the tender growing tips of corn plants. Catching them early and spraying recommended plant extracts or approved treatments into the center of the plant saves the crop from destruction.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered when soil water goes from very wet to very dry. Keeping the soil moist continuously allows roots to absorb calcium smoothly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni edɔ waa kɛtee nɔ ni egbi waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. When the soil lacks nitrogen or gets too waterlogged, the leaves lose their green color and growth slows down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Baai lɛ baafite amɛ su eŋɔli ni amɛdalɛ baafee blɛoo.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and cannot drain properly. Heavy clay soils or low spots retain water during heavy rains, causing fungal diseases that turn the roots soft and rotten.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni enyɛɛɛ etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔji ni mli wa loo hei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ekɛ fungal hela ko baa ni haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to capture sunlight, which the plant uses to make food. When the leaves get plenty of sun off the ground, the plant can grow much bigger yam tubers below.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa eniyenii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara kwraa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ hu.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak, thin stalks that produce tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni feɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I sow my farm seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain can be a false start followed by weeks of dry weather. If seeds sprout and the rain stops, the dry soil will scorch and kill the delicate young seedlings.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji otsii babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbe tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees from my farm clear to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. Larger trees act as a protective canopy, providing shade and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa plants establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ tswaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry stress. Without adequate water during high heat, the plant stops fruit production to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ he. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the surface. If insects damage the underground stem or if the soil is too soft, the heavy top weight easily pulls the roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji kooloi bibii fite shikpɔŋ shishi tsei loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Nɔ ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and get tight and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding under the leaves. Their feeding damages the leaf structure and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwa tsei amli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh local conditions. They take up nutrients and water much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If my farmland is always wet and muddy like a swamp, will digging small channels to clear the water help my crops grow better?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ muji be fɛɛ be tamɔ ŋshɔkpɔ bibioo ko ni mifoɔ Ani nu ni mijieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, digging simple drainage paths allows excess trapped water to flow away. This clears stagnant water so the soil can breathe, preventing crop roots from drowning and rotting.
ga: Hɛɛ, ewaaa akɛ oootsa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli. Ehaa nu ni etsi ehe fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ baajie nu ni ekã shi lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ amu. Etsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote nu mli ni amɛkafite.

english: If I successfully divert standing water off my flooded land, how soon can I start planting my crops?
ga: Kɛji miye omanye yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ni mikɛbaajɛ hei ni nu afua lɛ ebɔle he lɛ mli. Te manyɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ mra tɛŋŋ?

english: Once the water flows away, you should wait a few weeks for the muddy ground to dry out slightly until it is firm and moist. This lets oxygen return to the soil so seeds can germinate without rotting.
ga: Beni nu lɛ hoɔ lɛ Esa akɛ omɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni sũ lɛ agbi fioo kɛyashi ebaafee shiŋŋ ni edɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbooo.

english: Will clearing standing water off my swampy farm wash away all the rich nutrients in the soil?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ shi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-swamp ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baajie niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Controlled drainage mainly removes the excess water sitting on top. As long as the water drains out slowly through ditches without washing away your topsoil, most of the rich nutrients will stay in the earth for your crops.
ga: Nɔ titri ni he hiaa ji akɛ, nu ni hoɔ ni akudɔɔ lɛ jieɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Shii abɔ ni nu lɛ baaho kɛje kpo blɛoo lɛ Otsɔ nubu lɛ mli ni okɛ ŋwɛi sũ lɛ afɔɔɔ. Niyenii nibii ni jara wa lɛ ateŋ babaoo baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it important to keep the water channels on my farm clear of rubbish and weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni jwɛi kɛ jwɛi akafee nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds and dirt block the flow of water, causing it to spill back onto your farm during heavy rains. Keeping channels clean ensures surplus water leaves the field quickly before it can harm your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ muji tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa nu lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔji lɛ amli tse lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya dani eyeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and decay whenever heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu taraa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. When standing water covers the soil for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, suffocating the plant and causing leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why does swamp rice grow so well in muddy places where my maize plants usually die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni muji yɔɔ ni mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ fɔɔ gboi yɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have natural air tubes inside their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots under water, whereas maize roots lack this feature and quickly drown in waterlogged mud.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ bɛ enɛɛmɛi eko ni amɛboteɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: Can I plant tomatoes or pepper directly on land that stays soggy and wet throughout the year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers prefer well-drained soil and easily develop root rot and fungal diseases in swampy land. You must drain the water or construct high raised beds before planting them there.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ekɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa ŋmɔji amli oya. Esa akɛ ojie nu lɛ loo ofee saatso ni awo nɔ dani okɛdu yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees fail to survive on land that collects standing water during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei nyɛŋ ahi shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ toɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, airy soil to grow strong taproots. Land that holds standing water suffocates cocoa roots and encourages deadly black pod and root rot diseases.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu ekã shi lɛ baaha kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ekanyaa black pod hela kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela lɛ

english: Why do farmers build high soil mounds when planting cassava or yam in low-lying, wet areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi maa gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ́ amɛmiidu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Building raised mounds lifts the seeds and tubers above the excess water level, keeping the growing roots dry and safe from rotting in soggy ground.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaye abua ni awo dumɔwui kɛ bulb lɛ nɔ kɛho nu ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ. Ha shishifãi ni miida lɛ agbi ni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why does muddy ground become extremely hard like a rock after the sun dries it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ewo muji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ tɛsaa kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil expands when wet into mud, but as the hot sun bakes it, the soil particles pack tightly together and harden, making it difficult for new crop roots to spread unless the soil is properly tilled.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛji edɔ, ni etsɔɔ muji. Shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii lɛ baabua amɛhe naa ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi heei akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã, ja atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eda waa.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, meaning they have a special ability to take nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny bumps on their roots. When the plant dies after harvest, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before making any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani ewo pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by sudden heat, lack of water, or missing soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and adding compost gives the plant the strength it needs to hold onto its flowers until they turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni baa trukaa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi amɛbaawo yibii.

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close, their branches overlap and block sunlight, while their roots fight over the same water and food in the ground. Giving each tree proper space ensures it gets enough light and soil nutrients to yield a full crop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Niji lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: The first rain after a long dry spell can be deceiving because the soil underneath is still dry and very hot. If a dry week follows that first rain, your seeds will sprout and quickly dry up in the soil.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi waa lolo ni edɔ. Kɛji otsi ni mli egbi ba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for building big tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the wet ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and preventing fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs agboi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ baai lɛ awo hulu la mli ni otsi fungal rot naa.

english: How can I tell when cassava tubers are mature and ready to dig up without unearthing the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ ni akumɔɔɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava shows it is ready when the lower leaves on the main stem turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stalk, and the soil around the base begins to crack as the tubers swell beneath.
ga: Akɛɛ ŋmei efee klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ pɛ eshwɛ, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ daa yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and sunken before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually brought on by irregular watering. Water your plants regularly so the roots can continuously take up calcium from the soil.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ha tso lɛ nu daa koni shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ aŋɔ calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and loose instead of forming tight, hard balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to harden if the soil lacks sufficient water or if the weather is too hot during head formation. Ensuring consistent moisture and planting in cool, well-drained soil helps the leaves fold tightly together.
ga: Kaaba yitsei lɛ ewaŋ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni yitsei lɛ toɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ oha ehiɛ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which maize needs in large amounts to build green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure early in the plant's growth helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli. Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ebaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun and need shade to survive. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves, acting like living umbrellas that protect young cocoa seedlings from harsh heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, leaving a bare stem with thick roots underground. You can gently dig near the base of one plant to check if the roots have reached a good size before harvesting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ Ashiɔ tso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo atsa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso kome shishi koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ dalɛ sa dani okpa.

english: This damage is commonly caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf whorl during the cooler parts of the day. Catching them early and applying organic neem spray or recommended pesticides prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem spray loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when watering is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil causing lush foliage at the expense of fruit. Consistent morning watering and balanced nutrients help the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛji akɛ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nu daa leebi kɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Is it better for my soil if I burn the cleared bush or let it rot on the field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni atsuu he lɛ loo maha egbo yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: While burning clears the field fast, it kills valuable soil microbes and destroys organic material. Leaving cleared plant matter to rot—or mulching—rebuilds organic matter, improves soil moisture retention, and keeps the soil fertile for future seasons.
ga: yɛ be mli ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ jieɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ oya. Shi egbeɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni jara wa lɛ hu, ni efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni ajie amɛhe lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi—loo amɛfee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ—ebaatswa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ama shi ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Should I water my vegetable crops in the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because cool soil allows roots to take up moisture before heat causes high evaporation. Afternoon watering can shock hot plants and wastes water as steam in the heat.
ga: Nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu dani hulutsoo lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhe afee shoo ni eha nu lɛ afite tamɔ lasu ni mli edɔ waa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to manufacture food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, preventing leaf rot and ensuring maximum leaf area reaches the light.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ekwɛɔ koni baa lɛ he ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ aná la.

english: Too many side shoots compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one main stem and one or two young shoots ensures high yields of large plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ sɛɛ tsei babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ yibii titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ yibii bibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha aná plantains wuji babaoo.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help my soil produce better maize in the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the crop finishes growing and decays, it releases natural nitrogen into the soil, which feeds the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Beni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my okra plants turning white and silvery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi gumbo lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ futafuta kɛ shika tsuru lɛ?

english: Very small insects like whiteflies or thrips suck the juices from the underside of okra leaves. This sap-sucking creates pale, white, or silvery patches that ruin the leaves and weaken the whole plant.
ga: Kplukai bibii waa tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ nuɔ okra baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ. Nɛkɛ nu nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, yɛŋ, loo shika tsuru ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What causes my fresh okra pods to look dull, spotted, and white instead of smooth green?
ga: Mɛni haa mi okra ŋmɔji heei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛŋ moŋ fe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Tiny pests like mealybugs or spider mites feed on the skin of young okra pods. Their feeding leaves behind scar tissue and powdery residues, making the pods look unsightly and reducing their market value.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo ŋmeii yeɔ okra ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahewolo nɔ. Niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ shĩɔ fãji kɛ jwɛi. Enɛ haa pods lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa, ni ehaa jara ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my crop look very healthy early in the season, but later on small insects suddenly destroy it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi sɛɛ mli lɛ, kooloi bibii kpata lɛ hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Pest populations build up gradually over time. When your plants start flowering and fruiting, they produce tender growth rich in nutrients, which attracts larger swarms of insects later in the growing cycle.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ baaya hiɛ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli Beni otsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ shishi lɛ Amɛdaraa blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi akui wuji kɛbaa sɛɛ mli yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Can the tiny white insects attacking my okra move to destroy my pepper and tomato plants as well?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni tutuaa mi okra lɛ baanyɛ afã koni amɛfite mi pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, many small sucking insects like whiteflies feed on several types of vegetables. If you do not control them on your okra, they can easily spread to your peppers and tomatoes.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ yeɔ aduawai srɔtoi babaoo. Kɛji onyɛɛɛ okudɔ otsitsi lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato mli oya.

english: How can I safely get rid of tiny insects that are damaging my vegetables?
ga: Majie kooloi bibii kɛjɛ jɛmɛ. Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔfite aduawai ahiɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: You can use approved pest control methods such as neem seed oil solutions or recommended insecticides. Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening hits the pests directly when they are active without burning the plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ tswaa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ akɛwo nɔ ni ashãaa tso lɛ.

english: How should I test a new pest control method on my farm before using it on all my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka gbɛ hee ko ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ amli?

english: Choose a small portion or just a couple of plant rows to test the new method first. Monitor those plants for a few days to make sure the pests are controlled and the crop remains healthy before applying it to your entire field.
ga: Halamɔ fã bibioo ko loo tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ni okɛka gbɛ hee ko okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kwɛmɔ nakai tsei lɛ anɔ gbii fioo komɛi koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo dani okɛwo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is one single chemical spray enough to clear all insect problems on my farm?
ga: Ani tsofa kome ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baajie kooloi bibii ahe naagbai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛya?

english: No, different insects react to different treatments. Sap-sucking insects like whiteflies need specific treatments that differ from those used for chewing caterpillars, so you may need different solutions for different pests.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ tsofafeemɔi ahe. Kplukai ni nuɔ tamɔ whiteflies lɛ biɔ nifeemɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ nɔ ni akɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ tsofa sɔrɔto atsu nii kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko.

english: How can I tell if damage on my vegetable leaves is caused by insects or by a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo helai kɛ nɔ ni kɛ mi-vegetable baai lɛ efite lɛ baa?

english: Insects usually leave physical signs such as tiny bugs under the leaves, sticky liquid, or webbing. Diseases typically cause spreading spots, rotting, or wilting without visible insects present.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ kooloi bibii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi, nu ni shwieɔ shi, loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa lɛ bɛ mli baa.

english: Will vegetables damaged by small insects still be good to harvest and sell at the market?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akpa aduawai ni kooloi bibii efite lɛ lolo ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: While damaged vegetables might still be edible, buyers at the market prefer clean, bright produce. Insect marks make your crops look bad, which forces you to sell them at a much lower price or risk not selling them at all.
ga: Abaanyɛ aye aduawai ni efite po lolo. Shi mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ miitao aduawai ni he tse ni mli tse. Kplukai ahe okadii haa onibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii. Enɛ nyɛɔ onɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi kwraa nɔ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, okɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli ni okɛ ohe wooo mli kwraa.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and turn pale faster during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot and dry weather causes plants to lose moisture rapidly while encouraging pests like spider mites to multiply quickly. The combination of heat stress and insect feeding turns leaves pale, dry, and brittle.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu hewalɛ koni amɛshwere oya. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ kooloi aniyenii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbiɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are my young crop seedlings wilting and dying when the afternoon sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso shwane mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young sprouts are very tender and sensitive to harsh heat. Creating shade over them shields their delicate leaves from direct sunlight so they stay cool and healthy while establishing their roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ afee hulutsoo yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaabu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛhe jɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛmaa shishifãi hu.

english: Is it necessary to cover tender sprouts as soon as they emerge from the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni aha dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛji amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: Yes, newly sprouted crops are extremely delicate. Shading them as soon as they shoot up prevents the harsh sun from scorching them before they have a chance to grow strong.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ waaa kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ hulu la ni naa wa wo amɛmli beni amɛtswa amɛhe pɛ kɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekashã amɛ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Do young crop leaves actually get burned by too much sunlight?
ga: Ani hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, intense direct sunlight can scorch tender young leaves, causing them to dry up and die because they cannot handle extreme heat without protection.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii. Enɛ haa baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa kɛji abuuu amɛhe.

english: Why do my crops need shade when they are young, but can handle full sun when they grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiaa hulutsoo be mli ni amɛji bibii lɛ? Shi ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ́ eda.

english: When crops are young, their tissues are soft and delicate. As they mature, their stems and leaves grow tougher and their root systems expand, allowing them to absorb more water and handle direct heat.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ, fãji lɛ baafee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baawa. ni shishifã lɛ baagbɛ eshwa Enɛ haa eŋɔɔ nu babaoo ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out and crack so quickly during hot sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight beats down on uncovered soil and causes water to evaporate rapidly. Blocking direct sun with shade keeps the soil cool and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ahako nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya Hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛ hulutsoo be tsiɔ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Does strong, direct sunlight harm bare soil when no crops are covering it?
ga: Ani hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ awui beni tso ko bɛ ni baaha nɔ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, direct sun bakes bare soil, stripping away moisture and destroying essential nutrients, which makes it harder for seeds to germinate successfully.
