ga: No ji anɔkwale, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: How does creating shade over my farm help me save water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shading baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ nu akafite?

english: Shade shields both the crops and the ground underneath from extreme heat, reducing the rate at which soil water evaporates and helping plants stay hydrated longer.
ga: Shade buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ fɛɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Can I still successfully grow sensitive crops during hot periods when the sun is very strong?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lolo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ?

english: Yes, you can grow sun-sensitive crops even during hot weather if you build shade over them. This creates a safe environment that allows crops to thrive where they otherwise would not survive.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ po. Kɛji ofee hulutsoo yɛ nakai tsei lɛ anɔ Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ yɛ he ni tsei nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do some farmers plant tall leafy plants next to smaller delicate crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji yɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tall, leafy plants act as living umbrellas, providing natural shade that shelters smaller, sensitive crops and the surrounding soil from intense afternoon sun.
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni baai kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: How can I protect my fresh crop sprouts from direct sun without buying expensive shade cloth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mitso ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni miheee atade ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo be mli?

english: You can build simple shade shelters using local materials like wooden sticks, palm fronds, or dried grass woven together to block direct sunlight from reaching tender seedlings.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii tamɔ tsei, ŋmei tsei loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ afee hulutsoo hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni okɛtsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekashɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a living umbrella that shields the cocoa leaves and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa seeds fail to sprout when I plant them directly into my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa seeds lose their ability to germinate very quickly if exposed to direct sun and drying soil. Sprouting them first in a shaded nursery using soil-filled nursery bags ensures they stay moist and protected until they grow strong enough to be transplanted.
ga: Kookoo yibii heei lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei akwɛmɔ kotoku ni sũ eyi mli obɔ lɛ je shishi mra yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsake amɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crop turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed new green growth at the top, showing that manure or nitrogen fertilizer is needed.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ ahe hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋmeii heei ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy leaves but giving me tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Soil with too much nitrogen pushes the cassava plant to spend all its energy building stems and leaves instead of storing energy in the tubers. Adding wood ash or potassium-rich organic matter encourages tuber expansion.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ ato oyitsoŋ lɛ, tso mli sũ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni potassium yɔɔ mli ni okɛbaafata he lɛ baaha tuber lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or excessive leaf-boosting fertilizer. Keeping water levels consistent helps the flowers stay on the stem and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ babaoo Nu ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out thin and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ agboi ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, rock-free soil to push downward and expand. Hard or compacted soil blocks root expansion, forcing the tuber to bend and grow thin as it fights hard earth.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ baatsi shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ naa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ mlɛo beni ekɛ sũ ni wa miiwu lɛ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa tomatoi lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi?

english: Dark spots at the base of tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to uneven soil moisture. Regular watering helps the roots absorb essential nutrients steadily.
ga: He ni yɔɔ diŋ yɛ tomato shishi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling after just two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miifee diŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot quickly after harvest because cuts and bruises expose the flesh to air, triggering rapid chemical breakdown. Storing unwashed roots in moist sawdust or processing them quickly into gari delays spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fãji ni afolɔ kɛ fãji ni atswaa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ loo lɛ mli. Ehaa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ oya Kɛ́ akɛ shishifãi ni ahooo lɛ to ŋmei ni mli efɔ mli loo afee amɛ oya ni afee amɛ gari lɛ, ebaaha amɛfitemɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Cowpeas have natural root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, acting as a free fertilizer for nitrogen-hungry maize while spreading across the ground to stop weeds.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi ekome kɛhaa ŋmãa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa.

english: Why are tiny insects eating holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I naturally stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Soft cabbage leaves attract pests like caterpillars and flea beetles. Spraying a simple mixture of crushed neem leaves and water coats the leaves in a natural bitter taste that repels feeding pests without damaging the crop.
ga: Kaabeji baai bibii lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Neem baai ni atswa lɛ ni akɛ nu futuɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it always necessary for me to use a tractor to clear and plow my land before planting crops in Ghana?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ trakta atsu nii be fɛɛ be kɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni matsu nii dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana?

english: While tractors save time on large farms, they are not always required. For smaller plots or fragile soils, clearing by hand or minimal tillage can actually protect the topsoil from being washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ traktɔi haa be baa shi yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli moŋ, Shi jeee be fɛɛ be ehe hiaa. Kɛha shikpɔji bibii loo shikpɔji ni waaa lɛ Nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fioo lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naa koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil, leading to thin stalks and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa bibioo ko.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad, leafy shade and keep the soil moist, helping tender cocoa seedlings survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo, baai ni mli kwɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui ni mli tse lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the soil deeply two or three times consistently, rather than planting right after the first rain shower when the soil can quickly dry up again.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe ebɔ he. Mohu ɔ, duɔ ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ ɔ se amlɔ nɔuu benɛ zugba a ngɛ gbie oya ekohu ɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plants lack nitrogen fertilizer or that excess water around the roots is preventing the crop from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaye niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly at the base of my pepper plants' stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem burns the plant tissue. Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away so the roots can safely reach out and absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ fãji lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetables stay stunted even though I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for growth. Crops need nutrients from organic manure or fertilizer, and soil that is soft enough for roots to spread out properly.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha dalɛ. Tsei he miihia niyenii ni jɛɔ humus loo humus mli. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu yɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are worms eating the center leaves of my corn plants during the growing period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the central leaves of young corn to feed on tender foliage before the plant matures.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji fallworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ dani tsei lɛ adara.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and drop their leaves suddenly during the afternoon heat even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛbaai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in damp soil is usually caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that block the internal tubes of the plant, stopping water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli loo bacteria mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa trukaa yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baa. ni tsiɔ tsei amli paipii lɛ anaa Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava or maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ he?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the tall trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Taller trees or shade crops like plantains provide living shelter that protects young cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist while the tree establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains haa shĩa ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra unwanted branches from my cocoa trees if they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni misumɔɔɔ kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded branches so air and sunlight can reach the center of the tree. This stops moisture from staying trapped, which reduces fungal diseases and helps the tree direct its energy into growing larger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni mli ewo wu lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekabote mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni daraa lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or waterlogs the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant finishes growing and decays in the field, it leaves behind naturally rich soil that feeds whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔji amli Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain, but avoid putting it down right before a heavy downpour. It is best applied right after weeding so your crops consume the nutrients instead of weeds.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Esa akɛ akɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie jwɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe jwɛi.

english: Black pod is a water-borne fungal disease that thrives in high humidity and dark, bushy fields. Clearing weeds, pruning extra branches, and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps air flow through the farm and keeps the disease away.
ga: Black pod ji hela ko ni jɛɔ nu mli ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hei ni edɔ, ni jwɛi yɔɔ lɛ. weeding additional pruning Ni ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fall off and the plants stop growing during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop leaves during hot, dry periods to save water and protect themselves from drying out completely. When the rains start again, the plant will naturally sprout fresh green leaves and resume growing.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaada ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees, or will it affect their growth?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe? Aloo ebaaná edalɛ nɔ hewalɛ loo enaŋ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cassava spreads strong, heavy root systems that fight young cocoa trees for water and nutrients. It is better to use plantains for shade around young cocoa, as they do not aggressively compete for root space.
ga: Cassava gbɛɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni tsii ni kɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui atsu nii koni akɛha hulutsoo abɔle kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe, ejaakɛ amɛyeee akaŋ waa kɛha shishifãi ahe he ko.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Consistent watering and keeping the soil cool with mulch can help the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni feɔ pollen tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa Nu ni akɛhaa daa ni akɛ mulch haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds require moisture to trigger germination. If planted in dry soil, the seed will sit dormant or dry out before it can develop roots, preventing it from breaking through the ground surface.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ loo amɛgbiɔ dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi. Etsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wither and die even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: This usually happens because of soil-borne diseases like bacterial wilt or root rot. When the soil stays constantly wet without proper drainage, harmful germs attack the roots, stopping the plant from taking up food and causing it to collapse quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tamɔ bacteria wilt loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ahewɔ enɛ baa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔɔ be fɛɛ be ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: If I leave old, harvested crop leaves and stems on my field, will it harm my new plants?
ga: Kɛji mishi baai kɛ tsei ni akpa momo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani ebaaye mitsei heei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, leftover dead plants often hide pests and disease spores over the dry season. Burning or clearing away old crop waste prevents diseases from jumping straight into your new seedlings when the rains start.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni egboi lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai teeɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Nibii ni adu lɛ amli jwɛi momo ni ashãa loo ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã odumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and crowded farms. Pruning extra shade branches lets in sunshine and wind, which dries out the farm and keeps the disease away.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni efɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ he. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni helai akabote mli.

english: Can planting my crops too close together make them fall sick easily?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hela aba amɛnɔ oya?

english: Yes, crowded plants trap damp air around their leaves and stems, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to multiply and spread fast from plant to plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛbɔleɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize field turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen fertilizer or is being attacked at the roots by pests. Without enough food in the soil early on, the plant struggles to grow and produce healthy ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen fertilizer bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ etutua lɛ. Kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra lɛ, Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda ni efee toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from severe heat stress, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Mulching the soil to keep it cool and moist helps the plant keep its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava field has a disease before all the leaves dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ hela dani baai lɛ fɛɛ agbi?

english: Look out for leaves that show yellow-and-green mosaic patterns or start twisting upwards. These early signs mean a virus is inside the plant, even if the roots have not rotted yet.
ga: Taomɔ baai ni tsɔɔ mosaic mfoniri ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ni miije shishi amɛmiitsɔ ŋwɛi. Nɛkɛ mra be mli okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ egboko lolo po.

english: Why does my farmland produce good harvests in the first year but fails in the second year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi ewooo yibii yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating your crops or adding animal manure rebuilds the soil's strength.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo okɛ kooloi ashishifãi afata he koni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to snap or fall over easily during light wind?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny worms in the soil, called nematodes, or banana weevils destroy their roots underground. Without healthy roots to grip the ground, the heavy stem cannot support itself.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Tso ni tsii lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ehe nɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits turn black and rot at the bottom while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This rot happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the plant build strong, healthy fruits.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to get seeds from my local area in Ghana instead of buying imported ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Local seeds are already naturally adapted to Ghana's specific weather, rainfall patterns, and soil conditions. They sprout more reliably and fight off local pests much better than seeds brought in from different climates.
ga: Atsake maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ kɛha Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi amli lɛ.

english: Why do buyers in Ghana prefer specific varieties of cassava or maize over others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ko fe ekroko lɛ?

english: Ghanaians prefer specific crop varieties based on cooking traditional foods—such as cassava that pounded into smooth fufu or maize that makes good banku. Planting preferred varieties ensures your harvest sells quickly at the market.
ga: Ghanabii sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni damɔ kusum nihoomɔ nɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni atswa lɛ fufu ni mli tse. Aloo ŋmãa ni haa Bangkudi feɔ kpakpa lɛ? Kɛ́ odu tso srɔtoi ni otaoɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How do I know if a seed variety can survive the hot Ghanaian dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni sa? Ani ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Drought-resistant seed varieties grow deeper roots to find hidden underground water or mature faster so they produce food before the rain completely stops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ baatswa shishi kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ mra koni amɛwo niyenii dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: How does using a tractor or machine help my crops grow better than using just a hand hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta loo tsɔne ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsɔne ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ nii lɛ?

english: Machines loosen the soil deeper and faster, breaking up hard ground so that plant roots can easily push down, breath, and soak up nutrients and water.
ga: Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi oya. Efoɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anyɛ shi, amɛmu, ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu oya.

english: Why should I clear and prepare my land thoroughly before planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni masaa he dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Properly clearing the field removes weeds that steal sunlight and food from your crops, while soft, weed-free soil gives young seedlings a clean, strong start.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie jwɛi ni juɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa shishijee ni he tse ni mli wa.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing them to grow tall, weak, and produce very small fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɔ, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui bibii kwraa.

english: Why do my crops get weaker when I plant the same crop on the same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Changing crops helps the soil refresh itself naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ naa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry and need soil food like manure or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia mi?

english: Crops tell you they are hungry through their leaves; if the leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green or if the plant stops growing tall, it lacks essential nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ hɔmɔ miiye amɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ loo kɛji tso lɛ kpa dalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do some crop varieties resist bugs easily while others get eaten up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi yeɔ amɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties have built-in natural defenses, like tougher leaf skins or scents that insects dislike, keeping the plant safe without needing heavy chemical sprays.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ amɛhe, tamɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni wa loo ŋmɔlɔ ni kooloi sumɔɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: How does harvesting my crops at the wrong time affect how long they last after picking?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ saa be ni heɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ akpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Harvesting too early means crops shrink and spoil fast because they are not fully formed, while harvesting too late leaves them soft and prone to rot before reaching the market.
ga: Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ oya ejaakɛ eshɛko he kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛgboi dani amɛyashɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that easily burn under strong sunlight, so they need fast-growing shade crops like plantains to shelter them until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants compete underground for water and soil nutrients, resulting in many small, thin roots instead of large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtaoɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize crop help my soil?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen directly from the air and releases it into the soil, providing free, natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because afternoon heat causes water to evaporate before roots can soak it up, and hot moist soil can stress the plant roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. And hot, moist soil can stress plant roots.

english: Maize leaves roll up to conserve moisture and slow down water loss when the soil becomes dry, while yellowing indicates the plant is starving for water and essential nitrogen.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nu kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ he hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ.

english: If I add a very large amount of chemical fertilizer to my vegetables, will they grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma babaoo fata aduawai ahe lɛ Ani ebaada oya shii enyɔ?

english: Too much chemical fertilizer creates high salt levels in the soil that burn plant roots and can kill the crop or cause it to produce excessive leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii loo eha baai babaoo aba yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when bees and insects are not present to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ebɔle ehe Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi baaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep for light and air to reach them, if the soil is kept too dry, or if the seeds were stored in a hot place and lost their energy.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni mli edɔ ni hewalɛ sɛɛ fo.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to quickly snatch water and soil nutrients before your cultivated crops can build strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya. Dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ,.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers are fully mature and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the vines and leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has finished transferring its stored energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much water or not enough when I use a pump?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ he kɛ́ mikɛ pɔmp miitsu nii?

english: Crops usually show you when they are uncomfortable. Too much water causes leaves to turn yellow and roots to rot because they cannot breathe. Too little water makes leaves wilt, curl, or turn brown at the edges as the plant tries to save moisture.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ bo be mli ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Nu babaoo haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli. Nu fioo tsɔ baaha baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ, amɛkpãtã, loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up so fast during the dry season even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the hot, dry season, sunlight and dry winds pull moisture directly out of both the leaves and the soil surface very quickly. Mulching—covering the soil around the plant roots with dry grass or leaves—helps trap water in the ground for much longer.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli, hulutsoo be mli lɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Mulching—ni ji shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be babaoo.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in neat rows rather than scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in rows gives each crop its own space to get enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors. It also makes it much easier for you to walk through, weed, and care for the plants.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni ekɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo hu kɛhaa bo akɛ oootsɔ mli, ojie jwɛi, ni okwɛ otsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize turn yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. When soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to the top young leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without harming either crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ ŋmãa enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ akafite?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving the space open for the cassava to grow bigger underground later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko koni ŋmei lɛ adara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops help the soil stay fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer for other crops planted next to or after them.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ. loo no sɛɛ

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow very tall and thin without producing much fruit when planted under large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: When plants are shaded by tall trees, they spend all their energy stretching upward to search for sunlight. Because they waste energy growing tall, they don't have enough strength left to produce flower or fruit.
ga: Beni tsei kakadaji ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛtao hulu la. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛha dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo fɔfɔii loo aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and feeling sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni enuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Curled, sticky leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids. They hide on the undersides of leaves and drink the plant's juices, which weakens the plant and leaves a sticky waste behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids kɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni wa lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Cassava tells you it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the stem near the ground becomes thick. You can carefully scrape away a bit of topsoil around the base to check if the roots are large enough.
ga: Yucca kɛɛ bo akɛ edara beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajie. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ajie shishigbɛ lɛ koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year on the same plot of land even when rain falls well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your crops or adding organic manure replenishes the nutrients so future crops grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara waa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees naturally grow under forest canopies and burn easily under full sun. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantain to block harsh sunlight, young cocoa plants lose moisture too fast and get scorched.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ koo lɛ shishi ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo be loo tsei tamɔ plantains ni baaha hulu la ni naa wa lɛ aná hulutsoo. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Extra shoots steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant, which leads to smaller plantain bunches. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures your main plant grows big, heavy fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. ni kɛ mɔ yaa plantain tso bibioo ko mli Kɛ́ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ akwɛ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize plants need to build strong leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and crop strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa tso lɛ awo baai ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do other farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside maize feeds the soil naturally and improves your crop yield without needing as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abele masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Cassava stems planted upside down or cut from soft, immature parts of the plant rot easily. You should use mature stem cuttings and plant them with the bud nodes pointing upward in well-drained soil.
ga: Aduɔ cassava tsei lɛ ashwieɔ shi loo afoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fiteɔ oya lɛ amli. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds after the first rains arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting right after the very first rain is risky because the soil underneath stays dry and hot. It is best to wait until you get two or three deep rains so the soil holds enough moisture to keep seeds alive.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baagbi ni edɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni naa wa fioo koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: What is eating holes in the central leaves of my young corn plants and leaving dirty powder inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ powda ni mli ewo muji yɛ mli?

english: That damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the growing center of the corn plant. Applying recommended pest treatments directly into the center funnel early in the morning controls them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tso ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni akɛba ni akɛyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but all the blossoms drop off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Consistent watering and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does covering the ground with dry grass around my pepper plants help them grow?
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni ebɔle he lɛ Te mi-pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under strong sunshine, retains ground water, and prevents weeds from taking light and food away from your pepper plants.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni akɛtoɔ he ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkajie la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ o-pepper tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Yam plants need their leaves raised high to catch maximum sunlight to build large underground tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛbaai lɛ adara babaoo koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai ni ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth, or the roots are drowning because the soil has too much trapped water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Aloo shishifãi lɛ miiho ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo eto.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy seasons when cocoa farms are too bushy or heavily shaded.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Enɛ ji be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ yɔɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ loo hulutsoo babaoo.

english: What is making the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and show yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies; planting improved, disease-resistant stem cuttings prevents it.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Dumɔ etee hiɛ ni afee tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing leaf growth instead of fruit growth.
ga: Tomatoi fɔ̃ɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛ́ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, ehaa baai shwereɔ yɛ aduawai shweremɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so fast after I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they were cut or bruised during harvesting, or if they are stored in a hot place without good air movement to keep them cool and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli koni eha edɔ ni egbi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch starts growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by small soil pests called nematodes, leaving the plant too weak to hold up heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu aduawai akui ni tsii ahe nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants shrinking and rolling up tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, which causes new growth to become wrinkled and twisted.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ hee lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ.

english: How do groundnuts produce nuts inside the ground when the flowers grow above the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, the plant sends down long stems called pegs into the soil, where the groundnut pods actually form and grow under the ground.
ga: Beni tso lɛ efo ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ amli sɛɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean pods lɛ feɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is my swamp rice turning yellow even though there is plenty of water on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nu babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If water stays completely still without draining or moving, it removes oxygen from the soil, preventing the roots from breathing and causing the rice leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ efee dioo kwraa ni efooo loo etsiii ehe lɛ Ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu, ni ehaa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do tiny insects cover my cowpea flowers as soon as they open up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛji amɛfɔ̃ pɛ?

english: Insects like aphids and thrips are attracted to the sweet sap inside cowpea flowers; spraying natural mixtures like neem leaf extract early protects the flowers so pods can form.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids kɛ thrips gbalaa amɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cowpea fɔfɔi amli lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii afee ŋmeii.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal disease that thrives when the farm is too wet and dark. Removing diseased pods quickly prevents the fungus from spreading to healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa kɛji ŋmɔji amli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji black pods lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What should I do if I see a lot of ants crawling over my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina ŋmeii babaoo ni miiho yɛ kookoo tso ko nɔ?

english: Ants often carry and protect smaller insects like mealybugs that weaken cocoa trees. Clearing undergrowth, pruning heavy branches, and using safe pest controls help keep ant populations away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii woɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs, ni haa kookoo tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmɔ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ. Ni kɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akabote he.

english: Should I cut off cocoa pods that have already turned black, or leave them to fall on their own?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni etsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ loo mashi amɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbee shi?

english: You should cut off and destroy black pods immediately. Leaving them on the tree allows the disease spores to stay alive and infect new pods whenever it rains.
ga: Esa akɛ afolɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahi shi ni amɛtswa tsɛŋemɔ helai heei be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Why is too much darkness or shade bad for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ duŋ loo hulutsoo be babaoo ehiii kɛha mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Heavy darkness traps dampness and cold air around the trees, creating the perfect condition for fungal diseases to grow. Sunlight is needed to warm the farm and keep trees healthy.
ga: Duŋ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ. Hulu la he miihia koni ekɛha ŋmɔ lɛ mli adɔ ni eha tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does cutting off excess branches help my cocoa farm produce better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Trimming branches allows sunlight to reach the ground and lets fresh air circulate through the trees, which dries up disease-causing moisture and sends energy to growing pods.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu ni kɛ hela baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees too close together and never trim them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni mifolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When trees are overcrowded and untrimmed, they create a dense canopy that blocks all sunlight. This dark environment weakens the trees and makes them easy targets for diseases and pests.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni afolɔko amɛ Tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu la fɛɛ naa. Shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm is getting enough sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If the ground under your cocoa trees stays damp all day and you cannot see patches of sunlight hitting the soil, your farm's canopy is too thick and needs pruning.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni onyɛɛɛ ona hulu la ni tswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋtayaa ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ mli.

english: How can I keep animals like dogs or rodents from eating and damaging my cocoa pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi tamɔ gbee loo ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛkafite amɛ?

english: Harvesting your ripe pods on time and keeping the farm floor free of overgrown weeds reduces places for animals to hide and feed on your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be naa ni oha jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine akafee ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hei ni kooloi kɛ amɛhe baawo mli ni amɛye onibii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread so fast during the rainy season on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain spreads fungal spores through dripping water, and high humidity allows disease to grow rapidly, especially on farms with thick shade where sunlight cannot dry the leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu mli. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa helai yaa hiɛ oya. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ aha baai lɛ agbi lɛ amli.

english: Why are some cocoa trees on my farm dying off while others nearby stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigbo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi miigboi lɛ? He ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji lolo.

english: Trees in areas with poor airflow, heavy shade, or high pest activity get stressed faster and succumb to diseases, while trees receiving adequate light and care remain resilient.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ, he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ, loo hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɔɔ lɛ baaná haomɔ oya ni helai baaye amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni naa la kɛ kwɛmɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when planted under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sun. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside them provides necessary shade and soil moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aahu kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce food for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts leaves off the ground, maximizing sunlight exposure and preventing leaf diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Na hulu la babaoo ni otsi foliar helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: How do I choose the right stem cutting when planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso nine ni sa kɛ́ midu ŋmei?

english: Select cuttings from the middle portion of mature, healthy stems that are about a thumb's thickness. Avoid the soft green tips or old woody bases to ensure strong rooting and sprouting.
ga: Halamɔ tso nine ko kɛjɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ tsitsi bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli loo tsei ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe koni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a 'V'?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips moving inward usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant regain its green color and grow vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni yaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Growing maize continuously on the same plot depletes specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, reducing crop yields over time.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why is it harmful to place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baawo tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain strong salts that draw moisture out of plant tissue. Placing fertilizer directly against stems or roots burns and destroys the tissue, so it should be buried a few centimeters away.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni mli wa, ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi loo shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã ni efite fãji lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afu lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita fioo ko pɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is often caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites, which transmit viruses. Treating the plants early with organic or recommended pesticides controls these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, ni ji helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ abaanyɛ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do I find small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my maize whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mi-corn rings lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the soft, growing parts of the maize plant. Early monitoring and spraying with appropriate control agents protect the plant's growth point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ. Nɔkwɛmɔ mra kɛ nibii ni akudɔɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, extreme dry spells, or over-watering. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and adequate airflow around plants helps flowers set fruit properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fe nine. Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa abɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough moisture to start planting my seeds after the major dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be ni mli wa waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil taken from a palm's depth into a ball. If it holds its shape without crumbling immediately or leaving water dripping, the soil contains ideal moisture for seed germination.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ onine mli lɛ mli fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni egbeee shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo eshiuuu nu ni hoɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni sa kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn ears are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele toi lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize plants need to grow healthy green leaves and strong corn ears. The plant pulls food from its bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha nɔ hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their small flowers without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Yibɔ babaoo ni etsɔko kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can feed, but extreme heat, dry weather, or lack of soil nutrients cause them to drop flowers to survive and save energy.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha niyenii. Shi latsaa be ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi ni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upwards during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when plants try to protect themselves from intense heat and water loss, but it can also be a sign of a crop disease spread by tiny insects like whiteflies.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Shi ebaanyɛ efee tso hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi hu.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket that keeps the ground cool and traps soil moisture so crop roots do not dry out.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni tso shishifãi akagbi

english: Too much water standing in wet soil stops air from reaching cassava roots and encourages fungal diseases to grow, which makes the tubers rot quickly.
ga: Nu ni shwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ewoɔ ŋmei helai ahe hewalɛ. ni haa yitso lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning instead of late at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu leebi moŋ fe gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives roots time to drink before the sun gets hot, whereas leaving leaves wet overnight can attract fungal growth and plant diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi baai lɛ ni efɔ lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbala ŋmeii kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baa lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does mixing dried animal dung into my soil help my crops stay fresh during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Dried animal dung acts like a sponge in the soil, improving its ability to hold onto water and releasing slow nourishment to crop roots during periods without rain.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii fiofio koni ekɛdu shishifãi yɛ bei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy bunches start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ jwɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the top of the soil, so the weight of a heavy bunch or strong winds can easily tip them over unless you prop them up with sturdy wooden sticks.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ni tsii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbee shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Ja okɛ tso ni mli wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Climbing high on stakes spreads out the leaves so they catch the sun without crowding each other on the wet ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. climbing tall poles Amɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwãa koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la lɛ ni amɛkawo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with tiny fruits when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food, causing them to stretch tall for light instead of growing strong trunks and big fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why should I buy new hybrid maize seeds from dealers every season instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ŋmãa kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ daa afi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Saved hybrid seeds lose their strength in the second generation, leading to uneven plant growth, smaller cobs, and significantly lower yields. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures maximum growth vigor and pest resistance.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ eba shi waa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ naa dalɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is too much direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas until their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baadara.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the plant is lacking nitrogen or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots, preventing them from taking up essential nutrients from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the center leaves of my young maize plants ragged with holes and filled with saw-dust-like waste?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ bu ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which burrow into the central funnel of the plant to feed on tender leaves while hiding from predators and heat.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii yɛ be mli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ kɛ latsaa he lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stem without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes severe stress to tomato plants, leading them to shed their blossoms instead of developing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ shwane mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa Aloo, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ baagbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plants stretch upward to capture light instead of spending energy to form thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛmɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during continuous heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Persistent damp weather creates ideal conditions for Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads through rain splashes and destroys pods if the canopy is not pruned to allow airflow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ nɔ, ni ebaakpãtã ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nodes krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is my sorghum crop stunted and yellow even after I have cleared all visible weeds from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Beni mijie jwɛi fɛɛ ni anaa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ po.

english: Your crop may be attacked by Striga (Witchweed), a parasitic weed that attaches to crop roots underground and steals water and nutrients long before its stems show above the surface.
ga: Ekolɛ Striga (Witchweed), ni ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ tsei ashishifãi ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii be kakadaŋŋ dani eshishifãi lɛ jieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua onibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, helping it retain moisture and survive high temperatures.
ga: Baai ni akpɛ́ɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli.

english: Why does planting my maize in straight, spaced rows yield bigger cobs than planting them randomly close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii wuji baa fe ŋmãa ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe trukaa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Planting in straight, properly spaced rows ensures every plant gets equal nutrients to grow big cobs, while also leaving clear pathways for farm tools and machinery.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ ŋmei agbo ni aduɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔ mli nibii kɛ tsɔnei.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die when the ground becomes too hard and compacted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Hard soil acts like a wall, stopping plant roots from pushing deep into the earth to find hidden water and nutrients. Ploughing or loosening the soil allows roots to spread wide, anchoring the plant firmly and keeping it hydrated.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo. Etsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootsu nii loo otsi lɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Mɔ tso lɛ mli shiŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni oha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when water sits on my farm for many days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air just like human beings do. When heavy rain leaves standing water on the field, it drowns the roots, preventing them from drinking up soil nutrients, which makes the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haaa amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants leave the soil richer for the maize crop I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miishi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny bumps on their roots that capture invisible food from the air and store it in the earth. This acts as a free, natural fertilizer for hungry crops like maize planted afterwards.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛmɔ niyenii ni anaaa kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What will happen if I place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plant?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong, like hot salt, and touching the stem directly will burn and scorch the plant's skin. Placing fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away allows the roots to safely drink it without damage.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he wa waa, tamɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã ni ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli Inchi fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anu nu shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my young maize plants so aggressively instead of the older ones?
