ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ waa yɛ tsei ni eda lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Young maize plants have soft, tender leaves that are rich in water and easy for young worms to chew. Protecting the plant early saves the central growing point, which is essential for the crop to reach harvest age.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni ŋmeii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebaaye ebua ni amɛkwɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ mli yɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ he miihia koni tsei lɛ ashɛ kpamɔ afii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak if I do not clear them early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer intended for your plants. Clearing weeds in the first few weeks ensures your crop gets all the food it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by small invisible germs that thrive in cold, dark, and wet conditions. Pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight and wind dry out the farm, stopping the disease from destroying your harvest.
ga: Muawai bibii kɛ Black pod hela baa. invisible Eshwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsei krokomɛi ni abaakpa lɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kpa helai ni miifite onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the soil if I leave them past their harvest time to sell later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ koni ahɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers are living storage organs that soft-rot when kept in wet ground past their maturity peak. Harvesting on time and processing or selling them quickly prevents soil insects and fungi from eating them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni baafite kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe bɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ be naa ni atsu he nii loo ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil so fast when I store them immediately after cutting them from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grains still contain hidden moisture inside them, which attracts mould and grain-eating insects in storage. Thoroughly drying grains in the sun before bagging keeps them fresh for months so you can sell when market prices rise.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lolo. ni gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛbu he Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi yɛ hulu mli dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi nyɔji babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ jara lɛ tee ŋwɛi.

english: How do I know exactly when my maize is ready for harvest so it doesn't spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and a small black spot appears at the base of each kernel where it attaches to the cob. Harvesting at this time stops mold from growing and protects the grain from insects.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ shishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I wait too long to harvest them after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots absorb too much water during heavy rains, which drops their starch levels and makes them rot quickly. It is best to harvest cassava during moderate soil moisture to keep the roots firm and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha starch lɛ aba shi ni ebaaha efite oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakpa ŋmei be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fioo koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During harmattan, the dry wind and hot sun cause cocoa leaves to lose water very fast. The tree drops its leaves on purpose to conserve moisture in its trunk so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ kookoo baai lɛ anɔ oya waa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛtso lɛ mli lɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing any tomatoes when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Very hot temperatures destroy the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. The plant drops the unpollinated flowers to save its energy until cooler weather arrives.
ga: He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my maize crop grow better?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas have small nodules on their roots that absorb nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize crop.
ga: Cowpea yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa o-ŋmei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing is a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves its remaining nitrogen to the younger leaves at the top, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look twisted like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛtsi amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaf. As they drink the plant's sap, they distort the leaf's growth and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do Fall Armyworms always hide deep inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The center funnel of a young maize plant is soft, moist, and protects the worm from heat and predators like birds. The pest stays hidden there while eating the tender new leaves.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi ahe. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ jɛmɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do these new hybrid maize seeds need more water and fertilizer than my traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ŋmãa nɛɛ biɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mi maŋbii akusum dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are bred to produce much larger cobs, but building those extra grains requires extra nutrients and water. They act like high-performing workers that need more food to do their job.
ga: Afɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni dara kwraa. Shi nakai dumɔwui krokomɛi ni akɛfata he lɛ afeemɔ biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu krokomɛi. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa ni niyenii babaoo he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛtsu amɛnitsumɔi lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some leaves from my plantain suckers before I plant them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei lɛ ahe baai komɛi dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Large leaves lose a lot of water through evaporation. Trimming the leaves when transplanting stops the sucker from drying out while its roots are still struggling to settle in the new soil.
ga: Baai wuji laajeɔ nu babaoo kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai lɛ amli beni aduɔ lɛ, ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miitao ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cool environment and keeps moisture in the soil so the young cocoa can survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be mli ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room to grow large, heavy cassava tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food away from the main plantain stem. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets full nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo kɛjɛ mli ni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni efee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap out of the leaves. Controlling these insects early with neem spray or recommended treatments stops the curling and helps the plant produce good peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ akɛ neem spray loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii nɛɛ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akpa ŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important nutrient for leaf growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer gives the crop the energy it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like peanuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil. It holds water in the earth longer and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the growing center of maize. Checking your crops early and applying appropriate remedies into the center of the plant prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he. Nibii ni akwɛɔ mli mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni sa baatsu nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baatsi enaa koni ekafite nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and cool helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a sudden dry period before the main rainy season truly starts. If seeds sprout during that first rain and then face days without water, the young seedlings will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nakai klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ gbii ni nu bɛ mli lɛ kpe lɛ, Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: The rain pattern in my area has changed and it doesn't fall like it used to. How does this change affect when I should plant my maize?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ etsake ni enɛɛɛ tamɔ tsutsu lɛ. Te tsakemɔ nɛɛ saa be ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Maize needs steady moisture to germinate and grow strong roots. Instead of planting on fixed calendar dates like in the past, wait until the soil is consistently wet after the first major rains, or switch to early-maturing maize varieties that need less water overall.
ga: Abɛi taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛha kwɛ̃mɔ kɛ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ gbii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ yɛ kalanda lɛ naa tamɔ be ni eho lɛ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Aloo tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmã henɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni biɔ nu fioo yɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build healthy green leaves. It can also be caused by prolonged dry weather or cassava mosaic disease. Adding organic manure or compost helps restore soil nutrients and plant strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ loo cassava mosaic hela hu baanyɛ ekɛba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kɛ tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year, why does my harvest keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it continuously on the same land drains those specific nutrients faster than the soil can recover. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Nibii ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aná ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Tall shade trees act like large umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from direct sun heat and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Will planting my cassava stems very close together give me more tubers at harvest time?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa lɛ baaha ŋmeii babaoo aba yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: No, planting cassava stems too close together causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This results in thin, weak plants with very small roots. Giving each plant proper space allows big, heavy tubers to develop.
ga: Dabi, yucca tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awu yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shishifãi bibii waa baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto wood stakes instead of letting them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to be lifted off the ground to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal rot and diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by intense midday heat or irregular watering. When conditions get too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy just to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing in the soil alongside them?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. They can also hide dangerous pests and crop diseases that easily spread to your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ tsei ahe helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ hu ato mlɛo.

english: Why are small caterpillars suddenly eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ trukaa lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the growing center of young maize plants. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can control them before severe damage occurs.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii. Abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ dani nɔ ko ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli aba.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their ability to sprout if they are stored in damp conditions, damaged by heat, or attacked by weevils. Storing clean, completely dry seeds in airtight containers with ash or seed protectants keeps them alive until the next planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafee nɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. hulutsoo efite loo ŋmeii tutua Dumɔwui ni he tse ni egbi kwraa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni sũ loo nɔ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly when it stops raining for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from heat and reduce water loss through transpiration. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism when the soil drys out, warning you that the crop is suffering from water stress.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi. Ekaiɔ bo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miina nu he haomɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before setting fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When tomato plants face high heat and low soil moisture, they enter survival mode and shed their blossoms to conserve energy and water, which prevents new fruits from growing until conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tomatoi yaa wala shihilɛ mli ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Enɛ haaa aduawai heei akwɛ̃ kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What actually happens to cassava roots under the soil if the ground remains completely dry for months?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa nyɔji babaoo?

english: Cassava is tough and can survive dry ground, but prolonged drought forces the plant to feed on its own stored energy, resulting in smaller, woody roots with less starch.
ga: Cassava wa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Shi hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha tsei aye amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa, ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do crops in southern Ghana still need controlled irrigation if the region naturally gets two rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lolo lɛ? Kɛji kpokpaa nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ bei enyɔ

english: Rainfall in the south can be erratic and unpredictable. Short dry spells during critical growth stages—like flowering or pod filling—can destroy yield potential if farmers rely solely on rain instead of supplementary irrigation.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ejaaa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. be kuku ni akɛgbiɔ Yɛ shweremɔ bei ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔfɔi loo pod ni awoɔ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ kɛji okwaafoi kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe nu ni akɛfataa he lɛ.

english: How does providing a steady supply of irrigation water help my crops grow faster than waiting for rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ shi daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya fe nugbɔ ni mimɛɔ lɛ?

english: Irrigation gives plants a consistent feed of moisture directly to their roots without interruption, allowing them to absorb soil nutrients continuously rather than pausing their growth during dry weather gaps.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa nu kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, hɛ mi yami ɔ kpaa be bɔɔ ko ngɛ hwɔɔ be mi.

english: Can I safely plant water-loving vegetables like cabbage or pepper in the dry season without an irrigation setup?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu aduawai ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ kaabe loo ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ato nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo he gbɛjianɔ?

english: Vegetables require constant soil moisture to build leaves and fruit. Planting them in the dry season without a reliable irrigation water supply usually leads to stunted plants, wilting, and total crop failure.
ga: Aduawai biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee baai kɛ aduawai. Dumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ bɛ. Bei pii lɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: Does giving my crops too much irrigation water hurt them as much as not giving them enough water?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ fe nine lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui tamɔ bɔ ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fioo lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ?

english: Yes, over-watering suffocates crop roots by pushing oxygen out of the soil. This causes root rot, prevents the plant from taking up food, and turns the leaves yellow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye nii ni baai lɛ hu afee ŋmɔŋ

english: Will using drip irrigation improve my crop harvest compared to carrying water in buckets to each plant?
ga: Ani drip irrigation ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akpamɔ aya hiɛ fe nu ni akɛwoɔ baagi mli ni mikɛwoɔ tso fɛɛ tso mli lɛ he?

english: Drip irrigation delivers small, precise amounts of water straight to the plant root zone without wasting water or compacting the soil, resulting in healthier root systems and higher crop yields.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu fioo pɛpɛɛpɛ yaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni nu efiteee loo ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee shi Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa.

english: How can I easily check if my field soil has enough water for seeds to germinate properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mlɛo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil taken from a few inches deep; if it forms a moist ball that holds together without dripping water, it is ideal for seed germination. If it crumbles, it is too dry.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo ko mli lɛ mli nine kome. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni mli efɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Dumɔwui lɛ hi kɛha kwɛ̃mɔ. Kɛji egbɛ eshwa lɛ, no lɛ egbi tsɔ.

english: Why does lowland rice require so much standing water while crops like yam die if left in wet waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ gboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels that allow their roots to survive underwater, whereas yam roots need airy soil and quickly rot when submerged in stagnant water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sweet potato shishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee, ni kɛ́ akɛwo nu ni damɔ shi mli lɛ, egboɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps the leaves regain their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha amɛdara.

english: Why does adding dried animal manure to my land make crops grow better than untreated soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛfataa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu he nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure restores organic matter and essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium to the soil. It also helps sandy soil hold moisture longer and softens hard clay soil so roots can stretch easily.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hu ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight or heat. Leaving larger trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby creates necessary shade, protecting the young seedlings from burning until they are established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa aba. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ la he kɛyashi amɛbaatswa shi.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell. Planting too quickly can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up in the hot soil before the steady rainy season fully sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa loo nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni sa lɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to run off, keeping the roots safe from fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni nu shwieee shi Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops produce very small fruits if I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots fight for the same soil food and water, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrients to produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and yellow leaves from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛ baai ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive stems that drain energy from the plant. This directs the plant's food and water straight to developing flowers and pepper fruits, making them grow larger.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni wooo yibii ni jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ kudɔɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nu kɛyaa pepper fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ anɔ. Ha amɛfee wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my main crops every time it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally absorb soil nutrients and water faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing vital food away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and missing growing tips?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋaawoi ni elaaje ni esa akɛ adu lɛ nɔ?

english: This is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the center leaves of the plant. Spraying with recommended organic or chemical solutions early in the morning destroys them before they kill the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic solution loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛgbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without ever turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or during sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli trukaa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ tamɔ tomato.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings always droop and look like they are dying right after I move them from the nursery tray into my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui atoohe lɛ kɛtee miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you move young seedlings, their tiny roots get disturbed and suffer from 'transplant shock.' Just like a young child getting weak from a long journey, young plants need time, gentle handling, shade, and water to recover and adjust to their new environment.
ga: Kɛji okɛ tsei bibii shwie shi lɛ, amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnaa ‘Transplant shock’, tamɔ gbekɛ bibioo ko ni gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ egbɔjɔ Tsei bibii lɛ heɔ be. Nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo, hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akɛbaaku sɛɛ aba ni ekɛ ehe awo shihilɛ hee lɛ mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to transport delicate vegetable seedlings to my farm so they do not wither on the road?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ aduawai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo aya miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Bɔni afee ni akagbo yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to transport seedlings early in the morning or late in the evening. Moving them during cool hours protects the weak young plants from hot sun stress and keeps their soil moist during the journey.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ dumɔwui lɛ aya leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛfaa lɛ mli.

english: If I buy cassava stem cuttings from far away, why do some of them fail to sprout after I bring them to my farm?
ga: Kɛji mihe ŋmei niji kɛjɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei ni midu lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ?

english: Cassava stems can dry out or get damaged during long, hot journeys. If the growth nodes on the stems get bruised or lose too much moisture on the road, the stems lose their strength and cannot produce roots properly.
ga: Cassava tsei baanyɛ agbi loo amɛfite yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ hei ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ egbɔjɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine efo mli yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ. Hewalɛ baa shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni enyɛɛɛ efee shishifãi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very tender and cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them from the strong sun, their young leaves get scorched because their roots cannot take up water fast enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. If there are no trees to provide shade or seedlings to shade from strong sunlight, Their young leaves get scorched because the roots can't absorb water fast enough.

english: Why do officers ask me to cut off the top leaves of my plantain suckers before carrying them to plant in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ biɔ ni mifo plantain yiteŋ baai lɛ dani midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves lose a lot of water through evaporation. Cutting the large leaves off before moving the sucker keeps the young plant from drying out while its roots are recovering from being dug up.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ fiteɔ nu babaoo kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Cutting off large leaves before moving the vacuum cleaner This will prevent the seedlings from drying out while the roots are recovering from being dug up.

english: Why should I expose my nursery plants to full sunlight for a few days before transplanting them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha mi-nursery tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛ amɛ aya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This practice is called 'hardening off.' Exposing young plants to sun gradually builds up their strength so they do not get overwhelmed by the harsh weather when moved from the nursery to the main field.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ 'hewalɛ ni ajieɔ'. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo hulu la mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛwa fiofio. Hewalɛ Enɛ ji koni akafee kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ babaoo beni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams sometimes rot in the ground instead of growing green leaves after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ baai eŋɔli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If seed yams get bruised during transport or are planted in waterlogged soil, harmful fungi enter through the skin damage. The delicate seed rot sets in before the yam has enough strength to shoot out leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fã yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsɔɔ hewolo ni efite lɛ mli kɛboteɔ mli. Dumɔwui ni fiteɔ lɛ baa dani sweet potato lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa shwieɔ baai.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into thin tubes when the sun gets very hot at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ bo yɛ shwane mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By curling, the leaf reduces the surface exposed to the hot sun, stopping internal moisture from escaping until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. ni otsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa koni ekaje mli kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants wilt in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow, weak roots that cannot absorb water as quickly as the strong afternoon heat evaporates it from the leaves. They usually recover in the cool evening once sun intensity drops.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya tamɔ nɛkɛ. kɛ la ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why did my young maize shoots turn brown and wither right after I put chemical fertilizer next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ trukaa ni amɛgboi beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop roots are extremely sensitive. Placing dry chemical fertilizer too close to young stems draws water out of the fragile roots, burning them in the same way salt hurts a raw wound.
ga: Tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ nuɔ he waa. Tsofa ni mli egbi ni akɛfataa he ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ baajie nu kɛjɛ shishifãi ni waaa lɛ ahe. Ni oshã lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ŋoo yeɔ pilamɔ hee awui lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and looking weak even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rain usually mean the soil has lost nitrogen through leaching. While water is plentiful, the crop lacks the essential nutrients needed to make food and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ efo sũ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu lɛ fa moŋ Shi ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why did my maize plants grow very tall stalks but produce very small ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa shi ewoɔ toi bibii waa lɛ?

english: When crops receive excess nitrogen or are planted too close together, they spend their energy growing leaves and stems instead of feeding the grain.
ga: Kɛji tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ amɛshishifãi amli moŋ fe ni amɛaaha dumɔwui lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without plantains nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nɔ tse ni plantains bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides essential shade and keeps the surrounding soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: If my cassava plot gets infected with mosaic disease, should I try to save the plants or clear the whole farm?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mosaic hela emɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani esa akɛ makwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ loo majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Severe mosaic disease cannot be cured once established. Leaving infected cassava in the field allows whiteflies to carry the virus to nearby healthy crops, so uprooting infected plants protects the rest of your farm.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ atsa mosaic hela ni naa wa waa kɛji eba pɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before they can turn into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, drought, or nutrient stress. The plant sheds flowers to conserve water and energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ kpe amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense response where the plant reduces leaf surface area to prevent water loss during intense heat, though it can also indicate a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu hetoo. Tsei haa baa lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu akafite yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa moŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yam tubers every year even when I use the same farming method?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ.

english: Planting yams in the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating yams with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps restore nitrogen and soil fertility naturally.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Sweet potatoes ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nitrogen kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my cowpea seedlings right after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb initial moisture and soil nutrients much faster than young crops, allowing them to overpower seedlings unless cleared early.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei bibii. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kunim ja ajie amɛ oya.

english: Why is it bad to plant cassava directly under big mango or neem trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ mango loo neem tso shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Large trees cast dense shade and have extensive root systems that steal sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, leaving the cassava stunted with thin roots.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni mli wa ni amɛyɛ shishifãi babaoo ni juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings droop and look lifeless immediately after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by transplant shock. The delicate roots suffer damage during moving and get overwhelmed by sudden heat; transplanting late in the afternoon and watering immediately helps seedlings recover quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ, ni hulutsoo trukaa baa amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ oya.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large, broad leaves that shade young cocoa plants, keeping the soil moist and protecting them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni abu he kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How can I tell the exact time my paddy rice is ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80% to 85% of the grains on the panicle turn a bright golden-yellow color. Harvesting too early results in unfilled, weak grains, while waiting too long causes mature grains to shatter and fall off onto the ground.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji omɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ toi lɛ anɔ lɛ aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% batsɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ayi obɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni edara lɛ akumɔ ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nutrients away, so applying manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaves and strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut down extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: A plantain plant shares its food and water with all the shoots growing around it. Removing extra shoots leaves only the main stem and one strong follower sucker, ensuring the plant concentrates its energy on growing large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome ni he wa ni nuɔ nii lɛ pɛ. Bɔni afee ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ hiɛ kã nɔ lɛ, du plantain jwɛi wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it dangerous to bag my harvested rice or maize right after cutting it without drying it first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaawo ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni agbiko lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains moisture. If bagged immediately, heat builds up inside the sack, causing mold to grow and rot the crop, making the grain split and spoil before it can be sold.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ mli edɔ. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Dɔlɛ baabua ehe naa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ fãa ni efiteɔ dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my plantain suckers very close to each other?
ga: Ani mana yibii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: No, planting them too close together forces the trees to fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leads to thin, weak stems and small fruit bunches instead of a healthy harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai akui bibii baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ

english: How do I keep insects and weevils from eating my dried grains once they are bagged and stored?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye miŋmaa ni egbi lɛ beni mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Storing dried grain in airtight hermetic bags prevents air and moisture from entering. Without air, insect eggs cannot survive, which protects your stored grain from pests without using dangerous chemicals.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, kooloi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi. Enɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients your crops need to survive. Clearing weeds early allows young crops to establish strong roots and grow unimpeded.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko etsĩii amɛ gbɛ.

english: What happens to my crop when insects chew and create holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ kooloi bibii ŋmɔ ni amɛfee bu yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: Leaves act like solar panels that produce food for the plant using sunlight. When insects destroy the leaves, the plant cannot feed itself properly, leading to slow growth and reduced crop yields.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Beni kooloi bibii fiteɔ tsei lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii aha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why should I cover the soil around the base of my young crops with dry leaves and straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry organic leaves—called mulching—blocks harsh sunlight from drying out the earth. This keeps the soil moist for longer, prevents soil erosion, and cools the roots of young plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How deep should I dig the planting hole so that my young crops can grow strong roots?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo midumɔ bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni midumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa?

english: The proper depth depends on the crop, but generally, digging a hole wider and slightly deeper than the root ball loosens the surrounding soil, allowing delicate young roots to penetrate easily and absorb water.
ga: Bɔ ni mli kwɔ ha lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, bu ni mli kwɔ fioo ni mli kwɔ fe shishifã bɔɔlu lɛ ni atsa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ abote mli oya ni amɛmu nu.

english: What is the best way to clear thick brush and weeds from my farmland before digging planting holes?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse kɛjɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani mafo dumɔ bu?

english: Clearing brush manually and leaving cut vegetation on the ground as mulch protects topsoil from sun heat, preserves moisture, and adds organic material back into your farm over time.
ga: Brɔsh ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii ni ashiɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ mulch lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he ekoŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow if I plant them in very hard, unloosened soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa waa ni ajieee lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hard soil acts like a wall that stops roots from spreading out to find food and water. Loosening the earth when digging planting holes lets roots breathe and reach deeper nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni haaa shishifãi lɛ ashwã koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli beni atsaa dumɔ bu lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛshɛɔ niyenii mli nibii amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil in my planting hole holds too much water for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ midumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: If water collects in your dug hole and stays there for a long time after rain, the soil has poor drainage, which can suffocate roots and cause root rot.
ga: Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ bu ni atsa lɛ mli ni ehi jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha amɛgboi.

english: What should I do with the dry grass and leaves I clear off my land when digging planting holes?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mifoɔ dumɔ bu lɛ?

english: Instead of burning dry grass and leaves, place them around the base of your crops as mulch. This keeps the soil cool during hot days and reduces water loss.
ga: Yɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi ni oooshã lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Okɛwo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli, ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow when heavy rain floods the holes I dug for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ bu ni mifo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting in planting holes cuts off oxygen to the roots, preventing the plant from taking up essential soil nutrients needed to keep leaves green.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ dumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster inside the freshly dug soil of my planting holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ midumɔ bu lɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsa ehee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Digging disturbs the soil and brings buried weed seeds up closer to sunlight and rain, causing them to germinate rapidly alongside your main crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ gbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ni ehaa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ. Ha amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ masɛi.

english: Why does leaving wild brush growing right next to my crops slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi koo mli jwɛi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi.

english: Wild brush competes aggressively with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and moisture, leaving your main crops undernourished.
ga: Koo mli tsei bibii kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa otsei titrii lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni esaaa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I dig the planting holes too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ mifo dumɔ bui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight one another for the limited space, water, and soil nutrients available in that area, resulting in weaker plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ nakai he lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: How does using sharp digging tools properly help prevent damage to the topsoil layer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akafite?

english: Using clean digging tools allows you to target planting holes precisely without breaking apart the surrounding fertile topsoil crust that holds moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dɛŋdade ni he tse ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ ohiɛ fɔ̃ɔ odumɔ bu lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni efiteee shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ebɔle ehe ni haa ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I plant groundnuts on a field where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsutsu lɛ mikpaa ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have a natural ability to pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which enriches the land for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ hu yɛ bibii.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to make food, which is then sent down into the soil to grow large tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, atsuɔ amɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ bulb agboi.

english: Why should I cut away the extra young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots steal water and nutrients from the main tree, which causes the main plantain to produce much smaller bunches of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantain titri lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and drying up in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun, so they need shade crops like plantains to protect them while they are small.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, cacao tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: How is my cassava plant able to stay alive and green even when there is no rain for months?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tso lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi eŋɔli kɛji nugbɔ enɛko nyɔji babaoo po?

english: Cassava stores water and energy in its thick underground roots, allowing it to survive harsh dry spells when other crops wilt.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni mli wa mli beni tsei krokomɛi gboɔ lɛ.

english: Why do dark, rotting spots form on the bottom of my green tomatoes before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji ni egboi baa yɛ tomato eŋɔli shishi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is usually caused by irregular watering, which prevents the tomato plant from moving enough calcium into the growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni esaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tomato tso lɛ aya calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear and start eating my young maize leaves right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ba trukaa ni amɛbɔi mi-baby corn baai lɛ yeli beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs on tender green shoots right after the rains, and the eggs hatch into hungry caterpillars just as your young maize starts growing.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ be mli pɛ ni obi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops at the beginning of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep root systems already established in the soil, allowing them to absorb rainfall and nutrients much faster than young crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui bibii.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree suffers from extreme heat, lack of shade, or attacks from insect pests like mirids. Providing shade trees and protecting the farm from pests helps the flowers turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tutua tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough food and light to produce a big harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekpa nii babaoo.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly wears out specific nutrients in the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that feed on the plant's sap and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a blanket (mulch) over the soil. It shades the ground, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly so your crops stay hydrated.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Koni onibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why should I cut off extra side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Side shoots use up valuable food and water to grow extra leaves instead of fruit. Removing them directs all the plant's energy into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Lateral shoots kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni jara wa tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Tomato ni ajieɔ lɛ heɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛwo tomato ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting beans together with my maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome kɛduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Beans fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my crops remaining small and stunted even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth during rainy periods can be caused by underground root pests or sour (acidic) soil that prevents roots from taking up food. Adding organic matter or farmyard manure helps improve the soil so roots can feed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ (acidic) ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nii lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aha lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct Ghanaian sunlight burns their delicate young leaves and dries out the soil moisture quickly, causing them to wither before their roots are deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be mli ni Ghana hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ etee.

english: Removing extra suckers stops them from stealing precious water and soil nutrients from the main plant, which helps the main tree grow stronger and produce much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaaa amɛju nu ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ plantain tsei wuji babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green, grow tall, and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli, ekwɛ ni ewo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops produce plenty of green leaves but very few actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi anɔkwa ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen from the soil or fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow lush leaves instead of producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji cowpea nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ahe ŋmɔji moŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear old leaves and build wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie baai momoi lɛ? Ni ama tso tso kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes their leaves to full sunlight so they can make food for large tubers underground, while keeping the leaves off the damp ground prevents rot and leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafite kɛ baa lɛ mli helai.

english: Why is it important to prune old, dead fronds from my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ mu tsei ahe baai ni egbɔ kɛ nɔ ni egboi lɛ?

english: Trimming dead fronds allows more sunlight to reach the fruit bunches, makes harvesting much easier, and prevents pests like rodents and beetles from building nests in the tree.
ga: Baai ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ aduawai akuu lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ amɛ ŋmeii yɛ tsei amli.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my young ginger plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-ginger tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and moist while stopping weeds from growing and stealing food from your ginger roots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ o-ginger shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Too much standing water in the soil drowns cassava roots by cutting off oxygen, allowing soil fungi to infect and decay the roots before you can harvest them.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot and dry, or if the plant lacks water, because the heat causes too much stress for the plant to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu Enɛ ji akɛ, latsaa lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ babaoo baa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely and then gets soaked.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli baa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsɔ nu.

english: Why do some farmers in my community put NPK fertilizer in the soil before putting the seeds in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Applying a small amount of fertilizer before or during planting—known as basal application—gives the seed immediate access to nutrients as soon as its first tiny roots sprout, helping it grow strong right from the start.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo afata he dani odu loo yɛ be mli ni oduɔ lɛ. Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ base dressing) lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji shishifãi bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa kɛjɛɔ shishijee.

english: Is there a specific window of time after planting within which I must apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Ani be ko yɛ ni mikɛdu nii sɛɛ ni ehe baahia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Yes, young crops generally need their initial boost of nutrients within the first two weeks after planting because this is the critical period when they develop their early root systems and foliage.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, niyenii kpakpai babaoo he hiaa tsei bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ ni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eji be ni he hiaa waa kɛha amɛ koni amɛná amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ mra.

english: Is it better for me to put fertilizer in the soil before planting seeds or wait until the shoots come up?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu dumɔwui lɛ loo aaamɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Both approaches work, but putting a tiny starter dose in the soil at planting ensures the seedling never starves, whereas waiting until shoots emerge feeds the plant as it builds leaves.
ga: Gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi kɛ́ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ akaye dumɔwui lɛ. Beni emɛɛɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ baaje kpo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ebɔɔ baai lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I miss the early two-week window to apply my fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifo klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ samflɛ ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli?

english: Delaying early fertilizer can cause young plants to turn yellowish and become stunted, which permanently lowers your harvest potential because the crop missed its early growth spurt.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii mra Ebaanyɛ eha tsei bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ baaha onibii ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ aba shi kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya hiɛ oya mra.

english: How much fertilizer should I put into the planting hole so that I do not harm my seeds?
ga: Esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli koni mikafite dumɔwui lɛ?

english: You only need a very small amount—often just a bottle cap full per plant—because too much chemical fertilizer placed directly against a tender seed can burn and kill it.
ga: Nɔ ko fioo pɛ he miihia bo—bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso fɛɛ tso mli lɛ he tsɔi kɛkɛ—ejaakɛ kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo dumɔwui ni mli tse lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ ni egbe amɛ.

english: If I plant a different maize variety like Amankwaatia, do I need to change how I apply my fertilizer?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa srɔtoi tamɔ Amanquatia lɛ, ani ehe miihia ni matsake gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mikɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ?

english: The basic method of applying fertilizer remains the same across different varieties of the same crop, though early-maturing varieties might require their fertilizer slightly sooner than longer-season varieties.
ga: Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi nakai nɔŋŋ kɛha tso henɔ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ mra lɛ he baahia ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii mra fioo fe ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ moŋ.

english: Should I leave the NPK fertilizer on top of the farm soil or cover it with dirt?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mikɛ shikpɔŋ aha nɔ?

english: It is best to place the fertilizer slightly in the ground and cover it with a bit of soil so that rain does not wash it away and the sun does not evaporate the nutrients before the roots can take them in.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ ni hulu lɛ akajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.
