english: What is NPK fertilizer, and what does it actually do for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: NPK contains three essential foods plants need: Nitrogen for green leaf growth, Phosphorus for strong roots, and Potassium for general plant health and fruit development.
ga: Niyenii mli nibii etɛ ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ lɛ yɛ NPK mli: nitrogen kɛha baai eŋɔlii adalɛ, phosphorus kɛha shishifãi ni wa. kɛ potassium kɛha tsei ahewalɛ kɛ aduawai fɛɛ.

english: Do all chemical fertilizers in Ghana get applied to crops the exact same way?
ga: Ani akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ Ghana lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ?

english: Most granular fertilizers are applied near the root zone, but specific types like NPK are applied early for root growth, while others like Urea are applied later in the crop's life to boost leaves and grains.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji granular lɛ ateŋ babaoo woɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ. Shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ NPK lɛ woɔ mli mra. kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ Yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi tamɔ urea tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ wala mli koni eha tso lɛ baai kɛ ŋmaa lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Does my soil need to be wet when I apply fertilizer at planting time?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yes, soil should have good moisture when applying fertilizer because water is required to dissolve the nutrients so the plant's roots can drink them in safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo mli ejaakɛ nu he miihia koni ekɛjie niyenii mli nibii ni haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does eating food crops like rice give me the strength to work on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei aniyenii tamɔ ŋmãa ni miyeɔ lɛ haa mináa kanyamɔ ​​koni matsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice stores energy from sunlight in the form of rich carbohydrates. When you eat it, your body breaks down these carbohydrates into energy, giving you the stamina needed for hard physical work like clearing land and weeding.
ga: Omɔ toɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ yɛ carbohydrates ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli. kɛ oye nii Ogbɔmɔtso lɛ gbálaa nɛkɛ carbohydrates nɛɛ mli ni ehaa hewalɛ. Ehaa bo hewalɛ ni he hiaa bo kɛha nitsumɔ ni wa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ.

english: Is it true that the food I harvest from my field carries energy that our bodies can use?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ niyenii ni mikpaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hiɛ hewalɛ ni wɔgbɔmɔtsei lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii?

english: Yes, plants absorb nutrients and sunlight to create energy inside their grains and fruits. Eating those harvested crops transfers that stored energy directly to your body so you can perform daily tasks.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ yɛ amɛdumɔwui kɛ amɛyibii lɛ amli. Nibii ni akpa lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ yaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. koni onyɛ otsu nii daa gbi

english: What is happening when my planted rice seeds start showing tiny white shoots out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: That process is called germination. It means the seed has come alive with moisture and warmth, sprouting tiny roots and shoots that will grow into the crop you harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai gbɛ lɛ akɛ kwɛ̃mɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baa wala mli kɛtsɔ fɛ̃i kɛ dɔlɛ nɔ. shishifãi bibii kɛ ŋmeii Fɛɛ ŋmeii ni baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaakpa.

english: What does the word 'seedling' mean when officers talk about my growing crops?
ga: Mɛni ji wiemɔ ‘tso’ lɛ shishi kɛ́ onukpai miiwie ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe?

english: A seedling is simply the baby plant that comes up right after a seed sprouts. It is the young, tender plant before it grows tall and sturdy.
ga: Dumɔwu ji tso bibioo ko kɛkɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Eji tso bibioo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ dani edaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ewaa.

english: How do I know if my seeds are germinating well after planting them in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ miikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You will know they are germinating well when you see uniform, healthy green or white sprouts emerging across your farm rows within a few days of planting.
ga: Obaale akɛ amɛmiikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji ona ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo eyɛŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni odu lɛ.

english: How many weeks after my rice sprouts come up should I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Yɛ otsii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should apply your first follow-up fertilizer about two weeks after the seedlings emerge. At two weeks, the young roots are developed enough to soak up the food and grow faster.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Otsii enyɔ eho. Shishifãi bibii lɛ baaná bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my young crop plants need fertilizer early in their life?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ egbekɛbiiashi lɛ?

english: Just like growing children need good food to build strong bones, young crop seedlings need extra nutrients early on so they can build thick stems and green leaves before producing crop yields.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa gbekɛ ni miida lɛ koni enyɛ etswa wui ni wa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Dumɔwui bibii hu he miihia niyenii krokomɛi ni fata he mra. Koni enyɛ efee tsei bibii kɛ baai eŋɔli dani ewo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is Urea fertilizer, and what does it do for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji urea? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Urea is a strong fertilizer packed with nitrogen. It acts like heavy food for your crop, helping it grow rich green leaves and sturdy stems as the plant develops.
ga: Urea ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni tsii kɛha onibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa baai ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: When is the best stage to apply Urea or Ammonia to my rice field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ urea loo ammonia woɔ mi ŋmɔji amli?

english: Urea or Ammonia should be applied once the young plant has grown past the baby seedling stage and established roots, allowing it to take in the nitrogen and grow bigger.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ urea loo ammonia awo mli kɛji dumɔwui lɛ eda kɛho dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe ni amɛtswa shishifãi. Ha nitrogen lɛ abote mli ni eda.

english: Can I throw Urea fertilizer on my rice farm on the exact day I plant the seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ urea afata mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ gbi ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, you should wait until the seeds sprout into seedlings with active roots—usually around two weeks later—so the plant can actually drink up the fertilizer instead of letting it waste away in the dirt.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ dumɔwui ni shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii—bei pii lɛ, aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ—koni tsei lɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛaaha egbo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant plantains inside my coconut farm while the coconut trees are still young?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmei abɔɔ mli be mli ni ŋmei tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains between young coconut trees is a beneficial practice. Plantains grow quickly, providing shade and weed control for young coconuts while giving you food and early income while waiting for the coconuts to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ateŋ lɛ ji nifeemɔ ko ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Plantain lɛ daa oya. Kɛtsɔ hulutsoo kɛ jwɛi ni akudɔɔ ni akɛhaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shishijee shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant plantains so they do not block sunlight from my main tree crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ mi teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ koni amɛkatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ mi-tso titri lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: You should space plantains at least 3 meters away from main tree crops like coconut or cocoa. Proper spacing ensures both crops get enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without choking each other.
ga: Esa akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, okɛ otso titri, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tso lɛ akafee mitai 3. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛyeee amɛhe nɔ kunim.

english: Do young crop seedlings need shade from bigger plants to survive the sun in Ghana?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ahe miihia dumɔwui bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ Ghana hulu lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, young crop seedlings have delicate leaves and small roots that can dry out quickly under intense sunlight. Taller crops like plantains act as natural shade umbrellas to keep the young seedlings cool and soil moist.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni baanyɛ agbi oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo koni eha dumɔwui bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What short-term crops can I grow to get quick money while waiting for long-term tree crops like coconut to yield?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo manyɛ makwɛ koni maná shika oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ aba?

english: Fast-growing crops like plantain, cassava, maize, and vegetables can be harvested within months or a year. Planting them alongside slow-growing tree crops gives you immediate income to cover farm expenses and feeding.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi loo afi mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha oná shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛwo ŋmɔ kɛ niyenii he nyɔmɔwoo he nyɔmɔ.

english: Why does it take several years before my coconut trees start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mi-kokoo tso lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Coconut trees are long-term perennial crops that spend their first 3 to 5 years building strong trunk structures and deep root networks before they have enough strength and energy to produce coconuts.
ga: Kokoo tsei ji tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛheɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 lɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo kooko.

english: Why does my plantain plant die after producing only one bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gboɔ beni ewo aduawai akuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to produce fruit only once in its lifetime. After harvesting the bunch, the main stem naturally dies back, but it shoots out young offshoots called suckers at the base to grow the next harvest.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Mohu ɔ, tso bibihi nɛ a tsɛɛ mɛ ke tso ɔ jeɔ kpo ngɛ sisije konɛ a wa ngɛ ngmɔ kpami nɛ nyɛɛ se ɔ mi.

english: Will planting plantains next to coconut trees steal all the water and nutrients from the soil?
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani ŋmei tsei baaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: No, if spaced correctly, plantains and coconuts complement each other. Plantain leaves drop and decay on the ground, adding rich organic matter to the soil and reducing water evaporation during dry periods.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ plantains kɛ ŋmeii feɔ ekome. Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ. Okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. ni eha nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ aba shi

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants hold water in their fleshy stems. When rainfall stops during the dry season, the plant sheds outer leaves to conserve moisture and protect its inner core until the rainy season returns.
ga: Plantains lɛ kɛ nu toɔ amɛ tsei ni yɔɔ loo lɛ amli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbee yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛmligbɛ fã lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do I select the best plantain suckers to plant on my land for a strong harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad base. These suckers have strong root reserves and establish much faster and healthier than shoots with wide, flat leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse, ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ shishifãi ni ji enyɔ ni mli wa ni amɛfeɔ oya ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ fe tsei ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting fast-growing crops like plantain help me control weeds on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni daa oya ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maye jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Fast-growing plantains produce large, wide leaves that quickly cover the ground. This blocks sunlight from reaching the soil, preventing weeds from sprouting and saving you labor and money on weed clearing.
ga: Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ feɔ baai wuji oya ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ nitsumɔ kɛ shika ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ he lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees get easily burned by the strong hot sun. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that provide natural shade umbrellas and maintain soil moisture, protecting cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo he kɛyashi ebaatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food from the soil, resulting in weak, thin stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Yellow leaves near the base of maize usually mean the crop has used up the nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the essential food maize needs to stay green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etsu nii. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eha toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, which restores and enriches the soil after heavy-feeding crops like maize have used up the nutrients.
ga: Peanuts and Nuts Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa eyaa hiɛ beni kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, efite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni onyɛ okɛ nu awo mli fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight for energy. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping tubers grow bigger underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark and rotten while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni miyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot get enough water regularly or lacks calcium while the fruit is forming fast during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa loo amɛbɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars hiding and eating deep inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that prefers the tender inner leaves of young maize. If left unchecked, they destroy the central growing point of the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ shweremɔ he lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and yield small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's roots, effectively starving your plants so they cannot develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ aahu akɛ enyɛɛɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months, its lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop, and the soil around the base starts cracking as the roots swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛji tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: I want to start growing plantain on my farm in the Central Region, but I hear there are different types. How do I know which plantain variety is best for me to plant?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi plantains dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ kpokpaa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi minu akɛ henɔi srɔtoi babaoo yɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male plantains ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu?

english: Different plantain varieties serve different market needs. For instance, False Horn ('Apantu') produces larger individual fruits that are preferred for roasting, while French plantain ('Apem') yields bunches with many smaller fruits ideal for boiling. You should choose based on what buyers in your local market prefer to purchase.
ga: Plantain henɔi srɔtoi tsuɔ jarayeli hiamɔ nii srɔtoi ahe nii. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, False Horn (‘Apantu’) lɛ woɔ aduawai aŋkroaŋkroi wuji ni sa kɛha shãa. yɛ be mli ni French plantain (‘Apem’) lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni sa kɛha ŋmɔlɔ. Esa akɛ odamɔ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ taoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ ohala.

english: What are these small side shoots coming out around the base of my plantain tree, and what should I do with them?
ga: Nɛkɛ tsei bibii nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he fɛɛ he. Mɛni ji mi plantain lɛ shishitoo? Ni mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, which grow into new plantain plants. If you leave too many suckers around one parent tree, they will compete for nutrients and light, causing smaller fruit bunches; you should cut off the extra suckers and leave only one or two strong ones.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. ni daa ni etsɔɔ dumɔwui heei Kɛji oshi ŋmeii ebɔle Tso nyɛ kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How long does a plantain tree usually take from the time I plant it until the bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni miduɔ plantain ŋmɔ ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa?

english: In southern regions like Gomoa, a plantain tree generally takes about 9 to 12 months to produce a flower bunch, and another 3 to 4 months for the fruit to fully mature and fill out for harvest.
ga: Yɛ kooyigbɛ hei tamɔ Gomoa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii, ni amɛheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi hu dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛyiɔ obɔ kɛkpamɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks or stakes to climb on while they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ loo tso ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out in the sunlight to make food. When the vine climbs high and catches plenty of light, the plant sends more energy down into the ground, growing bigger and healthier tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Beni wain tso lɛ kwɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni enine shɛɔ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ. Tsei tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why do I need to make big soil mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani adu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Mounding creates deep, loose soil that allows the young yam tubers to expand downward without pushing against hard earth. Loose soil also improves drainage so rain can soak through without causing the tuber to rot underground.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ hu haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ anyɛ abote mli ni efiteee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting leaves or turning soft when I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ loo efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ mikpa lɛ?

english: Yams naturally want to break dormancy and grow into new plants after resting. Storing your yams off the ground in a cool, well-ventilated yam barn protected from direct sunlight will delay sprouting and keep the tubers fresh longer.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potatoes aku amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe lɛ mli ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tsei heei beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe sɛɛ. Kɛ sweet potato ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo ni ebaaha bulb lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I grow yams and plantains together on the same piece of land without them damaging each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potatoes kɛ plantains yɛ he kome ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting yams and plantains together works well because plantains grow tall and offer light shade, while yams utilize the space below. Just ensure you space them properly so both crops get enough sunlight and nutrients from the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu sweet potatoes kɛ plantains yɛ he kome lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ plantains lɛ daa ni ehaa hulutsoo be fioo baa. yɛ be mli ni sweet potatoes heɔ he ko yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ akɛ oto he lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do the dry seasons in southern Ghana affect my plantain trees, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ saa mi-plantain lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu plantains nɛɛ ahe?

english: During dry spells, plantain trees lose water quickly through their large leaves, which slows down growth and shrinks fruit size. Covering the soil around the base of the tree with dried leaves or grass (mulching) helps trap soil moisture and protects the roots from heat.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai wuji anɔ. Enɛ baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ afee bibioo. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves can naturally happen as older leaves age, but if many turn yellow quickly, it usually means the plant lacks water or nutrients like nitrogen. Clearing nearby weeds and adding manure or fertilizer around the base will help keep leaves green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni baai lɛ daraa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is losing its strength and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Soil losing its richness shows in crop behavior: plants stay small, stems remain thin, and leaves look pale or yellowish instead of dark green. Adding compost, animal manure, or recommended fertilizers will restore the food your crops need to grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ jieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ajeŋba mli: Tsei lɛ feɔ bibii. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Kɛjɛ be mli ni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their tender leaves get scorched by intense sun. Leaving some tall trees or planting plantains around them creates a cool protective canopy that holds moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ naa hulu la ni naa wa waa. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha ehi shi loo dumɔ dumɔwui ebɔle he. Ehaa hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to save water. It is a natural survival trick to prevent moisture from evaporating from the leaves, and fresh new leaves will sprout quickly as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni nu akafite. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to build green foliage. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves up to the new growth, showing that the soil needs more fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli kɛyaa dalɛ hee mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers dry up and fall off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Without steady moisture and moderate heat, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ ahaaa tsei lɛ nu yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni tamɔ ekome kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa bɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the green leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the undersides of leaves, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by insects. Treating the farm early for pests stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, baai lɛ efoŋ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in very wet and humid weather. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, which stops the fungal spores from growing on your pods.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa fungal spores lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ o-pods lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry grass and fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni jwɛi gboi kɛ baai ni egbee shi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It stops the strong sun from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, reduces weeds, and breaks down into organic food for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ baa shi, ni efiteɔ niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli kɛhaa onibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my yams under the ground are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines growing above ground start turning yellow and drying up naturally. This show that the plant has stopped growing leaves and has stored all its energy into the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ ebaa lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow before the bunch is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and very heavy stems, making them top-heavy when bearing fruit. Propping up the bearing stems with sturdy bamboo poles or wooden stakes gives them extra support against strong winds until harvest.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu tsii waa. Ehaa efeɔ tsii kɛji ewo yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa to bearing stems lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha abu he babaoo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans belong to a family of plants that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, providing free natural food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans fata tsei ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from surrounding trees or plantains to preserve soil moisture and protect their delicate leaves from burning until they are mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei loo tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ adɛŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, so applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmei aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm as my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ni miduɔ nii titri lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside main crops naturally improves soil fertility, helping your other plants grow bigger and healthier.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua tsei krokomɛi Ogbɔmɔtso lɛ daa ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa he ni agbele lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground on sticks exposes them to maximum sunlight. Sunlight gives the leaves energy to produce food, which is then sent down into the soil to grow larger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso wo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots compete heavily for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving them enough space allows the underground tubers room to expand and grow thick.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ efee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tuber tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does leaving dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my crops help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less often, and prevents weeds from taking over your plot.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes deep holes in the center leaves of my young maize, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl of the plant. Checking your field early and spraying with recommended biological treatments, like neem extract or approved pesticides, protects your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei ahe ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra. ni okɛ tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant all my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu aduawai dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell known as a 'false start.' If you plant immediately, seeds may sprout and then dry up and die before the main rains establish; it is safer to wait for consistent rain before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be kuku ni ale lɛ akɛ ‘apasa shishijee’ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ anɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plants experience extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops nearby during high heat helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to give a low yield even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your plant's root zone. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment needed to produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do my crops need air to breathe at night just like animals do?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛmu gbɛkɛ tamɔ bɔ ni kooloi feɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, crops need oxygen at night just like animals. During the day, plants use sunlight to make food and release oxygen, but at night, they consume oxygen from the air and soil to break down that food and grow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia oxygen gbɛkɛ tamɔ kooloi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii ni amɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Shi gbɛkɛ Tsei kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala niyenii ni amɛdara.

english: Why do the leaves of some of my crops close up or droop when night falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi ŋmɛɔ loo amɛgbeeɔ shi gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Many plants fold their leaves at night to conserve moisture and protect themselves from cooler night temperatures, as they do not need to catch sunlight until the morning.
ga: Tsei babaoo shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ he. Ejaakɛ ehe ehiaaa ni hulu la ashɛ nɔ kɛyashi leebi.

english: Why do my crops look weak and yellow when planted too close together in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Overcrowded crops trap stagnant air and block fresh airflow around their leaves. Without adequate air movement, plants struggle to exchange gases properly, leading to weak and yellowing growth.
ga: Tsei ni eyimɔ obɔbɔ tsɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekã shi lɛ ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei lɛ baaná naagba yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsakemɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔŋ baa.

english: Why do my crops die when water sits on the field for too long after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots require oxygen from air pockets in the soil to survive. When water sits on the field for days, it fills those air pockets and suffocates the roots because they cannot get oxygen.
ga: Tso shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo Nu lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Why is it helpful to loosen the soil around my crops with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ ebuaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil creates small spaces for air and oxygen to reach the roots. When roots have enough air in the soil, they absorb water and nutrients much more effectively.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hei bibii baa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ ná kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does heavy rainfall during the night affect my crops differently than daytime rain?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbɛkɛ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shwane mli lɛ?

english: At night, soil evaporation is low and plants are not actively using sun energy. Heavy night rain can waterlog the ground faster, temporarily blocking air spaces and limiting oxygen to the roots.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ faaa kwraa. Ni tsei kɛ hulu hewalɛ tsuuu nii babaoo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbɛkɛ baanyɛ aha nu lɛ afee oya. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ lɛ naa be kukuoo ko. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa

english: Can flooded crops survive longer if the floodwater is moving instead of standing still?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu afua lɛ ewo mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji nu afua lɛ tsi ehe moŋ fe ni eeehi shi diŋŋ?

english: Yes, moving water carries dissolved oxygen to the roots, whereas stagnant water quickly loses oxygen. Moving water gives crop roots a better chance of surviving flooding for a short time.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ baa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Nu lɛ nyiɛmɔ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nu afua mli yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Do my crops actually do their growing during the day or at night?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Crops gather energy and make food during the day using sunlight, but much of their actual cellular growth happens at night when they use oxygen to convert that stored food into growth.
ga: Tsei buaa hewalɛ naa ni amɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ gbi lɛ mli kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Shi wala yibii lɛ adalɛ diɛŋtsɛ Enɛ baa mli babaoo gbɛkɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsake niyenii ni ato lɛ amɛwo dalɛ mli lɛ.

english: Will putting bright streetlights or security lights near my fields at night help my crops grow faster?
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kanei ni kpɛɔ lɛ ni mikɛaawo mli Aloo shweshweeshwefeemɔ kanei ni miyɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ ahe gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: No, crops need continuous dark hours at night to rest and process their day's energy. Constant light disrupts their natural biological clock and can delay flowering and fruiting.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia gbɛkɛ be ni yaa nɔ gbɛkɛ koni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsu amɛ daa gbi hewalɛ he nii. La ni tsoɔ daa lɛ gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo asɛɛ afo.

english: Why do my young seedlings bend towards the sun during the morning hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Seedlings contain natural growth hormones that make them stretch toward light. Bending toward the morning sun allows them to capture the maximum light needed to start making food for the day.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni haa mɔ daa lɛ yɛ dumɔwui amli ni haa amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa la mli. Kɛ́ amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtee leebi hulu lɛ he lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛje niyenii homɔ shishi kɛha gbi lɛ.

english: How often should I apply chemical treatments or fertilizers to my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Most routine crop applications are done once a month, but if your field is facing a severe pest outbreak or heavy disease, you may need to apply treatments every two weeks until the plants recover.
ga: Aduɔ nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shikome yɛ nyɔŋ mli. Shi kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa loo helai ni naa wa miikpe hu? Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni oya nɔ otsa lɛ daa otsii enyɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if September or October is the right time to start planting my second-season crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji September loo October ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli tsei adumɔ shishi?

english: In Ghana, the minor rainy season typically begins around September and October. You should plant as soon as the rains become steady so the soil has enough moisture for seeds to germinate and grow.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ September kɛ October mli. Esa akɛ odu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be pɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and looking sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are suffering from too much water, drought, or a fungal disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo, hɔmɔ, loo tsɛŋemɔ hela.

english: What should I do to help my crops recover if a disease sets back their growth for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni maye mabua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛji hela haaa amɛkwɛ̃ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: First, clear out the heavily infected leaves or plants, apply the recommended fungicide or pesticide, and then give the surviving crops a light dose of nitrogen fertilizer to encourage new, healthy leaves.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, jiemɔ baai loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ. Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii. No sɛɛ lɛ, ha tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko koni ewo baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Is it good practice to mix sand into my farm soil or with my chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani ŋã ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa?

english: Adding sand to heavy clay soil helps loosen it so roots can spread and water can drain, while mixing sand with fine fertilizer granules helps you spread the fertilizer evenly across your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã fata shikpɔŋ ni mli wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋã ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ futu mli lɛ baaye abua bo ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aja oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Can I mix different farm chemicals and fertilizers together before spraying my crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsofai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli lɛ afutu. amɛfee ekome dani amɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Not all farm chemicals can be mixed together safely. Combining incompatible chemicals can burn your crop leaves or stop the chemicals from working, so always ask an extension officer before mixing them.
ga: Jeee tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni abaanyɛ afutu mli shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã otso lɛ baai lɛ loo eha tsofai lɛ akatsu nii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ obi mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛfutu.

english: How do I properly care for young seedlings in the nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings in a nursery need light shade from the strong sun, regular morning watering, and protection from harsh winds so their roots become strong enough for transplanting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he hulutsoo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa leebi kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by transplant shock when roots are damaged or exposed to hot afternoon sun. You can prevent this by transplanting late in the evening or on a cloudy day and watering immediately.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ mli shoofeemɔ beni shishifãi lɛ efite loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ loo gbi ni atatu ewo nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni awo mli nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the fertilizer I put in my soil?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away topsoil and leach fertilizer deep below the root level where crops cannot reach it, which is why applying smaller amounts of fertilizer more frequently works better during rainy periods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ ni efɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛya shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni haa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tsuɔ nii. shii abɔ, no hewɔ lɛ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers without producing any food when the weather changes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shĩɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwooo niyenii be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, sudden droughts, or unexpected heavy rains cause stress to the plant, making it shed its flowers to save energy for survival rather than producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa Loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why is it important for me to measure proper distance between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu gbɛ ni sa ni ka miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and leaves, leading to bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, abaakpa nibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my soil is fertile enough before I clear new land to expand my crop field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ dani majie shikpɔŋ hee koni mikɛgbala midumɔ nii lɛ amli?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels crumbly rather than hard, stays moist after rain, and contains earthworms. If wild plants and grass grow thick and dark green on the uncultivated land, it is a good sign the soil has strong nutrients for farming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe nɔ ni wa. Moisturize yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji koo mli tsei kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nɔ nii nɔ. Eji okadi kpakpa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If my farm is near a water source, can I water my vegetable crops at any time during the day?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko Ani manyɛ mawo mi tsei lɛ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening. Watering in the heat of the afternoon causes the water to evaporate quickly before roots can drink it, and hot wet leaves can encourage plant diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni baai ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ helai aba tsei anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when water sits on my field for too many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu ta miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water stays on the farm without draining away, it suffocates the roots, preventing them from taking up soil nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Etsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that target that crop to multiply. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant fast-growing crops like maize together on the same land with slow-growing crops like cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Maize grows tall and can be harvested quickly within a few months, leaving the cassava behind to take over the space and soil nutrients for the rest of its longer growing cycle.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Abɛi daa ni abaanyɛ akpa oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ he ko kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni eshwɛ ni ekɛbaa lɛ mli.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh weather and steal water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops do not starve.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ akaye onibii bibii lɛ.

english: Should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves during the hot season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Ani okɛ jwɛi loo baai duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Yes, this is called mulching. Dry grass acts as a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, prevents weeds from sprouting, and turns into natural manure as it breaks down.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji efite

english: Why do pests still appear on my crops even though I keep my farm plot clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli he tseɔ moŋ?

english: Insects and crop diseases easily travel through the wind, soil, or water from neighboring fields. Managing pests requires regular inspection of plant stems and under leaves, and coordinating timing with nearby farmers.
ga: Kplukai kɛ tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, shikpɔŋ loo nu mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ biɔ ni akwɛ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa. ni okɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ato be he gbɛjianɔ

english: Why do my crops produce lots of green leaves but very few fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi aduawai loo ŋmaa fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: This often happens when plants get too much nitrogen nutrient (like from animal dung or nitrogen fertilizer) without enough phosphorus and potassium. Too much nitrogen makes the crop focus only on growing leaves instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ (tamɔ ni jɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii amli) ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baa lɛ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Can I use human medicines or painkillers to cure diseases on my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ adesa tsofa loo tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ atsa helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: No, human medicines are designed specifically for human bodies, not plant biology. Using them on crops can scorch plant leaves, leave harmful chemical residues on your produce, and damage the soil without fixing the plant disease.
ga: Dabi, afee adesai tsofai pɔtɛɛ aha adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ. Jeee tsei ahe nilee ni. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. Tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni ashiɔ yɛ onibii amli ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni eyeee ebuaaa ni etsaa tsei ahelai.

english: Why did my crops burn and wither after I mixed two different pest medicines together in my sprayer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi enyɔ efutu mli yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Mixing different farm chemicals without checking if they go together can cause a harsh chemical reaction. This creates toxic mixtures that burn plant leaves, ruin the chemicals' power to kill pests, and waste your money.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ kɛji amɛkɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee loo amɛkpãaa gbee lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛha tsofafeemɔ ni mli wa aba. Enɛ haa tsofa ni yɔɔ gbeyei futuɔ ni baashã tso lɛ baai lɛ. Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni tsofai yɔɔ ni amɛkɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. kɛ oshika ni ofiteɔ

english: Can I spray a chemical meant for soil root treatments directly onto my crop leaves?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa shishifãi lɛ afɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, chemicals formulated for soil drenching are meant to be absorbed by roots. Spraying them directly on leaves can scorch the tender foliage and will not protect the crop as intended.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni afee kɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã baai bibii lɛ ni ekɛbuuu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe bɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ.

english: Will doubling the amount of chemical in my spraying tank kill farm pests faster?
ga: Ani tsofai ni yɔɔ mi-spray tanki lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛwo mli lɛ toi enyɔ lɛ baagbe ŋmɔ mli kooloi oya?

english: No, putting too much chemical in your sprayer damages your crops by scorching leaves, pollutes the soil, wastes money, and causes pests to build immunity to the chemical over time.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni okɛwoɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ baafite onibii kɛtsɔ baai ni ashãa lɛ nɔ. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, efiteɔ shika, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if an agrochemical sold in my local market is fake or dangerous for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji agrochemicals ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ mimaŋ jarayelihe lɛ ji amale loo eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Always look for an official regulatory seal (like EPA Ghana), an unbroken container seal, clear expiration dates, and printed instructions. Avoid buying unlabelled liquids sold in reused plastic drinking bottles.
ga: Taomɔ mlai ahe naatsii be fɛɛ be (nɔkwɛmɔnɔ EPA Ghana), tsɛnsi mli naatsii ni efiteee. gbi ni esa akɛ ekɛtsu nii lɛ mli faŋŋ kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni akala Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni aŋmalako nɔ ko nɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ plastic nu tsɛnsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ hemɔ he.

english: Why shouldn't I spray pest medicine on my crops during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Hot afternoon heat causes water in the spray to evaporate quickly, leaving high concentrations of chemicals that burn spots into leaves. High heat can also break down the active ingredients, making the treatment ineffective.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli la ni tsoɔ lɛ ha nu ni yɔɔ spray lɛ mli lɛ shwie oya. Eshiɔ tsofai ni fa babaoo ni baaha shãa okadii aba baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha nibii ni tsuɔ nii lɛ akumɔ. ni haa tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are insects still eating my crop leaves even after I sprayed them with pest medicine yesterday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ nyɛ moŋ?

english: Some chemicals take a few days to work through the insect's stomach, while others only kill pests that are touched directly during spraying. If you used the wrong chemical for that specific pest, it will also fail to work.
ga: Tsofai komɛi heɔ gbii fioo dani amɛtsɔɔ kooloo lɛ musu mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai komɛi baagbe kooloi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Kɛ okɛ tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii yɛ nakai tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ nɔ lɛ, Etsuuu nii hu.

english: Why shouldn't I spray medicine on my crops when it looks like rain is coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off crop leaves before the plant or pests can absorb it. This wastes your medicine and causes chemical runoff that can contaminate nearby streams and drinking water.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ahe dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ otsofai lɛ ni ehaa tsofai ni baanyɛ afite faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ nu ni anuɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even when I don't see any pests on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are not always caused by insects. They can mean your crops are missing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, getting too much water, or suffering from a fungal disease in the roots.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be kooloi ji mɛi ni kɛ baai ŋmɔŋ baa. Enɛɛmɛi baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni amɛmiiná nu babaoo tsɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying my vegetables before I can harvest and sell them at the market?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa shwie aduawai anɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani akpa amɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Every farm chemical has a required waiting period called the Pre-Harvest Interval, usually between 3 to 14 days. Waiting allows chemical residues to break down so your produce is safe for families to eat.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɛɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ be ni tsɔ ŋmaakpamɔ hiɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 teŋ. Mɛɛmɔ haa tsofa ni eshwɛ lɛ fiteɔ koni eha onibii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oweku lɛ ni amɛye.

english: How can I tell if my land is suitable for starting a cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ shishijee?

english: Good cocoa land needs deep, dark soil that drains water easily so the roots do not rot. It also requires an area with steady rainfall and protection from harsh dry winds.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ oya. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akafite Ehe miihia hu ni ená he ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be, ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why is it important to have an extension officer inspect my farmland before I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni extension officer ko akwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ?

english: An officer checks soil depth, drainage, and nutrient health to make sure you do not waste money and labor planting crops on land where they will fail to grow well.
ga: Nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii hewalɛ. Enɛ haaa ofite shika kɛ nitsumɔ ni okɛduɔ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that lose moisture rapidly in open sun. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. ni shwieɔ nu oya kɛji amɛyɔɔ kpo nɔ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛtoɔ shi lɛ.

english: How do temporary shade crops like plantains help my main farm crops grow?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade crops act as natural umbrellas that cool the soil, prevent moisture from evaporating too quickly, and shield young seedlings from heavy winds and direct sun heat.
ga: Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. ni ebu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning black and rotting before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, overly damp, and excessively shaded environments. Clearing excess weeds and pruning trees lets sunlight in to reduce fungal growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ tsɔ, edɔ, kɛ hulutsoo tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai adalɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when trees lack sufficient water or nutrients, or when small sucking insects damage the blossoms before tiny pods can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is overly waterlogged and suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: During Harmattan, dry air and hot winds cause trees to drop leaves to save water. Without adequate shade or soil moisture, young trees can dry out completely.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, tsei bibii baanyɛ agbi kwraa.

english: What happens to my yield if I plant my crops too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planted too closely, crops compete fiercely for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems, small harvests, and a higher risk of spreading diseases.
ga: planted too close Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji tsei bibii Nikpamɔ lɛ faaa. ni oshara babaoo yɛ akɛ helai baagbɛ ashwã

english: Why should I cut off side branches and excess leaves from my full-grown cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to airflow and sunlight, which prevents humidity-loving diseases and allows the tree to focus its energy on producing bigger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ he tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la nyɛɔ eshɛɔ tso lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ anaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmɔtɔi wuji afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow while the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and tall. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing new shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa ŋmeii heei adalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the plant's sap. Spraying the leaves with a mild neem oil mixture or soapy water helps clear these pests so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Akɛ neem fɔ ni mli ejɔ ni akɛfutuɔ baai lɛ baashwie nɔ. Aloo nu ni akɛ samla ewo mli lɛ baaye abua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves close up tightly at night or when it gets very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛkɛ loo be mli ni amɛgbi waa lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants fold their leaves to reduce water loss from heat and wind. It is a natural self-defense behavior that helps the plant save moisture until conditions improve.
ga: Peanut tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu subaŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam vines produce bigger tubers when their leaves are lifted into direct sunlight to make food. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases from damaging the crop.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ awó amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtee hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhoo nii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry up and fall off before they can form fruit. Providing light shade, mulching the base of the plants, and watering regularly keeps the plants cool enough to hold their blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani aduawai baa. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse ha, ni akɛha tso lɛ shishi, kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni efɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall with thick leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing big leaves and stems instead of flowers and fruit. Using a balanced fertilizer with higher phosphorus encourages the plant to make more okra pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baa kɛ tsei agboi ni amɛduɔ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ ahe nii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo okra ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my watermelons crack open on the field right before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons split when they take in a sudden, large amount of water after a long dry spell. The inside grows faster than the skin can stretch, so watering evenly throughout the growing season prevents this bursting.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu babaoo mli trukaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo amɛmli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkatswa.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot under the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater collects in the soil without proper drainage, it suffocates the roots and allows rotting fungi to attack them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua amɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests when I plant maize on the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the earth. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil richness naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baatsake ŋmãa Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛnamɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea will restore the green color and help produce larger corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans do the opposite—they pull nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the earth. Rotating crops this way naturally restores soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii feɔ nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ nakai. Egbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ otsake ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the bare soil around their crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket, keeping the soil cool under the strong sun, holding in water longer, and blocking weeds from growing and stealing nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny green droppings inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing center of the plant and chew the leaves from the inside out. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts early in the morning can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ he okadi, ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli ni ekɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kpo lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes in Ghana is often caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Spraying with organic neem oil solutions and clearing nearby weeds where whiteflies hide helps protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ Ghana lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem mu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ ni ogbe jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ he ni whiteflies kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them and cannot drain away, which creates an environment for fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excessive rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Ehaa shihilɛ baa shi kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy and maintains soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋwɛitsu lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots grow around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ?
