english: Allowing too many suckers to grow at once causes them to compete with the main tree for plant food and water, leading to thin stems and small bunches. Keeping only three shoots (a main plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot) ensures strong yields.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛɔ ŋmeii bibii tsɔ gbɛ ni amɛdaraa shikome lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ewoɔ tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii 3 pɛ to (ŋmei titri, ŋmeii 1 ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ ŋmeii bibii 1) lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa aba.

english: Why do I need to put wooden tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to manufacture energy to expand the underground tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ŋmeii helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Water your pepper plants regularly during dry spells and ensure the soil stays moist to help flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni bɛ hewɔ. Ha o-pepper tsei lɛ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Ni kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I nurse my crop seeds and transplant them instead of just scattering them directly on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli dumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛwo he kroko lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Nursing seeds in a protected bed helps young seedlings grow strong without competing with weeds or harsh sunlight. Transplanting healthy seedlings later gives them better spacing and survival rates than scattering (broadcasting) seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ saatso ni abuɔ he lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei bibii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi loo hulu la ni naa wa lɛ akaŋ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baaha gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ wala ni hi jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa. (gbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã)

english: What is the difference between broadcasting seeds and transplanting seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Broadcasting means scattering seeds across the soil by hand, which is quick but leads to crowded plants. Transplanting means growing seeds in a nursery first and placing selected healthy seedlings into neat, well-spaced rows in the main field.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo tsɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ, ni yaa oya shi ehaa tsei lɛ eyiɔ shi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaadu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. ni okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ahala lɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do transplanted crops often grow stronger than crops planted straight from seed into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛdara waa fe tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtee saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Transplanting gives seedlings a protected start in a controlled nursery with plenty of care, water, and rich soil, allowing them to build strong roots before facing the tougher conditions of the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ haa anyɛɔ abuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmɔ ni akudɔ lɛ mli kɛ hiɛdɔɔ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa dani amɛkɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kpeɔ.

english: Why is it recommended that I keep my farm plot small if I want to produce high-quality crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mafee miŋmɔ lɛ he bibioo kɛji miisumɔ ni mawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Smaller farm plots are much easier to inspect, weed, water, and care for properly. When you restrict your farm size to what you can handle, you can maintain high quality standards across all your crops.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ akwɛɔ ŋmɔ bibii amli, jwɛi, nu kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ ba shi kɛyashɛ he ko ni obaanyɛ okwɛ nɔ lɛ, Obaanyɛ okwɛ shishitoo mlai ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: How does trying to farm a very large piece of land affect the quality of my produce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mibɔɔ koni matsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni da waa nɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: When a farm area is too large for the available labor, crops receive less individual attention, leading to more pest damage, unchecked weeds, and an uneven, lower-quality harvest.
ga: Beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli kpokpaa lɛ da tsɔ kɛha nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaná hiɛdɔɔ fioo. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa. jwɛi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmaa ni ehiii kɛ ŋmaa ni akpaaa be fɛɛ be.

english: If I join a farming association, why might they set limits on how much land each member can plant?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ mihe wo okwaayeli kuu lɛ mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ amɛtoɔ he ni emlinyo lɛ mlinyo fɛɛ kuu baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ he husu?

english: Farming groups often limit individual plot sizes so every farmer can properly manage their field, ensuring that all produce collected together meets the strict quality levels required by buyers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi akui tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko dalɛ naa bɔni afee ni okwaafonyo fɛɛ okwaafonyo anyɛ akwɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni akwɛ akɛ nibii fɛɛ ni abua naa lɛ ashɛ shishitoo mlai ni mli wa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some plants on my farm have a different leaf color compared to the rest of the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baabii ahe sui srɔtoi yɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Differences in crop color across a field can happen because those specific plants are a different seed variety, were planted on a different date, or are receiving different amounts of soil nutrients.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ahe su mli yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ aba ejaakɛ nakai tsei pɔtɛɛi lɛ yɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi. ni adu yɛ gbii srɔtoi anɔ loo nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii srɔtoi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Does a unique color on my crop's leaves mean the plant is diseased?
ga: Ani su krɛdɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela emɔ tso lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. A unique color can simply mean that particular crop was transplanted at a different time or comes from a different variety, though severe pale or spotty colors can indicate nutrient needs or pests.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Su ni yɔɔ srɔto baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be kroko mli loo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi amli. Shi kɛlɛ, su ni mli tse loo nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiamɔ nii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: How can I tell if my planted crops are growing uniformly across my entire field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitsei lɛ miida pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Uniform crops will generally have similar height, leaf color, and growth speed. If you spot patches with different colors or sizes, it usually points to differences in planting dates, watering, or soil richness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ekome lɛ alɛɛmɔ, amɛbaai ahe sui, kɛ amɛdalɛ oyaiyeli lɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Kɛji ona hei ni sui loo amɛdalɛi srɔtoi yɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Etsɔɔ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii, nu ni akɛhaa, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Is it safe to apply farm chemicals to my young crops while they are still in the nursing stage?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ nu mli lolo lɛ?

english: Young nursery plants are delicate, so chemicals should be used very carefully and only in small, correct doses. Overusing chemicals on young seedlings can burn their leaves and destroy the crop before it gets transplanted.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsofai atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa pɛ mli. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani abaanyɛ adu amɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly and look weak during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism against severe heat and sunshine. When temperatures are high, the plant rolls its leaves inward to reduce surface area, conserve water, and avoid drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la he. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi, amɛbu nu he, ni amɛtsi baa lɛ naa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do the tips of my yam leaves turn brown and dry even when it rains once a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ ayiteŋ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ shikome yɛ otsi mli po lɛ?

english: Light or infrequent rains only wet the top layer of soil without reaching the deep root system of yam plants. When roots do not get enough moisture deep underground, the leaf edges scorch and turn dry from severe thirst.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo loo ni baaa shii abɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshɛɛɛ sweet potato tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kumai ni naa wa hewɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow even after I put fertilizer around the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Namɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle tso lɛ he?

english: Crops cannot absorb fertilizer if the soil is too dry or if the root system is damaged. Without moisture in the soil to dissolve the nutrients, the plant cannot feed on the fertilizer you applied.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo shishifãi lɛ efite. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are weeds growing very strong in my farm while my crop stays small and pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and soil nutrients much faster than young crop plants. If weeds are not cleared early, they starve your crops of the food they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ jɛmɛ mra lɛ, Amɛbaaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my newly planted tomato seedlings rot at the base and fall over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: This is a fungal issue called damping-off, usually caused by wet soil and poor drainage. Excess moisture rots the soft stems of young seedlings before their roots can establish strong growth.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmeii ahe naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa. Fɛ̃i babaoo baaha tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agboi dani shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Why do my bean seeds sprout easily but stop growing completely after two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya shi ekpaa dalɛ kwraa yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Early sprouts grow using energy stored inside the seed itself. Once that initial energy is used up after two weeks, the plant relies entirely on soil nutrients and sunlight, so poor soil stops its growth.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛdaraa. Beni shishijee hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ Tsei lɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ kwraa. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ haaa dalɛ akpa.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves look scorched and burnt around the edges during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni eshã yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia to protect them, intense heat burns the young leaves and damages the tree.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo gliricidia ni buɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni efite tso lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani eyibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save energy when conditions are difficult.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli wa.

english: Why did my green eggplant plant wilt completely and die in just one day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-eggplant lɛ shwie shi ni egbo yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting while leaves are still green is caused by bacterial wilt. Bacteria block the internal tubes that carry water from the roots to the leaves, causing the entire plant to collapse quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ trukaa be mli ni baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ baa. Muawai tsiɔ mligbɛ tsɔnei ni kɛ nu yaa kɛjɛɔ shishifãi amli kɛyaa baai amli lɛ anaa. ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbee shi oya

english: Why have my plantain leaves turned pale green and the trunk stopped growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Stunted plantain growth is often caused by tiny root pests called nematodes. They damage the root system underground, preventing the plant from pulling food and water from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni yeɔ dwarf plantains lɛ adalɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes Amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct heat from the sun. Large shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa roots can survive and grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara waa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that heavy rains have washed the plant food out of the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close to each other on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which makes all the plants grow thin and yield fewer fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ekome lɛ?

english: Beans take natural nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize and helps both crops produce a better harvest.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa kpakpa.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they face extreme sun heat, dry spells, or irregular watering, as the plant tries to conserve energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why are black spots appearing on my pepper fruits and turning them soft and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Black rotting spots are usually caused by fungal diseases that spread fast during warm, wet weather when water splashes dirty soil onto the lower fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Beni nu lɛ shwieɔ muji ni he tseee lɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are ready under the ground if I cannot see them?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji onaaa amɛ?

english: Cassava plants show they are mature when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the lower stems become thick and woody.
ga: Cassava tso tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest grow weaker than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor over generations and may carry diseases from the previous season, whereas fresh certified seeds are bred specifically to resist pests and yield more.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and stronger than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that adapt easily to hard conditions, allowing them to steal water and food from the soil faster than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli oya. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe shia tsei.

english: How can I tell the exact time my yam tubers are fully mature for digging up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ edara kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yams are mature and ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above the ground completely dry up and turn brown at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi kwraa ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient responsible for green leaves and strong stems. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eshishifãi lɛ hu waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves dry up and turn brown when there is direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full sun. They need shade from larger plants, like plantains or shade trees, to keep cool and hold moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni eha fɛ̃i ahi shi ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks water. The plant discards the flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying due to heat stress.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ mli baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the tight inner leaves of young maize. Checking your farm early and using recommended neem treatments or safe pesticides can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo ŋmeii bibii amli baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem tsofai ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like mites or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents them from spreading plant diseases that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkagbɛɔ tsei ahe helai ni haaa amɛdara lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants produce very small tubers even when the shoots look big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ dara moŋ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil so the roots can easily push outward and swell. If the ground is too hard, compacted, or waterlogged, the roots stay thin even if the stems above ground grow large.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia Cassava. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ ni amɛfuɔ oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yitso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ da po.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, light, and water. Leaving only two or three healthy suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, la, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Weed seeds sit buried in the dirt for long periods. When you clear the top soil and expose it to sunlight and rain, those hidden seeds wake up and sprout rapidly before your main crop can block the light.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Beni ojieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni okɛwoɔ hulu kɛ nugbɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ teɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to put into 50kg bags without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo 50kg kotoku mli ni egbooo?

english: Maize is ready for bagging when a kernel makes a sharp cracking sound when you bite it and doesn't leave a dent. Proper drying prevents mold and insects from destroying your grain inside the storage bag.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛbaawo kotoku mli kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ amɔ amɛ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my crops so rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a moderate rain, and gently cover it with dirt. Avoid putting fertilizer down right before a heavy downpour, which sweeps the nutrients off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ, ni okɛ sũ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ blɛoo. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food that keeps leaves green and strong. It can also happen when there is too much water sitting around the roots, preventing them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashɛ he ni ehaa mɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Do not plant after the very first shower because the soil is still hot and dry underneath. Wait until you get two or three steady days of rain that soak deep into the soil so your seeds have enough moisture to germinate and survive.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nu lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbi yɛ shishi. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ odumɔwui lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long in heavy or flat soil. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why should I bother planting my crops in straight lines instead of scattering seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe woɔ haomɔ mli akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every plant its own clear space to get sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also leaves clear pathways for you to walk, remove weeds, and apply fertilizer without stepping on your crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ hu yɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ, okɛ jwɛi awo mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okɛ onaji akashɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa tree flowers to fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed, usually from a lack of water during dry spells, too much heavy shade blocking sunlight, or insect pests like mirids attacking the young blossoms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Shade ni mli edɔ tsɔ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ muji ni tutuaa tsei bibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants dry up and die suddenly even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden dying is often caused by bacterial wilt, a tiny disease in the soil that enters the plant roots and clogs the internal tubes that carry water up to the stem and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ trukaa gbele nɛɛ baa. ni ji hela bibioo ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni boteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ nu yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them stay healthy?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ jwɛi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It blocks hot sunshine from drying out moisture, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly rots to feed the soil.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ agbi. Etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efite fiofio koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it harmful to plant the same crop on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani eyɛ oshara?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly uses up the same soil nutrients until the land is exhausted. It also creates a permanent home for specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Esa akɛ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii nakai nɔŋŋ kɛyashi sũ lɛ mli baaho. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi hu feɔ shia ni hiɔ shi daa koni amɛfɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: What makes my pepper fruits drop off the stem while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni eji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed young fruits when they experience stress, such as sudden hot spells, unpredictable watering, or when pests feed on the flowers just as the fruit starts to form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ ahum ni mli edɔ trukaa. Nu ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba Aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ beni aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce plenty of leafy branches but very few nuts under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo niji kɛ baai babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow green leaves instead of pods. Hard, packed soil can also prevent the plant's pegs from pushing underground to form nuts.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen fertilizer babaoo lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai eŋɔlii amli yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmeii anaa koni ekaya shikpɔŋ shishi ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a living umbrella that keeps the air cool and the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii ewo mli lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the upper leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older, bottom leaves up to the newer top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very big, bushy leaves but produce very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo shi ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to put all their energy into leafy foliage instead of flowering. Balancing the soil with fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to flower and produce fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ahe moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect itself from dying. Shedding leaves prevents water loss through evaporation, allowing the roots underground to stay healthy until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ nu ni laajeɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I wait for a few good rains before planting my maize instead of planting right after the very first light shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ kpakpa? enyɔ loo etɛ dani adu ŋmãa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: The first light rain only wets the surface of the dry soil. If you plant too early, the seed will sprout, but if hot weather returns for a few days, the shallow moist soil dries out and burns the young shoot.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ Shallow, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ baagbi ni eha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Staking holds the leaves off the hot ground and spreads them out so they can catch maximum sunlight. Better leaf exposure to sunlight helps the plant produce more energy, resulting in much larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking haa baai lɛ jɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ, ni egbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji babaoo baa.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small, poor ears when I put three or four seeds into the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii ni ehiii beni mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together, their roots compete fiercely for the exact same soil nutrients and water. Spacing seeds properly ensures every plant gets enough nutrients to produce full, heavy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekɛ ŋmãa toi ni tsiimɔ fɛɛ aba.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest in Ghana. They crawl into the tight central leaves of corn plants to feed on tender tissue, which stunts the plant's growth if they are not picked off or treated.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli koni amɛ ye fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi tsei lɛ adalɛ naa kɛji ajieee amɛ loo atsaaa amɛ.

english: Why is it a bad idea to plant peppers in the exact same bed where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ ooodu ŋmeii yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni mibua ŋmeii anaa yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Peppers and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and attract the same soil diseases and pests. Rotating crops breaks the disease cycle because pests in the soil won't have their favorite food when a different crop family is planted.
ga: Chili ŋmeii kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ji tsei akuu kome mli ni amɛgbalaa helai kɛ kooloi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hela lɛ akpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naaa niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ waa kɛ́ amɛdu tsei aweku kroko.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow around my cassava plants lower the amount of food I harvest at the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cassava tsei lɛ ha niyenii ni mikpaa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ ba shi.

english: Weeds act like thief plants that steal water, light, and fertilizer away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nutrients in the soil go directly into feeding your cassava plants.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, kane, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the surrounding air cool, maintaining moisture in the soil, and protecting the young cocoa foliage from heat stress while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee fɛ̃i Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize crops turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves near the bottom of maize stalks usually show that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green. Applying poultry manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early will help the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi eŋɔli su lɛ mli. Kooloi ashishi loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up without destroying the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni efiteee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is generally ready when the mature leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to swell and crack open as the tubers expand underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai ni egbɔ lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants instead of growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the air gets too hot, when the plant experiences drought, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and light shade during extremely hot days help the blossoms set into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ naa hɔmɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight so their leaves can make food for the tubers underneath the soil. Staking also keeps the vines off the wet ground, which prevents leaf rot and diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa wain tsei ahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafite kɛ helai.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts on my farmland after harvesting maize from it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but groundnuts belong to a family of plants that capture nitrogen from the air and return it into the ground. Rotating them helps replenish the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmei ji tsei akuu ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Kɛ́ otsake lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ ayi obɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the sap from under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or soap solution early on gets rid of these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla shwie nɔ mra lɛ, ebaajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Which type of sucker should I cut from a plantain tree to plant a new stand?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ dumɔwu mli koni makwɛ shidaamɔhe hee?

english: You should pick 'sword suckers', which are young shoots that have narrow, spear-like leaves and a heavy base. Avoid suckers with broad, wide leaves because they do not form strong roots or big fruit bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘klante ŋmei’, ni ji ŋmei bibioo ko ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo ni tsii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ enɛ baaha shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ loo aduawai akui wuji aba.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and nutrients in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them properly allows every plant to produce larger cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe feɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetable farm during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Early morning is the best time to water crops. Morning watering gives the plants time to drink before the sun grows hot, whereas watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why does the water disappear so quickly into the ground after I water my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu eshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Some soils have high drainage that lets water sink away fast. While crops need water to drain so their roots do not rot, adding organic matter like compost helps the soil hold enough moisture for the plant roots to drink before it all washes away.
ga: Shikpɔji komɛi yɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli babaoo, ni no haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni shishifãi lɛ akafite moŋ, shi kɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu dani nu lɛ fɛɛ ashwie.

english: Why do my plants get thirsty fast even after heavy rain falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kumai yeɔ mi tsei lɛ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain falls on very loose or sandy soil, the water drains right past the root zone where the plant cannot reach it. Adding mulch or manure keeps the moisture near the soil surface where your crop roots actually feed.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni etse loo ŋã nɔ lɛ Nu lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli he ni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Mulch loo ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Is it normal for water to drain away fast around the base of a coconut tree?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ nu hoɔ oya yɛ ŋmei tso shishi?

english: Yes, coconut palms prefer well-draining soil because standing water can rot their root systems. However, the soil must still have enough nourishment to feed the roots as the water passes through.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo ni baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ be mli ni nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: What do I need to do to make my coconut trees bear a lot of good fruit?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ afee koni akoko tso lɛ awo yibii kpakpai babaoo?

english: To get a heavy yield, you must give the coconut tree proper nutrients in the soil and protect its leafy crown, allowing the tree to use its energy to set strong, healthy fruit bunches.
ga: bɔni afee ni oná yibii babaoo Esa akɛ Oha ŋmei tso lɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni obu etsitsi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe. Ha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee aduawai akui ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do coconut flowers and fruits only grow right at the top of the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ pɛ lɛ?

english: A coconut tree forms its flower buds and fruit bunches in the leaf axils at the very top (the crown) because that is where the tree gets maximum sunlight and leaves produce the energy needed to grow heavy nuts.
ga: Kokoo tsei feɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai akui yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ (akɔɔble) ejaakɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni tso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo yɛ ni baai lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What specific care does a coconut palm need in the soil before it starts producing nuts?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akwɛ ŋmei tsei anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛje ŋmeii feemɔ shishi?

english: Coconut palms need soil rich in essential nutrients like potassium and proper organic care so their shallow root systems can absorb food continuously to support future fruiting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium yɔɔ mli babaoo, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmei tsei. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii be fɛɛ be koni eye ebua wɔsɛɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Does choosing a specific crop variety make a big difference in how much harvest I get?
ga: Ani tso pɔtɛɛ ko ni mihalaa lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, every crop variety has its own natural potential built into it. Even with good care, a low-yielding variety will produce less than an improved variety designed for high fruit production.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebɔɔ su mli nyɛmɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ, shi Srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ po wooo yibii fioo fe srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ ni afee koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: If two coconut trees get the same amount of water, why might one produce more fruit than the other?
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tsei enyɔ ná nu falɛ kome lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ tso kome woɔ yibii babaoo fe ekroko lɛ?

english: Different varieties have different inherent yield potentials. One tree variety might naturally convert water and soil nutrients into fruit far more efficiently than another variety.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi yɛ yibiiwoo hegbɛi srɔtoi. Tso henɔ kome baanyɛ atsake nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee adebɔɔ mli yibii jogbaŋŋ fe tso henɔi krokomɛi.

english: Why is it important to put nutrients into the soil instead of just watering my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ niyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni aaawo tso lɛ nu lɛ?

english: Water carries nutrients to the plant, but water alone does not feed it. Giving crops the specific soil treatment and fertilizers they require provides the actual food needed for strong growth and heavy fruiting.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tsei amli. Shi nu pɛ nyɛŋ aha tsei niyenii. Kɛ́ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ amli yɛ he ni ehe hiaa lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛnyɛ amɛwo yibii amli.

english: Can poor soil prevent a high-quality crop variety from reaching its full potential?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, even if you plant a variety with high yield potential, poor soil nutrients or bad drainage will prevent the plant from ever producing to its full capacity.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ odu tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo po. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkawo yibii bɔ ni sa.

english: Should I burn the bush cleared from my land before planting, or leave it to rot?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni mijie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu loo maha amɛgboi?

english: Burning destroys beneficial soil nutrients, kills earthworms, and dries out the land. Leaving cleared weed and crop remains to decay on top of the soil creates natural compost and retains soil moisture for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ehaa sũ lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting pepper repeatedly in the same spot allows soil diseases and pests specific to pepper to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like maize or beans starves out pepper pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Pepper ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ pepper pɔtɛɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaaye ebua ni ejie ŋmãa nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and covered in white sticky powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni akɛ powda yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by whiteflies or cassava mealybugs, tiny pests that suck the sap from your cassava leaves. You can spray them with mild soapy water or recommended neem-based sprays to clear them before they stunt your tubers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmeii yɛŋ loo ŋmei ŋmeii. ni ji kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmei baa mli nu lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ afɔ nɔ. Aloo neem spray ni ajieɔ yi akɛ okɛfɔ he dani etsɔ oyitso bibioo.

english: What is eating holes in the central leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central growing tip of the maize. Applying approved bio-pesticides early in the morning or late evening targets them effectively.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes my tomato stems rot and turn black near the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Excess water in the soil creates a wet environment where soil fungi thrive and attack the stem base. Staking your tomatoes and creating raised soil beds helps drainage and keeps the plant stems dry.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛtutuaa tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ o-tomato lɛ wo ŋtayaai amli ni ofee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ajɛ mli ni eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green leaves. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-composted manure will restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct harsh sunlight and lose water too fast. They need temporary shade from plantains or shade trees during their first two years until their own canopy develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Amɛbiɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwereɔ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable farm in the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Okɛ nu awo aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli shwane mli. Aloo ani leebi hi fe no?

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants the moisture they need before the sun gets hot, reducing water loss through evaporation. Afternoon watering can burn leaves and evaporate before reaching the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enáa nu ni he hiaa lɛ dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã ni amɛtsɔ la dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches even though the soil seems good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers around one mother plant forces them to fight for water and soil nutrients. You should trim excess suckers so only two or three strong ones remain per stool.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ he Enɛ baaha amɛwuu kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli bɔni afee ni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi ni hi kɛha ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Groundnut flowers self-pollinate above ground, and then send down small pegs into the soil where the pods mature. Keep the soil around the base soft so these pegs can easily bury themselves to grow nuts.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ pin bibioo ko awo mli. kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afu amɛhe oya koni amɛdu ŋmeii.

english: Why do people plant plantains next to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tso bibioo?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This produces weak, thin plants that give very small yields compared to crops planted with proper spacing.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally traps nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil. Planting groundnuts after maize restores soil fertility naturally for future crops.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ nɔ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Small ragged holes in maize leaves are often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. You can check the center funnel of the plant for pests and apply recommended insecticides or organic neem seed extracts early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo organic neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ awo mli mra.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and applying balanced manure or fertilizer helps fruits form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ aba.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, or by carefully digging around one plant to check if the tubers are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dalɛ ni amɛgbee shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tso kome he ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds while my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from young roots. Weeding early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need during their critical early growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛ mra be mli dalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Can I use dry animal dung to help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, dry animal dung like cow or poultry manure acts as natural fertilizer. It enriches the soil with nutrients, helps the soil hold moisture longer, and improves root growth without damaging the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni egbi tamɔ tsina ŋmei loo koolo ŋmei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni eha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to resist common local diseases, survive dry weather better, and produce higher yields than seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Ehi akɛ ooohi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and getting scorched by the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that cannot handle full sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees during their first couple of years to keep them cool and retain soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi

english: How do I choose the best plantain shoot to dig up when starting a new plantain farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafo beni mijeɔ plantain ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these are young shoots with narrow, blade-like leaves and a heavy bulb at the bottom. They grow much faster and produce stronger stems and bigger bunches than shoots that already have broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ bulb ni tsii yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni wa kɛ jwɛi wuji fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow right down the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make healthy green leaves. Applying fertilizer like NPK or adding well-rotted animal manure will give them back their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Which way should I point a cassava stem cutting when I push it into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi ohe kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ otsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ ni afo lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small raised bumps or buds where the old leaves used to grow; these buds must point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the roots will struggle to develop, and the plant might die.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Ebɛŋkɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai momo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛshweremɔ mli ni tso lɛ baanyɛ agbo.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are big enough to dig up without unearthing the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and small cracks begin to appear on the soil surface right around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Jeɔ shishi ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden poles to tie my yam shoots onto?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso kakadaŋŋ ko mli koni mikɛfi sweet potato lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to make food for the growing yam tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ bɔni afee ni eha niyenii aha sweet potato tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni akɛtsi baai helai anaa.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown sawdust inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekpɛtɛɔ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep funnel of young maize plants to eat the tender leaf whorl. Catching them early and applying an approved treatment saves the plant before the central growing tip is destroyed.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ahere tso lɛ yiwala dani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni daa lɛ afite.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants dropping off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani yibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed, which happens if the weather is extremely hot, if the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during the flowering stage helps fruit set properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ miihao. Enɛ baa mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛyibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable farm early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the plant can drink up the moisture before the heat sets in. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate before reaching the roots, and water droplets on foliage can burn leaf surfaces.
ga: Nu ni oooha tso lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani latsaa lɛ aba, ni kɛ́ oowo nu yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baa lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry bush grass around the base of their pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwereɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around the stem is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under the harsh sun, locks in water so you don't have to water as often, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ nu toɔ bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut down cocoa trees that have swollen stems even if they are still producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei ni ŋmeii efuu lɛ? No yɛ pods mli lolo?

english: That swelling is caused by the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. Even if the tree is still giving you some cocoa pods now, the virus will slowly kill it and quickly spread to all the healthy cocoa trees around it. Cutting down infected trees is the only proven way to stop the disease from wiping out your entire farm.
ga: Virus hela kɛ fuumɔ baa: kookoo tsei ni efuu. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ, tso lɛ baaha bo kookoo ŋmeii komɛi lolo. Shi hela lɛ gbeɔ lɛ fiofio. ni egbɛ eshwa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli. mra oya Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by planting cuttings taken from an infected stem. To fix this, always source clean, disease-resistant cassava stems and remove affected plants early before the whiteflies spread the disease to others.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmeii ni miida ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii Halamɔ he ni ŋmei tsei ni he tse ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ jɛɔ ni ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Dani ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ baagbɛ hela amɛshwã mɛi krokomɛi anɔ

english: What is eating the soft inner leaves of my young maize and leaving small black drops inside?
ga: Mɛni ye mi-baby corn lɛ baai bibii lɛ ni eshi ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji yɛ mli?

english: That is the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants to eat the soft leaves. You need to inspect your farm early and apply recommended bio-pesticides or chemicals directly into the central funnel before they destroy the growing point.
ga: No ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ awo mli dani ofite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Does leaving tall grass and weeds on my farm really harm my crops, or are they harmless?
ga: Ani jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi bibii ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, which makes your yields small. Weeds also act as safe hiding spots for harmful pests and crop diseases that can easily attack your main harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa onitsumɔ lɛ baa shi. Jwɛi hu tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ atutua onibii titrii lɛ baanyɛ atutua onibii titrii lɛ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a 'V'?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips in a 'V' shape mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the base of the plant will help restore its healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni feɔ ‘V’ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating your maize with crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, or soybeans puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, loo soybeans baatsake Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so that the rain does not waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni nugbɔ akafite shika?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain, but not right before a heavy downpour that could wash it away. Covering the fertilizer lightly with soil near the base of the crop also prevents the rain and sun from taking it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba, ni baanyɛ ashwie sũ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot and dry, or if the plant isn't getting enough water or nutrients. Ensuring your plants get consistent moisture and proper shade during extremely hot afternoons helps the flowers set healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tso lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks up for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make the food that grows the big tuber underground. Staking raises the vines off the damp ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ bulbs agboi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he, ni eha helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akaye ehe.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a long time to bear fruit compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need plenty of organic manure, constant soil moisture, and protection from wind. If you leave too many suckers growing around one mother plant, they will all fight for food; keeping only one or two strong suckers per plant helps them fruit much faster.
ga: Plantains he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ he lɛ Amɛ fɛɛ amɛbaatswa niyenii he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ to tso kome he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii oya kwraa.

english: This usually happens when your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves whatever nutrient it has left from its older lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die as soon as the Harmattan dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and thin leaves that lose water very fast under intense sun and dry winds. Without shade trees or plantain plants to shield them and hold moisture in the soil, the harsh heat dries them out completely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains bɛ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha amɛgbi kwraa.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main tree to focus its energy on producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, single main trunk Nakai ŋmeii lɛ hu baatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔii wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants grow long, leafy vines above the ground but yield very small yams underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tso ni baai kakadaji yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi sweet potato yibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo kwraa.

english: If the vine receives too much nitrogen from the soil or doesn't get a stake pole to climb, it spends all its energy making leaves instead of sending energy down to build a thick tuber underground.
ga: Kɛji wain tso lɛ miiná nitrogen babaoo kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ebɛ tso ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai moŋ fe ni eeetsu kɛya shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if heavy rain falls right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains soak the field and water sits for too long, the roots suffocate and soil fungi quickly attack them, causing them to turn soft and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni sũ mli ŋmeii tutuaa amɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck the plant's sap and spread a virus, or by extreme heat stress when the soil goes from dry to wet too quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli oya tsɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers instead of producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by high temperatures, erratic watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Without phosphorus, the plant cannot hold onto its flowers long enough for them to turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji fɔsfɔs bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ fɔfɔii amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my okra plants growing very tall with big leaves but producing almost no okra pods?
