ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi okra ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough balance from phosphorus and potassium, they focus entirely on growing tall stems and large leaves instead of setting flowers and pods.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ ni amɛnáaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us that planting cowpeas improves the soil for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots work with helpful natural soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, leaving natural fertilizer behind for your next crop.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get hard like concrete and make my crop roots struggle after a few years of clearing and burning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit lɛ? Ni ni ehaa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛjie amɛhe ni mikɛshã lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning farm clearing debris destroys organic matter like decayed leaves that keep the soil soft and sponge-like. Over time, heavy rain and direct sun pack the bare ground tight, making it hard for roots to penetrate.
ga: Okwaa mli jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ sponji. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ eyi he ni agbele lɛ obɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli.

english: Why does my soil lose its strength so fast after I harvest certain crops like cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa oya beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ?

english: Certain crops are heavy feeders that absorb large amounts of nutrients from the ground to grow. If you harvest them continuously without giving the soil rest or adding nutrients back, the land quickly becomes exhausted.
ga: Tsei komɛi ji tsei ni gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Kɛji okpaa nii be fɛɛ be ni ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho oya.

english: Are there specific crops that drain the nutrients from my land faster than others?
ga: Ani tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei krokomɛi?

english: Yes, crops like maize, cassava, and sugarcane consume high amounts of key nutrients like nitrogen and potassium, draining the soil faster than lighter feeders or legume crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium babaoo tsuɔ nii, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ waaa loo ŋmãa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has completely lost its fertility?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiɛ edɔ?

english: Common signs include crop leaves turning yellow early, stunted plant growth, low yields despite good rains, and soil that easily hardens into crusts when dry.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe ji: Tso lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. stunted plant growth Yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa oya ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa kɛji egbi lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my land become weak if I keep planting the exact same crop on it every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I stop my soil fertility from dropping so quickly after every farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni baa shi oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be sɛɛ?

english: You can protect your soil fertility by practicing crop rotation, leaving crop residues on the farm to decompose, applying manure or compost, and avoiding total soil clearing.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ shwiemɔ he.

english: Can I plant certain crops that actually restore nutrients back into my tired land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei komɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa mishikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, and soybeans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ soybeans. Emɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: What happens to my soil quality if I do not practice good land management on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ hu?

english: Without proper land management, rain washes away the fertile topsoil, organic matter breaks down completely, and the land becomes too poor to support healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa bɛ lɛ Nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baafite kwraa. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ji ohiafo tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Is it harmful to my soil fertility if I burn all plant bushes and crop remains when clearing my land?
ga: Ani ebaaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji mishã mijwɛi kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, burning destroys the natural organic matter and beneficial microbes that build soil fertility, leaving the ground dry, weak, and exposed to erosion.
ga: Hɛɛ, shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What natural things can I add to my field to keep the soil nutrients from disappearing?
ga: Mɛɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii manyɛ mikɛfata miŋmɔji lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ akafite?

english: Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or green cover crops adds organic matter to the soil, holding nutrients in place and improving water retention.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni eŋɔli fata he lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If my land is already exhausted from past farming, how long will it take to build back its strength?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efo kɛjɛ okwaayeli ni eho lɛ mli Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani matswa mihewalɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: With good land management—such as applying manure, growing cover crops, or letting the land fallow—you can start seeing noticeable improvement in soil health within one to three seasons.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ. aloo shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Obaanyɛ oje shishi ona hiɛyaa ni kadiɔ mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ mli yɛ be kome kɛyashi etɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is too much sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that easily lose water under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from intense heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high temperatures, lack of water, or soil that has too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Cassava grows best in loose, sandy soil where water drains quickly. If soil holds too much water like heavy clay, the roots will struggle to expand and may rot inside the ground.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaawa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite.

english: Why are holes suddenly appearing in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ko eba trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, such as the fall armyworm, feeding on the tender inner leaves. They hide inside the plant leaves during the day and eat the crop at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni egbee shi ni eye baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii gbɛkɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds close together so I can get more harvest from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over water and plant food in the soil, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. This results in thin, weak plants with smaller yields overall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu mli ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and smelly in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked with water for too long, air cannot reach the roots. This waterlogged environment allows fungal diseases to attack the tubers, causing them to rot inside the wet soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni nu eyi mli obɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii helai tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants remaining short and refusing to grow tall even after several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛdaraaa yɛ otsii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth usually happens when the soil lacks key nutrients, when the ground is too hard for roots to spread, or when tiny pests in the soil are damaging the roots quietly underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii titrii bɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ dioo.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that require soils rich in organic matter and moisture. If your soil lacks nutrients or if weeds are competing with the plantains, their growth rate slows down significantly.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo jwɛi kɛ plantains lɛ miitswa akaŋ. Amɛdalɛ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is enough space in the farm for all of them to grow?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ he ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly drink up the water and suck away the fertilizers meant for your crops. They also shelter insect pests and plant diseases that can spread to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni nuɔ nu oya ni amɛmuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã onibii amli lɛ hu ahi.

english: Why should I put fertilizer on my maize farm when the soil already looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ?

english: Even rich-looking soil loses specific nutrients after supporting previous crops. Fertilizer acts like extra food, giving crops essential elements like nitrogen and phosphorus so they can build thick stalks and full maize cobs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ nɔ ni baa nii lɛ po laajeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi beni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ sɛɛ. Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ baaha amɛná ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kwraa.

english: How do the subsidized fertilizers from the Ministry of Agriculture actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni Ministry of Agriculture lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Subsidized fertilizers provide balanced nutrients at an affordable price. When applied at the right stage, they strengthen plant roots and boost grain and fruit development, significantly increasing harvest yield.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛyeɔ abuaa lɛ haa niyenii ni sa yɛ jara ni waaa nɔ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli Ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ. ni ehaa dumɔwui kɛ aduawai yaa hiɛ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ tee hiɛ waa.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to turn yellow and curl, and how do chemicals help?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai baanyɛ aye abua?

english: Curling and yellow leaves are usually caused by small insects sucking the plant's juices or spreading viruses. Approved agrochemicals kill these harmful pests, allowing the plant to recover and produce healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli ni awo he hewalɛ lɛ gbeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara nɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will spraying crop chemicals on my farm harm my crops or help them?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ?

english: When used correctly in the recommended amounts, chemicals protect crops from destruction by pests, weeds, and fungal diseases without harming the crop itself, ensuring a healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ mli Tsofai lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, jwɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe. ni eyeee tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ awui Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I keep using the old traditional planting methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miyaa nɔ mikɛ gbɛi ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Soil quality and rainfall patterns change over time. Modern techniques, such as proper crop spacing and improved seeds, help plants absorb more sunlight and nutrients, leading to larger yields than traditional methods allow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la kɛ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa anáa yibii babaoo fe blema gbɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small when I plant the stems too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are overcrowded, their underground roots compete fiercely for water and soil nutrients, preventing them from swelling into thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ekafu ni etsɔ yitso ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: How do I know if my farm is ready to expand and grow crops on a large scale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa ni edu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: You are ready to expand when you have reliable access to high-quality seeds, fertilizers, labor, and a dependable way to transport your heavy harvests to the market before they spoil.
ga: Ofee klalo akɛ obaaha onitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛ́ oná dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nitsulɔi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. kɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛ onibii ni tsii lɛ aya jara nɔ dani efite.

english: Why is it important to get my harvested vegetables onto market buses as quickly as possible?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ awo jarayeli bɔs lɛ mli oya bɔ ni aaanyɛ lɛ?

english: Vegetables lose water and spoil rapidly after being picked in hot weather. Getting them quickly onto transport preserves their freshness, appearance, and market value.
ga: Nu fiteɔ aduawai amli ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa. Majemɔ oya haa ehee, hiɛ su kɛ jarayeli sɛɛnamɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How can using my mobile phone to access financial help or pay for inputs improve my harvest?
ga: Te mi-mobile phone ni mikɛaatsu nii koni maná shika loo miwo nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Using phone financing allows you to buy seeds and chemicals instantly at the exact start of the rainy season, ensuring your planting and fertilization are done on time for maximum crop growth.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tɛlifoŋ nɔ shika tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oheɔ dumɔwui kɛ tsofai amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi. Enɛ haa odumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ baagbe naa yɛ be naa koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my crops wither during short dry periods even if I water them occasionally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu wo mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli po?

english: In intense sun, water evaporates quickly from exposed soil. Regular watering combined with mulching—covering soil around crops with dry grass—keeps moisture near the roots so plants don't stress and wither.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa ni akɛ mulching fataa he—ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafee nɔ ni haoɔ amɛ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade trees or plantain plants around them to protect their leaves from scorching and to keep the soil moist while they build deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni afeɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for growth. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives them back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tso lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because they cannot breathe in soggy soil. Planting them on raised soil mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food for the tubers growing underground. Letting the vines climb tall stakes keeps the leaves exposed to maximum sunlight and away from damp ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ wain tsei lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni ebaaha helai akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with dry leaves or straw helps the plant hold onto its flowers so peppers can grow.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo be ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce smaller bunches when many small shoots grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ daa bibioo be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he?

english: When too many small shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients from it. Removing extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets enough food to grow big bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni etsɔ kuu agbo.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap natural food from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the ground to feed the next crop like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Niyenii ni atsĩ naa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛye sɛɛ mli tsei, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck the plant's juices and spread sickness. Controlling these small pests early or using healthy seeds stops the sickness from stunting your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ oye nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ anɔ mra Aloo dumɔwui kpakpai ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ, ebaaha hela akatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the dirt, stopping the sun from drying out the soil water too fast and keeping the plant roots cool during hot dry spells.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. ni ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted together, the crowded plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Giving each plant its own space lets it grow thick stems and produce big, full ears of maize.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome Tsei ni buaa amɛhe naa lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need plenty of sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. The stakes lift the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the yam tubers grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Pila titri lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ tsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off the dry brown leaves hanging down on my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo baai ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fĩ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Dead plantain leaves block sunlight from reaching lower parts of the crop and can harbor pests or fungal diseases. Removing them keeps the farm clean, improves airflow, and helps the plant direct its energy into growing big fruit bunches.
ga: Plantain baai ni egboi lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ hei lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse. ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii wuji

english: Why do I need to cut off the soft green shoots growing directly out of the main trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, often called chupons or suckers, consume water and food that the tree needs for pod production. Removing them helps the tree focus its energy on growing healthy cocoa pods on the main branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ chupon loo ŋmeii. Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ pod. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida yɛ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, strong sunlight because their roots cannot absorb water fast enough to replace what heat dries out. They need shade crops like plantains to cover them until their root systems grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛye la ni haa amɛgbiɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛha amɛhe aahu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawa.

english: Why do my young maize crop leaves have small ragged holes and dirt inside the leaf folds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni mɛɛ muji yɔɔ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests such as the fall armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the soft inner leaves of maize. Identifying this early allows you to apply recommended pest control treatments before the crop is ruined.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ ni oooyɔse mra Enɛ baaha okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ ayeɔ ŋmãa lɛ atsu nii dani akpãtã ŋmɔshi nibii ahiɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: One early rain is usually not enough because the deep soil stays warm and dry underneath. You should wait until you get two or three steady rains that soak the soil deeply so your seeds do not dry out after sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ faaa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ shishi. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ aba. Bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil turn very hard and cracked when it does not rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter, such as decayed leaves or manure, which acts like a sponge to hold moisture. Adding compost or leaving dead plant materials on the soil surface keeps it soft and workable.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fata he loo tsei ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo ni anyɛ atsu he nii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger than the crops I planted after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have deep, tough root systems that are naturally adapted to steal water and food from the soil quickly. Clearing weeds early ensures your planted crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni tsei ni miida lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open from the swelling tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: How can I keep my harvested rice fresh in storage for up to eight months without insects destroying it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi ehee kɛyashi nyɔji kpaanyɔ ni kooloi akafite lɛ?

english: To keep rice fresh for six to eight months, you must dry the grains thoroughly until they are hard and store them in airtight (hermetic) bags. These bags block oxygen, which prevents weevils from hatching and stops mold from growing.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni oha ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi kpaanyɔ lɛ, Ehe miihia ni Oha ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) amli. Nɛkɛ kotokui nɛɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ naa. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ afɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hu shwereɔ.

english: What basic steps can I take on my farm to protect my stored crops from rats and bugs?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Keep your storage area clean, store grains in sealed bags, and keep the bags elevated off the dirt floor using wooden pallets. Keeping bags away from walls stops dampness and makes it harder for pests like rats and insects to hide.
ga: Ha he ni okɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he atse. Okɛ ŋmaa lɛ awo kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli. ni okɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ awo kotokui lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ muji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ kotoku lɛ tsi he ko kɛjɛ gbogboi ahe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akaya hiɛ. Ni ehaa ewaa ahaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akɛ amɛaahi amɛhe.

english: Why does my harvested rice start rotting or smelling bad just a few weeks after I put it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ loo ewoɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Crops rot in bags when they are trapped with too much internal moisture. If grain is bagged before it is completely dry, the trapped wetness creates heat and fungi, causing the whole bag to spoil quickly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mɔmɔ amɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa lɛ, Trapped wetness haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmãa baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kotoku muu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: How do I know if my grain is dry enough to be safely stored for a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmaa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ?

english: A simple way is the salt test or bite test: if you bite a grain of rice and it cracks cleanly instead of bending, it is dry enough. Properly dried grain has low moisture, which stops fungal growth during storage.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ji ŋmei kaa loo ŋmei kaa. Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ko ŋmɔ ni efo mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ baagbi bɔ ni sa. Akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ akpa be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why does harvesting my crops during the rainy season make them spoil faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ehaa amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high humidity, making it difficult for harvested grains to dry properly under the sun. High moisture levels in harvested crops encourage rapid bacterial and mold growth.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ akɛ amɛaagbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii daa oya.

english: Why does my farm produce usually run out just two or three months after harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ?

english: Farm produce runs out quickly if all crops mature at once and proper long-term storage isn't used. Without long-term storage, farmers are forced to sell or consume everything right away instead of spreading supply over six to eight months.
ga: Okwaayeli mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite oya kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ shikome ni akɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ be kakadaŋŋ bɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ Okwaafoi anɔ koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ loo amɛye nɔ fɛɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, a gbaa ní ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ nyɔhiɔ enuɔ kɛ ya si kpaanyɔ mi.

english: How can I keep selling local produce during the long dry season when nothing is growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maya nɔ mahɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ mli nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can keep selling during the dry season by preserving and storing a portion of your yield during the main harvest using proper post-harvest treatments, allowing you to sell during peak market demand when local supply is low.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fã ko ni oookwɛ nɔ ni okɛto yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ gbɛi ni sa ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni jarayeli nibii taoɔ babaoo lɛ, be mli ni nibii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ.

english: Why does imported rice often stay good in stores longer than our locally harvested rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ sumɔɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shwapoi amli be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmãa ni wɔkpaa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Imported rice often lasts longer because it goes through strict commercial drying and cleaning processes that reduce moisture to precise levels. Local rice can last just as long if dried thoroughly and stored in airtight containers.
ga: Omɔ ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ etsɔɔ jarayeli gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni mli wa ni haa egbiɔ kɛ ehe saamɔ mli. Enɛ baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi kɛyashɛ he ko pɔtɛɛ. Kuu lɛ mli ŋmãa baanyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ nakai nɔŋŋ. Kɛji egbi kwraa lɛ, okɛto he ko ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli.

english: Are there specific varieties of crops that naturally last longer in storage after harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni abaanyɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, certain improved seed varieties produce grains with harder outer husks and lower natural moisture absorption, making them naturally more resistant to pests and decay during long storage periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to sell all my rice right after harvest or keep some in storage for later?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ loo makɛ eko ato kɛha sɛɛ mli?

english: Selling everything right after harvest often means getting low prices because the market is flooded. Storing your rice safely for several months allows you to sell later at higher prices when rice becomes scarce.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaaná jara ni baa shi ejaakɛ jara lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa to shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo lɛ, no haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ beni ŋmãa faaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut trees turning yellow and dying off before giving fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in coconut trees are often caused by deadly diseases like Cape St. Paul Wilt Disease or severe nutrient shortages in the soil, which stop the tree from absorbing the water and food it needs to produce nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni naa wa, tamɔ Cape St. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii.

english: How many years do I need to wait after planting coconut seedlings before I can start harvesting?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi amɛkpamɔ?

english: Improved dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall coconut varieties take about 6 to 8 years to produce their first full harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava in between my young coconut trees, or will it spoil the coconut growth?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ? Aloo ebaafite akokoo lɛ?

english: You can safely plant cassava between young coconut trees during their first few years, provided you leave enough clear space around the coconut bases so the cassava roots do not steal essential water and nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Esa akɛ oshi he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ he. Coconut base ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ ji koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akaju nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Why is it wrong for me to plant my crops very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak plants with thin stems and very low yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough to plant maize during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Good soil for maize is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, and holds moisture well without staying flooded or muddy for long periods after heavy rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ yɛ nine mli oya ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Ekɛ nu loo sũ ehiɛɛɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my crops so the heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie amɛ?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is already damp after a light rain, and you should lightly cover the fertilizer with soil near the plant roots rather than spreading it right before a heavy downpour.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha he fioo. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tsei shishifãi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ eshwa dani nugbɔ anɛ waa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme sun heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insect pests that damage the delicate flower stems.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Ebaa mli ni efiteɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: What is eating big holes into my cabbage leaves and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji wuji ni yɔɔ kaabe baa mli lɛ? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsĩ naa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars and worms feeding on them, which can be controlled by checking under leaves regularly, using recommended protective sprays, or removing visible caterpillars by hand.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii amli ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ amɛ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni akwɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ oniji ajie ŋmeii fɛɛ ni anaa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil food faster than farm crops, which is why clearing them early gives your crops the best chance to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot every year completely drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and plant diseases that target that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwraa. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the main difference between 'apem' and 'apentu' plantain varieties?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ ‘apem’ kɛ ‘apentu’ plantain henɔi lɛ ateŋ?

english: Apem' produces bunches with many small fingers, while 'apentu' produces fewer, but much larger and thicker fingers per bunch.
ga: Apem’ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ niji bibii babaoo aba, yɛ be mli ni ‘apentu’ baajie ŋmeii fioo komɛi. Shi amɛdara kwraa ni amɛhe wa yɛ kuu fɛɛ kuu mli.

english: How long do plantains usually take to mature before I can harvest them?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akpaa plantains?

english: Most plantain varieties take between 11 to 12 months from planting to reach maturity for harvest, depending on rainfall and soil health.
ga: Plantain henɔi babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 12 kɛjɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ dani eshɛɔ kɛha nikpamɔ. Edamɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ ehaa kɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant more than one type of plantain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain henɔi ni fe ekome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting different varieties like both 'apem' and 'apentu' helps you target different market buyers and reduces risk if one variety faces price drops or disease.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi tamɔ ‘apem’ kɛ ‘apentu’ ni aduɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ohiɛ fɔɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli hei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. ni ebaa oshara shi kɛji akɛ srɔtofeemɔ ko jara ba shi loo hela ba.

english: How do I know when my plantain bunch is ready to be harvested for market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-plantain tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits become plump, lose their sharp outer ridges, and the dried flowers at the tips rub off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔjɔ. Kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni baafite Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ baafo mlɛo.

english: How does growing plantains help bring quick money to my household?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni plantains ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ shika aba mishia lɛ oya?

english: Plantains are a daily staple food in local Ghanaian markets with high demand, meaning matured bunches can be sold quickly for immediate cash.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni ayeɔ daa gbi yɛ Ghana maŋ jarayeli hei ni mɛi biɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaanyɛ ahɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda kwraa lɛ oya koni aná shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What determines the price buyers will pay me for a single bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni tsɔɔ jara ni mɔ ko ni heɔ nii lɛ baawo mi kɛha plantains ŋmɔ ko?

english: The price depends on the overall size and weight of the bunch, the fullness of the fingers, the variety, and current market supply in your area.
ga: Jara lɛ damɔ kuu lɛ dalɛ kɛ etsiimɔ fɛɛ nɔ. Niji ni yeɔ emuu, srɔtoi kɛ nibii ni akɛhaa yɛ jara ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Can I make good profit selling plantains even if I only harvest a few bunches at a time?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa kɛtsɔ plantains ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ mikpa ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ yɛ be kome mli po?

english: Yes, because plantain bunches are sold individually or in small lots, even harvesting just one or two good quality bunches can bring in steady daily or weekly cash.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ amɛfeɔ ekãa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ kui amli loo yɛ fãi bibii amli. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ 1-2 pɛ ni akpaa lɛ po baanyɛ aha aná shika ni yaa nɔ daa gbi loo daa otsi.

english: How should I handle my cut plantain bunches so they don't spoil before I reach the market?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-plantain ni mifo lɛ nɔ koni amɛkafite dani amɛyashɛ jara nɔ?

english: Keep harvested bunches out of direct sunlight in a cool, shaded spot and handle them gently to prevent bruising, which causes rapid rotting.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. ni okɛtsu nii blɛoo koni akafite ni baaha efite oya.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce extra shoots around the main stem, and should I keep them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ?

english: Those extra shoots are called suckers; keeping one or two healthy suckers ensures a continuous cycle of new plantain crops after you harvest the main plant.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii ni fata he lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei heei lɛ aya nɔ atsake amɛhe yɛ be mli ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What happens to my plantain crops if they do not get enough water during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Lack of water slows down plant growth, causes leaves to turn yellow, and results in smaller, lighter bunches that fetch lower prices.
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ aniji lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛjara baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Without larger shade trees or companion crops like plantains to shelter them, the seedlings lose moisture rapidly through their leaves, scorch, and fail to establish strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei wuji ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei ni fata he tamɔ tsei bibii ni akɛhaa amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ, amɛshãa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll inward as a natural survival mechanism to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating too quickly during severe heat.
ga: Abele baai lɛ shwieɔ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ. Koni akɛba baai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves typically signal a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Because nitrogen is a mobile nutrient within the plant, the maize moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitrogen ji niyenii ni yaa nɔ yɛ tsei amli. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛ ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch rapidly upward to reach light, spending energy on tall stems instead of building thick branches and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei akutsei ni kɛlɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ Moŋ lɛ ewoɔ tsei niji ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants without setting fruit during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei ni wooo yibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity make tomato pollen wet and sticky, preventing it from transferring between flower parts. When flowers are not properly pollinated, the plant sheds them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa tomato pollen lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni ekagbee shi Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ akagbee shi jogbaŋŋ Tso lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Cassava roots need loose, uncompacted soil and a balance of nutrients to expand. Hard ground physical prevents tubers from swelling, while excess nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to produce thick foliage instead of storing energy in the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli ejɔɔɔ ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛshwere. Bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ji lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafu. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaato hewalɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant cassava on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil. It also allows soil-borne pests and diseases that feed on that specific plant to multiply in the ground over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei taoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi lɛ hu feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my pepper seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep inside dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds need warmth, air, and shallow damp soil to sprout. Planting them too deep cuts off the oxygen supply and light signals needed for germination, while dry soil keeps the seed dormant.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui taoɔ dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni efɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni wɔɔ.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers underground are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers reach maturity when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up. This signals that the plant has finished transferring its manufactured food down into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my okra plants covered in small holes and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi gumbo lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Small holes in okra leaves are typically caused by insect pests like flea beetles or caterpillars feeding on the plant tissue. This leaf damage reduces the plant's ability to catch sunlight and convert it into energy, causing the leaves to turn pale.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei ahe fãji lɛ kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ okra baai amli lɛ baa. Baai ni fiteɔ lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ hulu la baa ni etsakeɔ lɛ ewoɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni tsuɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the bright sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from sun damage and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods and cause them to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, shaded conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and pruning overgrown branches helps air flow through the farm to dry out excess moisture.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ oya kɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛgbi ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: Why should I keep some big shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Permanent shade trees protect cocoa trees from high heat and heavy winds, keep soil moist during dry spells, and shed leaves that rot into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ni baai ni fiteɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Why do I need to prune the extra branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or crowded branches so the tree does not waste energy on useless leaves. It allows sunlight to reach lower branches and forces the tree to direct its energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egbɔjɔ, ni egboi, loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni mli wa ni miida lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the right time to clear my land before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu nii?

english: Land clearing is best done during the dry season (December to February) so cut weeds and bushes can dry out completely. This ensures your field is clear and ready when the major rainy season starts in April or May.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. (December kɛyashi February) no hewɔ lɛ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni afo lɛ baanyɛ agbi kwraa. Enɛ baaha oyale lɛ mli afee faŋŋ ni efee klalo beni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ April loo May mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. It can also happen when weeds surround the maize and steal nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji jwɛi bɔle ŋmãa lɛ he ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster after I clear my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater awakens dormant weed seeds lying in the topsoil and supplies continuous water, allowing weeds to grow and root much faster than during dry weather.
ga: Nugbɔ nu teɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni ewɔ shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu haa be fɛɛ be Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi oya fe be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots remain thin and small even after a long time in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni mikɛ amɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell if planted in hard, packed soil that restricts root growth, or if planted too close to other stems where they must fight for soil nutrients.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi ni esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no bees and beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he fɛɛ he. koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why is it easier to raise my vegetable seedlings in small trays inside a sheltered nursery before moving them to the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa akɛ aaakwɛ aduawai amli dumɔwui yɛ tsɛnsii bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ mli dani aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Raising seedlings in a small, sheltered space protects them from scorching sun, heavy rain, and pests while they are young and tender. It allows one person to easily monitor and care for thousands of young plants at once before they face the harsher conditions of open ground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko bibioo Ni shĩa ko baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ji gbekɛbii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ehaa mɔ kome nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ tsei bibii akpei abɔ shikome ni ekwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. dani amɛkɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ akpee.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and fall over near the stem base right after they sprout in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni amɛdara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by damp soil fungi attacking tender stems near the ground surface. Keeping seedling beds properly drained and slightly elevated off the wet ground prevents the fungi from destroying the young plants.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni tutuaa tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ asaji lɛ amli nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni awó nɔ fioo kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ŋmeii akafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drying up when planted out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants lose water faster than their roots can absorb it under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a canopy shelter that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waaa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin instead of thick and strong when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close on open ground, the crops fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough light and food to build thick stalks capable of bearing large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni agbele naa lɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso ni mli tse ni baanyɛ akwɛ tso agbo ko nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves above the ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When the ground contains too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its growth energy into top leaves instead of storing energy in the roots. Balanced soil nutrition encourages the plant to direct its strength downward into root development.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛdaraa lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛba amɛhewalɛ shi, kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ atsɔsemɔ mli tɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do I need to mount wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally search for height to catch sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground using wooden stakes improves airflow, reduces leaf diseases, and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ wo baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my groundnut plants before they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Peanut tsei dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi

english: After groundnuts flower, the stems peg downward into the ground to produce nuts underground. If weeds cover the soil surface, the flower pegs cannot penetrate the ground easily to form nuts.
ga: Beni ŋmeii lɛ efɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Akɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Kɛji jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Fɔfɔii ahe ŋmeii nyɛŋ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and rolling upwards during hot dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes curl their leaves during extreme heat to prevent water loss, but rolling combined with yellowing often signals sap-sucking insects like whiteflies. Mulching the soil keeps roots cool while inspecting under leaves helps spot early insect invasions.
ga: Okɛ tomato baai lɛ abɔ he yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni nu akaje mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ efolɔ ehe, ni ekɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ fata he lɛ, etsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kooloi ni baa mra.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall down when strong winds blow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and soft wet soil loses its grip on heavy fruiting trees. Propping the stems with sturdy bamboo or wooden forks holds the tree upright until the bunch matures.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ, ni no haa amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eniji lɛ daraa.

english: Why are my garden eggs (eggplants) dropping their flowers without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli (eggplant) lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛfeee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants drop flowers when stressed by lack of water, extreme heat, or poor pollination. Maintaining steady soil moisture and encouraging helpful insects ensures flowers stay on the plant to produce fruit.
ga: Aduawai tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji nu ni bɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni awoɔ amɛ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, your maize is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is a nutrient that helps plants stay green and grow strong; when there is not enough in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the newest top leaves to survive.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ nitrogen. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do groundnuts and cowpeas make the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special relationship with friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant finishes growing and decomposes, that stored plant food remains in the soil for crops like maize or cassava planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ wekukpaa krɛdɛɛ ko kɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsei daraa ni amɛfiteɔ Tse niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil just as much as they need water. When heavy rains leave standing water in poorly drained soil, the roots drown because they cannot breathe, allowing soil fungi to infect and decay the tubers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi tamɔ tsei. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ hela ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die if I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the temperature cool, maintaining moisture in the air, and protecting the young leaves until the cocoa is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ Eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i ahi shi ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller with every new shoot that comes up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii heei baaje shishi lɛ?

english: When a plantain plant grows too many suckers at its base, all those shoots fight for the same food and water in the soil. By cutting away extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong stems, all the plant's energy goes into producing one large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ, ŋmeii babaoo yɛ amɛshishigbɛ. Tsoi lɛ fɛɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋmeii agbo kome ni tsii mli.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden poles to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground using energy captured by their leaves from sunlight. When the vines climb high on stakes, the leaves spread out widely to catch maximum sunlight, which results in larger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ. Beni wain tsei lɛ kwɔ kɛyaa akulashiŋi kakadaji lɛ anɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the tomato plant and dries out the pollen inside the blossoms. When pollen cannot fertilize the flower properly, the plant drops the flower to save energy rather than attempting to grow a weak fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Kɛji pollen nyɛɛɛ aha fɔfɔii lɛ afee fɛo jogbaŋŋ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔii anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Mohu ɔ, bɔɔ mɔde nɛ o du tso yiblii nɛ e he wami.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep hiding inside the central funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the central leaf funnel (the whorl) because it offers moist shelter and soft, fresh plant tissue to eat, protected from heat, rain, and predators.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii (rings) lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhaa he ko ni mli ejɔ kɛ tso mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ehee ni ayeɔ. Buu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on the soil around my pepper plants help them survive the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and helps the plant roots stay hydrated between waterings.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my mature orange trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tso ni ji citrus tso ni eda lɛ niji komɛi?

english: Trimming extra or dead branches opens up the center of the tree to sunlight and airflow. Good airflow dries out wet leaves quickly so diseases cannot take root, and better sunlight access helps the tree produce bigger, sweeter fruit.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛhaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa baai ni efɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya, no hewɔ lɛ helai nyɛŋ atswa shishifãi. Ni hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak with small harvests when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛ ŋmaa fioo pɛ ni mikpaa lɛ? Beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room and food to develop healthy roots and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa aba ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell. If you plant too early, the soil may dry out before the young seeds establish strong roots, causing them to wither and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi dani dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to make food for the plant. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground and helps the vine capture daylight, which directly leads to larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha tsei ahe tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ, ni eye ebua wain tso lɛ ni emɔ hulutsoo be mli la. Enɛ kɛ mɔ yaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know which part of the cassava stem to use as planting material for a good yield?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni esa akɛ akɛdu nii koni ená yibii kpakpai?

english: The middle section of a mature, healthy cassava stem works best because it contains enough stored food and strong buds. Avoid using the soft green top or the very woody base, as they do not sprout as reliably.
ga: Kasava tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyɛ niyenii ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse loo tsei ni akɛfee shishitoo lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraaa yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. The plant pulls food from its older lower leaves to keep the new upper leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ŋwɛi baa heei akwɛ̃.

english: Growing the same crop on the same land continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the soil over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and crops are actively growing. Applying it during heavy rains causes it to wash away, while applying it during severe drought can burn the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. yɛ be mli ni akɛtsu nii yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why do weeds around my pepper plants lower the quality and amount of peppers I pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle Mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ no hewɔ lɛ ebaa pepper ni mihalaa lɛ mli kpakpa kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​shi lɛ.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight away from pepper plants. They also hide insect pests that can spread diseases to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei amli. Amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbala helai kɛba onibii amli lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ
