english: Tiny holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by pest caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, eating the growing shoot. If untreated, these pests weaken the plant and prevent proper cob formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii ni afee jogbaŋŋ lɛ anaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, maize plants automatically move the remaining nitrogen from older, lower leaves up to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or low soil nutrients. The plant drops its blossoms to save energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a natural defense mechanism where the tomato plant reduces its leaf surface area to trap moisture and prevent water loss in intense heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tomato tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ naa.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts together with my maize on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa o-ŋmei lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I avoid applying chemical fertilizer immediately after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔtsi wɔhe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater flushes through flooded soil, washing the fertilizer away from your crops' roots into streams or deep underground before the plants can absorb it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli lɛ afɔ faa ko mli loo shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ dani tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants perfectly adapted to local soil and weather. They take up water, light, and soil nutrients much faster and more aggressively than domesticated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛheɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya kɛ hewalɛ fe shia tsei.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to produce energy for the tuber under the ground. Staking lifts leaves off the wet soil, catching more sunlight while reducing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni aná hulu la babaoo yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ fungal leaf helai lɛ shi.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches if I leave all the young suckers growing around the mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii yɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he lɛ

english: Young suckers compete directly with the main mother plant for food, water, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers leaves more energy for the plant to grow a large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Gbekɛbii lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛkwɛ̃ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy, prolonged rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen, which suffocates the roots and allows rotting fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni oha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I clear away all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need moderate shade to stay cool and retain humidity. Without shade trees, strong sunlight stresses the cocoa, burns the leaves, and reduces pod production.
ga: Cocoa tsei taoɔ hɔɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛhiɛ fɛ̃i mli. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ haa kookoo lɛ haoɔ, ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa pod lɛ feemɔ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and thin bark that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees act as a natural canopy, protecting young cocoa from harsh heat, conserving soil moisture, and reducing water stress until the cocoa leaves grow thick enough to shade themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha nu he haomɔ aba shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baatsi hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I stake them up with wooden poles instead of letting them crawl on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tsei ŋmɔɔ amɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛkpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves into direct sunlight, allowing the plant to catch more light for photosynthesis, which creates the energy needed to grow large underground tubers. It also keeps leaves off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha wain tso lɛ baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa tsei naa kane babaoo kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ baa. Etsiɔ baai hu anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba shi

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main plant food responsible for green leaves and fast growth, and when it is missing, the plant steals green energy from older leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso mli niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa oya. Ni kɛ́ etee lɛ Tsei juɔ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why does my cassava produce bushy top leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground rather than storing food in the tubers below. Tubers need balanced soil nutrients, especially potassium, to swell properly.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ, Tubers he miihia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ potassium koni ekɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is it good for my soil to plant cowpea or groundnuts on my plot before I plant my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baadu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpea and groundnut work with tiny, friendly organisms in the soil to pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the legume stems and roots decay after harvest, they leave natural nitrogen fertilizer behind for the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. naanyobɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ejie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme midday heat, too little water, or an attack by tiny insects like thrips. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. nu fioo tsɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ kɛji akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni wala ahi shi.

english: Why do some of my maize stalks produce tall tassels at the top but no cobs on the side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji yɛ ŋwɛi shi ŋmeii bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Maize plants fail to produce cobs if they lack water or nutrients right when the silks are forming. Heat and drought stress cause the pollen from the top tassel to drop before the cob silks are ready to receive it, preventing seeds from growing.
ga: Abɛi tsei nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli kɛji akɛ siliki lɛ efee pɛ. Dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ haa pollen lɛ shwieɔ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani cob silk lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ waaa.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato eŋɔli shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit while it grows. It often happens when watering is uneven—such as dry spells followed by heavy rains—preventing the roots from taking up calcium steadily.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji akɛ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up, shrink, and show yellow patches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Whitefly populations increase during warm weather, transferring a plant virus from infected bushes to healthy cassava crops.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Whiteflies ayibɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can I tell which plantain suckers are best to cut from an old mat to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ mafo plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ mi-mat momo lɛ nɔ koni mikɛje dumɔwui hee shishi?

english: The best suckers to plant are 'sword suckers'—shots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. They have strong root systems and high energy reserves, whereas 'water suckers' with wide, broad leaves early on grow weakly and yield small bunches.
ga: Suckers ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akwɛ̃ ji ‘sword suckers’ - ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo, yɛ be mli ni ‘suckers’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii.

english: How do I know if tiny, invisible insects are damaging my crops when I cannot see them flying around?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kooloi bibii ni anaaa amɛ lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Be ni minyɛɛɛ mana amɛ ni amɛmiiho kɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tiny airborne pests like thrips and whiteflies are hard to see with the naked eye, but they leave clear signs such as yellowing leaves, twisted shoots, or sticky spots on your crops where they feed.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, tamɔ thrips kɛ whiteflies Ni ewa akɛ akɛ hiŋmɛi baakwɛ. Shi amɛshiɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ, yiteŋ ni etsɔ loo he ni ŋmɔɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ he ni amɛye nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my fruits rot on the branch even when I do not see any big insects eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii lɛ miifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ be mli ni minaaa kooloi wuji komɛi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Very tiny flying insects often puncture the skin of young fruits to lay eggs inside; the larvae then feed inside the fruit, causing it to spoil from the inside out while looking normal on the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni foɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai bibii ahewolo mli koni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ aduawai lɛ. Egboɔ kɛjɛɔ emli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ bɔ ni sa yɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I sometimes see small swarms of tiny insects flying in circles above my farm in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ minaa kooloi bibii akui? Mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ leebi

english: Many small flying insects swarm in rising air currents during cool hours of the day to mate or travel across fields before landing on host plants to feed.
ga: Kplukai bibii babaoo ni foɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ amɛhe afee ekome loo amɛfo ŋmɔji amli dani amɛyashɛ tsei ni amɛyɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do some farmers hang small containers or bottles with liquid inside them on their crop branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsɛnsii bibii loo tsɛnsii ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aniji anɔ lɛ?

english: Those containers are pest traps containing an attractant liquid or chemical medicine that lures flying insects inside, trapping and killing them before they can damage your crops.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsɛnsii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni nu loo tsofai ni gbalaa mɛi kɛbaa jɛmɛ lɛ yɔɔ mli. ni baalaka kooloi bibii ni foɔ yɛ mli lɛ Mɔ ni ogbe amɛ dani amɛfite onibii.

english: How does a hanging container trap attract and kill pests if the bottle is so small?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ mli lɛ agbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni egbe amɛ kɛji akɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ ji bibioo kwraa?

english: The medicine or liquid inside produces a strong scent that attracts specific flying pests from a distance; once the insects enter through small holes in the container, they get trapped and die inside.
ga: Tsofa loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ko baa ni gbalaa kooloi ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii bote bu bibii ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ, amɛmɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ mli.

english: How often do I need to replace or refill the medicine inside hanging insect traps?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni atsake loo awo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ kooloi bibii ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ amɛhe lɛ amli?

english: The chemical scent or liquid inside the trap loses its strength over time, usually within two to four weeks, so you must clean out dead insects and refill the medicine to keep attracting pests.
ga: Tsofai loo nu ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie kooloi bibii ni egboi lɛ ni okɛ tsofa awo mli koni oya nɔ ogbala kooloi bibii lɛ.

english: Is hanging traps with medicine in my farm better than spraying chemical medicine directly on leaf surfaces?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Hanging traps target flying pests directly without covering your whole crop in chemicals, which helps protect beneficial farm insects like bees and reduces chemical residues on the food you harvest.
ga: Amalei ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi ni fɔ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai aha onibii fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ahe ni ehaa tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ niyenii ni okpaa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Can crop pests and diseases travel through the air from my neighbor's field into my farm?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, light winds can easily carry tiny airborne insects, fungal spores, and plant viruses across long distances, allowing pests to enter clean farms without crawling on the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ baanyɛ atere kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, fungal spores. kɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yaa he ko shɔŋŋ oya Eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛboteɔ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli ni amɛshwieee shikpɔŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable crops curling up tightly and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects hiding on the underside of leaves; as they drain plant sap, they distort leaf growth and can spread plant diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Ni amɛhiɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi Beni amɛjieɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tso helai amɛshwã.

english: What simple methods can I use to stop flying insects from reaching my young crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni mafee koni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ fiji lɛ akashɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: You can protect young plants by using fine netting covers, planting tall crops as windbreaks around field edges, or setting up hanging traps early in the planting season.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ ŋshɔŋlooi ni oookɛha amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he ko ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa. aloo mɔmɔ lɛ awo tsɔne ko ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing whenever heavy rain leaves standing water on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hiɔ ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Just like humans need air to breathe, plant roots need oxygen present in the soil spaces. When standing water covers the soil for too long, it pushes out the air, suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb nutrients.
ga: Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai koni amɛmu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli hei lɛ. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛje kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do raised mounds and ridges help my crops survive when my farm gets flooded during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nu eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Building ridges lifts the roots above the standing water level. This creates a dry zone above the flood line where air can remain in the soil, allowing the roots to breathe while excess water drains away.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni afeɔ lɛ woɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa he ko ni egbi yɛ nu afua lɛ nɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Ha shishifãi lɛ amu yɛ be mli ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why is it important to loosen hard clay soil before planting ahead of the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ mli dani adu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Hard clay soil packs tightly and holds onto water, leaving no room for air. Loosening the soil opens up small pockets for oxygen to enter, preventing water from suffocating your crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni ji shikpɔŋ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni emɔɔ nu, ni eshiuuu kɔɔyɔɔ ko kwraa. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha gbɛ bibioo ko aba. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli Enɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekatsi otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the roots of my crops spread out sideways near the top soil instead of growing deep down into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Roots naturally grow toward areas where water and air are balanced. If the deep soil is too hard or waterlogged with low oxygen levels, roots stay near the surface where oxygen is plentiful.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hei ni nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are dying from too much water rather than a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli lɛ miigbo moŋ fe hela?

english: When plants lack oxygen from overwatering, their leaves droop or turn yellow even while the soil is soaked. Disease usually causes spots, leaves dropping rapidly, or sudden drying without waterlogged soil.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fe nine lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ baagbee shi loo amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. baai lɛ shwieɔ shi mra loo egbiɔ trukaa ni shikpɔŋ bɛ ni hiɛɔ nu

english: Why do my tomato plants look wilted right after a heavy rain even though the ground is completely wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water replaces soil oxygen, which damages the roots. When roots suffocate from lack of air, they stop functioning and cannot pump water up to the leaves, causing the plant to wilt even in wet soil.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ. Beni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ Amɛkpaa nitsumɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛpomp nu kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei gboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Is there any crop I can grow in low swampy ground where water always settles during the rainy season?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ hei ni sũ faaa ni nu hiɛɔ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Swamp rice and specific water-tolerant root crops do well in waterlogged areas because their stems have natural channels that transport oxygen from above ground directly down to their roots.
ga: Swamp rice kɛ shishifãi krokomɛi ni nu nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why doesn't rice drown when it sits submerged in flooded fields for long periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwieee shi kɛ́ akɛwo ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes within their stems. These tubes act like snorkels, taking air from above the water surface and carrying oxygen down to keep the submerged roots alive.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifã lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛmuɔ nii. Enáa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi koni shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu lɛ shishi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Should I move my cassava farm to higher land if the valley section gets flooded every year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ aya he ko ni nɔ kwɔ kɛji nu hoɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli daa afi?

english: Yes, cassava tubers rot very quickly in standing water because they cannot survive without air in the soil. Moving cassava to higher, well-drained land prevents crop loss.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ oya waa yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmei kɛtee he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: If I put fish in my flooded rice farm, why do they move away from shallow warm water to deeper parts on hot afternoons?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ loo wo ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ amɛshiɔ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Warm water holds much less dissolved oxygen than cool water. During hot afternoons, fish move to deeper, cooler zones where oxygen levels are higher so they can breathe easily.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ hiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ fioo kwraa fe nu ni mli ejɔ. Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Loo yaa hei ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ koni amɛmu mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees protect young cocoa seedlings from excessive heat and keep the soil moist, helping them survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Plantain suckers steal water and soil nutrients from the main stem. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on lower maize stalks mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed for leaves to stay green and grow well. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer solves this issue.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air through their roots and trap it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that extra nitrogen stays behind to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ eshwɛɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if there is plenty of space on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ he ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Even if space looks adequate, the roots of weeds spread quickly and drink up the food your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni mli wa Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni he ni yɔɔ lɛ fa moŋ Shi jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain causes water to sit on the land without draining away, the roots drown, rot, and spoil under the ground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ha nu lɛ ta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboɔ, ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground into the air, preventing leaf rot and encouraging bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ewoɔ sweet potatoes hewalɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Sprays or natural insect controls are needed to protect new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ nɔ lɛ he miihia koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly damp and providing light shade during very hot afternoons helps flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ tomato he.

english: Why do my cabbage plants produce loose leaves instead of forming a tight, hard head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ yitso ni mli wa, ni wa?

english: Cabbages fail to head when temperatures are too high or when plants are crowded too close together. Proper spacing and consistent watering give the plant enough light and moisture to curl its leaves into a dense ball.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ ajie yitso kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. He ni sa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfo amɛbaai lɛ amli ni amɛfee bɔɔlu ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, cool, and humid conditions. The fungus attacks the pod surface, spreading rapidly if the air cannot circulate freely through the branches or if infected pods are left on the tree.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ he ni edɔ. Fungi lɛ tutuaa pod lɛ hiɛ. Ebaagbɛ eshwa oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli oya. aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the stems of some of my cocoa trees swelling up and turning thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ashishifãi lɛ fuɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a primary symptom of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread from tree to tree by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus interferes with how the tree moves water and nutrients, causing abnormal stem growths and eventual dieback.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ he okadi titri, ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Virus lɛ tsiɔ bɔ ni tsei tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ.

english: What causes tiny dark spots and dying shoots on the young stems of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? Ni gbohii lɛ shwieɔ mikoo tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by mirids, also known as capsids. These tiny bugs pierce the fresh stems and young pods to suck out the sap, injecting poisonous saliva that kills the surrounding plant tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ capsids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ tsɔɔ tsei ahe tsei heei kɛ tsei bibii amli koni amɛnu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ tsei ahe fãji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are most of the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support into full pods. Flowers drop off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree experiences stress from poor rainfall or lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ kwraa ni afee amɛ ŋmeii. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the plant is missing key nutrients in the soil, particularly nitrogen, or that the soil is overly waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and stops them from feeding the plant properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees taking so many years to bear fruit while my neighbor's trees are fruiting early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo cacao tso lɛ woɔ yibii oya lɛ?

english: Fruiting time depends on the variety of cocoa planted, soil quality, and care. Hybrid varieties bear fruit much faster than older traditional varieties, especially when given proper weed control, fertilizer, and protection from intense sun during early growth.
ga: Be ni akɛwoɔ yibii lɛ damɔ kookoo srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kpakpa kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ. Hybrid henɔi lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe blema henɔi ni etsɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ aha jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: During Harmattan, the dry winds and hot sun cause water to evaporate quickly from the leaves. The tree curls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and slow down water loss so it can survive dry spells.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow better when they are planted under big forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants naturally originated in the shade of dense forests. Large shade trees protect wild and young cocoa from harsh overhead sunlight, keep the soil moist, and lower ground temperatures during dry months.
ga: Koo tso lɛ jɛ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo, ni ebuɔ koo mli kookoo kɛ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni jɛɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa aba shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: How does cutting off healthy-looking branches help my cocoa tree yield more cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kokoo tso lɛ ni ewo kookoo babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary inner branches that block sunlight and air. This allows light to reach the main trunk where pods grow, reduces humidity that causes black pod disease, and directs the tree's energy into pod production.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ haa la shɛɔ tso titri lɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Ha hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ aba shi. ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee pods

english: Why will my cocoa trees produce fewer pods if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When planted too close together, trees compete aggressively under the ground for root space and water, and above the ground for light. This struggle leaves every tree weakened and unable to produce maximum fruit yield.
ga: Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ nu. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ena la Ta nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa enyɛŋ ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, a vital nutrient for leafy growth, or that the soil is waterlogged and drowning the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting; you will notice the bottom leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the stem will begin to crack as the tubers grow large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaayɔse akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Tomato flower drop usually happens when temperatures are too high, when the plants do not get enough water, or when there are no insects or wind to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kooloi loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my crops too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which causes them to grow thin and produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are holes suddenly appearing in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji eje kpo trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes in the center whorl of corn leaves are a classic sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which feed on the tender growing leaves inside the plant.
ga: Bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ he okadi, ni yeɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight; plantains grow quickly and provide tall, broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas to shade and protect the fragile cocoa plants.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni kɛlɛ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa cacao tsei ni waaa lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds in my field grow much faster than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted over time to steal water and nutrients from the soil much more aggressively than farm crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same patch of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases that target that crop to build up in high numbers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te pepper tsei ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, or mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, slows down water evaporation from the ground, and blocks weeds from springing up.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ jwɛi mli loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl up during the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and droop in intense heat to protect themselves; it is the plant's natural mechanism to slow down water loss when the sun is drying them out faster than their roots can drink.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe ni egbee shi yɛ la ni naa wa lɛ mli koni ebu ehe he. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi, ejaakɛ hulu lɛ haa tso lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ.

english: This yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means your soil is short on nitrogen. The maize plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does growing groundnuts in the same field with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and traps it in the soil. This natural fertilizer stays in the ground to nourish the maize plants.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin and fall over when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei babaoo amli lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves every plant with too little food, making them grow tall, weak, and thin.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii fioo tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɔ, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food that feeds the underground tuber. Lifting the leaves off the ground on stakes catches more sunlight and stops damp soil from rotting the leaves.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la babaoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside young cocoa protects them from direct heat and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ kookoo plantains bibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in standing water because they cannot get oxygen. Planting cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes in them with little green worms inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl into the tight central growing point of young maize plants to eat tender leaves before they open up.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers drop off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when weather gets too hot or when soil gets too dry. Extreme heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to drop flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen. Ha tso lɛ ajie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last maize harvest to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to grow strong, resist local crop diseases, and yield more harvest. Saved seeds lose these strong qualities over seasons, producing smaller yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛdara waa. Kuu lɛ mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni amɛwoɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ bei lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer into the hole at the exact same time I place the seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ efataaa bu lɛ he yɛ be kome too mli lɛ? Kɛ dumɔwui dulɔ lɛ?

english: Raw chemical fertilizer is very strong and can scorch or burn unsprouted seeds and tender roots. It is safer to apply fertilizer after the seed has sprouted and grown strong roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo eshã dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi ni ekwɛko. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl up as a survival trick to hide their surface from direct heat. This reduces water loss through evaporation when the sun is hottest, helping the plant hold onto moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni akɛteeɔ hiɛ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he. Enɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ baa shi beni hulu lɛ mli edɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the dry Harmattan wind begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: During Harmattan, the dry air pulls water out of cocoa trees faster than the roots can drink it from dry soil. The tree intentionally drops its leaves to conserve moisture in its trunk and branches so it can survive the dry season.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛtsei lɛ kɛ amɛniji lɛ amli lɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy leaves above ground but only small, thin roots below?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii komɛi yɛ shishigbɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen in the soil, it directs all its energy into growing big stems and leaves instead of storing energy underground. This leaves the plant with lush green leaves but tiny tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei ná nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo tsei agboi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ehiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my cowpea bean plants make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have tiny organisms living in their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When the cowpea plant dies, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ cowpeas mli. ni hiɔ shi yɛ eshishifãi amli ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni tsina tso lɛ gboɔ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers without growing any fruit during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, heat damages the pollen inside the tomato flowers, making it impossible for seeds and fruit to form. The plant aborts the unfertilized flowers to save energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kpataa pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui kɛ aduawai afee. Tsei baashi fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my maize plant put flower tassels at the very top before the corn ears show up on the side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi yɛ ŋwɛi dani ŋmãa toi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ afãi lɛ?

english: The tassel at the top makes pollen that needs to drop down through the air onto the soft silks of the corn ear below. Planting tassels high up lets the wind easily carry pollen to fertilize the kernels.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa pollen ni esa akɛ etsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli egbee shi yɛ ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli siliki ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Tassels ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ pollen woɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do my cowpea plants only start flowering during certain months even if I plant them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ lɛ mra moŋ?

english: Certain traditional cowpea varieties track the length of daylight. They wait until the days become shorter in late late season before their internal clock triggers them to stop growing leaves and start making flowers.
ga: Kusum mli tsina ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi nyiɛɔ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ha lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛmɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɛlɛtswai lɛ feɔ kuku kɛyaa be lɛ naagbee dani amɛmli ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ tsirɛɔ amɛ koni amɛkpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni amɛbɔi fɔfɔii afeemɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines try to climb trees and stakes instead of spreading out on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɔ tsei kɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants naturally reach upward to lift their leaves high above other plants where they can capture maximum sunlight. Elevating the leaves off the damp ground also protects them from leaf diseases caused by soil moisture.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei krokomɛi anɔ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep sprouting small shoots around the main stem, and do they hurt my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ni ani amɛmiiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce suckers to multiply themselves. If you leave too many suckers, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, resulting in smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛgbɛ amɛhe amɛshwã. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains akui bibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting upward into cup shapes and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoo ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting is usually a reaction to tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or a virus spread by those insects that disrupts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Is it safe for me to rely only on rainfall for my crops, or should I look for other ways to water them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii? Aloo esa akɛ matao gbɛ kroko ni matsɔ nɔ mawo nakai tsei lɛ nu?

english: Relying only on rain is becoming risky because rainy seasons in Ghana are changing and unpredictable. Using simple irrigation methods or storing rainwater helps protect your crops during unexpected dry weeks.
ga: Nugbɔ pɛ nɔ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ lɛ miifee nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara. Enɛ ji akɛ, nugbɔnɛmɔ be ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ tsakeɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Aloo, nugbɔ nu ni abua naa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe yɛ otsii ni nugbɔ bɛ ni okpaaa gbɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale and dry up when the rain stops for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need water to carry soil nutrients from their roots up into their leaves. When dry weather lasts too long, the plants cannot feed themselves, causing the leaves to dry up and turn pale.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What can I do on my land to keep earning money after the main harvest season is over?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni maya nɔ maná shika beni kpamɔ be titri lɛ eho lɛ?

english: After the main harvest, you can grow short-season vegetables like tomatoes and peppers, or start small-scale poultry farming to maintain steady income while waiting for the next main rains.
ga: Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ Obaanyɛ odu aduawai ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Aloo je kooloi bibii akwɛmɔ shishi koni oná shika ni yaa hiɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers start raising chickens on their farms right after harvesting their main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi jeɔ kooloi akwɛmɔ shishi yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli beni amɛkpa amɛŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Poultry gives farmers quick income from eggs and meat during the dry off-season. Additionally, chicken manure serves as rich, natural fertilizer for the crops in the upcoming planting season.
ga: Kooloi akwɛmɔ haa okwaafoi lɛ náa shika oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ loo mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ. Kooloo ŋmei hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni fa babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why does my maize stalk grow very tall but only produce small, weak ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa babaoo shi amɛwoɔ toi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the stalks stretch upward to fight for sunlight, but the plants lack enough nutrients and space to build large, heavy ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Shi tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ toi wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants start curling up during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves usually curl up because of sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, which multiply quickly in hot conditions and spread crop diseases across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ, ni fɔɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahewɔ, ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwaa ŋmɔji amli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Tired soil makes crops grow slowly, leaves turn light yellow instead of deep green, and yields drop smaller each harvest season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ fiofio. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi fioo yɛ kpamɔ be fɛɛ kpamɔ be mli

english: Why do extension officers tell us to stop burning our weed clearings before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkpa jwɛi ni wɔshãa dani wɔdu lɛ?

english: Burning kills healthy soil organisms and burns away vital topsoil nutrients. Leaving dried weeds to rot naturally feeds the soil and helps it hold onto moisture.
ga: Shãa gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshãa niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni egbi lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant only maize on my entire farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa pɛ yɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting only one crop attracts crop-specific pests that multiply easily, and leaves your income completely unprotected if market prices for that single crop drop.
ga: Tso kome pɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baagbala tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli kooloi ni shwereɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ni ehaa onine shɛɔ shika nɔ kwraa kɛji nakai ŋmɔshi nibii kome lɛ jara ba shi.

english: Why do store-bought certified seeds produce better harvests than seeds I save from my previous crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases, withstand short rains, and produce uniform, high-yielding crops compared to seeds saved over many years.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Edamɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ naa. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛto afii babaoo lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for maize. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves available nutrients from its older leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas can capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, that natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the maize you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall with many big green leaves, but no flowers or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Your soil likely has too much nitrogen fertilizer and not enough phosphorus. High nitrogen makes tomatoes grow bushy and leafy, but tricks the plant into putting its energy into leaves instead of producing fruit.
ga: Ekolɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa hu bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tomatoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛfeɔ baai. Shi elakaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them dry up and drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii babaoo gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support. Many drop off due to dry weather, poor pollination by tiny insects, or because the tree saves energy to mature only a small percentage of pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Tsei babaoo egbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hewɔ. Kplukai bibii ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii loo akɛni tso lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fã bibioo ko pɛ daa.

english: Why do heavy rains during flowering cause my crops to produce fewer seeds or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away pollen from blossoms before wind or insects can spread it. Strong downpours can also physically knock fragile open flowers off the stem before fruit can develop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi amli muji lɛ ahe dani kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni waaa lɛ agbo kɛjɛ tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai aba.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking plant juices, or viruses spread by these insects. They damage the leaves and prevent normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Does it matter which direction I stick my cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, it matters. Cassava stems have small buds pointing upward. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to bend unnaturally to reach sunlight, which weakens the plant and results in smaller tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia. Yucca tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei lɛ abɔle amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha bulbs bibii aba.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam plants if the yam leaves are already high up on stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ eshɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ahe momo lɛ?

english: Weeds near the ground compete directly with yam roots for water and nutrients. Even if yam leaves get sunlight high up, the plant cannot form big tubers if weeds steal its food from the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potato baa lɛ naa hulu la kɛjɛɔ hei ni kwɔ waa moŋ, shi Tsei hu nyɛŋ afee bulbs wuji kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by root pests or soil diseases attacking the roots. Damaged roots prevent the plantain tree from taking up water, causing leaves to dry out as if the plant were in a drought.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli loo helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ haaa plantain lɛ aŋɔ nu. Ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ tamɔ nɔ ni tso lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can check by carefully digging around one sample plant to inspect tuber size, or by observing the plant's leaves, which naturally turn yellow and drop off when the tubers are fully developed.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ he ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bulb lɛ dalɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ Amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi be mli ni bulb lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my mango trees drop so many small green fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Babaoo dani ebatsɔ agbo?

english: Mango trees naturally shed excess fruit if they do not get enough water, or if fungi attack the blossoms during rainy periods. Ensuring proper watering during flowering and maintaining healthy soil helps the tree retain more fruit until harvest.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ baawo yibii babaoo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni akɛ nu awo mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ aduawai babaoo kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Nitrogen moves to new top leaves first, leaving older bottom leaves to starve unless you replenish the soil with organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nitrogen lɛ baafã kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Shi shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ni hɔmɔ aye amɛ. Ja okɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do young cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Young cassava roots cannot reach deep underground water yet. During intense heat, the plant deliberately drops its leaves to reduce water loss, surviving the dry spell until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he lolo. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ baai koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell the exact time to pick my mangoes so they reach the buyer without rotting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be pɔtɛɛ ni ebaahe ni mango lɛ ashɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ ni efiteee lɛ?

english: Pick mangoes when they turn mature green with full, rounded 'shoulders' and yellowish flesh inside. Harvesting too early prevents them from becoming sweet, while harvesting too late causes them to soften and spoil during transport to factories or markets.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ mango ko kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃, ni ‘tsitsii’ ni yɔɔ kokroo kɛ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa amɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee blɛoo ni amɛfite beni akɛ amɛ yaa nitsumɔhei loo jarayeli hei lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack and eat my vegetable leaves more during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The rainy season creates a warm, humid environment with abundant tender leaves. Moths thrive in these conditions and lay hundreds of eggs on your crops, which quickly hatch into hungry caterpillars.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. kɛfata baai bibii babaoo he lɛ, ŋmeii shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi nɛɛ amli. ni okɛ ŋmeii ohai abɔ afɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. ni baatsɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why is it beneficial for my farm if I plant beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for neighboring maize plants while helping to cover the ground and suppress weeds.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall with lots of leaves but failing to give flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ebɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: When tomato plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or grow in heavy shade, they put all their energy into growing foliage instead of producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo amɛdu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot when rainwater collects on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe. When water sits on the farm for days, it smothers the roots and allows soil fungi to breed and rot the root system.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo Nu lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop seeds after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie sleeping in the soil for years and are adapted to sprout immediately when exposed to sunlight and rain, allowing them to steal water and nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to sprout out of the ground after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deeply for the shoot to reach the surface, if the soil lacks moisture, or if underground insects eat the seed before it can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: I see different numbers like 20-10-10 on fertilizer bags at the shop, what do these numbers actually mean?
ga: Yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ, onaa yibɔi tamɔ 20-10-10 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kotokui anɔ. Mɛni yibɔi nɛɛ tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Those numbers tell you the balance of three main plant food nutrients: Nitrogen for green leafy growth, Phosphorus for strong roots, and Potassium for disease resistance and crop yield. A 20-10-10 bag means it has more Nitrogen than Phosphorus or Potassium.
ga: Yibɔi nɛɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni tso mli niyenii titrii etɛ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ ha: nitrogen kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ; Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa. 20-10-10 kotoku tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ nitrogen babaoo fe fɔsfɔs loo potasium.

english: Is fertilizer the same thing as crop medicine like pesticides or fungicides?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ tsei tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ kome?

english: No, fertilizer is like food or vitamins that help a healthy plant grow big and strong, while crop medicines are used to cure diseases or kill insects that are attacking your crops.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ niyenii loo vitamini ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, akɛ tsei ahe tsofai tsuɔ nii kɛtsaa helai loo gbeɔ kooloi ni tutuaa onibii lɛ.

english: Can I just use one single type of NPK fertilizer for all the different crops on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Different crops require different nutrient balances to thrive; leafy crops and maize need higher Nitrogen, while crops that produce fruit or tubers often need higher Potassium and Phosphorus, so using the specific formula made for your crop gives the best yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ srɔtoi koni amɛshwere. Nibii ni akwɛɔ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ he hiaa nitrogen babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii loo ŋmeii lɛ he hiaa potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ okɛ fɔmula pɔtɛɛ ko ni afee aha onibii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why does my maize farm need fertilizer to produce good cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛ ŋmãa kpakpa aba lɛ?

english: Maize feeds very heavily on soil nutrients to grow tall and produce big cobs. Soil loses its natural fertility over time, so fertilizer replaces those essential nutrients so your maize doesn't become stunted or yield small cobs.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji. Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ nakai niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ baatsi o-corn lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ loo ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii aba.

english: How can I tell if my maize plant is hungry and needs extra food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-abele tsei lɛ ni amɛmiitao niyenii babaoo?

english: If your maize leaves begin to turn light green or yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips of the lower leaves, the plant is telling you it lacks Nitrogen and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-corn baa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ V su mli lɛ, je shishi kɛjɛ baa lɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miikɛɛ bo akɛ nitrogen bɛ emli, ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ fɔ.

english: Which type of NPK fertilizer is standard for starting off my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ji nɔ ni akɛjeɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishi?

english: An NPK blend like 20-10-10 or 15-15-15 is typically used early in the maize season because it gives the young plants the initial boost of Nitrogen and root-building nutrients they need.
ga: NPK ni akɛfutuɔ nii tamɔ 20-10-10 loo 15-15-15 lɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ shishijee mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ ni haa amɛshishifãi tswaa lɛ.

english: When is the right time to start giving fertilizer to my maize plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi mi-abele tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ?

english: The best time for the first fertilizer application is usually 1 to 2 weeks after your seeds germinate, when the crop has grown roots that can absorb the nutrients.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ ji otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei yɔɔ shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Should I throw the fertilizer loosely over my farm or place it near each individual plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo mikɛma tso fɛɛ tso he?

english: It is best to place a small measure of fertilizer in a circle or hole about two fingers away from the base of each plant and cover it with soil, which ensures the roots get it and rain does not wash it away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko awo kooyigbɛ loo bu ko mli aaafee inchi 2 kɛjɛ tso fɛɛ tso shishi ni okɛ sũ aha he. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ mli ni nugbɔ shwieee tso lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I apply too much fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can burn the roots and leaves of the plant, causing it to dry up, or it can produce very thick green leaves with small, empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ, ni eha egbi, loo ebaanyɛ eha baai eŋɔli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: What should I do if heavy rain falls right after I put fertilizer on my field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ afee kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii sɛɛ?

english: If you cover the fertilizer with soil when applying it, heavy rain will help dissolve the fertilizer into the soil near the roots instead of washing it away across the surface of the field.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ sũ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe beni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do some crops need to start in a nursery instead of planting the seeds directly on the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aje tsei komɛi ashishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhei moŋ fe ni abaadu yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A nursery acts like a protective home for delicate young seeds. It allows you to care for young plants under shade and protection from heavy rain and pests until they build strong roots to survive in the open field.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shia, ni ebuɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe. Ehaa okwɛɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ anɔ ni obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.
