english: What is the difference between a single-stage nursery and a double-stage nursery?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu kome kɛ ŋwɛitsu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsui enyɔ teŋ?

english: A single-stage nursery keeps seedlings in one location from germination until field planting. A double-stage nursery first germinates seeds in small beds or trays, then moves the healthiest young plants into larger polybags or beds to grow bigger before going into the main farm.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ he kome kɛjɛɔ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Nurseries ni yɔɔ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ dumɔwui klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ saatsoi bibii loo tsɛnsii amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ajieɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ awoɔ poly kotokui loo saatsoi wuji amli koni amɛfee wuji dani amɛboteɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my seedlings are tall enough to be transplanted onto the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu awo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Seedlings are ready when they reach the recommended height for that specific crop, with a thick central stem and 4 to 6 fully opened leaves that show the plant is mature enough to withstand outdoor conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛshɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛkwɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ. Eyɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli tse kɛ baai 4 kɛyashi 6 ni egbele kwraa, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ etsui shi yɛ kponɔgbɛ shihilɛi amli.

english: Why are my nursery seedlings growing very tall, thin, and weak instead of getting thick stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ daraa waa, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch and grow thin when they receive too much shade or are packed too closely together because they are fighting for sunlight. Giving them proper spacing and adequate light helps them grow thick and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala ni amɛbaafee bibioo kɛji amɛná hulutsoo be babaoo loo akɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ejaakɛ amɛmiitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do oil palm seedlings stay in the nursery for many months while vegetable seedlings only stay for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm dumɔwui hiɔ ŋmɔ mli nyɔji babaoo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni aduawai dumɔwui hiɔ shi otsii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Tree crops like oil palm develop slowly and need a long nursery period to establish a strong root bulb, whereas quick-growing vegetables mature fast and will become root-bound if kept in a nursery bag too long.
ga: Tsei tamɔ mu tsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni eheɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli wa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaaná shishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ kotoku mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my young nursery plants wilt and die soon after I plant them out in the open farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This happens because of transplant shock when plants move suddenly from cool nursery shade into hot, full sun. Gradually exposing them to more sun a few weeks before planting helps prevent this.
ga: Enɛ baa mli yɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ hewɔ beni tso lɛ tsiɔ ehe trukaa kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛyaa hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulu la babaoo mli fiofio otsii fioo komɛi dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How deep should I place a nursery seedling when putting it into the ground on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui lɛ awo mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miidu shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should place the seedling at the exact depth it was growing in its nursery container or bed. Burying the stem too deep can cause rot, while planting it too shallow leaves roots exposed to dry out.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo he ni mli kwɔ tamɔ bɔ ni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo saatso lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afu tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha egbo. Shi kɛ́ adu shishigbɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my seedlings right at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early in the rainy season allows young roots to take advantage of continuous soil moisture for several months, helping the plant grow strong enough to survive the dry season.
ga: Dumɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ he sɛɛ nyɔji babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do seeds planted in nursery polybags grow better than seeds planted straight into field soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ nursery polybags amli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Polybags hold rich topsoil and retain moisture directly around the seedling's roots, preventing heavy rains from washing seeds away and stopping weeds from choking the young plant.
ga: Polybags lɛ fiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ dumɔwui lɛ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akafite tsei bibii.

english: Why do I need to reduce the shade cover over my nursery a few weeks before planting out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi otsii fioo komɛi dani adu lɛ?

english: Reducing shade slowly prepares the young plants for the harsh outdoor sunshine and wind on the main farm—a process called hardening off—so they do not burn when planted out.
ga: Shade ni baa shi lɛ baaba fiofio. Saamɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ lá ni hoɔ. Koni akashã beni aduɔ nii lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical pesticides on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the air is cool and wind is calm. Spraying during hot sunshine causes the chemical to evaporate too fast and can scorch your crop leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee kpoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaashã tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves but producing tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller corn ears compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ hulu la he. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaf sap, or a virus spread by these insects that deforms the young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without turning into fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air destroy the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. The plant then drops the useless flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Young crop roots are short and weak. Weeds grow much faster and will steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your young plants before they can establish themselves.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛhe waaa. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni ebaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛma shi.

english: Look at the leaves of your crops. Pale green or yellow leaves, slow growth, purple-tinted leaves, or early leaf loss are clear signs that the soil lacks essential plant food.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ni daa blɛoo, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo baa ni fiteɔ mra lɛ ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ.

english: How can I stop insects from eating my harvested maize while it is stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Dry the maize completely until the grains are hard, clean the storage area thoroughly, and store the grain in airtight bags like PICS bags or treat it with approved grain-preservation dust.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsumɔ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, tamɔ PICS kotoku mli, loo okɛ nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛbuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my corn plants roll up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism against hot weather. By curling its leaves into tight tubes, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaakumɔ awo tsɔnei ni mli wa mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei baa amɛhe nɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea can help bring the green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cowpea plants have lots of leafy green growth but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miikwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to produce heavy leaf growth instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas make their own nitrogen from the air, so they need far less fertilizer than crops like maize.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsina ŋmei lɛ baa ni tsii shwereɔ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in water for plant roots to absorb them. Applying chemical fertilizer to bone-dry soil can burn the crop roots and ruin the fertilizer before the plant can use it.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni fãji yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite tsofa lɛ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juices from young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these small pests early keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when plants don't get enough water, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does striga weed keep damaging my sorghum and maize fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ efiteɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic plant that attaches directly to crop roots to steal food and water. Rotating your cereal crops with leguminous plants like groundnuts or cowpeas helps break the weed's life cycle.
ga: Striga ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tsei ashishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju niyenii kɛ nu. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ jwɛi wala shihilɛ mli

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water collects in the soil around them during heavy rain. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: You should keep only two or three healthy suckers of different ages around the main stem. Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ abɔle tso titri lɛ he - ŋmeii babaoo ni oshiɔ lɛ baaha amɛwuu kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves catch sunlight and stay safe from rot and damp soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ he

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: You can tell groundnuts are ready by digging up a few pods and opening them. If the inside of the shell has dark spots and the nuts firmly fill the skin, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni oootsi ni ogbele mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ ebɔle ŋshɔŋloo lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which helps it make green food for growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it, or the soil may simply need manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ niyenii ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛha dalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aho nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen awo mli.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa baadu tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When planted with maize, they share this free food with the maize plants, helping them grow stronger while reducing your need for chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa Amɛkɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ jaa niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa, yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe ehiaaa amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into tomato fruits when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot during the day or night, the pollen inside the tomato flowers dries up and fails to fertilize the plant. The plant drops the useless flowers to save its water and energy until the weather cools down.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ yɛ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ tso lɛ awo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and the fruits shrink during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun so they lose less water through evaporation. When water is scarce, the plant pulls moisture from the pepper fruits to keep its stem and roots alive, causing the peppers to wrinkle.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Bɔni afee ni nu ni jɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ akafite. Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yibii lɛ amli koni eha shishifã lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi. tsɔ chili lɛ nɔ

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my young maize leaves instead of the older ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms lɛ miitutua mi-corn baai bibii lɛ moŋ fe baai ni edara lɛ?

english: Young maize leaves are soft, tender, and easy for newly hatched caterpillars to chew and digest. Older leaves are tougher and harder for small pests to eat, so armyworms naturally target the fresh leaf funnels.
ga: Abɛi bibii ahe baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe jɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo kɛha ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ akɛ amɛaaye ni amɛye. Baai ni egbɔ lɛ mli wa ni ewaa kɛha kooloi bibii akɛ amɛaaye, no hewɔ lɛ fallworms lɛ kwɛɔ baa heei ni hoɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The heavy rain and high humidity create the perfect moist environment for a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread. The fungus enters through the skin of the cocoa pod, rots the beans inside, and turns the entire pod dark and hard.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Fuŋ lɛ boteɔ kookoo tso lɛ hewolo mli. ni eha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fite ni eha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ fee ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when the land stays flooded with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? He ni nu afua yɔɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When water logs the soil for too long, oxygen cannot enter, causing the root tissues to suffocate, die, and attract rotting fungi.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛŋ abote mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ, ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do onion leaves fall over and turn dry when the crop is almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sabala baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: When an onion bulb finishes growing, the neck of the leaf natural loses strength and collapses. This signal shows that the plant has stopped feeding the leaves and is transferring all remaining energy into storing food in the bulb under the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, baa lɛ kuɛ he waaa ni efoɔ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa niyenii yeli kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ miitsu nii kɛmiiya niyenii ni atoɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my soil is soft enough for my yam tubers to swell big under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni efuu lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing outward against the dirt. If the soil is hard and packed, the tuber gets choked and stays small or bent, but loose, raised mounds allow the yam to expand easily in all directions.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ kponɔgbɛ ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Yitso lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ bibioo loo ebɔle ehe. Shi gɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewó nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he mlɛo.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two different plant parents to give high yield, but their offspring do not keep those same strong qualities. If you replant saved hybrid seeds, the resulting crop will produce uneven growth and much lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ adɛŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi amɛshwiei lɛ náaa nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji odu hybrid dumɔwui heei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ Tsei ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baaná dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build strong green leaves, so adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does covering the soil around my tomato plants with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle o-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil too quickly, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from stealing water and nutrients.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the pepper plant and damages its flower pollen. To save its own water and energy, the plant naturally sheds its blossoms instead of trying to form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ e diɛŋtsɛ ehe moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing twisted yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsake lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that bite the leaves. Using stem cuttings from healthy, disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best way to keep your farm safe.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni akɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baatsu nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil gets very dry and then very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbi waa, ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants turn yellow and rot when rain leaves standing water on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa nu taraa miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. When standing water covers the roots for days, it starves them of oxygen, causing the roots to rot and the plant to choke.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants end up competing with one another for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them properly ensures each stalk grows thick and produces large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb up tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makudɔ sweet potato wain tso ko kɛya tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines up onto tall stakes spreads out the leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which sends energy down to make big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ baaha etso lɛ baagbɛ eshwa koni ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi koni ekɛha bulb agbo lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes, which means they have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni ooodu yɛ abele ni odu sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their tiny pods before they can grow full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? yɛ yibɔi babaoo mli dani eda kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ mli

english: This is called cherelle wilt, and it is a natural self-defense mechanism. If the cocoa tree feels it doesn't have enough water, shade, or nutrients, it drops small pods so it can save enough strength to keep the remaining ones healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Ni eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛji cacao tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Ebaajie ŋmeii bibii. kpo bɔni afee ni ená hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaha cacao tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I use water from a nearby river that looks polluted or oily to irrigate my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni mli ewo muji loo fɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Water that contains heavy metals or pollutants can be absorbed by your crops, stunting their growth and making the harvest unsafe to eat. Using clean groundwater from a borehole or testing your water source first ensures your plants and soil stay healthy.
ga: Nu ni dade ni tsii loo nibii ni fiteɔ nii yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. ni haa shweremɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni he tse ni jɛɔ nubu ko mli lɛ tsu nii loo aka he ni nu lɛ jɛɔ lɛ akwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is underground borehole water safe to pour directly onto my crops and soil?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafɔse miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Borehole water is generally clean and free from surface pollutants like chemical runoff or heavy metals. However, it can sometimes be cold or high in minerals, so letting it sit in a holding tank or pond before watering your crops helps it match the ambient temperature and settle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ nubu mli lɛ mli tse ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni fiteɔ nu, tamɔ tsofai ni hoɔ loo dade ni tsii. Shi kɛlɛ, bei komɛi lɛ, shika tsuru ni mli ejɔ baanyɛ ahi mli loo shika tsuru ni yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha eta nu ŋtayaa loo nu ŋshɔ mli dani okɛ nu awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akpã gbee ni ekɛ ehe awo mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and curling up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because they lose water faster than their small root systems can absorb it. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby acts like a natural umbrella, protecting the young trees until they grow stronger.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ. E nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni shwieɔ nu. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture before the sun causes rapid evaporation. Watering under the hot afternoon sun can stress plants, cause leaves to burn from water droplets acting like magnifying glasses, and create fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu la lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Baai shãa kɛjɛɔ nu mli nu ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the rest of the plant is green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for green leafy growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the newer leaves at the top, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, drought, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy and water rather than investing it into growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ shika awo aduawai akwɛmɔ mli lɛ

english: Can I put dry fertilizer directly against the main stem of my crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem will burn the plant's skin and roots because of concentrated salts in the fertilizer. You should always place fertilizer in a small ring or row a few inches away from the stem so roots can safely reach for it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashã yɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai bibii loo ŋwɛi ŋtayaai 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing fat roots underground, the plants will waste energy growing tall and thin stems to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa, amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo koni amɛná la.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing in the same dirt?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Weeds act like nutrient thieves in your field. They aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, which weakens your plants, slows their growth, and reduces your total yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔji amli. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ kɛ ekãa. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. shweremɔ blɛoo ni okɛ nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my crops get sick if I plant the same crop in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly allows pests and soil diseases that target that specific plant to build up in high numbers in the ground. Rotating different crops starves these pests out and keeps your soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsɔɔ nakai tso lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature enough to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha nikpamɔ, ni obaanyɛ ole be ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and burning during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight; without shade crops like plantains providing cover, the intense heat scorches the plant and dries out the roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baashã tso lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: What causes ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes in young maize foliage are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the central leaves of the plant and eat the leaves before the maize can grow fully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ daa kwraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fãa yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is dry or after rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should always be applied when the soil is moist after rain, because water helps dissolve the nutrients so the plant roots can take them in without burning the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ ni amɛshãaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat or water stress, causing the crop to drop its flowers to preserve energy and survive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to stick tall wooden poles next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb tall poles to lift their leaves up toward sunlight, which gives the plant energy to feed and grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ koni ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtaoɔ niyenii ni amɛduɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do weeds growing close to my vegetables affect my harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your vegetables, which weakens the main crop and reduces the size and amount of harvest you get.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ o-vegetables lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni okɛ ŋmaa ni onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help fix the soil for my next crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil so crops like maize can grow better afterward.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni tsei tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow with dark spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with dark spots near the bottom of a tomato plant are usually caused by fungal diseases that spread from damp soil splashing onto the leaves during rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baa lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋŋ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ baa.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground season after season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why is it important for me to buy certified seeds instead of just using seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli kɛkɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests and diseases, germinate reliably, and give high yields, whereas seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength over time and produce weaker plants.
ga: Certified seeds have been specifically bred to resist local insects and diseases. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Meanwhile, seeds collected from previous harvests lose strength over time and produce weaker plants.

english: Why do some vegetable seeds like tomatoes need to grow in a nursery before I move them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu aduawai amli dumɔwui komɛi, tamɔ tomato yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani akɛya ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are tiny and delicate, so growing them first in a protected nursery guards them against heavy rain, hot sun, and pests until they develop strong roots for the main field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Therefore, planting it early in a protected nursery will protect it from heavy rains. hot sunlight and pests until they have strong roots for their main area.

english: Should I burn the bush on my farm before planting, or is it better to clear it without fire?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu loo ehi akɛ majie amɛ ni la bɛ mli?

english: Clearing without fire is better because burning destroys vital organic nutrients in the soil and kills beneficial organisms, while clearing allows dead weeds to rot and naturally feed your crops.
ga: La ni bɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhaa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) retains soil moisture during dry spells, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop area.
ga: Mulching with dry grass (mulching) helps preserve soil moisture during the dry season. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stop growing when I plant too early before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ midu lɛ mra tsɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Without consistent rainfall, young plant roots cannot absorb nutrients from dry soil, causing stress that turns leaves yellow and slows down growth.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits when I plant the seeds very close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants that produce small yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cassava lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, providing free natural fertilizer that helps crops like cassava grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. They provide free natural fertilizer that helps crops such as cassava grow better.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: How do weeds harm my crops if there seems to be enough open space on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than regular crops, so they steal essential moisture, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's root zone.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa waa, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in my house?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mishia lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drying maize thoroughly and storing it in airtight containers or hermetic (PICS) bags cuts off oxygen, preventing insects from multiplying and destroying your stored grain.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmã jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (PICS) mli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafee babaoo ni amɛkafite dumɔwui ni ato lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems recommended by extension officers is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed inside the young leaves of the maize plant during the day and leave their waste behind, which weakens the crop if left untreated.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛshiɔ amɛjwɛi lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my young maize crop needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ he miihia ŋmãa?

english: If your maize leaves are pale yellow instead of deep green, or if the lower leaves show a yellow inverted 'V' shape starting from the tips, your soil is low in nitrogen and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji o-corn baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ loo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ jieɔ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kpo ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my sweet potato roots small and thin even though the leafy vines are very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes sweet potatoes to focus all their energy on producing leaves instead of expanding their roots. Using low-nitrogen, high-potassium nutrients encourages bigger tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni amɛbaafee lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛshwã. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni nitrogen faaa yɛ mli ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo ŋmeii wuji lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves scorch and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants require shade to shield their tender leaves from harsh sunlight and maintain moisture around their roots. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, intense sun scorches the plants and stunts their growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji tsei loo dumɔwui ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛɛɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã tso lɛ ni ebaaha edalɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant suffers from irregular watering. Extreme heat causes stress that prevents pollination, so the plant sheds its flowers.
ga: Tomato blossoms will drop when temperatures are too high or when the plant suffers from inconsistent watering. Extreme heat causes stress which inhibits pollination. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants lose water through leaves faster than their roots can drink during the hottest hours of the day. They usually bounce back by evening, but applying mulch around the roots keeps the soil cool and reduces heat stress.
ga: Pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can drink it during the hottest hours of the day. Bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa gbɛkɛ. But mulching around the roots will help keep the soil cool and reduce heat stress.

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This results in thin, tall stems and tiny ears of corn, lowering your total harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛnáa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii. Enɛ haa nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back so quickly after I clear my field with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade shwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spear grass has strong underground roots called rhizomes that remain alive even after you cut the grass above ground. Clearing requires digging up the deep root network or using appropriate herbicides.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes. ni yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ofolɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ po. Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ biɔ ni atsa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or kept in hot, unventilated spaces. Storing undamaged tubers off the ground on raised, shaded racks with good air circulation prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Keeping intact bulbs in the ground on a raised, shaded shelf with good air circulation will prevent rotting.

english: Why are agricultural extension officers telling me to plant my crops in straight lines using wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ mɛi akɛ amɛkɛ tsei atsu nii ni amɛkɛdu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines using poles helps you measure the right distance between plants. This ensures every crop gets enough sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil without competing with its neighbors, making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Planting in a straight line using stakes allows you to properly measure the distance between plants. This ensures that all plants receive enough sunlight, water and nutrients from the soil without competing with their neighbors. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together instead of using line spacing?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ line spacing baatsu nii?

english: When crops are crowded together, their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another, and their roots fight for nutrients. This leads to thin, weak stems, smaller yields, and a higher risk of fungal diseases spreading between plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. produce less And there is a high risk that fungal diseases will spread between plants.

english: How does setting up straight rows help protect my farm from weeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe?

english: Straight rows leave clear paths between your crops. This allows you to walk through easily to weed with a hoe or equipment without accidentally cutting or damaging your growing crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni ja lɛ feɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmei loo dɛŋdade nyiɛɔ jwɛi amli oya. ni okɛ oshara akafo loo ofiteee oŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do pests and farm animals seem to target my crops mostly in the late afternoon and evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many insects, birds, and rodents avoid the hot midday sun to save energy. They become most active in the cooler late afternoon and evening hours when crops are resting and easier to feed on.
ga: Kplukai, okpoi, kɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛkafite hewalɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii waa yɛ shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe ni efee mlɛo akɛ abaakwɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to stay on my farm until evening to watch over my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ koni makwɛ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Many destructive pests and destructive animals begin feeding right before sunset. Checking or guarding your field in the evening allows you to catch and stop pest attacks before they eat your crops overnight while you are asleep.
ga: Kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ babaoo jeɔ niyenii yeli shishi dani hulu lɛ nyɔ shi. Inspecting or protecting your crops in the evening allows you to catch and stop pest attacks before they eat your crops overnight while you sleep.

english: How can pests eat up an entire harvest so quickly if I don't guard my field daily?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ miŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ oya kɛji mikwɛɛɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ daa gbi?

english: Pests often move in large numbers or multiply rapidly when crops reach a tender, sweet stage of growth. If left undisturbed, a swarm or group of animals can destroy leaves and stalks overnight, leaving nothing behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fãa gbɛ babaoo loo amɛshwereɔ oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ shɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ mlɛo, ni ŋɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa lɛ, kooloi akui loo kui baanyɛ afite baai kɛ tsei ahe nyɔɔŋ kome ni amɛshiŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Why are my crops most vulnerable to pest damage when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite amɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ?

english: Young crop plants have soft, tender leaves that are easy for pests to chew and digest, and the plants are not strong enough yet to recover from losing their leaves.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya ni amɛyeɔ amɛmli. Ni tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa lolo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hewalɛ kɛjɛ amɛbaai ni elaaje lɛ mli.

english: Why am I seeing different pest behaviors and farm problems this year compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔ mli naagbai srɔtoi yɛ afi nɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pest patterns change with shifting weather, rainfall timing, and local farming activities. Changes in temperature or rain can cause new types of insects to hatch earlier or in larger quantities than usual.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsakeɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, nugbɔnɛmɔ bei, kɛ akutsoŋ okwaayeli nitsumɔi. Tsakemɔi ni baa hulutsoo loo nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi heei afɔ mra loo amɛfa babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why do pests prefer eating my planted crops over the wild weeds growing nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Crops are cultivated to be tender, juicy, and rich in nutrients, making them much easier and more rewarding for pests to eat than tough, bitter wild weeds.
ga: Aduɔ tsei koni amɛfee bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli nu ni amɛmli niyenii kpakpai babaoo. Ehaa eyeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he fe koo mli jwɛi ni wa ni mli edɔ.

english: How do modern farming methods recommended by officers help my crops survive unpredictable seasons?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi ni onukpai lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ be ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli?

english: Modern practices like proper row spacing, timely monitoring, and strategic planting strengthen crop root systems and boost plant health, making crops better able to withstand pest attacks and weather changes.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔi tamɔ sɛɛkuu ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ mlikwɛmɔ yɛ be naa kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛduɔ nii Wajeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi.

english: If foreign buyers want to buy my crops, how do I keep them fresh while waiting for the transport to arrive?
ga: Kɛji maŋsɛɛ hɔlɔ ko miisumɔ ni ehe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi ehee be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mi nibii ni mikɛmajeɔ lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Crops continue to breathe and lose moisture after harvest. Storing them in cool, shaded, well-ventilated areas or using proper storage crates slows down spoilage while waiting for buyers.
ga: Tsei yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛhe shwieɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli. Aloo nibii ni akɛtoɔ adekai ni sa ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni nibii ni efite lɛ asɛɛ afo be mli ni amɛmɛɔ mɔ ni baahe lɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes rot quickly after I harvest them from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested root crops have delicate skin that easily gets scratched, allowing fungi and bacteria to enter. Curing them in a warm, dry, shaded spot for a few days toughens the skin and extends their shelf life.
ga: Shishifãi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwieɔ shi oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ atsa lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ, ni egbi, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaawaje hewolo lɛ ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow in different sizes, and how can I get them to all grow big and uniform?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daa kɛyashɛɔ srɔtoi lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha tsei lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Uneven growth happens when plants compete for sunlight, water, or nutrients due to irregular spacing or uneven fertilizer application. Spacing seeds properly and applying nutrients evenly helps crops grow to uniform sizes.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji tsei kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ gbɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ po ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ adaramɔ feɔ ekome.

english: Why should I buy improved seed varieties instead of just using seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli kɛkɛ baatsu nii?

english: Improved seed varieties are specifically bred to resist local pests and diseases, mature faster, and yield higher-quality produce that market buyers prefer compared to older saved seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi bibii kɛ helai, amɛshwere oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jarayelɔi sumɔɔ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni etsɛ ni ato lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my seeds so my crops are ready when market prices are high?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo beni jara nɔ jara wa lɛ.

english: Every crop has a fixed growth duration (such as 3 months for maize). By counting backward from the months when market demand and prices usually peak, you can schedule your planting date accordingly.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni amɛdaraa (tamɔ nyɔji 3 kɛha ŋmãa), ni akaneɔ kɛjɛɔ nyɔŋ ni jarayeli nibii kɛ jara fɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ oto gbi ni obaadu lɛ yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow even though there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate a lack of essential nutrients in the soil, particularly nitrogen. Adding organic manure or a balanced fertilizer restores the soil nutrients needed for healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields if I plant maize on the same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally restores nitrogen to the soil and restores crop yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper fruits get small dark spots on them before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji lɛ? Dani amɛbaafee klalo akɛ amɛbaabua naa?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by insect bites or fungal infections triggered by excess humidity. Using field traps and applying appropriate organic or mild fungicides early protects the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ mɔ loo ŋmeii ni hulutsoo babaoo kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛtsɔ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni waaa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures are too high or when plants experience water stress during the flowering stage. Mulching around the roots keeps the soil cool and moist to prevent flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni tsei naa nu he haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ akashwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water or if they are dying of thirst?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo kumai miigbe amɛ?

english: Under-watered crops wilt, curl their leaves, and feel dry, while over-watered crops turn pale yellow and look soft because flooded roots cannot breathe. Checking the soil moisture 2 inches deep helps you balance watering.
ga: Tsei ni nu efite lɛ gboɔ, baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe egbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni nu babaoo náa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo ejaakɛ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ 2 inches lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ nu ni okɛhaa lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily scorch in harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides shelter and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I plant cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔsemɔ lɛ atsɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni afolɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems must be planted with the leaf buds or nodes pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the new growth to bend around, wasting energy and causing lower crop yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yitso lɛ shwere kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso hee lɛ atsɔ ŋwɛi. Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding decomposed animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves recover their green color and support grain growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does mixing dark, rotten leaves into my soil help crops grow better than hard red soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni tsuɔ ni egbo ni mikɛfutuɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe sũ tsuru ni wa lɛ?

english: Decomposed organic material acts like a sponge, holding onto water and releasing natural plant food slow over time, which helps plant roots spread and absorb nourishment easily.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjaraa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if the ground has enough moisture to plant seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the land receives several steady rains that wet the soil a full hand's depth down. Planting after just one light rainfall can cause seeds to sprout and dry out quickly if the rain stops.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be shii abɔ, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi ebaashɛ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to stay small and produce poor harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miifee bibioo ni ehaaa yibii kpakpai aba lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving weeds in the field steals essential nourishment away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and white waste inside the centers?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaves of the maize plant. Catching the infestation early and applying proper controls or neem-based sprays helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni aaamɔ helai ni baa lɛ mra Ni akɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa loo neem tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) growing from one root system forces them to compete for nutrients. Pruning to leave only two or three healthy shoots ensures the main stem produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛná ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã kome mli lɛ, no haa amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛji akɛ afolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ niji agboi ni tsii akwɛ̃.

english: This issue is known as blossom-end rot and occurs when tomato plants lack calcium or experience uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots transport calcium to the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the plant. Lifting the vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which feeds the growth of large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni ji niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ adalɛ

english: How can I check if the maize seeds or cassava suckers I want to buy are healthy before planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui loo ŋmãa ŋmeii ni misumɔɔ ni mahe lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani madu?

english: Look for seeds or stems that are clean, firm, and free from insect holes, rot, or strange spots. Healthy planting material ensures your crops start strong and are less likely to bring diseases into your field.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni he tse, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni kooloi akutsei, ŋmeii, loo hei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ helai baaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to check the leaves and stems of my crops regularly for signs of disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli daa koni mana kɛji hela ko yɛ he lɛ?

english: Checking your crops often helps you spot pests or diseases early before they spread to the whole farm, allowing you to treat them quickly and save your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii amli kwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai mra. Dani amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa amɛ oya ni okɛ onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ toɔ.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings look weak and droopy after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants causes transplant shock because their roots are disturbed and exposed to strong sunlight. Planting late in the afternoon and watering them immediately helps them recover faster.
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ haoɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shwane mli ni awo lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ oya.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This makes them grow weak and thin, producing small cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: I keep feeding and watering my cassava, so why is it taking so long for the tubers to grow under the soil?
ga: Miyaa nɔ mihaa ŋmei lɛ niyenii ni mihaa lɛ nu. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need time to first build strong stems and leaves so they can make food. Only after the plant is well established will it start storing that energy into big tubers.
ga: Tsei taoɔ be koni amɛma amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni wa dani amɛfee niyenii. Beni tso lɛ etswa shi pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebɔi nakai hewalɛ lɛ tomɔ yɛ ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds eat the food and drink the water in the soil that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds removes this competition so your crops get all the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ nii ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehe hiaa ni otsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛyaa. koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ

english: Do my crops still need fertilizer if the soil in my farm already looks dark?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nii lɛ he miihia mi lolo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ?

english: Yes, because as crops grow, they consume specific soil nutrients like nitrogen and potassium. Adding fertilizer replaces what the growing crop takes out so it doesn't starve.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ kɛ́ tsei dara lɛ Amɛyeɔ sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ nɔ ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ koni hɔmɔ akaye lɛ.

english: Will my crops get troubled and stop growing if they don't get water during a hot dry spell?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná he sɛɛ ni amɛkpa shweremɔ kɛji amɛnáaa nu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, extreme heat and lack of water cause severe stress to plants. The leaves will wilt to save moisture, and the plant will pause its growth until it gets water again.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei anɔ. Baai lɛ gboɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni tso lɛ baakpa dalɛ be kukuoo ko kɛyashi ebaaná nu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without turning into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pepper pods?

english: Flowers drop when the plant is stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of specific nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni bɛ lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does keeping my crops healthy throughout their growth help me get better prices from market buyers?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara kpakpa kɛjɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ adɛŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Healthy crops produce larger, cleaner produce that stays fresh longer during transport to the market. Market women pay more for high-quality crops because their buyers prefer them.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ adumɔi wuji ni he tse. Enɛ baahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ. Jarayeli yei woɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and turning yellow in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a natural shield that provides shade and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ daa lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ kɛha mi-sweet potato tso lɛ?

english: Yam plants grow long vines that need sunlight to create food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and allowing maximum sunlight to reach the leaves so the tubers can grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ duɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Tsi fitemɔ naa ni oha hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. koni anyɛ afee yitso lɛ agbo

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of burying them flat under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slight angle keeps some buds above the ground to sprout leaves easily, while the buried section develops roots into deep, healthy tubers in the loose topsoil.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. yɛ be mli ni fã ni afu lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bulbs ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etse lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even when it is raining well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy leaf color and leads to bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná su ni yeɔ emuu ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why should I rotate my field with cowpeas or beans instead of planting maize in the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔji ni mikɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ewo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating with leguminous crops like cowpeas actually puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Legumes ni tsakeɔ amɛhe tamɔ cowpeas lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.
