english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them stay healthy during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts as a protective blanket. It blocks the sun from evaporating water from the soil, keeps the roots cool, and reduces the need for frequent watering.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni afɔɔ amɛ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Why do my plantain shoots produce smaller bunches after two or three harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots produce extra underground shoots called suckers that steal water and nutrients from the main fruiting stem. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one strong replacement keeps fruit bunches large.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ tsei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi nɔ kome pɛ ni mli wa ni akɛto najiaŋ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai babaoo aba.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without producing fruit due to extreme heat stress, improper watering, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and allowing good airflow around plants helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni esaaa loo pollination ni esaaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli Tsei yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the funnels of my young maize plants have ragged holes and small waste dropping in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the leaf funnels of maize are a classic sign of fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the tender inner leaves. Early inspection and applying safe targeted treatments inside the leaf funnels stops the damage.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ fall armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yeɔ nii. Nibii amlipɛimɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ni helatsamɔi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ haa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning thick and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents severe leaf curling and protects your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ naa ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How can I turn just one plantain sucker into many plants for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ plantain tso kome matsɔ tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Using rapid multiplication techniques like the split-corm method, you can cut one healthy plantain sucker into small pieces and nurse them to create hundreds of new shoots for planting.
ga: Kɛ okɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ eshwaa oya, tamɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajaa bulb mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli bibii bibii. No sɛɛ lɛ, kwɛmɔ amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii heei ohai abɔ kɛha dumɔ.

english: How long do I need to wait to start collecting new planting material from my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mabɔi dumɔ nii heei ni jɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anaabuamɔ?

english: With good farm management, young shoots and multiplication materials start producing within a few months, allowing you to harvest your first batch around 6 to 7 months after starting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, abaaje ŋmeii bibii kɛ nibii ni akɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ shishi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa onáa oklɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 7 sɛɛ beni obɔi nitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my crop yield a smaller amount during the second harvest than the first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli fe klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: As plants age and nutrients in the soil get used up, the energy of the mother plant drops, which naturally causes later harvests to yield smaller quantities than the first batch.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ daraa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiho lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa sɛɛ mli ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I harvest my crops in batches over time instead of taking everything at once?
ga: Mibaanyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Yes, many crops allow for continuous harvesting where you can collect a large batch first, and then return every two months to pick mature smaller batches.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli, kɛji akɛ obua ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo naa klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ku osɛɛ oya daa nyɔji Enyɔ koni oyahala kuu bibioo ko ni eda fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: How often should I return to my field to remove excess side shoots from my plants?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maku misɛɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miyajie tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: It is best to check your field every two months to cut or transplant side shoots so they do not steal nutrients from the main plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa nyɔji enyɔ koni ofolɔ loo ojie sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli.

english: How many new planting shoots can I realistically get from a single stem in half a year?
ga: Tso kome mli tsei heei enyiɛ manyɛ makwɛ yɛ afi fã mli?

english: If you use proper nursing techniques and take good care of the soil, a single healthy stem can multiply into hundreds of new planting shoots within 6 to 7 months.
ga: Kɛ okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii ni okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii heei ohai abɔ yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 7 mli.

english: Is it normal for a plant to stop producing as many shoots as it gets older?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ tsei baakpa ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, plant growth follows a cycle where the initial growth burst produces the highest number of shoots, while later rounds produce fewer stems as the plant's energy declines.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei adalɛ nyiɛɔ shihilɛ ko ni shishijee dalɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa lɛ sɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni kpokpaa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baafee fioo be mli ni tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Do I need to buy new seeds every season to expand my farm size?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mahe dumɔwui heei daa afi koni mikɛgbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, you can generate your own planting materials by multiplying shoots from your existing healthy crops to cover larger areas of land over time.
ga: Dabi, obaanyɛ ofee bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔ nii kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ momo lɛ amli ŋmeii babaoo ni okɛbaafata he koni ekɛha he ko ni da yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How many months break should I leave between my harvesting visits?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ esa akɛ mafo mli yɛ kpamɔɔ saramɔi lɛ ateŋ?

english: Leaving a gap of about two months between harvests gives the remaining young plants enough time to grow big enough for the next collection.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi aaafee nyɔji enyɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to the soil if I keep harvesting shoots from the same plant over six months?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mibua tso kome mli ŋmeii anaa nɔ ni fe nyɔji enumɔ?

english: Continuous harvesting drains nutrients from the soil, which is why yield amounts drop over time unless you support the soil with manure or fertilizer.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni afee lɛ ayibɔ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow big, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients too deep into the soil for roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Aloo akɛni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he hewɔ lɛ?

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni miduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or when tiny pests damage the blossoms before fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii Fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cassava and maize together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting cassava and maize together lets you harvest maize quickly within three months while the slow-growing cassava takes over the land later, giving you two harvests from one piece of land.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, ehaa onáa ŋmãa oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my cabbage leaves and why is it bad for my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-cabbage baa lɛ nɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ ehiii?

english: Small green caterpillars are eating the leaves to grow. When leaves are destroyed, the plant cannot capture sunlight to make food, preventing the cabbage from forming a solid, heavy head.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye baai koni amɛdara. Kɛji baai lɛ fite lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ amɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haaa kaabii lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni etsiii.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and bent instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil in high mounds to expand easily. If the soil is hard or full of rocks, the growing tuber gets trapped and deformed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he miihia sweet potatoes yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ amli koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Bulb ni adu lɛ baakã shi ni ebaafite.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up like cups during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoo yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day to reduce water loss through their leaves and protect themselves from burning in strong sunlight.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die soon after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots that burn easily under full sun; they need shade trees like plantains around them to keep the moisture in the air and soil while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ koni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why is my cowpea plant growing lots of big bushy leaves but producing very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cowpeas put all their energy into growing heavy foliage instead of flowers, because cowpea plants naturally make their own nitrogen from the soil.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa cowpea yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛduɔ tsei ni tsii yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What causes this white dusty powder on the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni kɛ sũ yɛŋ ni yɔɔ eggplant baai anɔ yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: That white powder is a common plant disease called powdery mildew, which spreads in humid weather and blocks sunlight from reaching the leaf, weakening the plant.
ga: Powda yɛŋ lɛ ji tso hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so thin and weak if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that drink the water, steal the fertilizer, and block the sunlight that your main crops need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, amɛnuɔ nu, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa otso titri lɛ koni etsɔ hewalɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it helpful to leave my farmland to rest for a few years before planting on it again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mashi midumɔi lɛ afii fioo komɛi dani madu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving land idle, or fallowing, allows the soil to naturally restore its depleted nutrients, break pest and disease cycles, and improve its structure as decaying wild plants fertilize the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashiɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ loo nɔ ko bɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akumɔ ni aha eshishitoo lɛ aya hiɛ beni koo mli tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ.

english: What steps should I take when preparing a farm that has been left overgrown for a long time?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa ŋmɔ ko ni ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni esaaa lɛ?

english: You should cut back dense bush, clear dead wood, check for pests, and trim tall branches to open up the canopy so sunlight can reach and warm the soil before you plant.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ. tso ni egbo Kwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmeii yɔɔ mli Ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ amli koni ogbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ dani odu.

english: When clearing wild trees off my land for a new farm, how do I know which trees to keep?
ga: Beni mijieɔ koo mli tsei kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔ hee Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ?

english: Keep trees that provide light shade or act as windbreaks without creating heavy overhead leaf cover, and cut down trees that hold too much water or block all daylight from reaching young crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ tsiɔ naa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsei ahe tsei ni tsii akawo oyitso nɔ. ni afolɔ tsei ni hiɛɔ nu babaoo loo ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Can big trees on my farm hurt my smaller plants if rainwater drips off their leaves onto them?
ga: Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye tsei bibii awui. Ani manyɛ maná minɔ lɛ? Kɛji nugbɔ nu jɛ baai amli kɛba tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy water droplets continuously dripping from tall tree leaves can physically damage tender young shoots and create overly damp conditions that encourage leaf rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ ahe baai amli be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine ni woɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ baa.

english: Why are the small crops planted near big forest trees growing much slower than the ones in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ daraa blɛoo kwraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Big trees steal nutrients and water from the ground while blocking essential sunlight and dropping excess moisture, which slows down the growth of smaller crops underneath.
ga: Tsei wuji juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know when it is time to prune or cut back branches from large trees around my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mafo loo maŋɔ tsei ni eda ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: You should prune branches when they create a thick canopy that prevents direct sunlight from reaching your crops or when heavy dew and rain gather on their leaves and drop onto plants below.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei aniji amli kɛ́ amɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse koni hulu la akashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Aloo beni bɔ́ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛshwieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops need direct sunlight instead of sitting under heavy tree shade all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mata tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ ashishi gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight gives plants the energy they need to make food, strengthens their stems, and helps dry off leaf surface moisture to prevent diseases.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Woɔ tso lɛ shishi Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ koni hela akamɔ.

english: Will strong sunlight burn my young plants, or is full sun good for them?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã mi dumɔwui lɛ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi aha amɛ?

english: While some crops need mild shade when very young, most mature crops thrive in full sun because intense sunlight boosts crop growth, reduces moisture-loving pests, and improves yields.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi he hiaa hulutsoo be lɛ. Beni miji gbekɛ fioo lɛ Tsei ni eda lɛ ateŋ babaoo yeɔ omanye yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ anɔ ni oha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my young crops turn yellow when water sits on them under tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When leaves stay wet in deep shade without drying in the sun, they cannot breathe properly and become prone to fungal rot, turning yellow from stress and lack of daylight.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ edɔ lɛ, akɛ amɛ toɔ hulutsoo be mli ni hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ. Baai lɛ nyɛŋ amu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyɛ oshara akɛ ŋmeii baafite amɛ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ haomɔ kɛ hulu la ni bɛ lɛ mli

english: If I cut down tall branches to let the sun hit my field, will that help my crops grow better?
ga: Kɛ mifo tsei niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ koni hulu lɛ atswa miŋmɔ lɛ Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, letting sunlight directly hit the field warms the soil, speeds up plant development, and prevents humidity from building up around crop roots and leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni etswaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ. Ha tso lɛ ada oya ni otsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekabɔle ehe tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai

english: Why do some crops grow very well when planted next to each other, while others slow down each other's growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ amɛhe masɛi, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu haaa amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Crops interact with their neighbors through roots and light. Compatible plants share soil nutrients and may even repel pests for one another, while incompatible crops fight for the exact same minerals or release substances into the soil that harm neighboring roots.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛ akutsoŋbii yeɔ tsakpaa kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi kɛ la nɔ. Tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee lɛ baajara niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná minerals lɛ nɔŋŋ loo amɛjie nibii ni yeɔ shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ awui lɛ awo sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is cassava able to survive in the same field where other leafy vegetables die during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔji ni aduawai krokomɛi ni yɔɔ baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Gbomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Cassava has deep, tough root systems that can store water and food deep underground, allowing it to withstand harsh soil conditions long after shallow-rooted crops run out of moisture.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ato nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi ni mli wa lɛ anaa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ beni tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ bɛ nu lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees require shade trees like plantains around them when first planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Mɛɛ be adu klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops acts like a protective canopy, providing shelter and keeping the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shade tsei. Ehaa mɔ náa he ko ni ehiɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why are my cassava leaves getting eaten during the night when I cannot see any insects during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ayeɔ ŋmei baai gbɛkɛ lɛ? Ani ona kooloi komɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Many crop pests, like armyworms and cutworms, hide from the hot daytime sun in the soil and emerge at night to feed quietly on leaves and soft stems when it is cooler.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui srɔtoi babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Okɛ ohe awo hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛye baai kɛ tsei bibii dioo. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ

english: How can I catch insect pests on my vegetables before they destroy the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Regularly visiting your farm during the cool evening with a flashlight allows you to spot nocturnal pests feeding on the undersides of leaves before they multiply and spread throughout the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli kɛ kane lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsuɔ nii gbɛkɛ yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ dani amɛshwere ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot underground even when the leafy vine above looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Underground pests like nematodes and root-knot organisms attack crops silently beneath the soil surface, damaging the tuber long before visible symptoms appear on the leaves above.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes kɛ root-knot organisms lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii dioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi, ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii be kakadaŋŋ dani okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I look underneath crop leaves instead of just looking at the top when checking for plant sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ ashishi moŋ fe nɔ ni makwɛ ŋwɛi pɛ kɛ́ mikwɛ kɛji tsei ahe helai yɛ amɛmli?

english: Pests like whiteflies and aphids hide under leaves to stay protected from direct sunlight and heavy rain. Checking the undersides helps you catch early warning signs before leaves turn yellow.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ whiteflies kɛ aphids lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ okwɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra dani baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does the purple witchweed weed ruin my maize crop even before the weed grows above the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ purple witchweed lɛ miifite mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani jwɛi lɛ po eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Striga, or witchweed, attaches its roots directly to the maize roots underground, secretly sucking away water and nutrients before you can even see it growing on top of the soil.
ga: Striga loo Witchweed lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ teemɔŋ dani onaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some flowers planted along the edge of my farm keep insect pests away from my main crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ kpaaa gbee lɛ?

english: Certain border plants emit strong smells that confuse bad pests or attract beneficial insects like ladybugs, acting as a natural shield around your main field.
ga: Husu naa tsei komɛi jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni futuɔ kooloi fɔji loo egbalaa kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ladybugs, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni bɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Okwaayeli he titri

english: Why do maize plants turn yellow at the bottom leaves first when the soil is poor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi klɛŋklɛŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: When soil nutrients like nitrogen run low, the maize plant sacrifices its oldest bottom leaves to send remaining food up to the new growth at the top.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ eshishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje kɛya ŋmãa hee ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can drink it. If there is too much rain, the fertilizer gets washed away deep into the soil before the roots reach it, and if it is too dry, the plant cannot absorb the nutrients, causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ afɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Ni kɛji akɛ egbi tsɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Will applying double the recommended fertilizer make my crop produce twice as much yield?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ toi enyɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii shii enyɔ?

english: Plants are like humans—they only need a specific amount of food to grow well. Too much fertilizer burns the crop's roots and causes green leaves to grow very large while leaves fail to make strong, healthy cobs.
ga: Tsei tamɔ adesai. Niyenii falɛ ko pɛ he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli babaoo lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni ebaaha baai eŋɔli lɛ adara waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmeii ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes some stalks in my maize field to grow tall with big ears while others stay short with no cobs?
ga: What makes some of the corn plants in my field tall and have large ears? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yɛ kukuji ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. If seeds are planted too close together or weeds are not cleared early, the stronger plants starve the neighboring weaker plants.
ga: Abele kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo anyɛɛɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ oya. Tsei ni he wa lɛ baaye tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hɔmɔ.

english: How do I know by looking at the maize plant that it is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛ mikwɛ ŋmãa tso ko akɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When maize is ready, the outer husk leaves turn dry and straw-colored, the silks turn dark brown, and a tiny black spot appears at the bottom tip of each grain when you pull it off the cob.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ jwɛi su. Siliki lɛ baatsɔ blɔfo. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishigbɛ naagbee kɛ́ ogbala kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why does my maize shrink and lose weight after I leave it out in the sun for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ amɛ wo hulu lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize contains a lot of water inside the grains. Sun drying evaporates this excess water, making the grains harder, lighter, and safer from rotting.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu babaoo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ feɔ mlɛo, efeɔ mlɛo, ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ he.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop mold and turn black when I store it in bags inside my home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui amli yɛ shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize continues to 'breathe' after harvest and releases moisture. If you bag maize that is still slightly damp, the trapped moisture creates heat and warm damp air, which is the perfect environment for mold to grow.
ga: Abɛi yaa nɔ ‘emuɔ’ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ fioo lolo lɛ wo kotoku mli lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ ji he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects appear inside my sealed maize sacks even when I did not see any during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa kotokui ni mikɛwo mli lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa kooloi komɛi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli moŋ?

english: Insects like grain weevils lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the soft maize grains while the crop is still standing in the field. When the grain dries and sits in storage, the eggs hatch into visible insects.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo Beni dumɔwui lɛ egbi ni akɛwoɔ nitoohe. Wɔɔji lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni anaa.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism. The crop rolls its leaves into tubes to hide from the harsh sun and trap moisture, preventing water from escaping through the leaf pores.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛwoɔ paipii amli koni amɛkɛ amɛhe akawo hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli bu lɛ mli.

english: Why does my maize crop yield get smaller every year when I keep planting on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miyaa nɔ miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes heavy amounts of specific nutrients out of the earth each season. If you do not rest the field or rotate it with crops like beans and groundnuts, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed new plants.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Kɛji okɛ ohe ejɔɔɔ ohe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsakeee lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsei heei nyɛŋ aye abua.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous hybrid maize harvest yield much weaker plants than the original store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi tsutsu ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikɛwo mli lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred for high energy in the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs in the second generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ aha yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: If I keep my harvested maize seeds in a warm room for several months, will they still grow when I plant them?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ to tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli nyɔji babaoo Ani dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ lolo kɛ́ adu?

english: Storing seeds in a warm, unventilated place for too long damages their internal energy. Over time, heat and humidity destroy seed viability, meaning few or none will sprout when planted.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ amɛmli hewalɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashihilɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ baakwɛ̃ loo dumɔwui ko kwraa baakwɛ̃ kɛ́ adu.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my cassava tubers and leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akpamɔ sɛɛ tsɛ ni mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving cassava in the soil long past maturity causes the roots to become tough and fibrous. Over time, moisture and soil bacteria cause the tubers to rot, ruining your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni edara kwraa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmeii yɛ be ni sa mli. Fɛ̃i kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baaha bulb lɛ agbo. Kpatamɔ onibii lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why do my freshly harvested tomatoes burst and go bad when I keep them stacked in tight bags under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa ehee lɛ mli fãa ni efiteɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui ni mli wa amli yɛ hulu shishi lɛ?

english: Tomatoes naturally produce heat and moisture after harvest. Trapping them in closed bags under hot sunshine speeds up decay, causing them to split open, turn soft, and rot quickly.
ga: Tomato kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo kotokui ni aŋã mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbalaa, amɛfeɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛgboɔ oya.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting and becoming soft when kept indoors for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ akɛto shĩa mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that use their internal food reserves to sprout after a resting period. Warm storage rooms encourage early sprouting, which dries out the yam tissue and makes it soft.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni kɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ amɛmli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ wɔɔhe sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ mra. Enɛ baaha sweet potato lɛ mli fãji lɛ agbi ni efee blɛoo.

english: What will happen to my cocoa pods if I do not pick them as soon as they turn ripe on the tree?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji mifolɔɔɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: If ripe cocoa pods remain on the tree for too long, the seeds inside will start to sprout, and diseases like black pod rot can infect the pod, ruining the bean quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baabɔi shweremɔ, ni helai tamɔ black pod rot baanyɛ atswa ŋmeii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo yibii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my green plantains ripen and turn yellow so quickly after I cut them from the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ shwereɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural ripening gas after harvest. Keeping them in warm, enclosed places traps this gas around the fruit, causing them to soften and turn yellow rapidly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ shwereɔ lɛ kpo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛha edɔ ni okɛ nɔ ko ha nɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ gas nɛɛ ebɔle aduawai lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha efee blɛoo oya ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my dry cowpea pods split open and drop seeds on the ground if I wait too long to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔtɔi ni egbi lɛ miitswa ni ekɛ dumɔwui miishwie shikpɔŋ lɛ? Kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa

english: As cowpea pods dry under the sun, the pod walls dry out and tighten. Leaving them on the bush too long creates tension that causes the pods to pop open and scatter the seeds onto the soil.
ga: Beni tsina ŋmeii lɛ egbi yɛ hulu lɛ shishi lɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbogboi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ haomɔ baa ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fãa ni amɛgbɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested fresh peppers start turning soft and watery after staying in a basket for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-chili ni mikpa ehee lɛ miifee bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni mikɛwo tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fresh peppers contain high amounts of water. If stored in warm conditions without good airflow, fungi and bacteria break down the skin and flesh, turning the pepper soft and watery.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ chili ŋmɔŋ mli. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewolo kɛ loo lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu.

english: Will my oranges get sweeter if I leave them hanging on the tree past their harvest season?
ga: Ani mi-orange lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving ripe citrus on the tree does not make it sweeter. Once fully mature, fruit left on the tree starts losing juice, the skin hardens, and it becomes easy target for pests to destroy.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji eda kwraa lɛ Yibii fɛɛ yibii ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baabɔi nu sɛɛ tsɛmɔ. Hewolo lɛ baafee shiŋŋ. ni ebatsɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ akpata hiɛ oya

english: Why do my groundnuts grow mould and turn bitter if I heap them together right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mikɛto amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly dug groundnuts contain moisture from the wet soil. Stacking them in a pile without drying them in the sun traps heat and dampness, which creates dangerous moulds and ruins their flavor.
ga: Peanuts ni atsa ehee lɛ yɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to ŋtayaai amli ni okɛ amɛ wooo hulu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa ni efiteɔ eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Why does my orange tree take so many years to start producing fruits while my maize yields in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tree crops like oranges spend their early years building strong trunk and root systems to support years of heavy fruiting, whereas short-term crops like maize focus all their energy on rapid growth and immediate seed production.
ga: Tsoi ni ji jwɛi, tamɔ citrus lɛ yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee tso lɛ tso kɛ shishifã ni mli wa ni baaye abua afii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ oyaiyeli kɛ dumɔwui ni baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ he nii.

english: Why do grafted mango trees bear fruit much faster than mango trees grown straight from a seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe mango tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Grafting attaches a mature, fruit-bearing branch onto a strong young rootstock, giving the tree a head start as if it were already an adult plant ready to bear fruit.
ga: Akɛ tso niji ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jeɔ shishi tamɔ nɔ ni eda ni efee klalo akɛ ebaawo yibii.

english: Why do tomatoes grown inside a greenhouse produce so much more fruit than the ones I grow directly on my open farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni adu yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe tomato ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Greenhouses protect tomatoes from harsh rain, burning heat, and destructive insects while keeping water steady, allowing the plants to direct all their energy into producing healthy fruit instead of fighting stress.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ tomato he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulutsoo ni jɛɔ la mli kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ daa. Ehaa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ baawu.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant plantains on the same field when starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ́ wɔje kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad shade that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very tiny fruits if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii waa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil food, stretching upward to reach light instead of using their energy to grow big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛha la abote mli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo aduawai wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is missing nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives plants their dark green color and helps them build strong stems and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa su eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before turning into actual pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or lack of water, dropping the blooms to save energy and survive rather than feed new fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Amɛfɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii heei.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay green and alive during the long dry season when other crops dry up and die?
ga: Why does cassava stay green and survive during the long dry season? Beni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep roots that draw moisture from deep underground, and it can reduce its leaf size to conserve water until the rains return.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Ni obaanyɛ okɛ baai lɛ aba shi koni nu akafite kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the fertilizer, soil food, and water right out from under your crops before the crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is it good to cover the soil around my vegetable plants with dried grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ sũ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ awo mli lɛ? Mi-vegetable tsei ni akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔji woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out soil moisture, keeps root areas cool, and decays into natural fertilizer over time.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ akashã ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni efite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli

english: I hear people in my community talking about Jasmin 85 rice; is this variety good for my farm here in Ghana?
ga: Minu ni mɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ miiwie jasmine ŋmãa 85 he; Is this variety good for my farm in Ghana?

english: Jasmin 85, also known locally as Aggrey rice, is an improved rice variety widely promoted in Ghana because it produces high yields, has a pleasant aroma, and adapts well to local growing conditions.
ga: Jasmine 85, ni ale lɛ hu yɛ maŋ lɛ mli akɛ Agrey Rice Eji ŋmãa henɔ ko ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo babaoo yɛ Ghana. Ejaakɛ ewoɔ yibii babaoo, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa, ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds like Jasmin 85 instead of just planting grains saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase tamɔ Jasmine 85 lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to ensure high germination rates, strong disease resistance, and uniform growth, whereas saved grains lose these qualities over time and lead to smaller harvests.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hela ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ekɛ ŋmaa bibioo baa.

english: How do I know if my rice plants are behaving normally and growing well after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Healthy rice sprouts within a week, develops bright green leaves, and produces multiple strong shoots (tillers) from a single plant before it starts producing grain heads.
ga: Omɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ otsi kome mli. Ebaana baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ ni ebaakwɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso kome mli dani dumɔwui ayitsei aje shishi afee.

english: Why do some crop plants grow very tall with many leaves but end up giving very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Plants often put too much energy into leaves and stems instead of grains if there is too much nitrogen in the soil or if they do not receive enough sunlight during critical growth stages.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi amli yɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: How long does it usually take from the day I plant rice until it is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Most improved rice varieties promoted in Ghana take between 100 to 120 days (about 3 to 4 months) to fully mature and be ready for harvesting.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awoɔ he hewalɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee gbii 100 kɛyashi 120 (aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4) dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: What main factors determine whether the seeds I plant will actually lead to a good harvest on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii baatsɔɔ kɛji dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔ lɛ mli kpamɔ kpakpa aba?

english: A successful harvest depends on planting in fertile, moist soil, clearing weeds early so they do not steal plant nutrients, and protecting the crop from pests and birds when the grains start forming.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni yeɔ omanye lɛ damɔ nidumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra koni akaju tsei amli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ okpoi ahe kɛji dumɔwui lɛ je shishi amɛfee.

english: What will happen to my rice plants if they do not get enough water while growing?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Rice plants that lack water will roll up their leaves to save moisture, stunt in growth, and produce light, empty grain husks instead of full rice grains.
ga: Omɔ tsei ni nu efo mli lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ehaa edalɛ baa shi ni ewoɔ dumɔwui bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ omɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ

english: How can I tell if my land is suitable for growing rice before I spend money on seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ dani mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ahe?

english: Rice thrives in low-lying valley areas (valley bottoms) or fields with clay-heavy soils that can retain water and stay moist for long periods.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli (jɔɔ lɛ shishi) loo ŋmɔji ni shikpɔŋ sũ ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ahiɛ nu mli ni ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I visit another farm to see how a new crop performs in the field before I decide to plant it?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya ŋmɔ kroko mli koni mana bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ madu?

english: Yes, extension officers and local farmer groups organize demonstration farms where you can physically visit, observe how the crop grows in local conditions, and see the final harvest before buying seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni yaa hiɛ kɛ okwaafoi akui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baato ŋmɔji ni akɛtsɔɔ nɔ ni obaanyɛ oyasara diɛŋtsɛ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ. Kwɛmɔ tsei adalɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. ni okwɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ dani ohé dumɔwui.

english: How do local farmer groups help me understand how new crops behave on the field?
ga: Okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ye ebua mi ni minu ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yɔɔ lɛ shishi. Te amɛfeɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Farmer groups bring local growers together to visit test fields, share real-life experiences about how crops handle local weather, and learn the best farming practices directly from extension officers.
ga: Okwaafoi akui buaa maŋbii ni duɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛyakwɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Jajemɔ shihilɛ mli niiashikpamɔi diɛŋtsɛ ni kɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ he. ni amɛkase okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Why do tiny insects always destroy my stored beans after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, kooloi bibii fiteɔ kɔfi ni mikɛto lɛ beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Those insects are usually bean weevils, which lay eggs inside the beans while they are still in the field or right after harvest. If the beans are not dried properly or protected before storage, the eggs hatch into beetles that eat the beans from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii. Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo loo beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo abuuu amɛhe dani akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do insects keep attacking my crops even after I spray pesticide multiple times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii eshwie nɔ shii abɔ moŋ?

english: If you spray too frequently with the same chemical or use an incorrect mixture, insects can build resistance to the pesticide over time. Insects can also survive if the spray is applied at the wrong time of day when heat evaporates the chemical before it takes effect.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shwie shi shii abɔ tsɔ loo okɛ tsofa ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, Kooloi baanyɛ atswa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kplukai hu baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ ashwie tsofa lɛ yɛ be ni esaaa mli ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛjeɔ shishi.

english: Is it safe to eat or sell my harvested crops if they were sprayed with chemical pesticides?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maye loo mahɔ̃ɔ mikpamɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ?

english: Yes, provided you wait for the recommended 'pre-harvest interval'—the required number of days between spraying and harvesting for the chemical to break down safely. Washing the crops thoroughly with clean water after harvest also helps remove surface chemical residues.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji omɛ ‘be ni tsɔɔ akɛ abaakpa nii’ ni ji gbii ayibɔ ni he hiaa yɛ tsofai lɛ ashwiemɔ kɛ kpamɔ lɛ teŋ koni tsofai lɛ akumɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored grains rot or smell bad even when I keep them inside closed sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ loo eŋɔɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli moŋ lɛ?

english: Grains hold hidden moisture if they are not completely dried in the sun before bagging. Moisture creates a humid environment inside the sealed sack where mold and bacteria thrive, causing the grains to rot and spoil.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmaa mli lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛwo kotoku mli. Fɛ̃i haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa kotoku ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helatsɛmɛi daa yɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ.

english: What is the best way to keep pests away from my harvested beans without using strong chemicals?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ kɔfi yibii ni akpa lɛ ahe ni akɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can dry your beans thoroughly in the sun and store them in airtight containers, such as sealed plastic drums or hermetic triple-layer bags. Without air inside the container, insects cannot breathe or survive to damage the beans.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha o-beans lɛ agbi kɛtsɔ hulu ni oooha amɛgbi ni okɛto nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, tamɔ plastic baagi ni atsĩ naa loo kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛhi shi koni amɛfite kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How does drying my harvested crops directly on the bare ground affect their quality?
ga: Te mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛgbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ saa bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Drying directly on the ground allows dirt, stones, and soil bacteria to mix with your harvest, and the damp ground can draw moisture back into the grains at night. Using a clean tarpaulin or raised drying platform keeps the crop clean and prevents mold growth.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa muji, tɛi, kɛ sũ mli helai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ futuɔ. Ni hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛba dumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tarp ni he tse loo nɔ ni awó nɔ ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tseɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii shwereɔ.

english: How do I know if the chemical spray I put on my crops is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: A pesticide is working if you see a clear reduction in live pests, fewer damaged leaves, or healthier crop growth within a few days of spraying. It is important to follow correct mixing measurements so the chemical is strong enough to work effectively without damaging the plant.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ miitsu nii kɛji ona akɛ kooloi ni hiɛ ka lɛ ayibɔ eba shi jogbaŋŋ. Baai ni efite lɛ faaa loo tso lɛ dalɛ ni mli wa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ Ehe miihia ni anyiɛ tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ ahe susumɔi ni ja lɛ sɛɛ koni tsofai lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: Why do I feel dizzy and weak after spraying chemicals on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihe feɔ mi shoo ni migbɔjɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ mihe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical pesticides can easily enter your body through breathing in vapors or absorbing through your skin. You should always wear protective clothing, including a nose mask, long sleeves, and gloves, and avoid spraying when the wind is blowing toward you.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi baanyɛ abote ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli oya kɛtsɔ lasu ni ooomu loo kɛtsɔ ohewolo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ owo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji hiɛ he mama, nine kakadaŋŋ agboi kɛ glɔvs, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa bo.

english: Why do some new bean seeds resist insects better than the traditional seeds my elders used?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei Amɛhe wa fe ŋmeii dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii tsutsu lɛ. Nɔ ni mi onukpai lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Modern seed varieties are bred specifically to have natural physical or chemical defenses, such as harder outer skins or traits that deter pests, making it difficult for insects to feed on or lay eggs inside them.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɔmɔtsoŋ loo tsofa hebuu aha, tamɔ kponɔgbɛ ni wa loo sui ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa kooloi bibii akɛ amɛaaye nii loo amɛaawo wɔji yɛ mli.

english: Why do my bean leaves turn yellow and fall off before the pods are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ afee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the crop is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are suffering from waterlogging due to poor drainage. Pest infestations feeding under the leaves can also drain plant energy and cause premature leaf drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu miiho shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ hu baanyɛ afite tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eha baai lɛ afite oya.

english: How do I know if my plantain plants are getting enough nutrients to grow big fruit bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai akui wuji akwɛ̃?

english: Plantain plants need rich soil and plenty of water to produce large bunches. If the leaves stay dark green and thick, the plant is well-fed, but yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen or needs organic compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ekɛwo jwɛi wuji. Kɛji baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ tsei lɛ eye nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to plant on my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala banana tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these have strong bases and narrow, spear-like leaves. Avoid using suckers with wide, broad leaves as young shoots, because they tend to produce weaker plants with smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmɔlɔ’ ni yɔɔ shishi ni wa kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ he akɛ tsei bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfɔɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ plantain tsei bibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain plants turn brown and dry up at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Dry, brown leaf edges on plantains usually happen because of drought, extreme heat, or fungal leaf spot diseases. Clearing dead leaves around the base and keeping the soil moist helps protect the plant.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ, ni egbi yɛ dumɔwui anɔ lɛ fɔɔ baa yɛ hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo fungal leaf spot hewɔ. Baai ni egboi ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ Shishitoo lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Why do my mango trees drop their flowers before growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees often drop flowers due to strong winds, irregular watering, or insect pests like thrips. Keeping the soil moisture steady during flowering and protecting the trees from pests helps save the young fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hewɔ ni mango tsei lɛ fɔfɔi fiteɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii ashishijee mli, kɛ tso lɛ he buu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How far apart should I space my mango seedlings when planting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-mango dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu?

english: Mango trees grow very large over time, so they should be planted about 8 to 10 meters apart. Proper spacing gives branches room to spread and allows sunlight to reach every part of the tree.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ daa waa yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu amɛ aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10 kɛjɛ amɛhe. He ni sa ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ baaha niji lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni eha hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans alongside or after other crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe loo amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans belong to the legume family, which means they pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting beans naturally improves soil fertility for other crops growing on the same land.
ga: Beans yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Beans ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: What basic steps should I take to protect my bean plants from insect damage?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mi-bean tsei lɛ ahe koni kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: Keep the bean beds free of weeds, plant at the start of the rains, and regularly check the undersides of leaves for pests. Using organic neem sprays early on prevents destructive insects from ruining the crop.
ga: Ha bean pods lɛ akafee jwɛi. Aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli Ni akwɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ daa kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ mli. Organic neem spray ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What type of soil works best for growing healthy beans?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Beans grow best in loose, well-drained soil rich in organic matter. They do not do well in waterlogged clay soils, so preparing raised beds helps keep water from pooling around their roots.
ga: Beans kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, saatso ni awo nɔ lɛ ni ooosaa lɛ baaye abua ni nu akabɔle eshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow young mango trees and plantains together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu mango kɛ plantain tsei yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, you can plant them together while the mango trees are young. Plantains grow quickly and offer temporary shade, but as mango trees mature and expand, plantains should be moved to give the mango trees full sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome be mli ni mango tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Shi kɛ́ mango tso lɛ da ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ koni mango tso lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to inspect the health of my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha?

english: You should walk through your farm at least once or twice a week. Regular inspections help you catch pest invasions, diseases, or water stress early before they spread and destroy your whole harvest.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, loo nu mli haomɔ mra. Dani amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods now compared to when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛ akɛto shishijee lɛ he lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, they exhaust the nutrients in the soil and often become overcrowded with thick, unnecessary branches. Just like aging leaves, old trees need special attention like trimming (pruning) dead branches and feeding the soil so they can regain their strength and bear pods again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni bei pii lɛ, tsei niji ni mli tse ni he ehiaaa lɛ fa babaoo. Taakɛ baai momo ji lɛ, tsei momo biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko, tamɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ afolɔmɔ (afolɔ) amɛ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii Koni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ená ŋmeii ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better to cut down my very old, unproductive cocoa farm or can I bring the trees back to life?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi akɛ mafo mikookoo ŋmɔ momo ni wooo yibii lɛ mli? Aloo ani manyɛ maha tso lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ?

english: You do not always have to cut down old trees. By clearing heavy shade, trimming useless branches (pruning), and applying fertilizer, old cocoa trees can be revitalized to start producing plenty of fresh pods again without you waiting years for new trees to mature.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ehe baahia ni ofolɔ tsei momoi. Kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee kookoo tsei momo lɛ ehee koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛmɛ afii babaoo dani tsei heei lɛ adara.

english: Why should I cut off small shoots and extra branches growing out of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Kɛ niji krokomɛi ni miida kɛmiijɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ mli.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, steal food and water away from the main tree. Cutting them off lets the tree send all its energy directly into growing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers loo chupons lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ amɛfomɔ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni miida waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or shade trees alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees, especially young ones, get easily scorched and stressed under full direct sunlight. Planting plantains or shade trees creates a cool living canopy that protects the young cocoa leaves from heat and holds moisture in the ground.
ga: Cocoa tsei, titri lɛ gbekɛbii lɛ Eshãa oya ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa seedlings too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for food and water, and their branches block light from reaching every tree. Proper spacing gives each tree enough room, sunlight, and air to produce maximum pods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. ni eniji lɛ baatsi la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tso fɛɛ tso he. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a tiny fungal organism that spreads easily when air cannot flow through the farm and excess water sits on the pods. Trimming lower branches to let sunlight and air in, along with timely chemical spraying, stops the disease from destroying your harvest.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji ni egbo baa. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni nu ni fa fe nine yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be naa lɛ fata he Ebaaye ebua ni helai akafite onibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees dry up and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees lose water very fast through their leaves during intense heat and drought (Harmattan). If there are no shade trees or mulching to cover the roots, the tree sheds its leaves to protect itself from dying of thirst.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa baa (harmattan). Tsei hu shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kumai he.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your cocoa trees have pale green leaves, grow very slowly, or drop flowers before pods can form despite good rains, the soil has likely run out of essential food and needs fertilizer to nourish the trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekɛha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the main trunk of the tree instead of on the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally develop pods on the main trunk and thick sturdy branches because cocoa pods are heavy. The strong trunk easily supports the weight of the growing pods without snapping branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ amɛtso wulu lɛ nɔ kɛ amɛniji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ejaakɛ cacao tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ tsii. Tso lɛ yitso ni wa lɛ fiɔ tsei ni miida lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ mlɛo ni ekuuu tsei niji lɛ.

english: Why does clearing grass and weeds around my cocoa roots help the trees fruit better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ojie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mikookoo shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds act like thieves by drinking up the water and stealing nutrients from the soil right next to your cocoa roots. Keeping the base of your cocoa trees clean ensures all soil nutrients go directly into making pods.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi kɛtsɔ nu lɛ ni amɛnuɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ okokoo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha cacao tso lɛ shishi he tse lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living canopy that blocks harsh sunlight and retains moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii woɔ mli lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and excessive moisture. Rain drops bounce off infected soil or pods and spread the fungal spores to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fe nine. Nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. ni egbɛ fungal spores lɛ eshwa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and produce strong stalks, so adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia abɛi tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with yellowish powder inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ powda ŋmɔŋ yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest crawls into the growing center of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves before the plant can mature and produce cobs.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ koni amɛye baai bibii dani tsei lɛ adara ni amɛná fɔfɔii ashishifãi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the soil if I leave them past one year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ nɔ ni fe afi lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots continue absorbing water from wet soil during heavy rains. Over time, excessive soil moisture causes mature roots to suffocate, soften, and rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni eda lɛ baaya nɔ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines off the ground using tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tubers. Leaving vines on the ground exposes them to leaf rot and stifles tuber development.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbo ni ebaatsi tuber lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why should I remove the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Excess shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the parent plantain tree. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main plant gets all the nutrition it needs to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsoŋ loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tsei agboi ni tsii.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without producing any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo tomato yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry spells cause severe stress to tomato plants, leading to flower drop. High temperatures prevent successful pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers instead of forming fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baatsi fɔfɔii lɛ amli pollination naa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking plant juices, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Treating the crop for small sucking insects prevents leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ bɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my soil before maize make the next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving natural fertilizer behind for future cereal crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are small insects flying around my cocoa flowers important for my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni fɔ̃ɔ mi kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like midges carry pollen from flower to flower. Without these small insects visiting the blossoms, cocoa flowers cannot develop into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Koolooi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, woɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛji kooloi bibii bɛ Enɛɛmɛi ba koni amɛbasara fɔfɔi lɛ. Kookoo fɔfɔi nyɛŋ atsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers fall off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall when they do not get pollinated by insects, or when the tree does not have enough water and nutrients to support new growth.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso hee ni eda lɛ.

english: Will spraying chemicals on my farm harm the insects that help my cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye kooloi ni yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, heavy chemical sprays can kill beneficial pollinating insects. Spraying at specific times of the day or using targeted methods helps protect these helpful insects.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli loo akɛ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ ahe.

english: What light farm tasks can my family members assist with to save on labor costs?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni waaa miweku lɛ mli bii baanyɛ aye abua yɛ mli koni amɛkafite nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo?

english: Family members can safely assist with tasks like hand-weeding around young trees, collecting harvested pods into central piles, breaking pods, and turning drying beans.
ga: Weku lɛ mli bii baanyɛ aye abua yɛ nitsumɔi srɔtoi amli. Gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ekomɛi ji ni akɛ niji ajie jwɛi ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, abua ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ anaa awo tsɛnsii amli, ŋmeii lɛ akpãtãmɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ atsakemɔ.

english: How can I teach my family members to spot crop diseases early when they help on the farm?
ga: Matsɔɔ weku lɛ mli bii lɛ bɔ ni amɛaafee amɛna ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai mra. Be ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Show your family simple visual signs to watch for, such as white fungus on pods, dark spots, or yellowing leaves, so they can alert you during daily farm visits.
