ga: Tsɔɔmɔ okadii ni yɔɔ mlɛo Tsɔɔmɔ oweku lɛ nibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii anɔ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, loo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ koni amɛbɔ bo kɔkɔ yɛ be mli ni oyasaraa ŋmɔ lɛ daa gbi lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow better when planted under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Larger shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and creating a cool area where cocoa plants thrive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jɛmɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni kookoo tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: How does keeping shade trees on my farm help bring beneficial insects to my cocoa?
ga: Bɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ baa mikoo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Shade trees keep the ground cool and moist, which creates a good living environment for tiny pollinators like midges to breed and multiply.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Pruning removes weak or crowded branches, allowing sunlight and air to move through the tree. This directs the plant's energy into growing bigger pods and reduces disease.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads in wet, shaded conditions. Clearing thick weeds and pruning tree branches helps air dry the pods and prevents rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: How many years after planting will a new hybrid cocoa tree start producing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu cacao tso hee ni ji hybrid lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Most modern hybrid cocoa trees start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting if they receive proper water, shade, and care.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa tsei babaoo baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ, kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu, hulutsoo kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young crops right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Midumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ?

english: Young crops have small root systems and struggle to compete. Weeds quickly steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil, which stunts the growth of your main crop.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye akaŋ. Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Enɛ tsiɔ otso titri lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means your crop lacks nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and grow well, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting during the middle of the hot day even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Intense midday heat causes leaves to lose water faster than the roots can draw it up. If the soil is moist, the plant usually recovers by evening, but putting mulch around the stem helps keep root zones cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɔleɔ Tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and watery even though the leaves look healthy and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee jwɛi moŋ, shi

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy producing leaves instead of storing starch in the root. Adding potassium helps the cassava tubers swell.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the branch before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp environments. Pruning shade branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ, ni akpa tsei ni edara lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa ŋmeii lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa oya.

english: How can I stop small caterpillars from destroying the leaves inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms. Checking the centers of young plants regularly and applying neem leaf extract or approved insecticides early prevents them from destroying the crop's main growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi akuu lɛ mli ŋmeii. Dumɔwui lɛ amli kwɛmɔ daa kɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ebaatsi tsei bibii anaa koni amɛkafite he titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my tomato leaves during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity during rainy weather encourages fungal diseases like powdery mildew. Spacing your plants further apart improves air movement, allowing leaves to dry faster and reducing fungal growth.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew baa. Kɛ́ ogbala otsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my yam vines completely dry up and die before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ egbi kwraa ni egbo dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam vines dying back at the end of the rainy season is natural. It signals that the plant has finished growing and transferred all its food energy down into the tuber, meaning the yam is mature and ready to dig up.
ga: Eji adebɔɔ naa nɔ akɛ sweet potato wain tsei baagboi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe edalɛ naa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ eba shi kɛtee bulb lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when they start growing big bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and weak stems that struggle to hold heavy weight. Supporting the bearing stems with sturdy bamboo poles prevents the wind from snapping the plant before the fruit ripens.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ atswa tsei lɛ dani aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost around the base helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli ni ebɔle lɛ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but legumes like beans and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the earth through their roots. Rotating these crops restores natural soil fertility for your future harvests.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ otsake ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha owɔsɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches and dense cocoa stems lets light and air in, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ kookoo tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo lɛ baaha la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking nutrients from the leaves, or passing along a virus. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves so the plant can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli loo ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or when the plant doesn't receive consistent water. Keeping the root area mulched and watered regularly helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent instead of straight and big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni eyɛ agbo lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand by pushing into the soil. If the ground is hard or stony, the tubers struggle to grow; planting in high, soft, and well-loosened soil mounds gives the tubers room to swell smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Tubers lɛ shweremɔ wa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo bulb lɛ dalɛ kpakpa he hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better for my land if I clear weeds without burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji mijie jwɛi ni mishãaa lɛ?

english: Burning kills beneficial soil organisms and burns away organic plant matter. Letting cleared weeds rot naturally on the field builds rich topsoil and traps moisture for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni eshãa tsei amli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa onibii amli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop seedlings after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take up nutrients and water much faster than cultivated crops. Weeding early prevents them from crowding out your young plants and stealing their food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhe niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi otsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni amɛju amɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. Waterlogged soil cuts off air to the roots, causing them to drown and decay under fungal attack. Planting on ridges helps drain excess water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why do my vegetables wilt during the harmattan dry wind even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull moisture directly out of leaves faster than roots can drink from dry soil. Watering deeply at the roots and covering the soil with dry grass mulch stops moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Nu awo shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya tsɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals nutrients from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the leaves look big and healthy above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ, shi.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing lush green leaves above ground instead of expanding its food storage roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a woɔ sisi nɛ a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ sisi ɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during hot afternoons as a natural reaction to reduce their surface area, saving water and protecting themselves from drying out in direct sunlight.
ga: Tomato baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni baaha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi, ekɛ nu akafite, ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are my pepper flowers dropping off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the air gets too hot, when the soil lacks moisture, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, amɛfeɔ pollinate

english: Why does my groundnut plant produce flowers in the air, but the nuts grow underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow a special stem called a peg that bends downward and buries itself into the soil, where the nut develops safely away from heat and animals.
ga: Beni amɛwo ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen sɛɛ lɛ Amɛyɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ ni amɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ahe.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in heavy rain and damp shade, especially when trees are planted too close together.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into long ribbons after strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii kakadaji yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are naturally designed to split easily along their veins so that strong winds pass through them without snapping the main stem or knocking the whole tree over.
ga: Afee plantain baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbala mli mlɛo yɛ fãji lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa atsɔ mli ni ekumɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ loo etswaaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shi.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, or when tiny worms and fungi enter through small cuts in the seed yam.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Aloo beni ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. yɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui amli

english: Why do my cabbage plants form leafy branches instead of a hard, tight head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ niji ni yɔɔ baai yɛ yitso ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when the weather is too hot, when plants are crowded too close together, or when watering is uneven during their growth.
ga: Kaabaji yitsoŋ tight kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni abua tsei anaa babaoo tsɔ loo be mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ ejaaa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster in my farm than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants that are naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to steal sunlight, water, and nutrients faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni amɛduɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I leave locust bean trees standing on my farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha ŋmeii tsei lɛ adamɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Locust bean trees improve soil fertility by pulling nutrients into the ground, provide valuable shade for crops during hot weather, and yield seeds that can be harvested for extra food and income.
ga: Locust bean tsei haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni egbalaa kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni abaanyɛ akpa kɛha niyenii kɛ shika kroko

english: Will big trees on my farm steal all the water and food away from my crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: While large trees use water, their deep roots actually pull hidden nutrients up from deep underground to the topsoil, and their fallen leaves decompose into natural fertilizer that helps nearby crops.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei wuji kɛ nu tsuɔ nii moŋ Shi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni tsei lɛ ahe baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How close can I plant my food crops to large trees on my land?
ga: Te manyɛ makwɛ niyenii yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: It is best to plant food crops a few steps away from large tree trunks so your crops get enough direct sunlight and do not have to fight shallow tree roots for water.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu niyenii yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso agbo ko shishigbɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ninetalɔi fioo ko pɛ. koni tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ Ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu ni tso shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ.

english: Should I clear every single tree from my bush before I start planting crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛ tsei bibii amli dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Clearing every tree leaves your topsoil exposed to heavy rain and strong sun, which causes erosion. Keeping beneficial trees protects the soil and helps retain moisture during dry spells.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso ni ooojie lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my hoes and farming tools keep breaking when I work on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shɔvel kɛ okwaayeli nibii lɛ yaa nɔ efoɔ kɛ́ mitsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hard-packed soil, hidden rocks, and thick tree roots under the ground strain and break manual tools. Digging right after a light rain helps soften the earth so your tools don't snap.
ga: shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi ni akɛtee kɛ tsei shishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ nine nitsumɔ nibii. Nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, dɛŋdadei lɛ fiteee.

english: Can I bring a tractor or heavy machine to clear land that still has many tree stumps?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ trakta loo tsɔnei ni tsii atsu nii ni akɛjie he ko ni tsei akutsei babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Using heavy machinery on land filled with stumps can easily break tractor blades and ruin the equipment. Tree stumps must be removed first, or manual planting should be used around them.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei akutsei eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efo trakta lɛ ŋmeii lɛ oya ni efite nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. Esa akɛ ajie ŋmei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Aloo esa akɛ okɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔ nii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ atsu nii?

english: Why does my farmland get as hard as concrete during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses its moisture quickly under direct heat, causing soil particles to pack tightly together. Covering the ground with dried leaves or crop leftovers helps keep the soil soft and moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe waa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my seeds take so long to sprout when I plant them under thick tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ tsei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Seeds require warm soil and direct sun rays to trigger growth. Heavy leaf canopy blocks sunlight, keeping the soil cool and slowing down germination.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekanya amɛ dalɛ. Kpo lɛ yɛ baai ni mli tse ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why are my crops growing tall and thin instead of producing healthy fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiifee mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops stretch upward and become weak when they are struggling to find light under heavy tree cover. Without enough sunlight, the plant spends energy reaching for the sky instead of growing fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛna la yɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi lɛ. Kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Yɛ yibii ni amɛbaakwɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why does the soil directly under my trees stay dry even after a light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbi yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Thick tree leaves can act like an umbrella, catching light rain before it touches the ground. Trimming lower branches allows rain to fall through directly onto the soil.
ga: Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ ambrela. Mɛɛ nugbɔ fioo dani etswa shikpɔŋ. Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Large shade trees protect young cocoa from scorching, help retain soil moisture, and create a cooler environment necessary for seedlings to establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa koni dumɔwui lɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: The extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Pruning away excess suckers leaves the strongest shoot to concentrate energy on producing a larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ plantain wulu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ aba koni amɛha hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo plantains babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up from the bottom moving up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the primary nutrient maize needs for green foliage. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ, ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa kɛha ebaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my young maize and chew holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Mikɛ mihe ewo mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli ni mikɛ bu ko miiye mli.

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest that targets the tender leaves inside the central whorl of young maize plants. Early weed removal and targeted bio-pesticides or recommended sprays directly into the leaf funnel effectively manage them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are ready to harvest, and what happens if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? Ni mɛni baaba kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 and 12 months after planting, marked by lower leaves turning yellow and dropping. Leaving roots in the ground past maturity makes them woody, tough, and lowers their starch quality.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi. Kɛ́ ashi shishifãi lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ tsei, amɛhe wa, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need full sunlight on all leaves to make the food required to grow tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, maximizing sun exposure and preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛshɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ ahe koni amɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni otsi baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to extreme heat, insufficient watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade trees nearby to lower temperature spikes helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaaa loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Koni hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ aba shi lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that spread plant viruses. Spraying plants early with organic sprays like neem oil helps control these insects before they damage the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ, tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite baai lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them survive during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket over the soil. It traps moisture beneath the surface, prevents the sun from baking the ground, and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ. Tsi hulu la ni shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When these plants decay, they release natural fertilizer that benefits future crops planted in the same soil.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ fite Ebaajie adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua wɔsɛɛ tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that excessive rain is drowning the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars eat holes into the middle leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the central tube of the maize plant during the day to feed on soft new leaves. Applying appropriate biological or chemical controls early protects the plant before it is destroyed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ tsɔne lɛ mli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe dani amɛfiteɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water settles in the soil for too long, it drowns the roots and creates the right environment for fungus and bacteria to rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ koni amɛfite yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes in the ground for my yam leaves to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight gives the plant the energy it needs to grow large tubers underground, and keeping leaves off the ground prevents diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. kɛ baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni helai akabote mli

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable plants with dried grass stop them from wilting in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dried grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from the direct heat of the sun, keeping the roots cool and preventing soil water from evaporating into the air.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my crops help the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi tsei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a plant family that extracts nitrogen gas from the air and fixes it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the ground for other crops growing nearby.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely hot, when water supply is inconsistent, or when there is a lack of gentle wind and insects to move pollen inside the flower so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ bɛ ni tswaa Ni kooloi baa koni amɛbaye amɛbua ni amɛtsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices out of young leaves, or by viruses carried by these insects that distort normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do weeds make my main crop plants stay short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thief plants that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your main crops, leaving your crops without enough food to grow tall and strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ onibii titrii amli lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, onibii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out easily under direct heat. Without temporary shade trees like plantains or proper soil cover to hold moisture, the strong sun scorches the leaves and weakens the plant.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kɛ́ akɛwo la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, egbiɔ oya. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo mulch bɛ ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main stem to produce much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tso kome ŋmeii fɛɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant are a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why do you advise me to plant groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, while groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. Rotating groundnuts into your field restores nutrients to the soil for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ji ŋmei ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tsake kɛtee oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does leaving dry plant leaves on top of my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi ni mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaving dry leaves on the soil acts like a protective blanket that keeps the ground cool and traps rainwater so crop roots stay moist. As those leaves rot over time, they turn into natural plant food.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi koni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni nɛkɛ baai nɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, Amɛbafeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Why do I need to tie my young yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei bibii fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up to get plenty of sunlight, which helps the plant make food to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the vines off wet soil, preventing diseases and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa wain tsei ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ naa

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves naturally dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are allowed to spread around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your main crop. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and greenish dirt inside the middle shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the central shoot to feed on young maize leaves. Treating the crops early protects the growing tip so the stalk can produce corn.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebuɔ ŋmei ni miida lɛ he koni ŋmei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmei.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my vegetable crops during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛhaa mitsei lɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Watering in the full heat of the day causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before roots can drink it, and hot water drops left on leaves can damage them. Watering early in the morning or late in the afternoon is much better for the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite nii. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi loo shwane lɛ hi kwraa kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there are no big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have sensitive leaves and weak roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees protect them from extreme heat and help the soil retain moisture during dry spells.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do we build big soil mounds before planting yam tubers instead of planting on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔŋ agbo ko dani wɔduɔ sweet potato ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to swell and grow long. Mounds provide deep, loose earth for tuber expansion and prevent rainwater from pooling around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛfuu ni amɛdara be kakadaŋŋ. Gɔji haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛbaakwɛ bulbs lɛ nɔ, ni etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why should I wait for the rainy season to fully start before sowing my cowpea seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani madu tsina ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds require steady soil moisture to germinate and establish roots. Sowing during early, unpredictable rains can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if rain stops for several days.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ leebi maŋkpa kɛ nugbɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is essential for green leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes plant nutrients below root level.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat or water stress. The plant sheds its blossoms to conserve energy and survive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo latsaa ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ mli. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni amɛdalɛ shihilɛi lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain floods the soil without proper drainage, the roots suffocate from lack of oxygen and quickly rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide deep inside the central leaves of my maize plants during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms hide inside the inner leaves (the whorl) to protect themselves from hot sunlight and predators while feeding on the tender growing tip of the plant.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli (rings) koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stay small even after I apply fertilizer if weeds are growing near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ? Kɛji jwɛi bɛŋkɛ

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively absorb water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Fertilizer feeds weeds just as much as crops, so weeds must be cleared first for crops to benefit.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni gbalaa nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii waa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ niyenii tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dani tsei lɛ aná he sɛɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. It also allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in that field.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii momo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ hu baa nakai he lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my cassava help improve my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. This naturally adds nitrogen into the soil, fertilizing the surrounding cassava plants.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata ŋmei tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe

english: Is it better for me to water my crops directly at the roots or spray water over the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mafɔ nu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Watering directly at the roots is much better because plants drink water through their root systems underground, not their leaves. Spraying water over leaves wastes water through evaporation and can cause fungal diseases to spread on wet leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ nuɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ, shi jeee kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha tsɛŋemɔ helai agbɛ ashwã baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough water for my crops during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Push your finger about two inches into the soil near the plant stem. If the soil feels dry and warm at that depth, your crops need water immediately; if it feels cool and sticks slightly to your finger, the soil still has enough moisture.
ga: Nyɛɛ oniji anɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni edɔ yɛ nakai shishigbɛ lɛ. Nu he miihia onibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji enuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ onine he fioo lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo.

english: How does using small pipes to drop water near plant roots help my crops grow better than carrying buckets?
ga: Paipi bibioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Te nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ashishifãi ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ baagi miiwo mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Small drip pipes deliver water slowly and steadily directly to the plant's root zone. This prevents water from evaporating under the hot sun, stops weed growth in dry areas between plants, and keeps the root area consistently moist.
ga: Micro drip pipe lɛ kɛ nu yaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli blɛoo ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekpaa jwɛi ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni egbi yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ

english: Why do my vegetable crop leaves look droopy in the hot afternoon sun but look fresh again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaku osɛɛ kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi?

english: In the hot afternoon, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil, causing them to temporarily wilt. Overnight, as the air cools, the roots catch up and refill the plant with water.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko. Hii jɛmɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkɛ nu woɔ tso lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are sign of plant stress, often caused by irregular watering, excessive heat, or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant curls its leaves to reduce surface area and cut down on water loss.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji tso lɛ he haomɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. hulutsoo ni fa fe nine loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my garden egg plants keep falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden water shortage, extreme heat, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents the plant from dropping its flowers due to thirst stress.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nu ni faaa trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo pollination ni ehiii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi yɛ kumai ni yeɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Applying appropriate fertilizer or compost will restore their dark green color and speed up growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall and leafy stems but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai kakadaji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in its underground tubers. Balanced soil nutrients ensure strong tuber development.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tuber lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak if I plant them too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sun from one another. Proper spacing gives every plant enough light, air, and soil moisture to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing when I plant them under big trees with lots of shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need full daylight to make their own food through their leaves. Deep shade from big trees starves them of sunshine, stopping their growth and preventing them from bearing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia hulutsoo be muu fɛɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Tsei wuji lɛ ahe hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ lɛ haaa amɛná hulu la. Ekpaa dalɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ chili naa

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves to save water during severe dry spells, but excessive leaf loss happens when there are not enough shade trees or soil moisture to protect them from the hot Harmattan winds.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli. Shi baai ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu he kɛjɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he lɛ bɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can carry to full maturity. Unpollinated flowers drop off naturally, while severe flower drop is caused by lack of nutrients, water stress, or insect attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛwoɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa. Fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. yɛ be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa. nu mli haomɔ loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded and unproductive branches so sunlight and air can flow through the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and redirects energy into growing bigger, healthier pods rather than extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai baa shi ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii wuji ni he wa fe baai babaoo najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm needs extra food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Slow growth, thin stems, pale or yellowing leaves, and small pod sizes are clear indicators that your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium required for high crop yields.
ga: Dalɛ blɛoo, tsei bibii, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. Ni ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ko ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp conditions. It develops when farms have dense shade, weeds, or unpruned branches that trap moisture around the pods.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Ebaa kɛji ŋmɔ ko yɛ hulutsoo be ni tsii, jwɛi, loo tsei niji ni afolɔko ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: What are these tiny insects causing dark, burnt patches on my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni kɛ shãa diŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: These insects are mirids (also called capsids). They suck sap from stems and pods, injecting poisonous saliva that creates dark spots, kills tissues, and weakens the tree's overall pod production.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii. (Atsɛɔ lɛ capsids hu) Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei kɛ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ mɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ wo mɔ mli lɛ, efiteɔ fãji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni efeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What is this green plant growing directly on my cocoa tree branches, and will it harm my crop?
ga: Nɛkɛ tso eŋɔli nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo nine lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni ani ebaaye midumɔ nii lɛ awui?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasite that burrows into the branch to steal water and food from the cocoa tree. Left uncontrolled, mistletoe lowers pod production and can kill the host branches.
ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji mistletoe. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ tsei aniji amli koni eju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ cacao tso lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ Mistletoe lɛ, ehaa pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi ni ebaanyɛ efite tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ aniji.

english: Planting cocoa trees too close causes them to compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Overcrowded trees produce fewer pods and create a damp, dark canopy where diseases spread easily.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo duŋ ni helai baanyɛ aba. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even if there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and light from crop roots. Even with good rain, crops suffer because weeds grow faster and absorb the available soil nutrients before the main crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli waa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Dumɔwui hu naa amanehulu ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ dani dumɔ nii titri lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava alongside my young cocoa trees on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ cacao tsei bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: You can plant temporary shade crops like plantains or food crops with young cocoa, but heavy root crops like cassava compete strongly for nutrients and can damage young cocoa roots when harvested.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kookoo bibii adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi tsei ni shishifãi ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni kɛ́ akpa kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite amɛ.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my cocoa trees when they seem to be growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-kokoo niji lɛ beni amɛbɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ? He ni etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming or pruning extra branches helps air move freely through the tree and lets sunlight reach the main stems. This dries up hidden moisture quickly, preventing damp conditions where fungal diseases like black pod thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ afo loo afolɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli oya. ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tso wulu lɛ he Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Tsi shihilɛi ni mli edɔ yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ naa.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees have too many branches and need to be trimmed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo tso ko yɛ niji babaoo ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ?

english: If the inside of your tree canopy looks dark and stays wet long after rain stops, or if you see pods rotting on hidden branches, the tree is too dense and needs pruning to let air and light in.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ mli ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ. Aloo kɛji ona ŋmeii ni miifite yɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli tsii tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la abote mli.

english: When is the best time for me to cut back branches on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is best to trim your trees right after the main harvest or just before the heavy rainy season starts. This prepares the trees to stay dry and well-ventilated when damp weather creates conditions for diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpa tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ aje shishi. Koni asaa tso lɛ he koni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ helai srɔtoi baa lɛ.

english: How does letting wind blow through my crops help keep them healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mihaa etswaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ?

english: Wind and gentle breezes blow away trapped dampness around leaves and fruit. Since most crop diseases need wet conditions to grow and spread, good airflow acts as a natural shield against sickness.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle baai kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ kɛyaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai babaoo biɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ dani amɛdara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. No hewɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ hela naa.

english: Why do my crops seem to catch diseases faster when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, air gets trapped and creates a warm, moist climate around their leaves. This trapped moisture makes it very easy for mold and crop diseases to multiply and spread quickly from plant to plant.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ bɔleɔ baai lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ nɛɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo waa akɛ ŋmeii kɛ tsei ahe helai baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why does too much shade under my trees make my crop pods spoil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni mikɛhaa yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ haa mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy shade blocks sunlight and stops rainwater from evaporating off your pods. Prolonged wetness encourages pod rot and fungus, so letting light filter through keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Shade ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbo ni ŋmɔtɔ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni la tsɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I spray chemical medicine on my farm as soon as I see a problem on my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mina naagba ko yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ?

english: No, chemicals should only be used as a last resort. Simple natural practices like pruning branches, clearing weeds, and giving crops space often stop diseases on their own while saving you money.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ akɛ tsofai atsu nii akɛ naagbee gbɛ pɛ. Adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛ ni akɛhaa Bei pii lɛ amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiɔ helai anaa ni amɛtoɔ shika hu.

english: Can trimming tree branches really help me save money on buying farm chemicals?
ga: Ani tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mikɛ shika akafite yɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, pruning removes diseased parts and creates a dry, airy environment where pests and molds cannot easily survive. By controlling diseases naturally through pruning, you need to buy far fewer chemical sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ helai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli. he ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii nyɛŋ ahi shi mlɛo. Kɛtsɔ helai ni ayeɔ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehe baahia ni ohe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ babaoo.

english: What simple things can I do on my farm to prevent crop diseases without using expensive store chemicals?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛtsi tsei ahe helai anaa ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni jɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can prevent many diseases by keeping adequate space between crops, regularly trimming heavy leaves so air can circulate, weeding around the base of plants, and quickly removing any rotten pods from the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi helai srɔtoi anaa. Abaanyɛ ana enɛ kɛtsɔ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Kpãa baai ni tsii. daa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ. ni ojie ŋmeii ni egbo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya.

english: What should I do with the old branches and sick pods that I cut off my trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tsei niji momo kɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni mifo mitso lɛ?

english: You should gather infected branches and pods and move them far away from healthy plants, or destroy them. Leaving diseased prunings under your trees allows disease spores to stay alive and jump back onto healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ obua tsei niji kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaa ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe loo okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha hela mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahi shi ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do I properly care for small seeds in a nursery bed before transplanting them?
ga: Makwɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ. yɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ dani aŋɔwo mli?

english: Setting up a shaded nursery bed protects young, delicate seedlings from harsh heat and heavy rain, allowing them to grow strong root systems before being planted into the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa dani aduɔ amɛ yɛ saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to move my nursery seedlings into the main field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Transplanting in the late afternoon or on a cloudy day prevents seedlings from suffering severe heat shock and wilting under the hot afternoon sun.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni hulutsoo be lɛ akafite amɛ waa ni amɛkagboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some crops take up to six months from planting in January before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ nyɔji enumɔ dani amɛduɔ yɛ January mli dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha amɛkpamɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops have unique biological cycles; longer-term crops require several months to store enough energy and nutrients to develop healthy, full-sized fruits or tubers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ wala yibii sɔrɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ biɔ nyɔji babaoo koni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ato koni ekɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii ni da, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start harvesting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akpamɔ shishi?

english: Crops show distinct physical signs when mature, such as changes in fruit color, firmness, or the drying up of surrounding foliage, signaling maximum quality and weight.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ aduawai lɛ ahe su tsakemɔi, amɛhewalɛ, loo baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ muji.

english: How can I prevent my fresh produce from spoiling when transporting it across long distances or river crossings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi minibii heei ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite kɛ́ akɛmiiya he ko ni jɛkɛ loo mifo faai amli?

english: Harvesting during the cool early morning and packing produce in ventilated crates or shade-covered bags reduces heat buildup and physical damage during long journeys.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni hulutsoo be mli ni akɛ nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ woɔ adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli loo kotokui ni mli ewo hulutsoo mli lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni buaa ehe naa kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: How can using simple machines help me improve my farm work compared to using manual tools?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mahã miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fe nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Small agricultural machines like motorized tillers or mechanized seeders complete heavy labor much faster than hand hoes, allowing you to plant on time and reduce physical fatigue.
ga: Okwaayeli tsɔnei bibii, tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛduɔ nii loo tsɔnei ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsu nitsumɔi ni tsii oya fe nine ni akɛduɔ nii. Ehaa oduɔ nii yɛ be naa, ni ehaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ tɔlɛ baa shi.

english: What soil additions can I use to help my crops yield bigger produce?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi krokomɛi manyɛ mikɛtsu nii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Adding organic compost, well-rotted animal manure, or balanced fertilizers supplies vital nutrients like nitrogen and potassium that crops need to expand roots and produce larger yields.
ga: Organic compost ni akɛbaafata he Gbɛjianɔtoo ni egbo jogbaŋŋ Aloo, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium aba. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ alɛɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛwo yibii babaoo

english: Why are my tomato leaves turning yellow and dropping off while the plant is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in tomatoes are usually caused by fungal diseases triggered by high humidity or a lack of essential soil nutrients, which can be managed with proper drainage and feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ hulutsoo babaoo loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni sa nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the fiber crops I planted are healthy and growing well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fiber tsei ni miduɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy fiber crops like kenaf or jute display tall, straight stalks with thick outer bark and rich green leaves, showing that the inner fibers are developing high tensile strength.
ga: Tsei ni fibers ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli, tamɔ jute loo jute lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni ja. Kponɔgbɛ tso lɛ mli tse ni baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, tsɔne ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe waa.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well during dry spells even if the soil looks rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Water acts as the transport system for crops; without sufficient soil moisture, plants cannot dissolve and pull nutrients up from the soil into their stems and leaves.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli ni amɛgbala niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do oil palm trees keep producing fruit every year even when I cannot afford expensive fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei woɔ yibii daa afi lɛ? Ni minyɛɛɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa?

english: Oil palm trees have deep, extensive root systems that tap into deep groundwater and nutrients stored deep in the soil, allowing them to produce fruit bunches consistently year after year even with low fertilizer inputs.
ga: Mu tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ebuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ aduawai akui ni yaa nɔ daa afi fɛɛ afi kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ tsu nii po.

english: Why do tree crops like cocoa or oil palm give a more reliable harvest every year compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo loo mu ŋmei lɛ woɔ yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ babaoo afi fɛɛ afi kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Tree crops are perennial plants with strong roots and permanent stems, which make them resilient against brief dry spells. Once established, they yield every season, whereas annual crops like maize rely completely on the weather conditions of a single season.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni shishifãi ni wa kɛ amɛshishifãi ni hiɔ shi daa. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ. Kɛji adu lɛ, ebaawo yibii daa be mli. Yɛ be mli ni afi mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɔ kwraa yɛ be kome mli lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods or palm fruit bunches are mature enough for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔji loo ŋmei yibii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Most cocoa pods and palm fruits change color as they ripen, shifting from green or dark purple to bright red, orange, or yellow. This color change shows that the seeds and oils inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmei yibii babaoo tsakeɔ amɛhe su beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Amɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo purple ni mli edɔ kɛyaa etsuru ni mli tse, akutu, loo ŋmɔŋ. Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui kɛ fɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ etsɔ hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants ripen to red much faster during the hot dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures and direct sunlight speed up the natural ripening process and pigment production inside the fruit, causing green tomatoes to turn red much quicker during hot weather.
ga: He ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shweremɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ oya kwraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is the benefit of buying crop seeds directly from the agricultural research station instead of saving seeds from my market produce?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ hei tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mabua dumɔwui kɛjɛ mijarayeli nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ naa?

english: Seeds from research stations are scientifically bred for high yields, disease resistance, and local climate tolerance, whereas saved market seeds may give unpredictable growth and lower yields.
ga: Akɛ jeŋ nilee ebɔi dumɔwui ni jɛ niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe tsuishitoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jarayeli dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dalɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ aba babaoo ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi aba.

english: How do improved crop varieties from extension officers behave differently from the traditional seeds I have always planted?
ga: Te tsei srɔtoi ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ fee lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ ahe?

english: Improved varieties generally grow faster, mature earlier, resist local pests better, and produce larger or more uniform fruits compared to traditional seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa oya, amɛdaraa oya, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni dara loo ni yɔɔ ekome kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe.

english: Which crops can I plant on my farm that will still give me some harvest even if the rain fails completely?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baawo yibii lolo kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kwraa po?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like cassava, cowpeas, and established tree crops can withstand dry conditions because they store water in underground roots or have deep root systems that extract moisture from deep soil layers.
ga: Tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ cassava, cowpea, kɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aŋmɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa ejaakɛ amɛtoɔ nu yɛ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli loo amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some crop varieties start flowering and fruiting much earlier than others when planted in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi jeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo shishi mra fe ekrokomɛi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Different varieties have different genetic maturity periods; early-maturing varieties are specifically bred to complete their life cycle quickly so they can produce food before the rain stops.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ su mli dalɛ bei srɔtoi. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛgbe amɛshihilɛ naa oya bɔni afee ni aná niyenii dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: What can I do on my farm to keep getting food and income even when I run out of money to buy chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maya nɔ maná niyenii kɛ shika eyɛ mli akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ moŋ?

english: Intercropping cash crops with leguminous plants like beans or groundnuts adds natural nitrogen to the soil, while maintaining perennial crops provides a baseline harvest every year without high chemical costs.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsaa tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ haa shishijee yibiiwoo afi fɛɛ afi ni tsofai ahe nyɔmɔwoo babaoo fataaa he.

english: Why does cassava keep growing leaves and tubers even when I don't have money to weed the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lolo lɛ? Kɛji akɛ obɛ shika ni okɛbaajie jwɛi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa po?

english: Cassava is a naturally aggressive plant with large leaves that shade out light for weeds, and its energy is directed into underground tubers that store nutrients efficiently even under competition.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa. Eyɛ baai agboi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa. Ni akɛ ehewalɛ lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ akaŋshii shishi po lɛ amli.

english: Officer, why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in too much water. Applying a balanced fertilizer like NPK or clearing waterlogged soil helps the leaves regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he saamɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?
