english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so the crop roots can drink it in. When placed on dry soil, fertilizer cannot be absorbed, and the heat can burn the roots or cause the fertilizer to waste away in the wind.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, enyɛŋ etsɔ mli. Ni latsaa lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster and stronger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ.

english: What makes the green cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ dani akpaa?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly during damp weather and heavy shade. Pruning unnecessary branches to allow sunlight and airflow through the farm helps keep the pods healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Nibii ni he ehiaaa ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into small balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies that suck the juice from the leaves and leave viruses behind. Clearing surrounding weeds and spraying safe organic remedies or insecticides controls these pests.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. No shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni eshiɔ hela lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ ni akɛ tsofa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water flow away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, insufficient water, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Watering regularly at the base of the plant early in the morning helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and tiny yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and space to grow large fruits or grains.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaadu aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that bakes the ground and burns fresh seeds before they can establish roots. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady before sowing your seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni mli edɔ ni shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eshãa dumɔwui heei dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high up in the sunlight to produce food for the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, protecting them from disease and helping the yams grow much bigger.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees dry up and die whenever the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, intense heat causes water to evaporate quickly from cocoa leaves. If the soil does not have enough moisture or irrigation to replenish this water, the tree dehydrates, leaves turn brown, and the plant can die.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, okɛ nu afata he. Nu bɛ tso lɛ he. Baai lɛ tsɔɔ asarasu. ni tso lɛ baanyɛ agbo.

english: How can I bring water to my farm during the dry season if there is no stream nearby?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ nu aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛji faa ko bɛ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ?

english: You can install pipe networks connected to a water tank, dig a borehole, or set up simple drip irrigation systems to deliver water directly to the roots of your crops when rains stop.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ paipii ni akɛtsa nu tanki mli lɛ awo mli, otsa bu, loo okɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli ni yɔɔ mlɛo awo mli. Koni okɛ nu aya oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: How often should I water my cocoa seedlings during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-koko tso lɛ nɔ nu yɛ harmatta ni egbi lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa plants should be watered at least two to three times a week during harmattan, preferably early in the morning or late in the evening when sunlight is weak to prevent fast evaporation.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ afɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli yɛ harmattan beaŋ. Esa akɛ afɔ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni hulu la lɛ faaa lɛ koni ekɛtsi la ni hoɔ oya lɛ naa.

english: What can I put around the stems of my crops to keep the soil wet for longer?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛma he? Tsei ashishifãi ni baaha sũ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You can place dried grass, leaves, or crop residues around the base of the plant—a practice called mulching. Mulch blocks direct sun from hitting the ground, trapping moisture in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ abɔle otsei lɛ ashishi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Mulch baatsi hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism. When cocoa trees suffer from high heat and lack of water, they shed leaves to reduce the surface area through which water escapes.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta ni nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing flowers when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops experience heat and water stress, they enter a protective mode to conserve energy and water for survival rather than using their limited resources to make flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe lɛ Tsei lɛ yaa hebuu gbɛ nɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi. Mohu ɔ, ngɔɔ níhi nɛ a he hia kɛ pee fɔfɔi kɛ tso.

english: How does strong sunlight affect young cocoa trees during their first year?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that sunburn easily under direct intense light. Strong sunlight dries out their soil quickly, which can stunt growth or kill the seedling if shade is not provided.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ akadara loo egbe amɛ kɛji akɛ ahaaa amɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why does cocoa seem to grow better in rainy places like the Ashanti region compared to drier areas like Oti?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ tamɔ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ fe hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ tamɔ Oti lɛ?

english: Cocoa thrives in regions with regular rainfall, high atmospheric humidity, and soil that retains moisture well. Drier regions experience longer water shortages that stress cocoa trees unless artificial watering is used.
ga: Cocoa shwereɔ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Fɛ̃i babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Hei ni egbi lɛ naa nu ni faaa be kakadaŋŋ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa kookoo tso lɛ nɔ ja akɛ nu ni akɛfee lɛ tsu nii

english: Should I check for groundwater or stream access before choosing land for a new cocoa farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu loo faai yɔɔ dani mahala shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee?

english: Yes, having a reliable water source nearby makes it much easier to set up irrigation during dry spells, protecting your crop investment from dying during long droughts.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Buu onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe koni ekagbo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Will installing water pipes on my farm help my crops produce yields throughout the whole year?
ga: Ani nu paipii ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, pipe irrigation allows you to supply water to your crops even when rains fail, keeping the plants growing, flowering, and fruiting continuously across all seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, paipii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu haa onibii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po. Ha tsei ada, amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii be fɛɛ be yɛ be fɛɛ be mli.

english: Why does liquid fertilizer sprayed directly on crop leaves work differently than solid fertilizer put in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves have tiny pores that absorb liquid fertilizer almost immediately for a fast energy boost, while solid fertilizer put in the soil dissolves slowly over time to feed the roots gradually.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii. No shwieɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aya hiɛ oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baaho fiofio lɛ. Yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ koni akɛwo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ fiofio.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray liquid fertilizer or chemical medicine on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ nu loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the air is cool. During the hot afternoon sun, the heat evaporates the spray before the leaves can drink it, and high temperatures can cause the chemical to burn the leaves.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Ehi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani baai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni anuɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ashã baai lɛ.

english: How can I tell by looking at my crop leaves that they need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikwɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia amɛ?

english: When crops are hungry for nutrients, their lower leaves often turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and the whole plant stops growing tall as quickly as it should.
ga: Beni tsei he hiaa niyenii lɛ Bei pii lɛ, eshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kpa daamɔ oya taakɛ esa akɛ eda lɛ.

english: Will spraying fertilizer on my crop leaves right before rain falls ruin the work?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwieɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baa lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɔ lɛ baafite nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, heavy rain will wash the liquid fertilizer off the leaves into the ground before the crop has time to absorb it, wasting both your medicine and your labor time.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite otsofa kɛ onitsumɔ be fɛɛ.

english: How can using a motorized sprayer speed up work on my farm compared to a manual hand-pump knapsack?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ oya? Kɛ akɛto nine pɔmp sɛɛ kotoku ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he?

english: A motorized sprayer uses a small engine to blow liquid out faster and wider, covering large areas in a fraction of the time it takes to pump liquid manually by hand.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii lɛ kɛ tsɔne bibioo ko tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Ehaa he ko ni da waa yɛ be ni heɔ ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nu lɛ fã ko pɛ mli.

english: If I have a large farm like 10 acres, is leaf spraying better than putting solid fertilizer near the roots?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko, aaafee rai 10, ni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ hi fe ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa baafata he ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ, ani eji anɔkwale?

english: Solid fertilizer in the soil is better for long-term feeding on large farms because leaf spraying requires frequent re-applications and takes many days of heavy labor to cover big acreage.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii ni akɛyeɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli. Ejaakɛ esa akɛ atsake baai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shii abɔ. ni eheɔ nitsumɔ ni wa gbii babaoo dani anyɛɔ atsuɔ he ko ni da waa he nii.

english: What will happen to my crop if I spray too much liquid fertilizer on it at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu ni mli tse babaoo shwie shi shikome?

english: Too much chemical fertilizer creates high salt levels that pull moisture out of the leaves, causing the leaf edges to dry out, turn brown, and appear burned.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei ni fa babaoo lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. gĩ baa lɛ naa Etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshãa

english: Why do I need to clear weeds from my farm before spraying fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will quickly suck up the fertilizer from the air and soil, leaving your main crops hungry while making your weed problem worse.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli Ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai lɛ mli woɔ wu.

english: Should I spray my crops with fertilizer every week to make them yield quickly?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa otsi koni ekɛwo mli oya?

english: No, spraying every week can overload the plant and damage it. Crops only need extra feeding at key growth stages, such as early growth, flowering, and fruit development.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie tso lɛ nɔ daa otsi lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu nii fe nine ni efite tso lɛ. Tsei biɔ niyenii kroko pɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ bei titri tamɔ amɛdalɛ mra, fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Why is it hard for spray fertilizer to reach all parts of my crop if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baashɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their leaves overlap heavily and create a tight canopy, blocking spray from reaching the lower branches and undersides of leaves where it is needed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa. Tsi tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishi kɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ he ni ataoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep below where young roots can reach, so applying fertilizer like NPK early in the season helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛyaa hei ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas next to my maize help my maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu cowpea yɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mi ŋmãa lɛ mli waa?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When cowpea leaves fall and decompose, they naturally feed nitrogen to your maize crop without buying extra chemicals.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea baai lɛ gbee shi ni amɛfite lɛ Cowpeas baaha o-corn tsei lɛ nitrogen lɛ ajɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛheee tsofai krokomɛi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rainfall floods the field, water fills all the space in heavy clay soils, suffocating the roots and causing rot. Planting on raised mounds allows extra water to drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli Nu lɛ, shikpɔŋ sũ ni mli wa eyi jɛmɛ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl to shield themselves from extreme sun and reduce water loss. Covering the soil with dried leaves or straw keeps the soil cool and moist, reducing leaf curling.
ga: Akɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ shi

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft during the continuous rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp, and cold conditions. When rain stays on cocoa trees that have dense shade, the fungus spreads quickly. Pruning shade branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ anɔ. Fuji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper fruits fall off the plant before they turn red and ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruits when attacked by tiny pests like thrips or when stressed by severe heat. Inspecting under the leaves for pests and keeping soil moisture steady prevents early fruit drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ loo kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ mli, ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafite mra.

english: Why does striga weed make my cereal crops look stunted even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi lɛ haa mi-cereal tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Striga is a parasitic plant that attaches its roots underground directly to your crop's roots. It steals food and water before the crop can use it, so pulling striga out before it flowers is essential to break its cycle.
ga: Striga ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie striga lɛ dani ewo fɔfɔi koni ekɛfo esɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I let all the shoot suckers grow around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni miha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: Every shoot sucker competes with the main plantain stem for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers so only two or three remain gives the main stem maximum energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers fɛɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni eshi enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaawo tsei agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. If the tree experiences heat stress, strong Harmattan winds, or nutrient shortages, it sheds flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛwala.

english: Why won't my seed yams sprout immediately after harvest even if I plant them in good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ moŋ?

english: Yams go into a natural resting state called dormancy after harvest to survive the hot, dry season. They will only begin to sprout when this internal resting period finishes naturally and they sense warmth and rain.
ga: Sweet potatoes boteɔ shihilɛ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Amɛbaabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ beni mligbɛ hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Ni amɛbaanu hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to write down the exact date I spray my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋma gbi pɔtɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Recording your spray dates helps you track how long the chemical stays active, prevents you from spraying too often or too late, and ensures you harvest your crops safely.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmala gbi ni akɛ tsofa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ owo wolo nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ be ni tsofai lɛ yeɔ. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okashwie shi shii abɔ loo blɛoo tsɔ. ni eye ebua bo ni okpa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What bad things can happen to my crops if I do not spray them properly?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii gbohii baanyɛ aba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Incorrect spraying can burn the leaves of your crops, leave harmful chemicals on the plants, or fail to kill the pests attacking your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã otso lɛ baai lɛ. Eshiɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. aloo ni onyɛɛɛ ogbe kooloi ni tutuaa oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Does the time of day I choose to spray my crops really make a difference?
ga: Ani gbi lɛ mli be ni mihalaa akɛ mikɛbaafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ baa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, spraying early in the morning or late in the afternoon works best because the hot sun during midday will evaporate the spray before the plants absorb it.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo shwane lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ la dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why am I not seeing any improvements in my crops even after spraying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaaa hiɛyaa ko lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ po sɛɛ.

english: You might not see results if you sprayed at the wrong time, used the wrong chemical for the specific pest, or mixed the spray with too much water.
ga: Ekolɛ onaaa nɔ ko kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi loo ni akɛ nu babaoo futuɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli

english: If I miss the recommended week for spraying my farm, will my crop yield drop?
ga: Kɛji mifo otsi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Yes, missing the schedule allows pests and diseases to multiply and destroy the crops during their most fragile growth stages.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsuuu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwere ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: How do I know if I am putting the right amount of chemical or fertilizer on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa miiwo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You must measure using the exact mixing instructions provided on the package or by an extension officer; using too little won't work, and using too much will harm the crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ futumɔ he ni yɔɔ paketi lɛ nɔ loo mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ asusu he. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: How does applying the correct quantity of nutrients help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Giving the exact amount provides just enough food for the roots to feed on without burning the plant or wasting your money.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ yibɔ pɔtɛɛ ha lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshãŋ tso lɛ loo efiteee shika.

english: Why do crops on one side of my land react differently to farm treatments than crops on another side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛji akɛ atsa amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different areas of your land have different soil types, moisture levels, and shade, which affects how quickly your crops absorb nutrients and chemical treatments.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi. Humidity level kɛ shades sɔrɔtoi Enɛ saa bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ oya lɛ he.

english: Can putting too much chemical on my crops ruin my soil for the next season?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, over-applying chemicals can build up in the ground, kill beneficial living organisms in the soil, and make the land less fertile over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ abua naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli

english: How can I tell if my crops are actually benefiting from the treatment I applied to the land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You will notice new green leaves growing, stronger stems, and a reduction in insect damage or leaf yellowing within a few days to a week.
ga: Obaana baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni miida. Tso lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Ni kooloi ni fiteɔ loo baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa shi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛyashiɔ otsi kome mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Keeping bigger shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa leaves from scorching and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why is it good for my soil when I plant groundnuts on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmei?

english: Legumes like groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, naturally enriching the soil so that heavy feeders like maize can grow stronger.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ ŋmei, jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low on essential food like nitrogen. Water helps the plant drink, but if there are no nutrients in the soil, the leaves cannot stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my crops produce small fruits when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots fight each other for nutrients and water in the soil, while their leaves block light from each other, resulting in weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ amɛhe lɛ naa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpaa nii fioo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when heavy rains flood my farm before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits on the farm, it suffocates the roots and promotes fungus, causing the tubers to spoil underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baagboi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing peppers during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ harmattan hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry harmattan winds dry out the plant quickly. To save water and survive the heat stress, the pepper plant drops its flowers instead of spending energy to grow fruits.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ gĩɔ oya. Koni akɛ nu akafite ni ehi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni pepper tsei kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat prevents tomato flowers from pollinating correctly. When the temperature gets too high, the plant discards unpollinated flowers because it cannot support fruit growth under heat stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni shwieee nɔ lɛ ejaakɛ enyɛŋ eye ebua aduawai lɛ adalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ shishi.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield less crop than certified seeds bought from an extension officer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ extension nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and produce uniform yields, whereas seeds saved over multiple seasons lose their vigor and disease resistance over time.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛwo yibii ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato bei babaoo lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight gives the plant the energy it needs to build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ awo ebaa lɛ nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain suckers curling up and wrinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids sucking the sap from the plant, or by viruses carried by those insects that disrupt normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛ ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is too much rain during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much rain washes away nitrogen from the soil and prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, which causes maize leaves to turn yellow and struggle to grow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekɛ dalɛ he naagbai baa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before they can produce any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ mawo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular water supply, as the plant tries to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ mli lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tso lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do I need to leave space between my cassava plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaving proper space gives each cassava plant enough room for its underground tubers to expand, while ensuring every plant gets enough sun, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains next to young cocoa trees on new farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi miidu kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shadow and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant groundnuts on the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why does weed growth slow down the growth of my young yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miida lɛ miiha mi-sweet potato bibii lɛ adalɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal sunlight, water, and nutrients from the soil before your yam plants can reach them, leaving fewer resources for the yams to build tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani sweet potato tsei lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haaa nibii fioo pɛ aná kɛha sweet potato lɛ ni ekɛfee tubers.

english: How can I tell if the insects on my tomato plants are destroying them or helping them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifite amɛ loo amɛmiiye amɛmiibua amɛ?

english: Harmful insects chew holes in leaves or leave sticky liquid on leaves while sucking sap, whereas helpful insects feed on those pests without damaging your plants.
ga: Koolooi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ bu yɛ baai amli loo amɛshiɔ nu ni mli tse yɛ amɛsɛɛ. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ beni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ yeɔ nakai kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ awui.

english: Why do black pods spread so quickly across my cocoa farm during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The fungus that causes black pod disease spreads through splashing water drops and high humidity, making rainy weather ideal for the disease to jump from pod to pod.
ga: Fung ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai ni baanyɛ ajɛ pod kome mli kɛya ekroko mli.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local diseases, withstand drought better, and give reliable, high yields compared to grains saved from an old crop.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni fa babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmaa ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why must I dry my harvested cocoa beans thoroughly after fermenting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ kwraa beni mikɛwo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ?

english: Drying stops the fermentation process, removes excess water, and prevents mold from growing on the beans, preserving the quality and chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Gbimɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ nifeemɔ lɛ kpaa. Jiemɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mli. ni otsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekakwɛ kɔfi yibii anɔ Kɛtsɔ tsokolate ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ mlihilɛ kɛ ehiɛ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, an important food plants need to grow. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the newer top leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii tso ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before any pepper fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they get too hot, don't get enough water, or have too much soil fertilizer. The plant drops flowers to save its energy when it feels stressed.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji edɔ tsɔ. nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions during the rainy season. Too much shade and poor ventilation keep moisture on the pods, allowing the fungus to grow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Shade babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii baaha pods lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ adara.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground are small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are planted too close together, cassava spends all its energy growing leaves and branches instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit a plant virus, or by extreme heat and uneven watering causing the plant to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my land give me big harvests for the first two years after clearing forest, but small harvests afterward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni ajie koo lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ? Shi ejie yibii fioo yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Clearing fresh land releases many years of stored natural soil nutrients. After a couple of seasons of farming, crops consume those nutrients, and rains wash the rest away if you don't add manure or fertilizer back into the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ hee ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ afii babaoo lɛ kpo. Yɛ okwaayeli be fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaye nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ. Ni nugbɔ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right around the time they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ tswaa kɛji amɛje shishi amɛfee tɔrɔmɔɔ pɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when a dry spell is suddenly followed by heavy rain or heavy watering. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Yibii amli gbalamɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni hoɔ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ trukaa. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains when they are carrying bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miitsu nii?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that cannot support heavy bunches in wet, soft soil. Wind and heavy fruit pull the weak root system right out of the ground unless you prop the trunks with wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii gbalaa shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ja okɛ tso ni akɛfiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I see sawdust-like dirt and chewed holes inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa muji ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ bu ni atsɔ mli yɛ mi-ŋmã tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is damage caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the center funnel of young maize plants during the day and feed on the fresh inner leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai heei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do dark brown spots spread across my yam leaves until the whole vine dies early during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa sweet potato baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni ehaa wain tso lɛ gboɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Anthracnose, a fungal disease that thrives in warm, wet weather. Rain droplets splash the fungal spores from soil and old leaves onto fresh leaves, spreading the infection rapidly.
ga: Anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji fungal hela ko ni daa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ baai momo nɔ kɛyaa baai heei anɔ. Ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I plant them directly in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense sunlight and high heat. Plantain trees or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa seedlings from drying out and giving them the gentle shade and humidity they need to grow strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi. ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli jɔ koni shishifãi lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow lower leaves are a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food crop plants need. When the soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has from older lower leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, this extra plant food remains in the soil to naturally feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Tso niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my hot pepper plants to curl up into tight rolls and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips. As they suck the sap, they often spread plant viruses that cause the leaves to wrinkle, curl, and stop healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛnuɔ mliki lɛ Bei pii lɛ amɛgbɛɔ tsei amli helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa hewalɛ dalɛ lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving dark droppings behind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It burrows deep into the central growing funnel of the maize plant where it is safe from sun and heat, feeding on young tender leaves before they unfurl.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ bu kɛyaa ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ he. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, water stress, or excess nitrogen. When the plant feels too stressed, it sheds its blossoms to save energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. nu mli haomɔ loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine Kɛ tsei nuɔ he akɛ amɛmiihao tsɔ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall, thin, and weak when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight intensely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems, they stretch tall and thin to race past their neighbors for sunlight.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná tsitsi ni mli edɔ Moŋ lɛ, amɛgbala amɛhe kɛtee shɔŋŋ ni amɛfee shwiili koni amɛjo foi kɛho amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ ahe koni amɛyamɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: Why do I need to make big soil mounds before planting my yam sets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii akuu ko?

english: Yams need loose, soft, and well-drained soil to push downward and expand into big tubers. Building large mounds provides easy root penetration and prevents standing water from rotting the growing yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtsi kɛya shi ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ agbo ko ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ boteɔ mli mlɛo. ni etsĩ nu ni ekã shi lɛ naa koni ekafite sweet potato ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard, woody, and tough to cook if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei, ni kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ahoomɔ wa lɛ?

english: As cassava plants age past their ideal harvest time, the soft starch in the roots converts into tough plant fibers and wood-like structures, making the roots hard, stringy, and unpleasant to eat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ fe amɛkpamɔ be ni sa lɛ Starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ tsei ahe tsɔi ni wa kɛ nibii ni tamɔ tsei, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni wa ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer around my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ ehe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa.

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into a form that roots can actually drink up. On dry soil, concentrated dry fertilizer sits against roots and draws water out of them, causing severe chemical burns to the plant.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ fĩɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ekɛ tsofa shãa tsei waa.

english: Can I use water directly from a big river to water my vegetable farm during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa agbo ko mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, river water is very useful for dry-season farming, but you need a clear channel or a pump to direct the water smoothly onto your land so it doesn't flood your field or wash away your topsoil.
ga: Hɛɛ, faa mli nu he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛha okwaayeli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shi ehe miihia ni oná gbɛ loo pɔmp ni mli tse koni ekɛ nu aya oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni nu akaho ŋmɔji lɛ amli loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akaho.

english: How do I stop heavy rainwater from washing away my crops planted on a sloping land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: You can dig ridges across the slope rather than down it; this stops fast-moving water from carrying away your soil and directs it to soak gently into the ground around crop roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni ooofo shi. Enɛ haaa nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ akaho yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni etsɔɔ bɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio. Efoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong stems and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa ni amɛhi shi akɛ eŋɔli.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over my cowpea leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Tiny holes are caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars eating the leaves, which prevents the crop from soaking up enough sunlight to grow heavy pods.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee shwiili.

english: Young cocoa seedlings die easily under strong direct sunlight, so fast-growing plantain trees are planted alongside them to provide temporary living shade and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni daa oya yɛ amɛmasɛi. koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha be kukuoo ko ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from around my young cassava stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni mi-cassava tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight from young cassava plants, which stops the roots from expanding properly under the ground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or a lack of water, as the plant tries to save its energy until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tsei lɛ miitao ni amɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many green leaves but produces tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or green manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baatoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I buried fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mifu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were planted too deep for the shoot to reach light, if the soil was too dry, or if soil insects ate the seed before it could sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell that my plantains are mature enough to harvest while they are still green?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Plantains are mature when the sharp ridges on the sides of the fruit become full and rounded, and the dried flower tips at the bottom snap off easily.
ga: Plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ afãi lɛ eyi obɔ ni amɛfee ŋmeii. Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Can my cocoa trees grow well and yield good pods without using chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kpakpai ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, cocoa trees can thrive using organic alternatives like compost, decomposed poultry manure, and cocoa pod husks. These natural materials enrich the soil with nutrients, improve water retention, and produce chemical-free cocoa beans.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ atsɔ nibii krokomɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo lɛ anɔ akwɛ cacao tsei. kɛ cocoa pod shells Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni afee kookoo ŋmeii ni tsofai bɛ mli

english: Why do buyers care whether my cocoa beans have been touched by farm chemicals or not?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ he kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eshɛ mi-cocoa yibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: International markets test cocoa for chemical residues to ensure consumer health. Chemical-free or organic cocoa often fetches higher premium prices and protects your farm's soil health for long-term production.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei kaa kookoo amɛkwɛɔ kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ mli kɛha mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ ahewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni tsofai bɛ mli loo nɔ ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ biɔ ni awo lɛ nyɔmɔ babaoo. ni obu oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he kɛha nibii ni anáa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying if I don't spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwieee nɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be caused by sap-sucking pests like capsids or fungal diseases. Without intervention through organic remedies or targeted treatments, these pests drain the tree's nutrients and wither the leaves.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids loo fungal helai baanyɛ aha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aba. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo mli.

english: Will using chemical weed killers harm the root system of my cocoa crop?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ awui?

english: Harsh chemical weed killers can damage the shallow feeding roots of cocoa trees and burn young trunks. Manual clearing or controlled mulching is safer for keeping young trees healthy.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ baanyɛ afite kookoo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ, ni eshã amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ. Nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔ ni akudɔɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply treatments or sprays on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: The best time is early morning or late afternoon when temperatures are cooler. Spraying during hot sunshine causes liquid sprays to evaporate quickly before they can protect the tree or eliminate pests.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔ oya dani enyɛ ebu tso lɛ he loo egbe tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do capsid insects attack my cocoa shoots mostly during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ capsid ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Capsids thrive in hot, sunny conditions, especially where tree canopy leaves are thin. They feed on young green shoots and pods, causing them to dry out, turn black, and die.
ga: Capsids lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe baai lɛ mli tseee lɛ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii. gĩ amɛ Tsɔɔmɔ ediŋŋ ni ogbo

english: Why is it better for us cocoa farmers to form an organization instead of buying spraying machines individually?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ wɔ ni ji kookoo okwaafoi lɛ wɔɔfee gbɛjianɔtoo moŋ fe ni wɔɔhe tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Forming an organization allows farmers to pool funds to afford high-quality spraying equipment, maintain tools properly, and train dedicated spray teams so every member's farm is treated correctly and affordably.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni atoɔ shishi lɛ haa okwaafoi naa shika koni amɛkɛhe nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni otsɔse kuu ko ni kɛ amɛhe eha ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ Koni akwɛ koni akwɛ kuu lɛ mlinyo fɛɛ kuu mlinyo ŋmɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni jara hu waaa.

english: How does joining a cocoa farmers' group help me get better tools for my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe awo kookoo okwaafoi akuu ko mli lɛ aha mi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Extension services and agricultural programs prefer working with organized groups. Being part of a group makes it easier to access shared tools, subsidized inputs, and collective training on crop care.
ga: Nitsumɔi ni yaa hiɛ kɛ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoi sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ kui ni ato amɛ shishi lɛ atsu nii. Kuu mli ni mɔ ko fata he lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooona nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ. Saji ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa kɛ tsɔsemɔ ni akɛfee ekome yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he.

english: Why do earthworms disappear from my farm after heavy chemical spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii laaje kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akɛ tsofai babaoo shwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Strong chemicals kill beneficial soil organisms alongside pests. Earthworms are essential because they break down fallen leaves into plant food and burrow through soil to help cocoa roots breathe.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii he miihia ejaakɛ amɛgbalaɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua kookoo shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmu.

english: How does Black Pod disease move from one tree to another during the rainy season?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black Pod is caused by a fungus that spreads through rain splashes, high humidity, and contaminated pruning tools. Regular weeding and shade management reduce the moisture that allows the disease to spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo, kɛ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni haa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi.

english: If my mango tree produces plenty of flowers, does that automatically mean I will get a big harvest?
ga: Kɛji mango fɔfɔi babaoo lɛ, ani ebaawo yibii wuji diɛŋtsɛ?

english: No, seeing flowers does not guarantee a harvest. Many flowers will simply drop off due to pests, weather, or lack of nutrients if you do not actively care for and protect them as soon as they appear.
ga: Dabi, fɔfɔi ni ooona lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ abaakpa nii. Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ okwɛɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni obuuu amɛhe kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ kɛkɛ,.

english: Why do all the flowers on my mango tree keep falling off without forming any small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii bibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by drought, attacked by tiny insects, or infected by fungal diseases. Without proper protection right when flowering starts, the tree sheds the flowers before they can grow into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hɔmɔ miigba tsei anaa. Kplukai bibii tutuaa lɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ emɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ abuuu he jogbaŋŋ beni fɔfɔi jeɔ shishi lɛ, Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani etsɔɔ aduawai.

english: At what stage of flowering should I start taking action to protect my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ mafee nɔ ko koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: You must start protecting your crop immediately when the flowers first appear. Waiting until you see small fruits is often too late, because unprotected flowers will drop off before fruit set even begins.
ga: Esa akɛ oje oŋmɔshi nibii ahe buu shishi kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo klɛŋklɛŋ pɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaana hetoi bibii Bei pii lɛ, etsɛɔ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ fɔfɔi ni abuuu he lɛ baagbee shi dani yibiiwoo po aje shishi.

english: What basic steps can I take to make sure the flowers stay on my tree until they turn into fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii manyɛ mafee koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛyashi amɛbaawo yibii?

english: To keep flowers attached, ensure the tree has adequate water at its roots, protect the blooms from sap-sucking insects, and apply recommended, flower-safe treatments to prevent fungal rot.
ga: koni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he Kwɛmɔ ni tso lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Buu fɔfɔi ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe. Ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ fɔfɔii bɛ he lɛ atsu nii koni akɛtsi fungal rot naa.

english: What causes the flowers on my fruit trees to turn black and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black, dried flowers are usually caused by fungal diseases like anthracnose, which spread quickly in damp weather. Sprays applied early in the flowering stage help prevent this fungus from destroying the blooms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ anthracnose, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi diji ni egbi lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei nɛɛ efiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Can small insects really stop a whole tree from bearing even a single fruit?
ga: Ani ŋmei bibioo ko baanyɛ atsĩ tso muu ko naa diɛŋtsɛ koni ekawo yibii kome po?

english: Yes, tiny pests like flower thrips and mango hoppers feed on delicate flower parts, causing them to wither and drop completely, leaving the tree with no fruit at all by the end of the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔii a-thrips kɛ mango aphids yeɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ha amɛ fɛɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgbee shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ wooo yibii yɛ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Is it safe for me to spray chemical insecticides directly on my tree while it is full of open flowers?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni fɔfɔi eyi mli obɔ lolo lɛ?

english: You should be very careful, as harsh chemicals can burn delicate flowers and kill helpful insects like bees. It is best to use safe, recommended products or spray just before full bloom to protect both flowers and pollinators.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ohe nɔ jogbaŋŋ waa. Akɛni tsofai ni mli wa baanyɛ ashã fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni egbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ajieɔ yi akɛ atsu nii loo akɛshwie nɔ dani fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ kooloi ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why is my mango tree flowering every year but never producing even one fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango fɔfɔi daa afi shi ewooo yibii kome po kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: When a tree flowers but bears no fruit year after year, it means the flowers are being completely aborted before pollination occurs, usually due to unchecked pests, severe disease, or extreme water stress.
ga: Beni tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii afi fɛɛ afi. No tsɔɔ akɛ ajieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kwraa dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ, helai ni naa wa, loo nu he haomɔ ni naa wa kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do I see bees and flies hanging around my tree when it flowers, and should I chase them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni miiho kɛmiibɔle mihe lɛ? Mitso lɛ beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi Ni ani esa akɛ mashwie amɛ?

english: Do not chase them away; these insects are helping you. They carry pollen from flower to flower, which is necessary for the flower to stay on the branch and transform into a fruit.
ga: Kaashwie amɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ miiye amɛmiibua bo. Amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tsei lɛ aniji anɔ ni amɛwo yibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: How does water affect whether the flowers on my tree stay attached or drop off?
ga: Te nu saa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe loo amɛgbee shi?

english: Irregular watering causes shock. If a tree gets too dry while flowering and then receives sudden heavy water, or if it lacks moisture completely, it responds by dropping its flowers to save itself.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ baa. Kɛji tso lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli ni trukaa lɛ, egbɔjɔ. aloo kɛji nu efo tso lɛ mli kwraa. Tso lɛ haa hetoo kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni ejieɔ koni etsa ehe lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava provides living umbrellas that give cocoa seedlings the moisture and protection they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni haa cocoa dumɔwui lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hebuu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps soil moisture, keeps the roots cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly during hot, dry spells.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is often washed away by heavy rains. Applying compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same patch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally to the soil for future crops.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava roots suffocate and rot when trapped in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extremely hot days helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving small dark droppings in the funnels?
ga: Mɛni miiha bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the growing centers of young maize plants. Early detection and applying neem seed extract or recommended treatments into the leaf funnel can control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ enɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is then sent down into the ground to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, atsuɔ amɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛha bulb lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does my plantain take so long to produce a bunch if I leave all the suckers growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛji mishi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain tree, they steal water and food from the main trunk. Pruning away extra suckers and leaving only one or two ensures the main stem gets enough energy to fruit quickly.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii oya.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I sow seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Crowded crops compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to spread its roots and leaves for maximum growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize after the first rain falls?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because it might be a false start. Wait until rain falls steadily two or three times and the soil stays moist deep enough for your hand to feel it before sowing seeds.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ enɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo bɔ ni sa ni onine baanyɛ anu he dani odu dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow fast while others take forever to bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Healthy 'sword suckers' with narrow leaves have strong roots and grow fast, while 'water suckers' with broad leaves are weak and take longer to produce. Always choose narrow-leaved sword suckers for planting.
ga: Bamboo ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ mli tse lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya, yɛ be mli ni ‘bamboo ŋmeii’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ. Esa akɛ ahala klante tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why does my farm give me less harvest every year even though I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same soil every season drains specific nutrients without giving the land time to recover. Rotating different crops or adding animal manure helps restore the nutrients your crops need to grow well.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ Loo kooloi ashishifã ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or plants are placed too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves on top instead of feeding the tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo akɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ niyenii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmei lɛ baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not flooded, and cover it lightly with soil near the roots. Applying it during heavy downpours will wash it away, while applying it in dry soil can burn the plant.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ. ni okɛ sũ fioo ko aha he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafɔ ehe. yɛ be mli ni akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ashã.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny worms hiding inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They attack young leaves and hide in the central stem shoot, so checking your farm early and using recommended sprays or neem liquid can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛtutuaa baai bibii ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ neem spray loo tsofa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly dry up and die just when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: This is often bacterial wilt or stem rot caused by water staying around the roots for too long or infected soil. Planting on raised soil beds and avoiding fields where pepper or eggplant just grew helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji bacteria wilt loo fitemɔ ni nu ni ta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ kɛ hei ni adu ŋmɔtɔ loo eggplant yɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po?

english: Weeds steal food and sunlight directly from your crop's roots, and they also hide harmful insects and plant diseases that can spread to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ tsei ahe helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã onibii amli lɛ hu teeɔ.
