english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from plantain leaves or shade trees to protect them and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantain baai loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant pepper and maize together on the same piece of land without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them, but you must space the tall maize far enough apart so it does not block light from reaching the shorter pepper plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ ni okɛtsake amɛhe. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baatsi la naa koni ekashɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green leafy growth. It can also happen when heavy rain fills the soil with water and prevents the roots from breathing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ daa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: You can check the soil around the base of the main stem; when the cassava tubers grow large underground, they expand and create visible cracks on the surface of the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli. base of the main stem Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Ebaagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni anaa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani amɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support, so dropping some is normal. However, if too many drop, it means the tree is stressed by lack of soil moisture, poor nutrients, or damage from tiny pests like thrips.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ komɛi ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi, kɛji akɛ efo babaoo lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. niyenii ni ehiii loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips fiteɔ

english: Why haven't my planted maize seeds sprouted after standing in the soil for a full week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni adu lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji amɛdamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ otsi muu fɛɛ?

english: Seeds need a warm and moist environment to wake up. If the soil is too dry, if the seeds were planted too deep, or if insects and birds ate them underground, they will fail to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛte shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi yeɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Amɛbaakwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and carry very heavy bunches of fruit near the top. When rain softens the ground, the shallow roots cannot hold the heavy top, so the plant needs wooden props for support.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tso afĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by small insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by severe hot weather where the plant curls its leaves to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai amli koni nu akafite lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni midu yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, which acts as a free, natural fertilizer for nearby maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up to the sun and keeps them away from wet soil where diseases breed.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hulu lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni baanyɛ aha helai aba.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow thin and produce smaller yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for survival; they steal the groundwater, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients that your main crops need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhi shi. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their small fruits right after a sudden heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A sudden rush of rain after a dry spell shocks the plant due to the fast change in soil moisture levels. This sudden stress forces the plant to drop its young fruits to preserve its own life.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ lɛ haa tsei ahe feɔ shoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsakeɔ oya lɛ hewɔ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ aduawai bibii shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ehere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller maize harvests now compared to five years ago, even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ faaa kwraa fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your maize with nitrogen-fixing crops like groundnuts or beans helps rebuild soil fertility naturally so your yields can recover.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. koni onifeemɔ lɛ anyɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Why are my neighbor's cocoa trees producing so many pods while mine right next door produce very few?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni cacao tso ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: High cocoa yields usually come down to tree management. Pruning old branches lets in sunlight, removing diseased pods stops rot from spreading, and applying fertilizer at the start of the rains feeds the trees so they can hold more pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo damɔ tsei anɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. Niji ni egbɔ ni afolɔ koni hulu la abote mli Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ebua ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning pale green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Switching to improved, disease-resistant cassava stems from the agriculture office is the best way to keep your plants healthy and strong.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly lɛ Tsakemɔ kɛmiiya ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers before growing any actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani adu tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or lack of key nutrients in the soil. Providing light shade, watering consistently at the base, and using balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu bɛ, loo niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ. ni haa hulutsoo be Nu ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa. Ni kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my young pepper plants wilting during the hot afternoon sun even when the ground feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso bibioo lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense sun, pepper leaves lose water faster than young roots can drink it up, causing stress. Placing dry leaves or straw as mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and stops the roots from getting heat-stressed.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ anu. kɛ haomɔ baa Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand easily. If the soil is hard, compacted, or full of rocks, the tuber cannot push downward smoothly. Making higher, softer mounds or ridges gives the roots room to grow long and thick.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Tubers nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cashew trees fall off when an unexpected heavy rain hits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away the pollen from delicate cashew blossoms and encourages fungal diseases. Planting shelter trees as windbreaks around your farm helps protect the flowering canopy from harsh rain and winds.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cashew fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli lɛ, ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni ooodu yɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize stalks turning yellow and drying up while the top is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When maize turns yellow starting from the bottom leaves upward, it is usually hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from old leaves to feed the new growth at the top. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps keep the whole plant green.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli kɛtee ŋwɛi Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ nitrogen Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmãa hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I prevent all my vegetables from ripening at the exact same time so I don't lose money at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-vegetables lɛ fɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaho yɛ be kome mli? Bɔni afee ni mikafite shika yɛ jara nɔ?

english: You can use a method called staggered planting, where you sow small rows of seeds every two weeks instead of planting the whole field in one day. This spreads your harvest over many weeks so you always have fresh produce to sell.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ staggered planting lɛ atsu nii. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kukuji bibii amli daa otsii enyɔ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni aaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome mli. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã otsii babaoo amli. No hewɔ lɛ, oyɛ nibii heei ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do insects destroy my stored corn so fast after I put it in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive inside stored corn if the grains are still slightly wet when harvested. Drying your corn thoroughly under the sun until the kernels are completely hard, and storing them in airtight, hermetic storage bags, prevents bugs from surviving.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli efɔ fioo lolo beni akpaa lɛ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. ni akɛtoɔ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkahi shi.

english: Why do my crops wither even when I flood my field with water every few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nu shwieɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ daa gbii fioo komɛi moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops prefer steady, small amounts of water rather than being soaked all at once. Flooding can drown the roots and prevent them from taking up nutrients, whereas gentle, consistent watering keeps the soil moist without stressing the plant.
ga: Nu fioo pɛ he miihia tsei daa, moŋ fe ni amɛaawo mli fɛɛ shikome. Nu afua baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ haomɔ ko akafee tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my maize plants are getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When maize lacks water, its leaves will start curling inward during the hottest part of the day to save moisture. If they stay curled into the morning or turn yellow, the crops need a steady supply of water right at their roots.
ga: Kɛ́ nu bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ Ebaai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfoɔ kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi. Kɛji amɛfo amɛhe leebi loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants need different amounts of water as they grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu srɔtoi he hiaa mi tomato tsei lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and need just a little moisture near the surface, while fruiting tomato plants need deeper, consistent water to support heavy tomatoes and prevent fruits from cracking.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛhe ehiaaa ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tomato tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ he miihia nu ni mli kwɔ ni yaa nɔ daa koni ekɛfi tomato ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ ni ekɛtsi yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when they experience water stress, such as going from very dry soil to suddenly very wet soil. Maintaining a steady, balanced level of moisture helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ, tamɔ tsakemɔ trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Can giving too much water at once kill my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani nu babaoo ni mikɛhaa shikome lɛ baanyɛ afite mitsei lɛ?

english: Yes, standing water suffocates crop roots by cutting off oxygen, causing them to rot. Plants thrive best when given just enough water to stay hydrated without sitting in waterlogged soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi ni amɛtaraaa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to water my crops directly at the stem or splash water over all the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo makɛ nu ashwie baai lɛ anɔ?

english: It is much better to apply water directly near the roots at the base of the plant. Wetting the leaves can cause fungal diseases, while targeting the roots ensures the plant gets water right where it drinks.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, enáa nu yɛ he ni enuɔ nu yɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How does a drip irrigation system work for a farmer like me?
ga: Te nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii eha tɛŋŋ kɛhaa okwaafonyo ko tamɔ mi?

english: Drip irrigation uses thin pipes with small holes that release water slowly, drop by drop, right at the base of each plant. This gives the crops the exact amount of water they need without wasting water on weeds.
ga: Drip irrigation kɛ paipi bibioo ko ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli ni jieɔ nu lɛ blɛoo, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ ni amɛfiteee nu yɛ jwɛi anɔ.

english: Why do crops respond better when water is given slowly instead of all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nu blɛoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ fɛɛ aha shikome lɛ?

english: Slow watering allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply around the roots without washing away nutrients. The plant can easily drink as needed throughout the day without experiencing water shock.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fiofio lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ shwieee shi. Tsei baanyɛ anu nu mlɛo bɔ ni he hiaa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli ni amɛnaaa nu he shoofeemɔ.

english: Does pouring heavy buckets of water on my vegetables every day help them grow faster?
ga: Ani nu ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai anɔ daa gbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya?

english: Pouring heavy buckets often washes away topsoil and damages delicate roots. Delivering water little by little keeps the root zone consistently moist and helps the plant grow steadily without stress.
ga: Bakɛtii wuji ni ajieɔ nu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ fiofio lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edaa fiofio ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: How can I keep my crops healthy when rainfall becomes unpredictable in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Using controlled watering systems like drip irrigation delivers water directly to plant roots in small, precise amounts. This ensures your crops stay healthy and well-hydrated even during long dry spells.
ga: Kɛ akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akudɔ, tamɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ekɛ nu yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ yibɔ bibii ni ja mli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ po mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need me to plant plantains right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very sensitive leaves that easily scorch in full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and create wide foliage that shields the young cocoa from intense sun and keeps the soil around the roots cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves, showing it needs fertilizer or animal manure.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii. Tso lɛ baaye eshishigbɛ baai momo lɛ hɔmɔ koni eha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ atsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas on my land before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension officer lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plants die after harvest, they leave that rich plant food behind in the soil for your next crop of maize to use.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsina tsei gboi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛshiɔ nakai tso niyenii ni jara wa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmãa kɛha amɛ kooloi aniyenii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot dry weather or inconsistent watering. It can also happen if you give them too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to put energy into leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo ŋmɔ mli. Ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ woɔ baai amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why should I pinch off the top shoots of my young pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tso bibioo lɛ mli tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Removing the main growing tip stops the pepper plant from growing tall and thin. It forces the plant to branch out sideways, creating a bushier plant with more branches that can produce a larger harvest of peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmei titri ni miida lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei tso lɛ adara ni efee mlɛo. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niji jeɔ kpo kɛyaa afã. Enɛ haa tso ni yɔɔ niji babaoo ni baanyɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ baa.

english: If I leave my mature cassava in the ground past its harvest time, will it keep growing larger?
ga: Kɛ mishi ŋmei ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Ani ebaaya nɔ eda?

english: Cassava roots will stop growing bigger after full maturity and will start turning tough, woody, and watery. If left in the soil too long, especially into the rainy season, the roots will rot and lose their starchy value.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ kɛji amɛshɛ shweremɔ he. ni ebaaje shishi ewa Eji tso ni eji nu. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛ starch sɛɛnamɔ lɛ baaje mli.

english: Does it make a difference which direction I place my cut yam pieces when burying them in the mound?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko yɛ bɔ ni ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ́ afu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko mli lɛ mli?

english: Placing the cut surface or growing bud facing upward helps the shoot break through the soil surface much faster and easier, allowing the plant to establish roots and leafy vines early.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo lɛ nɔ loo ŋmei lɛ kwɛ ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai mra.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crop yield even when I give my plants plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa mitsei lɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete with your crop for plant food, root space, and light. Even if water is available, weeds absorb the soil nutrients faster than your crops, leaving your farm underfed.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná tsei niyenii, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ la, kɛ́ nu yɛ po. Jwɛi lɛ baaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔ lɛ nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why are small worms hiding inside the central funnels of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that prefers hiding in the deep center whorl of young maize leaves to eat tender leaves before they unfurl. Early spraying in the morning or late evening targets them effectively.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛje kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to settle before sowing my maize seeds in the dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds in completely dry soil before steady rain comes exposes them to heat, ants, and birds. If a light rain causes them to sprout but dry weather returns, the young seedlings will wither and die.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ anɛɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa dɔlɛ, ŋmeii kɛ okpoi. Kɛji nugbɔ fioo ko ha amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa. Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni awo amɛ ŋmãa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking nitrogen or that the fertilizer was applied at the wrong time or depth. Applying fertilizer when the soil is too dry or too wet can prevent the roots from soaking up the nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo awo lɛ fɔ yɛ be loo mlibotemɔ ni ejaaa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and gives pests a permanent home. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close together so I can get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni aná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting cassava too close makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives the roots enough room to expand and produce large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying when the hot sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them acts like an umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that attacks the growing tip of maize. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening reaches the worms before they destroy the crop's heart.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni tutuaa ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yitsei lɛ. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsui.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my garden leaves during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and moisture cause fungal infections like powdery mildew to spread across leaves. Clearing space between plants improves airflow and prevents damp conditions where fungi thrive.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ powdery mildew, gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ fɛɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa hei ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black rotten spots at the bottom before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents this condition.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune some leaves from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo loo majie mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning removes old or shaded leaves that waste energy, allowing the plant to direct all its water and nutrients into producing bigger, healthier pepper fruits.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baai ni egbɔ loo ni yɔɔ shade ni fiteɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli mlijalɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred in labs for high yield and disease resistance, whereas seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength and uniformity over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaafee daa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does leaving weeds on my farm harm my growing crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ awui?

english: Weeds act as aggressive thieves that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops, while also hiding harmful pests that can attack your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni yitsoŋ wa, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ atutua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ teeɔ.

english: If light rain starts falling in mid-July, should I start sowing my seeds immediately?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ July teŋgbɛ Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Light early rains may not provide enough deep soil moisture for seeds to germinate safely. It is best to wait until the rains become consistent and damp the soil several inches deep, preventing young roots from drying out if the rain stops for a few days.
ga: Ekolɛ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haaa sũ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ fiofio ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ inchii babaoo. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Is it good to apply fertilizer on my farm as soon as the rainy season begins?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already moist, but not during heavy downpours. Heavy rain can wash the fertilizer away before crop roots absorb it, while dry soil combined with fertilizer can burn the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ owoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Taakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi ashã lɛ.

english: How can I protect my young seedlings from being washed away when heavy rains follow light rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkaho kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ fioo ko nyiɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting along contour lines across slopes or making ridges helps slow down running rainwater. Placing dry grass mulching around seedlings also breaks the impact of heavy raindrops and holds the topsoil in place.
ga: Dumɔ ni aaadu yɛ kontu linei ahe loo ŋmeii ni afee lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Muji ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ hu haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi, ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during hot afternoons before the rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa dani nugbɔ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By rolling up, the leaf exposes less surface area to direct heat and sunlight, which reduces water loss until the roots can absorb fresh rain.
ga: Abɛi baai ni akpɛɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe Baai lɛ haaa hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ashɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nugbɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava and pepper plants turn yellow after long days of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rainwater fills all air pockets in the soil, preventing roots from taking in oxygen and nutrients. Good soil drainage allows extra water to escape so roots can breathe and keep leaves green.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and opportunistic, responding instantly to even tiny amounts of rain. Crops take longer to establish, so clearing weeds early gives your main plants room to access water and soil nutrients without competition.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛtaoɔ hegbɛi. Etsuɔ nugbɔ fioo ko he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ Tsei heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How does a late start to the rainy season in northern Ghana affect crops like millet and sorghum?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A delayed start to the rains shortens the growing period available for crops. Using early-maturing or drought-tolerant seed varieties helps ensure the crops reach full maturity before the rainy period ends.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha dumɔ be lɛ afee kuku. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee.

english: Why do black spots appear on crop leaves after rain showers begin in humid areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases spread quickly in damp, warm weather when water splashes spores from the soil onto plant leaves. Leaving enough space between plants improves airflow, helping leaves dry faster and reducing disease spread.
ga: Fungal helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Beni nu shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ gĩɔ oya. ni eha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi

english: How does damp or rainy weather during harvest time affect harvested grains like maize and rice?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ saa ŋmaa ni akpaa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: High moisture during harvest causes grains to absorb dampness, leading to mold growth and spoilage. Grains must be dried thoroughly on clean tarpaulins and stored in moisture-proof bags to stay safe.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ fɛ̃i. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ daa ni efiteɔ. Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tarpaulin ni he tse nɔ. ni akɛtoɔ kotoku ko ni nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ mli mli koni ehi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens to harvested yams if they are exposed to rain while being transported from the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wet yams stored in enclosed bags or trucks heat up quickly and begin to rot. Harvested tubers should be kept dry, well-ventilated, and covered with waterproof sheets during transport to preserve their quality.
ga: Atomɔ ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui loo lɔlei ni aŋã mli lɛ baadɔ oya ni ebɔi fitemɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni egbi. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ jɛmɛ. ni akɛ wolo ni nu nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ haa he yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Flower drop usually happens when plants face high heat, inconsistent watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and using well-composted manure helps the plants hold their flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa kɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What causes the bottoms of my growing green tomatoes to turn black and rot?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato eŋɔli ni miida lɛ shishi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular. Watering your tomato crop consistently helps the roots draw calcium from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli, ni bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and difficult to cut when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ewa akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Okra pods mature very quickly and turn woody if left on the plant too long. Harvesting them while they are still small, tender, and snap easily—usually 3 to 5 days after flowering—keeps them soft and good for eating.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Akpaa be mli ni eji gbekɛ, ni eyɛ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya, bei pii lɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 sɛɛ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ baaha amɛfee bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhi kɛha niyeli.

english: Why are my onion plants growing large leafy tops but no big bulbs underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onion lɛ hiɛ baai wuji shi bulbs wuji bɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If onions get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of expanding their bulbs. Reducing high-nitrogen fertilizers as the plant matures encourages the bulb to swell.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ he nii moŋ fe ŋmeii ni miida. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔtsemɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ baawo bulb lɛ dalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How can I stop green caterpillars from eating holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye bu ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cabbage caterpillars hatch from eggs laid by butterflies on the underside of leaves. Inspecting plants early, picking off caterpillars by hand, or spraying local neem leaf extract helps protect the leaves from destruction.
ga: Kaabeji ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ nine baabua ŋmeii anaa Loo ni akɛ neem baa mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baa lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: How do I know when sweet potatoes are ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Sweet potatoes are typically ready 3 to 4 months after planting when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow. You will also notice the soil around the base cracking as the tubers grow larger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Obaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why does rice require so much water on the field compared to my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Watering or flooding rice fields suppresses weeds that compete with the rice for light and nutrients. Rice plants are naturally adapted to wet soil, so keeping the field flooded promotes strong tillering and grain production.
ga: Nu loo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ baatsi jwɛi ni kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ anaa. Omɔ tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa.

english: Is it better for me to grow many different crops together or plant just one item on my whole field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsei babaoo yɛ he kome loo nɔ kome pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Planting a mix of crops like vegetables, tubers, and grains reduces your risk. If weather or pests destroy one crop, or if market prices for a single crop drop, you can still harvest and sell the others.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi tamɔ aduawai, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmaa ni ooodu lɛ baaha oshara ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ aba shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kpata ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko hiɛ loo kɛji jara ni akɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome lɛ ba shi Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lolo ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wither and die shortly after I transplant them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved during hot sunlight or if their tender roots dry out. Moving plants late in the afternoon and watering them immediately gives the roots time to settle coolly overnight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ amli kɛji ajie amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli loo kɛji shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gĩ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shwane mli ni awo lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛjɔɔ amɛhe nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Why do the leaves on my young crop plants turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or poor drainage causing root rot. Applying organic manure or well-balanced fertilizer restores nitrogen levels so leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛkɛ ni baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛshishijee su eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger on land that has been left untouched for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwere waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa nɔ afii babaoo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When land lies fallow without farming, wild plants rot and naturally feed nutrients back into the dirt. This rested soil builds up a fresh storehouse of plant food, giving new crops plenty of energy to grow healthy.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔtɔ ni okwaayeli bɛ mli lɛ, koo mli tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɛɔ shi nɛɛ feɔ tsei aniyenii heei atoohe. Enɛ haa tsei heei lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seeds right after I clear fresh land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni mijie he ko hee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can sleep underground in the dirt for years. When you clear the bush, direct sunlight and air wake those seeds up, causing them to sprout quickly before your planted crops have a chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ sũ lɛ mli afii babaoo. Kɛji otsi jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ baate nakai dumɔwui lɛ ashi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans make my dirt better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts have special natural helpers on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop is harvested, that stored plant food stays in the soil for the next crop to eat.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tse niyenii ni ato lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tight like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is how the plant protects itself from losing water. By curling its leaves, the plant hides part of its surface from the hot sun so it holds onto moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ baaha ehiɛ fã ko ahi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my young crop turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for a major nutrient called nitrogen, or the soil has too much trapped water choking the roots. When roots cannot eat properly, the plant loses its deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii titri ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ yeee jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baafite eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings look weak and flat on the ground right after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants breaks tiny, invisible hair roots that suck up water. The plant goes into shock and wilts for a day or two until it grows new root hairs to drink water from its new location.
ga: Tsei ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ haa yitsɔi shishifãi bibii lɛ daa. nɔ ni anaaa ni shwieɔ nu ni efiteɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baakpokpo ni ebaagbo gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ kɛyashi shishifãi ahe yitsɔi heei baakwɛ koni amɛnu nu kɛjɛ he hee lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and cooler soil during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɛ cocoa shade ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin when I plant the stems very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ, be mli ni adu tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for the same water and soil food. Without enough personal space, no single plant gets enough energy to build big, thick tubers.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ he ko ni mɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɔɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Tso ko bɛ ni náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee bulbs agboi ni mli tse.

english: Why do cassava stems sprout faster when I plant them at a slanting angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni adu lɛ shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting at a slant puts more sprouting nodes right near the warm topsoil layer where rainwater sits. This makes it easier for the stem to push roots down and green shoots up into the air.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ baaha nodes babaoo adara ni abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ he ni nugbɔ nu yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha efee mlɛo aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsi shishifãi lɛ kɛya shi, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ hu baatswa kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I plant maize on the exact same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Every crop pulls specific foods out of the dirt to grow. Planting maize over and over drains the same nutrients faster than nature can replace them, leaving the soil tired and empty.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni adebɔɔ baanyɛ atsake amɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni efeɔ efolo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a crucial nutrient for healthy green growth, or that excess water in the soil is preventing the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ Aloo nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus they spread, which distorts the leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing many green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpeas to put all their energy into leafy growth instead of producing the flowers that turn into pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when the soil stays wet for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air to breathe in the soil; standing water chokes the roots and creates the right environment for harmful soil fungi to decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ koni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is soft enough for growing yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ sweet potatoes?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the earth, so if you cannot easily dig deep, loose mounds by hand, the soil is too hard and will cause short, deformed tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ onyɛɛɛ okɛ oniji atsa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni ebaafite ŋmeii kukuji lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when the stem looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and heavy fruit tops, so when heavy rains soften the soil, strong winds can easily pull the roots right out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ashishifãi ni mli tse. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture suddenly changes from very dry to very wet, which shocks the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. ni haa tso lɛ he feɔ gbeyei lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight; fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that shield young cocoa from harsh sun and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: What causes my cabbage heads to split open right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kaabe yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani akpaa?

english: Cabbage heads split open when dry plants receive a sudden heavy watering or rain, causing the inside of the head to grow faster than the outer leaves can stretch.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji tsei ni egbi lɛ ná nu trukaa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: A shallow layer of water prevents weeds from taking over your field and maintains a stable soil temperature that helps young rice plants grow evenly.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct heat because strong sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out their roots. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains next to them provides cooler air and moisture so they can grow strong.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ agbi. Shade ni akɛhaa loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara waa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking food, especially nitrogen, or the soil has too much water, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients from the earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ tso lɛ he. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: When water stays in the soil for too long without draining away, air cannot reach the plant's roots. This lack of air causes the cassava tubers to suffocate and decay underground.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before any fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when small insects attack the blossoms before they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai.

english: What is making ragged holes in the center of my maize leaves and leaving dark waste inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛshiɔ gunk ni tsuɔ waa yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the leaf funnel during the hot part of the day and feeds on the soft green growing leaf tip.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni miida lɛ ashishifãi.

english: How does covering the soil around my crop roots with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you do not need to water as often, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli, no hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground on wooden stakes allows them to catch more sunlight and air. This extra energy helps the plant feed its underground tuber so it grows larger.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii koni amɛdara.

english: Why do my plantain trees give very small bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close to each other, their roots fight over nutrients in the soil and their leaves block sunlight from one another, leaving less energy for large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ kɛha aduawai wuji.

english: Should I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rain becomes steady. Sowing after only one short rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry period follows right after.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ kuku ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when I apply fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and the fertilizer you put down before your main crops have a chance to take it in.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛfataa he lɛ dani tso titri lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting beans together with my maize make my soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Beans have root helpers that pull nitrogen out of the air and store it in the soil. Maize feeds heavily on this nitrogen, so growing them together naturally fertilizes your maize and improves soil health.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii amli. Akɛ nitrogen babaoo haa ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo mli lɛ, ebaaha o-ŋmã lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ hu aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the small cocoa pods on my tree turning black and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during heavy rains. Pruning extra tree branches lets in sunlight and air, which keeps the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli. Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when we get too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess standing water chokes the roots and encourages fungal rot, which is why planting cassava on raised soil mounds helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping normal growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ ni sa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids that transmit viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early with neem spray or recommended farm treatments keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids, ni kɛ helai baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem spray loo ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they lack consistent moisture. Providing light shade and keeping the soil evenly watered prevents flower loss.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In hot sunshine, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink it up, making the plant temporarily droop to save moisture. As the weather cools in the evening, the plant stands upright again.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Ekɛ tso lɛ agbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ damɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Propping up the main stem with a strong wooden fork or bamboo pole gives the plant extra support until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akuu ni tsii lɛ haa efeɔ tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli loo ŋmei tso ni wa to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ kroko kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing sunlight and fresh air into the canopy. This prevents diseases and helps the plant direct its energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it important to weed around my yam vines as soon as they start sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Young yam sprouts grow slowly at first and cannot fight off fast-growing weeds for water, light, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures the yam plant gets all the nutrients it needs to produce large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha sweet potato tso lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct hot sunlight and will scorch and die. Plantain trees grow very quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ebaashã ni egbo. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha be kukuoo mli shade kɛ sũ mli nu ni mli ejɔ ni kookoo bibii taoɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes whatever food it has left to feed new growth, causing the older leaves at the bottom to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ koni amɛkɛha shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do I find small caterpillars inside the center funnel of my young maize plants eating holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mi-baby corn tsei ni yeɔ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ateŋ funnel lɛ mli.

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides inside the warm center of maize plants where leaves are soft. They feed on the tender young leaves, which ruins the plant's ability to grow properly if not treated quickly.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni no fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ lɛ oya.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects around them and cannot drain away. In heavy or waterlogged soils, fungi thrive and attack the tubers, causing them to turn soft, smelly, and rotten.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Fɛ̃i lɛ daa ni etutuaa ŋmeii lɛ, ni ehaa amɛfeɔ blɛoo, amɛhe ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops act like crowd members fighting over a small bowl of food. They compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stems with small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni adu lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ asafo babaoo ni miiwuu yɛ niyenii tsɛnsi bibioo ko he. Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why did the stems of my pepper plants burn and turn brown after I applied granular fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ granular fertilizer ewo mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. If you touch the fertilizer grains directly against the soft stems or roots of young plants, it sucks out their moisture and burns them. Fertilizer must always be placed a few inches away from the main stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi loo amɛshishifãi lɛ ta ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dumɔwui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛshã amɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi be fɛɛ be.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer on my land right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the top layer of soil away along with the fertilizer before your crops' roots have a chance to absorb it. This wastes your money and leaves your crops without the nutrients they need.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ lɛ, Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha onibii lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster and aggressive roots than cultivated crops. They steal the fertilizer and water from under the soil and block sunlight from reaching your crops, leaving your plants weak and underfed.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my tomato plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When the weather is too hot, the pollen inside the flower dries out, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ baagbi. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout out of the ground after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep in the soil, planted in completely dry dirt without water, or eaten underground by insects and ants. Planting seeds at the correct depth in moist soil ensures they can break through.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa ni nu bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. aloo kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ abote mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the plants the strength to grow dark green and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he mra Ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive water. When stressed, the plant saves its energy for survival rather than making fruit, so keeping the soil steadily moist helps keep flowers attached.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛbuɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, shady, and cool conditions. Pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, which dries out the pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni abaakpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my maize stalks snap and fall over when a light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks often fall over because stem borer pests eat away the inside of the stem, making it hollow and weak. It can also happen if the roots are shallow, which can be helped by mounding soil around the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mligbɛ. ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ hu baanyɛ aba mli kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Abaanyɛ aye abua enɛ kɛtsɔ sũ ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of big leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when the ground is packed too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of pushing roots outward to store food as big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, sisifã ɔmɛ tsiɔ kɛ yaa kpo nɔ konɛ a ya to niye ní ngɛ bulb nguahi a mi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get a dark, sunken spot at the bottom end before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This spot is called Blossom End Rot, and it happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil into the developing fruit. It is usually caused by irregular watering, so keeping the soil consistently damp prevents it.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot ni ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: It is not recommended to replant seeds saved from hybrid maize. Hybrid seeds are bred for one generation of high yield, so planting the second-generation seeds will result in uneven growth and much smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ anɔ kɛhaa yinɔ kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaha amɛdara ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting inside my barn before the next planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their sleeping period and sprout when temperatures rise inside the barn, as the tubers sense that rainy weather is returning. Keeping your storage barn dark, cool, and well-ventilated delays this sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔ be lɛ mli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ yitso lɛ baaná ale akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miiku esɛɛ eba. Kɛ́ okɛ otsu lɛ to he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my stored grains like cowpea get full of small holes and white powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni ato, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: The holes and powder are caused by tiny insects called weevils that hatch from eggs inside the seeds and eat their way out. Storing dry grains in airtight containers or Purdue Improved Crop Storage (PICS) bags suffocates the insects and protects your harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ he ni amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ powda lɛ baa.
