Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo Purdue Enhanced Crop Storage (PICS) kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do high-yield hybrid maize seeds produce less grain if I save them and plant them again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hybrid corn ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo kɛji mikɛto ni midu ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by crossing two specific parent plants to create strong first-generation crops. When you harvest seeds from those crops and plant them, that special genetic strength breaks down, resulting in uneven growth and much lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni akɛfee klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ tso ni he wa. Beni okpaa nakai tsei lɛ amli dumɔwui lɛ ni okɛduɔ lɛ. Nakai fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ ni fa lɛ baafite. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa.

english: Why does measuring exact distance between my vegetable plants work better than just scattering the seeds across my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ ni misusuɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛshwãa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Giving plants specific spacing ensures each crop gets its own fair share of sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without fighting its neighbors, while also allowing air to flow between them to prevent leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ ko ha lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu lɛ mli yɛ bɔ ni sa mli ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ ewuuuu yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni ekɛtsi tsei lɛ ahe helai anaa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with plenty of leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich organic matter, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build large storage roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo tsɔ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ yaa si konɛ a pee sisi agbohi nɛ a toɔ níhi a mi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before setting fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, pepper plants get stressed and lose excess water. Dropping flowers is the plant's survival defense mechanism to conserve moisture and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ebu ehe koni ekagbi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees shed many of their tiny green pods early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Babaoo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: This natural shedding is called cherelle wilt. The cocoa tree thins out its own extra pods because it lacks enough water, shade, or nutrients to feed all of them to full maturity.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Cacao tsei lɛ baajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ejaakɛ amɛbɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛdara.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting shoots after a few months even inside a dark storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ tsũ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli po

english: Yam tubers have an internal biological clock called dormancy. Once this natural resting period ends after two to three months, the tuber automatically uses its stored nutrients to sprout new shoots, light or no light.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Beni adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ baa naagbee yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Tubers lɛ kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii heei. la kpɛɔ loo la bɛ kwraa

english: Why do tomato leaves turn yellow and develop brown spots during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves create the perfect condition for fungal fungal spores like blight to grow, which attack the leaves, block them from absorbing sunlight, and cause them to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight, ni tutuaa baa lɛ, ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ lɛ adalɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my young maize plants mostly overnight while hiding during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ fiteɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɔɔŋ kome mli, ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms are sensitive to heat and direct sunlight. They hide deep inside the moist whorl of the maize leaves during the hot day to avoid drying out and emerge at night when it is cool to feed aggressively.
ga: Asraafoi akuu lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai ni mli efɔ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Koni ekagbi ni eje kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni fɛ̃i miiye lɛ koni eye niyenii yɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why does the witchweed plant attach to my maize roots but does not grow on my groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ witchweed lɛ kpɛtɛɔ mi ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ahe shi ekɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ kpaaa gbee lɛ?

english: Witchweed seeds only germinate when triggered by chemical signals released specifically by grass and cereal roots like maize or sorghum. Legumes like groundnuts do not produce these signals and actually help starve out the weed.
ga: Witchweed dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ pɛ kɛji tsofai ni jɛɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmaa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa mli lɛ tsirɛɔ amɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ okadii nɛɛ tsuuu nii ni eyeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ jwɛi akudɔmɔ mli.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow healthy and green even when I do not add nitrogen fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria living in their roots to capture nitrogen gas directly from the air and convert it into natural plant food.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Keeping large shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool environment that protects young cocoa during its early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei wuji akwɛmɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe yɛ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips before the corn matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitseiaŋ dani abele lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the crop stay green and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans in my field help my other crops grow better?
ga: Cowpeas loo beans ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli. Te minɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When the plant leaves and roots break down, they release natural fertilizer into the soil for future crops to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fite Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water cuts off air supply to the roots and lets harmful fungi grow. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpaɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking the vines helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight, which travels down to swell the subterranean yam tuber.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli koni eha tso lɛ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwereɔ

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, making the plant top-heavy when carrying bunches. Tiny worms called nematodes or stem borers can also weaken the roots, so propping the stalk with bamboo helps support the tree until harvest.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii kɛ́ ewó ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi tso lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when temperatures get extremely hot or if the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests and diseases to multiply in the ground, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some seeds fail to sprout while others in the same bag grow very well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ kotoku kome mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are stored in damp places, planted too deep, or if the soil is too dry. Storing seeds in a cool, dry place and planting them at the proper depth helps them sprout uniformly.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛwo ŋmɔtɔ mli. adu mli tsɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi ni adu yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce such small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa yibii babaoo aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to develop strong leaves and full yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight, which scorches their leaves and dries out their roots. Planting shade crops like plantain or leaving large trees nearby provides a cooler microclimate and moisture that protect the young cocoa until it is mature enough to tolerate full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ hulutsoo be aba. Enɛ buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are a common sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to make healthy leaves and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plants produce green leaves and grow properly.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ awa ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ baai eŋɔli ni edaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Extra shoots and dense branches steal water and nutrients that should be going into flower and pod production. Pruning them allows more air and sunlight to move through the tree canopy, which keeps the farm dry and prevents fungal diseases from forming.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni esa akɛ akɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la babaoo boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔɔ, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ aba.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients in the soil. This competition leaves plants weak and results in small, thin roots rather than large, healthy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mohu ɔ, e ji kaa tso agbo nɛ e he wa.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa trees before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A tree naturally drops flowers it cannot support, but excessive flower loss is usually caused by dry soil, pest damage, or high heat. Keeping the soil covered with mulch helps preserve soil water so the tree can hold on to more of its flowers.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ ashwie shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine baa. Akpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ. loo la ni mli edɔ waa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mulching baaye abua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and cold conditions. Rain splashes the fungus onto the pods, so clearing weeds and keeping the canopy pruned lets sunshine and air dry out the farm to control the disease.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akwɛɔ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni helai akudɔ.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops lower the amount of food I harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal the fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight that your main crops need to grow. Removing weeds early ensures that all the nutrients in the soil go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛkwɛ tsei.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plantain and cocoa trees with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle kookoo dumɔwui kɛ tsei ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps plant roots cool and moist, and as the leaves decay, they turn into natural fertilizer for the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu akatsɔ oya Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni kɛ́ baai lɛ fite Ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes have a natural ability to take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the ground with plant food, making the soil more fertile for other crops planted with or after them.
ga: Legumes yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei krokomɛi ni adu kɛfata he loo yɛ esɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods show they are ready for harvest when their outer skin changes color, usually turning from green to bright yellow or red to orange. Harvesting when pods are fully colored ensures the beans inside are mature and ready for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji amɛkponɔgbɛ lɛ tsake su. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo etsuru kɛyaa akutu mli. Nikpamɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔlɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees bend or break when they produce too many pods at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛkuɔ kɛji amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo shikome lɛ?

english: When a tree bears too much fruit at one time, the heavy weight strains the trunk and branches. Without proper support or early harvesting, the tree can collapse under the heavy load and damage itself.
ga: Kɛ tso ko woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ Muji ni tsii haa tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni sa bɛ loo akpaaa mra Tso lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ shi yɛ muji ni tsii shishi ni efite ehe.

english: What happens if I leave ripe fruits on my trees for too long without picking them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa?

english: Leaving mature fruits on the tree forces the plant to keep feeding them, which drains all its energy. This makes the parent plant weak, exhausted, and less capable of producing healthy crops in the next season.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabi ni tso lɛ aya nɔ aye nii. Enɛ baaha hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. Enɛ haa tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔɔ, ni enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some extension officers advise me to pluck off some small fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ aduawai bibii dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Removing excess small fruits reduces the strain on the plant. It allows the crop to direct its strength into making the remaining fruits larger and healthier without exhausting the main plant.
ga: Yibii bibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ ehewalɛ nɔ koni eha aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni ehi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: How do I keep my plantain trees from falling down when the bunches get very large?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi be mli ni niji lɛ dara waa lɛ?

english: You can prop up the stems using strong wooden stakes or bamboo poles. Supporting the plant takes the heavy load off the main stem so strong winds or high weight won't knock it over.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni wa loo ŋmei ni akɛfee ŋmei lɛ afi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ sɛɛfimɔ jieɔ jatsu lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo muji ni tsii haŋ tso lɛ agbee shi.

english: Why does my maize fall to the ground right before harvest when the ears get heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ? He ni toi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: This is called lodging, which occurs when weak stems or weak roots cannot carry the heavy weight of mature cobs. Proper fertilization helps build stronger stems to keep the plants standing tall.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shihilɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei bibii loo shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmei ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: What causes the main branches of my mango tree to split and snap during the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni haa mango tsei aniji titrii lɛ fãa ni amɛkuɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Branches split when the weight of the fruit exceeds what the wood can carry. Pruning weak branches early and propping heavy ones with sticks prevents the tree from suffering structural damage.
ga: Tso lɛ niji lɛ gbálaa kɛ́ tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsiimɔ fe nɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ atere lɛ. Niji bibii ni aaafo mra Ni niji ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛfi niji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ shishitoo nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my plantain crop look weak and yellow after producing a huge bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni amɛwo yibii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Producing heavy fruit draws out most of the plant's stored nutrients. If you do not feed the soil extra nutrients after a heavy harvest, the plant becomes starved and physically weak.
ga: Yibii ni tsii ni anáa lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni ato lɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni wa sɛɛ. Hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: What can I give to a weak crop to help it recover quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ maha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Applying fast-acting fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the base provides quick food to the root system, helping the plant rebuild its strength and recover from exhaustion.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii oya loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Konui lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tɔlɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to add manure to the soil right after I finish harvesting my tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Harvesting takes away the goodness that the tree absorbed from the ground. Adding manure feeds the soil again, encouraging the tree to regain its health for future seasons.
ga: Nikpamɔ jieɔ kpakpa ni tso lɛ shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Can putting fertilizer around the base of a collapsing plant bring it back to strength?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso ni efite lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha eku esɛɛ eba ni ehiɛ hewalɛ?

english: If the plant is falling over due to nutrient depletion and weakness rather than root rot, giving it water and fertilizer provides direct nourishment that helps it regain vigor and stay alive.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ gbee shi yɛ niyenii ni esaaa kɛ bɔjɔmɔ hewɔ Yɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ najiaŋ Nu ni okɛwoɔ otsei lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa amɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are some farmers in Ghana using plastic sheets to cover their vegetable crops instead of growing them in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ kɛ plastic ŋmɔji miiha aduawai ahe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Plastic covers protect sensitive crops from heavy rains, harsh sunlight, and severe pests, creating a safer environment where plants can grow year-round.
ga: Plastic nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Feemɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do crops inside a plastic greenhouse sometimes wither even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ plastic greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Trapped hot air inside a plastic structure can raise the temperature too high, stress the plants, and make them burn or wither even if the soil is wet.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni emɔ plastic tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo lɛ aya hiɛ tsɔ. haomɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni eha eshã loo egbo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why is it important to have openings or vents at the top of a greenhouse roof?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ko loo ŋwɛi ŋta ko yɛ greenhouse lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Hot air naturally rises to the top, so roof vents allow that trapped heat and steam to escape, keeping the air inside cool enough for healthy plant growth.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baate shi kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋwɛi ŋtayaai yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nu mli lasu ni emɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do water droplets collect on the inside of plastic farm covers, and does this harm my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ plastic ni akɛhaa ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani enɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Water droplets form when moisture from the soil and plants gets trapped. High humidity inside can cause fungal diseases, so the moist air needs a way to escape through vents.
ga: Nu mli ŋmeii baa kɛji nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ batsɔ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ aná he ko ni etsɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli.

english: Does the shape of a plastic farm shelter affect how heat stays inside it?
ga: Ani bɔ ni plastic ŋmɔ mli shĩai lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ saa dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, rounded or dome-shaped covers naturally trap heat at the very top, which makes proper roof ventilation especially important to release the trapped hot air.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ ni yɔɔ kokroo loo dome lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tsũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ he hiaa waa koni ajie kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ.

english: How can I keep my crops cool under plastic covers during the hottest months of the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ plastic ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ shishi yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can keep crops cool by opening top and side vents to allow fresh air to flow through, or by using shade netting over the plastic to block direct burning sunlight.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi kɛ sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii ni ooogbele koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ shade net atsu nii yɛ plastic lɛ nɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsĩ naa.

english: What happens to tomatoes or peppers if the temperature inside a plastic shelter gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni baa tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ plastic shĩa lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ?

english: Extreme heat causes plant flowers to drop off before turning into fruits, which lowers your total harvest.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii. Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ aba shi.

english: What happens if a plastic greenhouse is completely sealed without any windows or air gaps?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ atsĩ plastic tsũ ko mli kwraa ni samfɛji loo kɔɔyɔɔ ŋmeii bɛ mli?

english: Without airflow, heat and moisture build up like an oven, suffocating the crops and creating an environment where plant diseases spread very fast.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i buaa amɛhe naa tamɔ flɔnɔɔ. ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ baa.

english: Which crops grow best under plastic shelters in warm climates like Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ plastic tsũi ashishi yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ tamɔ Ghana?

english: High-value vegetables like tomatoes, sweet peppers, and cucumbers benefit most because they are easily damaged by excessive rain and pests in the open field.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi babaoo yɛ aduawai ni jara wa tamɔ tomato, bell pepper, kɛ kukumba he fe fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ fiteɔ nɛkɛ aduawai nɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops need fresh air moving around them if they are already protected inside a greenhouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Kɛji akɛ abu tsei lɛ ahe momo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Moving air brings fresh carbon dioxide that plants need to make food, strengthens their stems, and carries away extra heat and humidity.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji carbon dioxide ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii lɛ. Wo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ojie dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them in an open field without any larger crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni ŋmɔshi nibii wuji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Without shade from faster-growing plants like plantains or tall trees, the intense sun scorches their tender leaves, dries out the soil, and causes the young plants to wilt and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ ni jɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo tsei kakadaji amli lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai bibii, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ, ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why should I cut down extra small suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the mother plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight from the same root system. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, allowing the main stem to produce larger, heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ shishifã kome lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ woɔ plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Abɛi gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛha baa heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baawo mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside or after maize, they enrich the soil naturally, helping food crops grow better without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up. Rotating your crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ni efoɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter which direction I point a cassava stem cutting when I stick it into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaatsɔɔ he ni esa akɛ afo ŋmei tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, it matters greatly. Cassava stems have small leaf nodes or buds that must point upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow properly, leading to weak plants and low tuber yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia waa. Kasava tso lɛ yɛ baai bibii loo ŋmeii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tsobii lɛ baawa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do we make big dirt mounds to plant yams instead of just putting the seed yam flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa sũi wuji ni wɔkɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft, well-drained soil to expand and grow deep tubers. Creating mounds loosens the earth so the tuber can swell easily without hard soil blocking it, while also keeping water from pooling and rotting the root.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afu oya ni shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ etsĩii amɛnaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekabua ehe naa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the ground when I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often waters only the top layer of soil while the deeper soil remains dry and hot. If a dry spell follows immediately, the seeds get just enough moisture to swell, but get trapped in hot dry dirt and rot before they can establish deep roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi ni edɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ he okadii ba amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfu. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ zugba nɛ mi dɔ nɛ e gbi ɔ mi nɛ a puɛɔ loko a nyɛɔ nɛ a woɔ sisi nɛ mi kuɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers just dry up and fall off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when exposed to extreme heat or severe dry weather. Very high temperatures damage the pollen inside the flower, preventing fruit from forming and causing the plant to drop its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi mli. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so quickly even if I make sure to give my field plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutua miŋmɔshi nibii oya nɛkɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo ha ŋmɔji lɛ po.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than your crops can. Even with regular watering, weeds leave your main crops starving for the basic food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nu wo mli daa po lɛ, jwɛi lɛ hu haa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and cocoa together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant cassava with young cocoa to maximize land use and harvest food early, but cassava grows very fast and can easily overpower young cocoa if not properly managed.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ kookoo bibii adu ŋmei koni shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ aya hiɛ ni okpa niyenii mra. Yucca daa oya waa, ni ebaanyɛ eye kookoo bibii anɔ kunim yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I plant cassava from my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei kɛjɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ he ni yɔɔ teŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: You should leave enough space—usually at least 2 to 3 meters—between cassava and cocoa so that the wide cassava branches do not spread over and block sunlight from the young cocoa.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi gbɛ ko yɛ tapioka lɛ kɛ kookoo lɛ teŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, mitai 2 kɛyashi 3 bɔni afee ni akagbɛ ŋmei niji ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ ashwã. Egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees growing so slowly under my cassava plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Cassava grows quickly with large, bushy branches that can steal essential sunlight, air, and nutrients from young cocoa trees if planted too close.
ga: Yucca daa oya kɛ niji agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baanyɛ aju hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ cacao tsei bibii amli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ.

english: What should I do if my cassava leaves are completely covering my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai lɛ ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kwraa?

english: You can cut back or prune the overgrown cassava branches that are leaning over the cocoa, which frees up sunlight for the cocoa while keeping the cassava alive.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo loo ofolɔ yucca tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kookoo lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha kookoo lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abuɔ ŋmei lɛ he.

english: Will my cassava plant die if I cut off some of its branches to help my cocoa?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tso lɛ baagbo kɛji mifolɔ niji komɛi koni mikɛhere kookoo lɛ yiwala?

english: No, cutting back some branches from a cassava plant will not kill it; it will continue growing roots while allowing sunlight to reach your cocoa.
ga: Dabi, o-yucca lɛ niji lɛ ekomɛi ni ooofo lɛ egbeŋ lɛ. Ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shishifãi yɛ be mli ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ okoo lɛ he.

english: How do I know if another crop is choking my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kroko miigba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anaa?

english: If your young cocoa trees look thin, stretched, or pale because heavy branches from neighboring plants like cassava are blocking light, the neighboring plant is choking your cocoa.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo, egbɛ eshwa, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ejaakɛ tsei niji ni tsii ni jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ yucca lɛ amli lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ miiye o-cocoa lɛ.

english: Is full shade from cassava branches good for young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani hulutsoo ni jɛɔ ŋmei niji amli lɛ hi kɛha kookoo dumɔwui?

english: No, while young cocoa needs gentle shade, thick overhead branches from cassava create too much shade, which weakens the cocoa and traps too much dampness.
ga: Dabi, yɛ be mli ni kookoo gbekɛ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔlɔ ni mli jɔ. Shi tsei niji ni mli tse ni jɛ yucca lɛ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli.

english: Which crop should I prioritize if my cassava is fighting space with my cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ mikɛfee nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛji akɛ mi-yucca lɛ kɛ mi-cocoa he lɛ miiwu?

english: Cocoa is your long-term income investment, so you should prioritize cocoa by trimming back or removing any surrounding cassava branches that are disturbing it.
ga: Cocoa ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli koni akɛná shika ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ kookoo afee nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei niji ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ooofo loo ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. No gbaa kookoo lɛ naa.

english: Will my cassava tubers still develop if I chop back some of its leafy branches?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ lolo kɛji mifo tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Yes, trimming excess branches will not ruin your harvest; the cassava will still produce tubers, and your cocoa tree will get the light it needs to grow properly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni oookpa lɛ efiteee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Cassava baawo ŋmeii lolo. Ni o-cacao tsei lɛ baaná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How often should I check my farm to make sure fast-growing crops aren't harming my cocoa?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ eyeee mikoo lɛ awui?

english: You should check your field regularly every few weeks so you can catch overgrown cassava or plantain branches early before they stunt the growth of your cocoa trees.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be. otsii enyɔ komɛi Koni amɔmɔ ŋmei loo dumɔwui ni daa oya dani kookoo tsei lɛ afee amɛdalɛ fioo.

english: What does it mean when an extension worker says my rice is in the milking stage?
ga: Kɛji extension nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi-rice lɛ yɛ mlikimɔ mli lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: The milking stage is when the young rice grains are filling up with a white, liquid starch that looks like milk. It shows that the grain is actively forming and growing inside the head of the plant.
ga: Be ni akɛwoɔ mliki mli lɛ ji be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji nu yɛŋ ni tamɔ mliki woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli obɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui miifee ni amɛmiida waa yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do the rice grains feel soft and milky inside before they get hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ mliki yɛ mli dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Inside the grain, the plant stores food as a liquid starch at first. As the crop matures and dries under the sun, that milky liquid solidifies into the hard rice grain we eat.
ga: yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli Shishijee lɛ Tsei toɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji nu mli. Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛgbi yɛ hulu la shishi lɛ Nakai nu ni tamɔ mliki lɛ mli wa ni etsɔɔ ŋmaa ni wa ni wɔyeɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I divide my fertilizer into different applications instead of putting it all on my farm at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aja ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo nitsumɔi srɔtoi amli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome lɛ

english: Applying fertilizer in stages gives your crops food right when they need it most during growth. If you put it all at once, much of it gets washed away by rain before the plants can use it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ waa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ okɛ amɛ fɛɛ to he lɛ Nugbɔ shwieɔ amɛteŋ babaoo dani anyɛɔ akɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: How can I tell that my final fertilizer application is actually working on my rice crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ tsu nii diɛŋtsɛ eha miŋmɔji lɛ?

english: You will notice a clear change in the look of your farm—the plants will look stronger, the leaves will stay healthy, and the rice heads will start filling out quickly.
ga: Obaana tsakemɔ ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa. Baai lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa. ni ŋmãa yitsei lɛ baabɔi eyimɔ oya.

english: Does my rice crop still need food or fertilizer when the grain heads start showing?
ga: Ani niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ lolo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ bɔi kpojiemɔ pɛ?

english: Yes, this stage requires nutrients to fill the grains properly. A late fertilizer boost provides the energy the plant needs to build full, heavy grains instead of light or empty ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo dumɔwui ni tsiimɔ fa babaoo. Yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ

english: What happens to my harvest if I miss or delay the late fertilizer application?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ fɔmɔ nii lɛ shwieee shi loo mikɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ hu?

english: Delaying late fertilizer means the plant will not have enough food during grain development, resulting in small, weak, or empty rice grains that reduce your total yield.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ ni akɛbaagbe naa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmaa lɛ shweremɔ be mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii, ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Rice is ready for harvest when most of the grains turn from green to a golden-yellow color and the grains have hardened, showing that the growth phase is completely finished.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmaa lɛ mli babaoo tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dalɛ fã lɛ egbe naa.

english: What will happen if I harvest my rice while the grains are still soft and milky?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ mliki lolo lɛ?

english: Harvesting too early when grains are soft causes them to break easily during milling, rot during storage due to high water content, and fetch a lower price at market.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ mra tsɔ beni ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛkuɔ oya yɛ ŋmãa be mli. Rot yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. ni oná jara ni baa shi fe nɔ ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ

english: Why is it important to have an agricultural officer inspect my farm before I start harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko akwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpamɔ aje shishi lɛ?

english: An officer can check the exact maturity of your crops and guide you on the best days to harvest so you don't lose crop quality or harvest too early or too late.
ga: Nitsulɔi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ afii pɔtɛɛ ni onibii lɛ yeɔ ni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ gbii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ okpa lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni okafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo okpa mra loo sɛɛ tsɔ.

english: Why does the overall appearance of my rice farm change so quickly after it reaches its final growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bɔ ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɔɔ lɛ tsakeɔ oya beni mishɛ naagbee dalɛ fã lɛ he lɛ?

english: Once the plant finishes taking up its final nutrients, all its energy shifts from growing leaves to filling the grains, causing the plants to change color and heavy heads to bend naturally.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná naagbee niyenii lɛ, hewalɛ fɛɛ jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli kɛyaa dumɔwui lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ su tsakeɔ ni eyitso ni tsii lɛ tsɔɔ ehe.

english: How do I know if the early rains are enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture in the soil to sprout properly. If you plant after just one short shower, the hot dry ground will dry out and kill the seeds before they can grow, so it is best to wait until the soil is soaked deep down.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji odu yɛ nu ni okɛwo nu mli kuku sɛɛ shikome pɛ Hot, hei ni egbi lɛ baagbi ni ekpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ ebote mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow when there is too much rain in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil with water, which smothers the plant roots. Without air, the roots cannot breathe or feed the plant, causing the leaves to turn yellow from stress.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni kɛ tso shishifãi fiteɔ Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛhaŋ tso lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ haomɔ mli.

english: How does heavy rain affect my crop plants while they are in flower?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lolo lɛ?

english: Strong rains can beat delicate flowers off the plant or wash away the pollen needed to produce fruit, which reduces the total amount of grain or produce your crops will form.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atswa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ anɔ loo efɔ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii lɛ kɛya. Enɛ haa ŋmaa loo onibii ni oduɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do improved seeds grow better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are selected to resist local diseases, endure weather changes better, and grow stronger roots, whereas saved seeds lose their vigor over time and produce smaller yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli waa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: What happens to my crop plants if I apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall will wash away the fertilizer from the top of the soil before your crop roots have time to absorb it, wasting your inputs and leaving the plants without nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ni afiteɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my crop leaves grow greener and faster after I add fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ oya beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers provide essential nutrients like nitrogen that act as direct food for the plant, helping it build strong stems and green leaves to make its own energy.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa tsei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni emaa tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli koni ekɛfee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from lack of water during a dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu efo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During hot dry periods, crop leaves will roll up or droop during the day to save water; if they stay wilted in the cool early morning, the plant is under severe water stress.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ, ni egbiɔ Tse lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛji amɛgboi lolo yɛ fɛ̃i mli leebi maŋkpa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa shishi.

english: How can I tell by looking at my crops that they are ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛ mikwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Crops show they are ready when their leaves turn yellow and dry out, and the seeds, pods, or tubers harden and reach their full color, showing the plant has stopped growing.
ga: Akɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi ni dumɔwui lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ, loo ŋmeii lɛ amli wa ni amɛhiɛ su fɛɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains rot or get moldy when I keep them inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛto shĩa mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops contain trapped moisture. If you store them before drying them completely, mold and insects thrive in that moisture and quickly spoil the crop.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpɛtɛ amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ okɛto dani egbi kwraa. Mold kɛ kooloi bibii shwereɔ yɛ nakai ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo oya.

english: Why does keeping my harvested crops in a cool, well-ventilated room keep them fresh longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ to tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Good airflow carries away the heat and dampness released by harvested produce, preventing mold growth and keeping insects from multiplying while you wait for better prices.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ nibii ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anaa ni etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my oil palm trees turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Oil palm leaves naturally age and turn yellow as the tree grows and directs energy to producing fruit bunches. Pruning these dead or yellow lower leaves helps the tree focus its nutrients on healthy growth and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Mu tso lɛ baai lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ daa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai akui. Nɛkɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egboi loo ni miifee ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ni aaafo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my young palm fruit bunches fall off the tree before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm yibii bibii lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Palm fruit bunches often drop early because of severe drought, nutrient shortages in the soil, or pest attacks. Ensuring your soil stays moist and feeding the trees proper fertilizer prevents the palm from aborting its fruit.
ga: Palm yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa hewɔ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa aha tso lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafo aduawai.

english: How can I make sure the palm produce I harvest is high quality and full of oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmei ni mikpaa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni fɔ eyi mli obɔ?

english: High-quality palm produce comes from planting certified improved seed varieties, maintaining proper soil nutrients through fertilizer, and harvesting only when the fruit bunches are fully mature.
ga: Palm tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni anáa lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni sa lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkpaa pɛ kɛji aduawai akui lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my oil palm fruit bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mu tso yibii lɛ?

english: An oil palm bunch is ready to harvest when a few loose, ripe fruits naturally detach and fall to the ground around the tree trunk, showing that the oil content inside the bunch has reached its peak.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji tso lɛ yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ekomɛi shwie shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ mu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ he ni eshɛɔ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellowish-green even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellowish leaves usually mean your maize crop is lacking essential soil nutrients, particularly nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the crop the strength it needs to develop deep green leaves and big, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ená baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural shield to reduce water loss during intense heat. While temporary curling is normal, covering the soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps keep the roots cool and moist.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ tsei ahe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehi akɛ oootsɔ oyitsɔi nɔ be kukuoo ko moŋ, shi kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) wo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and space, resulting in many thin tubers. Proper spacing gives roots enough room to expand into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitsei babaoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Does leaving weeds around my crops really reduce the amount of yield I harvest?
ga: releasing weeds around Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act like crop thieves by stealing water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get full nourishment to grow strong and yield well.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii julɔi kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei titrii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans naturally trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my crop roots stay shallow instead of growing deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ shi moŋ ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Roots stay shallow when crops receive frequent, light watering that only wets the top layer of soil. Deep, less frequent watering encourages roots to grow downward searching for water, making the plant stronger against dry conditions.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ shii abɔ kɛ nu fioo pɛ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli kwɔ ni anyɛɛɛ awo mli shii abɔ lɛ baawo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara kɛya shi koni amɛyatao nu. Ehaa tsei lɛ waa kɛji amɛyɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Can I safely grow food crops like maize or cassava on land that was previously used for illegal mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Land used for mining often loses its fertile topsoil and may contain harmful chemicals or heavy metals. Before planting food crops, the soil needs testing, heavy restoration, and organic treatment to ensure crops grow well and produce food that is safe to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa shika tsuru lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni baa nii, ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo dade ni tsii baanyɛ ahi mli. Dani abaadu niyenii Ehe miihia ni aka sũ lɛ akwɛ. hewalɛ ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ he nii koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ.

english: Why do farming officers recommend planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts before planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa dani adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and trap it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it uses this stored nitrogen as natural fertilizer to grow faster and greener.
ga: Legumes yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any larger trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that shade the delicate cocoa seedlings and keep the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ hulutsoo. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small tubers when I plant the stems very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant nutrients in the soil. Giving each stem proper space allows the roots room to expand into large, healthy cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifã tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni efeɔ ŋmei shishifã agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize crop, and will it destroy my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani ebaafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that eats the growing leaves of young maize. If they are not controlled early, they destroy the plant's heart, preventing it from forming healthy corn ears.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji fallworms, ni ji kooloi ni fɔɔ baa ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra Ebaakpata tso lɛ tsui lɛ hiɛ. ni etsĩ ŋmãa toi ni mli wa lɛ feemɔ naa

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so much slower if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that grow aggressively and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your main crops, effectively starving your planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does cassava manage to survive through the dry season while my maize crop dries up completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Cassava is naturally drought-resistant; it stores water in its deep roots and naturally drops its leaves to save moisture during hot, dry weather. Maize has shallow roots and requires continuous water to stay alive.
ga: Cassava ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Ekɛ nu toɔ eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli, ni ejieɔ ebaa lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ehe hiaa nu daa koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves drop and wilt in the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso shwane mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. Applying dry leaves or grass as mulch around the plant base keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi tsu nii ni akɛha tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees snap or fall over right before the fruit bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ miikumɔ loo amɛmiigbee shi dani aduawai akui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold up the heavy weight of mature fruit bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with wooden stakes or bamboo poles prevents the tree from tipping over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni eda lɛ akutsei ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings die right after I transplant them from the nursery bed into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ trukaa beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving young plants causes transplant shock due to root disturbance and sudden exposure to harsh sunlight. Watering seedlings well and moving them in the late afternoon or on cloudy days helps them adjust without dying.
ga: Tsei bibii ni aduɔ awoɔ he kroko lɛ kɛ tso lɛ he shoofeemɔ baa yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa mɔ naa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni ajie amɛ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbooo.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft stems and shallow roots that cannot pull enough water from the soil during hot days, so bright sun quickly burns their leaves unless they have shade plants like plantain nearby.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ oya. Ja tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ.

english: Leaving too many side shoots forces the main plant to share its food and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches instead of one large, healthy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu aha. Enɛ haa plantains akui bibii feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives crop leaves their deep green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ahe baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars chew holes right in the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These pests, often fall armyworms, target the soft inner leaves of the maize plant funnel because that is where the growth is tender and easiest for them to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ. Ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ mlɛo kɛha amɛ akɛ amɛaaye.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy; when heavy rains flood the land without good drainage, the roots drown and rot in the waterlogged dirt.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts naturally suck nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, leaving free soil food for the maize planted in the next season.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shi niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmãa ni adu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it a mistake to spread fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji tɔmɔ akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the dry fertilizer away off the surface of the land before your crop roots have time to drink it in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young plants with dry palm leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground, or mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching, loo mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too hot or the plants do not get consistent water, the tomato plant gets stressed and drops its blossoms to save its own energy.
ga: Be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Tomato tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so slowly and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal the light, water, and soil nutrients meant for your main crops, starving your plants of what they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ náa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for leafy growth, or that the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and pull up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛjie niyenii.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil swings from very dry to very wet, which stresses the plant and prevents pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Strong midday heat causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than roots can absorb it, leading to temporary wilting until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Gbi lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How does growing vegetables inside a greenhouse protect my crop better than open field farming?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli okwaayeli?

english: A greenhouse acts as a barrier against heavy rains, scorching sun, and insect pests, creating a controlled environment where plants suffer less stress and produce higher yields.
ga: Greenhouses tsuɔ nii akɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulu ni tsoɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔ lɛ baa ni tsei lɛ bɛ haomɔ babaoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing big, leafy stems above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and leafy tops rather than storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai bibii kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: How can I figure out if a new crop will bring me a profit before I buy seeds and farm tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko baaha miná sɛɛnamɔ dani mahe dumɔwui kɛ okwaayeli he nibii?

english: Calculate your total production costs—like land preparation, seeds, fertilizer, and labor—and compare that total against your expected harvest sale price to see if a profit remains.
ga: Buu shika fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ he akɔntaa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ, dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nitsumɔ, ni okɛ nakai shika lɛ fɛɛ ato jara ni okpaa gbɛ akɛ obaahɔɔ yɛ nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe lɛ he koni ona kɛji sɛɛnamɔ ko yɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and smaller overall yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cabbage plants have small holes chewed through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni ashɛreɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by insect pests like caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves, which reduces the plant's ability to make food and grow properly.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same piece of ground every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Continuous planting of the same crop depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field year after year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and brittle, and the inside of the pods shows dark brown or black markings when shelled.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Ni pod lɛ mli baaná okadii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛji ajie lɛ.

english: Does a bigger cocoa pod always mean I will get more cocoa beans from it?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni da lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ minine shɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo nɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: Not necessarily. Sometimes a large pod has a very thick husk with smaller or fewer beans inside. What matters most is how full and mature the beans are, not just the size of the outside pod.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmeii wuji lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa waa, ni ŋmeii fioo loo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ji bɔ ni kɔfi lɛ shwereɔ kɛ bɔ ni edara ha. Jeee bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ pod lɛ dalɛ ji lɛ pɛ.

english: How can I tell if a small cocoa pod on my tree actually has good beans inside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko hi kɛha mi? Kookoo yibii kpakpai yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ. Ani eyɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can check by looking at its color and firmness when ripe. If a small pod is fully ripe (yellow/orange) and feels firm rather than hollow, the beans inside are usually full and ready for harvesting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ shiŋŋ ha beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa (yellow/orange) ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eyi ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Is it good practice to harvest small ripe cocoa pods together with the big ones?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaakpa kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kɛfata kookoo ŋmeii wuji ahe?

english: Yes, as long as the small pod is fully ripe. Ripe small pods still contain good quality beans that contribute to your total weight, so you shouldn't leave them to waste.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be ni pods lɛ ji bibioo lɛ. Beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lolo lɛ, ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amli lolo, ni no haa ogbɔjɔmɔ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ esaaa akɛ ohaa efeɔ yaka.

english: Why are the beans inside some of my harvested cocoa pods flat instead of full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii ni yɔɔ mi kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Beans stay flat when the pod is harvested too early before maturity, or if the tree did not get enough water and nutrients while the pod was filling up.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akpa pods lɛ mra tsɔ dani amɛdara. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ náaa nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: How can I estimate how many bags of cocoa I will harvest before the season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu kookoo abɔ ni esa akɛ akpa dani be lɛ aje shishi lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can estimate your yield by counting the full, healthy pods on a few average trees in your farm. On average, it takes about 10 to 12 full cocoa pods to yield one pound of dried beans.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ni obaawo lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyi obɔ lɛ akanemɔ nɔ. Kɛ aja mli lɛ, eheɔ aaafee kookoo ŋmeii 10 kɛyashi 12 ni eyi obɔ dani anyɛ afee kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi ni tsiimɔ ji pound 1.

english: How many pods does a single cocoa tree usually produce in a good season?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tso kome fɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ woɔ yɛ be kpakpa mli?
