english: A healthy mature cocoa tree under good care typically produces between 20 to 80 pods per year, depending on soil quality, rainfall, and farm maintenance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tso ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baawo ŋmeii 20 kɛyashi 80 daa afi, ni enɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Should I count every single small pod on my tree when calculating my expected crop yield?
ga: Esa akɛ makane pods bibii lɛ. Ani pod fɛɛ pod ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ ebaaba lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: No, you should not count tiny pods (cherelles) because the tree will naturally shed many of them before they grow full. Only count pods that have reached medium to large sizes and look healthy.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii bibii (cherelles) lɛ anɔ, ejaakɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii babaoo dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Pods ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛyashi agbo ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni akaneɔ.

english: Why do some of the tiny cocoa pods on my tree dry up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Ani mitsei lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaafee ediŋŋ dani amɛdara?

english: This natural dropping is called 'cherelle wilt.' The tree drops extra young pods it cannot support with its available water and nutrients. However, if blackening spreads fast, it could also be Black Pod disease.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ 'cherelle wilt'. Tso lɛ baajie ŋmeii bibii krokomɛi ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ diŋ lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee black pod hela hu.

english: Can I use seeds from a small cocoa pod to raise new seedlings for my farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii atsu nii. Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: It is better to pick seeds from large, healthy pods taken from your highest-producing trees. Planting seeds from strong pods gives your new trees a better chance of high yield.
ga: Esa akɛ ahala dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ haa tsei heei náa hegbɛ kpakpa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What causes cocoa pods to stop growing full even when the weather is good?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei lɛ kpaɔ kwɛ̃mɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi po?

english: Pods often stop filling up if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium, or if pests like capsid bugs are feeding on the tree sap and weakening the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kpaɔ nu ni amɛkɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛji akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛji kooloi tamɔ jellyfish ye tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛha tso lɛ gbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the soft leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger crops like plantains or shade trees because direct overhead sunlight scorches their soft tender leaves and dries out the soil around their shallow roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ eyitso nɔ lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn pale yellow after heavy rain flooding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits in the field for too long, it pushes air out of the soil and washes away plant nutrients like nitrogen, causing the roots to suffocate and the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsei amli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I plant the stem cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If cassava plants are placed too close, their leaves block sunlight from each other and the roots fight for nutrients under the ground, resulting in many small thin roots instead of large fat tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo Babaoo yɛ yitsei wuji ni yɔɔ fɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ shweremɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Removing the extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, which ensures the main plant gets all the water and food from the soil needed to produce big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ nɔ koni ewo aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: How does leaving dry grass on top of my farm soil help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves acts like a blanket that blocks direct sun, keeping the soil cool and trapping water underneath so crop roots stay wet longer.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu yɛ eshishi koni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes right in the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the deep, protected center of young maize plants where the leaves are softest and easiest for them to chew.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni abuɔ amɛhe waa lɛ ateŋ, he ni baai lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden extreme heat or when the soil changes rapidly from very dry to overly wet.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ nɔ.

english: Weeds are wild plants with tough seeds already resting in the soil that react immediately to rainwater, absorbing nutrients faster than nursery-raised or newly planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛdumɔwui wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo. ni baatsu nugbɔ nu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and feeling hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids that spread a virus while feeding on the juices inside the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa be mli ni enuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help the maize crop I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmeii ni midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull natural fertilizer (nitrogen) out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, leaving richer soil behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tips down the leaf center, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which the crop needs to make green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa lɛ naa kɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my maize plants and leaving small holes everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni maye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ ni mashi bu bibii. Ani eyi he fɛɛ he?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides deep inside the growing center of maize plants. Checking your field regularly and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended bio-pesticides into the plant center will stop them from destroying your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tso ko ni edaa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and tender roots that easily burn under strong direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective umbrella that keeps the soil cool and humid during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ ehe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from high heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving your plants consistent moisture during dry periods and balancing your fertilizer will help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛ́ ooha tso lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahi shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are mature and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You know it is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the base of the main stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. O le kaa e pee klaalo benɛ tsohi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ tsɔ blɔ nya ngɛ adebɔ mi ɔ nɛ a ngmɛɛ si ɔ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without killing my yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works very well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the remaining field space after the maize is cleared.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli, ni eŋɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper distance ensures every stalk receives enough light and food to produce thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ sa lɛ, ehaa amɛ fɛɛ amɛnáa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark brown spots and dry up during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by fungal leaf blight, which spreads quickly when raindrops splash soil onto lower leaves in warm, humid weather. Spacing plants properly for good airflow and keeping the soil covered with straw mulch helps prevent splash-back and disease.
ga: Fuŋɔ ko ni kɛ baa tsɛŋemɔ baa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔi shwie shikpɔŋ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ to he ko jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni akɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no tsiɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi kɛ helai anaa.

english: What can I do to keep the soil on my farm from drying out and hardening so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi ni efee ais oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast because direct sun evaporates the water. Covering the soil surface around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulching) acts as a blanket, keeping the ground cool and holding water for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ ni oooha Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) baatsu nii akɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right day to sow my seeds when the early rains are unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ bɛ mlɛo kwraa lɛ?

english: Instead of sowing seeds right after the very first light shower, wait until the soil is thoroughly wet to a depth of at least a hand's length. Sowing in deeply wet soil ensures seeds germinate evenly and form strong roots that survive short dry spells.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni kɛ hoo lɛ, tso nine kome baashɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa ni hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them acts like a living umbrella, protecting the young cocoa until it grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize turns pale yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to make green leaves and grow large ears. Adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen fertilizer will give the plants the food they need to turn dark green again.
ga: Abɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ toi wuji Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, but waterlogged soil starves them of oxygen and causes rot. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ebaaha egbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: My tomato plants are producing many flowers, so why are the flowers dropping off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough steady water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extreme afternoon heat helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with my other crops help my farm?
ga: Peanuts kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi adumɔ Te minɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which means their roots work with natural soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally feeds and enriches the soil for nearby crops.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ nii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are there small holes and dark dirt inside the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli.

english: Small holes and leaf damage are signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center whorl of the corn stem. Spraying natural neem leaf extract or approved pest controls early in the morning destroys the caterpillars before they destroy the crop's main growing tip.
ga: Buu bibii kɛ baai ni efite lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ateŋ lɛ he okadii. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ shi leebi lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ fãi titrii lɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and weak with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and light to grow thick stems and produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa baa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my pepper plants right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to steal water and nutrients from the soil faster than domestic farm crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures your pepper plants get all the water and fertilizer you give them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe shia ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-pepper tsei lɛ aná nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okɛhaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to lift their leaves off the ground and spread them out into the sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more energy the plant sends down to swell the yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baaha amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã hulu la lɛ mli. Babaoo ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo lɛ, babaoo ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves on my garden egg plants droop during the hot afternoon but stand up straight again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi te shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: Garden egg leaves droop in intense heat to close their tiny air pores and save water from evaporating. Once the sun sets and temperatures cool down, the roots absorb water again and the leaves recover.
ga: Wɔɔji ahe baai ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ koni ekɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ bu bibii lɛ anaa. ni etsĩ nu naa koni ekaho Kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ekoŋŋ ni baai lɛ he waaa.

english: Why does my cassava crop take around 9 to 12 months in the soil before it is ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani eshɛɔ he ni ebaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava spends its first few months building a strong stem and large leaves to catch sunlight. It is only in the middle and later months that it starts transferring that energy underground to grow thick, starchy root tubers.
ga: Yucca heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ dani enáa tsei ni wa kɛ baai wuji ni ekɛ hulu la lɛ baatsu nii. Yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ nyɔji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli pɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebaaje nakai hewalɛ lɛ shishi kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee shishifãi ni mli tse ni tamɔ powda.

english: Why do plantain suckers take nearly a full year to yield fruit while my maize produces in just three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi muu fɛɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli.

english: Plantains are large, heavy perennial plants that need many months to build a thick false stem and broad leaves to support heavy fruit bunches, whereas maize is a fast-growing annual crop with a short life cycle.
ga: Plantain ji tso agbo ni tsii ni yeɔ afii babaoo. Akɛ nyɔji babaoo feɔ tso ni akɛ niji fee ni mli tse ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ koni eye ebua yibiiwoo ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ji tso ko ni daa afi ni daa oya ni ewala be kukuoo lɛ.

english: How can I know that my yam tubers underground are fully matured and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: You can tell your yams are mature when the vines and leaves above ground start turning yellow and drying naturally, showing that the plant has stopped growing and stored all its energy in the tuber.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ o-sweet potato lɛ edara beni wain tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ miito bulb lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if the first rain of the season is the real planting rain or just a temporary shower?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji dumɔ nugbɔ diɛŋtsɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko kɛkɛ?

english: A single rainfall can be misleading; it is best to wait until the soil stays moist for several inches deep over a few consecutive days before sowing your seeds so they do not dry up.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ atsɔ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ inchii babaoo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli dani odu dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and wilt when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a plant's natural defense to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, which helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out during hot daylight hours.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaaa amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant short-term crops like cowpea alongside crops that take many months to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo tamɔ tsina ŋmei yɛ tsei ni heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting short-term crops like cowpea between slow-growing crops covers the open soil to prevent weed growth and adds vital nitrogen back into the soil to feed the main crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ tsina ŋmei yɛ tsei ni daa blɛoo lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃. ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade trees planted around them during their early years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ afee hulutsoo tsei yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective canopy umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and cool until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than the food crops I planted on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, resilient plants naturally adapted to survive on very little water and poor soil, allowing them to absorb available nutrients faster than cultivated domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ nu fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ maji ni aduɔ amɛ yɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow during periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away key soil nutrients like nitrogen below the root line, or waterlog the soil so roots cannot breathe and pull up food for the leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie sũ mli nibii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ. aloo nu ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛjie niyenii amɛha baai lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear crop residues from my farm after a long harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Old crop stems and leaves can host pests, fungal spores, and diseases over the dry season, so clearing them breaks the pest cycle before you plant your next crop.
ga: Tso shishifãi kɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Fungal spores kɛ helai srɔtoi baanyɛ aba yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ otsi amɛhe lɛ, efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli dani oduɔ tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin plants with small cobs, giving you a smaller overall harvest than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa fɛɛ ni obaakpa lɛ bibioo fe tso ni akɛto he ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, showing it needs fertilizer or organic manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli he miihia bo.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right when heavy downpours begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away off the surface of the land or pushes it too deep into the soil before the crop roots can absorb it, wasting your money and effort.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eshɛreɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eheɔ shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Why is planting legumes like cowpea good for my land before I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ hi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the center whorl of my maize leaves during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide in the cool, moist center of the maize plant to avoid the hot afternoon sun and to protect themselves from birds and surface chemical sprays.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni wɔtsi wɔhe kɛjɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ koni obu ohe kɛjɛ okpoi kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if heavy rain stays on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting on the land blocks air from reaching the roots. Without oxygen, the cassava roots suffocate, allowing waterborne fungi and bacteria in the soil to rot the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafo. Ha ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there seems to be enough dirt for all of them?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛ fɛɛ yɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal vital sunlight, ground moisture, and nutrients. They also act as hiding places for insects and diseases that attack your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la ni he hiaa waa lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni tutuaa onibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli.

english: Why does cutting off small suckers or side branches help my tomato plants yield bigger fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Aloo jiemɔ niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ koni eye ebua mi-tomato tso lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Removing extra side branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on leaves and stems it doesn't need, allowing it to send all its food and water into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive warm dry spells?
ga: Mulching around Te fee tɛŋŋ ni mikɛ jwɛi ni mikɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, blocks the direct heat of the sun. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, keeping moisture available for crop roots longer.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are certified planting seeds so much more expensive than the regular maize I buy at the local market to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jara wa kwraa fe ŋmãa ni miheɔ daa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred, tested, and treated to sprout easily, resist diseases, and produce heavy yields. Grain sold in the market for food lacks this genetic strength and protective treatment, so planting it often leads to weak growth and poor harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, akaa amɛ akwɛɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Enyɛɔ helai anaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo. Nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ kɛha niyenii lɛ bɛ fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ kɛ hebuu. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu baaa.

english: Why should I buy fresh tomato seedlings from a nursery instead of just saving seeds from tomatoes I buy to cook?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe tomato dumɔwui heei kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli? Mohu ɔ, i ngɔɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ ngɛ tomato nɛ i heɔ kɛ hoɔ ɔ mi ɔ kɛ toɔ.

english: Nursery seedlings come from high-quality hybrid seeds nurtured in disease-free soil, giving them a strong start. Seeds saved from kitchen tomatoes often carry diseases and produce plants that grow unevenly with small, disappointing fruits.
ga: Nursery dumɔwui lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela bɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Ha amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, tomato dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tomato ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shĩa mli lɛ hiɛɔ helai ni ehaa tsei ni daa kɛ yibii bibii ni nijiaŋ jeɔ wui lɛ yeɔ egbɔ.

english: Can I replant an old yam head that has already produced tubers before, or do I need to buy fresh seed yams?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potato ŋmeii momo ni tsutsu lɛ amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ ekoŋŋ? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Fresh seed yams contain full energy reserves needed to sprout strong stems and grow large new tubers. Yam heads that have already completed a full growing cycle are drained of nutrients, which leads to weak sprouts and tiny tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni ji dumɔwui heei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni yeɔ emuu ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo tsei ni wa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii heei wuji amli. Akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni eda lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why does my cassava turn hard and woody when I leave it in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants pass their mature stage, they convert soft starches into tough, woody fibers to strengthen their root structure for survival. Harvesting at the right age ensures the tubers stay soft, starch-rich, and easy to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ho dalɛ be lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ Amɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ tso ŋmeii ni wa. Koni ewaje shishifã lɛ koni ehi shi. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni ahoomɔ waaa.

english: Why do my sweet pepper bushes produce smaller and thinner fruits as the plants get older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Aging pepper plants spend more of their energy maintaining old woody branches rather than feeding new fruit. Over time, the nutrient flow slows down, resulting in smaller, thinner-skinned peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei ni egbɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ niji ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ fe ni amɛkɛwoɔ aduawai heei. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhewolo lɛ mli tseee.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits start tasting bitter near the end of the plant's life cycle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa beni tso lɛ wala be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ naagbee lɛ?

english: As garden egg plants grow old and face environmental stress, they naturally produce bitter defense chemicals within their fruits, making late-season harvests tougher and less flavorful.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eggplants ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔ ni amɛnaa shihilɛ mli haomɔi. Amɛfeɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ ni afeɔ yɛ naagbee be lɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing far fewer pods now than when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Like all living things, cocoa trees naturally decline in vigor as they age. Their internal sap channels slow down, making it harder to push nutrients to flowers and pods, which is a sign that the farm needs pruning, soil feeding, or replanting.
ga: Taakɛ wala yibii krokomɛi ji lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Amɛmli lá fãji lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaatsi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afolɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, aha lɛ niyenii, loo adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do suckers taken from very old plantain stumps produce smaller bunches than fresh tissue culture plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ plantain shishifãi ni etsɛ waa lɛ amli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii fe ŋmeii heei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: Suckers cut from old plantain stumps often carry hidden pests, parasitic worms, and soil diseases from the mother plant. Laboratory-grown tissue culture plantains start completely pest-free and vigorous, allowing them to yield much bigger bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akutsei momo amli lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmeii, kɛ sũ mli helai ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Tso dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ laboratori mli lɛ jeɔ shishi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ babaoo.

english: Why does a mature coconut turn dry and oily inside instead of staying full of sweet water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni edara lɛ mli egbi ni amɛkpɛɔ yɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: As a coconut ages on the tree, the plant converts the sweet liquid inside into solid white meat (copra) to store oil for seed germination, changing the fruit's texture and primary use.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ dara lɛ Tso lɛ tsɔɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ mli efeɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni yɛŋ. (ŋmei loo) ni akɛtoɔ fɔ kɛha dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ Tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai amli kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why does my harvested oil palm fruit fetch a lower price if I wait a few days before selling it to the processor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm ni mikpaa lɛ jara baa shi kɛji mimɛ gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛhɔ̃ɔ mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once oil palm fruit is cut from the tree, it rapidly breaks down internally, raising its free fatty acid content. Processors pay less for older fruit because high acid levels degrade the quality and taste of the extracted palm oil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo mu tso lɛ yibii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ Ebaafite oya yɛ emli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fatty acids ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ ni yaa hiɛ. Mɛi ni feɔ aduawai lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo kɛha aduawai ni etsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, acid ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei fɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ ŋɔɔmɔ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand direct sunlight because their tender leaves lose water very quickly. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted beside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya waa. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of green leaves, but when I dig it up, the roots are thin and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi beni mifo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ amli tseee ni amɛji bibii?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from enriched soil or fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers underneath.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato bulbs amli yɛ amɛshishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape right down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main stem on older leaves is a clear signal that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the primary food crop plants use to build green leaves and grow sturdy.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my plantain tree give me very small bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains haa tsei niji bibii lɛ? kɛha mi kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: Every shoot growing around the mother plantain stem acts like an extra mouth to feed, taking water and nutrients away from the main stem. Cutting away excess suckers leaves all the plant food for the main tree so it can form large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain nyɛ lɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ naabu krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛhaa niyenii. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso lɛ niyenii fɛɛ yɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni efee aduawai akuu agbo.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants wither and fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. If the plant gets too hot or dries out completely, it sheds flowers to save its own strength instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ fe nine loo egbi kwraa Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do I need to provide tall sticks for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ aha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high in the air to capture sunlight for making food. Staking keeps leaves off the wet soil, preventing damp foliage diseases and allowing the plant to generate big tubers below ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi helai ni yɔɔ baai ni mli efɔ lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the new leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Twisted and curling leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath, sucking out leaf sap and causing the tender growing leaf tissues to grow unevenly.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo amɛshishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nuu nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ amli fãji ni miida blɛoo lɛ daa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee baa.

english: How does planting cowpea on my farmland help make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have natural partnerships with friendly bacteria in their roots that suck nitrogen gas directly from the air and trap it in the soil, leaving free fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ni kɛ helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ helai ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ tsakpaa. Enɛ shwieɔ nitrogen gas lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my oil palm tree produce flowers for months but fails to grow any palm fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii nyɔji babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ palm aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Young oil palms often produce only male flowers first to produce pollen before female flowers appear. It takes time for the tree to reach full maturity and produce both male and female flowers needed for pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso dumɔwui woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni amɛwoɔ pollen dani fɔfɔi yei lɛ jeɔ kpo. Eheɔ be dani tso ko daa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha pollination kɛ aduawai afeemɔ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize grains are dry enough to store without moulding?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-corn kernel ni akpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akɛto ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli?

english: When maize kernels are dry enough for long storage, they feel glass-hard under your thumbnail and make a sharp, metallic ringing sound when you rattle a handful of them together inside a bucket.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa tamɔ glase yɛ onine shishi. Ni efeɔ dade gbɛɛmɔ ko ni tswaa kɛji okɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii akuu ko shwie baagi lɛ mli.

english: This yellowing usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is a main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away from the roots, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea around the base of the plants will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants twisting up and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Ni ani eji ŋmɔŋ?

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. To prevent this, always plant disease-free cassava stems and ask your local extension officer for improved varieties that naturally resist the virus.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Bɔni afee ni atsĩ enɛ naa Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei tsei ni hela bɛ mli. Ni obi oakutsoŋ extension agent lɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe sane.

english: Why are the tips of my rice leaves turning a rusty orange color in my lowland swamp farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice grits lɛ miitsɔ rust orange yɛ mi-lowland peat ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This happens when there is too much iron dissolved in flooded soil, which poisons the rice roots. You can fix this by draining excess water from the field periodically to let air into the soil and applying potassium fertilizer to help the roots block the iron.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ dade babaoo ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsofa fɔŋ kɛha ŋmãa shishifãi Obaanyɛ osaa enɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni ooojie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ nɔ. koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni akɛ potassium ŋmɔshi nibii aye abua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsi dade naa.

english: Why are my tomatoes getting black, sunken spots on the bottom of the fruits before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebote shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular soil moisture during dry spells. Mulching around your plants to keep soil moisture steady and adding agricultural lime to the soil before planting will prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Mulching ni akɛbaabɔle Tsei lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ lime ni akɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my harvested groundnut pods mostly empty inside when I crack them open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods ni mikpa lɛ mli babaoo lɛ mli efee efolo kɛ́ migbele amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are expanding underground. Applying agricultural lime or gypsum around the base of the plants when they start flowering will ensure full, healthy seeds inside.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔi ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Okwaayeli mli lime loo gypsum ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛbɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or when the tree is stressed by drought. Maintaining adequate shade trees and avoiding spraying harsh chemical insecticides during peak flowering allows pollinating insects to do their work.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo be mli ni hɔmɔ miigba tsei anaa lɛ. Tso ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pollinators ni amɛtsuɔ amɛnitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored yams rot quickly in the barn just a few weeks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot in storage usually starts from tiny wounds created during harvesting or from microscopic pests in the soil. Be gentle when digging up yams, store only undamaged tubers, and ensure your storage barn has plenty of airflow and shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato ni fiteɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ pilamɔ bibioo ko. Nakai baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ awo mli blɛoo. Ha tubers ni bɛ muji pɛ ahi shi. Ni kwɛmɔ ni otsu lɛ mli aná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni sa.

english: Why do my full-grown plantain trees fall over easily during light rain or wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall when tiny underground pests like nematodes or plantain weevils destroy the root system. You can protect new plantings by peeling the roots of new suckers clean and dipping them in hot water or ash water before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo plantain weevils fite shishifãi lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu tsei heei ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii heei lɛ ashishifãi ni oootsi amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo nu ni mli edɔ loo sũ mli dani odu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why am I seeing small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Inspect your field regularly and apply recommended biopesticides or soapy water directly into the center funnel early in the morning before they dig deeper.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ daa ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo samla ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa dani otsa mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni shwane hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause heat stress, forcing pepper plants to drop flowers to preserve water. Covering the soil around your pepper plants with dried grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Mulching around Dumɔ pepper tsei kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi koni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving some shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective cover and keeps the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does my maize yield drop every year if I keep planting it on the exact same farm patch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients, especially nitrogen, from the soil. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally and keeps it rich.
ga: Kɛji oodu ŋmãa yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba titri lɛ nitrogen Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ Okɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake o ŋmãa lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni ewo fɔmɔ nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems during the heaviest part of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Excess water during heavy rains can saturate the soil and cause fresh cassava stem cuttings to rot before they can grow roots. Planting right when steady rains begin allows cuttings to root securely without drowning.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ niji heei lɛ agboi dani amɛshishifãi akwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tsei ni afo lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni nu lɛ shwieee amɛmli.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni miduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they lack consistent water. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, forcing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ bɛ amɛmli. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus stops the plant from producing food efficiently, resulting in stunted growth and small tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Viruses lɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my crops grow huge green leaves but produce very few fruits after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baabii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to focus all their energy on leaf and stem growth instead of fruit production. Using a balanced fertilizer containing phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit development.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai yaa hiɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition forces the plants to stretch upward to reach light, leaving them weak and unable to nourish large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni ená la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid corn ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their special strengths—such as high yield and disease resistance—in the next generation. Planting saved hybrid seeds leads to uneven growth and much lower yields compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛi krɛdɛɛi tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee aba ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing vital water, sunlight, and food from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or develop mold when I put it into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo nitoo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if it is bagged before it is fully dried. Trapped moisture inside the grains creates an environment for mold and insects to multiply, so drying maize thoroughly in the sun before storage is essential.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves and grow fast. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shi waa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi aha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for your next crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop stay green and keep growing even when it hasn't rained for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni eedara eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko otsii babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep underground roots that store water and food during rainy periods, allowing the plant to draw on those reserves and survive long dry spells when other crops wither.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ nyɛɔ enáa nakai ŋmei lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli beni tsei krokomɛi gboɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi beni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Trimming extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes through the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu ko yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing tip of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves. Spraying early or applying neem oil gets rid of them before they destroy the whole stalk.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ. Mra ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Aloo okɛ neem fɔ ajie dani ofite tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crop seedlings and will steal all the soil water and fertilizer. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops a head start to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui ni amɛbaaju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛje shishi amɛdara waa.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto wooden tall stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food. Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes gives them more sun, which sends extra food down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa niyenii krokomɛi baa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my pepper plants fall off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil moist and mulched helps the plant stay cool enough to hold onto its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni awo mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate like human babies and burn easily under strong, direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees next to them acts like a living umbrella, protecting the young leaves from drying out while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii, ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build strong leaves and stay green. Adding compost, manure, or the right nitrogen fertilizer will replenish the soil and help the maize recover its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii kɛha tsei ni miisumɔ ni amɛfee baai ni wa ni amɛhi shi akɛ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rainwater collects around the roots and stays trapped in the soil for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa. shishifãi ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms before any tomatoes actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani tomato lɛ eda diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects. Watering consistently at the root zone and keeping the soil cool helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ Nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ daa ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Te cowpeas loo beans ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have a natural ability to pull plant food (nitrogen) out of the air and fix it into the soil. The neighboring maize plants then drink up this extra nutrient from the earth to grow taller and yield more grain.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ krokomɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden stakes and train my yam vines to climb them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to produce the food that swells the tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes keeps the leaves healthy, exposes them to sun, and prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe, ni ebaatsi helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds after the very first rain of the season instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that heats up the ground again. If you plant too early, your seeds will sprout, but the young shoots will dry up and die before the steady rains truly return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting into tight curls and stopping the plant from growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. Clearing weeds around the farm and applying natural neem oil or mild insecticidal soap clears these pests so fresh leaves can expand.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ Okwaayeli kɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli ejɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã

english: Why should I prune and cut off some of the healthy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni majie lɛ?

english: Cutting away unnecessary inner branches allows fresh air and sunlight to pass through the tree's center. This extra airflow stops fungal diseases like black pod from growing and directs the tree's energy toward making large pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ mli ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ adalɛ kpaa ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji afeemɔ nɔ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do people spread dry grass and fallen leaves over the bare soil around their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ? Amɛŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching, and it acts like a blanket against the hot sun. It prevents water in the ground from evaporating, keeps the roots cool during hot days, and stops weeds from choking your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akashwie shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve water. It is a natural defense mechanism to stop moisture loss through the leaves, and the plant will grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my okra plants wilt during the hot afternoon even if the soil still feels a bit moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lolo moŋ?

english: On very hot afternoons, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Wilting is the plant's way of folding its leaves to reduce sun exposure and save water until the evening cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Withering ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu nu lɛ he kɛyashi ebaajɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn plants turning yellow from the tip downward in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiya shi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing down the center of older corn leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Corn needs nitrogen to stay green and build heavy ears, so applying fertilizer like urea or compost can correct this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmãa baa momo lɛ teŋ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi ni tsii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, improving air circulation to prevent leaf rot and helping the plant produce bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ebaa akafite ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛwo bulbs wuji.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they compete with it for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only the main plant and one successor, ensuring you get large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, dumɔwu titri lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni ena niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ esɛɛyelɔ kome pɛ ahi shi koni ona plantains ni tsii babaoo kɛ babaoo.

english: Why do farmers plant cocoa trees under the shade of bigger trees instead of clearing the land completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ kookoo tsei yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaatse shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Forest trees act like giant natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while protecting cocoa leaves from harsh sun and strong winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes when it gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛjieee tomato ko kwraa kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot get pollinated. When a flower fails to pollinate, the plant cuts off its energy supply and drops the flower to save resources.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ pollination tsuuu nii. Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollination lɛ Tsei lɛ baafo hewalɛ ni amɛshɛrɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie koni amɛkɛbu nibii ahe.

english: Why should I avoid spraying pest chemicals on my watermelon farm when bees are visiting the flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-watermelon ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe beni ŋmeii miisara fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants depend on bees to move pollen from male flowers to female flowers so fruit can form. Spraying chemicals while bees are active kills them, which leaves flowers unpollinated and reduces your harvest.
ga: Watermelon tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ wuobii anɔ koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo yibii. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baagbe amɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieee ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa onibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my pepper farm cause the pepper plants to stay short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from pepper roots. Clearing weeds gives the pepper plants full access to those resources so they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishifãi amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ náa nakai nibii lɛ fɛɛ. koni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting the young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Ebuɔ cacao tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start turning dark brown inside just two days after I dig it out of the ground?
