ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ feemɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots undergo rapid post-harvest deterioration as soon as they are separated from the plant. Chemical reactions trigger internal discoloration and rotting within 48 to 72 hours, which is why cassava needs to be processed or taken to market immediately after harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ he pɛ. Tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa emli su lɛ tsakeɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli, no hewɔ ni esa akɛ atsu ŋmei lɛ he nii loo akɛba jara nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying mulch helps the plant retain its flowers so they can turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛmiifee nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land make my next maize crop grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plant leaves and roots decay, they leave behind rich natural nitrogen that feeds the following maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsina ŋmei lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my leafy vegetable plants dry up so fast during the Harmattan season even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa leebi moŋ.

english: The dry Harmattan winds pull moisture out of plant leaves much faster than roots can absorb water from the soil. Covering the soil around your vegetables with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots in the barn after sitting for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mita shi nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally go into a resting state after harvest called dormancy. Once this period naturally ends, warmth and air signal to the tuber that it is time to grow a new plant, causing it to use its stored energy to push out sprouts.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛ be nɛɛ ba naagbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ bulb lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu tso hee. Enɛ haa ekɛ hewalɛ ni eto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjeɔ kpo.

english: Why do all my harvested tomatoes ripen at the same time and quickly turn soft and spoiled in the market basket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome ni efeɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya yɛ jarayeli tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes naturally produce an invisible gas called ethylene that speeds up ripening. When packed tightly together in wooden crates or baskets, this gas gets trapped, causing every tomato in the container to ripen rapidly at the same time.
ga: Tomato jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso adekai loo tso tsɛnsii amli jogbaŋŋ Gas nɛɛ baakã he. Enɛ haa tomato fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why did my maize cobs produce missing kernels and small grains when the rain stopped during the silk stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn cob lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni elaaje kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ nɛmɔ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Maize requires the most water during its flowering and silking period. If drought occurs while silks are receiving pollen, the fertilization process fails, resulting in cobs with missing or poorly developed grains.
ga: Nu he hiaa abele fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ ba yɛ be mli ni siliki ŋmeii lɛ miiná pollen lɛ, Fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ eshɛɛɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni ekumɔ loo ŋmãa ni edako jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; their roots spread shallowly near the topsoil. As the fruit bunch grows large and heavy, the top of the plant becomes heavier than the root anchor can support, which is why farmers support them with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ da ni etsii Tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ baafee tsiimɔ tsɔ ni shishifã lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni haa okwaafoi kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do birds attack and destroy my rice field much more than my neighbors' fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi babaoo tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: When farmers in a community plant at different times, birds concentrate on whichever farm matures first or last. Planting your rice at the exact same time as your neighbors spreads bird activity across all fields instead of focusing all the pests onto your single farm.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ du ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ Okpoi kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ ni baakwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ loo sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Oŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ be kome mli kɛ okutsoŋbii lɛ haa okpoi anifeemɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama tsɛŋemɔ helai fɛɛ anɔ yɛ oŋmɔ kome lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Can I feed my spoiled or strange-looking cassava roots to my pigs?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha bo ŋmei shishifãi ni egbo loo ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ? Ani abaanyɛ akɛha tsinai?

english: While pigs can eat crop leftovers, feeding them rotten cassava or raw cassava with green patches can make them sick. It is best to peel, boil, or dry surplus cassava before feeding it to livestock so it is completely safe for them.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsinabii baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ moŋ, Shi kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo loo ŋmei ni egbo ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ha amɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛye hela. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie ŋmei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ahoo loo agbi lɛ dani akɛha kooloi koni amɛná shweshweeshwe kwraa.

english: Is it safe for me to give leftover crop leaves and grains to my chickens?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maha mikooloi lɛ baai kɛ ŋmaa ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, crop leftovers like maize, millet grains, and clean green leaves are great for poultry. However, make sure the crops are free from mold and heavy chemical sprays, which can poison your chickens.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui. Ni baai ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha kooloi. Shi kɛlɛ, kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsina he ajɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that the roots are drowning in too much water. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing small and thin even though the foliage above ground looks huge and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much foliage-boosting nutrient (nitrogen) and not enough root-boosting nutrient (potassium), the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves instead of swelling its roots below ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa baai lɛ yaa hiɛ (nitrogen) babaoo tsɔ, ni niyenii ni haa shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ (potassium) lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo yibii ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when tiny pests damage the blossoms. Providing light shade and steady watering helps the fruit form properly.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii miifite fɔfɔi lɛ, hulutsoo ni mli tse kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes split open in the soil right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes crack when very dry soil suddenly receives heavy rain. The sudden rush of water makes the inner flesh grow faster than the skin can stretch, causing the tuber to split open.
ga: Sweet potatoes baagbala kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa trukaa. Nugbɔ nɛ waa. Nu ni hoɔ trukaa lɛ ha mligbɛ fãji lɛ dara oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ akpã mli. ha yitso lɛ atswa

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die whenever rainwater sits on my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When standing water covers the soil for too long, it suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and the plant to wither.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: What types of crops can I grow on low-lying land that easily gets flooded?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ oya lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops like swamp rice, cocoyam, and sugarcane love wet soil and thrive in flooded or low-lying areas where crops like maize or pepper would rot and die.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, kookoo kɛ ŋmei sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo hei ni ŋmei tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei baanyɛ afite ni amɛgboi yɛ lɛ.

english: If I build a fish pond on my farm, will the water from it help my vegetable crops?
ga: Kɛji mima loo nubu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani nu ni jɛɔ nubu lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi aduawai lɛ?

english: Yes, water from a fish pond is rich in waste from the fish, which acts as a rich liquid fertilizer. Watering your crops with fish pond water helps them grow faster and healthier.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, loo ŋshɔ mli nu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ loo sũ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋshɔ mli nu shwie oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested leafy vegetables wilt and spoil so fast before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ oya dani anyɛɔ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops in the middle of the hot afternoon sun causes them to lose water quickly and spoil. It is best to harvest early in the morning and store the produce in a cool, shady spot to keep it fresh for market buyers.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni efiteɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa nii lɛ leebi maŋkpa ni okɛ onibii lɛ ato he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ koni ehi shi ehee kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil or turn soft so quickly when left out under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ loo efeɔ blɛoo oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Heat from strong sunlight speeds up the natural ripening process inside fruits and vegetables while causing rapid water loss. This makes the produce mature too fast, soften, and rot much quicker than if kept cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ aduawai kɛ aduawai amli lɛ yaa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ oya tsɔ. Ehaa efeɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya fe nɔ ni akɛwoɔ friji mli.

english: Is strong sunshine good for my growing corn crop, or can too much heat harm it?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hi kɛha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ? Aloo ani dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine baanyɛ aye tsei awui?

english: Maize needs sunlight to generate food, but extreme heat without enough water causes stress. High heat makes the plant lose moisture rapidly, causing leaves to curl and reducing grain size.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee niyenii. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: What happens to my maize crop if extreme heat hits the farm while the plants are flowering?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa ba ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Intense sun and high temperatures during flowering dry up the silks and damage pollen. This stops proper pollination, resulting in empty cobs or missing grains.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa siliki lɛ mli gĩɔ ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haa pollination lɛ kpaa jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ efolo loo dumɔwui ni elaaje.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants dry up and turn yellow during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is intense, plants lose water faster than their roots can drink it from dry soil. The plant sheds its lower leaves to conserve water and protect the rest of the crop.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ tsoɔ waa Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I prevent my fresh produce from ripening all at once before market day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi minibii heei ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ shikome dani magbele jara lɛ naa?

english: Harvest your produce early when it just starts to change color, and keep it under shade or in a well-ventilated room to slow down the heat-driven ripening process.
ga: Kpaa onibii lɛ mra. Beni ejeɔ shishi etsakeɔ ehiɛ ni ekɛ amɛ toɔ hulutsoo shishi loo yɛ tsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli koni ekɛha hulutsoo ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsirɛɔ lɛ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do I need to dry my harvested corn in the sun before putting it into bags for storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo kotokui amli koni akɛto lɛ?

english: Sun-drying removes moisture from the grain. Storing wet corn causes mold, rotting, and dangerous toxins like aflatoxin to grow inside the bag.
ga: Hulu ni egbiɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Abele ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. fitemɔ Ni tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ, kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli.

english: How can I make sure I earn a profit on my maize after spending so much money to plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ maná sɛɛnamɔ kɛjɛ ŋmãa mli beni mifite shika babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You must calculate your total costs for land preparation, seeds, and fertilizers, then use proper plant spacing and pest control to increase yield per acre so your sales earnings exceed your total investment.
ga: Esa akɛ obu shika fɛɛ ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he akɔntaa. Dumɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, no sɛɛ lɛ okɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ atsu nii koni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ acre kome mli. Bɔni afee ni shika ni onáa kɛjɛɔ jarayeli mli lɛ afee nɔ ni fe shika fɛɛ ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: Why do buyers pay very low prices for crops that are already fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ momo lɛ jara ni baa shi nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Over-ripe produce spoils rapidly during transport, placing high financial risk on buyers. Because the farmer must sell quickly before total spoilage, buyers hold more power to offer lower prices.
ga: Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ shika he oshara waa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ oya dani amɛ fɛɛ amɛfite. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛ jara ni baa shi baaha.

english: How do I calculate the total amount of money I spend on my farm so I know what price to sell my crops for?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shika fɛɛ ni mifite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he akɔntaa? Bɔni afee ni male shika ni mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Add up every single expense including seeds, land clearing, labor, fertilizers, sprays, and transport. Any selling price above this total represents your real profit, while selling at total cost leaves you with zero profit.
ga: Kɛ shika fɛɛ ni he hiaa, tamɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni ajieɔ, nitsumɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi, kɛ gbɛfaa afata he. Nihɔɔmɔ jara ni fe yibɔ nɛɛ damɔ shi kɛha sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni jarayeli yɛ nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha oná sɛɛnamɔ ko kwraa.

english: What can I do to lower the high costs of buying chemical fertilizers for my farm?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shika babaoo ni akɛheɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: You can combine smaller amounts of chemical fertilizer with organic manure or rotate your crops with legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas, which naturally add nitrogen back into the soil for free.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fioo ko afutu ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa yaka.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from intense heat and keeping the soil moist enough for them to establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is a major food source for crop growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant pulls it out of older lower leaves to feed the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa Kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars attack the inside leaves of my young maize plants during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii tutuaa mi-babi corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm thrive in warm, dry weather and hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant where it is cool, moist, and protected from predators and sprays.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni ekɛ ehe tee baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Eyɛ fɛ̃i, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long, it pushes the air out, causing the roots to drown and encouraging soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛje kpo. ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any tomatoes during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato plants stress, making their pollen dry out. When flowers cannot be pollinated due to high temperatures, the plant drops them to conserve its water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. kɛ pollen lɛ ni egbiɔ Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger yams when I give them tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ sweet potatoi wuji fe tsutsu lɛ beni mihaa amɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni amɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tuber lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni etsĩ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa

english: Why does my mango tree give me a massive harvest one year, but very little fruit the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ewo yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Producing a heavy harvest takes almost all the tree's stored food reserves. The tree often needs the following year to rest, grow new leaves, and rebuild its energy before it can bear a large crop again.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni tsii biɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso lɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei taoɔ be ni amɛkɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli, amɛkwɛ̃ baai heei, ni amɛná hewalɛ hee dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves or grass around my vegetable plants keep them from wilting in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ he lɛ Enɛ tsiɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves acts like a blanket, keeping the hot sun from evaporating moisture from the ground and keeping the plant roots cool.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger in my field than the maize crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmãa tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to steal water, light, and nutrients faster than cultivated crops, which need targeted care and space to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni miida. ni biɔ kwɛmɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛ he ko bɔni afee ni eshwere

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which maize needs to build strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are tiny insects causing the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up and turn dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Those tiny insects are likely aphids or whiteflies. They feed by sucking the juices out of the leaves, which causes the leaves to curl, dry up, and lose energy.
ga: Ekolɛ nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji aphids loo whiteflies. Amɛ yeɔ nii kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛ nuɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my cassava plants while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ehe miihia ni madu mi-cassava tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young cassava plants have small roots and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures the cassava roots grow big and strong.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves scorch and dry up when I clear all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need partial shade, especially when young, because intense direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil faster than their roots can absorb water.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ hulutsoo be fioo. Titri lɛ kɛ́ eji gbekɛbii Enɛ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose water to the dry air faster than the roots can pull water from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from heat and usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu koni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why do my garden egg plants produce plenty of flowers but drop them without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi egbeeɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when there are not enough bees and insects to move pollen around inside the flower. Extreme heat or lack of pollination prevents fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii lɛ kɛbɔle fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ bɛ lɛ, latsaa ni naa wa loo ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ tsiɔ aduawai lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When planted too close, maize plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach the light, spending energy on height instead of growing big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu Abele tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds fail to sprout after planting them in dry soil during the harmattan?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ harmattans ateŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds require moisture to soften their hard outer skin and trigger internal growth. Without enough water in the soil, the seeds remain dormant or dry out before sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu koni eha amɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo ni eha amɛmli dalɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛhiɛ aka shi. loo egbi dani ekwɛ̃

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts show maturity above ground when the leaves turn yellow and dry up. You can also dig up a sample plant; if the inner pod lining has dark brown markings, the crop is ready.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ hu atsu nii. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ emli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why does placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my yam plant burn it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts. When placed right against a tender plant stem, it draws moisture directly out of the plant tissue, causing severe chemical burns.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso ko shishifã ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ masɛi Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ tsofa shãa ni naa wa baa.

english: Why does rice need so much water compared to other crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice naturally thrives in wet conditions. Water acts as a blanket for rice—it helps control weeds, maintains a stable soil temperature, and provides the heavy moisture rice roots need to absorb nutrients and produce healthy grains.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Nu lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ jwɛi lɛ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa ahi shi daa. ni ehaa hulutsoo babaoo haa omɔ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfee omɔ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: My farm land is currently giving me very small yields, so how can I make it produce more crops again?
ga: Miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ekoŋŋ?

english: Low yields happen when the soil loses its food (nutrients) after many harvests. You can rebuild your soil by adding animal manure or compost, rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts, or letting the land rest.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ) fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi babaoo sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ otswa oshikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake ŋmɔshi nibii. aloo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe

english: Why is it important to make sure water fully reaches into the soil before I start planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ koni nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwraa dani aje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Soaking the soil softens the ground so young crop roots can easily spread and drink. It ensures the seeds or seedlings get immediate moisture to sprout quickly without drying out in the sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛnu nu mlɛo. Ehaa dumɔwui loo dumɔwui lɛ naa nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni hulu lɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: How can I make sure rain or irrigation water reaches every part of my rice field evenly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: You can level your land before planting and build low mounds of earth (called bunds) around your plot. This traps water in the field so it spreads across all your crops instead of flowing away.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome dani odu ni ofee gɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ bundle) ni bɔle oshikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni egbɛ eshwa onibii amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeejo foi.

english: If my land is yielding very little right now, which crops are best for me to plant?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ bianɛ Mɛɛ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ?

english: Hardy crops like cassava, cowpeas, or groundnuts grow relatively well in poor soil. Planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts will actually help feed the soil and restore its power for future crops.
ga: Nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to get experienced labor to help me plant my crops properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ maŋɔ nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ koni amɛye amɛbua mi ni madu tsei jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Experienced planters know the correct depth and spacing for seeds. Planting too deep, too shallow, or too close together can prevent seeds from growing well and lower your final harvest.
ga: Abɔɔ mli nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ le dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛ ni sa. Dumɔwui ni ooodu mli tsɔ, ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ, loo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: At what stage of growth does a rice plant need the most water?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli ŋmãa tsei lɛ nu he hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli?

english: Rice needs moisture right at planting to germinate, but it needs the most water when it starts flowering and forming grains. If the soil dries out during flowering, the rice heads will end up empty.
ga: Omɔ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni ekwɛ̃ bɔni afee ni ekwɛ̃. Shi nu he hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ beni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Omɔ yitso lɛ baafee efolo.

english: Can flooding or putting too much water on my land harm crops that are not rice?
ga: Ani nu afua loo nu babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, most crops like maize, peppers, and cassava will rot if their roots sit in standing water for too long because their roots cannot breathe. Only crops like rice are adapted to grow in flooded soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa baafite kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ hi nu ni damɔ shi mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa pɛ ji nɔ ni atsakeɔ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does soil become tired after a few years of farming on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take away nutrients from the earth. If you do not replace those nutrients using organic manure, fertilizers, or soil-enriching plants, the land becomes tired and yields drop.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaagbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo sũ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: What basic steps should I take on low-yielding land to get it ready for planting low-land rice?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nitsumɔi esa akɛ mafee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii faaa nɔ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛsaa mihe kɛha ŋmãa ni baa shi lɛ dumɔ?

english: First, clear the weeds and level the land so water stays flat. Next, flood or thoroughly soak the soil to make it muddy, which makes it easy to plant seedlings and gives them immediate water to start growing.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nu ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo okɛ nu awo mli jogbaŋŋ koni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaha efee mlɛo akɛ adu dumɔwui ni eha amɛ nu ni amɛbɔi dalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: If I spray medicine on the leaves of my crops, how does it reach the rest of the plant to do its job?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Ebaashɛ hei krokomɛi. Te tsei baanyɛ atsu amɛnitsumɔi lɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Certain crop chemicals, called systemic chemicals, enter through the leaf surface and are carried by the plant's natural sap channels to all parts, including other leaves, stems, and roots.
ga: tsofai komɛi ni yɔɔ tsei amli Atsɛɔ lɛ tsofa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. Eboteɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli kɛyaa hei fɛɛ, ni baa, shishifãi, kɛ shishifãi krokomɛi fata he.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical pest medicine on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the afternoon because cooler weather gives the leaves enough time to absorb the chemical before the hot sun dries it up or burns the leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse ji leebi loo shwane mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛjie tsofai lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ agbi loo eshã amɛ.

english: If heavy rain falls right after I spray my crops, do I have to spray them a second time?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ Ani ehe baahia ni mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ shi ni ji enyɔ?

english: If rain falls within 2 hours of spraying, it will usually wash the chemical off the leaves before it is absorbed, meaning you will need to reapply the spray once the plant leaves are dry.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 2 mli yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ Tsofai lɛ hoɔ baai lɛ ahe dani amɛshɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ egbi.

english: Why do I need to make sure chemical spray covers the leaves properly instead of just spraying the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ koni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ aha baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Many crop pests and diseases live directly on leaves, and leaves are designed to quickly absorb specific liquid treatments that protect the plant from the top down.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai babaoo hiɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni afee baai lɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu pɔtɛɛ ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa shishi lɛ oya.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves in dry weather to save water and protect themselves from dying, and they will sprout fresh green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni nu egbi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Leaves curl up in hot weather to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, which helps the plant reduce water loss until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: How do armyworms cause so much damage to my young maize plants in such a short time?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii afite mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛkɛ?

english: Armyworms feed on the tender leaf growth inside the central funnel of the maize plant, destroying the plant's ability to trap light and produce energy for growing corn ears.
ga: Cutworms yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbaamɔ la ni ekɛ hewalɛ baa kɛha ŋmãa toi ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my elders tell me to plant plantains on the farm before putting my young cocoa trees in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu plantain yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight, so fast-growing plantains are planted first to create shade umbrellas that protect the delicate young cocoa leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni daa oya lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekɛfee hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmã duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, providing free, natural fertilizer to neighboring maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer right before a huge rainstorm arrives?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ wulu ko aba?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer off your field into drains and streams before the roots of your crops have time to soak up the nutrients.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛya nu tsɔji kɛ faai amli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛjie niyenii mli nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ready to be harvested so I do not pick it too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ kaabua naa mra tsɔ.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and husks turn brown and dry, and the grains become hard with a visible dark mark where they attach to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni anaa ni akɛkpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my neighbour's cassava tubers so much bigger than mine even though we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmei lɛ da kwraa fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Cassava tubers grow larger when the soil is well-loosened, properly weeded, and rich in nutrients like potassium, whereas compacted soil and weeds stunt tuber growth.
ga: Cassava ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni niyenii tamɔ potassium babaoo yɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ jwɛi tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during wet weather when there is too much shade or poor drainage around the trees.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: What specific signs should I look for when walking through my farm to know if my crops are healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ matao beni mitsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ?

english: Healthy crops have bright, uniform green leaves, strong stems, no visible insect holes or spots, and show active new growth without wilting during normal daylight.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shishifãi ni wa, ni bu loo kooloi ahe ŋmeii ni anaa bɛ mli. ni ejieɔ dalɛ hee kpo kɛ ekãa ni egbooo yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow curling leaves are usually a sign of insect pests like aphids or mites feeding on the plant juice, or a lack of key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ tso nu lɛ he okadi, tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso mli nu. aloo niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by root rot or bacterial wilt, where waterlogged soil or soil-borne diseases destroy the roots so they can no longer drink water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. He ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ aahu kɛyashɛɔ he ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with very few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete for sunlight and nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of spending energy on making fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe koni ekɛ la awo mli moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans or groundnuts alongside their main crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes and improves the growth of nearby crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa, ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures are extremely high, when the plant lacks water, or when there are not enough bees or wind to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my crops produce a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops; removing them ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce heavy yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them directly in an open sunlit field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out their delicate root systems. Planting them under fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize uses to build strong green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help my soil grow better maize in the next planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ ŋmãa be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into tiny nodules on their roots. When the crop leaves and roots decay after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays behind in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛyeɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ beni tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants yield much bigger tubers when I stake the vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs ni dara kwraa kɛji mikɛ wain tso lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows the leaves to spread out and catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to manufacture food for growing big tubers. Leaves left lying on the damp ground get shaded by weeds and are easily destroyed by fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ Baai ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, jwɛi shwieɔ amɛhe oya, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ fiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers spoil and rot inside the soil during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater collects in the field without proper drainage, it suffocates the roots and allows waterlogging fungi to attack and rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni oha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu mli lɛ atutua ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do my leafy vegetable plants droop in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the soil, causing temporary wilting. As temperatures cool down in the evening, the plant regains its balance and stands upright again.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ naa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and becoming small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are a reaction to tiny sap-sucking pests like whiteflies or thrips, which often transmit viruses to the crop. These pests drain the plant's energy and distort leaf development, reducing flower and pepper growth.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hetoo kɛha kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa hela lɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni efiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ ni baa shi.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of essential soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ mulching ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ tomato.

english: Why do my maize plants produce thin stalks and tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight one another for limited sunlight, root space, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to develop thick stalks and large, fully filled cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and stunted even when the weather is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi moŋ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and aggressively steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Removing weeds early removes this competition so your main crop can use all available resources for growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baajie akaŋshii nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ anyɛ ekɛ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my maize crops are getting enough water during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Look at the leaves early in the morning. If they are curled up tight like tubes or turning light green, the maize is thirsty. Healthy maize leaves stay flat and broad to catch sunlight and produce food.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ leebi.. Kɛji ebɔle ehe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ tsɔne loo etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse Etsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye ŋmãa lɛ. Abɛi baa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni elɛɛ koni emɔ hulu la ni ekɛ niyenii aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants start wilting when my watering schedule gets interrupted for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mi-nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ fite gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Tomatoes store very little water in their stems and leaves. When water stops coming, the plant sacrifices its lower leaves and wilts to conserve whatever moisture is left for its main stem and fruits.
ga: Tomato kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ toɔ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ nu lɛ kpa shwiemɔ Tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shaa afɔle ni egboɔ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ enɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Can watering my vegetables too much actually harm their roots?
ga: Ani nu ni oooha o-vegeduries lɛ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛshishifãi lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, plant roots need air in the soil just as much as they need water. If the soil is continuously flooded, the roots drown, rot, and can no longer feed the plant, causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni tsei shishifãi he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagbo, amɛbaagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii dɔŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply water to my crops to help them grow strong?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Early morning is best because the soil is cool, allowing roots to soak up water before the intense sun evaporates it. It also keeps leaves dry overnight, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ nyɔɔŋ kome, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ naa.

english: Pale green leaves usually mean your plants lack nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build green foliage. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field after harvesting a heavy crop like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, making it fertile again for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha efee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do weeds growing around my young crops affect their development?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te midumɔwu lɛ saa ehiɛyaa he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Removing them early allows your main crops to grow faster and establish deep root systems.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛ ni ooojie mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa otso titri lɛ ni edaa oya ni ehaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin roots when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand and leaves need space above to catch sunlight. When planted too close, the crops compete for soil space and light, resulting in smaller tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Ni ehe miihia ni baai lɛ aná he ko yɛ amɛyiteŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, shikpɔŋ kɛ la he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why are the flowers on my garden egg plants dropping off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences sudden stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil fertility. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant retain flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na haomɔi trukaa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look soft and droopy in the afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. They droop temporarily to protect themselves and usually stand back up by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkoto shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi gbɛkɛ

english: How do I know the right time in March to start planting my crops after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa yɛ March mli ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the land receives two or three consecutive heavy rains in March that soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if rain stops for a few weeks.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ March mli ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi.

english: No, planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller yields. Giving plants proper spacing allows each crop to grow strong and yield more harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What is causing tiny holes in the center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ funnel lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars known as Fall Armyworms feeding on the tender leaves inside the plant funnel. Early detection and spraying with recommended biological agents like neem oil or approved insecticides can protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ale amɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ ona nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii, tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ mra ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites that carry plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with soapy water sprays or neem extracts helps keep leaves flat and growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni hiɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem mli nu afɔ nɔ koni eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, which happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding organic manure or agricultural lime helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo okwaayeli mli lime awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young corn usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overly waterlogged soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or organic manure helps restore the green color and supports fast growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why does my farm give me smaller harvests each year when I plant maize in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same plot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen naturally back to the dirt and restores soil health.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ. Ebaaha niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha sũ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my farm with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade jie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing the land exposes bare soil to direct sunlight, triggering dormant weed seeds buried in the ground to sprout. Planting cover crops like mucuna or mulching with dry leaves shades the ground and suppresses weed growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni bɛ nitsumɔ baa. Kɛ́ afu lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, edaa. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ mucilage loo mulching ni akɛ baai ni egboi woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my small cocoa seedlings die when planted in a wide open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Minɔ lɛ gbeɔ mɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli kwɔ ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, such as plantains or shade trees, planted nearby to protect them during their first few years in the field.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Adu nakai nɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛye yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools in the soil and cannot drain away during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to run off and keeps the tubers healthy underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I put fresh pig manure directly onto my crops to help them grow, or will it hurt them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara? Aloo ebaaye amɛ awui?

english: Fresh pig manure produces intense heat and contains strong chemicals as it breaks down, which can burn plant roots. You should heap the manure and let it dry or compost for a few weeks until it cools down before placing it near your crops.
ga: Kplotoo ŋmɔshi nibii heei kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ tsofai ni mli wa baa be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato ni oha egbi loo afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi ebaajɔ dani okɛma oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas make my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant finishes growing and dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli beni tso lɛ daa ni egboɔ lɛ. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing good yield when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plant stretches upward quickly to reach sunlight, spending all its energy on growing tall instead of forming large roots or fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni eeefee shishifãi wuji loo aduawai.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted next to them when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Beni ajeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leafy shade that shelters the young cocoa trees and keeps the surrounding soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo baa agboi ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves turn yellow when root soil stays completely waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing, or when the plant lacks vital nutrients like nitrogen. Improving field drainage helps oxygen return to the roots so leaves stay green.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lolo, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu. Aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli

english: Why are there tiny holes appearing on my young maize leaves as soon as they shoot up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo kɛji ekwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Small holes on fresh maize leaves are usually caused by tiny caterpillar pests, like fall armyworms, feeding inside the center leaves. Catching them early and applying approved pest treatments or natural repellents protects the crop from heavy leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ fall worms ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai heei amli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ baai ni fiteɔ nii waa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does putting dried leaves around the base of my plantain trees help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi fata mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks harsh sunlight from reaching the dirt, preventing water from evaporating quickly and keeping the plant's roots cool and moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekashɛ muji lɛ he. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering. When the plant feels it doesn't have enough water to sustain fruit, it sheds flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni amɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ bɛ Ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific nutrients that maize relies on, leaving the soil exhausted. It also gives pests and diseases that feed on maize a permanent place to live and multiply in the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that have adapted to local soils over generations, allowing them to absorb rainwater and nutrients instantly. Domestic crops take longer to build strong roots and establish themselves compared to wild weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shia tsei lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe shi kɛ akɛto jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important for me to clear a good road or path leading directly to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ tsɔne kpakpa he hiaa mi lɛ? Aloo gbɛ ni yaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Having a clear access road makes it easy to bring in farm inputs like seeds and fertilizer, and allows vehicles to reach your farm so you can safely move harvested crops to the market before they spoil.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ kɛyaa jɛmɛ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baa. ni ehaa tsɔnei baanyɛ abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ okpamɔ lɛ aya jara nɔ shweshweeshwe dani efite.

english: I have a large piece of land, but should I clear and plant everything all at once or start bit by bit?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ agbo ko. Shi ani esa akɛ mafo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli ni madu shikome loo mabɔi bibioo?

english: Starting bit by bit allows you to manage your limited money and labor effectively without getting overwhelmed. As you gain experience and earn money from the smaller plot, you can gradually expand to cover the rest of the land.
ga: Kɛ́ oje shishi bibioo lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ oshika kɛ nitsumɔ fioo ni oyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni onuuu he akɛ ogbɔjɔ. Beni onáa niiashikpamɔ ni onine shɛɔ shika nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔji bibii anɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli fiofio ni okɛtsu he ni eshwɛ lɛ he nii.

english: Why should I plant my crops in neat, organized rows instead of just scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, properly spaced rows ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to grow strong. It also makes weeding, spraying, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo.

english: How can visiting demo farms or learning from other successful farmers help my crop production?
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ ko saramɔ loo nikasemɔ kɛjɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ adɛŋ Te ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Visiting successful farms allows you to visually see proven practices—like correct plant spacing and proper water management—so you can copy what works and avoid costly mistakes on your own land.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ saramɔ haa ona nifeemɔi ni ana he odaseyeli tamɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja kɛ nu he nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okase nɔ ni tsuɔ nii lɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ni jara wa he yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Farming takes so much physical labor; how can I make my daily field work easier and more manageable?
ga: Okwaayeli biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ babaoo. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi daa gbi shiɛmɔ nitsumɔ lɛ afee mlɛo ni manyɛ matsu he nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Breaking your farm into smaller manageable sections, using simple line-and-peg planting techniques, and keeping weeds down early prevents farm work from becoming overwhelming.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mlijaa yɛ hei bibii ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ Okɛ dumɔwui ahe ŋaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ line kɛ pin tsuɔ nii. kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ naa koni ekafee nɔ ni tsii fe nine.

english: How will building a small water dam on my land help my crops during the dry season?
ga: faa bibioo ko maa Te mishikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A farm dam stores excess rainwater during the wet season so you can irrigate your crops when the rains stop, allowing your plants to survive and letting you farm all year round.
ga: Okwaafoi atoohe lɛ toɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo onibii amli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi ni ehaa otsuɔ okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I choose the best spot on my farm to build a water storage dam?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni matswa faa?

english: A dam should be built at the lowest part of your land where rainwater naturally flows and gathers, and in soil that contains enough clay to hold the water without leaking.
ga: Esa akɛ ama faa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ he ni nugbɔ nu hoɔ ni ebua ehe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni shwieee shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How does inconsistent watering affect the behavior and growth of my crops?
ga: Te nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ amɛdalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Too little water makes crops wilt, stunt, and yield small fruits, while too much standing water drowns crop roots and causes root rot. Controlled watering keeps the plants healthy and productive.
ga: Nu fioo ko pɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo, ni ebaaha amɛgboi. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it helpful to consult an expert or extension officer before laying out my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mabi mɔ ko ni le nii jogbaŋŋ loo mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ ama shi lɛ?

english: Agricultural experts can assess your land, soil, and water supply to show you the best layout for your crops and structures, saving you money and preventing future failures.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi baanyɛ akwɛ oshikpɔŋ, shikpɔŋ, kɛ nu ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli koni amɛjie gbɛjianɔtoo ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ bɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha lɛ kpo. Ekɛ shika toɔ ohe ni etsĩɔ wɔsɛɛ be mli shigbeemɔi anaa.

english: What basic steps do I need to follow to make my farm project successful and profitable?
