ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni miŋmɔ nitsumɔ lɛ aye omanye ni maná sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Success requires proper site selection, starting with a manageable farm size, setting up a reliable water source for irrigation, planting in clear rows, and planning how to transport your produce to buyers.
ga: Omanyeyeli biɔ ni ahala he ni sa. Kɛjɛ ŋmɔ dalɛ ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛha nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo Dumɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni mli tse kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ooofee okɛ onibii lɛ aya mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ aŋɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help bring the dark green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. Curling or drooping is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss, and they usually stand back up when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Curling loo drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very good for your soil. Cowpea roots take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, which naturally feeds your maize crop and saves you money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Cowpea shishifãi lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii ni ehaa onáa shika yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, will I get more cassava tubers at harvest?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Beni akpa lɛ, ani ŋmei shishifãi babaoo baaba?

english: No, planting cassava too close together makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and produce large, heavy tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni efeɔ bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: What makes tiny green insects gather under the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ Bua naa yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishi

english: Those tiny insects are usually aphids, which hide under leaves to suck the sweet juices out of your pepper plants. You can control them by spraying a simple mixture of soapy water or diluted neem oil directly onto the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ ni oookɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are fall armyworm caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall caterpillars miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay their eggs in the soft, tender inner leaves of young maize because it provides easy food and shelter. Clearing weeds around your field early helps prevent the adult moths from nesting on your farm.
ga: Caterpillar ŋmei lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ amli, he ni ewaaa akɛ aaana niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe yɛ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ajiemɔ Omɔ ŋmɔji kɛjɛ shishijee Ye obua ni ŋmeii akafee amɛ ŋmeii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my okra plants without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ gumbo tsei anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off when the plant is stressed by dry weather, intense heat, or a lack of water. It can also happen if there are not enough bees around to pollinate the flowers so they can turn into okra pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ bɛ bɔni afee ni amɛfee roselle ŋmeii.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Check the main plant leaves; when they start turning yellow and dry up, pull up one plant to test. If the inside of the pod shell has dark veins and the seeds are firm and full, your groundnuts are ready for harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ baai titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ ebɔi ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ Gbalamɔ tso kome ni oka lɛ okwɛ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ fãji ni tsuɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I planted fail to come out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the soil, if insects or ants eat them underground, or if the soil is too dry for the seed to absorb enough water to open up.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kplukai loo ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbele.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong heat, just like young babies. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains planted next to them to act as living umbrellas during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Tamɔ gbekɛ bibioo pɛpɛɛpɛ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Why is my maize crop suddenly yielding poorly even though it grew very well in previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous cropping on the same land drains essential soil nutrients like nitrogen over time. Without proper crop rotation or balanced soil restoration, soil health degrades, causing yields to drop even if farming practices remain unchanged.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji akɛ atsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ loo atsakeee shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ baafite. Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ eba shi eyɛ mli akɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi lɛ tsakeee moŋ.

english: Why are my crops not growing well even after I applied fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔji lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer requires adequate soil moisture to dissolve and reach plant roots. If applied during dry spells, or if the wrong type or amount of fertilizer is used for the specific crop and soil conditions, plants cannot absorb the nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli ni eshɛ tso shishifãi ahe. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii kɛha tso kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil needs a different type of fertilizer to support my corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni baaye abua mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves, stunted growth, or poor cob development often indicate nutrient deficiencies. Testing the soil or consulting an extension officer helps identify which missing nutrients need to be supplied by specific fertilizers.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo cob ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ Bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo sanegbaa ni akɛ extension nitsulɔ ko baasusu he lɛ baaye abua ni ana niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje ni esa akɛ ana kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko mli.

english: What causes healthy crops to suddenly lose vigor and give low yields near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi trukaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo beni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Late-season nutrient exhaustion, lack of water during grain filling, or improper fertilizer application timing can cause plants to fail right when they need energy to produce grains.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee Nu ni bɛ yɛ be mli ni awoɔ ŋmaa mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How does a combine harvester work to harvest maize and rice fields?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni ekɛkpa ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji?

english: A combine harvester performs three main operations at once: cutting the standing crop, threshing to separate the grain from the stalks or husks, and cleaning the seed, which saves labor and time on large fields.
ga: Nibii ni akɛkpaa nii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsuɔ nitsumɔi titrii etɛ yɛ be kome mli: ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi lɛ afolɔ; Massage koni akɛgbala dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ amli. kɛ dumɔwui ahe saamɔ ni haa nitsumɔ kɛ be baa shi yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli.

english: Can I use specialized machinery to harvest my bean farm in Northern Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi akpa mi-bean ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana Kooyigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, specialized mechanical bean harvesters or crop-specific tractor attachments exist that cut, pull, or thresh beans, reducing the high labor required for manual pod picking.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni akɛkpaa ŋmeii loo trakta ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe ni baanyɛ afo, agbala, loo atswa ŋmeii. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛ niji ajie ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is machine harvesting common for corn and rice but less common for beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ? Shi efɔɔɔ kaa kɛha ŋmeii.

english: Corn and rice grow tall with grains at a consistent height, making them easy for combine harvesters to process. Bean plants grow low to the ground with delicate pods that require specialized cutter bars to avoid loss.
ga: Abɛi kɛ omɔ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ ŋmaa lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa mɛi ni kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ tsuɔ nii. Bean tsei lɛ daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ atsu nii koni amɛkafite.

english: Where can a local farmer go to ask about hiring farm harvesting machinery in Tamale?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi baanyɛ aya ni amɛyabi saji yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ ni amɛbaahe yɛ Tamale lɛ he?

english: Farmers can visit the local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) district offices or agricultural mechanization service centers to inquire about tractor and harvester availability.
ga: Okwaafoi baanyɛ aya amɛ maŋ lɛ mli Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe loo okwaayeli tsɔnei anitsumɔhe lɛ koni amɛyabi trakta kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ ahe saji.

english: Why do bean plants mature and behave differently than cereal crops like corn and rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei daa ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that fix their own nitrogen in the soil and produce seeds in pods, whereas cereal crops like corn and rice are heavy nutrient consumers that store grain in tassels or panicles.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa dumɔwui ŋmeii baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni kɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ toɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa mli lɛ waa.

english: What steps should I take if my current crop yield keeps dropping every farming season?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ baa shi daa afi?

english: You should seek advice from an extension officer to evaluate soil nutrient levels, check if your fertilizer type matches your soil needs, and consider rotating crops or improving soil organic matter.
ga: Esa akɛ otao ŋaa kɛjɛ o-extension officer lɛ dɛŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ ha. Kwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he hiamɔ nii kpãa gbee. ni osusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: How can I check if my cassava tubers are growing big underground without killing the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni migbeee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can carefully scoop away a small amount of soil around the base of one plant to inspect tuber size, then gently cover the roots back up. This gives you a quick check on growth progress without disturbing or destroying the entire crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shɔvel abɔle muji fioo ko he. Tso kome ni akɛkwɛɔ bɔ ni bulb lɛ da ha, no sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ blɛoo aha shishifãi lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lɛ oya ni okɛgbalaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ loo okpaaa amɛhiɛ.

english: Why does an extension officer take small handfuls of soil from different parts of my field instead of taking from just one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ shwieɔ sũ ni eyi obɔ kɛ niji kɛjɛɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ? mi ŋmɔji lɛ amli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafolɔ kɛjɛ he kome

english: Soil quality and nutrients change from one corner of your farm to another. Taking tiny samples from multiple spots gives an accurate overall picture of your farm's soil health without disturbing your entire field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli he kome kɛyaa he kroko. Kɛ́ oŋɔ nibii bibii kɛjɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ, ebaaha ona shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he mfoniri ni ja. ni ogbalaaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on my crops, and what signs should I look for?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mɛɛ okadi esa akɛ matao?

english: It is best to walk through your field every few days to inspect leaf color and stem health. Observing your crops regularly helps you catch early signs of pests or poor growth before the problem spreads.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli. gbii fioo komɛi koni akɛkwɛ baa lɛ su kɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo amɛdaramɔ ehiii mra dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow after I weed heavily around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeding too deep or too close to the stem damages shallow feeding roots near the surface. Disturbing these roots stops the plant from taking up water and fertilizer properly, causing stress and leaf yellowing.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala shishifãi nɛɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akaŋɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my pepper blossoms fall off whenever I cut weeds roughly around the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Aaafee tso ko?

english: Pepper plants are sensitive during their flowering stage. Heavy shaking or rough physical disturbance shocks the plant, causing it to drop its flowers before they can mature into pepper pods.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kpokpomɔ ni naa wa loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ haomɔ ni naa wa haa tso lɛ he feɔ shoo. Ha amɛgbee shi dani amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ pepper pods.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt immediately after I move them from the nursery bed into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants causes root shock because fine root hairs get torn during digging. Moving them late in the afternoon reduces heat stress and allows the roots time to settle undisturbed overnight.
ga: Tso lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi bibii lɛ fãa yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my young cocoa trees are developing properly in their early months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli?

english: Healthy young cocoa trees regularly shoot out soft, light-green or reddish new leaves at the top. If the main stem thickens and fresh shoots appear every few weeks, your plant is building a strong root system.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ baai bibii, ni ji eŋɔli loo tsuru yɛ amɛyiteŋ daa. Kɛji tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli tsɔ ni ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo daa otsii enyɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ miitswa shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why should I pull out some healthy-looking seedlings if I planted too many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When too many plants grow closely together, they fight for soil nutrients, light, and water, leaving all of them weak. Removing a few extra plants gives the remaining ones room to grow big and produce better yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei babaoo tsɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, la kɛ nu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ, ni no haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ekomɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it better to pick all my tomato fruits at once or harvest them little by little as they turn red?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makpã mi-tomato lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo makpã fiofio beni efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Picking ripe tomatoes bit by bit encourages the plant to keep flowering and growing fresh fruit, giving you a longer harvest season without stressing the plant all at once.
ga: Tomato ni ekwɛ̃ ni oookpa fioo fioo lɛ baawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo aduawai heei. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaakpamɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni okɛ haomɔ haaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up if I clear away all the bigger trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because harsh, direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out soil moisture. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains protects the tender young trees while they establish roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛdara lɛ Shading loo plantains ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leafy foliage that acts as a living shade umbrella, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛha wala. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Maize heavily consumes specific soil nutrients every season. Planting it continuously drains those nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Alternating with legumes like beans or peanuts restores vital soil nutrients.
ga: Abɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi tsuɔ nii daa be. Tsei ni miida lɛ shwieɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ amli be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When rainwater sits stagnant in heavy clay soil without draining, root tissues cannot breathe, causing oxygen starvation and root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ faaa, ni shishifãi lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Why do my yams grow out short and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ kuku ni etsɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and bend when they encounter hard, compacted soil or buried stones beneath the surface. Creating deep, loose earth mounds allows the tuber room to expand downward freely.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛbaabɔle amɛhe kɛji amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ loo tɛi ni afu yɛ nu lɛ shishi lɛ kpe. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa yitso tsu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ yɛ heyeli mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, overly damp conditions. Pruning excess branches allows sunlight and airflow to dry out the canopy and prevent fungus growth.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be fe nine yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akadara.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes in the leaves and center whorl of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ni maye bu bibioo ko Yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets young green leaves. Inspecting the field early and applying targeted sprays before heavy damage occurs protects the crop canopy.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. Gbɛjianɔtoo mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii dani nɔ ni fiteɔ nii waa lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips transmitting a plant virus. Controlling insect populations early keeps the foliage healthy and broad.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kplukai ayibɔ ni akudɔɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛlɛɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize draws stored nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves, signaling that nitrogen fertilizer or compost is needed.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without producing any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme daytime heat stresses tomato plants, causing flowers to drop off to conserve energy rather than setting fruit. Ensuring adequate watering during cool morning hours helps reduce heat stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi mli lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha gbɔmɔtso lɛ yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: Why is my cowpea crop producing lots of big leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai wuji waa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpeas to grow thick foliage instead of flowers. Since cowpeas make their own nitrogen naturally, extra nitrogen fertilizer should be avoided.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ cowpea hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃ baai ni mli tse yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmei feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn and the soil dries out too fast; keeping larger shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young plants while they establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my farm before planting maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which enriches the land naturally and helps the next crop of maize grow stronger without relying heavily on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ tsɔ.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to save water and protect its roots underground, but extreme leaf drop can be reduced by keeping dry grass or crop leaves around the base to retain soil moisture.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shi abaanyɛ aba baai ni laajeɔ waa lɛ shi kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ nɔ. cones koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi

english: Why do my plantain plants take much longer to produce fruit when rain is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that need a steady water supply to grow big stems and heavy bunches; spreading mulched leaves or grass around the trunk holds water in the topsoil and speeds up stem development.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni biɔ nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei wuji kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse. Baa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbɛɔ ashwãa tso lɛ he lɛ haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why does my maize crop produce small, thin cobs when I plant late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ, ŋmãa woɔ toi bibii lɛ?

english: Maize needs plenty of soil moisture while forming its ears; planting late causes the crop to flower when rains are ending, leaving the plant without enough water to fill out the seeds completely.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni edaa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awo fɔfɔi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Enɛ haaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli kwraa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of yellow flowers but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers dry up and fall off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no insects or wind to help pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni baaye abua ni ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites on the undersides of leaves, which can be controlled early by spraying local neem leaf extracts or soapy water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. ni abaanyɛ akudɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo nu ni akɛ samla eshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together in the same field without them destroying each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛfiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, because maize grows rapidly and is harvested in three to four months, while cassava grows slowly in the beginning and takes over the space only after the maize has been harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, shishijee lɛ daa blɛoo, ni kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly when I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot easily if they get bruised during digging or if stored in warm, unventilated spaces; keeping tubers tied on raised, shaded racks allows air to flow around them and prevents decay.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ bulb lɛ to shɛlɛf ni nɔ kwɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ abɔle amɛhe. ni atsĩ fitemɔ naa

english: Why should I buy certified maize seeds instead of using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Saved hybrid seeds lose their strength in the second generation, leading to smaller yields and irregular growth, whereas certified seeds are specifically treated and bred for high yields and disease resistance.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe nii pɔtɛɛ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over during strong winds even when they have heavy, healthy cobs on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ miyɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni mli wa moŋ?

english: Heavy cobs make the top of the plant very heavy. When strong winds blow, this top weight acts like a lever, pulling on the stem and roots. If the roots are shallow or the stem is thin, the wind easily pushes the whole heavy plant over.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmei ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ tsii waa. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa Nɛkɛ muji ni fe fɛɛ nɛɛ baatsu nii tamɔ lever ni akɛgbalaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo eshishifãi lɛ mli etse Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ oya.

english: How can I prevent strong winds from knocking down my plantain trees when they start bearing heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa mi-plantain tsei lɛ amɛshwie shi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ aduawai wuji lɛ?

english: You can support heavy plantain trees by 'propping' them with bamboo or strong wooden poles pressed against the stem under the fruit bunch. Planting windbreak trees around your farm boundary and mounding soil around the base of the plantain also gives roots a firmer grip.
ga: Obaanyɛ oye obua plantain agbo kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo tso ni wa ni akɛmiimi tso lɛ shishi yɛ aduawai akui lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ ‘okɛfi’ amɛ sɛɛ. Tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni aduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husui kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ Plantain shishitoo lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops with heavy yields sometimes get uprooted more easily after a rainstorm than crops with small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ fe tsei ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Rain softens the soil, making root anchorage weaker. At the same time, heavy yields add extra weight to the top of the plant. When wind hits a heavy, top-heavy crop in wet soil, the soft ground cannot hold the roots down.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. ehaa shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi yɛ be kome too mli Nibii ni afee lɛ babaoo baaha tso lɛ yiteŋ afee muji. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii, ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Should I cut the tops of my tall cassava or maize plants to keep them from falling over in the wind?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ayiteŋ koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli?

english: No, cutting the leaves or tops damages the plant's ability to make food from sunlight, which will reduce your harvest. Instead, mound soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) or choose shorter seed varieties that resist wind naturally.
ga: Dabi, baai loo ŋmeii ni afoɔ lɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Okɛ shikpɔŋ abɔle tso lɛ shishi (kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afata he) loo halamɔ dumɔwui kukuji ni teɔ shi woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do some crop varieties grow very tall while other types stay short on the exact same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi bɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Plant height is mainly controlled by the crop's genetics, just like human height. Tall varieties are bred to reach up for sunlight, while dwarf or short varieties are bred to direct their energy into thick stems and early fruit production.
ga: Tso lɛ mli wala yibii ji nɔ ni kudɔɔ tso lɛ nɔyaa. Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ adesa kwɔlɛ he. Afɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ koni amɛshɛ hulu la he. yɛ be mli ni afɔɔ dwarf loo kukuji srɔtoi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tsei ni mli tse kɛ yibii ni woɔ oya.

english: Why do tall crop varieties get damaged by wind more easily than shorter crop varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Tall plants catch much more wind force high up in the air, creating a stronger pull on their base. Shorter plants stay closer to the ground where wind speed is lower, making them much harder for the wind to bend or snap.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kwraa. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni gbalaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli waa. Tsei ni yɔɔ kukuji lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ oyaiyeli lɛ baa shi yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa kɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akɛ ebaaku loo ebaakumɔ.

english: Is it better for me to plant short crop varieties rather than tall ones if my farm experiences a lot of strong wind?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kakadaji najiaŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, short or dwarf varieties are usually better for windy areas because their lower center of gravity keeps them upright. They spend less energy growing tall stems and more energy developing sturdy roots and heavy yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, henɔi kukuji loo bibii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa yɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishigbɛ nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jaŋŋ. Akɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ. kɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni baaha shishifãi ni wa aba ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How do crop breeders create seeds that grow into short plants while still producing plenty of heavy food?
ga: Te mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee tɛŋŋ amɛfee dumɔwui ni baatsɔ tsei kukuji shi amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo lolo lɛ?

english: Breeders carefully select and cross-pollinate parent plants that naturally have thick stems, deep roots, and heavy yields over many generations. This creates seed varieties that use their food energy to grow big cobs or fruits instead of tall stems.
ga: Yɛ yinɔi babaoo ni eho lɛ amli lɛ, mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ehala tsei ni ji nyɛ ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe ewo mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui srɔtoi ni kɛ niyenii hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji loo aduawai yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ baa.

english: What kind of plant food or fertilizer helps my crops build strong stems that won't snap under heavy yield?
ga: Mɛɛ tso niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni efoŋ kɛji amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Potassium (found in NPK fertilizers) is essential for building strong, sturdy stems and thick cell walls in crops. Combining potassium with good plant spacing ensures stems grow thick and tough rather than thin and weak.
ga: Potassium (ni anaa yɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii amli) lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ amamɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee mɔ ni he waaa ni egbɔjɔ

english: Why do seeds I save from a tall crop plant sometimes grow into plants of different heights next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ amli lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ srɔtoi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds often carry mixed genetic traits from bees or wind cross-pollinating different plants in your field. If the parent plant was a hybrid, its seeds naturally separate into tall, medium, and short plants in the next generation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yɛ wala yibii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni haa tsei srɔtoi feɔ ŋmeii. yɛ oŋmɔji amli Kɛji tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ ji tso ni akɛfee ekome Edumɔwui lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛfeɔ tsei kakadaji, teŋgbɛ kɛ kukuji yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and small root systems that cannot drink water fast enough to survive intense sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees protects the young cocoa from burning until their roots are deep enough to handle direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ, ebaabu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from older lower leaves to feed the tender new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy and breathe. When land stays flooded with water for too long, oxygen gets cut off, creating the perfect conditions for soil fungi to attack and rot the cassava tubers underground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛmu. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, afoɔ Oxygen lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or dead leaves—a practice called mulching—acts as a protective blanket. It stops the hot sun from evaporating water directly out of the ground, keeping the soil moist and roots cool for much longer.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbo Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do protective chemical sprays keep black pod disease from destroying my cocoa pods?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ black pod hela lɛ naa koni ekafite mi-cocoa pods lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Black pod is caused by tiny fungal spores that travel through rain drops and enter the pod skin. Protective sprays create a invisible shield on the outer layer of the pod, killing the spores on contact before they can penetrate inside and spoil the beans.
ga: Fungal spores bibii kɛ pods diji baa. ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ amli kɛboteɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hewolo lɛ mli Nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni anaaa ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ dani amɛboteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ.

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Nearby crops like maize feed on this natural nitrogen to grow stronger and produce better grain.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa yeɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce small yields even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your main crops. If weeds are left unchecked, your crops end up starving because the weeds consume most of the plant food you apply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni okwɛɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ jwɛi lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye Oŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ jwɛi yeɔ tsei niyenii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ babaoo.

english: Why do caterpillars hide deep inside the leaf funnels of my young maize plants during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-abɛi tsei bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day to protect their soft bodies from hot sunlight and predators like birds, while secretly chewing on the tender young leaves inside.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Koni amɛbu amɛgbɔmɔtsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ teemɔŋ

english: Why should I prune off extra branches and chupons from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ niji krokomɛi ni jɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extra branches and chupons suck water and food away from the tree without producing many pods. Removing them forces the tree to direct its energy into healthy pod growth, while allowing sunlight and air to flow through, which lowers disease risk.
ga: Niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmeii babaoo. Amɛjiemɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai aba shi.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo yibii ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience severe heat stress, uneven watering, or excess chemical nitrogen. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself until growing conditions become cooler and more stable.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni naa wa he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo tsofa ni ji nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli baajɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen or moisture. When the soil gets too dry, plants cannot absorb nutrients properly, so they pull stored food from older leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ otso lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjieɔ niyenii ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon heat even after I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes leaves to lose water faster than the roots can draw it up from the ground. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself and conserve moisture.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dried grass help them grow better?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ jwɛi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass or leaves keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, stops weeds, and adds nutrients back into the soil as it decays.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya, ehaa jwɛi lɛ kpaa, ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward for light instead of growing strong roots and big fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ la lɛ, ni no najiaŋ lɛ, amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why did my seeds fail to sprout after I buried them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need air and warmth near the surface to sprout. If buried too deep, the seed runs out of stored energy before the seedling can push through the dirt to reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Hewalɛ ni dumɔwu lɛ eto lɛ baa shi dani dumɔwu lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛje kpo kɛya hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Why should I pinch off some of the side branches growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Removing extra branches focuses the plant's energy on producing larger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting strength on excess leaves and stems.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaafite hewalɛ kɛjɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why is it helpful to plant beans or cowpeas in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but leguminous crops like beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, restoring fertility.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni ekɛ fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aba

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small dirt-like specks in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli buji ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ muji bibii ni tamɔ muji yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pest caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which chew on tender central leaves and leave behind waste as they feed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi yɛ amɛsɛɛ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai adalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is ready to be dug up from under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants usually signal maturity when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off naturally, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida beni amɛshishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Is it good to use water from my fish pond to irrigate my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ loo nubu mli lɛ baafɔ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu?

english: Yes, fish pond water is full of natural nutrients from fish waste and decaying feed. It acts like a natural liquid fertilizer, providing nitrogen that helps crops like vegetables grow green and strong.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋshɔ mli nu lɛ eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ loo mli nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ niyenii ni fiteɔ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Ehaa nitrogen ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ aduawai ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does rainwater make my maize grow faster than water I fetch from a borehole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu haa ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nubui amli lɛ?

english: Rainwater picks up free nitrogen from the air as it falls, which plants absorb immediately for quick growth. Borehole water often lacks this natural nitrogen and can contain minerals that slow down nutrient absorption.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli beni egbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni tsei lɛ baaŋɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛdara oya. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ nubu mli lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen, ni ekolɛ mineral ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ yɛ mli.

english: Can dirty river water harm my crops if I use it for watering my fields?
ga: Ani faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛtsu nii kɛshwie miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ nu?

english: It depends on what is in the river water. While eroded topsoil and organic matter in river water can nourish crops, water polluted with agricultural chemicals, sewage, or excess salt can damage roots and slow down crop growth.
ga: Edamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ faa mli nu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aná hewalɛ moŋ, shi nu ni akɛ okwaayeli mli tsofai, nu ni fiteɔ nii, loo ŋoo ni fa fe nine ewo mli lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why does water sit on top of my field for days after rain instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: This happens when soil has heavy clay content or has become packed hard by farm activities. Adding organic compost or dried manure creates tiny spaces in the soil so water can drain properly down to plant roots.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni tsii loo ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ, ehaa he ko bibioo baa. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛdu shishifãi

english: Why are the roots of my pepper plants rotting even though the top soil feels dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛmiifite moŋ lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi?

english: Water often gets trapped beneath the surface layer due to poor subsoil drainage. When roots sit in trapped, stagnant water without air, fungus grows and causes root rot even if the top soil looks dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ taraa nu ni ekã shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Fuji lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaafite shishifãi lɛ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi po.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl and droop their leaves to protect themselves from severe heat. Shrinking the leaf area exposed to the sun reduces water loss through evaporation so the crop stays hydrated until evening.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. He ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with lush green leaves but producing no flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi fɔfɔii bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: The soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, which tells the plant to keep building stems and leaves instead of fruit. Plants need phosphorus and potassium in the soil to form healthy flowers and tomatoes.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ kɛɔ tso lɛ akɛ ewo tsei kɛ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves show that your soil is low on nitrogen. The plant copes by taking whatever nitrogen it has from its old bottom leaves and sending it to the new top growth to stay alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei nyɛɔ amɛkpeɔ naa kɛtsɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛmajeɔ ŋmeii heei amli koni amɛhi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry out so fast during the Harmattan season even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ Harmattan be lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa leebi moŋ?

english: The dry, windy Harmattan air rapidly sucks moisture directly from leaves and soil surface. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the moisture trapped in the soil longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ oya. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) baadu lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so quickly along the stream near my farm compared to the crops in my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ faa ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Stream banks constantly collect washed-away soil, organic waste, and dissolved plant nutrients carried by flowing water. This nutrient-dense moisture supply allows weeds to thrive naturally without added fertilizer.
ga: Banks buaa sũ ni afɔ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni nu kɛbaa be fɛɛ be lɛ anaa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli nɛɛ haa jwɛi lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade, protecting delicate cocoa plants from drying out during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Ebuɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds along the cassava stem—they should always point upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the plant to grow poorly and reduces the harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ ŋmei lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plants stay green and grow healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people cover the soil around young crop plants with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weed growth.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ naa

english: Why are ragged holes appearing in the young leaves at the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the growing point of maize. Inspecting fields early and applying appropriate treatments protects the crop before major damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why should I avoid growing maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ŋmãa dumɔ he afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with crops like cowpeas restores soil nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tso pɔtɛɛ ko he tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that grows large tubers underground. Staking holds leaves off the damp ground where they catch light better and stay safe from rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɛɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni enaa la ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ, ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe koni ekafite.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off pepper plants when the weather is extremely hot or when the plants do not get consistent water. Keeping soil evenly moist helps flowers turn into full peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛjɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings droop and die after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings experience transplant shock when moved into hot sun. Transplanting during cool late afternoons and watering immediately gives roots time to recover without losing water.
ga: Dumɔwui naa shoofeemɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli ni awo lɛ nu lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe ni nu lɛ sɛɛ efooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do insects destroy my dried maize inside storage bags after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni yɔɔ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils multiply quickly if maize is stored while still holding moisture. Maize kernels must be thoroughly dried until hard before storage to prevent insect attacks.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii babaoo baa oya kɛji akɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ kɛyashi amɛhe wa dani akɛto koni kooloi akatutua amɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants make the soil better for my maize in the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bean plants have tiny bumps on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the bean crop is done, that nitrogen stays in the ground to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Bean tso lɛ yɛ bɔɔt bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji ogbe ŋmeii adumɔ naa Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha otso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I put fresh chicken droppings directly from the coop onto my young crop plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee ni jɛ tsina ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ awo midumɔwui lɛ anɔ?

english: Fresh chicken droppings are too strong and hot because of raw nitrogen, which can burn young plant roots. You should let the droppings dry out or rot with dried grass for a few weeks before applying them to your farm.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ yɛ nitrogen ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ hewɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã tso shishifãi bibii Esa akɛ oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi loo egbo kɛ jwɛi otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and roll inward during the dry January weather in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ mli yɛ January be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: During the dry Harmattan season in January, hot dry air pulls water out of leaves very quickly. Plants roll their leaves inward to protect their tiny water pores and conserve humidity inside the leaf.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ January mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni amɛkɛbu nu bu bibii ahe. ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi baai lɛ amli

english: Why do my bean plants shed their flowers before turning into bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Bean plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or a lack of water during flowering. The plant drops flowers as a survival mechanism to keep itself alive when stressed.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ amɛmiihao.

english: Why are the leaves on my bean crop turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant roots are sitting in excess water and cannot breathe, or pests are damaging the roots underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu babaoo ebote tsei shishifãi amli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai miifite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do small insects bore tiny holes into my harvested beans while they are in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu bibii yɛ kɔfi ni mikpaa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ he ko lɛ?

english: Those insects are bean weevils whose eggs are often laid on the pods while still in the field. Once stored, the eggs hatch inside the dried beans and the young insects eat their way out.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji bean weevils, ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ akɛto lɛ Akpɔlɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli. ni kooloi bibii baaye gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds immediately after the very first light rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first light rain is often followed by a long dry period. Seeds planted too early will sprout, but the hot dry sun that follows will kill the delicate young roots before the main rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi hulu ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. If you don't clear them early, your crops starve and cannot grow strong or produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ojieee amɛ mra lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara waa loo amɛwo yibii ni fa.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and soil food, while their leaves block each other from sunlight, leading to small and weak crops.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the blazing sun from evaporating moisture from the soil and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa hulu tsoɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry for fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often turn pale yellow, growth becomes slow and stunted, or stems become thin and weak, signaling that the soil needs fertilizer to help them grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni ehiɛɛɛ shi loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua tso lɛ ni edara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow during growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the bottom leaves usually means the maize plant is missing nitrogen, a crucial nutrient that keeps the plant green and helps it build food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛfeɔ niyenii.

english: Will applying double the recommended fertilizer make my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ toi enyɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, using too much fertilizer can burn the roots of your crops, dry out the plants, and severely reduce your harvest or kill the crop entirely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã onibii lɛ ashishifãi, ni eha tsei lɛ agbi, ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and droop in extreme heat to reduce water loss through their leaves, helping the plant conserve moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Flowers drop off when the plant suffers stress from excessive heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ babaoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ hao. Enɛ haaa yibii lɛ afee.

english: Why do my cowpea plants stop flowering when it rains heavily for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi beni nugbɔ enɛ waa gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy and continuous rain encourages the cowpea plant to spend energy growing leaves and vines instead of flowers and pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ wain tsei amli yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without producing good fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall and weak instead of producing fruit.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does planting my crops in straight rows instead of scattering seeds help them yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja yɛ dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets equal sunlight, air, and root space, while making it easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes crack open on the farm after a sudden rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tswaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when a dry period is followed by heavy water intake, causing the inside of the fruit to grow faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Tomato baatse kɛji nu babaoo ni anuɔ lɛ nyiɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout even when I pour plenty of water on them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo wo amɛmli daa gbi po lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen as well as water to germinate; soaking the soil completely without good drainage rots the seeds in the ground before they can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli kwraa ni nu kpakpa hoɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: This is usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants draw nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer top leaves when nutrients in the soil are low.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ faaa.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm help make the soil good for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small root nodules, which enriches the soil naturally with fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade from plantains or bigger trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni plantains loo tsei wuji aná hulutsoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade trees protect their delicate leaves from intense heat and help keep the surrounding soil moist so the roots can establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning rather than at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Morning watering lets soil absorb moisture before heat causes evaporation, and it gives foliage time to dry during the day so fungal diseases do not spread.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani dɔlɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ akagbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does swamp rice need to grow in standing water while my other crops die if flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo mli shi ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi Nu afua, nu afua?

english: Swamp rice has special internal air channels in its stems that carry oxygen down to its roots even underwater, while the standing water prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Swamp ŋmãa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ emli yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi po. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Extremely high heat, dry winds, or irregular watering stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms before pollination can convert them into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa tomato tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi dani pollination lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ amɛ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses that stop the leaves from expanding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when there is too much rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive rain creates waterlogged soil, which cuts off air to the cassava roots and creates ideal conditions for root-rot fungi to attack the crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. ni baafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli ni eha shihilɛ ni sa aba koni shishifãi ni egboi lɛ atutua ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce energy, which directly helps the tubers under the ground grow larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Enɛ baaye abua tɛ̃ɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy foliage, making them fall easily if their roots are weak or damaged by stem borer insects.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni tsii. Amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo kooloi ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ efite amɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to turn over the soil before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Turning over the soil breaks up hard ground, buries old weeds, and mixes air and nutrients into the dirt so your young crop roots can spread easily and grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ otsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Fuu jwɛi momo ni okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni otso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do people cover the soil around young crops with dry leaves and plant material?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ tsei ahe nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil traps moisture in the ground during hot days, prevents weeds from taking over, and slowly rots down to feed the growing crops.
ga: Mulching baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: How long should I keep my young crop seedlings in the nursery before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ dumɔwui bibii ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Keeping seedlings in a protected nursery for about 6 to 7 weeks gives them time to develop strong roots and stems so they can survive the harsh weather in the main field.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni abuɔ he aaafee otsii 6 kɛyashi 7 lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná be ni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli yɛ ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli.

english: What causes my seeds to sprout unevenly when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ?
