english: Seeds sprout unevenly if the soil moisture is inconsistent or if they are planted at different depths. Keeping the seedbed evenly damp ensures they all germinate at the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ mli edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why are tiny insects laying eggs on the undersides of my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Insects lay their eggs under leaves to hide them from the sun and predators. Once hatched, the young pests eat the leaves and drain strength from your crop.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛwui lɛ woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛkɛtee hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Kɛji efɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Can leaving decaying plant matter on my farm cause my next crops to get sick?
ga: Ani tsei ni egboi ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aná hela?

english: Yes, if infected plant waste is left to rot in the open field, it can trap fungi and germs that infect new crops when you plant them in the same spot.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ashi tsei ahe jwɛi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni amɛgbo yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli. Ebaanyɛ emɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ tsei heei lɛ kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ he kome.

english: Why do pest numbers increase so fast on my farm right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya beni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Rain encourages new green leaf growth, which provides abundant food and moisture for pests, causing them to breed and lay eggs much faster.
ga: Nugbɔ haa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ gbalashihilɛ ni amɛwoɔ wɔji oya kwraa.

english: Is it safe for my farm animals to graze on old crop residues left in the field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ baaye jwɛi ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ mli lɛ amli?

english: Animals can get good energy from crop leftovers, but if the plant matter has started to mold or carries disease, eating it can make your animals weak or sick.
ga: Koolooi baanyɛ ana hewalɛ kpakpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli. Shi kɛji tso lɛ bɔi tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela Ingesting ebaanyɛ eha kooloo lɛ agbɔjɔ loo hela mɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my soil if I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant needs and allows pests and soil diseases that target that crop to build up over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my crop is weak and lacks nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ bɛ mli?

english: A weak crop usually has yellowing leaves, thin stems, and slow growth, showing that the soil does not have enough food to give the plant full strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baa yɛ ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo, ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct, intense sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil. Retaining large canopy trees or planting food crops like plantains provides living shade and traps soil moisture, which helps young cocoa survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Tsoi wuji akwɛmɔ loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I remove the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, compete directly with the main stem for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Removing excess suckers leaves enough food for the main stem to grow strong and produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, kɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa baa koni tso lɛ yitso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii aba.

english: Why does my maize crop yield much better when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the plot first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, the maize feeds on this natural soil fertilizer and grows faster and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa yeɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni edaa oya ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to apply chemical fertilizer when the soil is wet rather than when it is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsofai baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni edɔ moŋ fe be mli ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve into a liquid form that roots can absorb. If applied to dry soil, fertilizer sits unused and can burn the roots under hot sun.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ nu ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ Fertilizer lɛ hiɔ shi ni akɛtsuuu nii ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: What is causing the central leaves of my young maize plants to look chewed up with small caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛmli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft inner leaves (the whorl) of maize plants. Catching them early and applying approved pesticides or localized sand/ash mixtures helps protect the growing point of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai bibii (rings) lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo ŋã/sũ ni akɛfutuɔ he ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the day even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks the plant's internal water pipes. Even if water is in the soil, the stems cannot transport it to the leaves, causing the plant to collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ tsei amli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ Anyɛɛɛ akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ aya baai lɛ anɔ. gbee tsei ashwie shi

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early from my cassava field when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ amli mra lɛ? Beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal available sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives young cassava plants room to establish strong root systems without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa yucca tsei bibii lɛ hegbɛ koni amɛto shishifãi ni mli wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Yam vines produce leaves that need sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which speeds up food production that flows down to grow bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi lɛ feɔ oya koni eha ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry heat spell that can last for weeks. Seeds that sprout in the first rain can quickly scorch and die before the main rains reliably settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ ahi shi otsii babaoo sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã oya ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning soft and brown if I leave them in the ground too long during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When mature cassava roots stay in soggy, waterlogged soil for too long, they lose access to oxygen and begin to rot under the ground. Harvesting mature roots promptly prevents root rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Amɛnáaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Shishifãi ni eda lɛ ni akpaa lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ ni fiteɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure will help the plants recover their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo ŋmei baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, keeps the soil moist by preventing water from evaporating in the hot sun. It also suppresses weed growth, keeps root temperatures cool, and adds nutrients to the soil as the plant material breaks down.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni ehaaa efo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu adalɛ naa. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni tsei amli nibii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight can dry them out and burn their leaves. Retaining large forest trees or planting shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa plants from heat stress until they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔ ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbi ni eha baai lɛ ashã. Koo mli tsei wuji ni abuɔ he loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he.

english: No, planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough resources to produce large, healthy ears of maize.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: How do I stop tiny caterpillars from eating holes in the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing funnels of maize plants. You can control them early by applying approved pest sprays or putting clean, dry sand mixed with neem powder into the central whorl of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ loo ŋã ni mli tse ni egbi ni akɛ neem powder efutu mli lɛ ni akɛaawo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to turn soft and rot in the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water gathers in the soil without draining, creating wet conditions where fungal diseases thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants dropping off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from environmental stress, such as extreme midday heat, irregular watering, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady soil moisture and shaded surroundings reduces this stress.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ he amanehulu. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ haa nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt and droop in the afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In hot weather, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. Deep watering early in the morning or late in the evening helps roots absorb water properly to handle heat during the day.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee hulutsoo be lɛ naa yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do store-bought hybrid seeds produce more crops than seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed for uniform strength, high yield, and disease resistance in their first generation. Saved seeds lose these strong traits in the next generation, leading to smaller, less uniform yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa, yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ feɔ bibioo ni esoro lɛ kwraa.

english: Why is it important to weed my farm during the first four weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first four weeks are when young crops establish their root systems and need uninterrupted light, water, and nutrients. Weeds that grow during this critical early stage steal these vital resources and permanently stunt crop growth.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ ji be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ni ehe hiaa la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai daa. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishijee be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ juɔ nɛkɛ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ daa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily in direct sun. Shade trees like plantains or forest trees act as natural shields, protecting the young cocoa plants from harsh heat while keeping humidity in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural survival tactic to protect itself from heat. By curling its leaves inward, the maize plant reduces the amount of leaf area exposed to the sun, which slows down water loss and keeps the plant from drying out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Abɛi haa baa lɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ baa lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for healthy leaf growth. When nitrogen in the soil runs low, the plant takes food from its older lower leaves and sends it up to keep the new top leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ ni mli wa Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkwɛ ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce tall stem growth and bushy green leaves, but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive rain early on, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leafy branches instead of storing food in its roots. Balancing soil nutrients encourages the plant to direct its energy underground into building large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo mra. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ amaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agboi.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller and weaker harvests when I plant the same crop on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo ni egbɔjɔ beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover. Over time, the soil becomes depleted and tired, which leaves plants hungry, weak, and more vulnerable to diseases unless crops are rotated or rest periods are allowed.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ. ja aŋmɛ gbɛ ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ajɔɔ he.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any tomatoes when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages their pollen, preventing pollination from taking place. To conserve energy and moisture during hot spells, the plant naturally drops its unpollinated flowers until cooler temperatures return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. Enɛ haa pollination nyɛɛɛ aba. Bɔni afee ni hewalɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ kpo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do yam tubers know when to start sprouting underground during the dry season before the rain even begins?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛnáa?

english: Yam tubers have an internal natural timer called dormancy. After resting underground for a set period, internal chemical changes tell the tuber that its sleep period is ending, triggering it to sprout and search for sunlight and moisture ahead of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli be he ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Beni ehi shikpɔŋ shishi be ko sɛɛ Tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli tsakemɔi lɛ kɛɔ yitso lɛ akɛ ewɔ be lɛ efo. Wo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtao hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants get thin and tall with few fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛlɛɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of branching out to produce plenty of fruits, the plants spend all their energy stretching upward to reach light before their neighbors block them.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ niji anɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshwieɔ shi koni emɔ la lɛ dani ekutsoŋnyo lɛ atsĩ enaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches of fruit when I leave many young shoots growing around the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young shoots, called suckers, share the root system of the main plantain tree and consume the food and water meant for the main tree. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strong shoots, ensuring the main tree has full energy to produce big fruit bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Jaa dumɔwu titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni oye niyenii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha tso titri lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly like tiny cups and stop expanding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids feeding on the soft leaf juices under the leaf, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. The damaged leaf tissues shrink and warp into curls as a reaction to the attack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa bibii lɛ amli nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Baa lɛ mli fãji ni efite lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ tutuamɔ lɛ hetoohamɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like newborn babies that cannot handle direct, strong heat. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside them shields the tender plants from direct sunlight and keeps the soil cool until the trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tso bibioo tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee ni nyɛɛɛ atsu dɔlɛ ni naa wa he nii tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaabu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why should I clear and prepare my farmland in small stages rather than trying to clear the whole area at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ni masaa he yɛ gbɛ bibii bibii anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ojie jɛmɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Clearing land all at once exposes huge areas of soil to heavy rains and baking sun, which washes away topsoil before you can plant. Doing it in stages helps you manage weeds easily and protects the soil quality.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ shikome lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa baa hei wuji anɔ. Enɛ baaho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ dani obaanyɛ odu. Nifeemɔ ni afeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ oya ni obuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is struggling to extract enough nutrients like nitrogen from the soil or that the soil has too much trapped water. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni ejie niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo ehi mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not hold the heavy weight of a full bunch well during strong winds. Supporting the stalk with a branched wooden pole or bamboo stick holds the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛtsiii nubu ni eyi obɔ lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni akɛ niji ni baaha tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ afi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or pest attacks. Keeping the soil constantly moist with mulch and protecting the crop from insects allows the flowers to set fruit properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii eba tso lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ mulch haa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai baa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does putting dry leaves or grass around the base of my crops help them survive dry spells?
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around crops with dry leaves acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground and blocks direct sunlight, stopping the water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Mulching around Dumɔwui ni baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce small, thin roots when planted in hard, unworked soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers expand underground, so if the soil is hard and tightly packed, the roots struggle to grow thick. Loosening the soil before planting gives the tubers space to grow big.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ehaa bulb lɛ náa he ko ni da ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my pepper plants more during the dry hot season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids reproduce faster in warm, dry conditions, while heat stresses pepper plants and makes them weaker against insect attacks. Regular watering helps the plants stay strong enough to withstand pests.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ aphids fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baanyɛ atutua amɛ oya. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden poles to climb instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso ni akwɔɔ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to grow healthy tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which boosts growth and prevents damp ground diseases from damaging the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajie kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dalɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that grows in dark, overly wet conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to reach the pods, keeping them dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Ha niji lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a vital food crop plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná su ni ji eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree is stressed by harsh dry weather, lacks soil nutrients, or is attacked by tiny insects like mirids. Providing adequate shade trees and protecting the trees from pests helps the flowers set into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni tutuaa lɛ Ni akɛ hulutsoo ni sa haa tso lɛ ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually because the soil moisture is inconsistent. Regular and steady watering helps the plant transport calcium from the soil into the fruit properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa ni afeɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil remains soaked with water for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to grow if I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often wet only the top layer of dirt, leaving the deeper soil hot and dry. Waiting for a few steady rainfalls ensures the soil holds enough deep moisture for seeds to sprout and survive without drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Nugbɔ ko ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make the food necessary for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing leaf diseases and encouraging bigger yam growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Etsiɔ foliar helai anaa ni ehaa sweet potatoes wuji lɛ daraa.

english: Why does my plantain mat produce smaller bunches of plantains after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ plantain bibii lɛ? Afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: As a plantain tree grows, it sprouts many young shoots called suckers that steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Cutting away excess suckers and leaving only two or three strong stems ensures the plant has enough energy to grow large bunches.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Ebaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii, ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize in the exact same spot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ he kome daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows maize-loving pests to build up in the ground. Changing crops breaks pest cycles and gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: How do groundnuts and beans help improve the soil for other crops planted after them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the plant dies, this stored nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when there seems to be plenty of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ lɛ? No tamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively drink up the soil water and eat the plant food intended for your crops. They also block sunlight, effectively starving your crops of the resources they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛmuɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛyeɔ tsei aniyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Amɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ hu naa. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ náaa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are vulnerable to direct sunlight, which burns their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly. Keeping big shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a umbrella canopy that protects young cocoa until they mature.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ waa. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi be mli ni cacao lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do black spots spread rapidly across my cocoa pods after a week of continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ otsi kome ni nugbɔ enɛɔ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall creates high moisture and humidity, which allows the black pod fungal disease to multiply and spread across pods. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and wind dry out the trees faster, stopping the mold from spreading.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa black pod fungus hela lɛ feɔ babaoo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa pod lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi oya kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to build leaf strength and green coloring. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow bigger cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my farm make the next maize crop grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through small nodules on their roots. When you harvest the legumes, that natural fertilizer remains in the ground to nourish the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmãa lɛ, Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I avoid applying chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a form that roots can safely drink. On dry land, concentrated fertilizer sits directly against the roots and burns them, which causes the plant to wilt and wither.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia nu koni etsɔ gbɛ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu shweshweeshwe. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baakpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni ebaashã amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants yield small cobs when I put four or five seeds in a single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ

english: When too many seeds share one hole, their roots battle each other for the same limited food and water in the soil. Spacing plants out gives every individual root system enough room to gather nutrients and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ, jaa amɛ awo bu kome mli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa shishifã fɛɛ shishifã naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ naa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to turn sunlight into food, which is sent downward to grow the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil into maximum sunlight while preventing leaf diseases caused by wet ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ tsakeɔ hulu la amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni atsu kɛba shi koni amɛyadu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ mli yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ baai helai ni hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hu naa.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the roots of my pepper plants help them stay alive in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛfataa mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around the stem with dry grass acts like a protective shade blanket. This practice keeps the soil underneath cool and prevents water from evaporating into the air, keeping root moisture intact.
ga: Mulching around Tsoi ni jwɛi ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo tsɔne. Nifeemɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afite.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming fruits during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High afternoon temperatures dry up the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from forming seeds. When a flower cannot form seeds, the plant drops it to conserve its water and energy for survival.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui afeemɔ naa Kɛji fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui Tsei shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: Cassava signals maturity when its lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the tubers expanding beneath.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ dalɛ kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ eshwɛ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa yɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why should I buy commercial seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my previous local harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe jarayeli dumɔwui moŋ fe ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from previous local harvests often lose their strength and disease resistance over time, leading to smaller yields. Commercial seeds are specially bred to withstand local pests, resist diseases, and produce much higher yields under proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi.

english: Can I plant tall crops like maize together with ground crops like cowpea on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa, yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows tall to capture sunlight while cowpeas spread across the ground, providing a live cover that suppresses weeds and adds nitrogen to the soil to nourish the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni enyɛ eŋɔ hulu la yɛ be mli ni tsina ŋmãa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli haa koni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young crops are usually a warning sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogging in the soil. Without early attention and nutrient support, the crops will not grow strong enough to produce full ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii kpakpa mli yelikɛbuamɔ mra lɛ, Nibii ni adu lɛ edaŋ waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why does commercial crop farming require so much more daily attention than growing a small garden behind my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ biɔ daa gbi kwɛmɔ babaoo fe abɔɔ bibioo ko adumɔ lɛ? yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ

english: Commercial farming involves planting larger fields closely together, which makes it easier for pests and diseases to spread rapidly. Frequent supervision, proper feeding, and quick intervention are necessary to protect your larger financial investment.
ga: Jarayeli okwaayeli biɔ ni adu shikpɔji wuji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi kɛ helai baagbɛ amɛshwã oya. regular care proper feeding Ni ehe miihia ni akɛ he awo mli oya koni akɛbu oshika babaoo ni okɛwo mli lɛ he.

english: Why is it recommended to plant plantains on my farmland before introducing young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in strong, direct tropical sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantain trees first creates a temporary shade layer that protects the young cocoa plants until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience environmental stress, such as extreme heat waves or sudden lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and maintaining organic cover helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be, ni akwɛɔ nɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop plants are easily choked out by fast-growing weeds that steal essential sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your primary crop the space and nutrients it needs to establish dominant root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ gbeɔ tsei bibii oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaaha otso titri lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi ni sa kadimɔ waa aba.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes at the very peak of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ oduɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive continuous rain creates humid conditions that lead to fungal blights and rot roots in tomato plants. Planting towards the end of the heavy rains allows crops to utilize ground moisture while benefiting from adequate sunlight for flowering.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni kɛ fungal blight kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ baa tomato tsei amli lɛ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naagbee lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: What will happen to my soil if I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Repeatedly growing heavy-feeding crops like cassava on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific soil diseases to accumulate. Rotating your crop types helps restore nutrient balance naturally.
ga: Nibii ni haa kooloi niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei, ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ashikpɔŋ nɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahenɔi ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot so quickly after I collect them from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rapid post-harvest rot happens when tubers get bruised during harvest or are stored in warm, damp places. Storing undamaged yams in a cool, shade-covered, and well-ventilated barn prevents decay and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ atswa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli loo akɛha amɛhe edɔ ni amɛhe edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni efiteee lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ akafite, ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to use tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to make food that grows large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they get maximum sunlight and avoids leaf rot diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni ekwa baai ni sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛma tsei ashishifãi ni wa.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but cowpeas and beans put nitrogen back into the soil naturally through their roots, restoring fertility for your next planting cycle.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni okɛ babaoo aku sɛɛ aba odumɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto my soil when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ mli be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so the crop roots can drink it up. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn root tips or blow away in the wind.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atswa kɛya.

english: Why are small worms eating ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni etse yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms that target the soft growing center of the maize plant. Catching them early with recommended sprays or neem extracts stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni tsɔɔ he ni ŋmãa tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ neem spray loo nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ekpa amɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off healthy-looking branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning lets sunlight and fresh air enter the tree canopy. This dries up excess moisture that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and stops weed seeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry spells in the soil, which prevents the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi akawo yibii.

english: Why does my cassava start rotting within just two days after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lose water rapidly and react quickly to air once dug up. Processing them immediately into gari, flour, or dough preserves them before spoilage begins.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ nu oya ni kɛ́ atsa amɛ lɛ, amɛtsuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he nii oya. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛfee gari ashikishaŋ loo ashikishaŋ koni ehi shi dani ebɔi fitemɔ.

english: Maize needs a nutrient called nitrogen to stay green and healthy. When there is not enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant moves whatever food it has left to the fresh new leaves at the top, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before they turn into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ebafeɔ anɔkwa tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry air, or irregular watering can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers as a survival trick to save energy instead of spending it on growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ shi akɛ teemɔŋ sane ko ni hiɛ kã ni akɛtoɔ hewalɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛbaafite yɛ aduawai akwɛmɔ mli.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water. By dropping leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through transpiration and protects its roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ kpaɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do dark, watery spots appear on my vegetable leaves right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji kɛ nu jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain splashing on the ground bounces soil-dwelling fungus spores onto lower leaves. The standing moisture on wet leaves allows these fungi to grow rapidly, causing dark spots and leaf rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Fɛ̃i ni damɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ daa oya. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baai ni fiteɔ baa.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special root nodules that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food. When the plants die, that extra plant food stays in the soil for the next crop to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso ko gbo lɛ, nakai tso niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my pepper fruits develop black rotten patches at the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: This rot is usually caused by a lack of calcium in the plant. Even if calcium is in the soil, uneven watering prevents the roots from absorbing it properly while the fruit is forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ calcium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ Shi nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even if I am giving my farm plenty of water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo haa ŋmɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that quickly soak up water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops, leaving your main plants starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei titrii lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need to grow up wooden stakes instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the wet ground so they catch more direct sunlight for photosynthesis, while keeping the leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases from soil contact.
ga: Staking jieɔ sweet potato baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni ekɛha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha fotosintɛsis. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha sweet potato baai lɛ agbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete intensely for sunlight. They spend all their energy stretching upwards to outgrow their neighbors instead of building thick stems and large ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋshii mli waa. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛye amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii agboi.

english: What does it mean when people say a piece of land has a high water table?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ nu lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A high water table means that underground water is sitting very close to the surface of the soil. Because the ground below is already filled with water, any new rain has nowhere to sink, leaving the surface soaked.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ waa. Ejaakɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ momo. Nugbɔ hee lɛ bɛ he ko ni ebaagbee shi. Okɛ ŋwɛi lɛ awo nu mli

english: Why is it important for me to observe my land through a full year before deciding what to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ dani makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ nɔ ni madu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Watching your land through both dry and rainy seasons shows you how water behaves on your farm over time. It helps you see whether the soil floods easily or dries out quickly so you can choose the right crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo bɔ ni nu feɔ enii ehaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ oya loo egbiɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa.

english: How can I test if my soil holds water too close to the surface before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ miimɔ nu ni ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: You can dig a small test hole on your farm after a light rain. If water quickly gathers near the top of the hole and stays there, your land has a high water table.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kaa bu bibioo ko atsu nii. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛji nu shwie shi oya yɛ bu lɛ yiteŋgbɛ ni ehi jɛmɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why does my farm get flooded with water after just a light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This happens because the underground water table on your farm is very high. Since the soil underneath is already full of water, even a small amount of rainfall stays on top of the ground and creates flooding.
ga: Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fa babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yɛ nu momo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo po hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu afua baa.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast even after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Your land likely has a low water table and sandy or loose soil. Water quickly drains very deep into the ground rather than staying near the surface where crop roots can reach it.
ga: Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa, ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ. Nu lɛ baaho oya kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, a bɛŋkɛ hehi nɛ tsehi a sisi numi ma nyɛ maa ya su ɔ.

english: Why does water gather on one section of my farm while another section stays dry after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome nɔ yɛ be mli ni fã kroko lɛ kã he egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Different parts of the same farm can have different soil types and water table levels. One area might have a high water table that traps rain, while another area allows water to sink deep into the earth.
ga: Okwaafoi akuu kome mli hei srɔtoi baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi kɛ nu ni falɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi. He ko baanyɛ aná nu babaoo ni baaha nugbɔ lɛ ahi shi. yɛ be mli ni he kroko hu haa nu boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to dig very deep on some parts of my farmland to find moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ hei komɛi koni mana shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ?

english: In those areas, the water table is very low. Rainwater drains deep into the earth quickly, leaving the top layer of soil dry and requiring deep digging to reach moisture.
ga: Yɛ nakai hei lɛ, nu lɛ baa shi waa. Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ oya. Ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. ni esa akɛ atsa mli shɔŋŋ koni ana ŋmɔtɔ

english: Can having water standing on my farm for a long time damage my crops?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, waterlogging fills the air spaces in the soil. When soil stays soaked for too long, crop roots cannot get air, which causes them to rot and destroys the plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu miiyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Which crops can I plant if my land naturally holds a lot of water after rain?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops like rice and sugarcane grow well in soil that holds a lot of water, whereas crops like cassava and cocoa prefer well-drained soil where water sinks deep quickly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ kookoo sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieɔ shi oya lɛ.

english: How can I protect my crops if my farm has a high water table that causes flooding?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha nu afua aba?

english: You can build raised soil mounds or dig drainage channels across your farm. This allows excess rainwater to flow away from your crop roots instead of sitting on the soil surface.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How many times in a single year can I plant maize on my farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi mli?

english: In Ghana, you can plant maize twice a year because we have two distinct rainy seasons: the major season starting around March or April, and the minor season starting around September.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli ejaakɛ wɔyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei srɔtoi enyɔ: Be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ March loo April aaafee. ni be ni ji enyɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ September aaafee.

english: Is it possible for me to harvest rice two times within one year?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makpa ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, if you have adequate water access or follow the natural rainy seasons, you can cultivate and harvest rice twice a year—once during the major rainy season and once during the minor season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji oyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa nɔ. Obaanyɛ odu ni okpa ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli. Shikome yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli, kɛ shikome hu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be bibioo lɛ mli.

english: Does corn grow differently during the second rainy season compared to the first?
ga: Ani ŋmãa baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, the second rainy season is usually shorter, so corn often needs quick-maturing seed varieties and precise planting timing to yield well before the dry season starts.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ feɔ kuku. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa biɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra kɛ be ni sa ni akɛduɔ lɛ koni ewo yibii kpakpai dani hulutsoo be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why does a crop inspector need to visit my field during the planting period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ayasara miŋmɔji lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Inspectors visit your farm to check that your seeds and planting methods meet proper standards, ensuring healthy crop growth and preventing seed-borne diseases from spreading.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baasara oŋmɔ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ kɛ gbɛi ni otsɔɔ nɔ oduɔ nii lɛ kɛ shishitoo mlai ni sa lɛ kpãa gbee lo. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩ helai ni tsei dumɔwui kɛbaa lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: If I plant my crops twice in a year, do inspectors need to come to my farm both times?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli Ani ehe miihia ni kwɛlɔi aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, because each planting season brings different weather conditions and field preparations, inspectors must evaluate your farm during both seasons to maintain crop quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ sɔrɔtoi. Esa akɛ mɛi ni baakwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ bei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my seed crop without letting the inspectors check the field first?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni mihaaa mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akwɛɛɛ jɛmɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: If inspectors do not check your field at the required stages, your harvest cannot be officially certified, which prevents you from selling it as approved certified seed to major buyers.
ga: Kɛji kwɛlɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛi ni ataoɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ he odaseyeli yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Enɛ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okahɔ̃ɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ aha mɛi wuji ni heɔ nii lɛ.

english: How does the corn I grow on my small farm help supply all of Ghana?
ga: Abele ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miyelikɛbuamɔ lɛ aha Ghana fɛɛ niyenii?

english: When individual farmers plant certified high-yielding corn, their combined harvest creates a national food supply that feeds markets, schools, and cities across the entire country.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi aŋkroaŋkroi du ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ, Amɛ ŋmãa ni abua naa lɛ haa maŋ niyenii ni haa jarayeli hei, skul, kɛ maji ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ baa.

english: What do I need to do if I want to produce crop seeds to sell to other farmers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji miisumɔ ni mafee dumɔwui ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: You must register your land for official seed production, buy certified foundation seeds, and allow agricultural officers to inspect your farm throughout the growing cycle.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ awo wolo nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ kɛha dumɔwui akwɛmɔ. Hemɔ shishijee dumɔwui ni awo he odase. ni oha okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni okwaayeli lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do rice crops require so much water to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in high-moisture conditions, which help the roots absorb nutrients efficiently while suppressing weeds that compete with the crop.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ shihilɛi ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efoɔ jwɛi ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ lɛ naa.

english: How quickly should I clear my land after harvesting the first crop to get ready for the second crop?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya tɛŋŋ beni mikpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni mikɛsaa mihe kɛha nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ?

english: You should clear remaining crop stalks and till the soil immediately after the first harvest so your field is ready to receive seeds as soon as the second rains begin.
ga: Esa akɛ ofɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔji lɛ afee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛji nugbɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ je shishi pɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When maize plants are too crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ mlɛo ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ hu ji bibii waa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from growing and taking food from your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key food for plants. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep into the ground where the plant roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Severe heat prevents the flowers from forming fruits properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and watery when I dig them up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛji atsa mra lɛ?

english: Cassava plants need time to build up starch in their roots. Harvesting too early means the root has mostly water and hasn't had enough time to store the food that makes it thick and firm.
ga: Be he hiaa cassava tsei koni amɛfee starch yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nu lɛ fa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni akɛtoɔ niyenii ni haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing shoots in the barn before planting time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani dumɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from their resting period when the air in the barn becomes warm. This warmth tricks the yam into thinking it is time to grow new plants.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ nɛɛ lakaa sweet potato lɛ ni esusuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ edu tso hee.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck the sap from tender leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Spraying for pests early protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai fɔji shwieɔ nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: What causes small ragged holes and green droppings in the middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ fɛɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the soft inner leaves (the funnel) of the young corn plant and eats the leaves as they try to open.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai bibii (cones) lɛ amli. ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbele lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that provide cool shade and protect the fragile cocoa plants during their first two years.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei ni waaa lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Plantains do not have deep roots to hold them in the ground; their roots grow shallowly near the top of the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the plant easily tips over and needs wooden sticks for support.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaha amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ fioo ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ feɔ shwiili lɛ. Tsei gbeeɔ shi oya ni esa akɛ akɛ tsei afi amɛhe.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop if the tree lacks water, if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium, or if tiny insects are attacking them. Regular weeding, proper shade management, and using recommended fertilizers help flowers stay on the tree to form healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii miitutua lɛ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi daa. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa Ni kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: How long will it take for my new cocoa seedlings to start giving me pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ aje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years. Good care, proper shade management, and sufficient rainfall speed up early fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Kwɛmɔ kpakpa, hulutsoo be ni sa Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ yibii oya.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods small and deformed instead of growing big and full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ji bibii ni efite yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ?

english: Small or deformed pods usually happen when the tree does not get enough nutrients during pod development or when pests damage the young pods early on. Applying compost or recommended fertilizer at the start of the rains helps pods grow to full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ni ehiii lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli loo kɛ́ ŋmeii fite ŋmeii bibii lɛ mra. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and hard while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection triggered by high humidity, heavy rains, and excessive shade. Pruning excess branches, harvesting ripe pods promptly, and spraying approved fungicides keep the pods healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal helai ni hulutsoo be babaoo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛbaa. niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ Akpaa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baashwie nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What are these tiny insects making dry spots on my cocoa branches, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ mi-kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These are likely capsids (also called mirids), which suck sap from young branches and cause them to dry up. You can manage them by spraying recommended insecticides during their peak season between August and December.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji capsids. (Atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mirid) ni shwieɔ tsei niji bibii amli nu lɛ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ oooshwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo yɛ August kɛ December teŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to cut down all the big trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkafo tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?
