english: Big shade trees protect cocoa leaves from harsh direct sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist during the dry season, and prolong the lifespan of your cocoa trees.
ga: Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni oha okkoo tsei lɛ awala aya hiɛ.

english: Is it better for me to burn cleared weeds or leave them on the farm floor?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ loo mashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the farm floor as mulch is better because as they rot, they return rich nutrients to the soil, preserve moisture, and prevent soil erosion during heavy rains.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cash crops turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi shika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains often mean the soil is waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and stops them from absorbing nitrogen. Digging simple drainage channels around your farm helps excess water flow away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛŋɔ nitrogen. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootsɔ Oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akaho.

english: Why do my young cashew seedlings dry up and die even after I plant them properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew dumɔwui lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Young cashew plants need protection from extreme heat and deep watering during their first dry season. If the soil dries out completely, the tender roots burn and fail to transport water to the leaves.
ga: Cashew tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni mli kwɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ Shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ nu aya baai lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the best time to harvest my oil palm bunches so I get maximum oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa mu tsei akui lɛ? Koni ená mu babaoo

english: An oil palm bunch is ready for harvest when a few loose fruits fall to the ground naturally and the outer fruits turn a bright orange-red color, indicating high oil content.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekpogbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Etsɔɔ akɛ mu babaoo yɛ mli.

english: How do I know which direction to push cassava stalks into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Cassava stems have tiny buds or 'eyes' located right above the leaf scars, and these buds must point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stalk upside down, the plant wastes energy trying to bend its new shoots upward, resulting in delayed growth and fewer tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni esa akɛ nɛkɛ hiŋmɛii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii heei abɔle ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa edalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes in the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei kakadaji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much direct sunlight as possible to produce the food needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, which maximizes sunlight exposure and prevents leaves from rotting due to soil-borne diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni haa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni ehaaa baai lɛ afite yɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my green maize plants rolling up tightly like pencils during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei eŋɔli lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ pensil yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural survival mechanism when the soil is dry and the sun is hot. By rolling inward, the leaf hides its pores from direct wind and sun, reducing the amount of water the plant loses through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni hulu lɛ mli edɔ. Akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni tsei laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my groundnut plants forming small round bumps on their roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miifee ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Those small bumps are beneficial root nodules that house friendly soil bacteria. These bacteria take nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into natural plant food, which helps the groundnut crop grow without needing as much synthetic fertilizer.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ji shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ mli helai. Nɛkɛ muawai nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ daa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmei ni akɛfee ŋmei babaoo awo mli.

english: Why are the bright yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when bees do not pollinate them. When stressed, the tomato plant sheds its blossoms to save its limited energy and moisture for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei bɛ nu Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii efeee pollination. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees act as a protective blanket, lowering the surrounding temperature and keeping humidity high so the delicate cocoa leaves do not burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baa shi ni eha hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ. Bɔni afee ni akashã kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with very few peppers when I plant them under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni midu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need intense sunlight to produce the food required for flowering and fruiting. Under heavy shade, the plant stretches upward searching for light, becoming thin and weak with little energy left to make peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛwo yibii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Ebafeɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ ni hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ ni ekɛfeɔ chili.

english: Why are the young leaves on my chili pepper plants curling upwards and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding on the undersides of leaves. As they feed on the sap, they damage the plant cells, causing the leaves to grow unevenly and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. be mli ni enuɔ mliki lɛ Ebaakpata tsei amli wala yibii lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daraa kɛ amɛhe shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while my maize plants die if water stays on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baagboi kɛji ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air tubes inside their stems that send oxygen from the air down to their underwater roots. Maize roots lack these air channels, so standing water smothers the roots and cuts off their oxygen, causing them to rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abele shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to shoot up during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry harmattan, low air moisture and dry soil cause plantain suckers to enter a resting state to conserve water. Growth naturally resumes once rain returns and moistens the root zone.
ga: Yɛ harmatta ni egbi lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa shi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa dumɔwui boteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Dalɛ baaje shishi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nugbɔ enɛ ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ edɔ.

english: Why should I wash my cutlass and boots before moving from one field to another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ mihiŋmɛigbelemɔi kɛ mi-boots lɛ he dani mashi ŋmɔ kome mli kɛya ekroko mli lɛ?

english: Plant diseases and tiny pests can travel on the mud stuck to your boots or cutlass blade. Cleaning your tools and footwear prevents you from accidentally carrying diseases from an infected patch to your healthy crops.
ga: Tsei amli helai kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aya muji ni akɛkpɛtɛ o-boots loo dagger blades lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsumɔ odɛŋdadei kɛ okotokui lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ ni okɛ hela akajɛ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oshara mli.

english: Can visitors or farm workers walking into my fields make my crops fall sick?
ga: Ani saralɔi loo ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ni nyiɛɔ kɛboteɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee hela?

english: Yes, visitors can carry fungal spores, bacteria, or tiny insect pests on their clothes, hands, and shoes from other farms. Restricting unnecessary entry and ensuring clean clothing helps protect your field from external infections.
ga: Hɛɛ, saralɔi baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, bacteria, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii awo amɛtadei, amɛniji, kɛ amɛ tokotai anɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli. Kɛ́ otsi nibii ni he ehiaaa ni boteɔ mli lɛ anaa ni oha atadei ahe atse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oyale lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my cassava or cocoa crops are starting to get sick before the whole farm dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava loo cocoa tsei lɛ miibɔi hela mɔmɔ dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ gbo?

english: Crops show early signs through subtle changes like leaf yellowing, unusual spots, leaf curling, or stunted growth. Regular inspection allows you to spot these signs early and remove sick parts before the sickness spreads.
ga: Tsei jieɔ mra be mli okadii kɛtsɔɔ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, hei ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe loo amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona okadii nɛɛ mra. ni ojie hei ni hela mɔ lɛ dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How often should I walk through my field to inspect my crops for problems?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli koni makwɛ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii amli naagbai yɛ?

english: Walking through your field at least twice a week lets you monitor plant behavior, check under leaves, and catch pests or diseases early when they are still easy and cheap to manage.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔji amli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tsei lɛ ajeŋba. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni omɔ kooloi bibii loo helai mra. ni ji nɔ ni hu waaa ni ejara waaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: If I find one cocoa tree with yellowing leaves or odd spots, should I pull it out immediately or wait to see if it heals?
ga: Kɛ́ ona akɛ o-cocoa tsei lɛ eko yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo he ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ, ani esa akɛ ojie amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo omɛ ni okwɛ kɛji ebaatsa?

english: You should isolate or remove infected plant parts immediately. Sick plants rarely heal on their own, and leaving them allows insects or the wind to carry the disease to surrounding healthy trees.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tso lɛ fãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo ojie amɛ. Ewa akɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛŋ aná hewalɛ. Ni kɛ́ ashi lɛ agbele lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ helai aya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves droop and curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward during intense heat to reduce water loss from their surfaces. It is a natural survival mechanism, but if they remain wilted into the cool evening, it indicates severe soil moisture loss or root damage.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ amɛgboi lolo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ hu? Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ elaaje waa loo shishifãi lɛ efite.

english: Why do vegetables grown in nursery beds die off suddenly right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ gboiɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This usually happens because of soil-borne fungi that thrive in overly damp or unsterilized nursery beds. Keeping the nursery soil clean, well-drained, and protected prevents root and stem decay in young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei ni mli efɔ fe nine loo ni afɔɔɔ hela lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehe atse Nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni kɛ́ abu he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akatsi shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do crops planted too close together seem to catch leaf diseases more easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsei ahe helai oya lɛ?

english: Crowded crops trap moisture and block airflow, creating humid conditions that fungal diseases need to grow. Proper spacing lets sunlight and air dry the leaves, keeping the plant environment healthy.
ga: Dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ he hiaa koni amɛdara lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa baai lɛ agbiɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ shihilɛhe lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi

english: Is it better to treat crops after they show signs of disease or take steps to prevent sickness early?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaatsa ŋmɔshi nibii beni hela okadii lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ loo afee nibii ni baaha hela akaye mɔ mra?

english: Preventing disease through proper field sanitation, healthy soil, and clean practices is far cheaper and more effective than trying to treat crops once a disease has already damaged them.
ga: Helai ni atsĩɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli hetsemɔ ni sa nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ nifeemɔi ni he tse lɛ jara waaa ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni abɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ahere ŋmɔshi nii ko yiwala be mli ni hela efite lɛ momo lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds around the base of my crops make them more likely to get sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ haa hela mɔɔ amɛ waa lɛ?

english: Weeds act as living shelters and alternate hosts for pests and diseases. Keeping the base of your crops clear removes these hiding spots and reduces disease pressure on your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ wɔɔhe kɛ shihilɛhe ni ji enyɔ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ ni ebaaha helai ni baa onibii titri lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow before the crop is fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which acts as its essential food, or when heavy rains flood the field and prevent the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from heat stress during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Crops show heat stress when their leaves curl up, droop during the hottest part of the afternoon, or develop dry, brown edges as they try to save moisture.
ga: Tsei jieɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpo kɛji amɛbaai lɛ shwie shi. Egbee shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli Aloo eyɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in high humidity, wet weather, and dense shade where air cannot circulate freely around the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Fungal hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle he. Sheath heyeli

english: Extremely high temperatures or a sudden lack of water can cause tomato plants to drop their flowers as a survival mechanism, preventing the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi. ni etsĩ tomato tsei anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Why does planting the same crop on my land year after year make the harvest smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining small and thin instead of getting big and starch-filled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay small if the soil is too hard and compact for the roots to expand, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium that help the plant store starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli nibii titrii tamɔ potassium ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ starch toɔ lɛ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even if they aren't touching them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji mitaaa amɛhe po?

english: Weeds steal critical nutrients, water, and sunlight from the surrounding soil, leaving your crops weak and malnourished even without direct physical contact.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe kpaaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ po.

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves toward maximum sunlight so they can make food for the underground tubers, while keeping the leaves off damp soil where rot and diseases thrive.
ga: Staking baaha wain tso lɛ baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai fɔɔ baa lɛ he.

english: Which fast-growing crops can I plant to harvest quickly and get money to pay off farm expenses?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu koni maná oya ni maná shika ni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔ?

english: Short-season vegetables like okra, peppers, and garden eggs can be harvested within 2 to 3 months, giving you quick income compared to long-term tree crops like cocoa or oil palm.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ okra, ŋmei kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni ehaa onáa shika oya kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei fɔ he.

english: How does placing fertilizer right at the crop base help me cut down on wasted effort?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei ashishi lɛ haa hewalɛ ni afiteɔ lɛ baa shi?

english: Targeted fertilizer application ensures your crops get maximum nutrients directly at their roots with less physical labor, rather than feeding the surrounding weeds.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa otsei lɛ naa niyenii babaoo tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni nitsumɔ fioo pɛ tsuɔ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ niyenii

english: Why do extension officers ask us to cut down and burn cocoa trees infected with swollen shoot disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ ni afolɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi efuu lɛ?

english: Swollen shoot is caused by a virus with no cure. Removing and destroying the infected trees stops the virus from spreading through insects to neighboring healthy cocoa trees on your farm.
ga: Virus ko ni bɛ tsabaa ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei ni efuu baa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ ni akpataa he lɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ kɛyaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave rotten or insect-damaged fruits lying on the ground near my healthy crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ aduawai ni egbo loo kooloi efite lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Rotten produce attracts pests like fruit flies and harbors fungal spores. Leaving them in the field gives pests a home to multiply and attack the rest of your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni efite lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ toɔ. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ naa shia ni amɛbaafɔ ni amɛtutua onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if wild animals are damaging my crops instead of a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji koo mli kooloi miifite miŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe tsei ahe helai?

english: Animals leave clean bite marks, broken branches, or footprints, whereas diseases usually cause leaf discoloration, spots, wilting, or unnatural growths without physical chewing.
ga: Koolooi baaná ŋmɔlɔ he okadii ni he tse, niji ni ekumɔ, loo naji ahe okadii, yɛ be mli ni helai Bei pii lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su, amɛnáa ŋmeii, amɛgboiɔ, loo amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛyeee.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green growth and healthy crop production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally to conserve water when the ground is dry. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue feeding its underground roots.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi.

english: Why do my green tomatoes turn black and rot at the bottom while still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It occurs when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering, causing the bottom tissue of the fruit to break down.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Ehaa fãji ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds growing very close to my vegetable crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ mi aduawai lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your vegetables, while also providing shelter for harmful pests that feed on your plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-vegetables lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni yeɔ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ he ko amɛhiɔ.

english: How does storing harvested grain in sealed airtight bags stop insects from destroying it?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: Airtight containers and bags cut off the oxygen supply inside. Without oxygen, insects and their eggs cannot survive or multiply, keeping your grain safe.
ga: Vacuum tsɛnsii kɛ kotokui lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa mli lɛ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Kooloi kɛ amɛwui lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi loo amɛshwere. Koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my maize plants grow better when I plant cowpeas alongside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for neighboring maize plants.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: Why are bees gathering around my cashew trees during flowering, and should I chase them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa lɛ? Mi cashew tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli Ni ani esa akɛ mashwie amɛ?

english: You should leave the bees alone because they are pollinating your flowers. As they move from bloom to bloom, they transfer pollen, which allows the tree to form cashew nuts.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi ŋmeii lɛ ejaakɛ amɛmiiwo ofɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii. beni amɛjɛɔ panɛl kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ Amɛbaawo pollen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ cashew ŋmeii.

english: How can I plant my cassava so that I do not harvest everything at the exact same time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmei koni mikakpa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Planting your cassava in small batches a few weeks or months apart allows the crops to mature at different times, giving you a continuous food supply and income throughout the year instead of all at once.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ kui bibii amli Otsii loo nyɔji fioo komɛi ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ shikome.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my maize when the rain patterns keep changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Beni nugbɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ

english: It is best to wait until the major rainy season fully establishes and the soil stays consistently moist for several days, or check with local agricultural extension officers for weather updates before sowing.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baaho aya. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be gbii babaoo. Aloo bi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe lɛ koni ena kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land where I just finished harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni migbe ŋmãa kpamɔ naa amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously on the same land drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up, which reduces your yields in the following season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa sũ mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ baaha onibii ni obaawo lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: What crop can I plant after harvesting my yam to help restore the strength of my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu kɛji mikpa sweet potatoes lɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba?

english: Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, or beans after yam puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally, making it fertile for your next major crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha efee nɔ ni woɔ yibii kɛha onibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: If I did not get a good harvest from my pepper farm this year, what can I do differently for the next season?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai anɔ kɛjɛɛɛ pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli afi nɛɛ, Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: You can improve your harvest by mixing compost or well-rotted manure into the soil before planting, using healthy certified seeds, and removing weeds early so they do not steal nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni okɛaafutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. koni akaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ

english: Can I leave my cassava tubers in the ground for a few extra months after they are mature without them spoiling?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi beni amɛdara lɛ sɛɛ ni amɛfiteee?

english: Yes, cassava can be stored naturally underground for several months after reaching maturity, though leaving it in the soil for too long can make the roots woody and reduce their food quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa nyɔji babaoo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee tsei, ni ebaaha niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to plant vegetables between my young cocoa trees while waiting for the cocoa to grow?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu aduawai yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ cacao lɛ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Yes, growing short-term crops like peppers, garden eggs, or tomatoes between young cocoa trees makes good use of your land and provides early income while the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmeii, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, loo tomato yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha oná shika oya be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How can I prepare a new piece of land for planting while I am still busy harvesting my current plot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ hee kɛha dumɔ nii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ mihe miiwo shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can clear and prepare your new land in small sections during off-peak days, ensuring the soil is tilled and ready for seeds immediately after your current harvest ends.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ ni osaa he yɛ fãi bibii amli. Yɛ be mli ni shisharalɔi babaoo bɛ lɛ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsu nii ni efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okpamɔ ni okpaa amrɔ nɛɛ eba naagbee lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain plants taking longer to yield fruits this year compared to last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ he be babaoo dani ewo yibii afi nɛɛ fe afi ni eho lɛ?

english: Plantain maturity can be delayed by long dry spells, low soil fertility, or excessive shade from nearby large trees, as the plant requires sufficient water and sunlight to flower.
ga: Hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ baanyɛ aha plantain lɛ adalɛ asɛɛ afo. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi loo hulutsoo babaoo ni jɛɔ tsei wuji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei hia nu kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do some tomato plants on my farm produce large fruits while others right next to them stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi wooo lɛ? Mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daraaa.

english: Differences in fruit size happen when certain plants receive more sunlight, water, or nutrients, or when some plants suffer early root damage from hidden soil pests.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji tsei komɛi ná hulu la, nu, loo niyenii babaoo. aloo beni tsei komɛi shishifãi fiteɔ mra lɛ. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ adɛŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and thin bark that scorch easily under direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting crops like plantain alongside them provides necessary shade, keeps the air humid, and protects the tender plants until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ Aloo aduɔ tsei tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi. Tsei baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Should I leave all the small plantain shoots growing around my main plant, or cut some of them off?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashɛ plantain tsei bibii lɛ ashwie? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi tso titri lɛ he loo efoɔ ekomɛi?

english: You should remove most of the extra shoots, leaving only two or three strong ones. If you leave all of them, they will fight with the main plant for water and nutrients, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ fɛɛ, ni oshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ pɛ lɛ, amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ baawu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii, ni no baaha amɛná plantains bibii.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni he hiaa koni afee niyenii ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil get so hot and dry quickly during the dry season, and how can I keep it moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nu yɛ mihe?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly to the heat of the sun. Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass, leaves, or crop stalks—a practice called mulching—acts like a blanket that traps soil moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ nu fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la ha edɔ. Ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai loo tso shishifãi baaha he ni oŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni mɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny pods on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. Planting them enriches the ground naturally, which feeds hungry crops like maize that grow there later.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni sɛɛ mli lɛ ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together, will I harvest more cassava tubers?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani wɔbaakpa ŋmei shishifãi babaoo?

english: No, planting cassava stems too close together causes them to crowd each other out and compete for sunlight and soil food. Giving each plant proper space (about one meter apart) gives the tubers room beneath the soil to grow thick and heavy.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu yucca tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ekome ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa (aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe) lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into big mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua shikpɔŋ agbo ko naa dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards and need soft, loose earth to expand properly. Making high soil mounds softens the ground, prevents rain from drowning the roots, and makes it much easier for large tubers to form.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni ehe miihia ni amɛná shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Tsĩɔ nugbɔ naa koni shishifãi akagbee shi ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa yitsei wuji akɛ amɛbaafee.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides deep inside the growing tip of the maize stalk. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extract can stop them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off the plant without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly, or if sucking insects attack the blossoms. Keeping soil moisture steady and protecting plants from extreme heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ lɛ. aloo kɛji kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same plot of land where I harvested pepper last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa mi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Planting the same crop in the exact same soil year after year allows pests and soil diseases that feed on pepper to multiply in the ground. Rotating your pepper crop with cassava, maize, or legumes breaks the disease cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Pepper ni akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa duɔ lɛ fiteɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but very few of them turn into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need to be pollinated by tiny insects called midges or by hand to form pods. If a flower isn't pollinated within a day or two of opening, it dies and falls off the tree without growing into fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge loo abaanyɛ akɛ nine agbele pods lɛ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔii lɛ amli pollin yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛfɔ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is hand pollination, and how can it help my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually transfer pollen from one cocoa flower to another using tiny tools like forceps. It ensures that far more flowers get fertilized, which helps your trees yield significantly more cocoa pods than relying on wild insects alone.
ga: Nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ ji be mli ni okɛ onine shwieɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo ko tamɔ pliers nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni fɔfɔi babaoo aná fɔfɔi. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ pɛ anɔ.

english: Is it worth hand pollinating just one or two flowers on a branch, or does it only work if I do the whole tree?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ mikɛ niji baawo fɔfɔi 1-2 pɛ yɛ tso nine nɔ loo ebaatsu nii pɛ kɛji mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ wo fɔfɔi lɛ amli?

english: Every single flower you pollinate has the chance to become a full cocoa pod. Even if you only pollinate one or two flowers at a time, those specific flowers will still develop into healthy pods and add to your overall harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ hegbɛ akɛ ebaatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ fɔfɔi kome loo enyɔ pɛ woɔ pollination mli yɛ be kome mli po. Nakai fɔfɔi lɛ baaya nɔ atsɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni oooha lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are natural insects not enough to give my cocoa trees a good harvest these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha mi cacao tsei lɛ aná ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Natural pollinators like midges are very small and sensitive to dry weather, direct sunlight, and farm chemicals. When their numbers drop, many cocoa flowers go unpollinated unless human help or better shade management is introduced.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛnuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ahe. Beni fɔfɔi lɛ ayibɔ baa shi lɛ Kookoo fɔfɔi babaoo bɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ja adesa yelikɛbuamɔ loo shade nɔkwɛmɔ ni hi fe no yɛ.

english: Why do healthy-looking cocoa flowers dry up and fall off the tree after just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: A cocoa flower only stays open and fertile for about 24 to 36 hours. If it does not receive pollen during that short window, or if the tree lacks water and nutrients, the flower naturally drops off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii aaafee ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 36 pɛ. Kɛji akɛ anáaa pollen yɛ nakai be kukuoo lɛ mli, loo kɛji akɛ nu kɛ niyenii bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Where on the cocoa tree do the flowers actually come from, and how do I protect those spots?
ga: Nɛgbɛ fɔfɔi nɛɛ jɛɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nakai ŋmeii lɛ anaa?

english: Cocoa flowers grow from small bumps on the trunk and main branches called flower cushions. You should be careful not to scrape or cut the bark in these areas during weeding or harvesting, as damaging a cushion prevents flowers from growing there in the future.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Atsɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji wuji lɛ akɛ fɔfɔi akushɛi. Esa akɛ okwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okafo loo okafo tso lɛ yibii yɛ hei nɛɛ yɛ jwɛi loo ŋmaakpamɔ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpata kushɛŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi akakwɛ̃ yɛ nakai he lɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: How long does a cocoa flower take to grow into a ripe pod after it has been pollinated?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once a flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about five to six months for it to develop from a tiny cushion bump into a fully mature, ripe cocoa pod ready for harvesting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli lɛ Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5-6 dani ejɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko mli baa. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa ni amɛbaafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How does joining a government cocoa pollination initiative help my farm's income?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ he nitsumɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ mihe woɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ shika ni mináa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Government pollination programs bring trained workers to your farm to hand-pollinate your trees. This increases the total number of pods each tree produces, leading to a larger harvest and higher sales revenues without requiring extra land.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ pollination gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kɛ nitsulɔi ni atsɔse amɛ baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛ amɛdɛŋ afee pollination yɛ otsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni tso fɛɛ tso woɔ lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa akpaa nibii babaoo ni anáa shika babaoo kɛjɛɔ jarayeli mli ni shikpɔŋ kroko he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a sudden burst of flowers right after the dry season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally react to rain following a dry spell. The sudden intake of water signals to the tree that conditions are good to reproduce, triggering a heavy flush of new flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli trukaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shihilɛi lɛ hi kɛha fɔmɔ. Wo fɔfɔi heei babaoo he hewalɛ.

english: Why does cutting back excess branches and shade help my cocoa trees produce more flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning allows filtered sunlight and air to reach the trunk and main branches where flower cushions live. Proper light and air circulation reduce fungal diseases and give the tree more energy to form flowers and support growing pods.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji wuji ni fɔfɔi lɛ akutsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. La kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni eyeɔ ebuaa pod lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the tops are green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow from the tip inward, it usually means the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to nourish the newer top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛtee mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas act as natural food producers for the soil. They take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the ground, which feeds the neighboring maize plant and makes it grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing green and yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus weakens the leaves so they cannot trap sunlight, resulting in very small root tubers.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shishifã lɛ yitso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa.

english: If I spray chemical pesticides on my crops, will it hurt the small insects that don't harm my food?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, Ani ebaaye kooloi bibii ni bɛ awui ni yɔɔ miniyenii lɛ mli lɛ awui?

english: Yes, standard chemical pesticides kill both bad insects and helpful ones, like bees that pollinate crop flowers and ladybugs that eat crop-damaging pests, leaving the farm without natural defenders.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ gbeɔ kooloi fɔji kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ fɛɛ. kɛ ladybugs ni yeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni aaashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni adebɔɔ mli bulɔi bɛ mli

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper plants shrinking, curling upward, and feeling thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ, amɛmiibɔle amɛhe, ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This behavior is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves and feeding on sap, which causes the leaf tissue to deform as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ baai ashishi ni amɛyeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees abort their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of shade, drought, or poor soil nutrients. Without enough moisture and protection from harsh weather, the tree sheds flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ laajeɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haaa mɔ he waa lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to uneven watering or dry soil spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce very small fruit bunches when many small shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii waa yɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe.

english: The small shoots (suckers) compete directly with the main mother plant for soil nutrients and water. Leaving too many suckers starves the main stem, leading to smaller bunches.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ (tso lɛ) kɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii babaoo ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ hɔmɔ aye lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bafeɔ bibioo.

english: Why does that green weed with pink flowers make my maize and sorghum stop growing nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi eŋɔli ni fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ pinki yɔɔ mli nɛɛ miiha mi ŋmãa kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ miikpa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, a parasitic plant. Its roots attach directly to the roots of maize or sorghum under the ground, stealing water and food straight from the crop before it can grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Koni aju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛdara.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines up onto tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting them on stakes keeps the leaves healthy and exposed to light, which powers the plant to build large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Kɛ́ awó nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains provides them with necessary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need lots of direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines onto stakes ensures maximum leaf exposure to light and keeps them off the wet ground, resulting in bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo. ni etsĩ wain tsei anaa koni amɛkahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ feɔ wuji.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves near the base usually show that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient, or that excess water in the soil is preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do other farmers say planting groundnuts makes my land richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei dumɔ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni baakwɛ̃ wɔsɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer when the soil is completely dry and the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so roots can safely absorb it. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil under scorching sun can burn the plant's roots and leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai.

english: Why should I space my seeds apart instead of planting several in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala midumɔwui lɛ amli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take up nutrients, water, and sunlight very aggressively, often sprouting faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la waa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots. Excess standing water allows harmful rot-causing fungi and bacteria to multiply and destroy the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ ayi fa babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Extreme heat or dry conditions stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to conserve water and energy rather than growing new fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu aduawai heei

english: Why are small caterpillars attacking the soft leaves inside my young corn stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ tutuaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm feed on the tender, sweet growth points inside young maize leaves because that part contains the highest moisture and nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Ejaakɛ nakai fã lɛ ji he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the field has too much standing water drowning the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or improving field drainage helps the leaves green up again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiho. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii, loo okɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my farmland after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring the soil's fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more plants in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space ensures they grow strong and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eda waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground using stakes gives them full sun and keeps the leaves away from soil-borne diseases, leading to bigger tubers.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tsu nii kɛwo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ená hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni ebaaha helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in wet and shady conditions. Pruning heavy canopy branches lets sunlight and air in to keep pods dry, which stops the fungus from growing.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Afolɔ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ akpa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with small green worms hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli buji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Ani akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft growing leaves inside the maize funnel. Spraying appropriate remedies into the plant center early in the morning helps kill the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ shwie tsei lɛ ateŋ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and making the whole plant stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays prevents the virus from spreading across your field.
ga: Virus ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Providing consistent water during hot periods helps the plant retain flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibii amli.

english: Why did my planted seeds fail to come up out of the soil even after it rained?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ po?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep, if heavy rain forms a hard top layer of soil that shoots cannot break through, or if waterlogged soil rots the seeds before they germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa sũ ni wa ni ŋmeii nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baa. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ha dumɔwui lɛ fite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is sick even if the leaves still look green?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ cacao tso ko kɛji akɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo po?

english: Crop diseases often start underground in the root system before visible signs appear above ground. Checking the base of the trunk or gently inspecting roots for rot helps catch diseases early before the whole tree dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli dani okadii ni anaa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi loo fiofio Kwɛmɔ kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbo. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ hela naa kɛjɛ shishijee. Dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbo

english: Why are some of the branches on my tree drying up while the rest of the tree looks normal?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi egbi ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ?

english: Each underground root supplies water and food to specific branches above ground. If a particular root rots or dies underground, the specific branch connected to it will wither and die first.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã fɛɛ shishifã kɛ nu kɛ niyenii haa tso nine pɔtɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi komɛi fite loo amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Niji ni kɛ lɛ tsa lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why are healthy roots so important for the survival of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni wa he hiaa koni mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi lɛ?

english: Roots act as both an anchor and a feeding mouth for the plant. If the underground roots and their offshoots decay, the tree loses its ability to drink water and absorb nutrients, leading to slow death.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ ŋtayaa kɛ enaabu ni haa niyenii lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu nu ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gboɔ blɛoo.

english: What causes the roots of my crops to become soft and rot underground?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Root rot is usually caused by excessive water sitting around the roots alongside microscopic fungi in the soil. Without proper air in the soil, roots suffocate and decompose.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu babaoo ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafite.

english: Is it safe for me to dig around the base of my tree to check if the roots are healthy?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo tso lɛ shishigbɛ koni makwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lo?

english: Yes, carefully removing a small amount of topsoil near the base with a clean tool allows you to check for discolored or rotting roots without harming the main root system.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋwɛi sũ fioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ni akɛ nibii ni he tse jieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa okwɛɔ kɛji shishifãi lɛ etsake amɛhe loo amɛmiifite ni oyeee shishifãi titri lɛ awui.

english: Should I uproot a cocoa tree if I discover that its roots are rotting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ magbala kookoo tso ko kɛji mina akɛ eshishifãi lɛ miifite?

english: If root rot is severe, completely digging out and safely removing the infected tree prevents the disease from spreading underground through the soil to neighboring healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbo waa lɛ Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaakumɔ shweshweeshwe ni ashɛrɛ ashwie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Can root diseases travel underground from an infected tree to healthy trees nearby?
ga: Ani shishifã hela baanyɛ aya shikpɔŋ shishi kɛjɛ tso ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ mli kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, root diseases easily spread underground when the healthy roots of neighboring trees grow to touch diseased roots, or when infected water moves through the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifã hela gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kpe. aloo kɛ́ nu ni hela emɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What steps can I take to protect my young plants from developing root rot?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Ensuring good soil drainage so water does not gather around plant bases, clearing old infected roots from the field before planting, and using healthy seedlings help prevent root decay.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi nu ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ naa. Jiemɔ shishifãi ni egbɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ saatso lɛ nɔ dani odu. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the roots of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mi-kokoo shishifãi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains can flood the soil and choke the roots by depriving them of oxygen. If water stays logged around the roots for days, it creates ideal conditions for rot to set in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu afu ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji nu ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo Ebaaha ŋmeii aba.

english: How should I clean my farming tools after working near a tree with rotting roots?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsumɔ miŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ ahe beni mitsu nii yɛ tsei ni shishifãi egboi lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Washing tools with clean water and disinfectant after digging near sick plants prevents you from accidentally transferring disease spores in the soil to healthy parts of your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ helai tsu nii yɛ be mli ni okɛtsu nii yɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akaya oŋmɔ lɛ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient it needs to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea around the base of the plants helps them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tso lɛ akwɛ̃ ni eyɛ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans in my farm help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny bacterial pods on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it directly into the soil. When the crop season ends, this extra nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria pods bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves and central whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛteŋ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ

english: These holes are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl into the central funnel of the corn plant to eat the soft inner leaves. Applying recommended insecticides or neem oil solution early in the morning or late evening targets these pests effectively.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ nɛkɛ bu nɛɛ, ni amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, mites, or thrips feeding on the sap, which can also spread viruses to the plant. Spraying the underside of the leaves with soapy water or appropriate pest sprays controls these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo thrips ni yeɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ hela lɛ ashwã tsei amli Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we receive heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long, cutting off oxygen to the roots and encouraging fungal diseases. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji fungal disease lɛ baa Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Do I really need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the damp ground to prevent leaf diseases and exposes more leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more food energy and form bigger tubers underground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi baai lɛ ahe hela naa ni eha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo. ni amɛma ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over easily right before the bunch is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and when the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, strong winds can easily pull the plant down. Using strong wooden props to support the main stem prevents the trees from uprooting before harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ aduawai akui ni tsii kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei kɛba shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa tsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafo dani akpa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when soil moisture changes suddenly between wet and dry, or when the plant lacks nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent daily watering and balanced fertilizer application help flowers stick and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa gbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are my watermelons getting white, dried-out patches on the side facing the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi lɛ? Beni okɛ ohiɛ miikwɛ fã ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is sunscald, which happens when direct, intense sunlight bakes the fruit surface because there aren't enough leaves covering it. Leaving enough leaf canopy over the melons or placing light dry straw over them shields the fruits from intense sun.
ga: Enɛ ji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ha aduawai lɛ hiɛ shã. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa. Shi baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha melon lɛ nɔ loo okɛ jwɛi ni egbi bibioo ko awo nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo melon lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: How should I prepare my farmland before the new planting season begins?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee lɛ aje shishi?

english: Proper land preparation involves clearing weeds, removing dead or diseased plant debris, and loosening the soil. This allows roots to spread easily and helps the soil absorb rain and nutrients for a better harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Tso ni egbo loo hela emɔ lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛkpamɔ kpakpa aba.

english: What can I do to make my cocoa trees yield more pods this year?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-cacao tsei lɛ awo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo afi nɛɛ?

english: To get a higher yield, you need to clear heavy weeds around the base, prune excess branches so sunlight can reach the pods, and apply the right fertilizer and pest treatments at the proper times.
ga: koni onine ashɛ yibii babaoo nɔ Ehe baahia ni ojie jwɛi ni tsii ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ, ni ofolɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does clearing weeds regularly improve the harvest of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them ensures that your crops get all the food they need to grow strong and produce more fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Can an old cocoa farm that is no longer producing well be restored?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ asaa kookoo ŋmɔji momoi ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, old farms can be revived by cutting back overgrown branches through heavy pruning, clearing excess shade, applying fertilizer, and replacing dead or weak trees with healthy seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ aha ŋmɔji momoi lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni afoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Tsumɔ he ni shade yɔɔ lɛ, wo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ato tsei ni egboi loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune or cut branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ loo majie niji kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or unnecessary branches. This opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can flow through, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages new flowers and pods to grow.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is deep pruning, and when is the best time to do it on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ? Ni mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Deep pruning means cutting back major branches to reshape and rejuvenate old or overgrown trees. It is best done during the dry season so the tree can rest and sprout fresh, healthy growth when the rains return.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsɔɔ niji agboi ni ajieɔ koni akɛtsake tso ni egbɔ loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni afee lɛ ehee. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafee enɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni tso lɛ ajɔɔ ehe ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ, ni ekwɛ̃ waa kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How much shade do my mature cocoa trees need to produce good fruit?
ga: Mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ he hulutsoo be enyiɛ he hiaa koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: While young cocoa trees need heavy shade to protect them from heat, mature trees need filtered sunlight to flower properly. Cutting back thick overhead shade trees allows enough light for maximum pod growth.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii po he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shi kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni atsɔ mli koni amɛfɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afolɔ ashwie shi Jiemɔ yiteŋ koni la ni fa bɔ ni sa aha pod lɛ dalɛ babaoo.

english: How do spray treatments help protect my cocoa farm from dying?
ga: Te tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he koni ekagbo lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Chemical or organic treatments target destructive insects like mirids and fungal diseases like black pod. Protecting the leaves and stem keeps the tree healthy enough to feed its developing pods.
