ga: Tsofai loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ kɔɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, tamɔ mirids, kɛ fungal helai, tamɔ black pods lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ abu tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eye ebua ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: This is usually black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in overly damp, shady conditions. Pruning branches to let in sunlight and spraying recommended fungicides helps control it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni edɔ tsɔ ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Ni aaafolɔ tso lɛ mli koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: How does treating the soil before planting help my young crops survive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ dani aduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi?

english: Treating the soil kills harmful insects, worms, and disease-causing fungi hiding underground. It ensures young root systems can establish themselves without being attacked early on.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsamɔ gbeɔ kooloi, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ato amɛhe shi ni tutuamɔ ko bɛ mli mra.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantains bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and sensitive root systems that cannot tolerate direct intense sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture, acting as a natural shield until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During mid-day peak heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up from the soil. The temporary wilting is a natural defence mechanism where the plant closes its leaf pores to conserve water until the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi lɛ mli be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be kukuoo mli ŋmɔtɔ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tsei lɛ ŋaa amɛbaai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ koni nu lɛ ahi mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What will happen to my young maize if I am unable to clear the weeds during the major June and July rains?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mafolɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ June kɛ July mli lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops during heavy rains. If left uncontrolled, weeds will steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from the maize, causing the plants to turn yellow, remain stunted, and produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa mli. Ha tsei lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ Ehi shi lolo ni ewo ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my tomato plants help them grow better during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around plants is called mulching. It traps moisture in the soil by preventing the hot sun from evaporating water quickly, keeps the roots cool, and reduces weed growth around the crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baa shi

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava turning yellow and falling off early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is waterlogged from heavy rain. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves nutrients from older leaves to feed young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni baai bibii lɛ ahi nɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops yield less grain when I plant them on the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific soil nutrients that crop relies on most. It also allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply in the ground year after year, weakening overall plant performance.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ amli lɛ hu faa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nitsumɔ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do fall armyworm caterpillars seem to destroy my maize field faster right after a short dry period in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ oya yɛ be kukuoo ko ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Warm and dry spells during rainy periods speed up the egg-hatching process and lifecycle of fall armyworms. The sudden rise in caterpillar population combined with crop heat stress causes rapid, visible destruction across the farm.
ga: Ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ baaye abua ni fall armyworms lɛ afɔmɔ kɛ amɛshihilɛ aya hiɛ oya. Katɛi ayibɔ ni tee hiɛ trukaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli dɔlɛ he haomɔ lɛ kɛ fitemɔ ni yaa oya ni anaa lɛ ba ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates unpredictably. Under extreme stress, the plant sheds its flowers to preserve energy for basic survival rather than investing in new fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ. yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa shishi Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ o sika kɛ wo yiblii ehehi nɛ a maa hwɔɔ ɔ mi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight for limited sunlight. The plants stretch upward to outgrow their neighbours instead of spending energy developing thick stalks and full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa. Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛdara oya fe amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a hyi nɛ a he wami ɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop black mold inside the sack when I store it immediately after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli beni mijieɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize grains contain high internal moisture. If bagged without being thoroughly sun-dried first, trapped humidity creates ideal conditions for mold and fungi to grow rapidly, spoiling the stored grain.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ mli nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ kotoku lɛ wo kotoku lɛ mli ni okɛ hulu lɛ egbiko lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Trapped moisture lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Enɛ baafite dumɔwui ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees keeps the soil cool and moist, giving young cocoa plants the protection they need until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growing season fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmãa damɔ ehiɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hewalɛ kpakpa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut for planting next season's crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ kɛha tso ni baa lɛ?

english: Select stems from healthy, fully mature plants that are 8 to 18 months old with no signs of disease. Cut pieces from the strong middle portion of the stem that have at least 4 to 6 active buds.
ga: Halamɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 ni hela ko bɛ he lɛ mli tso lɛ shishifã. Okɛ fã ko kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ fɔfɔii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni tsuɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: What is causing small holes in my young corn leaves and powdery waste inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ starch bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding on young leaves inside the stalk. Checking fields early and applying organic solutions like neem oil extract, ash, or recommended insecticides into the central funnel controls them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, sũ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ baakudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots sprouting around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Midumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ Ajieɔ.

english: Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight with the main plant for water and soil nutrients. Keeping only two or three strong shoots of different sizes allows the main plant to produce much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni dalɛi srɔtoi yɔɔ mli lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui ni dara kwraa.

english: How does covering the soil around my garden vegetables with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops heat from drying out the ground, keeps weeds from sprouting, and slowly rots into natural food that keeps the soil rich.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa la ni tsoɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the heat is too intense or when plants do not get enough steady water and soil minerals like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly watered during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu kɛ mineral ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help the crop I plant there next?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop, such as maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall tall sticks and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Ni adu sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in full sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves away from damp soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛɔ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if they were stored in warm or damp places where insects damaged them or moisture spoiled their inner buds. Storing completely dry seeds in sealed containers with clean wood ash keeps them strong until planting time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni kooloi yeɔ amɛ loo ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ. Dumɔwui ni egbi kwraa ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni akɛ tso sũ ni he tse yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi dumɔ be lɛ mli.

english: If I plant seeds saved from my best bean harvest last year, why don't they yield as well as the certified seeds I bought?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ ekɛ yibiiwoo ni tamɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase ni mihe lɛ baa lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength and unique qualities in the next generation. Just like children do not look exactly like one parent, replanted crop seeds inherit mixed traits that reduce their overall yield and quality.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ kɛ sui krɛdɛɛi yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Tamɔ gbekɛbii pɛpɛɛpɛ Amɛjeee amɛfɔlɔi lɛ ateŋ mɔ ko mɔ ko. Dumɔwui ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ baaná sui ni efutu ni baaha yibiiwoo kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba shi.

english: If I plant white maize next to yellow maize, will the harvested cobs end up with mixed seeds?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ masɛi Ani dumɔwui ni efutu yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, maize relies on wind to carry pollen from plant to plant. When pollen from yellow maize lands on white maize plants, the offspring seeds on the cob will inherit traits from both parents, creating mixed-color grains.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ekɛ pollen aya tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ. Beni pollen ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ gbee ŋmãa tsei yɛŋ nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ gboshinii ji sui kɛjɛ fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ adɛŋ. Ewoɔ dumɔwui ni sui sɔrɔtoi yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do some plants in my field grow very tall while others of the same crop stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shwereɔ waa lɛ? Yɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, eyɛ kuku?

english: This happens when using uncertified or mixed seed stock. Certified seeds carry uniform genetic traits so that every plant grows at the same speed, flowers together, and yields predictable harvests.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ odaseyeli loo ni akɛfutu mli miitsu nii. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ su kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei fɛɛ daa oya yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. fɔfɔii kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome ni amɛjieɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ.

english: My cowpea pods look big on the outside, but when I shell them, why are the beans inside small and empty?
ga: Mi-cowpea ŋmɔtɔi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara yɛ kponɔgbɛ. Shi kɛ́ mifolɔ Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: The outer pod grows first like an empty container. If the crop lacks water or nutrients like phosphorus during the seed-filling stage, it cannot produce the energy needed to fill out the seeds inside the pod.
ga: Pod ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ tamɔ tsɛnsi ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs yɛ be mli ni awoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni akɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees have big pods with small beans, while others have smaller pods full of heavy seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni dumɔwui ni tsii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Different cocoa varieties store their harvest energy differently. Some varieties spend energy building thick outer husks, while improved varieties pass more nutrients directly into developing large, heavy beans inside.
ga: Kookoo henɔi srɔtoi toɔ hewalɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli. Henɔi komɛi kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛi amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ amɛmli.

english: Why are my maize cobs missing grains at the very tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa yɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Unfilled tips occur when the plant faces drought, heat, or low nitrogen when the cob is forming. The silks at the tip pollinate last, so if the plant is stressed, it stops feeding those top grains.
ga: Tips ni eyiko mli lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ, loo nitrogen ni faaa mli beni cob lɛ miifee lɛ. Siliki ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ baafee pollination be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji tsei lɛ miihao Ebaakpa nakai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does the produce buyer pay less for my harvested beans even if the bag weighs the same as my neighbor's?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ woɔ mi kɔfi ni mikpaa lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo lɛ? Kɛji akɛ kotoku lɛ tsiimɔ tamɔ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kotoku lɛ nɔŋŋ po.

english: Buyers measure grain density and seed quality, not just bag volume. Beans with large, full, disease-free seeds have better internal quality than light or insect-damaged seeds, making them worth more cash per kilo.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ayibɔ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Jeee kotokui lɛ ayibɔ pɛ he sane ji no. beans with large seeds Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ baaná mligbɛ su ni hi fe dumɔwui ni la loo kooloi fiteɔ lɛ. ni haa ejara wa fe kilogram kome.

english: How do I choose a crop variety that gives heavy yield instead of just big green leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo moŋ fe baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛkɛ?

english: Look for seed varieties bred for a high 'harvest index.' These specialized crop varieties are designed to direct the plant's food into the grain or fruit rather than wasting energy on thick stems and excess leaves.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ Kɛ ‘kpamɔ he okadi’ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ, afee nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ koni amɛkɛ tso lɛ niyenii awo ŋmaa loo aduawai lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ,

english: If I take a branch from a high-yielding cocoa tree and graft it onto a young seedling, will it bear the same good pods?
ga: Kɛ mijie kookoo tso ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ nine ni mikɛkpɛtɛ tso bibioo ko he lɛ, Ani ebaawo yibii kpakpai tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Yes, grafting transfers the exact biological traits of the high-performing parent tree. The new branch will grow and produce the same heavy, high-quality beans as the original parent plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, grafts lɛ gboshinii ji wala yibii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ fɔlɔ tso ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nine hee lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaawo kɔfi yibii ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ shishijee fɔlɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my crop's flowers falling off before producing any pods or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii loo aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers stress from pest attacks or severe drought. If the flowers drop before successfully pollinating, the plant cannot develop the pods that hold your final harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa ko ba tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi dani agbe pollination naa lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee pods ni baahiɛ onaagbee nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava crops get completely destroyed when a disease hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ kwraa kɛ́ hela ko ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop diseases attack essential parts of the plant like the leaves and roots, preventing the crop from taking in food and water. Without these nutrients, the plant rots or dries up completely before harvest.
ga: Tse helai tutuaa tso lɛ fãi ni he hiaa tamɔ baai kɛ shishifãi, ni no haaa tso lɛ aye niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagboi loo amɛbaagbi kwraa dani abaakpa.

english: Can I use cuttings from a diseased cassava plant as seeds for my next planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni afo lɛ atsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha midumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: No, planting stems from sick crops transfers the disease directly into your new soil, causing your new crops to get infected right from the start.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni jɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oshikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Okɛ hela awo oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: Why do diseases spread so quickly from one cassava plant to the rest of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Diseases are often spread by insects, wind, rain splashes, or contaminated farm tools, allowing a sickness on just one plant to easily reach neighboring healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso kome pɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe oya.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crops are getting sick before they get destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela mɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ dani amɛfite?

english: Watch for early warning signs like leaf yellowing, unusual spots, leaf curling, or sudden wilting even when the soil has moisture.
ga: Kwɛmɔ mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, hei ni yɔɔ srɔto, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo trukaa ni shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: What is an improved crop variety, and why should I plant it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: An improved variety is a crop carefully developed by plant breeders to resist common farm diseases, survive tough weather, and yield more food than traditional varieties.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji tsei ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe blema ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ

english: How do plant breeders make new cassava varieties that don't easily catch diseases?
ga: Te mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee tɛŋŋ amɛfee ŋmei henɔi heei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɛɛ amɔ amɛ oya?

english: Breeders select strong plants that naturally resist diseases and cross-breed them with high-yielding plants over several years to combine the best traits into one new variety.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ halaa tsei ni wa ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ni amɛkɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo fɔɔ amɛ yɛ afii babaoo mli koni amɛkɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ afee ekome ni amɛfee tso hee kome.

english: Why are there so many different varieties of cassava developed in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ afee ŋmeii srɔtoi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Different regions in Ghana have different soils, rainfall patterns, and disease risks, so researchers create specific varieties tailored to thrive in each environment and for different food uses.
ga: Ghana kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi, bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa, kɛ helai ahe osharai. No hewɔ lɛ niiamlitaolɔi feɔ tsei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hei srɔtoi kɛ niyenii srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: How do I benefit from buying planting materials developed by research institutes like CSIR?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná sɛɛnamɔ kɛjɛ dumɔ nibii ni niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei tamɔ CSIR fee lɛ ahemɔ mli?

english: Planting materials from research institutes are clean, disease-free, and tested to ensure high harvests, giving your farm a healthier start compared to unverified seeds.
ga: Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii kɛjɛɔ niiamlitaomɔhe lɛ he tse, helai bɛ mli, ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo. Ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some cassava varieties mature faster while others take over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ nɔ ni fe afi lɛ?

english: Plant breeders design different varieties for different needs; early-maturing types are bred to produce tubers in 6 to 9 months, while late-maturing types take up to 15 months to fully grow.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ tsei srɔtoi koni amɛkɛtsu hiamɔ nii srɔtoi ahe nii. Akwɛɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ nyɔji 15 dani amɛshɛɔ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why am I getting smaller cassava harvests even though I use the same farmland every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ ŋmei nɔ yibii babaoo nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii daa afi moŋ?

english: Continuous farming on the same plot exhausts soil nutrients and allows crop diseases to build up in the soil, which reduces plant growth and tuber size over time.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsei ahelai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛtuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests and soil diseases to build up in that area.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny organisms on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, acting as a natural food supply for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Excess water in heavy rain starves cassava roots of air and encourages destructive fungi to grow, causing the tubers to decay underground.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baagboi.

english: Extreme heat dries out tomato pollen, which prevents flowers from being fertilized; when a flower cannot make seeds, the plant drops it to save water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha tomato pollen lɛ agbi. ni tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ naa koni ekawo fɔmɔ nii. Kɛ fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ Tsei shwieɔ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why should I cut off the extra suckers growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: Extra suckers compete directly with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients, leading to smaller, weaker bunches of fruit if they are not reduced.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ ajieee lɛ shi.

english: Why do I need to push tall wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can create energy, which is then sent down into the soil to build large, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight, so larger shade trees are needed to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ he miihia koni akɛbu kokoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before any pods grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when under stress from dry weather, poor nutrients, or insect attack so they can save energy to keep the main tree alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miihao amɛ. niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Koni akɛ hewalɛ ato koni akɛkwɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough, meaning they can soak up water and soil food much faster than cultivated farm crops unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ja ojie amɛ kɛjɛ ohe kɛtsɔ hiɛ.

english: Is watering my young cocoa plants with a bucket enough to keep them alive during the dry season?
ga: Ani mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni mikɛ baagi baawo amɛ nu lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Bucket watering helps young seedlings survive extreme heat, but cocoa trees need deep soil moisture to thrive. Combining light watering with mulching—covering the soil with dry leaves—keeps the roots cool and preserves moisture much longer.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tanki lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ he miihia kookoo tsei koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nu fioo ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fata he—ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ—eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be babaoo.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are dying from lack of water or from disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miigboi yɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli loo hela hewɔ?

english: When cocoa trees lack water, their leaves wilt, turn crisp brown at the edges, and dry up from the bottom leaves first. Disease usually causes dark patches on pods, swollen stems, or yellow leaves even when the soil is wet.
ga: Beni nu bɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi. Baai lɛ ashishi baatsɔ asarasu ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni egbi kɛjɛ baai lɛ ashishi klɛŋklɛŋ Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, ŋmeii lɛ efuu, loo baai lɛ ŋmɔŋ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: How can I protect my young cocoa farm from being destroyed by the dry Harmattan winds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ he koni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ akafite lɛ?

english: Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides a natural shield against dry winds, while spreading dry grass or leaves around the base of the trees keeps the soil from drying out.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ naa. be mli ni egbɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi eshwaa Tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: What does fertilizer actually do to help my cocoa trees yield more?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa yɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ? Koni eye ebua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer provides essential food that soil loses over time. It strengthens the tree's roots and leaves, helping it produce bigger pods, resist diseases, and recover faster after harvesting.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa pods wuji, eteɔ shi ewoɔ helai ni ehiɛɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my cocoa farm so it does not waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo kookoo ŋmɔ mli koni ekafite?

english: Apply fertilizer at the start of the rainy season when the soil is moist. If you apply it during dry weather, the plants cannot absorb it, and if applied during heavy downpours, the rain will wash it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Kɛ okɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ. ni kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Nugbɔ lɛ baaho lɛ.

english: Can I use chicken manure or decomposed plant waste instead of chemical fertilizer for my cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei loo tsei ni egbo ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ atsu nii yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli kɛha kookoo lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, well-rotted animal manure and compost add rich nutrients to the soil, help the ground hold water better, and improve long-term soil health for young cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo baa sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ aya hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa tree turning yellow even when the soil feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is flooded with excess water, which prevents the roots from breathing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny cocoa pods dry up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni egbi ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani eda lɛ?

english: This condition, known as cherelle wilt, happens when the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect attack, causing it to drop pods it cannot afford to feed.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt lɛ baa kɛji hɔmɔ miigba tsei anaa. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Enɛ haa ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ he ni enyɛɛɛ ena niyenii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce plenty of flowers but very few actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi anɔkwa ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen between flowers. If your farm lacks shade or leaf litter on the ground where these insects live, flowers will fall off without turning into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ. Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ bɛ hulutsoo loo baa ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Does cocoa grow differently across the border in neighboring countries like Togo compared to here in Ghana?
ga: Ani esoro bɔ ni aduɔ kookoo yɛ husui asɛɛ yɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tamɔ Togo lɛ amli kɛ akɛto Ghana he?

english: Cocoa grows similarly in both places because the soil type and weather patterns are almost identical, though yields can differ based on local farming practices and access to fertilizer or water.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ nakai nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ miihe afee ekome. Eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ akutso lɛ mli okwaayeli nifeemɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni anáa lɛ naa moŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees creates a cool, humid environment that helps the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo ashiɔ cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni haa cocoa shishifãi lɛ daa lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor root drainage due to heavy rains. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers or well-rotted manure helps restore leaf color and improves the maize's growth and cob development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ ehiii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest, and why do they spoil if left in wet ground too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? Ni mɛni hewɔ egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. Leaving tubers in waterlogged soil starves the roots of oxygen, causing soil fungi to break them down and rot the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ, be mli ni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ ni ehaa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines with wood instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on as many leaves as possible to generate energy for the underground tuber. Lifting vines off the warm ground reduces disease infection from soil fungi and allows the plant to produce much larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha amɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Should I let all the shoot suckers grow around my main plantain stem or cut some away?
ga: Esa akɛ maha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe. Mi plantain tso titri lɛ loo mifolɔ eko?

english: You should trim away excess suckers because they steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller bunches. Maintaining a system of one main fruiting stem, one medium follower sucker, and one small shoot ensures continuous large harvests.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine akɛni amɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmeii bibii Ekwɛɔ yibiiwoo tso titri kome gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔ Mɔ kome ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ lɛ sucker Ni ŋmeii bibii kome haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ, ni da waa baa.

english: Why am I finding small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillar droppings inside the centers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on tender leaf whorls inside the plant stem. Applying appropriate neem extracts or recommended insecticides directly into the plant whorls early in the morning stops them before they ruin the entire crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ. Ni akɛ neem mli nu ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass help them grow better during dry spells?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔle he lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ mi-vegetables lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with organic mulch acts as a barrier that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating into the air. As the dry grass decays over time, it also breaks down into organic nutrients that feed your crops.
ga: Organic mulch tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni haa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Beni jwɛi ni egbi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ hu fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the farm after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize consumes heavy amounts of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it low in nutrients. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix nitrogen naturally from the air into the soil through their roots, restoring fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi baa Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛsaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni ekɛ fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Why do my pepper and tomato crops yield small and poor fruits when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crowding plants together forces them to compete intensely for ground water, soil nutrients, and air movement. Giving plants adequate space ensures each stem gets full sunlight and sufficient food to produce larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Tsei ni fa babaoo lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ waa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la ni fa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my fresh tomato seedlings suddenly fall over and rot right at the ground surface after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui heei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as damping-off, caused by soil-borne fungal pathogens that multiply in overly wet and shaded seedbeds. Reducing nursery watering, exposing seedbeds to gentle morning sun, and keeping soil well-drained prevents the fungi from destroying the young stems.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni fɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui akutsei ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ nɔ ni abaajie lɛ kpo Dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo atsɔɔ leebi hulu la ni tsoɔ blɛoo lɛ Ni akwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water in the hot sun. It is the plant's natural way of conserving moisture, but if the leaves stay rolled up even in the morning, it means your crop is suffering from severe water stress.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi po lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are my tomato plants remaining very short and refusing to produce flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛwooo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water consistently, their root systems cannot expand to absorb soil nutrients. This causes stunted growth and forces the plant to conserve energy instead of producing flowers or fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ daa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi loo aduawai.

english: Why are my young citrus trees dropping all their small fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Ani ooogbee shi dani oshɛ dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu he?

english: Fruit trees drop their young fruits when water becomes scarce. The tree naturally sacrifices its fruit to conserve remaining water and save its own life during dry periods.
ga: Yibii tsei shwieɔ yibii bibii kɛji nu faaa. Tso lɛ kɛ eyibii shaa afɔle yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛhiɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ mli ni ehere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli.

english: Is it harmful to water my crops in the middle of the day when the sun is very strong?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ aaashwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ gbi mli be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yes, watering under strong sunlight causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching the roots. Additionally, water droplets left on the leaves can heat up and burn the plant tissues.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ adɔ ni eshã tso lɛ mli fãji.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are dying from too little water or too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ miigbo yɛ nu fioo loo nu babaoo hewɔ?

english: If pepper plants lack water, their leaves wilt, feel thin, and dry out. If they receive too much water, the leaves turn yellow, drop off, and the roots rot because wet, soggy soil prevents them from breathing.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ pepper tso lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi, amɛbaanu he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛbaagbi kɛji amɛná nu babaoo. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe.

english: At what stage of growth do my vegetable crops need the most water?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli mi-vegetables lɛ he hiaa nu fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli?

english: Vegetable crops need the most water during flowering and fruit formation. Lack of water during this stage causes flowers to fall off and fruits to remain small, cracked, or dry.
ga: Nu he hiaa aduawai tsei fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛwoɔ yibii. Nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi bibii, amɛgbala loo amɛgbi.

english: Why do crops like cassava and sorghum survive dry weather much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cassava and sorghum have deep root systems and natural mechanisms to store moisture or slow down growth during dry spells, whereas maize has shallow roots that dry out quickly without regular water.
ga: Cassava kɛ sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli loo amɛhaa amɛdaraa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni egbiɔ oya ni nu he ehiaaa daa.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I cover the soil around them with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ sũ wo amɛhe lɛ? Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, shades the earth and traps moisture so it doesn't evaporate quickly. This keeps the roots cool and moist, allowing the crop to absorb water steadily.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli bɔni afee ni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛheɔ nu.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wilt and fall over right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as transplanting shock. Moving seedlings damages their delicate feeder roots, making it hard for them to drink water immediately. Moving them in the late afternoon and watering right away helps them recover overnight.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni haa niyenii lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaanu nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ shwane mli Ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waa nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: If my crops wilt completely during a dry period, will they grow back normal if I start watering them again?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli hu? Kɛ mibɔi nu shwiemɔ ekoŋŋ Ani amɛbaakwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa?

english: If the wilting is mild, crops can bounce back once watered. However, if the plant has dried out to the point where its internal stems are brittle, the tissues are permanently damaged and the crop will not recover fully.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli wa waaa Tsei lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji tso lɛ gĩ kɛyashɛ he ni emli tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Fãji lɛ baafite kwraa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiɛ ekpãŋ kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and shriveling up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight or heat without shade. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the plants cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ gbɛ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantain, ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tso masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high, when watering is irregular, or when the soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus required for fruit development.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni niyenii titrii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops look soft and wilted in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. They temporarily droop to conserve moisture and usually recover when the sun sets.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaa shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe feɔ shoo kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves return to a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the field over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crop roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant matter, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes in them with small dirt-like powder inside the plant central core?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ muji bibii ni tamɔ muji lɛ? Ani eyɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central funnel of the plant. Applying recommended treatments directly into the funnel early kills the caterpillars before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ woɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baagbe ŋmei lɛ dani afite lɛ waa.

english: Does leaving weeds to grow close to my crops harm them or do they just grow alongside each other?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui loo amɛmiida kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds actively compete with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Leaving weeds unchecked weakens your crops and significantly lowers your total yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi ni okwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Why do I need to put long bamboo sticks next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ awo ŋmei tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need support to lift their leaves upward toward sunlight. Maximum sunlight exposure helps the plant generate energy to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Hulu la ni anáa babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare main stem. You can also carefully dig around the base of one sample plant to inspect the size of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shi tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ni efee nɔ ko. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Obaanyɛ okwɛ tso kome ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ona bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ dara ha.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots that cannot pump water fast enough to replace what high heat evaporates from their leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a cooler microclimate that protects tender seedlings until their roots fully establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛto dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when rain falls continuously for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy, continuous rain washes essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil away from roots and waterlogs the ground, preventing roots from breathing. Without nitrogen and oxygen, the leaves cannot produce bright green chlorophyll.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu Kɛji nitrogen kɛ oxygen bɛ Baai lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ afee chlorophyll ni ji eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when exposed to stress, such as extreme midday heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. The plant conserves energy by dropping flowers until growing conditions become stable.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛna nɔnyɛɛi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni amɛdalɛ shihilɛi lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop producing lots of thick green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii ni mli tse babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical nitrogen fertilizer encourages cowpeas to focus energy purely on leafy foliage instead of flowering. Cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air, so extra nitrogen tricks the plant into staying vegetative.
ga: Tsofai ni ji nitrogen ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ woɔ tsina ŋmei hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ama tso lɛ baai pɛ nɔ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefɔ lɛ, Cowpeas lɛ ŋmɛɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ni yaa hiɛ lɛ lakaa tso lɛ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: As a cassava plant grows past its ideal harvest window, it stops storing soft starch in its roots and starts converting stored energy into tough wood fibers to support the heavy stems above ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara fe ŋmaakpamɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ Ekpaa ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni ebɔi hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsakemɔ ewoɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli koni ekɛfi tso ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up completely toward the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi kwraa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing vines are a natural signal that the yam plant has finished its seasonal growth cycle above ground and shifted all its remaining food energy downward into the underground tuber for storage.
ga: Wein tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ egbe ebe mli dalɛ be lɛ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ aya shi kɛya ŋmeii lɛ amli koni akɛto.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning brown and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe lɛ?

english: Lower leaves often curl and spot when soil-borne fungal spores splash onto them during watering or rain. As tomato plants direct energy to growing fruit, older lower leaves lose strength and become vulnerable to fungal infections.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ni anaa kɛ́ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie amɛnɔ yɛ nu loo nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ mli. Baai ni darako lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Why do my garden eggs get small dark spots and rot while still attached to the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Ni fitemɔ be mli ni ekpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by fungal fruit rot, which spreads easily in humid, overcrowded farms, or by a lack of calcium in the soil during fruit development. Spacing plants properly allows air to dry wet leaves and reduces rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei ko ni fiteɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. aloo kɛjɛ calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ yɛ he ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii aba shi.

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they rely on shallow root systems near the topsoil. When heavy bunches of fruit make the top heavy, rain-softened soil can no longer hold the shallow roots in place.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ e hɛ fɔɔ sisi fã ko nɛ e mi kuɔ we nɛ e kɛ zugba a yi mi kpɔ ɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, amɛyitsei lɛ feɔ shwiili. Shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right when they look ready for market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ amɛfee klalo akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when a dry soil period is immediately followed by sudden heavy watering or rain. The internal leaves absorb water rapidly and expand faster than the firm outer leaves can stretch, forcing the head to burst.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai ni edɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni no haa bulb lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They require shade trees or fast-growing shade crops like plantains above them to shield their leaves from sunburn and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains. Bɔni afee ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I prune the bushy extra branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to reach the main trunk where cocoa pods form. Proper airflow reduces humidity around the pods, preventing fungal diseases like black pod while directing energy into growing healthy fruit.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso titri lɛ he ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ tsiɔ naa, yɛ be mli ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa aduawai lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it that when I plant my cassava stem cuttings upside down, they fail to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ matsɔ ŋmei nine agbo ko nɔ matsɔ ŋwɛi?

english: Cassava stem cuttings have buds that point upward. When planted upside down, the new shoots must bend completely around to reach light, wasting precious plant energy that should go toward establishing strong roots and building tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ abɔle ŋmeii heei lɛ fɛɛ koni la lɛ abote mli. Efiteɔ tsei ahewalɛ ni jara wa ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii koni akɛwo shishifãi ni wa ni afee bulbs lɛ.

english: Does placing tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants actually help produce larger yams under the ground?
ga: Tso tsei kakadaji ni akɛwoɔ mli Ani mi-sweet potato lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛ sweet potato agbo aba shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yes, staking allows yam vines to climb high and capture maximum sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to produce plant food, which travels down into the root system to build bigger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking haa yucca wain tso lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni enáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ tsei niyenii. Enɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize often indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, and applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant stay green and grow full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. Ni kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara kɛyashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do agricultural officers encourage me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi hewalɛ koni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas fix nitrogen gas from the air into the soil through their roots. This natural plant food feeds the nearby maize plants and improves the fertility of your farm without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii saa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɔmɔ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why do my maize seeds sometimes rot in the soil if I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rainfall often heats up dry soil, and if followed by a dry hot spell, the seeds begin germinating but then lack enough moisture to survive, leading them to wither and rot underground before emerging.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ. ni kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ shi amɛnaŋ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa egboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture is unpredictable. Heat stress causes the flowers to dry out before pollination happens, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Dɔlɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛwoɔ amɛmli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai efeee.

english: Why do my hot pepper plants drop leaves and stop growing when rainwater collects and stays on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ beni nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need oxygen from the soil to survive. When water sits on the land without proper drainage, the roots drown, rot, and cannot feed the plant, causing leaves to drop and growth to stall.
ga: Pepper shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdalɛ kpaa.

english: Why should I select plantain suckers with narrow, thin leaves instead of ones with broad leaves when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala plantain tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baai lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe nɔ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Suckers with narrow, spear-shaped leaves have strong underground bulbs that focus energy on growing new roots after planting. Broad-leaf suckers spend too much energy supporting old leaves, making them slower to establish and weaker overall.
ga: Suckers ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ lance lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni mli wa ni kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ shishifãi heei ni amɛduɔ lɛ ahe nii beni amɛdu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nuɔ nii lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ baa momoi lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ haa etswaa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest hours to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛtsi nu naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water crops early in the morning. Watering in the afternoon causes much of the water to evaporate in the heat before roots can soak it up, and wet leaves in hot sun can burn.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsei lɛ nu leebi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la yɛ latsaa be mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni baai ni efɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã.

english: What will happen to my pepper plants if I pump too much water onto the field every day?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi?

english: Excess water fills up air pockets in the soil, which smothers the roots. Without air, the roots rot, causing the plant's leaves to turn yellow, wilt, and eventually die.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ baafite. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ wuɔfɔ, amɛgbiɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no big trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi koko tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that scorch under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains protects the young cocoa from strong sun and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the soil so you water less often, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why are the flowers falling off my garden pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high temperature stress or irregular watering. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to save its energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ ato.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and drop their leaves even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛbaai miiho eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil-borne diseases like bacterial wilt. The disease attacks the water pipes inside the plant stem, blocking water from reaching the leaves even if the soil has plenty of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tamɔ bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tutuaa nu paipii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shɛɛɛ baai lɛ ahe eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves during dry periods to reduce its water needs. This helps the plant protect its underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛba nu he hiamɔ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ abu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry during a drought?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant's roots and waste your money because the crop cannot use it.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Weeds are wild, aggressive plants naturally adapted to local soil conditions. They quickly absorb available water and food faster than crop plants, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni tsakeɔ ehe ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ.

english: Why should I bury or cover the plastic water pipes I lay on my farm instead of leaving them on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafu plastic nu paipii ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo maha nɔ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving pipes exposed on the ground allows the strong sun to weaken and crack the plastic quickly. Covering them with soil protects them from intense heat, accidental damage from weeding tools, and livestock, making your irrigation system last much longer.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi paipii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni naa wa lɛ afee mlɛo, ni ebaaha plastic lɛ akumɔ oya. Mulching baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Nibii ni akɛkwɛɔ jwɛi nɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ yɛ oshara mli lɛ baanyɛ aha o-irrigation system lɛ ahi shi be babaoo.

english: Why do the tiny holes in my drip irrigation pipes keep getting blocked, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-drip paipi lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Drip holes usually get blocked by fine dirt, sand, or algae in your water source. Installing a cleanable mesh or screen filter at the main water source will catch these particles before they enter your pipes and keep the water flowing freely to your crop roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muji, ŋã, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ onu jɛɛhe lɛ tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ okɛ mesh loo screen filter ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii wo onu jɛɛhe titri lɛ mli lɛ, ebaamɔ nɛkɛ nibii bibii nɛɛ dani amɛbote opaipii lɛ amli. ni ehaa nu hoɔ oya kɛyaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: What is the best way to lay out my irrigation pipes on a sloping land so all my crops get equal water?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ? Bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Pipes should be laid across the slope following the natural contour of the land rather than straight down the hill. This prevents water from rushing to the bottom, ensuring equal water pressure and even watering for crops at both the top and bottom of your farm.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ paipii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ paipii lɛ ama gɔŋ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ baatsi nu naa koni ekaho kɛya shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ mli tsiimɔ feɔ ekome kɛ nu po ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ shishi lɛ.

english: What is the difference between using a drip irrigation system and a sprinkler system for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ teŋ?

english: Drip irrigation drops water directly onto the soil at the roots of each plant, saving water and reducing weed growth. Sprinklers spray water over the air like natural rain, covering larger areas quickly but losing more water to evaporation under hot sun.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu baa shi ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shweremɔ baa shi. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ. Ehaa he ko ni da oya Shi nu babaoo laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Which crops benefit most from drip irrigation compared to sprinklers?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei náa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he sɛɛ fe fɛɛ kɛ akɛto nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, and cucumbers benefit greatly from drip irrigation because keeping their leaves dry prevents fungal diseases. Fast-growing leafy greens or maize often do better with sprinkler systems that cover wider soil areas.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ kukumba náa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ he sɛɛ waa. Ejaakɛ baai lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ha shikpɔŋ ni da nɔ lɛ nɔ.
