english: Is it better to irrigate my crops in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Watering in the hot afternoon causes much of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it, and droplets left on leaves can cause severe heat stress or burn marks.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo loo shãa ni naa wa aba.

english: How can I tell if my crops are receiving too much water from my sprinklers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ mi-sprinklers lɛ amli?

english: If crops receive too much water, their leaves often turn pale yellow, growth slows down, and the soil stays continuously waterlogged. Excess water starves roots of air and causes root rot, so you should reduce spraying time if you notice these signs.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ blɛoo Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu lolo be fɛɛ be. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ be ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi kɛji ona okadii nɛɛ.

english: Why does heavy sprinkler spraying make the top layer of my farm soil wash away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sprinkler ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When sprinklers spray large droplets too forcefully, the water hits the bare ground hard and breaks up the soil structure. If the soil cannot absorb water fast enough, the excess runs off across the surface, carrying away fertile topsoil and fertilizers.
ga: Beni tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu agboi anɔ waa tsɔ Nu lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ waa ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔne lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa Nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Efoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ.

english: How can getting electricity on my farm help me grow crops better throughout the year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ sarawa hewalɛ ni mikɛaaha miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Electricity allows you to power electric water pumps efficiently to lift water from wells or rivers into irrigation pipes, enabling you to farm continuously during the dry season when rain is scarce.
ga: Srawa hewalɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ srawa hewalɛ nu pɔmp ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni ewo nu kɛjɛ nu ŋshɔ loo faa mli kɛya nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ he paipi mli. Ehaa onyɛɔ oyaa okwaayeli lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo lɛ.

english: Can I use solar power to run my water pump if my farm is far from electricity lines?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ hulu hewalɛ atsu nu pɔmp he nii? Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtswaa la lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ

english: Yes, solar-powered pumps use sunlight to pump water into elevated tanks during the day. This stored water can then flow naturally through your drip or sprinkler pipes without requiring expensive grid electricity or petrol fuel.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu pɔmpii kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛpompɔ nu kɛyaa tanki ko ni nɔ kwɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni ato nɛɛ baanyɛ atsɔ paipii ni hoɔ nu loo tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ anɔ atsɔ ehe ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ srawa hewalɛ loo pɛtrol ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show that the crop is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea early in the season keeps the leaves green so the plant can make big, full corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmãa agboi ni eyi obɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my farmland better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth as free food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) blocks the harsh hot sun from drying out the earth, keeps moisture in the soil longer, and stops weeds from popping up around your crops.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need lots of direct sunlight on their leaves to produce food that grows big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, catches more sunlight, and keeps leaves safe from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ jɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Na hulu la babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ he jɔɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain tree, they fight with the main plant for nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots and leaving only two or three allows the main tree to produce a much bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dumɔwu kome Ekɛ tsei ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ baawu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tsei 2-3 pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei niji ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. Keeping the water supply steady and protecting young plants from extreme heat helps the flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Nu ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tomato he.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground if left in heavy waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy clay soil stays soaked with water for too long, air cannot reach the cassava roots, causing harmful soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers. Planting on raised ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from tender leaves and passing viruses to the plant. Spraying neem oil or organic insect sprays early helps protect the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo organic insect spray baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when planted in open sunshine without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that dry out easily under harsh tropical sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a living canopy that keeps seedlings cool until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ baa.

english: The first rain often tricks farmers because a long dry spell usually follows before the main rainy season truly starts. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up and die from heat before the next rain comes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ lakaa okwaafoi ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ latsaa lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct sunlight. They require shade crops like plantains or cassava when young to protect them from intense heat and conserve soil moisture until their canopy develops.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ he. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca beni amɛdarako lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baaje shishi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing rot and disease while maximizing leaf exposure to sunlight.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbele amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Tsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai anaa yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ naa hulu la fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many suckers compete with the mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce big, healthy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ tsei krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni he wa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When they die, this acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ amɛgboi Ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ nitrogen tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to plant my maize right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or a long dry spell before the main rains fully start. Planting too early can cause your seeds to germinate and then wither in the dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why are small holes appearing in my maize leaves with caterpillars inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Kɛ ŋmei ko yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the growing center of the maize plant to eat tender leaves before they fully open.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ koni eye baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kwraa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the daytime even when the soil has enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ amɛ moŋ lɛ? Ani nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the tubes inside the plant stem, preventing water from traveling from the roots up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my farm chemicals in the afternoon when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ tsofai yɛ ŋmɔji amli shwane mli beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes liquid chemicals to evaporate quickly into the air before they work. Intense sunlight mixed with chemicals can also scorch and damage crop leaves.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛtsuɔ nii. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni akɛ tsofai efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei ahe baai.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants age beyond maturity, they begin using stored starch to build tough fibers for stem growth, making the roots tough and unpleasant to eat.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ eye fe afii pɔtɛɛ ko. Kɛkɛ ni amɛbɔi ŋmeii ni ato lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii ni wa kɛha ŋmeii ni miida. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhiɛ kpaaa nɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my pepper plants before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. It is the plant's way of conserving energy to survive harsh conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Eji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive their early years. Direct sunlight burns the delicate leaves and dries out the soil, so keeping shade trees or planting plantains around them protects them until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Ehe lɛ baabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen. When there is not enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant moves what little food it has to the new growing leaves at the top, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains flood my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When standing water covers your field for too long, it cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing rot and harmful fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but no fruits come out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers must be pollinated by wind or insects to set fruit. Extreme heat, drought, or giving the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer can cause flowers to drop off before they can grow into tomatoes.
ga: Esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii atsɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo yibii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ni akɛhaa tso lɛ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to manufacture energy for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground so leaves receive sunlight and are protected from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit or irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant draw calcium to the growing fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛgbalaa calcium kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts or cowpeas helps my soil for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dumɔ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant naturally decomposes, that trapped nitrogen feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it better to plant narrow-leaf sword suckers instead of broad-leaf suckers when starting a plantain farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ moŋ fe baai bibii ni mli kwɔ beni ajeɔ plantain ŋmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Sword suckers have strong root bases and food reserves stored inside, allowing them to grow faster into strong fruiting plants. Broad-leaf suckers are weaker and take much longer to produce good yield.
ga: Klante ni shwieɔ nu lɛ yɛ shishitoo ni wa kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ emli. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni he wa. Broad leaf suckers lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which attack the tender growing center of corn. Targeting the funnel early with recommended sprays or neem extracts stops them before they destroy the growing plant.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni miida blɛoo lɛ. Ni akɛ neem spray loo nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ maa funnel lɛ nɔ mra Ekpaa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to fit more plants in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak, skinny stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the stalks are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of a maize plant usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves whatever food it has left to the young, top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: How can I tell that my maize is dry enough on the farm to harvest without it spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni efiteee?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and paper-dry. You can also pull a kernel from the cob and check the tip; if a tiny black spot or 'black layer' has formed where it connects to the cob, the maize has stopped growing and is fully mature.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbi tamɔ wolo lɛ. Obaanyɛ ojie ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli hu ni okwɛ naagbee lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii diji bibii loo ‘ŋmeii diji’ je kpo yɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee yɛ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni egbɔ.

english: Why do people say planting beans on my farm will help my other crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? Mine grows better?

english: Beans and other legumes are unique because their roots trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the bean plants die and decay, they leave this natural fertilizer behind in the soil, which helps feed crops like maize planted after them.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ srɔto ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmeii tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my bean pods burst open on their own and scatter seeds on the ground before I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean pods lɛ mli gbalaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbɛɔ dumɔwui amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Bean pods naturally crack and pop open when they become extremely dry in the hot sun. This is the plant's natural way of spreading its seeds, so you must harvest the pods as soon as they turn brown before they get too dry.
ga: Bean pods lɛ baagbala ni amɛgbele yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛgbi waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ egbɛɔ dumɔwui eshwaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okpa ŋmeii lɛ kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ, dani amɛgbi tsɔ.

english: Why do my ginger roots start to turn soft and rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ginger shishifãi lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Ginger roots rot when water collects and stays around the roots for too long. Ginger needs loose, raised soil beds that drain water easily, because waterlogged soil attracts fungal diseases that destroy the underground rhizomes.
ga: Ginger shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ginger he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni nɔ kwɔ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do I know that the ginger under the ground is ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ?

english: Ginger is ready for harvest when the green shoots and leaves above the ground naturally turn yellow, dry up, and fall over. This happens about 8 to 10 months after planting, showing that the roots have grown to their full size.
ga: Ginger efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbi, ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Enɛ baa mli aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ edara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping young green fruits off the branches before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho yibii bibii ni ji eŋɔli kɛmiijɛ eniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young oranges fall off early when the tree experiences water stress during dry periods or when pests like fruit flies lay eggs in the soft skin. Providing steady water and managing pests prevents the tree from shedding its young fruit.
ga: Akɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. aloo beni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ baatsi tso yibii bibii ni woɔ yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje kpo.

english: Why do some orange trees take many years to fruit while others produce fruit very quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ citrus tsei komɛi heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ yibii oya waa lɛ?

english: Trees grown directly from an orange seed take 5 to 7 years to produce fruit because they grow naturally slow. Trees that are grafted—where a branch from a mature producing tree is joined to a young stem—will start bearing fruit in just 2 to 3 years.
ga: Tsei ni jɛɔ ŋmei dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwoɔ yibii ejaakɛ amɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli amɛdaraa blɛoo. Tsei ni akɛwo tso ni egbɔ lɛ mli—he ni akɛ tso nine ni jɛ tso ni egbɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tso nine bibioo nɔ lɛ—jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop white mold and small insects after I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Grains develop mold and attract pests like weevils if they are put into bags while still holding dampness. Crops must be thoroughly sun-dried until the seeds are hard before storage, because trapped moisture creates the perfect home for mold and insects.
ga: Ŋmãa lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaagbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku lɛ mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baafee shiŋŋ dani akɛto. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii.

english: Why do crops planted on the same day in my farm mature at different times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ?

english: Crops mature at different rates because different spots in a field have varying levels of soil fertility, moisture, and sunlight shade. Plants growing in rich, well-watered soil will grow faster and mature earlier than plants in poorer spots.
ga: Tsei daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Yɛ otii srɔtoi ahewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulutsoo kɛ hulu la srɔtoi. Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu kpakpa nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni ohiafoi yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from larger trees or plantains because direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their root system is deep enough to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ amli aba mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Flower drop happens when the tree experiences stress from dry spells, a shortage of nutrients in the soil, or attacks from insect pests like mirids that feed on the flower stems.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ iris ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil, which causes the maize plant to move its remaining nutrients to the upper leaves to keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young corn plants before the cobs appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which lay their eggs in the central whorl of young maize so the caterpillars can feed on the soft growing tissues before the cob forms.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ aye ŋmãa ni miida blɛoo lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ afee.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in waterlogged soil that lacks air; planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can receive full sunlight, allowing the plant to make more food and produce larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots coming up around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers allows them to steal water, light, and soil nutrients from the main tree, which leads to smaller bunches and weaker stems.
ga: Suckers babaoo ni ashiɔ lɛ baaha amɛju nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ feɔ bibii, ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ hu gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning thick and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curling is commonly caused by a plant virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat and uneven moisture in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ mli

english: Why is it better for me to water my pepper plants early in the morning instead of during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ haa nu leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning gives roots time to soak up moisture before the hot sun evaporates it, and helps prevent fungal diseases caused by wet leaves sitting in the sun.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛjieɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛmli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa ni efɔ ni ta hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why is the top of my farmland soil dry and hard, but when I dig down it is still very wet and muddy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ akumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lolo ni eyɛ muji?

english: Sun and wind dry out the surface layer of your soil very quickly, while heavy soil underneath traps water longer. Even when the top looks firm, the ground below can stay soft and soaked for days after heavy rains.
ga: Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ gbiɔ oya waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni wa moŋ Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi blɛoo ni edɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: How can I test if the ground on my farm is dry enough underneath to start land preparation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ?

english: Dig a small hole about hand-depth and pick up a handful of the lower soil. Squeeze it into a ball; if it stays wet and sticky or drips water, the subsoil is still too wet for tilling or planting.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko ni miihe ashɛ onine mlibotemɔ he. Kɛkɛ ni efolɔ shishigbɛ sũ lɛ mli nine kome. squeeze into a ball Kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nu ni hoɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo tsɔ ni esaaa akɛ atsuɔ nii loo aduɔ nii.

english: Why do my crops fall over easily during high winds even though the surface ground feels firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: If the soil underneath the surface remains soft and waterlogged, crop roots cannot hold onto the earth firmly. The weak root anchorage in the soft subsoil allows strong winds to pull the plant down.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Tse lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa tso lɛ shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and rot when rainwater stands on my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When standing water covers your land, it suffocates the roots by blocking oxygen, causing root rot and turning the leaves yellow.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my plants wilt in the hot sun even when the soil around them is soaked with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Eyɛ mli akɛ nu efo mli po.

english: When roots stay in waterlogged soil for too long, they rot and stop working. Damaged roots cannot pump water up into the plant, so the leaves wilt from thirst despite being in wet soil.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi lɛ hi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaakpa nitsumɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu awo tso lɛ mli. Baai lɛ gboɔ yɛ kumai hewɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: What happens to my maize seeds if I plant them in soil that has water trapped underneath?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eta shishi lɛ nɔ?

english: If the soil below is too wet and airless, the seeds will absorb excess moisture and rot underground before they get the chance to sprout into healthy seedlings.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do crop roots fail to grow deep into the soil in areas where water gathers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ?

english: Roots avoid growing down into wet, airless subsoil. Instead, they stay near the surface to get oxygen, which leaves the plant with a shallow, weak root system.
ga: Shishifãi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ ni amɛaada lɛ he. Shi ebaahi he ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ koni enine ashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava right after floodwater leaves my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nu afua lɛ eshi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is best to wait a bit after surface water disappears. Even if the surface looks dry, the ground underneath remains very soft and wet, which can cause cassava stem cuttings to rot before they root.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ be fioo beni nu ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ elaaje sɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi moŋ Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei tsei lɛ agbo dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: How can I keep rainwater from gathering and standing in low areas of my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can dig shallow drainage channels to lead water away from low spots, or build raised mounds and ridges so your crop roots stay elevated above standing water.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko. koni ojie nu kɛjɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ Aloo ofee gɔji kɛ ŋmeii ni baaha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ fe nu ni damɔ shi lɛ.

english: Does making high soil ridges help protect vegetables in areas where water collects easily?
ga: Ani ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ baabu aduawai ahe yɛ hei ni nu baanyɛ abua naa oya lɛ?

english: Yes, planting on high mounds or ridges lifts the crop roots above the excess water level, letting them get air while allowing surplus water to collect safely in the furrows between ridges.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ he. Ha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over and lie flat on the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiikã shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over (a condition called lodging) when strong winds hit plants with weak or shallow root systems, or when stem borer pests weaken the stalks. Planting seeds at the correct depth, building up soil around the base of the stems (hilling), and avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer will help roots grow deeper and stalks grow stronger.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy) kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa tsei ni shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ. Aloo beni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi ni eha tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni atswaa abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (hilling) kɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni tso lɛ mli awa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall to the ground with heavy fruit bunches before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ kɛ aduawai babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily because parasitic nematodes or root borers destroy their shallow root system, leaving them unable to support heavy bunches. Propping up fruiting trees with strong wooden poles and planting clean, pest-free suckers prevents root destruction and keeps trees standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ parasitic nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. ni ehaa enyɛŋ eye ebua kuu ko ni tsii Yibii tsei ni akɛ tsei ni wa baadu kɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite ni eha tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my crops drying up and failing even though I planted during the same month I always do every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ nyɔŋ ni miduɔ daa afi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli moŋ?

english: Rains in Ghana are becoming erratic due to changing weather patterns, meaning traditional planting months no longer guarantee sufficient moisture. Farmers now need to check seasonal weather forecasts, use early-maturing seed varieties, or practice water conservation like mulching to survive sudden dry spells.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ miifee nɔ ni ejaaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nyɔŋ ni akɛyeɔ nii yɛ kusum naa lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa aba dɔŋŋ. Amrɔ nɛɛ ehe miihia ni okwaafoi lɛ akwɛ be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he akɔntaabuu. Kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ oya atsu nii. Aloo feemɔ bɔ ni atoɔ nu he gbɛjianɔ ahaa, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, koni onyɛ ohi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni baa trukaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot survive direct hot sunlight and dry Harmattan winds on an open field. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa creates a living canopy that shelters seedlings and retains soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ naa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmei dumɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do Fall Armyworms attack my maize farm again every single year after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworms tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ daa afi lɛ? Afii komɛi asɛɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ lɛ

english: Fall Armyworm moths survive between crop seasons by laying eggs on wild grasses, weeds, and leftover crop stubble. Rotating maize with non-grass crops like cowpeas or cassava, clearing farm borders, and destroying crop residue breaks the pest's breeding cycle so they cannot return in large numbers.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ yɛ koo mli jwɛi, jwɛi kɛ tsei ahe ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsakeɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee jwɛi tamɔ cowpea loo cassava. ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ akpãtamɔ Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ fɔmɔ sɛɛkuu lɛ naa koni ekaku esɛɛ eba babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow, curled leaves on cassava are caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural extension services ensures your plants stay healthy and grow large tubers.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni oootsɔ Agricultural Extension Service lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my crop yields getting smaller every year even though I use the same field and seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji kɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Soil loses vital nutrients when the same crop is planted repeatedly without rest or soil feeding. Practicing crop rotation, adding organic manure or compost, and planting nitrogen-fixing legumes like groundnuts restores soil health and yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. ni akɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo niyenii haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ nifeemɔ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli baafata he Ni aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi, tamɔ ŋmei, baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ nibii ni baa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off to the ground without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant suffers from heat stress, erratic watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping soil moist through regular watering and mulching, along with balanced fertilization, stops flower drop and encourages fruit formation.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ. kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ he Ehaa fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kpaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa.

english: If I plant seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close causes crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin, weak plants that yield very little. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong roots and produce maximum output.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and choke my crops even when I apply fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛtsiɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔji lɛ amli po?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb water and chemical fertilizer faster than young crops can. Clearing weeds early within the first three to four weeks of planting ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to outgrow wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baanyɛ afee. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ, enɛ haa otsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya fe koo mli tsei.

english: Why do my crops keep struggling even when I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer alone cannot save land that lacks organic matter. Poor soil structure or high acidity prevents roots from absorbing nutrients, so mixing compost or manure into the soil is needed to help the land hold moisture and food for crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ atsu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ehiii loo acidity ni fa babaoo lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔtɔ afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if my land is tired and needs a rest before I plant on it again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni mijɔɔ mihe dani madu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Tired soil shows clear warning signs like yellowing leaves, stunted crop growth, rapid soil washing away during rains, and a sudden increase in stubborn weeds that take over the farm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baatsɔɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ. Sũ lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. kɛ jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa ni yeɔ ŋmɔji anɔ lɛ ni yaa hiɛ trukaa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can make food efficiently. Staking keeps the leaves away from wet soil diseases and helps the plant send energy down to build bigger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. yɛ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni ebaai lɛ anyɛ ahoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ Staking haa baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa shi koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly in the storage barn after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when they are harvested with knife cuts, exposed to high heat right after digging, or stored in dark rooms without proper airflow to dry out natural surface moisture.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmei kpa. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo yɛ la ni mli wa mli beni atsa shi lɛ sɛɛ. aloo akɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha adebɔɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential food that gets washed away easily during heavy rains or depleted by continuous farming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli loo ni okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer stress from extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of balanced nutrients in the soil.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna shwane mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up and show pale green or yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, a disease spread by tiny whitefly insects that suck sap from young leaves and weaken the whole plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ŋmei baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. No shwieɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Is it better to mix different crops like maize and beans on the same field or grow only one crop?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafutu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo ookwɛ tso kome pɛ?

english: Mixing compatible crops like maize and beans protects your income if one crop fails, feeds the soil natural nitrogen from the beans, and reduces pest damage compared to growing a single crop.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ Ebuɔ oshika he kɛji ŋmãa kome fite. Ha amɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni aduɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my seeds take so long to sprout when I plant them immediately after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours compact the soil and fill air spaces with water, which smothers seeds and creates a hard top crust that delicate sprouts cannot easily push through.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmei ni wa ko baa nɔ ni tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do insects attack my vegetables much more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Pests multiply much faster in warm weather, and plants weakened by dry conditions lose their natural strength to resist insect damage.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayi fa oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Ni tsei ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or lack of tiny insects called midges that pollinate the flowers. Providing adequate shade and moisture helps the tree hold onto its flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulu la ni egbi. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni sa ha tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni efeɔ fɔfɔii akutsei.

english: How do I know if my land in Ghana is suitable for growing high-yielding cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ dumɔ?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, rich soil that drains water well so the roots do not rot. If your land stays flooded after heavy rain or is very rocky and sandy, cocoa roots will struggle to grow deep enough to support a good yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia kokoo tsei. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akafite Kɛji nugbɔ eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ loo eyɛ tɛi kɛ ŋã babaoo. Cocoa shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade crops like plantain planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily in strong, direct sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide living shade and keep the soil humid, protecting young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The harmattan brings dry, hot winds that quickly suck moisture out of soil and leaves. Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during severe dry weather to conserve water and protect their trunks from drying out.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ baa. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛtso lɛ he koni amɛkagbi.

english: Does cutting off extra branches on my cocoa trees really help them produce more cocoa?
ga: Ani niji krokomɛi ni fata he ni mifoɔ yɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, pruning removes weak or hidden branches that waste the tree's energy. Opening up the tree canopy allows air and light to circulate, which stops damp fungal diseases and directs the tree's strength into growing bigger pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni miifite tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbele tso lɛ shishi lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ kpaa, ni ekwɛɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni eda ni etsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings very close together to get more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, their roots fight each other for soil food and water, and their tops block sunlight from reaching lower branches. Proper spacing ensures every tree gets enough sunlight and nourishment to yield heavily.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekpa nii babaoo.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a water mold that spreads fast during heavy rains and cool, wet conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning dense branches, and removing infected pods keeps humidity down and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black rot ni yɔɔ pods mli lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. weeding dense pruning Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops every year if I don't give it fertilizer or rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli loo mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull minerals and food out of the soil every single season. If you harvest continuously without replenishing the soil through natural compost, fertilizers, or resting period (fallow), the soil becomes empty and crops grow weak.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa shika tsuru kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji oya nɔ okpa ŋmɔshi nii ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo hejɔɔmɔ be (fallow) wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava together with my young cocoa trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛfata kookoo tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Cassava grows very fast and has greedy roots that spread wide, taking away water and nutrients that young cocoa needs. It is better to use plantain or cocoyam for shade, as they do not compete as aggressively with cocoa roots.
ga: Cassava daa oya waa ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he. Ejieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ plantain loo cocoa baatsu nii kɛha hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛkɛ cocoa shishifãi lɛ yeee akaŋ waa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa seedlings die right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings go into shock if their roots are broken during transplanting or if they are moved directly into hot sun without water. Moving them on a cloudy day, protecting their root ball, and watering them right away prevents seedling loss.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakpokpo kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fã yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ ajie kɛtee hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni nu bɛ mli. Amɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ atatu gbi nɔ Shishifã bɔɔlu lɛ he ni oookɛ nu awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: I want to start growing soybeans on my land, but why do people say this crop is good for improving my soil?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi soybean dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tso nɛɛ hi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔyaa lɛ?

english: Soybean plants have small nodules on their roots that work with friendly soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the ground. This naturally enriches your soil, making it fertile for the soybean crop itself and for other crops you plant in that field later.
ga: Soybean tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ fɛo kɛha sɛɛ mli soybean ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni oduɔ yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my soybean roots have small round bumps on them when I pull them out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Be ni mijieɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those bumps are called root nodules, and they are actually a great sign. Inside those bumps, microscopic organisms turn air into plant food (nitrogen) for your crop, which helps the soybeans grow big without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ shishifãi, ni amɛji okadi kpakpa diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ nakai gɔji lɛ amli lɛ, nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsakeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) kɛhaa onibii. Enɛ haa soybean lɛ daa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: Why do my crops sometimes stop growing and look weak halfway through the season even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ be lɛ fã mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Crops often stall in growth when the nutrients in the soil get completely used up or when the soil becomes too hard for roots to spread. Giving plants organic manure or the right fertilizer at the mid-growth stage gives them the boost they need to keep flourishing until harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kpaa kwɛ̃mɔ kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ha tsei yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop plants grow very tall and thin with few leaves when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to one another, the plants compete for sunlight. They waste all their energy stretching upward to reach the sun instead of growing thick stems and strong branches that can hold lots of grain or fruit.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛshɛɔ Hulu lɛ he lɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo du tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa nɛ ma nyɛ maa ngɔ dumɔwuhi loo yiblii fuu.

english: My soybean leaves are turning yellow while the pods are still small. Is my crop sick?
ga: Mi soybean baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ. Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during early pod formation usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or the field has too much standing water suffocating the roots. Soybean leaves should stay green while the pods grow and should only turn yellow naturally when the crop is fully mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ pod feemɔ shishijee mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Esa akɛ soybean baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Ni esa akɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa pɛ kɛji tso lɛ eda ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: I noticed many flowers falling off my soybean plants. Will this destroy my harvest?
ga: Miyɔse fɔfɔi babaoo ni miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-soybean tsei lɛ anɔ. Ani enɛ baafite midumɔ nii lɛ?

english: It is normal for soybean plants to drop up to half of their flowers if they experience heat or dry spells. The plant naturally sheds extra flowers so it can concentrate its remaining energy on turning the healthiest flowers into full seeds.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ soybean tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii lɛ fã kɛji amɛyashɛ latsaa loo hɔmɔ he. Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔii krɛdɛɛi kɛjɛ ehe. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛtsake fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni etsɔ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: My maize crop failed in my field last season. Can I restart farming that same land with soybeans this year?
ga: Mi ŋmãa lɛ fite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli. Ani manyɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ okwaayeli kɛ soybeans ekoŋŋ afi nɛɛ?

english: Yes, planting soybeans after a failed maize crop is a great choice. Switching to a legume like soybean breaks the cycle of pests and diseases that lived on the maize and helps restore nitrogen back into the tired soil.
ga: No hewɔ lɛ hɛɛ, soybeans ni aduɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ egbo lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ atsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ soybeans nɔ lɛ, efoɔ ŋmãa kɛ helai ni hiɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What simple step can I take with my soybean seeds before planting to make sure my farm yields well?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ soybean dumɔwui dani madu koni miŋmɔ lɛ awo yibii kpakpai?

english: You can mix your soybean seeds with a special powder called an inoculant before planting. This coats the seeds with beneficial bacteria that help the roots form healthy pods earlier and boost your final yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ soybean dumɔwui afutu powda krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leavening agent dani okɛdu. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa oya, ni ehaa onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the flowering period affect how my soybean plants grow?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa soybean tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Too much standing water during flowering can drown the roots and cause the plant to shed its blossoms before pods can form. Making small drainage paths in your field allows excess rainwater to flow away so the plant can make healthy seed pods.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha tso lɛ agbo dani ŋmeii aba. Nu shwiemɔ tsɔne bibioo ko ni ooofee Yɛ oŋmɔji amli lɛ enɛ baaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ afee dumɔwui akui ni mli wa.

english: Can I feed fresh sugarcane directly to my farm animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ ŋmãa hee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Sugarcane can be fed to farm animals, but it is best to crush or chop it first so they can chew it comfortably. You should also mix it with a dry starchy food like gari so the high sugar does not upset their stomach.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ sugar cane aha ŋmɔ mli kooloi. Shi ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsɔ amɛ loo okɛ amɛ atsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ koni efee mlɛo akɛ oooye. Esa akɛ okɛ niyenii ni mli egbi ni starch yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ghari, afutu mli koni sugar ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akagbala omusuŋ.

english: Why do I need to crush sugarcane stalks before giving them to my livestock?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei dani mikɛha kooloi lɛ?

english: Crushing sugarcane breaks down the hard outer rind, allowing animals to chew and extract the juice to their satisfaction without wasting energy or damaging their teeth.
ga: Sugar cane ni akumɔ lɛ fiteɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ. Enɛ haa kooloi yeɔ nii ni amɛnuɔ nu bɔ ni he hiaa ni amɛfiteee hewalɛ loo amɛfiteee amɛnyanyɔji.

english: What is the proper way to prepare sugarcane crop harvest for animal feed?
ga: Te esa akɛ asaa ŋmei ni afeɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ akɛ kooloi aniyenii?

english: After harvesting sugarcane, crush or chop the stalks thoroughly and combine them with a small amount of gari to dilute the heavy sugar content before feeding.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Gbalamɔ loo ofolɔ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ bibii ni okɛ ghari fioo afutu mli koni ŋmei ni tsii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee mlɛo dani okɛye nii.

english: Can feeding my animals too much sweet sugarcane make them sick?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ha mikooloi lɛ babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hela?

english: Yes, sugarcane has a very high sugar content. Feeding it alone in large amounts can overload an animal's digestive system and make them feel unwell.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei yɛ sugar babaoo waa. Kɛ́ aha amɛ niyenii babaoo pɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kooloo lɛ niyenii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii fe nine, ni eha amɛnu he akɛ hela miimɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know if a sweet crop like sugarcane is too rich for my animals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ fa tsɔ kɛha mikooloi lɛ?

english: Crops high in sugar can cause digestive discomfort if given alone; if an animal eats pure sugarcane continuously, the excessive sugar can make them sick, so it must be balanced with dry feeds.
ga: Tsei ni sugar babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii lɛ mli agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ aye amɛ pɛ. Kɛji kooloi yeɔ ŋmei krɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ Sugar babaoo baanyɛ aha hela amɔ bo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ekɛ niyenii ni egbi lɛ afee ekome.

english: How can I prevent my livestock from getting stomach upsets when eating sweet fodder crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mikooloi lɛ anaa koni amɛmli akafee shoo kɛ́ amɛye niyenii ni ŋɔɔ?

english: You can prevent stomach upsets by crushing the sweet fodder to aid digestion and mixing in a dry ingredient like gari to tone down the concentrated sweetness.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsĩ musu ni mli ewo wu lɛ naa kɛtsɔ niyenii ni sugar yɔɔ mli ni oootsɔ mli koni eye ebua niyenii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni egbi tamɔ Gari mli koni ekɛba ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa lɛ shi.

english: Why is gari mixed into sugarcane feed for livestock?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ ghari futuɔ ŋmei niyenii ni akɛhaa kooloi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Gari is a dry cassava product that absorbs excessive sweetness and balances the heavy sugars in sugarcane, preventing animals from getting sick from too much sugar.
ga: Gari ji ŋmei ni egbi ni shwieɔ ŋmei fe nine. ni ehaa sugar ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ feɔ ekome Etsiɔ kooloi anaa koni amɛkaná hela kɛjɛ sugar babaoo mli.

english: Can I use sugarcane as the main fodder crop for my animals during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shɛ̃ atsu nii akɛ niyenii titri ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: While sugarcane provides good energy and moisture, it should not be fed alone due to its heavy sugar level. It must be crushed and balanced with dry feeds like gari.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei haa hewalɛ kpakpa kɛ fɛ̃i moŋ, Shi esaaa akɛ ahaa lɛ pɛ niyenii yɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ atsɔ mli ni akɛ niyenii ni egbi tamɔ ghari afee ekome.

english: How does cassava gari interact with high-sugar crop feeds in animal digestion?
ga: Te cassava kari kɛ tso niyenii ni sugar eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ kooloi aniyenii mli?

english: Gari acts as a dry starch buffer that balances the rapid sugar release of crushed sugarcane, helping the animal digest the feed safely.
ga: Gari tsuɔ nii akɛ starch ni egbi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sugar ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei mli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni amɛyeɔ niyenii shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it safe to feed crushed sugarcane to farm animals every day?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaaha ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atswa lɛ daa gbi?

english: It is safe as long as it is not given in isolation; mixing a bit of gari into the crushed sugarcane each time ensures the animals enjoy the sweetness without suffering sugar-induced illness.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ agbalaaa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ghari fioo ko futu ŋmei ni atswa lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ, ehaa kooloi lɛ náa ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ he miishɛɛ ni hela mɔɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which it needs to build strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain causes water to sit in the soil, preventing roots from breathing and soaking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ he miihia koni afee baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and rotting while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium to the developing fruit, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells that prevent roots from taking up calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛyibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be ni haaa shishifãi lɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or a plant virus spread by whiteflies. The feeding damages the leaf tissue, causing it to roll and distort as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ thrips loo mites yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi. loo tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Niyenii haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa efoɔ ni efoɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do so many small flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Te ejɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but only have enough energy, water, and soil nutrients to feed a small percentage of them into mature pods. The tree drops extra flowers to protect its health and keep only what it can support.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, shi hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eda. Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi ashwie shi koni ekɛbu ehewalɛ he. ni okɛ fã ni abaanyɛ aye abua lɛ pɛ ato

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow very bushy with lots of green leaves but produce very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, cowpeas focus all their energy on growing leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas make their own nitrogen naturally, so extra artificial fertilizer causes them to put foliage growth over bean production.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, Cowpeas kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ahe tsei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfee lɛ haa ŋmeii baa lɛ daa fe ŋmeii ni afeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt under the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, water leaves the plant's leaves faster than the roots can draw moisture up from the soil. This temporary wilting is the plant's way of protecting itself from drying out, and it usually recovers once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shĩɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli ni egboɔ nɛɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest when they are hidden under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa be mli ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: As cassava matures underground, the lower leaves on the stem dry up and drop off, the stem turns thick and woody, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack open because the expanding tubers are pushing the soil upward.
ga: Beni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni yitso ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ miitsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my groundnut plants start turning brown and dropping off near the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi beni be lɛ miiba naagbee lɛ?

english: When groundnut plants mature, they naturally redirect energy away from leaves and into filling out the underground nuts. Leaf yellowing and leaf fall at this stage show that the plant has finished growing and the nuts are ripening.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Amɛtsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe dalɛ naa ni ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why am I finding small holes in my maize leaves with tiny powdery waste inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm or stemborers. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant where it is soft, chewing the young tissue and leaving behind sawdust-like droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms loo stem borers. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. Ekɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need full sunlight to produce heavy tubers. Staking lifts the leaves high into the light so they can make food efficiently, while also keeping leaves off the damp ground to prevent fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu muu lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛfee bulbs ni tsii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kane lɛ mli koni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and heat without protection. If they do not have enough shade trees or plantain plants growing around them, the hot sun scorches their leaves and dries up the soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛji akɛ abuuu amɛhe. Kɛji amɛbɛ tsei loo plantains ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbɔle amɛhe lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Why do I see small worms eating holes into the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack maize early in its growth by eating the central leaves. Catching them early with recommended extension officer sprays or hand-picking helps protect your corn yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-corn ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft while still growing on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo yɛ be mli ni edaa lolo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium, usually caused by uneven watering or sudden dry spells in the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ trukaa lɛ.
