english: Cassava roots rot mostly when planted in waterlogged soil with poor drainage or when infected by root rot fungi. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight with their leaves. Gathering maximum sunlight allows the plant to produce food and build big, healthy underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ amɛbaa lɛ mli. Hulu la ni abua naa bɔ ni aaanyɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How do I know if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer before I plant my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani madu tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If your previous crop grew slowly, had pale yellowish leaves, or yielded very small harvests, your soil is low in nutrients and needs compost, manure, or chemical fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewoɔ nibii fioo ko pɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant cowpea or beans together with my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally feeds the neighboring maize plants and keeps the soil rich.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops while the plants are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛji bibii waa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal the soil's water, sunlight, and fertilizer, which starves your young plants right when they need nutrients most to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi bibii lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei bibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni niyenii he hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for space, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in thin stems, weak plants, and much smaller produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—keeps the ground cool and moist by stopping soil water from evaporating fast in the heat, while also slowing down weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehaaa efo oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ hu shwereɔ fioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ hulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct harsh sunlight burns their tender leaves. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa protects the young trees until they grow strong enough to tolerate full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow tall and green, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving fine waste inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ jwɛi fioo ko yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center shoot of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves, and early treatment with appropriate organic or chemical sprays is needed to protect the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei. ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ mra. Kɛ organic loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to turn soft and rot inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens mainly when water collects in the soil around the roots without draining away properly. Planting cassava on raised ridges helps excess rainwater drain off and keeps roots healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. shishifãi ni nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes for my yam leaves to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to sunlight so the plant can make food efficiently. Keeping leaves off the damp ground also prevents fungal leaf diseases and allows the plant to direct its energy into growing larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baai helai ni ji fungal lɛ anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on the sap beneath the leaf, or a leaf-curl virus transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo leaf curl hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Removing excess suckers ensures that water and soil nutrients go directly to the main tree, allowing it to yield a much larger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii lɛ yaa tso titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa plantains ŋmɔji ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, or mulching, blocks direct sunlight, keeps the ground cool, reduces water evaporation, and stops weeds from stealing water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaaa jwɛi akaju nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up. Alternating maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmãa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny organisms on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that extra nitrogen stays in the earth to nourish your next crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I remove all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally require soft, indirect sunlight to grow safely. Bright, direct heat from an open sky burns their delicate leaves and dries out their roots faster than they can absorb moisture.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii. yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ koni enyɛ eda shweshweeshwe Dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shãa ebaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly into tubes on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a plant's natural defense against extreme heat. By curling up, the leaf exposes less surface area to the sun, preventing the plant from losing too much precious water through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ haaa hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe fioo. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu ni jara wa babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other underground for soil nutrients and water, and above ground for sunlight. This competition leaves all the plants thin, weak, and low-yielding.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ana hulu la Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to lift and tie my yam vines onto tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso nɔ ni mikɛfi tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high above the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more energy the plant sends down into the ground to build huge yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Babaoo ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over right when the fruit starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that sit close to the soil surface. When heavy bunches of fruit develop, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for winds to push it over unless it is supported with strong wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ je kpo yɛ kui agboi amli lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsɔ mli mlɛo. ja tso ni mli wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and staying very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Curled, small leaves are a classic sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is carried and spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease prevents the plant from producing energy, leading to stunted stems and very small tubers.
ga: Baai bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi ni ale waa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛyitsei lɛ feɔ bibii waa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the plant experiences sudden drought stress. Severe heat or lack of water stops pollination from completing successfully, causing the flower to drop off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baatsi pollination naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to grow slowly and produce small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ daa blɛoo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your main crops before your crops have a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli dani onibii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn moldy and spoil even after I dry them in the sun for two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ mli ewo muji ni efite beni mikɛ amɛ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii enyɔ po lɛ?

english: Maize grains can look dry on the surface while still holding moisture inside. If the moisture level inside the grain is too high when bagged, heat and mold build up quickly, causing the entire bag to rot during storage.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni egbi yɛ hiɛ shi amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lolo. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ fa tsɔ beni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa oya. Enɛ haa kotoku muu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: What is a moisture testing machine, and why should I test my crops with it before taking them to sell?
ga: Mɛni ji hulutsoo he kaa? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka miŋmɔshi nii lɛ makwɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: A moisture meter measures the exact amount of water inside your harvested grains. Buyers use it to ensure grains are dry enough not to rot in transit, so testing beforehand helps you know if your crop meets market standard without being rejected.
ga: Moisture meter susuɔ nu abɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmaa ni okpa lɛ mli lɛ he. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni efiteee beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kaa ni ooofee dani ofee lɛ baaye abua bo ni ole kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jarayeli he mlai lɛ kpãa gbee ni akpooo bo.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my harvested cocoa beans directly on a bare concrete floor under the strong sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ kɔnkrit ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Concrete heats up too fast under the sun and can scorch the cocoa beans, making the shells brittle while spoiling the flavor. Drying on raised wooden mats allows air to flow underneath for an even, gentle dry.
ga: Kɔnkrit lɛ mli dɔɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ebaanyɛ eshã kookoo ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋshɔŋloo lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ egbi yɛ tsɔne ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ yɛ shishi koni egbi blɛoo, ni egbi po.

english: Why does my harvested paddy rice smell bad after I leave it packed tightly in wet sacks overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ shi waa kɛ́ ashi yɛ kotokui ni mli efɔ mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain breathes and produces heat. When wet rice is trapped in a sack, the trapped warmth and water cause rapid fermentation and bacterial growth, creating a sour smell and lowering grain quality.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ muɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni efɔ lɛ efo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ oya ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do small insects appear inside my sealed bags of cowpeas a few weeks after storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cowpeas kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevil insects often lay invisible eggs inside bean pods while the crop is still in the field. If the beans are not properly dried or treated before storage, those eggs hatch inside the bag and start eating the grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo atsuuu he nii dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni amɛjeɔ dumɔwui lɛ yeli shishi.

english: Why do grain buyers offer me a lower price when my maize contains broken grains and chaff?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmaa lɛ haa mi jara ni baa shi yɛ be mli ni miŋmaa lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni ekumɔ lɛ?

english: Broken grains spoil much faster, absorb humidity easily, and attract insects quicker than whole grains. Buyers pay less because broken pieces reduce the overall storage life and quality of the crop batch.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekumɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kwraa. Eheɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya ni egbalaa kooloi oya fe ŋmaa. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo ejaakɛ fãi ni ekumɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ashihilɛ fɛɛ kɛ bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and turning yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from intense heat and slow down water loss. If soil moisture is too low, the plant drops leaves to stay alive until it gets water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa tsɔ Tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ehi shi kɛyashi be mli ni enine baashɛ nu nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When groundnuts mature, the outer leaves of the plant start turning yellow. You can test by pulling up a plant; if the inner lining of the pod shell is dark brown or black with distinct veins, the crop is ready.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso ko ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni eyɛ fãji ni mli tse lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots rot in the ground if I leave them unharvested during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni akpaaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, the mature starch in the cassava breaks down rapidly and rots in the waterlogged ground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ bɛ lɛ Starch ni eda ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need to be properly dried and kept cool to stay alive. If saved seeds absorb moisture or get too hot in storage, the embryo inside dies or enters a deep dormancy, preventing them from germinating.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji dumɔwui ni ato lɛ shwieɔ nu loo edɔɔ tsɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ Fɔmɔ kotoku ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbo loo ebote wɔɔhe ni mli kwɔ mli. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or leaves the roots sitting in too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ bote nu mli tsɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I keep planting maize in the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ awui kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans or peanuts puts good nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I clear the weeds from my farm before I apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and will drink up the fertilizer before your plants can reach it. Clearing weeds first ensures that your crops get all the food from the fertilizer so your money is not wasted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ, ni ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani otsei lɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, oshika lɛ efeŋ yaka.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects in the soil for too long, creating conditions for root rot diseases to grow. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifã hela aba. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree experiences stress from hot dry weather, a lack of soil nutrients, or attacks from tiny insects like mirids. Keeping soil cool with mulch and managing shade helps trees hold onto their flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tutuamɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli jɔ, ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark black spots at the bottom as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ ebɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular. Giving your plants a steady amount of water helps them draw up calcium from the soil smoothly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ ni faaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu babaoo ha tso lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ejie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ, beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes them stretch up tall and weak to reach the sun, leaving them with little energy to make big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Foidamɔ nɛɛ haa amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa koni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haaa amɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to put stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the energy required to swell the tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them away from wet soil where fungal diseases easily spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily blow over and fall during heavy rain, even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them easy to push over. Tiny worm-like pests called nematodes often eat the roots underground without you seeing, which weakens the tree's hold in the soil.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ewoɔ aduawai ni tsii ni abua naa. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oootsi Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni onaaa amɛ. Enɛ haa bɔ ni tso lɛ kpɛtɛɔ sũ lɛ he lɛ baa shi.

english: How do weeds harm my crops if there is plenty of space between the rows in my field?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ?

english: Even if there seems to be space, weed roots travel underground to steal water and plant food away from your crops. Weeds also shade lower crop leaves and can hide dangerous insect pests that spread diseases.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni he ko yɛ moŋ Shi jwɛi shishifãi hu yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛyaju nu ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli. Jwɛi hu haa tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ ato.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farmland is rich enough to plant maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Good soil for maize should feel dark, loose, and crumbly when squeezed, holding moistness without staying soggy. If the soil is very pale, hard, or sandy, the maize roots will struggle to extract water and essential nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ afee ediŋŋ, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ ŋã waa Abɛi shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young crops with dried leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops heavy rain from washing away the good topsoil.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works very well. Maize grows rapidly and is harvested in a few months, leaving the space open for the slower-growing cassava to expand and produce its tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ shwieɔ shi koni ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ewo ŋmei.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves fight above ground for sun. This leaves all the plants thin, weak, and with very small harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo, egbɔjɔɔ, ni ekpaa nɔ ko bibioo kwraa.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up and dying during the hot sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn under intense direct sunlight. They require fast-growing shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to block the harsh heat and keep the surrounding air humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant produce huge leafy branches but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly. The plant sends all its energy into growing big green leaves above ground instead of pushing roots down to form swollen cassava tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi shishifãi lɛ kɛba shi kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the stems turn woody, and the ground right around the base of the plant starts to crack open due to expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ tso. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni bulb lɛ daa yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for strong green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How many rains should I wait for at the start of the year before planting my seeds?
ga: Yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, tsei enyiɛ esa akɛ wɔmɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ dani wɔdu dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait for two or three heavy rains rather than planting after the very first light shower. Early rain can dry up quickly, leaving seeds to rot or die in hot dry soil before they can settle.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi oya. Shi dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛgboi loo amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ dani amɛba shi.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted to live in harsh conditions. They naturally drink water and consume soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops, which is why clearing them early is essential.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛnuɔ nu yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains next to new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? kookoo dumɔwui heei

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as temporary shade trees, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko. Ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same farm where I am starting my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mije kookoo dumɔwui lɛ shishi yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, but you must keep enough distance between them. Cassava provides quick food and income while cocoa grows, but if planted too close, its thick roots will steal moisture and nutrients away from the young cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni okɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi amɛteŋ. Cassava ji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe oya yɛ be mli ni kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ juɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo bibii lɛ amli.

english: Will my plantain plants keep producing good fruit after my cocoa trees grow big and form a thick shade?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii kpakpai beni mikokoo tsei lɛ eda ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, mature plantains need full sunlight to produce heavy bunches. Once cocoa trees mature and create a dense canopy, the shade will cause plantain yields to drop, which is when farmers usually remove them.
ga: Dabi, hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia plantains ni eda lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni tsii aba. Beni kookoo tso lɛ eda ni efee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ. Shadows baaha plantains yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi. Be nɛɛ ji be ni okwaafoi fɔɔ amɛ jiemɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots that cannot reach deep underground water. In intense heat without shade, the leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can suck it up, causing the edges to dry out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. gĩ baa lɛ naa

english: How long do I have to wait after planting cocoa before I can harvest my first pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years under proper care, whereas older, traditional cocoa varieties can take between 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 teŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and turn yellow when the weather becomes very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants hold a lot of water in their soft trunks. During long dry spells, they naturally drop their outer leaves to save water and keep the main stem alive until the rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui toɔ nu babaoo yɛ amɛtso ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli. Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ, kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and skinny with very small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight and soil nutrients. Instead of expanding their roots into large tubers, they waste energy stretching high into the air to get sun.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, sisifã ɔmɛ lɛɛɔ nɛ a peeɔ bulb nguahi. Mohu ɔ, e puɛɔ he wami nɛ e kɛ yaa kɔɔhiɔ mi konɛ e ná hulu la ɔ.

english: How can keeping goats on my farm help my cassava and plantain crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tooi ni mikwɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cassava kɛ mi-plantain lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Goat manure is rich in natural nutrients like nitrogen and potassium. Collecting their droppings and adding them to the soil feeds your plantains and cassava naturally, helping them grow bigger without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Too ŋmɔtɔ mli eyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. Kɛ́ obua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha o-plantains kɛ o-cassava lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛdara ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo.

english: How do I protect my young farm crops from being destroyed by my goats?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni tooi akafite?

english: Goats love eating tender leaves from young plantains and food crops. You should keep the goats fenced or tethered in a designated grazing section rather than letting them roam freely through young crop fields.
ga: Tooi sumɔɔ ni amɛye tsei bibii kɛ niyenii tsei amli baai bibii. Esa akɛ okɛ gbogbo awo otooi lɛ ahe loo okɛ amɛ awo he ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ kooloi yɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngmɛ mɛ blɔ nɛ a nyɛɛ ngɛ ngmɔ nyafii ɔmɛ a mi.

english: Why does my land yield less cassava if I keep replanting it on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmei fioo kɛji midu lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava draws high amounts of nutrients out of the earth to form its tubers. Continuous planting on the same spot without adding manure or resting the soil starves the ground, leading to smaller harvests each year.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fataaa he loo akɛ sũ lɛ ejɔɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen or is not getting enough water. Applying fertilizer or organic compost early in the plant's life keeps the leaves green and leads to larger cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmã tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli baafata he mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is the main difference between planting brown rice and white rice?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni ji white ni aduɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Brown rice and white rice actually come from the same plant. The difference happens after harvest: brown rice keeps its nutritious outer bran layer, while white rice has that layer removed during processing.
ga: Omɔ ni tsuɔ kɛ omɔ yɛŋ jɛ tso kome mli diɛŋtsɛ. Srɔtofeemɔ lɛ baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ: ŋmãa ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɛɔ e-bran layer ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yɛŋ lɛ jieɔ nakai ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ.

english: Why does my millet survive dry weather better than my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-millet lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi-ŋmã lɛ?

english: Millet has deep, efficient roots and tough leaves that prevent water loss. This makes it naturally adapted to hot, dry conditions with very little rain compared to maize.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, kɛ baai ni mli wa ni tsiɔ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmãa he.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce large tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, preventing leaves from rotting and helping the plant direct energy into growing bigger tubers under the ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo bulbs wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu ŋmei lɛ, efeɔ klalo. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi gbee.

english: Why do small cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by black pod disease, which spreads fast in humid, shady conditions. Pruning thick branches lets sunlight and air into the farm, which helps keep the cocoa pods healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my coconut trees before fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Coconut trees drop their flowers mainly due to water stress, poor soil nutrients, or insect attack. Providing regular water during dry spells and adding compost around the base keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Nu he haomɔ hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ babaoo lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Nu daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata tso lɛ he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi nɔ.

english: Why should I prune the lower leaves of my oil palm trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning dead or overgrown palm leaves makes it easier to inspect and harvest fruit bunches, prevents pests from hiding, and ensures nutrients go directly into fruit production.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ahe tsei ni egboi loo amɛdara fe nine lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakwɛ aduawai akui lɛ amli ni akpa amɛ. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe ni ekwɛɔ koni niyenii mli hewalɛ aya aduawai afeemɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ

english: How can I process my harvested cassava roots so they don't rot after a few days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu mi-cassava shishifãi ni akpa lɛ ahe nii koni amɛkafite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Fresh cassava spoils quickly, but you can process it into gari, high-quality flour, or dried chips. These processed forms last for months without spoiling and sell for a higher price at local markets.
ga: Kasava hee fiteɔ oya. Shi obaanyɛ otsake lɛ ofee gari tsɔne. Ashikiŋsha ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni afee lɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee, ni ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei.

english: What simple steps can I take to stop my harvested fresh fruits from spoiling fast?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni aduawai ni akpa ehee lɛ akafite oya?

english: Harvesting fruits during the cooler morning hours, keeping them shaded from the hot sun, and processing them into products like juice or dried snacks prevents rapid spoiling and increases your income.
ga: Yibii ni ajieɔ yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli Ha ehi he ko ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nyɛŋ etswa lɛ. ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ nibii tamɔ aduawai amli nu loo niyenii ni egbi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efiteɔ oya, ni ehaa shika ni onáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant plantains on the same land with my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop large leaves that provide temporary shade and retain moisture, acting like living umbrellas to protect the young cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka koni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: What is causing the leaves of my young maize plants to have ragged holes with caterpillar dirt inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds inside the central leaves of maize plants. You can protect your crop by checking the field early and applying recommended insecticides or sand/ash mixtures into the plant funnels.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ he ni okwɛɔ lɛ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo ŋã/ashwishwɛ ni akɛfutu mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, won't I harvest more crops from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stems and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to produce larger, healthier harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and twisting up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow and twisted leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease or a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Using disease-free stem cuttings for planting and maintaining soil fertility helps keep the foliage green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he okadi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛ́ adu nii, ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural root bacteria that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes naturally restores soil fertility for future crops without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Flower drop occurs when plants face extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and balancing fertilizer application helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn dark brown and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning farm trees to allow sunlight in, removing infected pods early, and applying approved fungicides help keep the pods healthy.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Tsei ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni hulu la abote mli Jiemɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I keep seeds from this year's hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ afi nɛɛ hybrid ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving and replanting seeds from hybrid maize is not recommended because the second-generation seeds lose their high yield capacity and resistance to disease. Planting fresh certified hybrid seeds every season ensures consistent, strong yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ ni adu ekoŋŋ ejaakɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai. Hybrid dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aduɔ yɛ Seasonality fɛɛ Seasonality mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa ni mli wa aba.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops lower the final harvest I get?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te baafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ aba naagbee ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growing cycle ensures your crops receive all the food and light they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ onibii anɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Vegetative cycle lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know if spending money on chemical fertilizer will make me extra profit at harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shika ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he lɛ baaha maná sɛɛnamɔ kroko yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Fertilizer increases yield when applied correctly, but profit depends on comparing the input cost against the extra bags harvested. Calculating the cost of fertilizer bags versus the market value of the expected extra produce shows whether the investment yields a net profit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa lɛ damɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jara ni akɛtoɔ ŋmaa kotokui krɛdɛɛi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ jara he akɔntaa kɛto jarayeli jara ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ abaaná babaoo lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ kɛji akɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ miiha sɛɛnamɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from dying. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing its tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaakwɛ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die if I do not plant plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have huge leaves that act as shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist until its roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha kookoo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants rolling up into tight tubes in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons to reduce their exposure to the sun and stop moisture from evaporating too fast. It is a natural self-defense mechanism against heat stress.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ naa. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my groundnuts yield fewer nuts when I plant them on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts in the exact same spot continuously exhausts specific nutrients and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating your crops gives the soil time to recover and keeps diseases away.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe, ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their blossoms without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil gets too dry, too wet, or when temperatures get extremely high. The plant drops its blossoms to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Tsei baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize yield change so much from one year to another even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ srɔtoɔ waa kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwu kome pɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Yearly maize production depends heavily on rain patterns, temperature changes, and soil health during critical growing weeks, which naturally vary from season to season.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa daa afi lɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. hulutsoo tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he hiaa waa yɛ otsii ni he hiaa waa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ amli. Nɔ ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ esoroɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ be kɛ be kroko mli.

english: Why does Striga weed keep attached to my maize roots and killing the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miikpɛtɛ mi ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed whose seeds stay dormant in the soil and latch onto maize roots to steal water and food. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas helps trap and clean Striga seeds out of the soil over time.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni edumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ Striga dumɔwui lɛ ni etsuuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits crack open on the sides just as they start to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden soak of heavy rain after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit fills up with water faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to crack.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji amɛná nugbɔ ni naa wa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Nu yiɔ aduawai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly while my neighbor's yams last for many months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ sweet potato lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut during digging or kept in hot, closed spaces. Storing unbruised yams on open racks in a cool, shaded yam barn with fresh air keeps them healthy.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni aŋã. Kɛ atomɔ ni etseko lɛ ato adekai ni agbele nɔ yɛ atomɔ shĩa ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young maize plants have purple colors on their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ yɛ baai ni ji purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize plants usually show a lack of phosphorus, which often happens when cold or dry soil prevents the young roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji purple ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ loo egbi, ni no haaa shishifãi bibii lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the seedlings from the sun and keep the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo tsei ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ haa. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer (like NPK or Urea) or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the boost it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii (tamɔ NPK loo urea) loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiamɔ nii yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away the topsoil along with the freshly applied fertilizer before plant roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp or when only light rain is expected so the nutrients sink into the soil around the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛwo mli lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo beni nugbɔ enɛ fioo koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rain becomes very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the soil cannot drain fast enough. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots aerated and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food that grows big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live and lifts them high into the sunlight to feed the growing tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ hiɔ lɛ. ni owó baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ koni eha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ

english: Why do agricultural workers encourage me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli mli nitsulɔi woɔ mi hewalɛ koni madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby maize plants extra nutrients to grow better without requiring as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ naa niyenii babaoo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: What is making ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the center funnels?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miifee bu ni amɛshi muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant and eats tender leaves. Applying approved treatments or biological remedies directly into the leaf funnels early in the morning kills the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoot suckers growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ etee.

english: Too many shoot suckers fight with the mother plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to small fruit bunches. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the mother tree to focus its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la, ni no haa aduawai bibii baa. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but drop them off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi eshiɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps cool the roots and keep flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaawo tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee nibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Twisted and curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit leaf curl viruses while feeding on plant sap. Controlling these pests early using neem oil or insecticidal soap stops the damage and restores normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni etsilɛ ni ebɔle lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ leaf curl virus lɛ eshwaa be mli ni enuɔ tso mli nu lɛ Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baakpa nɔ ni efite lɛ ni ebaaha baa lɛ adalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: What protective gear should I use when clearing thick bush and overhead branches with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛɛ hebuu nibii esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛ́ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ miifo jwɛi ni mli tse kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Clearing land with a cutlass exposes you to sharp blades and falling branches. Wearing boots, thick trousers, long sleeves, and head protection prevents severe cuts and injuries from heavy manual labor.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsi he ko lɛ, okɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei niji ni egbee shi lɛ kpeɔ. womɔ atadei Pantaloi ni tsii, nine kakadaŋŋ agboi, kɛ yitso hebuu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ fãji kɛ pilamɔi ni naa wa ni jɛɔ nitsumɔ ni wa mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to cut down the upper tree branches when preparing a new plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tso niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ amli kɛ́ asaa shikpɔŋ hee ko he lɛ?

english: Cutting the upper tree canopy allows direct sunlight to reach the soil so your crops can grow, while also preventing heavy overhead branches from falling later and destroying your crops or injuring you.
ga: Tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni oookpa lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋwɛi gbeeɔ shi ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo epilaa bo.

english: Why is clearing land for a new farm so physically demanding to do by myself?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ niji atsu shikpɔŋ ni akɛbaatsu ŋmɔji heei ahe nii lɛ he nii lɛ?

english: Land clearing involves heavy manual labor like chopping thick brush and cutting tall branches. Doing it alone leads to fast exhaustion and high risk of injury, which is why land preparation is usually done with helpers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ ni tsii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ, tamɔ brɔsh ni mli wa ni afoɔ kɛ tsei niji ni kɛlɛ ni afoɔ. Kɛ́ mɔ pɛ feemɔ lɛ, ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe oya, ni ekɛ pilamɔ he oshara kpele baa. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ tsuɔ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ he nii.

english: What is the safest way to carry my cutlasses and farm tools to the field?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mawo mi-dagger kɛ okwaayeli nibii kɛya ŋmɔ mli?

english: Carrying bare cutlasses while walking on rough farm paths can cause dangerous slips and accidental cuts. You should always use protective sheaths or dedicated tool bags to transport sharp tools safely.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko hiɛ dade be mli ni enyiɛɔ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha mɔ ko atsɔ oshara mli ni ekɛ pilamɔi aba. Esa akɛ okɛ tsɔnei ni buɔ mɔ he loo nibii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ oya aya shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is harvesting oil palm fruit bunches so much harder than harvesting other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni oil palm yibii lɛ akpamɔ wa kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi akpamɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm bunches grow deep inside a dense base surrounded by sharp, thorny fronds. Removing the heavy fruit bunches requires significant physical effort, specialized tools, and careful cutting to avoid injury.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ daa kɛyaa shishigbɛ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii ebɔle he. Yibii ni tsii ni ajieɔ lɛ biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo. Ebiɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ koni akapila

english: Why does the base of my oil palm tree get so crowded and thick with growth as it matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As oil palms mature, old fronds naturally stack around the trunk base to support fruit bunches and protect the tree, creating a thick area that must be pruned so you can reach the fruit easily.
ga: Kɛ́ mu tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, akɛ baai momo lɛ toɔ amɛhe. Tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli shishitoo lɛ fiɔ aduawai akui lɛ asɛɛ ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he. Enɛ haa hei ni mli tse ni esa akɛ afo mli lɛ baa koni onyɛ onine ashɛ nɔ ni jɛ mli ba lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why do I need extra helpers or family members when harvesting my oil palm farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yelikɛbualɔ loo weku mlinyo kroko he hiaa mi beni mikpaa mi-palm oil ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm bunches are very heavy and the trees are difficult to work around. Having extra helpers allows you to share the heavy work of cutting fronds, harvesting bunches, and carrying the yield out of the farm.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ tsii ni tsei lɛ asaamɔ wa. Yelikɛbualɔ kroko ni oyɔɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nitsumɔ ni wa ni ji baai afolɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Akpaaa yɛ kui amli ni akɛ nibii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa

english: How can I protect my hands and body from getting cut by sharp oil palm fronds during harvest?
ga: Ebaabu oniji kɛ ogbɔmɔtso he kɛjɛ mu tso baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ he. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ opila yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Oil palm fronds have rigid, spiky edges surrounding the fruit. Wearing thick protective gloves and long sleeves, and using long-handled harvesting chisels keeps your body at a safe distance from thorns.
ga: Mu tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle aduawai lɛ ahe. Glɔvs ni buɔ mɔ he ni mli tse kɛ nine kakadaŋŋ agbo Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkpaa nii ni hiɛ nine kakadaŋŋ aaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ogbɔmɔtso lɛ akatsi ŋmeii lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are oil palm fruit bunches surrounded by tight, spiky fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm aduawai lɛ baai ni mli tse ni ŋmeii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: The oil palm plant naturally grows sharp spines and tight fronds around its fruit to protect the nutrient-rich palm nuts from wild animals, which is why you must prune the surrounding fronds before harvesting.
ga: Mu tsei yɛ ŋmeii ni naa wa kɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe waa. natural results Koni abu palm nuts ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛ koo mli kooloi ahe Nɔ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ofolɔ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. dani akpa kpamɔ

english: What is the best way to move heavy oil palm fruit bunches after cutting them down?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ mu tsei ni tsii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Carrying heavy, prickly oil palm bunches directly by hand causes severe back strain and skin punctures. Using tools like wheelbarrows, head pans, or carrying baskets makes transport safer and easier on your body.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ niji tsu oil palm tsei ni ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe nii tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ekɛ sɛɛ piŋmɔ ni naa wa kɛ hewolo nɔ fãji baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii tamɔ shwiili, yitso, loo tsɛnsi tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nyiɛmɔ afee shweshweeshwe ni efee mlɛo yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant ordinary flowers on my food farm when I am not selling flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ fɔfɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ mi niyenii ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Be ni mikɛ fɔfɔii hɔ̃ɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Bright flowers attract bees and other helpful insects to your farm. As these insects move between the flowers, they carry pollen to your crop flowers, which helps your crops produce more fruits and bigger harvests naturally.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ba oŋmɔ lɛ mli Beni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ lɛ, Amɛwoɔ pollen kɛyaa otso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do small insects like bees actually help my crops grow more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Bees move tiny grains of yellow dust called pollen from one flower to another while looking for food. This process fertilizes the flower so it can develop into a full fruit instead of dropping off.
ga: Wuobii tsiɔ sũ bibii ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ pollen ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli beni etaoɔ niyenii lɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔmɔ kotokui lɛ amli bɔni afee ni amɛdara kwraa ni amɛtsɔ aduawai moŋ fe ni amɛaagbee shi.

english: What does pollination mean, and why is it important for my crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Pollination is how plants reproduce to make seeds and fruits by transferring pollen between flowers. Without pollination, crops like watermelon, cocoa, peppers, and cucumbers cannot form yield.
ga: Pollination ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfɔɔ bii ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai kɛtsɔ pollen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ lɛ, tsei tamɔ watermelon, kookoo, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ kukumba nyɛŋ awo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can the wind alone pollinate all the crops on my farm, or do I need insects?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ pɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ? Aloo ŋmeii he miihia mi?

english: Wind can pollinate a few crops like maize, but many fruit, vegetable, and tree crops depend heavily on insects to move pollen properly so they can set fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa afee ŋmɔtɔ, shi aduawai, aduawai, kɛ tsei babaoo kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii anɔ waa koni amɛjie ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: Will planting flowers near my coconut trees really help me get more coconuts?
ga: Ani fɔfɔii ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebua bo diɛŋtsɛ ni onáa ŋmei babaoo?

english: Yes, coconut palm flowers need insects to pollinate them before they can form coconuts. Having colorful flowers nearby brings in more pollinators, which leads to more coconuts on your trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ehe miihia ni ŋmeii awo ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ amli dani amɛtsɔ ŋmeii. Ni aaana fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ sui sɔrɔtoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ babaoo baahi jɛmɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei tsei ayi afa.

english: Does spraying chemical insecticides on my farm affect my crop yield?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Yes, heavy chemical spraying can kill or chase away beneficial insects like bees that pollinate your crops. Without these pollinators, fewer flowers will turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ agbe loo ashwie kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ baatsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Are the bees visiting my crop flowers going to damage my plants?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni saraa mifɔfɔi lɛ baafite mitsei lɛ?

english: No, bees do not harm your crops. They only visit to collect sweet nectar for food, and while doing so, they perform a vital service by helping your crop flowers turn into harvestable produce.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii yeee oŋmɔshinii lɛ awui. Amɛsaraa koni amɛyabua nu mli nu kɛha niyenii pɛ. Ni yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ nakai lɛ Amɛtsuɔ nitsumɔ ko ni he hiaa he nii kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni amɛhaa ni amɛtsakeɔ fɔfɔi ni oduɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ nibii ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I naturally bring more bees and helpful insects onto my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ aba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can attract them by planting flowering plants along the edges of your farm, reducing harsh chemical sprays, and providing a clean water source nearby.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbala amɛ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔii ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shi. kɛ nu ni mli tse ni akɛhaa yɛ akutso lɛ mli

english: Why do the flowers on my vegetable plants dry up and fall off without producing any food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni niyenii ko bɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ?

english: Flowers usually fall off when they fail to get pollinated. If there are not enough insects around to transfer pollen from flower to flower, the plant cannot form a fruit and sheds the flower.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ anyɛɛɛ afee pollination. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ Eshɛɔ ni ekɛ pollen baajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my fruit tree flower heavily every season but only yield a few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo daa be shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: A tree can produce many blossoms, but if pollinators do not visit to transfer pollen between those blossoms, most of them will fail to turn into actual fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ baanyɛ awo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi kɛji akɛ pollinators baaa koni amɛbajie pollen kɛjɛ nakai fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, Fɔfɔi babaoo efeŋ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees need enough room so their roots and leaves don't fight for light, water, and food. Planting them about 10 feet apart gives each tree enough space to spread out, catch sunlight, and bear plenty of healthy pods.
