ga: He ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa kookoo tsei koni amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ akashi akaŋ yɛ la, nu, kɛ niyenii he. Kɛ́ adu amɛ aaafee ninetalɔi 10 lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshwaa, enine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ, ni enáa ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains planted beside them to shield them from the heat and keep the soil moist while they are young.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji, ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni mli wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ latsaa he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ gbekɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough nutrients to grow healthy maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aná ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark and crumbles easily in your hand. If your maize plants start turning pale or yellow while they are still small, it usually means the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ diŋ ni efiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli. Kɛji akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɔi ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ awo mli.

english: Is it helpful to leave cleared weeds on the field instead of burning them?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni aaashã amɛ?

english: Yes, leaving cleared weeds on top of the soil acts like a blanket that traps moisture and keeps the ground cool. As those weeds decay, they break down into natural compost that feeds your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Kɛ nakai jwɛi lɛ fite lɛ Ebaafite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Curled and patchy leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers prevents this problem.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi bibii bibii. Bei pii lɛ, eji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ du ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What causes black pod disease on my cocoa trees, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ black pod hela baa mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp, and crowded conditions. You can prevent it by pruning excess branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm and by harvesting ripe pods quickly.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, ni mli ewo muji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ oya lɛ ni akpaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Beans and maize work as partners in the field. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil to nourish the maize, while the tall maize stalks give climbing bean vines a structure to grow on.
ga: Beans kɛ corn tsuɔ nii akɛ hefatalɔi yɛ nɛkɛ nitsumɔ nɛɛ mli. Beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ naa gbɛjianɔtoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjɛ mli amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as very high heat, uneven watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How does trimming extra branches off my crops help them produce more yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni mifoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary or diseased branches so the plant stops wasting energy on them. This allows the plant to direct all its water and nutrients into growing healthy fruit, seeds, or pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akpa hewalɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ nakai niji lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdu aduawai, dumɔwui, loo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the exact right time to sow my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: The best time to sow seeds is right after two or three steady rains have deeply soaked the ground. Sowing too early after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if the rain stops for a long time.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ji beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Clearing all shade trees exposes young crops to direct hot sun and strong winds, which dries out the soil quickly and causes the delicate seedlings to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ni enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong, or that the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: What causes the leaves on my young corn plants to look like something shot holes through them?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ko miitsɔ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant's funnel during the day and feed on the soft, growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stems and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii bibii loo ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch before the rainy season fully sets in. Seeds planted too early may germinate and then dry up and die from lack of follow-up water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu oya tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nu ni bɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during cold, wet, or damp weather, especially when there is too much shade and no air moving through the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i loo fɛ̃i be mli, titri lɛ, kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant receives irregular watering, or when insects fail to pollinate the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni afɔɔ tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut away some of the healthy branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ mikoo tso ni eda lɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning healthy branches lets sunlight reach the main trunk and improves air circulation, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to produce more pods instead of leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ baai najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil has lost its fertility before I plant my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛ edɔ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Soil has lost fertility if crops from the previous harvest were unusually small, if weeds grow poorly, or if the topsoil looks pale and hard instead of dark and loose.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ faaa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Jwɛi lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ediŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to grow green and leafy. It can also happen when heavy rainfall washes nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and saw-dust-like dirt inside the top of the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ayitsei lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that crawls into the center leaves of young maize plants to eat the tender growing parts. Controlling them early prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli koni eye ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a field without plantain trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong direct sunlight and high heat. Plantain trees grow quickly and have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and cooler air that cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off small green shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food, water, and sunlight. Leaving only two or three strong shoots allows the main tree to focus its energy on producing big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛkɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to flow off easily, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni enyɛŋ ejɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mlɛo. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do I need to clear small weeds away from the base of my young yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ sweet potato tso ni yɔɔ gbekɛ lolo lɛ shishi?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your young yam vines. Keeping the soil clean around the yam mound gives the vines total access to nutrients so they can build thick, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ o-sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni he tse ni ebɔle Piles of sweet potatoes lɛ he lɛ haa wain tsei lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as very high daytime heat, extremely dry soil, or sudden irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps protect the flowers so they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly and stop growing fresh shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛmiikpa ŋmeii heei lɛ adalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from fresh leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests keeps the leaves expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. small pest control Enɛɛmɛi yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do farmers say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for the next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli beni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant all my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell before the main rains begin. Seeds that germinate after the first rain can easily scorch and die in the hot, dry soil if no rain falls for the next week.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ otsi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves burn and dry out easily. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them during their first two to three years to shield them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build strong leaves, so when it runs short, the plant drains nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ efee kuku Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops make the soil richer?
ga: Te tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny beneficial organisms on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil for neighboring crops and future planting seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ kɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ bei.

english: Why are my cassava plants dropping all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural survival trick to save water. The plant remains alive underground by storing energy in its roots, and it will quickly sprout fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava gbeeɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛbaahere nu. Tsei hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baaje kpo oya.

english: Why is dry weather during the flowering stage more harmful to my maize crop than dry weather when the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ awui fe kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni tsei lɛ ehi shi lolo lɛ?

english: Flowering is the exact time when maize forms its grain. If the plant lacks water during flowering, the silks dry out and pollen fails to fertilize the cob, leading to empty or half-filled cobs.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ ji be pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmãa woɔ dumɔwui. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Siliki lɛ gĩɔ ni pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ awo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ feɔ efolo loo eyiɔ kwraa.

english: Extreme heat and irregular watering cause heat stress that makes tomato flowers drop off before fruit can set. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the plants hold onto their blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa, ni no haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why will my crop produce smaller yields if I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants must fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the plants tall and thin, resulting in smaller cobs, roots, or fruits.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Esa akɛ tsei ni miida lɛ awuu koni hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii, shishifãi, loo aduawai.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds away from my young crop seedlings during their first month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have weak, small root systems and cannot outgrow aggressive weeds. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the available water and soil food without competing.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ bibioo. ni enyɛŋ etsɔ jwɛi ni baatutua mɔ lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool under hot sunshine, and stops heavy rains from washing the topsoil away.
ga: Mulch ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and saw-dust-like powder inside the central funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This pattern of damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows inside the tender growing point of the maize plant. Early monitoring allows you to spot them early and apply control measures before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ona amɛ mra. ni amɛfee gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛyeɔ nɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and look weak right after I transplant them into my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seedlings are moved from a nursery, their roots suffer shock from being disturbed and exposed to strong sunlight. They wilt temporarily until their roots spread out, grip the new soil firmly, and start drinking water again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajieɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ Haomɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ahe. Amɛbaagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã. Mɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ mli shiŋŋ. ni ebɔi nu numɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop shoots after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ je shishi mra nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and tough plants naturally suited to the local environment. They quickly steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crop seedlings have time to fully establish their root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya dani otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow and stop growing tall even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your crops are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Rain helps plants drink, but if the soil lacks nutrients, the crop remains hungry.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei lɛ lolo.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Every crop you harvest takes away nutrients from the earth. If you keep planting without putting food back into the ground through animal manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil gets drained and tired.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu ni okɛ niyenii efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu baatsɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: If I plant seeds saved from my previous harvest, why do they yield much less than certified seeds I buy from the store?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength and uniformity in the next generation. Store-bought certified seeds are carefully bred to resist diseases and produce maximum yield, making the purchase worth the cost.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ kɛ ekomefeemɔ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni helai akamɔ amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Ehaa nɔ ni aheɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sa

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin, watery roots when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ nu yɔɔ mli beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other underground for space, water, and food. Spacing them properly allows each cassava plant enough room to build thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu kɛ niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and drying out during the warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and spreading viruses. The plant curls its leaves as a reaction to stress and infection to stop losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ haomɔ kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahetoohamɔ mli koni amɛkpa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Vegetable plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat, lack of soil moisture, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Aduawai tsei baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. aloo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the leafy branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the tree canopy. This keeps humidity down, which stops fungal diseases like black pod from destroying your crop, while directing energy into growing pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ afite onibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ majeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready for harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the lower leaves of the plant turn yellow and begin to fall off. You can test by pulling up one plant; if the inside of the pod shells has turned dark brown or black, they are ready.
ga: Peanuts shɛɔ dalɛ he beni tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji pod lɛ mli lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ofee klalo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential food for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant stay healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: How do cowpeas or beans help make my farm soil better for the next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny organisms on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped around them in the soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo tsɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn under direct Ghanaian sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa yɛ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small yields when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they compete with each other for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. Giving crops proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei koni amɛkwɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to build large soil mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ agbo dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil so their tubers can expand without resistance. Mounding loosens the earth, creates space for large tuber growth, and prevents water from pooling around the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potatoes koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaawo lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Bɔɔ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. Keeping the soil moist with regular watering and spreading dry grass around the base as mulch keeps the plant cool and saves the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha amɛ daa kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ni oooshwie shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ ŋmeii haa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Growing maize on the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with beans or nuts breaks the pest cycle and refreshes the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he pɔtɛɛ aba. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop harvest even if I water my field regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ miŋmɔji amli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients directly from your main crops. Removing weeds early stops them from consuming the fertilizer and water meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu akatsu nii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from hybrid crop harvests to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid plant harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one high-yielding generation, but the seeds harvested from them lose those special traits. Planting saved hybrid seeds leads to uneven growth and much smaller harvests in the second year.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yinɔ kome koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ ni aaadu lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ akafee nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baafee bibioo kwraa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are insects attacking my pepper plants so much this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi pepper tsei lɛ shii abɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids, thrips, and whiteflies are attracted to pepper plants because their leaves and fruits are soft and full of sap. Weather changes and a lack of beneficial insects that eat pests can cause insect numbers to increase quickly.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids, thrips, kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, mɛi gbalaa pepper tsei ejaakɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛyibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ayibɔ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Will spraying more chemical pesticides on my crop kill insects faster?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii lɛ oya?

english: Spraying too many chemicals can harm your farm. Overusing chemicals can cause insects to build resistance so the spray stops working, and it leaves dangerous residues on your crops that make them unsafe to eat.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye oŋmɔ lɛ awui. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ hela lɛ. Spray lɛ kpa nitsumɔ. ni eshiɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Is there a way to protect my peppers from insects without using expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ abu mi-pepper lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, you can manage insects by practicing crop rotation, placing insect nets over nursery beds, removing weed hides around the field, and using natural remedies like neem leaf extracts.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ kooloi anɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Okɛ kooloi bibii ahe ŋshɔŋlooi awo ŋshɔŋlooi akwɛmɔhe lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem baa mli nu lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why is the pesticide I used last year not working on the bugs on my farm this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛtsu nii nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe afi nɛɛ?

english: Insects can build up tolerance if you use the same chemical over and over. Switching between different types of approved pesticides prevents bugs from becoming immune to the treatment.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ aná tsuishitoo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Tsofai srɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ateŋ tsakemɔ Ebaatsi kooloi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ tsofa lɛ he nii.

english: How long should I wait after spraying chemical pesticides before I harvest my vegetables?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie shi lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani okpa aduawai?

english: Every pesticide has a mandatory waiting period, usually between 7 to 14 days, printed on the container label. Harvesting too early leaves toxic chemicals on the vegetables, making them unsafe for consumers.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi fɛɛ yɛ be ni esa akɛ amɛmɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 teŋ, ni akala yɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei shwieɔ aduawai lɛ amli. ni haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are often caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that spread viruses to the plant while feeding, or by a lack of balanced nutrients and water in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa tsei amli be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. aloo nɔ ni kɛbaa ji niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ja ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Does healthy soil help my plants resist insect attacks naturally?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ kpakpa baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ ni amɛte shi amɛwo kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Yes, well-fertilized and organic-rich soil grows strong plants with thick cell walls, making it harder for pests to chew or suck on the leaves compared to weak plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni awo mli jogbaŋŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni wala yibii ahe gbogboi lɛ mli edɔ lɛ aba. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛbaaye loo amɛnu baai lɛ ahe kɛ akɛto tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe.

english: What do buyers from foreign countries look for before buying vegetables from Ghanaian farmers?
ga: Mɛni majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ dani amɛheɔ aduawai kɛjɛɔ Ghana okwaafoi adɛŋ?

english: Export buyers look for vegetables that are uniform in size, free from insect holes or spots, and completely clear of dangerous chemical pesticide residues.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ taoɔ aduawai ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Ebɛ bu loo kooloi ahe tsɔi. Ni tsofai ni eshwɛ ni jɛɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli lɛ eko bɛ.

english: Why would a buyer reject my harvest even if my vegetables look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mikpamɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mi-aduawai lɛ dara ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Buyers can reject big vegetables if laboratory tests reveal high chemical spray residues inside the fruit, or if there are hidden insect larvae inside that ruin the crop during transit.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpoo aduawai wuji. Kɛji akɛ laboratori mli kaa hetooi tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ fa babaoo yɛ aduawai lɛ amli. Aloo kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ni akɛtee mli ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Can I get a better price if I grow my vegetables with fewer chemical sprays?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni faaa lɛ tsu nii kɛdu aduawai Ani manyɛ maná jara ni hi fe no?

english: Yes, many premium markets and exporters pay higher prices for clean, safe vegetables that use minimal or natural pest controls, because consumers pay more for healthy food.
ga: Hɛɛ, jarayeli hei ni jara wa waa kɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha aduawai ni he tse ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni kɛ tsofai fioo ko pɛ loo adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai tsuɔ nii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miiwo nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa plants from heat stress and keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does my maize crop perform so poorly when I plant it on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Maize heavily consumes nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the ground; rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps replenish nitrogen in the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo aahu akɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee shoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural self-defense mechanism against drought. By shedding leaves, the plant conserves water within its stems and root tubers until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ buɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress tomato plants. When stressed, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy rather than developing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ lɛ, tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why did my yam farm produce very huge leaves but small tubers after I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ naa baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to direct all its energy into lush leaf and stem growth above the ground, leaving very little energy to expand the tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ahi shi koni akɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: The early rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rainy season starts. If the soil dries out completely, young seeds that have just germinated will scorch and die in the hot ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Young, dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and die when rain water collects and stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pepper plant roots need oxygen to breathe. Standing water suffocates and rots the roots, preventing the plant from absorbing nutrients and leading to yellowing leaves and eventual plant death.
ga: Pepper tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbeɔ tso lɛ.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting oil palm seedlings before I can start harvesting fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ wɔdu oil palm dumɔwui lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ wɔmɛ dani wɔje yibii lɛ akpamɔ shishi?

english: Improved hybrid oil palm varieties typically take between 3 to 4 years of proper weeding, watering, and fertilization before they begin producing harvestable fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni ji hybrid oil palm henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani ajieɔ jwɛi jogbaŋŋ, awoɔ amɛ nu ni awoɔ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. dani ebɔi aduawai akui ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ feemɔ

english: Why should I allow grass and natural vegetation to grow on my land for a year or two without farming it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha jwɛi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei krokomɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi loo afii enyɔ ni mikɛtsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow gives soil microbes and vegetation time to decompose and naturally restock organic matter and nutrients into the earth, restoring its productivity for future crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii bibii kɛ aduawai lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii bibii kɛ aduawai lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛfiteɔ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. koni ekɛ yibiiwoo aba ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why does planting cover crops like mucuna help keep weeds off my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ mucilage ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ kponɔ lɛ anaa lɛ?

english: Cover crops spread densely across the ground, blocking sunlight from reaching weed seeds in the soil. This prevents weeds from sprouting while simultaneously conserving soil moisture.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ egbɛ eshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when excessive water drowns the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or well-decomposed manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu babaoo ha amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally restores fertility to the soil for the next crop season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective canopy that keeps them cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ buɔ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.
